name = "entity.alliance_battleship.name"

class = "battleship"
hull_id = "AEV-2001"
power_rating = 120

# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] Unratified — the heaviest shipped
# hull.
mass = 55000.0
# Player identity (the `player` tag + `playerShip` radar icon) is NOT authored
# here — it is injected onto the selected hull at the player game-start spawn
# (see `player_ship_identity` in `src/server_app.rs`). A world-spawned copy of
# this hull is an ordinary NPC ship, so it must not masquerade as the player.
tags = [ "ship" ]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"

# ── Composition (issues #875, #876) ──────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Everything below `includes` is what this hull SPECIALISES; the shared AI
# doctrine it flies comes from the fragment library under
# `assets/entities/fragments/ai/`, whole policy block at a time, and is tuned
# here by PARAMETER only.
#
# Order is significant: fragments merge in declared order and this file merges
# last, so the includer always wins. `movement_artillery.toml` is listed after
# `fleet_baseline.toml` because it REPLACES the baseline's two travel axes and
# its Impulse policy.
#
# Resolution happens at authoring time. The runtime never sees a fragment — it
# sees one resolved document, and PRD #774's "every AI-capable fine system
# declares a policy" is satisfied by that document, not by this file.
includes = [
  "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
  "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml",
  "fragments/ai/movement_artillery.toml",
]

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_battleship_recreated.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 1.5
length = 4
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Default doctrine for a backfilled/unmanned player battleship (#842 — the other
# half of #838's human/AI symmetry). See the fuller note on `alliance_cruiser.toml`;
# authoring `[behaviour]` is what makes `spawn_entity` attach the
# `BehaviourSection` on the player game-start path, so a backfilled battleship
# proactively engages instead of only returning fire once hit.
#
#   Destroy (45) — UNTARGETED (no `directive_target`) → licenses the
#                  nearest-hostile scan and proactive engagement.
#   Hold    (20) — no directive when no hostile is visible: the helm holds station.
#
# Engage priority stays LOW (45) so scenario `spawn_entity` overrides (Destroy at
# 80) merge by id and dominate (#842 AC3). No Retreat — a capital defender holds
# the line. `maintain_range = 38` is the widest of the four hulls: the battleship
# is slow (max_speed 10) and stands off, keeping the enemy inside its 40-unit
# phasers and 50-unit heavy blaster rather than closing to knife-fight range.
#
# `imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6` (issue #780 AC4): see the fuller
# note on `alliance_cruiser.toml`. Every shipped hull left this at its 1.0
# (effectively off) default, so avoidance only ever bent travel and never
# actually turned the ship's facing away from a closing obstacle — the fix for
# the "AI flies through asteroid fields" report against the backfilled player
# hull. Worth watching on the battleship specifically: it is the slowest hull
# (max_speed 10), so an override that fires only just in time has the least
# room here to actually out-turn what it is dodging.
[behaviour]
imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id             = "destroy-hostiles"
text           = "entity.alliance_battleship.behaviour.doctrine.destroy_hostiles.text"
directive_kind = "Destroy"
base_priority  = 45.0
target_speed   = 0.8
maintain_range = 38.0

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "hold-station"
text          = "entity.alliance_battleship.behaviour.doctrine.hold_station.text"
base_priority = 20.0
target_speed  = 0.0

# ── The tactical radar, and why it is 100 rather than 75 ─────────────────────
#
# This is the ACQUISITION horizon, not a reach: it is what the Tactical officer's
# scope shows and — the half that bites — the range through which a target lock
# may be taken, by a human at this console or by a backfilled `ai_target_selection`
# ranking candidates. Since #955 nothing scales a gun's reach, but a lock is still
# a PRECONDITION for firing, so a horizon authored under this hull's guns would
# cap them again by the back door.
#
# The number below is the one that clears them, and since #952 it is the WHOLE
# story: that issue retired the `sensors` power group, so
# `ModifierSlot::RadarRange` has no power producer at all and this horizon is
# exactly what is written here unless the radar takes hull damage or the ship is
# inside a dampening region.
#
# It was not always, and the history is why the figure moved from 100 to 66.7
# without the hull's behaviour changing at all. Until #952 the slot was driven
# off SENSORS, this hull rested that group at 1 to keep its four groups inside
# the reactor's sustainable total, and level 1 folded to ×0.667 — so the live
# horizon was two thirds of whatever was authored here, for the hull's entire
# life, because #955 had already removed the only rule that raised the group.
# 100 was chosen in #955 to put the LIVE horizon at 66.7; with the multiplier
# gone, 66.7 is simply written down.
#
# At the pre-#955 value of 75 the live horizon worked out to 50.000002, against
# a `heavy-fore` blaster authoring `range = 50.0` and an artillery envelope
# authoring `max_artillery_range = 50.0` below. The doctrine's `shadow` and
# `reposition` legs are entered on `range_to_target > max_artillery_range` —
# exactly where the candidate filter culls every contact including the retention
# one — so the hull dropped its lock at the instant its own doctrine stepped out
# to reacquire, and a gun line that cannot hold a lock past its own envelope is
# a gun line that cannot fight the pattern it was authored to fly.
#
# 66.7 keeps a third of daylight over both. Pinned fleet-wide by
# `every_hulls_acquisition_horizon_clears_its_longest_gun_at_rest`
# (`src/modifiers/coordination.rs`), which walks every shipped hull and demands a
# fifth of daylight beyond its longest gun — retune this down and that test names
# the file and the number to write instead.
# Re-authored by issue #952, which retired the `sensors` power group and with it
# the only thing that ever scaled this number. Every tactical radar range in the
# fleet was tuned against a live horizon of `range x 0.667` — the rung those
# hulls rested `sensors` at — so leaving the authored figures alone would have
# widened every acquisition horizon in the fleet by half, silently, as a side
# effect of a reactor change. The multiplier is folded into the number instead:
# the live horizon is unchanged, and it is now simply what is written here.
[weapons_console.radar]
range = 66.7
shows = [ "player", "ship", "asteroid", "station", "missile", "torpedo", "region" ]
selects = [ "ship", "station", "asteroid" ]

# Standard fore + aft phaser banks — fore bank deals double-damage (8.0 dps = 2× Cruiser's 4.0)
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "fore"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 270
auto_arc_deg = 180
beam_range = 40
beam_damage_per_sec = 8.0
beam_duration_secs = 6
cooldown_secs = 6
beam_color = [ 0.25, 0.75, 1, 1 ]
marker = "phasers_fore"

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed
  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below
  # is the SAME text on every armed hull in the fleet. Only this threshold
  # differs: 1 means "hold fire until the captain calls red alert", 0 means
  # "always armed". This hull has a captain's console (human, or an AI backfill
  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "aft"
facing_deg = 180
fire_arc_deg = 270
auto_arc_deg = 180
beam_range = 40
beam_damage_per_sec = 4
beam_duration_secs = 6
cooldown_secs = 6
beam_color = [ 0.25, 0.75, 1, 1 ]
marker = "phasers_aft"

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed
  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below
  # is the SAME text on every armed hull in the fleet. Only this threshold
  # differs: 1 means "hold fire until the captain calls red alert", 0 means
  # "always armed". This hull has a captain's console (human, or an AI backfill
  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0

  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

# Heavy blaster bank: hold-to-fire, twin fore barrels with a patterned attack
# (issue #765). The timed pattern alternates single-barrel shots, then finishes
# with a simultaneous both-barrel volley:
#   t=0.0s  → barrel 0 (port)
#   t=0.6s  → barrel 1 (starboard)
#   t=1.2s  → barrels 0 AND 1 together (simultaneous)

id = "heavy-fore"
marker = "blaster_fore"
barrels = [ "blaster_fore_port", "blaster_fore_starboard" ]
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 22.5
charge_time_secs = 3.0
volley_count = 3
volley_interval_secs = 1.0
cooldown_secs = 12.0
projectile_speed = 35.0
collision_radius = 3.0
visual_scale = 3.0
damage = 80
shield_pierce = 0.15
recoil_impulse = 6.0
screenshake_magnitude = 1.0
range = 50.0

[[weapons_console.blaster_banks.pattern]]
barrels = [ 0 ]
offset_secs = 0.0

[[weapons_console.blaster_banks.pattern]]
barrels = [ 1 ]
offset_secs = 0.6

[[weapons_console.blaster_banks.pattern]]
barrels = [ 0, 1 ]
offset_secs = 1.2

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Mirror of the phaser banks on the `blaster_fire`
  # channel: unconditional, with the host still enforcing availability,
  # cooldown, range, arc and target validity before the volley starts.
  [weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed
  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below
  # is the SAME text on every armed hull in the fleet. Only this threshold
  # differs: 1 means "hold fire until the captain calls red alert", 0 means
  # "always armed". This hull has a captain's console (human, or an AI backfill
  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "blaster_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_blaster"

# 5-tube torpedo layout: 3 fore + 2 aft, volley_max=3, 30-round magazine, burst_interval=0.5s
#
# The two damage fields are ALTERNATIVES, not two halves of one payload
# (issue #929): a round meets the one arc it flew into, and that arc's own
# reading picks which of them it delivers. `damage_shields = 4` if the arc is up
# — offered to it through the same absorption seam a beam takes — and
# `damage_hull = 40` whole on the plating if it is down. Both numbers are
# unchanged and both keep their meaning; what changed is that the 40 is now
# CONDITIONAL, and the ten-to-one gap between them is precisely what the tubes'
# `fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0` guard below is buying.
#
# This hull's effective torpedo output therefore FALLS against a screened target
# and is unchanged against a stripped one, which is the intended shape: it has
# two phaser banks and a heavy bow blaster to open an arc with, and thirty rounds
# to spend once one is open.
[torpedoes]
count = 30
damage_hull = 40
damage_shields = 4
speed = 15
turn_rate_deg_per_sec = 45
lifespan = 20
load_time = 10
detonation_radius = 5
burst_interval_secs = 0.5
# How many rounds an AI-crewed Tactical keeps in each tube (the AI issues the
# same SetTorpedoVolleyTarget a human console does — see `ai_torpedo_load`).
# Deliberately below `volley_max = 3`: five tubes at full volley would park 15
# of this hull's 30 rounds inside the tubes, leaving the magazine half empty
# and every reload competing for the same stock. Two per tube keeps a standing
# 10-round broadside with 20 in reserve.
ai_volley_target = 2

[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "fore-port"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 90
load_time = 3
volley_max = 3
marker = "torpedo_port"

  # Load + launch policy for this tube (issue #782), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Two rules on two DIFFERENT channels, so they never
  # contend: keep the tube loaded, and launch when the alert is up AND the arc
  # the round would strike is down. Loaded state, magazine stock, target
  # validity, range and arc stay host-side gates.
  #
  # `fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0` is the fleet's torpedo doctrine —
  # "phasers strip the shields, torpedoes finish the hull" — and issue #956
  # moved it HERE from `auto_fire_torpedo`, where it was a Rust gate sitting
  # upstream of every policy: no doctrine could authorise a round while the
  # striking arc was up, and none could retune the threshold. It is an HP
  # reading rather than a boolean, resolved per-arc through the target's own arc
  # router, so this gate and the eventual hit agree about which arc is in the
  # way. A hull that wants to spend rounds differently edits this line;
  # `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` is the worked example of tightening it further,
  # and `idle = true` of declining launches altogether.
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed
  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below
  # is the SAME text on every armed hull in the fleet. Only this threshold
  # differs: 1 means "hold fire until the captain calls red alert", 0 means
  # "always armed". This hull has a captain's console (human, or an AI backfill
  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"

[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "fore-starboard"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 90
load_time = 3
volley_max = 3
marker = "torpedo_starboard"

  # Load + launch policy for this tube (issue #782), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Two rules on two DIFFERENT channels, so they never
  # contend: keep the tube loaded, and launch when the alert is up AND the arc
  # the round would strike is down. Loaded state, magazine stock, target
  # validity, range and arc stay host-side gates.
  #
  # `fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0` is the fleet's torpedo doctrine —
  # "phasers strip the shields, torpedoes finish the hull" — and issue #956

# own ship gets the `playerShip` icon injected at spawn (see hull tags note).

[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.alliance_battleship.power_groups.helm.label"
# `min_level` is the COMMANDABLE floor: the lowest level any operator, human or
# AI, may order this group to. `PowerSystem` stores it per group and clamps
# every order to it — `set_group_allocation`, `decrease`, `restore` and the AI
# planner's `plan_allocation` all read this number (issue #1395 — before that it
# was a drawing hint the engine ignored, and the console's pip row is still the
# other thing it decides).
#
# It reads 1 because Helm must never be switched off: a ship with no power to
# the drive cannot manoeuvre out of anything, and losing the ability to run away
# is not a trade a Power officer should be able to make with one press. Turning
# it down to 1 to free a point for the 8-point budget IS a legal order, so rung
# 1 has to be reachable and drawn. NOMINAL — the rung whose multiplier is 1.0 —
# is 2, and that is `default_level`, where the group boots.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.alliance_battleship.power_groups.weapons.label"
# `min_level = 1`: the COMMANDABLE floor, as on Helm above — the lowest level
# this group may be ordered to, clamped to by the whole allocation API since
# issue #1395. No group on the battleship may be taken COLD; only the
# destroyer's and the cruiser's weapons author `min_level = 0`. A capital ship
# is the one hull whose guns nobody may switch off with a single Engineering
# order: it is here to keep shooting.
#
# STANDING NOTE (issue #1398): that sentence used to end "…and the restraint
# those two smaller hulls express by going cold, this one expresses by holding
# fire." The captain's Weapons Hold is retired, so a battleship now has NO way
# to express restraint short of standing down from Red Alert. That may be the
# right answer for a capital ship; it is at least a live question, and the only
# change that would settle it the other way is authoring `min_level = 0` here —
# a decision for whoever owns this hull's doctrine, not one #1398 took.
#
# NOMINAL (×1.0) is 2, which is where this group boots; dropping it to 1 is a
# legal order that spends the freed point elsewhere, so rung 1 has to be drawn.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.shields]
label = "entity.alliance_battleship.power_groups.shields.label"
# Nominal at 2 alongside Helm and Weapons: those three groups make the
# sustainable resting total of 6. Higher levels buy shield regeneration.
# `min_level = 1` is the COMMANDABLE floor (see Helm above): shields may be
# turned down to 1 but not switched off. Nothing on this hull authors 0.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── AI: what is composed, what stays inline (issues #875, #876) ──────────────
#
# The five target selectors, the stateless helm axes, Shields focus, Power
# allocation and the Comms response all come from
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. The Captain's red-alert doctrine comes from
# `fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml`. Engines and Steering come from
# `fragments/ai/movement_artillery.toml` — the artillery class doctrine,
# posture-gated, which is what makes this hull hold position at range while the
# alert is down and establish a predictive firing position once it is up.
#
# That fragment also owns `[helm_console.impulse_ai]`, as an explicit IDLE: the
# hold band lies inside the impulse drive's default cruise window, and an engaged
# drive hard-overrides commanded throttle, so the hull would otherwise sail
# through its own gun line at eight times cruise. Boost is NOT composed: the
# fleet baseline's `idle = true` stands and this hull's AI leaves the drive it
# mounts cold.
#
# Three things deliberately stay inline, and each for a reason about PRESENCE
# rather than about taste — authoring a sub-table brings its parent into
# existence, and the spawner gates capabilities on those parents:
#
#   * `[torpedoes.ai]` below. A fragment carrying it would create `[torpedoes]`
#     on every hull that included the fragment, and a `[torpedoes]` table with no
#     `[[torpedoes.tubes]]` is a torpedo system with zero tubes.
#   * the per-bank and per-tube fire gates, up with their banks. Those arrays
#     merge by `id`, so a shared fragment could only name ids it cannot know, and
#     an unmatched id APPENDS a weapon with no geometry.
#   * `[power]` and `[shields_console.base]`, up above. The fragment library
#     carries the POLICIES that read them, never the hardware.
#
# For the same reason no fragment this hull includes carries `tags`,
# `repair_team_count` or `[[hull.system_hull]]`: `tags` UNIONS on compose, so a
# fragment carrying `"npc"` would silently flip this hull out of
# `is_player_flyable`, and the other two would hand this hull equipment it never
# authored or erase the system-hull entries it did. `[[shield_arc]]` is on the
# same list, and this hull's five arcs are the reason it has to be.

# Torpedo magazine — two axes on one authored block.
#
# GRANT: always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The offline +
# non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this rule is the authored arbiter
# layered on top, and it is where a hull would ration rounds between its tubes.
#
# CONSERVATION (issue #943): whether a launch the ship has already authorised may
# SPEND its round here, or should hold it for later in the mission. Resolved
# inside `handle_fire_torpedo`, the one consumer of an admitted `FireTorpedo`, so
# a human Tactical operator and an AI backfill meet this guard identically — the
# per-tube `torpedo_launch` doctrine gates only the AI, and a gate that
# constrains NPCs alone is how a player empties the whole magazine into wave one.
#
# `rounds_per_threat` is a host reading, not an authored number: every round the
# ship still HAS — the magazine PLUS whatever is already parked in the tubes —
# divided by the mission threat still ahead, which the SCENARIO publishes as the
# world counter `mission_threat_remaining`. A world that publishes none leaves
# the ratio unbounded and this rule always fires, because pacing is something a
# mission asks for and never something a hull decides for itself.
#
# `min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5` reads "keep one round for every TWO things still
# coming". Before retuning it, understand what kind of gate it is: a ONE-WAY
# LATCH. `rounds_aboard` only ever FALLS inside a mission, and the threat count
# only falls when something DIES — so a hull that dips under its own reserve
# stops firing, stops killing the thing that would bring the count down, and
# never climbs back over the line. Whatever is authored here is not a soft
# brake. It is a floor the ship must never be pushed below mid-mission.
#
# 0.5 is chosen for the margin it leaves, not for a tidy identity:
#
#   * The middle of the mission stays open. Over every position combat_test can
#     put this hull in while it still carries half its payload or more, the
#     reserve clears at least 4 rounds — two full volleys — against the wave in
#     front of it. A wave that survives one volley is a wave that never dies,
#     and a wave that never dies freezes the threat count and the latch with it.
#   * Nothing is stranded. At the last unit of threat the floor is half a round,
#     so anything still aboard clears the gate and can be spent on the last
#     fight. A reserve measured against the magazine COUNTER rather than the
#     rounds aboard strands the parked volley whatever this number is, because
#     the counter is debited the moment a tube starts loading.
#
# What it trades away is the front of the mission. The floor at eight published
# waves is 4 rounds rather than 8, so an engagement lasting as long as the hull
# is willing to keep shooting may now take 10 of the 12 rounds while the whole
# schedule is still published, where 1.0 capped it at 6. That ceiling is a
# licence rather than a forecast — flown for real the destroyer spends 6 across
# that stretch either way, because the engagement ends before the gate does —
# but it is what 0.5 permits, and it is the price of the margin above.
#
# The tidy identity is what 1.0 bought (issue #943): the reserve came to exactly
# one round at the last unit of threat, so on paper nothing could ever be
# stranded. It shipped with ZERO margin and it broke. Against the old asteroid
# layout the destroyer bottomed out at exactly 7 rounds against 7 remaining
# waves — a ratio of exactly 1.0, the last reading the gate still passes. #946
# reshuffled which rock lands in which cell (same radii, same split), that moved
# the engagement by one round, the ratio fell under, the latch shut, and
# combat_test's wave chain stalled at wave 2 with the hull holding rounds it
# would never fire.
#
# All of it is measured, not asserted by hand.
# `the_shipped_destroyer_spends_its_whole_payload_across_the_eight_wave_mission`
# (`src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs`) walks this doctrine through the real
# torpedo system over the world's whole authored schedule, INCLUDING a wave that
# outlives the engagement fought against it, and states the latch directly on
# the doctrine.
# `combat_test_paces_the_player_magazine_against_the_whole_eight_wave_threat`
# (`tests/headless_runner.rs`) flies it for real and prints the magazine's
# shape bucketed by remaining threat, (entered, lowest) per bucket:
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 2), 6: (2, 2), 5: (2, 2)}. Read a bucket as a STRETCH OF
# THE MISSION rather than as one engagement — since #960 a wave arrives on its
# own clock whether or not the last one is dead, so the top bucket spans wave 1
# and the opening of wave 2, and bottoms lower than the death-gated chain used
# to show. Ten of the twelve rounds go while six or more waves are still
# published; the last two then sit under the floor (2/6 and 2/5 are both below
# 0.5) until the count reaches 4. At 1.0 the same run reads
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 6)} and stops there: the latch shuts the moment wave 1
# dies, and wave 2 never does.
#
# `sole_objective_count = 1` is the carve-out, and it counts NAMED Destroy
# targets rather than doctrine entries. A world's `spawn_entity` override
# APPENDS its brief to the template's standing orders — doctrine reconciles by
# `id`, and an instance override may not remove what the template authored — so
# combat_test's raid cruisers carry their template's untargeted
# `destroy-hostiles` alongside the `assault-starbase` the world hands them: two
# entries, one named target, one engagement they will not outlive. Those spend
# freely. A hull whose brief names no target reads 0 and paces — which is the
# player's destroyer, the ship #943 was filed about.
[torpedoes.ai]
param = { min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5, sole_objective_count = 1.0 }

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_magazine_grant"
when = "true"
verb = "grant_torpedo_round"

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_conservation"
when = "fact(targeted_objective_count) == param(sole_objective_count) or fact(rounds_per_threat) >= param(min_rounds_per_threat)"
verb = "release_torpedo"

# ── Doctrine tuning: parameters only (issue #876 AC3) ────────────────────────
#
# The whole specialisation of a shared class doctrine, and the entire authoring
# interface a hull has to it. No rule, state or transition is restated here: the
# `param` table is an ordinary TOML table and deep-merges, so naming one key
# retunes that threshold and leaves the machine alone.
#
# Both range params are restated on both axes because they are two INDEPENDENT
# copies of one machine that agree by reading the same facts — a copy left on the
# fragment's default would reach `hold` at a different range from the other and
# the axes would disagree about which leg they are flying.
#
# The envelope belongs to the ARTILLERY PIECE, and this hull's is the 50-unit
# heavy bow blaster rather than the 200-unit gun the class default was sized
# against. So the outer edge comes in to 50 — where the bolt stops existing — and
# the inner edge to 45, the same ninety per cent of it the class authors. At 45
# the target sits inside the heavy blaster the doctrine exists to point and just
# outside the 40-unit close-defence phasers, which join in only if it closes;
# nothing in the doctrine gives ground when it does.
#
# The band still lies inside the impulse drive's default cruise window (engage
# 200, cancel 40), which is what makes the fragment's `impulse_ai` idle
# load-bearing on this hull rather than superstition.
#
# The DEFENSIVE ring is not retuned. `safe_range_margin` is derived from the
# TARGET's reach rather than from this hull's, so the class default already puts
# this ship well outside anything that could shoot at it, and there is no
# battleship-specific statement to make about a number that is not about the
# battleship. Two keys per axis is the whole authoring interface this hull has.
[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
max_artillery_range = 50.0
artillery_hold_range = 45.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
max_artillery_range = 50.0
artillery_hold_range = 45.0

# ── AI sensing horizon ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Authored, not defaulted. `AiProfile.sensor_range` is what `ai::lod::evaluate_lod`
# measures an NPC copy of this hull against: a ship further than
# `sensor_range * 1.2` from the player for `LOD_DWELL_SECS` loses
# `AiHighFidelity`, and with it every helm/captain/weapons decider it carries.
# `simulate_low_lod_ships` then dead-reckons it on its LAST heading and speed
# for ever — a hull demoted mid-manoeuvre at speed simply leaves the scenario
# and never comes back.
#
# Every Harrow hull has always authored this (`ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`
# 400, `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` 350). No Alliance hull did, so an Alliance
# hull spawned as an NPC fell to the 100.0 Rust fallback in
# `entities::spawner` — INSIDE its own authored doctrine envelope, whose
# `commit_range`/`safe_range_margin` legs work out past 120 units. The value
# below is sized to the doctrine this hull flies, so the ship stays decided-for
# across its own manoeuvre.
[ai_profile]
aggression = 0.7
sensor_range = 400.0
base_files.assets/entities/alliance_courier.toml:
# Alliance Courier — a compact two-player hull.
#
# Captain owns command, Comms, Navigation, Power, Repair and Shields. Tactical

# client derives the data for each station from those TOML assignments.

class = "courier"
hull_id = "AEV-0912"
# Independent of the (absent) [power] block: feeds the lobby card and

# >=90 / >=100 bonus-spawn gates, which is the point of flying solo.
power_rating = 25
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] Unratified — the lightest shipped
# combat hull.
mass = 3500.0
# Player identity (the `player` tag + `playerShip` radar icon) is NOT authored
# here — it is injected onto the selected hull at the player game-start spawn
# (see `player_ship_identity` in `src/server_app.rs`). A world-spawned copy of

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Default doctrine for a backfilled/unmanned player courier (#842 — the other half
# of #838's human/AI symmetry). See the fuller note on `alliance_cruiser.toml`;
# authoring `[behaviour]` is what makes `spawn_entity` attach the
# `BehaviourSection` on the player game-start path, so a backfilled courier
# proactively engages instead of only returning fire once hit.
#
#   Destroy (40) — UNTARGETED (no `directive_target`) → licenses the
#                  nearest-hostile scan and proactive engagement. Priority a notch
#                  below the warship hulls: the courier is a lightly-armed scout,
#                  willing to fight but not the fleet's spearhead.
#   Hold    (20) — no directive when no hostile is visible: the helm holds station.
#
# Engage priority stays LOW (40) so scenario `spawn_entity` overrides (Destroy at
# 80) merge by id and dominate (#842 AC3). No Retreat authored. `maintain_range =
# 22` keeps the courier inside its single 35-unit fore blaster's range.
#
# `imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6` (issue #780 AC4): see the fuller
# note on `alliance_cruiser.toml`. Every shipped hull left this at its 1.0
# (effectively off) default, so avoidance only ever bent travel and never
# actually turned the ship's facing away from a closing obstacle — the fix for
# the "AI flies through asteroid fields" report against the backfilled player
# hull.
[behaviour]
imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id             = "destroy-hostiles"
text           = "entity.alliance_courier.behaviour.doctrine.destroy_hostiles.text"
directive_kind = "Destroy"
base_priority  = 40.0
target_speed   = 0.9
maintain_range = 22.0

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "hold-station"
text          = "entity.alliance_courier.behaviour.doctrine.hold_station.text"
base_priority = 20.0
target_speed  = 0.0

# ── Per-system hull ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One entry per damageable system, plus "core" — the ownerless bucket that
# RepairTarget::Core dispatches to. Shield-arc hull comes from
# [[shield_arc]].hull_max_hp, not from here.

# ── Durability ladder (#915 tuning pass) ─────────────────────────────────────
# The whole fleet was re-pegged in one pass, because these numbers only mean
# anything relative to each other. Dynasty hulls carry a monolithic
# `[hull] hull_integrity`; Alliance hulls have none, and their equivalent pool
# is the SUM of the per-system `max_hp` below. Shields sit on top of both.
#
#   Dynasty   destroyer 200 | patrol/cruiser 300 | warhawk 400
#   Alliance  courier 200 | destroyer 300 | cruiser 500 | battleship 800
#
# The Alliance figures were reached by scaling each hull's authored system HP
# proportionally, so the relative weighting between systems is unchanged.
#
# RADAR SYSTEMS CARRY NO HULL. `helm-radar`, `tactical-radar` and `sensor-radar`
# have no `[[hull.system_hull]]` entry on any Alliance hull, so they cannot be
# damaged, disabled or repaired — their points were redistributed across the
# surviving systems and the totals above are unchanged. The code that reacts to
# a downed radar (weapons-console arc gating, the helm radar overlay, the
# captain's repair targeting) is untouched and still fires for any hull that
# authors those entries; these four simply never trigger it.
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "core"
display_name = "system_hull.core.display_name"
max_hp = 32
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.10

# Re-authored by issue #952, which retired the `sensors` power group and with it

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than

  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below

  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

# ── Power ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Small-hull values are authored here rather than inferred from ship class.
[power]
capacity = 35
sustainable_total = 6
max_commanded_total = 8
# Index 3 (a ship-wide total of 6) is +1, not a 0. 6 is this hull's RESTING
# total (`helm 2 + weapons 2 + shields 2`), so a 0 rate there would mean
# a courier sitting quietly at anchor never recovers a point of charge — the
# resting draw must recharge, however slowly.
rates = [ 3, 2, 1, 1, -1, -3 ]
emergency_threshold = 10

# The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003), same numbers as
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` — see that file's param note for the full
# reasoning. In short, AT COMBAT STATIONS UNDER THRUST (helm's elevate needs red
# alert AND `thrust >= thrust_threshold`; weapons' needs the alert): >= 50 the
# ship holds helm 3 / weapons 3 / shields 2 = 8; below 50 the helm hold and
# elevate guards both read false and its `priority = 0` baseline takes the
# channel back at 2 (total 7, a slow drain on this hull's `rates`); below 25
# weapons does the same (total 6, which index 3 above authors as +1, so the
# reserve REFILLS). Away from combat stations the ship rests at 6 throughout.
#
# Each channel sheds and RESTORES at different charges — 50/60 for helm, 25/35
# for weapons — and the `power_<group>` clause on each hold rule is what tells
# the two apart with no policy state. One threshold per channel would be both
# the shed floor and the re-elevate floor, and the AI would flip that channel on
# every tick the charge sat on it. The battery therefore oscillates across the
# 25–35 band and — with the reactor undamaged — never reaches 0, the charge at
# which `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to 1 and locks the reactor until
# `emergency_threshold` is back. A Disabled or Destroyed reactor is a different
# story and out of this ladder's scope: the AI stops operating power at all
# while the reactor keeps integrating at the last commanded total.
#
# The hold rules carry the SAME trigger clauses as the elevate rules they sit
# above (helm's red alert AND thrust, weapons' red alert), not only the shed
# floor, and that is deliberate: one tick with the trigger false sheds the
# channel exactly as a battery breach would, and the channel cannot climb back
# on the trigger returning alone while the charge is under the restore floor —
# the elevate rule that would re-raise it is gated on the RESTORE floor, not
# the shed one. A one-way ratchet on trigger flap for as long as the reserve is
# in the band — elevated posture belongs to combat stations, not to an alert or
# a throttle that blinked for a single tick.
#
# AI-shed only: a human Power officer's `SetPowerGroupAllocation` is applied by
# `handle_power_messages`, which never reads `battery_pct`, so these floors do
# not constrain the human seam at all.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair, the mirror of the battery pair one axis over: elevate at
# 0.7, release at 0.6. Without it a throttle DWELLING near the single threshold
# strobes helm 3<->2 at the AI tick rate, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 MaxSpeed swing --
# a ship thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn. [ai] The
# ratifiable quantity is the BAND WIDTH (0.1), not either endpoint. See
# fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml for the full note and the measurement.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's shed/restore pair.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair. At the 10 this hull shipped with before issue #1003 it shed its
# last point with 3.5 charge of its 35-point battery left; 25 sheds while a
# quarter of the reserve is still in hand.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm: elevate to 3 under sustained thrust with a healthy battery, AT RED
# ALERT, hold it down to the shed floor, else 2. The `red_alert` guard keeps
# ordinary transit (which also commands near-max thrust) off the elevated
# allocation — see the identical rules' comments in
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` for the brownout this fixes and for what
# the hold rule's `power_helm` clause is doing. Must stay byte-identical to that
# fragment's `helm` rules: this hull composes no fragment and owns its own copy
# (see the header above).
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons: elevate to 3 on red alert once the battery is back over the restore
# floor, hold it down to the shed floor, else 2.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.alliance_courier.power_groups.helm.label"
# `min_level` is the COMMANDABLE floor: the lowest level any operator, human or
# AI, may order this group to. `PowerSystem` stores it per group and clamps
# every order to it — `set_group_allocation`, `decrease`, `restore` and the AI
# planner's `plan_allocation` all read this number (issue #1395 — before that it
# was a drawing hint the engine ignored, and the console's pip row is still the
# other thing it decides).
#
# It reads 1 because Helm must never be switched off: a courier that cannot
# move is a courier that cannot do the one thing it is for, and on a hull this
# fragile the drive IS the defence. Turning it down to 1 to free a point for
# the 8-point budget IS a legal order, so rung 1 has to be reachable and drawn.
# NOMINAL — the rung whose multiplier is 1.0 — is 2, and that is
# `default_level`, where the group boots.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.alliance_courier.power_groups.weapons.label"
# `min_level = 1`: the COMMANDABLE floor, as on Helm above — the lowest level
# this group may be ordered to, clamped to by the whole allocation API since
# issue #1395. No group on the courier may be taken COLD; only the destroyer's
# and the cruiser's weapons author `min_level = 0`. Going cold is a statement a
# warship makes about restraint, and this hull carries too little armament for
# switching it off to read as anything but a malfunction. Since issue #1398
# retired the captain's Weapons Hold that also means the courier has no
# restraint lever at all — see the standing note on the battleship, which the
# same question applies to.
#
# NOMINAL (×1.0) is 2, which is where this group boots; dropping it to 1 is a
# legal order that spends the freed point elsewhere, so rung 1 has to be drawn.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.shields]
label = "entity.alliance_courier.power_groups.shields.label"
# Nominal at 2 alongside Helm and Weapons: those three groups make the
# sustainable resting total of 6. Higher levels buy shield regeneration.
# `min_level = 1` is the COMMANDABLE floor (see Helm above): shields may be
# turned down to 1 but not switched off. Nothing on this hull authors 0.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4
