# ── AI target selectors (PRD #774 US7, issue #885b) ───────────────────────────
#
# The five per-system target selectors, AUTHORED rather than synthesised. Each
# answers "which entity is this system's target?" for whoever operates the
# station, and each reproduces exactly what the matching
# `default_*_target_selector_config()` in `src/entities/config.rs` used to
# invent at spawn. The reasoning behind every number lives on those functions
# and on the constant blocks above them; `default_ai_policy_pins` spawns every
# shipped hull and compares the two, so a transcription slip fails the build
# rather than quietly changing how this ship picks targets.
#
# All five attach on `[behaviour]` ALONE, not on the console section they name,
# so a hull owes all five whether or not it declares `[sensors_console]`,
# `[navigation_console]`, `[repair]` or `[comms_console]`.
#
# `horizon` is a static outer bound, NOT the live range gate — each host owns
# its own (Sensors' damage-scaled radar reach, Comms' authored `[comms].range`).
# Do not "helpfully" tighten it to look like a range.
#
# A score term's magnitude is its own `weight` field. A `param` entry exists
# only where a `when` guard names one: Repair's `deficit_band_*` and Comms'
# `score_band_*` are the whole set.

# Sensors — rank detectable hostiles by which SOURCE surfaced them:
# combat-lock >> objective >> radar. `switch_margin` is 0 because the gaps
# between the tiers ARE the anti-thrash mechanism.
[sensors_console.selector]
sources = ["combat-lock", "objective-destroy", "radar-contacts", "debris-assessment"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
# The `source_debris_assess` disjunct (issue #1347) is what lets a NON-hostile
# contact reach this seat at all: a moving hazard has no faction, so the
# `hostile` test that gates every other source refuses it. Kept byte-for-byte
# identical to the shared `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` selector, which is
# where the reasoning lives (this hull authors it inline).
#
# INERT ON THIS HULL AS IT STANDS, and deliberately left declared. This ship
# authors no `[scan]` table, and `operate_sensors_ai` offers the debris source
# no contact a hull's own suite could not take a reading of - so the terms below
# score nothing here until somebody gives it an instrument, at which point they
# start working with no further edit. Diverging this block from the shared
# fragment to say so would cost that, and would put a second, subtly different
# Sensors doctrine in the fleet.
eligibility = "candidate_fact(detectable) > 0 and (candidate_fact(hostile) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_debris_assess) > 0)"

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_combat_lock) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0"
weight = 100.0

# Working down a debris field (issue #1347): a hazard outranks an incidental
# radar hostile but never a named objective, and the unread bonus is what makes
# the seat go to the next unknown rather than admire the rock it just read.
# 10 + 15 = 25 < 40, so a confirmed-but-read contact never displaces an unread
# one. See `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`.
[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_debris_assess) > 0"
weight = 10.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_unassessed) > 0"
weight = 30.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_confirmed) > 0"
weight = 15.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_radar) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# ── The WEAPONS DOCTRINE: which gun the ship turns to present (issue #956) ────
#
# The fleet baseline, authored inline because this hull composes no fragments.
# The CHANNEL is the rank and the VERB is the family: beams first, then
# blasters, then tubes — the order that used to be a Rust array in
# `tick_weapons_arc_request`. The full reasoning lives in
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`; a courier has no reason to depart from it,
# and the ranks naming families it does not carry are inert (a family with no
# emitters never qualifies).

[weapons_console.ai]

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_first"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_phasers_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_second"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_blasters_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_third"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_torpedoes_to_bear"

# Tactical — the ship's firing target. `combat-lock` is deliberately ABSENT from
# the sources: it is Tactical's own output, so unioning it would be circular.
# The current lock reaches the ranking as the host-pushed `source_retained`
# retention candidate, which is why that marker appears in the guards but in no
# source list.
#
# PRECEDENCE INVARIANT — terms are additive and one candidate can carry several
# markers at once, so the weights are sized to beat the maximum non-objective
# stack by more than `switch_margin`: 500 + 200 + 100 + 1 = 801 < 1000 - 50.
# A named Destroy objective therefore always wins AND survives hysteresis
# retention, while `retained` still exceeds `last_attacker` so an established
# engagement is not broken off by a fresh attacker. Retune against that
# inequality, not term by term.
[weapons_console.selector]
sources = ["sensors-designation", "objective-destroy", "last-attacker", "radar-contacts", "objective-operate", "confirmed-debris-threat"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 50.0
# The two urgency bands are read against these, in seconds of dead-reckoned
# time-to-impact (issue #1347). An inline table because a sub-table header here
# would swallow every sibling key below it, `eligibility` included. Kept in step
# with `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`, where the reasoning lives.
param = { debris_pressing_secs = 60.0, debris_urgent_secs = 25.0 }
# Independent revalidation: `detectable` is required of everything, and beyond
# that a candidate is engageable either because the host already vetted it
# (objective order / last attacker / retained lock) OR because it is
# independently hostile. That disjunction honours a mission naming a factionless
# target while refusing a FRIENDLY Sensors designation, which carries only
# `source_sensors_designation`.
#
# The final `source_operate` disjunct (issue #1162) is DIRECTIVE-GATED: the
# `objective-operate` source injects a candidate ONLY when an active per-verb
# operate directive names that target, so the tractor and external-repair
# dispatch reach a NON-hostile lock. Inert when no operate directive is active,
# so combat auto-lock is unchanged. Kept byte-for-byte identical to the shared
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` selector (this hull authors it inline).
#
# The `source_debris_threat` disjunct (issue #1347) is ASSESSMENT-GATED at the
# host: the marker is only ever attached to a contact whose threat state a scan
# actually raised, so Backfill cannot fire on a rock the crew were never told
# about.
eligibility = "candidate_fact(detectable) > 0 and (candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_last_attacker) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_retained) > 0 or candidate_fact(hostile) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_operate) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_debris_threat) > 0)"

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_sensors_designation) > 0"
weight = 500.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_retained) > 0"
weight = 200.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_last_attacker) > 0"
weight = 100.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_radar) > 0"
weight = 1.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_operate) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

# Confirmed debris, ranked by deadline (issue #1347). 120 puts a confirmed rock
# above the ordinary fight and below a named Destroy objective; the two bands
# rank several rocks against each other so Tactical works the queue
# earliest-deadline-first. Both bands are guarded on `debris_deadline_known`
# because an ABSENT `impact_secs` reads as 0, and 0 is a real answer here.
# See `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` for the precedence invariant.
[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_debris_threat) > 0"
weight = 120.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_deadline_known) > 0 and candidate_fact(impact_secs) < param(debris_pressing_secs)"
weight = 60.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_deadline_known) > 0 and candidate_fact(impact_secs) < param(debris_urgent_secs)"
weight = 60.0

# Navigation — rank destinations into the shared Waypoint. Only the objective
# source marks its resolved destination `reachable`, so this policy drives the
# AI waypoint from objectives alone; `chart-contacts` is surfaced so an author
# can widen the eligibility, and by default only ENRICHES a coincident objective
# destination rather than independently steering the ship.
[navigation_console.selector]
sources = ["navigation-objectives", "chart-contacts"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(reachable) > 0"

[[navigation_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_nav_objective) > 0"
weight = 100.0

[[navigation_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_chart_contact) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# Repair — rank this ship's damaged stations for the next free team. Two
# additive ladders whose tier rungs STRICTLY dominate the deficit rungs
# (3 x 100 = 300 < 1000), reproducing the retired `(tier desc, deficit desc)`
# comparator. `assigned < 1` is what makes N free teams pick N DISTINCT
# stations. `tier_ordinal` is the DamageTier discriminant (Operational 0,
# Damaged 1, Disabled 2, Destroyed 3) — a structural enum ordinal, which is why
# its lower bound is a literal rather than a param. The Destroyed rung (3) is
# REACHABLE: since issue #1013 an on-site team repairs a destroyed system like
# any other — `SystemHull::restore` has no tier gate and the first restored HP
# un-latches it — so a destroyed station is real repair work and the eligibility
# must not refuse it. The only tier excluded is Operational (0), which has
# nothing to repair.
#
# Authored on every hull whether or not it crews repair teams: the teams gate
# dispatch, so a ship that gains them later already has its ranking.
[repair.selector]
sources = ["damaged-stations", "core-bucket"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(source_repair_request) > 0 and candidate_fact(assigned) < 1 and candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) > 0"

# The bands sit INSIDE the urgent range and deliberately NOT at the DamageTier
# thresholds — because tier strictly dominates, the deficit ladder only ever
# discriminates within one tier, so bands at the tier boundaries would all fire
# together for every Disabled station and discriminate nothing.
[repair.selector.param]
deficit_band_low = 0.80
deficit_band_mid = 0.90
deficit_band_high = 0.95

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 1"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 2"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 3"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_low)"
weight = 100.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_mid)"
weight = 100.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_high)"
weight = 100.0

# Comms hail — rank who to hail. The most gated of the five, and the only one
# whose eligibility reads a `self_fact`: `comms_available`, so a Disabled or
# Destroyed Comms system stops the ship hailing at all. `source_hail_objective`
# keeps the baseline — only targets an active Hail directive actually names are
# ranked. `has_open_hail_thread < 1` is the anti-respam gate and it TERMINATES:
# a hail arms it even when it fires no `on_hailed` template, and it re-arms on a
# human `ClearComms` or on the target ceasing to be a live candidate, which is
# what an unmanned ship relies on. `switch_margin` is 0 and the host passes no
# current target: a hail is a ONE-SHOT event, so there is nothing to retain.
[comms_console.selector]
sources = ["hail-objectives", "comms-contacts"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(source_hail_objective) > 0 and candidate_fact(in_range) > 0 and candidate_fact(objective_score) > 0 and candidate_fact(has_open_hail_thread) < 1 and self_fact(comms_available) > 0"

# The bands straddle the `base_priority` values the shipped content actually
# authors (20 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 80 / 100), splitting them four ways.
# Bands outside that range would fire for all or none and collapse the ranking
# onto the smallest-UUID tie-break.
[comms_console.selector.param]
score_band_low = 25.0
score_band_mid = 45.0
score_band_high = 75.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_low)"
weight = 100.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_mid)"
weight = 100.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_high)"
weight = 100.0

# ── AI fine-system policies (PRD #774 US7, issue #885b) ───────────────────────
#
# The ship-level AI policies, AUTHORED rather than synthesised. Each answers
# "which verb does this fine system emit on which channel?" for whoever operates
# the station, and each reproduces exactly what the matching
# `default_*_ai_config()` in `src/entities/config.rs` used to invent at spawn.
# The reasoning behind every rule lives on those functions;
# `default_ai_policy_pins` spawns every shipped hull and compares the two, so a
# transcription slip fails the build rather than quietly changing how this ship
# behaves.
#
# Like the selectors above, these attach on `[behaviour]` ALONE, not on the
# console section they name — so a hull owes them whether or not it declares
# `[captain_console]`, `[shields_console]` or `[power]`. Authoring them is what
# brings those sections into existence on hulls that carried none.
#
# A rule's `when` is a guard, not a capability check: the host keeps every
# availability, cooldown, range and arc gate it had. `idle = true` (see Boost) is
# a first-class declaration meaning "this system deliberately takes no AI
# action" — it is NOT the same as an empty block, which validation rejects.

# Captain — raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within
# `combat_window_secs`, otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so
# a designer retunes the ship's nerve without recompiling.
[captain_console.ai]
param = { combat_window_secs = 10.0, alert_on_hostile_within = 150.0 }

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(secs_since_combat) < param(combat_window_secs)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

# First contact (issue #912). `secs_since_combat` starts only on damage taken,
# hostile fire taken, or own weapon fired — and since #872 this hull's guns hold
# until Red Alert — so the rule above ALONE can only ever return fire: a fully
# backfilled Alliance hull could not open an engagement at all. This rule is the
# other half. A faction-hostile inside `alert_on_hostile_within` is enough to
# call the alert, and that range is a named parameter, so a designer authors a
# nervous hull or a patient one without recompiling.
#
# `hostile_range` reads 0.0 when there is NO contact — both readings are ALWAYS
# seeded, so a guard reads "clear" rather than "absent" — which is why this
# guard pairs it with `hostile_contact`. The presence clause is load-bearing,
# not decoration.
#
# A Harrow authors no rule like this. It is always armed
# (`min_alert_to_fire = 0`) and stands its alert down out of combat on purpose,
# so first contact is not its captain's decision to make.
[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 5
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(hostile_contact) > 0 and fact(hostile_range) < param(alert_on_hostile_within)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false

# Helm longitudinal — always actuate the planner's desired travel. The
# continuous magnitude comes from `DesiredMotion`, so no thrust number is pinned
# here; this rule is only the DECISION to actuate, which a designer can gate.
[helm_console.engines_ai]

[[helm_console.engines_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "longitudinal"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

# Helm yaw — the mirror of `engines_ai` on the facing axis: always actuate the
# planner's desired facing.
[helm_console.steering_ai]

[[helm_console.steering_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "yaw"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

# Helm lateral — always actuate. The dodge (and the docking translation) run off
# the shared hazard surface, so again only the decision is authored here.
[helm_console.lateral_ai]

[[helm_console.lateral_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "lateral"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_lateral_thrust"

# Helm vertical — always actuate. `VerticalMovementMode` stays a host-side
# CAPABILITY gate rather than a policy scalar, so a Planar hull still takes no
# vertical component no matter what this rule says.
[helm_console.vertical_ai]

[[helm_console.vertical_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "vertical"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_vertical_thrust"

# Helm impulse — always PERMIT the manoeuvre. The engage-vs-cancel decision is
# still made host-side from the doctrine's `use_impulse` fact and the
# `decide_impulse` geometry; this rule is the authored gate layered over it, and
# `ship_harrow_warhawk.toml` is the worked example of closing it.
[helm_console.impulse_ai]

[[helm_console.impulse_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "impulse"
when = "true"
verb = "engage_impulse"

# Helm boost — an explicit IDLE declaration, and the only one in the set. No AI
# on this hull engages the boost drive, so the honest declaration is "takes no
# AI boost action" rather than a rule that never fires. `idle = true` is a legal
# declaration distinct from silence; an empty block is rejected at load. A hull
# opts in by replacing this with a rule on the `boost` channel —
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml` is the worked example.
[helm_console.boost_ai]
idle = true

# Shields focus — two rules on one channel, both emitting the value-less
# `focus_shield_arc`. WHICH of the four arcs is focused is not in the policy: it
# comes from the retained ranking kernel, which reads the four params below
# directly out of `param`. `damage_window_secs`, `min_damage_window_secs` and
# `health_ratio_threshold` are therefore live tunables even though no `when`
# names them — do not delete them for looking unreferenced.
#
# The priority-10 damage rule and the priority-0 fallback emit the same verb and
# the fallback is unconditional, so today the channel resolves identically
# whatever `recent_damage_pct_max` reads. The rule is transcribed as-is because
# this migration changes no behaviour; the redundancy is recorded on #885.
[shields_console.ai_policy.param]
damage_window_secs = 4.0
min_damage_window_secs = 1.0
damage_pct_threshold = 50.0
health_ratio_threshold = 50.0

[[shields_console.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "shield_focus"
when = "fact(recent_damage_pct_max) >= param(damage_pct_threshold)"
verb = "focus_shield_arc"

[[shields_console.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "shield_focus"
when = "true"
verb = "focus_shield_arc"

# Comms dialogue response — answer an open hail with its FIRST response. Guarded
# twice, and both guards matter: an unguarded rule would re-emit a response the
# router refuses, every tick, for as long as the dialogue stays open.
#   * `comms_available` — a Disabled or Destroyed Comms system stops the ship
#     answering as well as hailing.
#   * `sender_in_range` — the router refuses a response whose sender has left
#     comms range, so without this the officer's rejection re-flashes forever.
# WHICH message is being answered comes from the host; only the response INDEX
# rides the verb. A ship that should answer nothing declares `idle = true`.
[comms_console.ai]

[[comms_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "comms_respond"
when = "fact(comms_available) > 0 and fact(sender_in_range) > 0"
verb = "respond_to_message"
response_index = 0

# ── AI sensing horizon ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Authored, not defaulted. `AiProfile.sensor_range` is what `ai::lod::evaluate_lod`
# measures an NPC copy of this hull against: a ship further than
# `sensor_range * 1.2` from the player for `LOD_DWELL_SECS` loses
# `AiHighFidelity`, and with it every helm/captain/weapons decider it carries.
# `simulate_low_lod_ships` then dead-reckons it on its LAST heading and speed
# for ever — a hull demoted mid-manoeuvre at speed simply leaves the scenario
# and never comes back.
#
# Every Harrow hull has always authored this (`ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`
# 400, `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` 350). No Alliance hull did, so an Alliance
# hull spawned as an NPC fell to the 100.0 Rust fallback in
# `entities::spawner` — INSIDE its own authored doctrine envelope, whose
# `commit_range`/`safe_range_margin` legs work out past 120 units. The value
# below is sized to the doctrine this hull flies, so the ship stays decided-for
# across its own manoeuvre.
[ai_profile]
aggression = 0.5
sensor_range = 200.0
base_files.assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml:
name = "entity.alliance_cruiser.name"
# Player-facing proper name (the flagship). John-specified as "AEV Phoenix".
display_name = "entity.alliance_cruiser.display_name"
class = "cruiser"
hull_id = "AEV-1864"
power_rating = 90
css = "gui/themes/cruiser.css"
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] #1154 tuning, separately ratified
# as a mass-mechanic input rather than by #1082's combat matrix.
mass = 24000.0
# Player identity (the `player` tag + `playerShip` radar icon) is NOT authored
# here — it is injected onto the selected hull at the player game-start spawn
# (see `player_ship_identity` in `src/server_app.rs`). A world-spawned copy of
# this hull is an ordinary NPC ship, so it must not masquerade as the player.
tags = [ "ship" ]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"

# ── Composition (issues #875, #876) ──────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Everything below `includes` is what this hull SPECIALISES; the shared AI
# doctrine it flies comes from the fragment library under
# `assets/entities/fragments/ai/`, whole policy block at a time, and is tuned
# here by PARAMETER only.
#
# Order is significant: fragments merge in declared order and this file merges
# last, so the includer always wins.
#
# The class MOVEMENT doctrine is `fragments/ai/movement_broadside_orbit.toml`
# (issue #876 AC1): a wide defensive standoff ring while the alert is down, and
# at red alert a fighting ring at this hull's own `combat_orbit_range` with a
# TORPEDO RUN cut into it. Everything this hull says about it is the four `param`
# keys below, across two axes — no rule, no state, no transition.
#
# ── Why the ring needs the torpedo run, on THIS hull in particular ────────────
#
# A settled ring holds the target at EXACTLY the beam: a circular path makes the
# hull's heading the tangent, so the bearing is 90 degrees by construction rather
# than merely near it. All three of this hull's tubes are 90-degree fore/aft
# cones, so the whole torpedo battery is permanently out of arc for as long as the
# ring is flown — and that is not only a damage cost, it is what stopped the ring
# being flown at all on the first attempt.
#
# Weapons raises a channel-3 `ArcBearingRequest` for the first family with the
# target in reach that cannot bear (`src/console/weapons/mod.rs`). The phasers'
# 270-degree FIRE arcs always bear, so the request is always the TORPEDO family's,
# whose reach is `speed * lifespan` = 300 units and so is effectively never out of
# reach. `apply_arc_bearing_request` (`src/ship/helm_ai.rs`) does not bias the
# doctrine's facing, it OVERWRITES steering with a full bow-on solution after the
# planner has solved the ring tangent, for every yaw verb including
# `hold_combat_orbit`. A ring with loaded tubes and no torpedo leg is therefore
# dragged bow-on by Channel 3, snaps back to the tangent when a tube bears, and is
# dragged bow-on again. Measured on the PLAIN RING VARIANT — a `combat_orbit_range`
# of 32 with no torpedo leg, which is the configuration those figures belong to and
# not the one shipped below — the sawtooth ran eight units deep, walking the hull
# from 33 units down to 13 and straight through the 35-unit blaster envelope of the
# ship it was fighting; in `probe_aggressor` that inverted the engagement, 64 dealt
# / 0 taken uncomposed against 50 dealt / 136 taken composed.
#
# The fragment answers this in two places, and they are different answers to
# different halves of it. The `torpedo_run` leg is a DOCTRINE decision:
# `evaluate_family_arc_request` emits nothing for a family in which some emitter
# is READY, so a hull that points its own bow when it has a salvo ready satisfies
# the request by flying its own doctrine, and the ring it returns to is the ring
# the planner solved. The `orbit` leg's `yields_to_arc_requests = false` (issue
# #918) is a PRECEDENCE decision, and it covers the ticks the first cannot reach
# — a hull on its ring with tubes it has no run-range for. The host asks the leg
# the helm is flying, so the ring declines while `acquire`, which is only
# travelling, still yields; nothing anywhere asks who sent the request.
#
# ── The ring converges; there is no controller bug ───────────────────────────
#
# The first attempt recorded a claim that `hold_combat_orbit` "does not converge
# on this hull's max_speed = 10 / max_yaw_rate = 0.4". That is withdrawn. The
# correction is proportional with no integral term, so the ring settles a little
# OUTSIDE the authored radius, at
#
#     r * (r - R) = v * R * tracking_full_steer_rad / (max_yaw_rate * gain)
#
# With R = 32, v = 10 * 0.6 = 6, full_steer = 0.3, max_yaw_rate = 0.4 and
# gain = 4.0 that predicts r = 33.09. Flown on this hull's own physics envelope
# against a stationary bogey it settles at 33.1 from INSIDE the ring, from ON it
# and from OUTSIDE it (starts of 12.8 / 32.0 / 80.0 units). It sustains
# 6 / 33.1 = 0.18 rad/s against the 0.4 this hull has, and 33.1 is eight units
# inside the 40-unit beam range. What the earlier sweep most likely reproduced is
# the documented failure of a HALF-AUTHORED arm: `COMBAT_ORBIT_PARAMS` gates on
# all three orbit names being present on the STEERING axis, and "one authoring the
# throttle but not the range would fly a tangent of a ring of radius zero".
#
# ── The AI arcs WIDENED, and what that did and did not buy ──────────────────
#
# Both phaser banks author `auto_arc_deg = 270`, matching their `fire_arc_deg`,
# so an AI-operated hull double-broadsides on the beam exactly as a human gunner
# always could. Owner-directed, issue #929's third pass. Until then both banks
# authored 180, and this block said the opposite — that the abutting pair was
# deliberate and widening it "is a player-facing balance change, not an
# implementer's call". It was, and it has now been made.
#
# WHAT IT BOUGHT IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE, and this is the finding worth
# keeping. The expectation was that two banks bearing instead of one halves the
# `beam_damage_per_sec` the hull needs. Measured, it RAISED it: the swept knee
# went from 24 to 32 (the ladder is above the `fore` bank). Instrumented on
# `probe_duel` seed 3, same seed, same damage, one variable:
#
#                       auto 180 (abutting)   auto 270 (overlapping)
#   beam activations     7                     7
#   simultaneous pairs   0                     1
#   union beam-on-target 34.4 s of 90 (38 %)   28.4 s of 90 (32 %)
#   enemy arc collapses  5                     3
#
# WHAT THAT TABLE MEASURES, corrected. The first reading of it was that the
# abutting pair STAGGERED the two banks — one coming off cooldown into a bearing
# as its sibling went cold — and that overlapping arcs let both fire and both
# cool together. That explanation is WITHDRAWN: instrumented over 90 s on this
# world, every beam this hull lights ends on `!bank_in_arc` and not one of them
# ever runs its 6 s burn to expiry, so there is no cooldown rhythm here to
# synchronise or stagger. The union figures above are ARC DWELL — how long the
# target stays inside a bank's fire arc — and what widening the arcs changed is
# which windows exist and how long each lasts, not the duty cycle. The
# `cycle_jitter` block further down carries the instrumentation and the A/B that
# settles it. Coverage is still what beats a regenerating screen; the thing that
# limits coverage on this hull is geometry.
#
# So the wider arcs are worth having for the player-facing reason (the AI now
# fights the ship the way the manual arcs always allowed, and a big burst is a
# real tactical shape) and are paid for with the higher knee. Anyone revisiting
# this should look at what actually binds first, and on this world that is ARC
# DWELL and the full cooldown paid after every arc-cut burn — not the duty cycle.
# `cooldown_secs` is still the untouched lever, and it is now the interesting one
# for a different reason: this hull pays 6 s of rest for burns that geometry
# routinely cuts to a fraction of their authored length.
#
# Pinned by `the_player_hulls_270_degree_auto_arcs_both_bear_off_the_beam_line`
# (src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs), which also holds the blind-wedge control
# — dead ahead is still the aft bank's 90-degree gap, so these are 270 and not
# 360. [ai] Ratified by #1082's fixed five-seed, four-opponent report
# (`scripts/balance-runs.cruiser.toml`): its all-Backfill cruiser wins every
# row; the gate protects the resulting envelope alongside the damage value.
#
# Resolution happens at authoring time. The runtime never sees a fragment — it
# sees one resolved document, and PRD #774's "every AI-capable fine system
# declares a policy" is satisfied by that document, not by this file.
includes = [
  "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
  "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml",
  "fragments/ai/movement_broadside_orbit.toml",
]

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_cruiser_recreated.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 1.5
length = 4
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Default doctrine for a backfilled/unmanned player cruiser (#842 — the other
# half of #838's human/AI symmetry). A player hull that nobody is flying is
# AI-crewed exactly like an NPC; giving it a `[behaviour]` block is the single
# missing piece that makes `spawn_entity` attach the `BehaviourSection` on the
# player game-start path, so the ship's per-ship blackboard carries scored
# objectives and its Tactical AI is licensed to acquire and engage — not merely
# return fire once hit. A world-spawned copy of this hull (an ordinary NPC) reads
# the same doctrine, which is correct: it should fight like any other ship.
#
# Two standing objectives, scored each tick in priority order:
#
#   Destroy (45) — an UNTARGETED Destroy (no `directive_target`), which is what
#                  every shipped hostile authors and what licenses the
#                  nearest-hostile acquisition tier (see the root-cause note in
#                  `src/console/weapons/mod.rs::ai_target_selection`). This is
#                  what makes the ship PROACTIVELY engage rather than wait to be
#                  shot at.
#   Hold    (20) — the default when no hostile is visible: no directive
#                  (`AiDirective::None`), so the helm holds station rather than
#                  wandering to a world anchor this hull's worlds need not declare.
#
# The engage priority sits deliberately LOW (45). Scenario objectives authored as
# `spawn_entity` overrides (combat_test / probe_duel author Destroy at 80) merge
# by id and dominate this band, so mission doctrine always wins over the standing
# default (#842 AC3). No Retreat is authored: this is a defending warship — it
# fights rather than flees. `maintain_range = 30` keeps the cruiser inside its
# 40-unit phaser range while giving its torpedoes room.
#
# `imminent_collision_facing_threshold` (issue #780 AC4, and the "AI ships fly
# through asteroid fields" report against the backfilled player hull): every
# shipped hull left this at its parse-time default of 1.0, and at the time that
# was effectively OFF — the old urgency measure only reached 1.0 when two hulls
# occupied the same point — so ordinary avoidance only ever BENT this hull's
# travel a little and never actually turned its facing away from a closing rock.
# 0.6 authors the override for real: once hazard urgency crosses 60%, the
# desired facing snaps to the escape heading (self-clearing the moment urgency
# drops back under it) instead of relying on a mild bend to out-turn the
# obstacle in time.
#
# WHAT 0.6 MEANS CHANGED IN ISSUE #968, and the value was left alone rather than
# re-tuned. Urgency is no longer "projected centre separation as a fraction of
# the avoidance radius" — it is the share of the authored `avoidance_buffer` the
# SURFACE clearance has spent, squared. So this threshold used to trip at a
# centre separation under 40% of the avoidance radius, which varied with the
# obstacle's size; it now trips at a fixed surface clearance of
# `avoidance_buffer * (1 - sqrt(0.6))` = 1.13 units with the shipped 5-unit
# buffer, whatever the obstacle. Against the `huge` asteroid class (#947) that
# is the repair the issue is about: the old form did not fire until this hull
# was already ~6 units INSIDE the rock. Against a `small` rock it now fires
# about fourteen times further out (1.13 units of clearance instead of 0.08), so
# the facing override takes the helm off its gunnery solution earlier around
# small debris than it used to. That is the deliberate trade; retune HERE, not
# in the severity curve, if a hull wants the old lateness back.
[behaviour]
imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id             = "destroy-hostiles"
text           = "entity.alliance_cruiser.behaviour.doctrine.destroy_hostiles.text"
directive_kind = "Destroy"
base_priority  = 45.0
target_speed   = 0.85
maintain_range = 30.0

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "hold-station"
text          = "entity.alliance_cruiser.behaviour.doctrine.hold_station.text"
base_priority = 20.0
target_speed  = 0.0

# ── Durability ladder (#915 tuning pass) ─────────────────────────────────────
# The whole fleet was re-pegged in one pass, because these numbers only mean
# anything relative to each other. Dynasty hulls carry a monolithic
# `[hull] hull_integrity`; Alliance hulls have none, and their equivalent pool
# is the SUM of the per-system `max_hp` below. Shields sit on top of both.
#
#   Dynasty   destroyer 200 | patrol/cruiser 300 | warhawk 400
#   Alliance  courier 200 | destroyer 300 | cruiser 500 | battleship 800
#
# The Alliance figures were reached by scaling each hull's authored system HP
# proportionally, so the relative weighting between systems is unchanged.
#
# RADAR SYSTEMS CARRY NO HULL. `helm-radar`, `tactical-radar` and `sensor-radar`
# have no `[[hull.system_hull]]` entry on any Alliance hull, so they cannot be
# damaged, disabled or repaired — their points were redistributed across the
# surviving systems and the totals above are unchanged. The code that reacts to
# a downed radar (weapons-console arc gating, the helm radar overlay, the
# captain's repair targeting) is untouched and still fires for any hull that
# authors those entries; these four simply never trigger it.
[[hull.system_hull]]

# ── Operational-system damage entries (issues #1388, #1390) ──────────────────
# The dock, the tractor and the umbilical (all authored as systems further down)
# each carry a hull entry so a storm can KNOCK THEM OUT — coupling gear is gear
# on the OUTSIDE of the hull, and a radiation band's `damage_zone` picks it the
# same way it picks any other system (issue #1052's ordered `RegionDamage` draw
# over `EntitySystemHull`). Damaged to `Disabled` the dock refuses
# (`dock.refused.disabled`) and a held mate parts, the tractor drops its hold and
# the umbilical's flow stops — so danger reaches the crew's external work exactly
# as it reaches a gun or an engine.
#
# 30 HP and the 0.5/0.15/0.15 shape MIRROR the destroyer's own dock, tractor and
# umbilical rows (`alliance_destroyer.toml`) and the NPC hulls carrying the same
# gear a row at a time — `alliance_tender.toml`'s dock and umbilical,
# `ship_harrow_tug.toml`'s tractor. That sameness IS the player/NPC symmetry PRD
# #1143 is built on: a storm costs a crewed hull's tractor exactly what it costs
# a tug's.
#
# THESE ARE THIS HULL'S OPERATIONAL (non-combat) SYSTEM ROWS. Every entry above
# is part of the 500-point combat durability ladder the #915 tuning pass pegged;
# these three sit OUTSIDE it, so the hull's combat pool is unchanged in intent
# even though the raw `is_destroyed` sum now includes their 90 points. The
# standing `npm run balance:cruiser` gate checks this against the thresholds in
# `scripts/balance-runs.cruiser.toml`.
[[hull.system_hull]]

disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

# Security teams (issue #1389, PRD #1371). The cruiser musters the same two
# teams the Alliance Destroyer does, dispatched and recalled independently from
# whichever station the `[[system]] kind = "security"` block at the end of the
# system list gives them to — Tactical, on this hull as on that one — with no
# Duty Officer standing between the seat and the order.
#
# What a team may DO once it gets somewhere is authored on the TARGET, never
# here: this table is only the hull's own half — how many people it can send,
# how long they take to get across and come back, and how far they can reach. A
# hull that authors no `[security]` table musters nobody.
#
# [ai] All four carried across from `alliance_destroyer.toml` unchanged, and
# unratified there too. The crossing is a transfer to another structure under
# way rather than a run down a corridor, so it is slower than this hull's own
# `[repair] travel_duration_secs = 5`, and the asymmetry (out slower than back)
# is the encumbrance of going equipped. `range = 400` is the reach the destroyer
# shares with its `[repair.external_dispatch]`; this hull shares that reach
# too (issue #1391), for the same reason — a repair team and a
# security team cross the same gap by the same means, and two different reaches
# on one hull would be a difference the crew could see and nobody could explain.

# External repair-team dispatch (issue #1161), mounted on this hull by #1391 —

# `DispatchRepairTeam { team_idx, target: External }` verb: the named team crosses to the

# works there, unavailable to this hull's internal damage-control sweep for the
# duration. Nothing below the TOML is hull-specific — `ExternalRepairDispatchSpawn`

#

# from the retired `field_repair` capability (#1164 S11a) and have never been
# re-tuned — lives on `alliance_destroyer.toml`'s copy of this table rather than

# ── `beam_damage_per_sec = 32`: what a bank has to be worth once torpedoes
#    stop ignoring shields (issue #929) ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# [ai] Ratified by #1082's fixed five-seed, four-opponent report
# (`scripts/balance-runs.cruiser.toml`), which records 20/20 Backfill wins and
# gates the outcome. Was 4, went to 24 on the second pass with
# `auto_arc_deg = 180`, then 32 when both banks began to bear (see "The AI
# arcs WIDENED" in the header), and remains 32 after the damaged-arc latch
# keeps that broadside on target. This is the hull's whole anti-shield tuning and it
# belongs on the ratification list; the argument, the arithmetic and both swept
# ladders are here so a ratifier can move it on evidence.
#
# WHY IT HAD TO MOVE AT ALL. Torpedoes no longer bypass a raised arc: a round
# delivers `damage_shields = 4` into a live screen and `damage_hull = 40` into a
# collapsed one, so "phasers strip the shields, torpedoes finish the hull" is now
# literally how this battery works rather than a slogan over a launcher that
# pierced anyway. That makes the BEAMS load-bearing. At 4 they were not: over 28
# seeds of `probe_duel` before this change the destroyer's hull took exactly 240
# points from this hull — 6 rounds x 40 of torpedo pierce, and NOT ONE POINT from
# the beams, on any seed.
#
# THE ARITHMETIC THE BANK HAS TO BEAT. The target that matters is a self-focusing
# warship's struck arc, and three factors stack against the beam before a point
# of it reaches the arc's HP:
#
#   x1.25   `ModifierSlot::PhaserDamage` at the WEAPONS rung `fleet_baseline`
#           walks to at combat stations (3 => `power_multipliers[2] = 0.25`).
#           This one is FOR the bank.
#   x0.50   duty cycle. `beam_duration_secs = 6` on `cooldown_secs = 6`, and the
#           cooldown hands the defender exactly as much recovery time as the
#           burst takes.
#   x0.50   `focus_focused_damage_multiplier` on the arc the target's Shields AI
#           has focused — and it WILL focus this one, because
#           `tick_shield_focus_ai` focuses whichever arc took >= 50 % of the
#           recent damage window, which is the arc this hull is shooting.
#
# So the arc loses `D x 0.3125` hp/s per bearing bank, against an
# `alliance_destroyer` focused arc regenerating at `2.5 + focus_bonus_regen 4 =
# 6.5` hp/s. With ONE bank that is break-even at D = 20.8. THE NAIVE READING OF
# TWO BANKS — halve it to 10.4 — IS WRONG, and the measurement says so
# emphatically. Two banks that bear TOGETHER also cool together, so the naive
# doubling assumes a coverage the hull does not get; what the abutting pair used
# to give it was a STAGGER (the header has the instrumented numbers). Coverage
# beats burst against a screen that regenerates, so the real knee went UP.
#
# THE LADDER, `probe_duel --deterministic --hz 30 --sim-seconds 90`, seeds 1-12,
# one variable, at the shipped `auto_arc_deg = 270`:
#
#   D    launches>0   mean bow hold   cruiser deals   duels resolving
#   6      0/12          26.0 s           107          0/12
#   8      0/12          26.0 s           144          0/12
#   10     3/12          25.1 s           208          0/12
#   12     6/12          23.5 s           274          0/12
#   14     8/12          24.3 s           336          1/12
#   16     8/12          23.7 s           401          2/12
#   18     8/12          23.6 s           402          2/12
#   20     8/12          23.4 s           437          4/12
#   22     8/12          23.8 s           471          7/12
#   24    10/12          23.5 s           520          8/12
#   28    10/12          19.4 s           540          8/12
#   32    12/12          10.6 s           516         10/12
#   40    12/12           5.8 s           517         11/12
#
# …and the same ladder at the PREVIOUS `auto_arc_deg = 180`, kept because it is
# the evidence that the wider arcs cost rather than saved:
#
#   D     4     8    12    16    20    24
#   seeds 0/12  0/12 5/12  8/12  9/12  12/12   <- knee was 24
#
# 32 WAS the knee on that ladder — the first rung at which every seed opens the
# gate — and it is not any more. RE-DERIVED once the arc-keeping and
# weak-broadside doctrine landed (see `[helm_console.steering_ai.param]`), on the
# same command line and the same 12 seeds:
#
#   D    launches>0   mean bow hold   cruiser deals   duels resolving
#   8      0/12          27.0 s           168          2/12
#   12     7/12          25.0 s           323          3/12
#   16    11/12           7.3 s           467          8/12
#   20    12/12           9.2 s           509          9/12
#   24    12/12          14.7 s           510          8/12
#   32    12/12           0.5 s           503         12/12
#
# Twelve seeds put the knee at 20; the WIDER 28-seed sweep does not confirm it —
# 20 reaches only 25/28. This table records the earlier 24-damage pass; the
# current ratified value is 32 after the damaged-arc latch changed the broadside
# hold behaviour.
#
#   28 seeds, 90 s     D=20     D=24 (historical) D=32
#   launches>0         25/28    28/28            28/28
#   duels resolving    18/28    22/28            28/28
#   this hull wins     17/28    21/28            28/28
#   damage taken       555      495              299
#
# THE COST IS STATED PLAINLY: 32 was better on every quality reading in this
# earlier sweep. The current fixed five-seed report above is the ratification
# evidence for retaining it with the damaged-arc latch.
#
# WHAT 32 IS NOT, AND WHAT IT IS. On paper this is now the fleet's heaviest beam
# battery, and the comparison only means anything if the BEARING is stated —
# where a pair overlaps depends on where the banks point, and no two hulls here
# agree. Time-averaged over each bank's own duty cycle:
#
#   hull                 banks              peak (both bear)   abeam
#   this hull at 32      0/180, auto 270    32 /s              32 /s
#   ship_harrow_warhawk  -90/+90, auto 270  16 /s              8 /s
#   ship_harrow_cruiser  0/180, auto 270    6.7 /s             6.7 /s
#   ship_harrow_patrol   -90/+90, auto 180  never doubles      4.4 /s
#   alliance_battleship  0/180, auto 180    never doubles      4 /s (fore) / 2 (aft)
#   alliance_destroyer   one omni, auto 360 1.5 /s             1.5 /s
#
# The two shapes differ in WHERE they double. Banks on the centreline (this hull,
# `ship_harrow_cruiser`) overlap through the BEAM quadrants, which is exactly
# where a broadside ring holds its target — so the peak is the number this
# doctrine actually gets. Banks on the beam (`ship_harrow_warhawk`,
# `ship_harrow_patrol`) overlap dead ahead and dead astern instead, so a warhawk
# working a target abeam is on 8 /s and reaches 16 only on a bow or stern
# aspect. The battleship's abut on the beam line and never overlap at all.
#
# So this hull is genuinely the heaviest in the geometry its own doctrine flies,
# by a factor of four over the warhawk abeam. The honest gloss is that the paper
# figure overstates it even so: all 32 /s arrives inside a 6-second window and
# then nothing arrives for six, and against a focused screen the dead half is
# worth less than the arithmetic says — which is the whole finding recorded in
# the header. `cooldown_secs` is the lever that would change that, and neither
# it nor any other pass of this issue has touched it.
# ── `cycle_jitter = 0.33`, and the measurement that qualifies the block above ─
#
# [ai] Ratified by #1082's fixed five-seed, four-opponent report
# (`scripts/balance-runs.cruiser.toml`). Each time a bank LIGHTS it draws one factor
# uniformly from [0.67, 1.33) (seeded, `SimStream::BeamCycleJitter`) and applies
# it to BOTH that cycle's burn AND the cooldown behind it. Linked, so a cycle
# that fires longer also rests longer: the mean duty cycle is exactly what
# `beam_duration_secs` and `cooldown_secs` say, and only the PHASE moves. The
# mechanism is general and defaults to `0.0` — an exact fixed cycle, and no draw
# taken at all — so only this hull's two banks are affected this round.
#
# IT WAS ADDED TO DE-SYNCHRONISE THE PAIR, and on `probe_duel` it does nothing.
# The swept ladder with jitter is the same ladder without it, rung for rung:
# D=8 0/12 seeds launching, D=12 6/12, D=16 8/12, D=20 8/12, D=24 10/12,
# D=32 12/12. Same knee, same 28-seed sweep (28/28 launch, 25 wins, 3 losses).
# A 30 s A/B at seed 3 with the ONE variable is byte-identical.
#
# WHY, and it corrects the block above. The two banks in `probe_duel` are not
# cadence-limited, they are ARC-limited. Instrumented over 90 s, counting how each
# beam END was reached (this hull's own banks only):
#
#   world             ends by duration   ends by arc
#   probe_duel        0                  4
#   probe_aggressor   1                  2
#   combat_test       6                  1
#
# On `probe_duel` the hull lit five beams, four ended on `!bank_in_arc` — the ring
# takes the target out of the bank's fire arc — the fifth was still burning at the
# cutoff, and NOT ONE ever ran its 6 s burn to expiry.
#
# So on the world the whole ladder is measured on, `beam_duration_secs` is not
# the constraint and jittering it changes nothing; the cooldown gaps it also
# jitters are 6 s against arc windows tens of seconds apart, so they do not bind
# either. The "x0.50 duty cycle" term in the break-even arithmetic above is
# therefore an UPPER BOUND on this hull's coverage rather than a description of
# it — the real figure is 30-38 % of the engagement, measured — and the
# "synchronised dead window" reading of why the 270-degree arcs raised the knee
# is withdrawn. What the wider arcs actually changed is which arc windows exist
# and how long the target dwells in them; the union-coverage numbers in that
# table are arc dwell, not duty.
#
# WHERE IT DOES BIND, so the field is not inert everywhere: `combat_test`, where
# 6 of 7 ends are duration-driven. Same seeds, 150 s, one variable:
#
#            jitter 0.0                 jitter 0.33
#   seed 1   737 dealt / 165 taken      516 / 100, one MORE kill
#   seed 2   737 / 152                  646 / 126
#   seed 3   737 / 167                  516 / 100, one MORE kill
#
# Less damage dealt and considerably less taken, with a kill more on two of the
# three. That asymmetry is the honest cost of linking the two halves: when a burn
# is cut short by geometry the long draws buy nothing, while the long cooldowns
# are always paid — so against an arc-limited target the mechanism is a small net
# tax. `beam_damage_per_sec` is NOT re-derived for it (the knee is unmoved), and
# whether 0.33 earns its place on this hull is exactly the ratification question.
#
# WHAT IT COST ELSEWHERE: nothing. A bank at the `0.0` default takes no draw, so
# `SimStream::BeamCycleJitter` never moves for it and no other world's sequence
# is perturbed —
# `an_unjittered_bank_does_not_move_the_beam_cycle_jitter_stream` pins that.
# Resume safety is structural rather than added: the drawn cooldown is written
# onto the beam slot when the bank lights and every end site reads it there, so a
# run restored mid-cycle continues the cycle it was in
# (`a_beam_cycle_serves_the_cooldown_it_drew_rather_than_the_authored_one`, and
# `snapshot_resume::a_beams_drawn_cooldown_survives_capture_and_restore`).
#
# AI INTERPLAY: nothing downstream assumes the fixed cadence, and the one place
# it could have leaked in refuses it explicitly. `evaluate_family_arc_request`
# passes `false` for cooldown with the comment "arc-bearing is a facing request,
# not a timing one", so whether a bank is mid-cooldown cannot change whether the
# phaser family qualifies for a Channel-3 request. The blackboard's `on_cooldown`
# / `cooldown_remaining` are live derivations for the console, read by no
# doctrine. No authored guard in the fleet reads a beam duration. The one real
# interaction is with the TARGET: the shields AI focuses on a 4 s recent-damage
# window, and a jittered gap between bursts is 4.0-8.0 s where it was exactly
# 6.0 — so the defender's focus lapses on some cycles and not others, which is a
# consequence of the mechanism rather than a coupling to it.
#
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "fore"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 270
auto_arc_deg = 270
beam_range = 40
beam_damage_per_sec = 32
beam_duration_secs = 6
cooldown_secs = 6
cycle_jitter = 0.33
beam_color = [ 0.25, 0.75, 1, 1 ]
marker = "phasers_fore"

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed
  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below
  # is the SAME text on every armed hull in the fleet. Only this threshold
  # differs: 1 means "hold fire until the captain calls red alert", 0 means
  # "always armed". This hull has a captain's console (human, or an AI backfill
  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

# `beam_damage_per_sec = 32` here too, and for the same reason — the argument,

  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed

id = "fore_port"
facing_deg = 0

marker = "torpedo_port"

  # Load + launch policy for this tube (issue #782), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Two rules on two DIFFERENT channels, so they never
  # contend: keep the tube loaded, and launch when the alert is up AND the arc
  # the round would strike is down. Loaded state, magazine stock, target
  # validity, range and arc stay host-side gates.
  #
  # `fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0` is the fleet's torpedo doctrine —
  # "phasers strip the shields, torpedoes finish the hull" — and issue #956 moved

  # was up, and none could retune the threshold. It is an HP reading rather than
  # a boolean, resolved per-arc through the target's own arc router, so this gate
  # and the eventual hit agree about which arc is in the way. A hull that wants
  # to spend rounds differently retunes it; `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` is the
  # worked example of tightening further (`fact(in_arc) > 0` as well, with
  # `torpedo_run_shield_gap = 1.0` on the helm to match), and `idle = true` of
  # declining launches altogether.
  #
  # ── Why this hull is back on the fleet reading (issue #929, second pass) ────
  #
  # #929's first pass switched this conjunct OFF here, with
  # `max_striking_shield_hp = 1000000.0` — a threshold beyond any arc reading.
  # That is gone. The gate is the fleet's literal `<= 0` again, and it is a REAL
  # decision rather than a formality, because both halves of the argument that
  # retired it have been answered rather than argued with.
  #
  #   1. THE ROUND NOW NEEDS THE ARC DOWN. The first pass's third reason was
  #      that `damage_hull` always pierced, so holding a round for a collapsed
  #      arc forwent 40 points of a 44-point payload to protect 4. That is no
  #      longer how a torpedo resolves. A round meets the ONE arc it flew into
  #      and that arc's own reading picks its payload: `damage_shields = 4`
  #      offered to a live screen through the same absorption seam a beam takes,
  #      or `damage_hull = 40` landing whole on bare plating. Ten to one. The
  #      gate is now worth more than the round it delays.
  #
  #   2. THIS HULL CAN CREATE THE GAP AGAIN. The first pass's headline reason
  #      was that it could not: one 4 dmg/s bank at a time against an
  #      `alliance_destroyer` arc its Shields AI focuses to 6.5 hp/s regen and
  #      x0.5 incoming — measured at about 1 dmg/s into the arc, with
  #      `hull_taken: 0` on the target across a whole `probe_aggressor` run.
  #      That was true, and the answer is the bank, not the gate:
  #      `beam_damage_per_sec` is 32 on both banks, which both bear since the
  #      arcs widened to 270 (the ladder above the `fore` phaser bank has the
  #      sweep, and the header has why the wider arcs RAISED the knee rather
  #      than halving it). Over the same 28 seeds the striking arc now collapses
  #      3-4 times a run, and every round this hull launches detonates on a DOWN
  #      arc for its full 40 — traced tick by tick on seeds 3, 12 and 34.
  #
  #   3. THE HELM LEG STILL ASKS THE WEAKER QUESTION, AND THAT IS NOW SAFE.
  #      `movement_broadside_orbit`'s `torpedo_run` opens on readiness alone here
  #      (`torpedo_run_shield_gap = 0.0`) and its only armament exits are
  #      `tubes_full < 1` / `tubes_fillable < 1`, both of which need a round to
  #      have LEFT a tube. That pairing is a deadlock only while the launcher
  #      cannot fire; with a bank that opens the arc it is the ordinary authored
  #      cycle — ring, bow hold, salvo, ring — and this hull escapes it the same
  #      DYNAMIC way `alliance_battleship`, `alliance_destroyer` and
  #      `ship_harrow_warhawk` do: on its guns. The fleet census pin
  #      `a_bow_hold_a_hull_can_reach_and_a_launcher_that_can_answer_it` buckets
  #      it there, and that bucket is only honest while the ladder above holds.
  #
  # MEASURED, `probe_duel --deterministic --hz 30 --sim-seconds 90`, 28 seeds
  # (1-14, 17, 21, 31, 34, 41, 43, 47, 55, 59, 61, 89, 144, 792, 838), against
  # the first pass's shipped state on the same command line:
  #
  #                      first pass    second pass   HERE
  #                      (gate off,    (gate on,     (gate on, 270 arcs,
  #                       4 dmg/s)      180, 24)      32)
  #   launches            4 every seed  2-5, 28/28    2-4, 28/28
  #   bow hold            0.0-3.9 s     12.2-27.2 s   0.5-13.4 s
  #   damage dealt        290-489       350-623       272-591 (mean 524)
  #   damage taken        348-852       186-785       190-707 (mean 414)
  #   target hull damage  240 on 25/28  198-433       150-422
  #                       (240-306)     (mean 385)    (mean 389)
  #   resolve in 90 s     12/28         23/28         25/28
  #   THIS HULL WINS      0 of 28       22 of 28      25 of 28
  #   this hull DIES      12 of 28      1 of 28       0 of 28 (3 at 180 s)
  #
  # That 240 is the sharpest line in the table: it is 6 rounds x 40 of torpedo
  # pierce and nothing else, on 25 of the 28 seeds, because the beams never once
  # reached hull. (The three that differ — 31, 55 and 838 — read 268, 306 and 273,
  # i.e. the same magazine plus a few points of collision or region damage. The
  # RANGES on the two later columns are the full 28 seeds and their low tails are
  # the seeds the fight does not finish inside the window, not a weaker salvo: at
  # 32 the three unresolved seeds give 150, 267 and 312 against a mean of 389.) At 180 s every one of the 28 resolves and the split is 25 wins
  # to 3 losses (the hull dies on seeds 9 at 95.0 s, 2 at 142.1 s and 89 at
  # 176.7 s). `combat_test`, 150 s, seeds 1-3: 4 launches, 737 dealt against
  # 152-167 taken, two kills apiece. `probe_aggressor`: the passive target,
  # previously never killed inside 90 s, dies at 17.2-17.4 s.
  #
  # AN 89 PER CENT WIN RATE AGAINST A DESTROYER IS A RATIFICATION QUESTION, not a
  # claim this file is making. It is what the measured knee produces, and the knee
  # was chosen to satisfy the LAUNCH criterion (every seed opens the gate) rather
  # than to hit a target win rate. Turning the rate down is a separate tuning pass
  # with its own sweep; the levers are the same ones named above the `fore` bank.
  #
  # The bow hold moved twice and is worth reading as a pair: 0.0-3.9 s when the
  # launcher was unconditional (a hull that may fire at any moment never has to
  # hold for a window), 12.2-27.2 s when the gate came back at 24, and 0.5-13.4 s
  # now that the guns open the arc sooner. A long occupancy is not the failure; an
  # occupancy with no launch in it is, and there are none of those left.
  #
  # Retuning is still one number, and it is now the fleet's: `0` is what every
  # other armed hull authors. A hull that wants to spend rounds into live screens
  # raises it — and whatever it raises it to, `torpedo_run_shield_gap` on the two
  # helm axes has to be able to answer the same question, or the bow hold has no
  # way out again.
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed
  # fact — 1 while this ship is at red alert, 0 otherwise — and the guard below
  # is the SAME text on every armed hull in the fleet. Only this threshold
  # differs: 1 means "hold fire until the captain calls red alert", 0 means
  # "always armed". This hull has a captain's console (human, or an AI backfill
  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"

[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.alliance_cruiser.power_groups.helm.label"
# `min_level` is the COMMANDABLE floor: the lowest level any operator, human or
# AI, may order this group to. `PowerSystem` stores it per group and clamps
# every order to it (issue #1395 — before that it was a drawing hint the engine
# ignored, and the console's pip row is still the other thing it decides).
#
# It reads 1 because Helm must never be switched off: a ship with no power to
# the drive cannot manoeuvre out of anything, and losing the ability to run away
# is not a trade a Power officer should be able to make with one press. Turning
# it down to 1 to free a point for the 8-point budget IS a legal order, so rung
# 1 has to be reachable and drawn. NOMINAL — the rung whose multiplier is 1.0 —
# is 2, and that is `default_level`, where the group boots.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.alliance_cruiser.power_groups.weapons.label"
# `min_level = 0`: this group may be taken COLD (issue #1395). Weapons is the
# one group on the hull that can be switched off outright, and that is how this
# ship expresses RESTRAINT — an Engineering order, visible to anyone watching the
# reactor, rather than a hidden captain's toggle. Zero is a real commandable
# level here, not a drawn rung: the console paints four pips whatever the floor
# says, and level 0 is all four dark under a COLD tag.
#
# Helm and Shields keep their floor of 1 (see Helm above). Cutting the drive or
# the shields to nothing is a way to lose a ship, not a way to make a statement
# with one; weapons at 0 costs the crew their guns and nothing else.
#
# NOMINAL (×1.0) is 2, which is where this group boots; dropping it to 1 is a
# legal order that spends the freed point elsewhere.
default_level = 2
min_level = 0
max_level = 4

[power_groups.shields]
label = "entity.alliance_cruiser.power_groups.shields.label"
# Nominal at 2 alongside Helm and Weapons: those three groups make the
# sustainable resting total of 6. Higher levels buy shield regeneration.
# `min_level = 1` is the COMMANDABLE floor (see Helm above): shields may be
# turned down to 1 but not switched off. Only Weapons authors a floor of 0.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# Command stance catalogue (issues #1107, #1387).
# The cruiser directs Tactical for the same reason the destroyer does: weapons
# posture is the hull's one AI branch that reads Red Alert directly (the
# `min_alert_to_fire` fire gate), so a stance is a posture fact that gate
# already understood rather than a newly invented behaviour.
# When nobody claims Tactical, the auxiliary Command station (below, normally
# hosted by Captain) lists it and applies one of these authored stances. A
# stance supplies the weapons AI hosts their alert POSTURE the same way Red
# Alert does — it never buffs a stat or fires a gun itself. The two neutral
# fallbacks are the migrated Red Alert path: `high_alert_neutral` behaves as
# "at red alert", `normal_alert_neutral` as "stood down", and changing the
# ship's alert switches between them without overwriting a standard order.
# [ai] The four stance ids and the `persist_behind_human` / `ai_engaged`
# choices mirror the destroyer's catalogue deliberately, so a Captain who
# learned Command on one hull reads the same vocabulary on the other.

# The posture an uncrewed Command seat adopts at Red Alert (issue #1109). When

# alert-neutral otherwise — the same authored stance a human would pick,

# authored in the rig sidecar (`assets/models/alliance_cruiser_recreated.model.toml`).

# On the `helm` power group at the table's `min_power_level = 2`, exactly as the
# destroyer's dock is, and for the reason spelled out there: docking gear adds no
# new resting draw of its own, and a Power officer who robs Helm below level 2
# takes the docking clamps down with the drive. It is listed in NO rating's
# `automated_systems` — an unmanned Helm flies, it does not dock on its own.
[[system]]

kind = "dock"
station = "helm"
power_group = "helm"

# ── Tractor and Umbilical (issue #1390) ──────────────────────────────────────
# The other half of this hull's external work, and the half the dock exists to
# serve: a beam that takes a craft under tow, and a transfer line that moves a
# capacity across a mate the Helm has made.
#
# ENGINEERING-owned, not Helm-owned, and that split is deliberate rather than
# incidental: the dock is FLOWN (the server flies the mate manoeuvre, so the seat
# that flies the ship presses Dock), while the coupling and the flow are RUN — an
# engineer grips a hull and watches a ledger drain, which is the destroyer's own
# arrangement since #1156/#1160 and the one PRD #1143's player/NPC symmetry is
# built on. The `kind` is what maps each onto the Engineering Console Family
# (`ship::system_registry`) and what makes `TractorBeam`/`UmbilicalLine` appear at
# spawn; the terms they run under are the `[tractor]` and `[umbilical]` tables at
# the foot of this file.
#
# On the `helm` power group at each table's `min_power_level = 2`, exactly as the
# destroyer's pair is, and for the reason spelled out there: a power group draws
# by its LEVEL, not per system, so hanging these off `helm` adds NO new resting
# draw and leaves the reactor budget untouched — a fresh `ops` group would rest a

# Helm below level 2 takes the tow and the transfer down with the drive and the
# clamps together. Neither is listed in any rating's `automated_systems` — an
# unmanned Engineering runs power and repair, it does not tow on its own.
