# ── AI: what is composed, what stays inline (issues #875, #876) ──────────────
#
# The five target selectors, the stateless helm axes, Shields focus, Power
# allocation and the Comms response all come from
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. The Captain's red-alert doctrine comes from
# `fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml`. Engines and Steering come from the
# baseline too — see the note on `includes` for why this hull takes no class
# movement doctrine, what a retry would have to decide first, and the numbers
# behind both halves of that.
#
# Three things deliberately stay inline, and each for a reason about PRESENCE
# rather than about taste — authoring a sub-table brings its parent into
# existence, and the spawner gates capabilities on those parents:
#
#   * `[torpedoes.ai]` below. A fragment carrying it would create `[torpedoes]`
#     on every hull that included the fragment, and a `[torpedoes]` table with no
#     `[[torpedoes.tubes]]` is a torpedo system with zero tubes.
#   * the per-bank and per-tube fire gates, up with their banks. Those arrays
#     merge by `id`, so a shared fragment could only name ids it cannot know, and
#     an unmatched id APPENDS a weapon with no geometry.
#   * `[power]` and `[shields_console.base]`, up above. The fragment library
#     carries the POLICIES that read them, never the hardware.
#
# For the same reason no fragment this hull includes carries `tags`,
# `repair_team_count` or `[[hull.system_hull]]`: `tags` UNIONS on compose, so a
# fragment carrying `"npc"` would silently flip this hull out of
# `is_player_flyable`, and the other two would hand this hull equipment it never
# authored or erase the system-hull entries it did. `[[shield_arc]]` is on the
# same list, and this hull's four arcs are the reason it has to be.

# Torpedo magazine — two axes on one authored block.
#
# GRANT: always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The offline +
# non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this rule is the authored arbiter
# layered on top, and it is where a hull would ration rounds between its tubes.
#
# CONSERVATION (issue #943): whether a launch the ship has already authorised may
# SPEND its round here, or should hold it for later in the mission. Resolved
# inside `handle_fire_torpedo`, the one consumer of an admitted `FireTorpedo`, so
# a human Tactical operator and an AI backfill meet this guard identically — the
# per-tube `torpedo_launch` doctrine gates only the AI, and a gate that
# constrains NPCs alone is how a player empties the whole magazine into wave one.
#
# `rounds_per_threat` is a host reading, not an authored number: every round the
# ship still HAS — the magazine PLUS whatever is already parked in the tubes —
# divided by the mission threat still ahead, which the SCENARIO publishes as the
# world counter `mission_threat_remaining`. A world that publishes none leaves
# the ratio unbounded and this rule always fires, because pacing is something a
# mission asks for and never something a hull decides for itself.
#
# `min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5` reads "keep one round for every TWO things still
# coming". Before retuning it, understand what kind of gate it is: a ONE-WAY
# LATCH. `rounds_aboard` only ever FALLS inside a mission, and the threat count
# only falls when something DIES — so a hull that dips under its own reserve
# stops firing, stops killing the thing that would bring the count down, and
# never climbs back over the line. Whatever is authored here is not a soft
# brake. It is a floor the ship must never be pushed below mid-mission.
#
# 0.5 is chosen for the margin it leaves, not for a tidy identity:
#
#   * The middle of the mission stays open. Over every position combat_test can
#     put this hull in while it still carries half its payload or more, the
#     reserve clears at least 4 rounds — two full volleys — against the wave in
#     front of it. A wave that survives one volley is a wave that never dies,
#     and a wave that never dies freezes the threat count and the latch with it.
#   * Nothing is stranded. At the last unit of threat the floor is half a round,
#     so anything still aboard clears the gate and can be spent on the last
#     fight. A reserve measured against the magazine COUNTER rather than the
#     rounds aboard strands the parked volley whatever this number is, because
#     the counter is debited the moment a tube starts loading.
#
# What it trades away is the front of the mission. The floor at eight published
# waves is 4 rounds rather than 8, so an engagement lasting as long as the hull
# is willing to keep shooting may now take 10 of the 12 rounds while the whole
# schedule is still published, where 1.0 capped it at 6. That ceiling is a
# licence rather than a forecast — flown for real the destroyer spends 6 across
# that stretch either way, because the engagement ends before the gate does —
# but it is what 0.5 permits, and it is the price of the margin above.
#
# The tidy identity is what 1.0 bought (issue #943): the reserve came to exactly
# one round at the last unit of threat, so on paper nothing could ever be
# stranded. It shipped with ZERO margin and it broke. Against the old asteroid
# layout the destroyer bottomed out at exactly 7 rounds against 7 remaining
# waves — a ratio of exactly 1.0, the last reading the gate still passes. #946
# reshuffled which rock lands in which cell (same radii, same split), that moved
# the engagement by one round, the ratio fell under, the latch shut, and
# combat_test's wave chain stalled at wave 2 with the hull holding rounds it
# would never fire.
#
# All of it is measured, not asserted by hand.
# `the_shipped_destroyer_spends_its_whole_payload_across_the_eight_wave_mission`
# (`src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs`) walks this doctrine through the real
# torpedo system over the world's whole authored schedule, INCLUDING a wave that
# outlives the engagement fought against it, and states the latch directly on
# the doctrine.
# `combat_test_paces_the_player_magazine_against_the_whole_eight_wave_threat`
# (`tests/headless_runner.rs`) flies it for real and prints the magazine's
# shape bucketed by remaining threat, (entered, lowest) per bucket:
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 2), 6: (2, 2), 5: (2, 2)}. Read a bucket as a STRETCH OF
# THE MISSION rather than as one engagement — since #960 a wave arrives on its
# own clock whether or not the last one is dead, so the top bucket spans wave 1
# and the opening of wave 2, and bottoms lower than the death-gated chain used
# to show. Ten of the twelve rounds go while six or more waves are still
# published; the last two then sit under the floor (2/6 and 2/5 are both below
# 0.5) until the count reaches 4. At 1.0 the same run reads
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 6)} and stops there: the latch shuts the moment wave 1
# dies, and wave 2 never does.
#
# `sole_objective_count = 1` is the carve-out, and it counts NAMED Destroy
# targets rather than doctrine entries. A world's `spawn_entity` override
# APPENDS its brief to the template's standing orders — doctrine reconciles by
# `id`, and an instance override may not remove what the template authored — so
# combat_test's raid cruisers carry their template's untargeted
# `destroy-hostiles` alongside the `assault-starbase` the world hands them: two
# entries, one named target, one engagement they will not outlive. Those spend
# freely. A hull whose brief names no target reads 0 and paces — which is the
# player's destroyer, the ship #943 was filed about.
[torpedoes.ai]
param = { min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5, sole_objective_count = 1.0 }

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_magazine_grant"
when = "true"
verb = "grant_torpedo_round"

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_conservation"
when = "fact(targeted_objective_count) == param(sole_objective_count) or fact(rounds_per_threat) >= param(min_rounds_per_threat)"
verb = "release_torpedo"

# ── Doctrine tuning: parameters only (issue #876 AC3) ────────────────────────
#
# [ai] The four values below are ratified by #1082's fixed five-seed,
# four-opponent report (`scripts/balance-runs.cruiser.toml`). The report's
# station-activity rows are Human=0, Offline=0, AI>0 for every active station,
# so this is explicitly the composed #876 Backfill path, not a legacy AI route.
#
# The whole specialisation of a shared class doctrine, and the entire authoring
# interface a hull has to it. No rule, state or transition is restated here: the
# `param` table is an ordinary TOML table and deep-merges, so naming one key
# retunes that threshold and leaves the machine alone.
#
# FOUR keys across two axes, and the split is not arbitrary.
#
# `combat_orbit_range` and `combat_orbit_speed` are read by the HOST off the
# STEERING axis — Steering's yaw verb is what tells the host which leg is being
# flown — and no predicate on either axis references them, so restating them on
# Engines would author a param nothing reads.
#
# `torpedo_run_range` is the opposite case and MUST be restated. No Rust reads it;
# it is referenced by the entry guard of the doctrine's own `orbit` state, which
# exists on BOTH axes because they are two independent copies of one machine that
# agree by reading the same facts rather than by sharing state. A copy left on the
# fragment's class default would break its ring at a different range from the
# other, and the two axes would disagree about which leg they are flying — the
# silent failure the fragment's header warns about, pinned in both directions by
# `the_torpedo_run_opens_on_a_loaded_salvo_and_closes_on_the_hulls_own_armament`.
#
# ── The ring, and the range it is actually sized against ─────────────────────
#
# 22 units, which is a long way inside the 40-unit `beam_range` both phaser banks
# author — and the margin is not caution, it is what a proportional ring costs.
#
# The RANGE this is sized against is now simply 40. Since issue #955 a phaser
# reaches its authored `beam_range` at every power level: the multiplication by
# `ModifierSlot::RadarRange` that used to sit in every firing path is gone, and
# with it the reason this note used to give two numbers.
#
# What it used to say, and why the ring did not move when #955 landed: the slot
# was driven by the SENSORS power group (retired entirely in #952, which put
# `shields` in its place), this hull rested that group at 1, that rung
# contributed `-0.5`, and `ShipModifiers::rebuild_cache` folds a negative sum as
# `1 / (1 + |sum|)` — so the banks reached 26.7 rather than 40.
# Bracketed by measurement rather than derived: the bow hold is flown at
# `torpedo_bearing_speed = 0`, so opening `torpedo_run_range` out parks the hull
# at a chosen range, and swept on `probe_aggressor` over 40 s it dealt 80 parked
# at 26.3-28.3 and ZERO parked at 27.4-29.2. Every number below that predates
# #955 was measured against that shorter reach.
#
# The ring stays at 22 anyway, and the reason is the CONTROLLER rather than the
# gun: the orbit's correction is proportional with no integral term, so the hull
# settles slightly outside whatever radius it is given, and 22 is the value the
# throttle sweep below was measured at. A ring is an authored fighting distance,
# not a derived one — retuning it is a balance decision with its own sweep, and
# #955 supplies no evidence for a new value. What #955 buys this hull is a
# faster opening: the run-in opens fire at 40 instead of closing to 26.7 first.
#
# ── The throttle, and why the class default is not kept ──────────────────────
#
# 0.7 rather than the fragment's 0.6, and the honest reason is that the fragment's
# default measurably loses this hull ENGAGEMENTS, not that it looks wrong.
#
# The mechanism is real and is documented in the fragment's header: while the
# tubes are loaded and out of arc, Channel 3's `ArcBearingRequest` overwrites this
# hull's STEERING with a bow-on solution and leaves the doctrine's THROTTLE alone,
# so whatever fraction of the ring Channel 3 is flying is flown bow-on at this
# speed. But the conclusion an earlier revision drew from it — that SLOWER is
# therefore safer — is the opposite of what the probes report, and the numbers it
# cited for that (a break-off to 380 units at 0.6, a kill at 0.35) do not
# reproduce at all. They are withdrawn.
#
# Re-measured, `--deterministic`, 30 Hz, one variable:
#
#   * `probe_aggressor`, 30 s, the hull's own world seed. Damage dealt rises with
#     throttle to a FLAT optimum and then breaks:
#         0.35 → 62   0.40 → 63   0.45 → 64   0.50 → 65   0.55 → 65
#         0.60 → 67   0.65 → 67   0.70 → 67   0.75 → 67   0.80 → 67
#         0.85 → 67   0.90 → 67 but 46 TAKEN, where every other row takes 0
#     Uncomposed on `main` this probe is 64 dealt / 0 taken, so 0.35 shipped a
#     hull that fought WORSE than the doctrine it replaced, and anything in
#     0.60-0.85 beats it.
#   * `probe_duel`, 45 s, 30 seeds against a destroyer that closes and shoots
#     back. Survivals, against uncomposed `main`'s 14/30:
#         0.35 → 0/10   0.50 → 3/10   0.60 → 5/20   0.68 → 15/20
#         0.70 → 18/30  0.72 → 11/20  0.75 → 17/30  0.78 → 20/20
#         0.80 → 27/30  0.82 → 6/20   0.85 → 8/20
#
# Two things follow, and the second is why this is 0.7 and not 0.78.
#
# The duel is USABLE ONLY TO RULE VALUES OUT. Its outcomes are quantised — whole
# blocks of seeds return byte-identical damage totals — so the seed is not
# sampling a distribution, it is nudging a nearly-deterministic two-body geometry
# across thresholds. Read as a function of throttle it is not smooth: 0.78 wins
# every seed and 0.82 loses fourteen of twenty. A value picked at the top of that
# curve is fitted to this one hostile, which is exactly the mistake this comment
# is replacing. What the duel DOES say reliably is that everything below 0.65 and
# everything from 0.82 up is worse than uncomposed, and the whole of 0.68-0.80 is
# at least as good.
#
# So the value is chosen from the AGGRESSOR's flat optimum and the hull's own turn
# authority, and only checked against the duel. A settled ring demands a sustained
# yaw rate of `v / r`; at `R = 22` the equilibrium radius is ~23.3, so 0.6 asks
# 65 per cent of this hull's `max_yaw_rate = 0.4`, 0.7 asks 75, 0.8 asks 85 and 0.9
# asks 95 — and 0.9 is precisely where the aggressor probe starts taking damage.
# 0.7 sits mid-band on the probe with a wide flat optimum, keeps a quarter of the
# hull's turn authority in hand for tracking a target that is itself manoeuvring,
# and lands inside the duel's ≥-uncomposed region rather than on its best point.
#
# It is NOT the best number measured. 0.78 and 0.80 both score higher on the duel
# and neither is authored, because 0.82 collapses and a value four hundredths from
# a cliff is a fit, not a choice.
#
# What shipping this fixes, said flatly. At 0.35 this hull dealt LESS and died
# SOONER than the uncomposed one on every seed tried, turning two survivals into
# two deaths — a balance regression. At 0.7, over the same 30 seeds, it survives 18
# against uncomposed's 14, deals a mean 29.0 against 22.5 and takes a mean 189
# against 281. The regression is gone rather than merely narrowed, on all three.
#
# WITHDRAWN (issue #929). This paragraph read: "What is NOT claimed: that this
# hull WINS `probe_duel`. At every throttle tried, composed or not, the best
# result against that destroyer is a draw. The doctrine improves a fight the
# cruiser still does not win." That was true of the hull it was measured on and
# is now flatly false — the cruiser wins 25 of 28 `probe_duel` seeds and loses 3.
# Nothing about the throttle changed; the guns did (`beam_damage_per_sec` 4 -> 32
# with both banks bearing) and torpedoes stopped bypassing raised screens.
#
# READ EVERY NUMBER IN THIS SECTION AS HISTORICAL. The whole throttle sweep above
# was measured at `beam_damage_per_sec = 4` under the old torpedo impact model,
# so its damage totals (62-67 dealt on `probe_aggressor`, "a mean 29.0 against
# 22.5") and its survival counts belong to that hull. What survives the change is
# the SHAPE the sweep establishes and the reason 0.7 is authored: a flat optimum
# across 0.60-0.85 on the aggressor probe, a cliff at 0.82 on the duel, and a
# yaw-authority argument that is pure geometry (`v / r` against `max_yaw_rate`)
# and does not depend on the guns at all. Re-running the sweep against the
# current guns is a ratification job, not a correction — none of the evidence
# above argues for a different value, it merely no longer measures this hull.
#
# ── The torpedo run's range gate ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# 25 units: comfortably inside the 40 the beams reach since issue #955 — it was
# sized when they reached only 26.3-27.4, and the decoupling widened the margin
# rather than closing it — and just outside the 21.8-22.0 the hull holds against
# a passive target.
#
# Authoring it TIGHTER than the range the hull settles at is the failure that
# matters — the leg never opens, and the hull flies a ring nothing ever
# interrupts, which is the sawtooth the leg exists to end.
#
# The opposite failure is real but does not currently bind at this throttle, and
# that is worth saying rather than implying. Opened out, the run can trigger during
# the RUN-IN and cut thrust at whatever range the tubes finished loading at: swept
# on `probe_aggressor` at throttle 0.35, a gate of 28 parks the hull at 27.4-29.2
# dealing NOTHING for the whole run, against 80 at the shipped 25. At 0.7 the
# approach is quick enough that the tubes have not finished reloading before the
# ring is reached, so gates from 25 all the way out to 200 all park the hull at
# 21.8-22.0 and all deal the same 83. The gate is authored because the doctrine's
# contract needs it on both axes and because a slower approach makes it bind, not
# because it is doing visible work in this probe today.
[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
torpedo_run_range = 25.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
combat_orbit_range = 22.0
combat_orbit_speed = 0.7
torpedo_run_range = 25.0

# ── Arc-keeping and the weak-broadside flip (issue #929) ─────────────────────
#
# [ai] Ratified by #1082's fixed five-seed, four-opponent report
# (`scripts/balance-runs.cruiser.toml`). They are the doctrine half of the arc-dwell finding:
# instrumented on `probe_duel`, EVERY beam this hull lights ends because the
# target left the burning bank's arc, not because the burn expired. The banks are
# arc-limited, so arc dwell is what is actually being wasted, and these are the
# two levers the ring has to spend on it.
#
# ARC-KEEPING. `arc_keep_margin_deg` is how close to an arc EDGE the target may
# drift before the ring stops flying for position and starts flying for the guns;
# `arc_keep_speed` is the throttle it drops to when that happens.
#
# The mechanism this leans on is NOT new and this hull already carried it:
# `[helm_console] low_speed_turn_boost = 0.2` (below) makes the effective yaw
# rate `max_yaw_rate * (1 + 0.2 * (1 - speed_fraction))`, so backing the throttle
# from 0.7 to 0.3 of the cap buys about 8 % more turn authority — and, the larger
# half of the effect, shortens the arc the ring has to sweep per second. The
# doctrine is finally spending a capability the physics has always offered.
#
# WHICH READING IT ACTS ON took a correction worth recording. The obvious one —
# the best-bearing bank's margin — is useless here: two 270-degree arcs on the
# centreline overlap so heavily that their union has no gap, and the best margin
# never falls below 45 degrees at ANY bearing, so a threshold under 45 could
# never fire and one over it would fire always. `tick_beams_prepare` asks about
# the ONE bank that is burning, so the reading a helm can act on is the MINIMUM
# over bearing banks: how soon the broadside goes from two guns to one. At 20 the
# lever fires on about 83 of a 90 s run's AI ticks.
#
# THE FLIP. `weak_shield_flip_hp` / `weak_shield_restore_hp` reverse the ring so
# the OTHER broadside faces the enemy once the presented arc has been beaten
# down, and hold it reversed until the hurt side has genuinely recovered. Owner's
# priority order: shield protection beats arc-keeping, and the flip is allowed to
# cost arc dwell — the guns swap sides and the target crosses the blind wedge to
# get there. Measured active on about 399 of that same run's AI ticks, so this
# hull spends a real fraction of a fight presenting its good side.
#
# The pair is a DEADBAND and the gap between them is the whole point. This hull's
# arcs are 100 hp and regenerate 2 (7 focused), so a single threshold would have
# the ring reversing every few ticks as the arc bobbed across it. 25 to flip and
# 60 to come back is thirty-five points of travel in each direction.
#
# Nothing else in the doctrine has to know. The flip mirrors the DIRECTION only:
# same radius, same speed, same tangent geometry, other side — so the
# `torpedo_run` bow hold opens from either broadside exactly as it did, and the
# 28-seed launch count is unmoved by it.
#
# WHAT THEY BOUGHT, `probe_duel --deterministic --hz 30 --sim-seconds 90`, 12
# seeds, one variable at a time, at the `beam_damage_per_sec = 32` this hull
# carried when they were written:
#
#                     arc off   arc off   arc ON    arc ON
#                     flip off  flip ON   flip off  flip ON
#   duels resolving    10/12     10/12     12/12     12/12
#   this hull kills    10/12     10/12     12/12     12/12
#   damage taken       479       479       296       270
#   damage dealt       516       513       511       503
#   bow hold (mean)    10.6 s    10.6 s     0.5 s     0.5 s
#
# Arc-keeping is the large effect and it is not subtle: a 38 % cut in damage
# taken, every duel resolving, and a bow hold that all but disappears because a
# hull that keeps its guns on the target does not need to break the ring to point
# them. The flip is a smaller, additive win on the same axis — another 9 % off
# damage taken for about 1 % of damage dealt, which is the trade it was asked
# for.
#
# WHAT THEY DID NOT BUY, recorded because it was the stated goal. "Beam-on-target
# coverage", measured as the distinct sim ticks on which a phaser bank actually
# landed damage, does NOT rise: 4.5-5.3 % of ticks before, 4.2-5.5 % after, noise
# either way. The gain is real but it is not dwell — the ring holds a better
# firing position and takes far less in return, and the coverage proxy is
# dominated by how fast damage accumulates per landing tick rather than by how
# long a bank bears. A future pass wanting to measure dwell directly should count
# BURNING ticks at the beam site, not landing ticks from the balance ledger.
arc_keep_margin_deg = 20.0
arc_keep_speed = 0.3
weak_shield_flip_hp = 25.0
weak_shield_restore_hp = 60.0
weak_shield_flip_dwell_secs = 4.0

# ── AI sensing horizon ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Authored, not defaulted. `AiProfile.sensor_range` is what `ai::lod::evaluate_lod`
# measures an NPC copy of this hull against: a ship further than
# `sensor_range * 1.2` from the player for `LOD_DWELL_SECS` loses
# `AiHighFidelity`, and with it every helm/captain/weapons decider it carries.
# `simulate_low_lod_ships` then dead-reckons it on its LAST heading and speed
# for ever — a hull demoted mid-manoeuvre at speed simply leaves the scenario
# and never comes back.
#
# Every Harrow hull has always authored this (`ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`
# 400, `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` 350). No Alliance hull did, so an Alliance
# hull spawned as an NPC fell to the 100.0 Rust fallback in
# `entities::spawner` — INSIDE its own authored doctrine envelope, whose
# `commit_range`/`safe_range_margin` legs work out past 120 units. The value
# below is sized to the doctrine this hull flies, so the ship stays decided-for
# across its own manoeuvre.
[ai_profile]
# [ai] The selected aggression and sensing envelope participate in the #1082
# four-opponent Backfill report and are therefore ratified with the combat
# doctrine above; do not retune them outside the same seeded matrix.
aggression = 0.8
sensor_range = 350.0

# ── Dock terms (issue #1388) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The approach terms the `[[system]] kind = "dock"` above runs under. The table's
# PRESENCE is also the opt-in that makes this hull dockable at all: it, and only
# it, triggers the one spawn-time read of the rig sidecar for `dock`-prefixed
# markers (`entities::spawner`'s `DockSpawn`), so a hull that authors no `[dock]`
# reads no sidecar and its world's `content_digest` is unchanged.
#
# The values are the shipped fleet dock vocabulary verbatim
# (`alliance_destroyer.toml`, `alliance_tender.toml`, `dock_probe`): the reach the
# control appears within and a held dock parts past, the close-in engage distance,
# the low approach speed, the mate tolerance, how far undock backs clear, and the
# lowest powered rung. Deliberately IDENTICAL to the destroyer's rather than
# scaled to this bigger hull — a berth is a berth, and a shared reach is what lets
# one authored structure be dockable by either hull without per-hull tuning. The
# dock MARKERS themselves are authored in the rig sidecar
# (`assets/models/alliance_cruiser_recreated.model.toml`), not here. [ai] Unratified.
[dock]
range = 200.0
engage_distance = 400.0
approach_speed = 60.0
mate_tolerance = 4.0
undock_clear_distance = 120.0
min_power_level = 2

# ── Tractor terms (issue #1390) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The coupling terms the `[[system]] kind = "tractor"` above runs under: how far
# the beam reaches, where the held load rides relative to the operator, and the
# lowest powered rung. Like `[dock]`, the table's PRESENCE is the opt-in — a hull
# that authors no `[tractor]` spawns no `TractorBeam` and its consoles are
# unchanged.
#
# `range = 500` and `coupling_offset = [0, 0, -90]` are the destroyer's values
# verbatim, and deliberately so rather than scaled to this bigger hull, for the
# reason `[dock]` above gives: a shared reach is what lets one authored hulk be
# towable by either hull without per-hull tuning. The offset is not a hull
# dimension either way — 90 units astern is dozens of hull radii on both hulls
# (this rig's `[collider] radius = 1.5`), far enough that nothing about the
# cruiser's extra beam brings the load inside it. The load rides astern in the
# operator's OWN frame, so turning the ship swings the tow round rather than
# dragging it sideways (`tractor::coupling::coupled_position`). [ai] Unratified.
[tractor]
range = 500.0
coupling_offset = [ 0.0, 0.0, -90.0 ]
min_power_level = 2

# The fleet tow-load curve the tug, the tractor probe and the destroyer all
# author: a laden hulk costs the helm half the penalty at #1154's default entity
# mass and approaches — but never reaches — a 0.8 ceiling. Shared for the same
# reason the reach is: the cost of towing a given hulk should be a fact about the
# hulk, not about which Alliance hull picked it up. [ai] Unratified.
[tractor.tow_load]
half_penalty_mass = 10000.0
max_penalty = 0.8

# ── Umbilical terms (issue #1390) ────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# What the transfer moves, how fast, which way, and the lowest powered rung. The
# capacity id both docked ends must carry is `reserve_fuel`, the shipped resupply
# ledger (`alliance_tender.toml`, `umbilical_probe`, `alliance_destroyer.toml`);
# `direction = "deliver"` sends the operator's capacity to the docked partner,
# which is a crew pumping load INTO a depot's demand rows. `rate = 20` is the
# shipped flow rate. [ai] Unratified.
#
# This hull authors NO `[infrastructure]` ledger of its own — deliberately, and
# for the destroyer's reason: a condition/capacity track on the crew's own hull
# would fold into every world it flies. Until a scenario gives the transfer an
# end to draw from, the flow refuses `NoCapacity`, which is inert in combat_test
# and patrol where the cruiser never docks. A world that wants the crew to pump
# says so itself, by overriding `[infrastructure]` onto the picked hull the way
# `tests/smoke/operations-dock-umbilical.spec.js` does.
[umbilical]
capacity = "reserve_fuel"
rate = 20.0
direction = "deliver"
min_power_level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml:
name = "entity.alliance_destroyer.name"
display_name = "entity.alliance_destroyer.display_name"
class = "destroyer"
hull_id = "AEV-0741"
power_rating = 70
css = "gui/themes/cruiser.css"
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit. Surfaced on a
# Sensors scan and the deterministic input a mass-driven mechanic (the
# tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of guessing from the hull's other
# stats. [ai] Unratified — a destroyer-class weight, mid-ladder between the
# courier and the battleship.
mass = 14000.0
# Player identity (the `player` tag + `playerShip` radar icon) is NOT authored
# here — it is injected onto the selected hull at the player game-start spawn
# (see `player_ship_identity` in `src/server_app.rs`). A world-spawned copy of
# this hull is an ordinary NPC ship, so it must not masquerade as the player.
tags = [ "ship" ]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"
# ── Composition (issue #875) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The first COMPOSED shipped hull. Everything below `includes` is what this hull
# specialises; the shared AI doctrine it flies comes from the fragment library
# under `assets/entities/fragments/ai/`, whole policy block at a time, and is
# tuned here by PARAMETER only.
#
# Order is significant: fragments merge in declared order and this file merges
# last, so the includer always wins. `movement_attack_pass.toml` is listed after
# `fleet_baseline.toml` because it REPLACES the baseline's three travel axes.
#
# Resolution happens at authoring time. The runtime never sees a fragment — it
# sees one resolved document, and PRD #774's "every AI-capable fine system
# declares a policy" is satisfied by that document, not by this file.
includes = [
  "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
  "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml",
  "fragments/ai/movement_attack_pass.toml",
]

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_destroyer_recreated.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 1.2
length = 3
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Default doctrine for a backfilled/unmanned player destroyer (#842 — the other
# half of #838's human/AI symmetry). See the fuller note on `alliance_cruiser.toml`;
# in short, authoring `[behaviour]` is the single missing piece that makes
# `spawn_entity` attach the `BehaviourSection` on the player game-start path, so a
# backfilled destroyer engages through the same path an NPC does instead of only
# returning fire once hit.
#
#   Destroy (45) — UNTARGETED (no `directive_target`) → licenses the
#                  nearest-hostile scan and proactive engagement.
#   Hold    (20) — no directive when no hostile is visible: the helm holds station.
#
# Engage priority stays LOW (45) so scenario `spawn_entity` overrides (Destroy at
# 80) merge by id and dominate (#842 AC3). No Retreat — a fast attack hull fights.
# `maintain_range = 24` keeps the destroyer inside its 30-unit omni phaser and
# 35-unit blaster range.
#
# `imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6` (issue #780 AC4): see the fuller
# note on `alliance_cruiser.toml`. Every shipped hull left this at its 1.0
# (effectively off) default, so avoidance only ever bent travel and never
# actually turned the ship's facing away from a closing obstacle — the fix for
# the "AI flies through asteroid fields" report against the backfilled player
# hull.
#
# Issue #968 changed what 0.6 MEANS without changing the number: urgency is now
# the spent share of the authored `avoidance_buffer` measured surface-to-surface
# (squared), so this trips at a fixed 1.13 units of clearance whatever the
# obstacle's size, rather than at 40% of an avoidance radius that grew with it.
# Later against `huge` rocks in the sense that matters (the old form only fired
# once this hull was already inside one), and about fourteen times earlier
# against `small` ones. The cruiser's note has the arithmetic.
[behaviour]
imminent_collision_facing_threshold = 0.6

maintain_range = 24.0

[[behaviour.doctrine]]

base_priority = 20.0
target_speed  = 0.0

# ── Durability ladder (#915 tuning pass) ─────────────────────────────────────
# The whole fleet was re-pegged in one pass, because these numbers only mean
# anything relative to each other. Dynasty hulls carry a monolithic
# `[hull] hull_integrity`; Alliance hulls have none, and their equivalent pool
# is the SUM of the per-system `max_hp` below. Shields sit on top of both.
#
#   Dynasty   destroyer 200 | patrol/cruiser 300 | warhawk 400
#   Alliance  courier 200 | destroyer 300 | cruiser 500 | battleship 800
#
# The Alliance figures were reached by scaling each hull's authored system HP
# proportionally, so the relative weighting between systems is unchanged. The
# three COUPLING systems (tractor/umbilical/dock, issue #1164) added below are
# operational rather than combat systems and sit OUTSIDE this ladder — see the
# note on their damage entries — so the 300 is the combat pool the balance pass
# tuned, not the raw `is_destroyed` sum.
#

# the caveat written beside the three coupling compartments above rather than an
# oversight. Those three already sit outside the 300-point combat ladder "in intent
# even though the raw `is_destroyed` sum now includes them"; each one a hull
# authors widens the pool `SystemHull::apply_damage` spreads incoming hull damage
# across, so it buys durability the ladder never priced.
#
# A fourth was not free. Authored at the coupling systems' 30 HP it took this
# hull's system pool from 390 to 420 and the measurement is on the record:
# `probe_aggressor` at seed 3 — where a player Alliance cruiser kills a passive
# one of these — ran 105 ticks longer, and every one of those ticks fell inside
# the cruiser's torpedo-run bow hold, tipping
# `headless_runner::the_composed_player_cruiser_rings_its_target_and_breaks_off_
# to_bear_its_tubes` from 129 bow-hold ticks against 176 on the ring to 234
# against the same 176. Dropping the entry restores that run tick for tick.

# System on this hull, which musters two teams, dispatches them across the same
# 400-unit reach, and carries no compartment of its own either. Twenty of this
# hull's thirty-three `[[system]]` blocks author no damage entry; a box is what a

range = 400.0

# The two damage fields are ALTERNATIVES, not two halves of one payload

# lose is the opening — its two 45-degree blaster banks land 16 points a shot in
# a lump, which is how it collapses a 100 hp cruiser arc in the first place, and
# the rounds still go through the hole afterwards.

damage_hull = 45
damage_shields = 5
speed = 18
turn_rate_deg_per_sec = 60
lifespan = 18
load_time = 8

# Two launchers, ONE round of headroom between them (issue #942).
#
# The tube COUNT is unchanged — one fore, one aft, as the `torpedo-tube-fore` /
# `torpedo-tube-aft` hull entries above have always said. What changed is how
# many rounds a single opportunity may spend: fore 4 -> 2, aft 2 -> 1.
#
# The old pair parked six of the twelve-round magazine in the tubes and let one
# bearing dump all six, so the first wave met the whole payload and every wave
# after it met a hull with nothing left to launch. Halving the volleys makes a
# launch a DECISION about which wave deserves it rather than a button that
# empties the ship, and it keeps the two launchers meaningfully different: the
# fore tube (120-degree cone, the arc the doctrine's attack pass actually
# brings to bear) is the one that fires a pair, the aft tube spends its round
# one at a time on whoever got behind.
#
# `ai_target_count` is not authored on either tube, so an AI backfill keeps each
# at its own `volley_max` — 3 rounds parked across the hull instead of 6.
#
# Magazine SIZE is deliberately untouched here: `count = 12` still gates the
# ship's whole payload. Pacing that payload against the remaining mission was
# the sibling ticket, and it has landed — see the `torpedo_conservation` rule on
# `[torpedoes.ai]` below (issue #943). The two are complementary and neither
# subsumes the other: the volley caps here decide how much ONE opportunity may
# spend, and conservation decides whether the ship can afford to take the
# opportunity at all, given how many engagements the world says are still ahead.
[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "fore"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 120
load_time = 4
volley_max = 2
marker = "torpedo_fore"

  # synthesised (#885b). Two rules on two DIFFERENT channels, so they never
  # contend: keep the tube loaded, and launch when the alert is up AND the arc
  # the round would strike is down. Loaded state, magazine stock, target
  # validity, range and arc stay host-side gates.

  # "phasers strip the shields, torpedoes finish the hull" — and issue #956
  # moved it HERE from `auto_fire_torpedo`, where it was a Rust gate sitting
  # upstream of every policy: no doctrine could authorise a round while the
  # striking arc was up, and none could retune the threshold. It is an HP
  # reading rather than a boolean, resolved per-arc through the target's own arc
  # router, so this gate and the eventual hit agree about which arc is in the
  # way. A hull that wants to spend rounds differently edits this line;
  # `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` is the worked example of tightening it further,
  # and `idle = true` of declining launches altogether.
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872). `red_alert` is a host-seeded typed

  # operating the same system) to call it, so it holds. Delete the param and the
  # guard and the weapon is ungated again — the gate is content, not code.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 1.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"

#
# Both bands are scaled to the long-range radar's own 250-unit reach above: a
# contact the captain cannot select is a contact there is no point authoring a
# band for. Inside 120 the suite reads whole percent and counts capacities;
# beyond that it reports condition to the nearest quarter and stops claiming to
# count anything. That is the decision the slice exists for — the reading the
# crew have is worth what their range and their power bought.
[scan]
# The sensor bus rides the shields group, which is what #952 put in the retired
# sensors group's place. Level 2 is where the group boots, so a nominal ship can
# always scan and a Power officer who robs shields to feed weapons has taken the
# survey suite down with it.
power_group = "shields"
min_power_level = 2
# The storm bands Falling Skyway is built around. A destroyer sitting in one
# reads a band coarser; sitting in one at long range gets nothing at all.
degraded_by = [ "nebula_fog", "sensor_blind", "radar_dampening" ]
interference_bands = 1

[[scan.band]]
id = "detailed"
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.scan.band.detailed.label"
max_range = 120.0
condition_step = 0.01

[[scan.band]]
id = "coarse"
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.scan.band.coarse.label"
max_range = 260.0
condition_step = 0.25
# A sweep this coarse resolves whether a system is up or down but does not
# pretend to count berths.
report_capacities = false

# The BULK ladder (issue #1347), beside the fidelity ladder and for the same
# reason: what a reading says about a contact's weight is a property of this
# instrument, not of the contact. "Heavy" is a thing this suite says; the rock
# just has a mass. A hull that authors no ladder reports no class at all, which
# is what every hull did before this table existed.
#
# Unlike the bands above it does NOT coarsen with range — mass is content
# identity, so the class is the same answer from 40 units or 240. What range
# still decides is whether there is a reading at all.
#
# The four steps are cut against the masses actually authored in the fleet, so
# each one separates things a crew would want separated: a courier or a piece of
# corridor plating from a working hauler, a hauler from a warship, and a warship
# from a depot or a skyhook. The last class is the open top — anything heavier
# than 60,000 reports as the heaviest.
#
# [ai] All four thresholds unratified.
[[scan.mass_class]]
id = "light"
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.scan.mass_class.light.label"
max_mass = 5000.0

[[scan.mass_class]]
id = "medium"
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.scan.mass_class.medium.label"
max_mass = 20000.0

[[scan.mass_class]]
id = "heavy"
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.scan.mass_class.heavy.label"
max_mass = 60000.0

[[scan.mass_class]]
id = "massive"
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.scan.mass_class.massive.label"
max_mass = 1000000.0

[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.power_groups.helm.label"
# `min_level` is the COMMANDABLE floor: the lowest level any operator, human or
# AI, may order this group to. `PowerSystem` stores it per group and clamps
# every order to it (issue #1395 — before that it was a drawing hint the engine
# ignored, and the console's pip row is still the other thing it decides).
#
# It reads 1 because Helm must never be switched off: a ship with no power to
# the drive cannot manoeuvre out of anything, and losing the ability to run away
# is not a trade a Power officer should be able to make with one press. Turning
# it down to 1 to free a point for the 8-point budget IS a legal order, so rung
# 1 has to be reachable and drawn. NOMINAL — the rung whose multiplier is 1.0 —
# is 2, and that is `default_level`, where the group boots.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.power_groups.weapons.label"
# `min_level = 0`: this group may be taken COLD (issue #1395). Weapons is the
# one group on the hull that can be switched off outright, and that is how this
# ship expresses RESTRAINT — an Engineering order, visible to anyone watching the
# reactor, rather than a hidden captain's toggle. Zero is a real commandable
# level here, not a drawn rung: the console paints four pips whatever the floor
# says, and level 0 is all four dark under a COLD tag.
#
# Helm and Shields keep their floor of 1 (see Helm above). Cutting the drive or
# the shields to nothing is a way to lose a ship, not a way to make a statement
# with one; weapons at 0 costs the crew their guns and nothing else.
#
# NOMINAL (×1.0) is 2, which is where this group boots; dropping it to 1 is a
# legal order that spends the freed point elsewhere.
default_level = 2
min_level = 0
max_level = 4

[power_groups.shields]
label = "entity.alliance_destroyer.power_groups.shields.label"
# Nominal at 2 alongside Helm and Weapons: those three groups make the
# sustainable resting total of 6. Higher levels buy shield regeneration.
# `min_level = 1` is the COMMANDABLE floor (see Helm above): shields may be
# turned down to 1 but not switched off. Only Weapons authors a floor of 0.
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── Reference grid ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A faint lattice lying in the y = 0 plane, drawn under THIS hull on the
# viewscreen when it is the ship the player is flying. Space is featureless: a
# destroyer at full burn against a skybox reads as stationary, and the crew lose
# the only cue that says the helm is doing anything. The lines are locked to
# WORLD coordinates and the drawn patch follows the ship, so what moves on
# screen is the ship — which is the entire point of the table.
#
# Authoring one of these is opt-in per hull. An NPC never gets a grid whatever
# it authors: the renderer only ever reads the LOCAL ship's resolved config.
#
# [ai] Every number below is unratified. The two that most want a human eye are
# `patch_radius` and the two alphas — see the calibration note.
#
# HDR CALIBRATION. The viewscreen camera is HDR and tonemaps through
# `tony_mc_mapface`, with bloom thresholded at 1.0 and a softness of 0.4 (so the
# knee starts near 0.6) — `[render]` in the world file. Two consequences:
#   - keep the RGB components well under 0.6. They are pre-multiply values in a
#     linear buffer, and a navigation aid that blooms is louder than the ships
#     it is meant to sit behind.
#   - carry "faint" in the ALPHA, not the brightness. tony_mc_mapface has a
#     filmic toe that lifts near-black, so a dim-but-opaque line survives the
#     display transform far more assertively than its authored number suggests.
#     These values composite to roughly 0.07 linear over empty space, which the
#     transform brings up to a faint but legible grey. To make the grid quieter,
#     halve an alpha; halving an RGB triple mostly just changes its hue.
[reference_grid]
# The round-number idiom the radar rings already read in: ten and fifty. Major
# lines MUST fall on a whole multiple of minor ones — the loader refuses
# anything else — so that a major line brightens a minor line rather than
# sitting a fraction beside it.
minor_spacing = 10.0
major_spacing = 50.0
# Linear RGBA 0-1. Same desaturated instrument blue for both classes; the major
# lines are distinguished by being twice as opaque, not by being a second
# colour.
minor_colour = [ 0.45, 0.62, 0.78, 0.1 ]
major_colour = [ 0.55, 0.74, 0.9, 0.2 ]
# Master dimmer over both classes, so the whole grid can be taken down in one
# move without editing two alphas in step.
opacity = 1.0
# How far the drawn patch reaches from the ship, and how much of that reach is
# spent fading to nothing. [ai] The band was widened from 150 to 250 so the
# fade starts much closer in — at patch_radius - fade_band = 150 world units
# from the ship — and the lattice dissolves fast toward the rim rather than
# carrying legible lines almost to the edge. Wider still would leave no full-
# strength grid under the ship at all.
patch_radius = 400.0
fade_band = 250.0
# [ai] Exponent on the (smoothstepped) radial fade: the curve is
# smoothstep(...) ^ fade_exponent, and 2.5 pulls the whole band down so the grid
# is already faint a short way out and gone well before the rim — the harder
# distance falloff John asked for. The endpoints stay pinned at full and zero,
# so this never lights a bright far rim. 1.0 would be the plain smoothstep.
fade_exponent = 2.5
# [ai] World-space height of the grid plane. Dropped half a unit below the hull
# so it reads as a floor slightly beneath the ship rather than a lattice
# co-planar with it; the follow system parks the patch at this y.
plane_y = -0.5
# [ai] Height of the plane in the first-person camera only. That eye sits at
# hull height, where a floor half a unit down cuts straight across the view;
# ten units down it reads as a deck again. Cinematic and the overlays keep
# plane_y.
first_person_plane_y = -10.0
# Line widths in PIXELS, not world units. A world-space width makes near lines
# slabs and far lines sub-pixel shimmer, and this grid is read at every distance
# at once. Major lines are barely wider — brightness is what separates them.
minor_line_width_px = 1.0
major_line_width_px = 1.6

[cinematic_camera]
position = [0, 6, 12]
default_pitch_deg = 16
entity_look_range = 50
look_ahead_distance = 80
hysteresis_secs = 3
yaw_follow_deg_per_sec = 45
# [ai] Aim point lowered (world units) so the hull rises toward the lower
# third of the frame instead of crowding the bottom edge. The pitch above was
# steepened in step: both lower where the camera looks, the pitch across the
# whole no-target view and this offset also when tracking a target.
look_target_y_offset = -4.5

# ── AI: what is composed, what stays inline (issue #875) ─────────────────────
#
# The five target selectors, the three stateless helm axes (lateral, vertical,
# impulse), Shields focus, Power allocation and the Comms response all come from
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. The Captain's red-alert doctrine comes from
# `fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml`. Engines, Steering and Boost come from
# `fragments/ai/movement_attack_pass.toml` — the destroyer attack-pass doctrine,
# posture-gated, which is what makes this hull shadow at standoff while the alert
# is down and fly committed fly-through passes once it is up.
#
# Three things deliberately stay inline, and each for a reason about PRESENCE
# rather than about taste — authoring a sub-table brings its parent into
# existence, and the spawner gates capabilities on those parents:
#
#   * `[torpedoes.ai]` below. A fragment carrying it would create `[torpedoes]`
#     on every hull that included the fragment, and a `[torpedoes]` table with no
#     `[[torpedoes.tubes]]` is a torpedo system with zero tubes.
#   * the per-bank and per-tube fire gates, up with their banks. Those arrays
#     merge by `id`, so a shared fragment could only name ids it cannot know, and
#     an unmatched id APPENDS a weapon with no geometry.
#   * `[power]` and `[shields_console.base]`, up above. The fragment library
#     carries the POLICIES that read them, never the hardware.
#
# For the same reason no fragment this hull includes carries `tags`,
# `repair_team_count` or `[[hull.system_hull]]`: `tags` UNIONS on compose, so a
# fragment carrying `"npc"` would silently flip this hull out of
# `is_player_flyable`, and the other two would hand this hull equipment it never
# authored or erase the fourteen system-hull entries it did.

# Torpedo magazine — two axes on one authored block.
#
# GRANT: always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The offline +
# non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this rule is the authored arbiter
# layered on top, and it is where a hull would ration rounds between its tubes.
#
# CONSERVATION (issue #943): whether a launch the ship has already authorised may
# SPEND its round here, or should hold it for later in the mission. Resolved
# inside `handle_fire_torpedo`, the one consumer of an admitted `FireTorpedo`, so
# a human Tactical operator and an AI backfill meet this guard identically — the
# per-tube `torpedo_launch` doctrine gates only the AI, and a gate that
# constrains NPCs alone is how a player empties the whole magazine into wave one.
#
# `rounds_per_threat` is a host reading, not an authored number: every round the
# ship still HAS — the magazine PLUS whatever is already parked in the tubes —
# divided by the mission threat still ahead, which the SCENARIO publishes as the
# world counter `mission_threat_remaining`. A world that publishes none leaves
# the ratio unbounded and this rule always fires, because pacing is something a
# mission asks for and never something a hull decides for itself.
#
# `min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5` reads "keep one round for every TWO things still
# coming". Before retuning it, understand what kind of gate it is: a ONE-WAY
# LATCH. `rounds_aboard` only ever FALLS inside a mission, and the threat count
# only falls when something DIES — so a hull that dips under its own reserve
# stops firing, stops killing the thing that would bring the count down, and
# never climbs back over the line. Whatever is authored here is not a soft
# brake. It is a floor the ship must never be pushed below mid-mission.
#
# 0.5 is chosen for the margin it leaves, not for a tidy identity:
#
#   * The middle of the mission stays open. Over every position combat_test can
#     put this hull in while it still carries half its payload or more, the
#     reserve clears at least 4 rounds — two full volleys — against the wave in
#     front of it. A wave that survives one volley is a wave that never dies,
#     and a wave that never dies freezes the threat count and the latch with it.
#   * Nothing is stranded. At the last unit of threat the floor is half a round,
#     so anything still aboard clears the gate and can be spent on the last
#     fight. A reserve measured against the magazine COUNTER rather than the
#     rounds aboard strands the parked volley whatever this number is, because
#     the counter is debited the moment a tube starts loading.
#
# What it trades away is the front of the mission. The floor at eight published
# waves is 4 rounds rather than 8, so an engagement lasting as long as the hull
# is willing to keep shooting may now take 10 of the 12 rounds while the whole
# schedule is still published, where 1.0 capped it at 6. That ceiling is a
# licence rather than a forecast — flown for real the destroyer spends 6 across
# that stretch either way, because the engagement ends before the gate does —
# but it is what 0.5 permits, and it is the price of the margin above.
#
# The tidy identity is what 1.0 bought (issue #943): the reserve came to exactly
# one round at the last unit of threat, so on paper nothing could ever be
# stranded. It shipped with ZERO margin and it broke. Against the old asteroid
# layout the destroyer bottomed out at exactly 7 rounds against 7 remaining
# waves — a ratio of exactly 1.0, the last reading the gate still passes. #946
# reshuffled which rock lands in which cell (same radii, same split), that moved
# the engagement by one round, the ratio fell under, the latch shut, and
# combat_test's wave chain stalled at wave 2 with the hull holding rounds it
# would never fire.
#
# All of it is measured, not asserted by hand.
# `the_shipped_destroyer_spends_its_whole_payload_across_the_eight_wave_mission`
# (`src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs`) walks this doctrine through the real
# torpedo system over the world's whole authored schedule, INCLUDING a wave that
# outlives the engagement fought against it, and states the latch directly on
# the doctrine.
# `combat_test_paces_the_player_magazine_against_the_whole_eight_wave_threat`
# (`tests/headless_runner.rs`) flies it for real and prints the magazine's
# shape bucketed by remaining threat, (entered, lowest) per bucket:
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 2), 6: (2, 2), 5: (2, 2)}. Read a bucket as a STRETCH OF
# THE MISSION rather than as one engagement — since #960 a wave arrives on its
# own clock whether or not the last one is dead, so the top bucket spans wave 1
# and the opening of wave 2, and bottoms lower than the death-gated chain used
# to show. Ten of the twelve rounds go while six or more waves are still
# published; the last two then sit under the floor (2/6 and 2/5 are both below
# 0.5) until the count reaches 4. At 1.0 the same run reads
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 6)} and stops there: the latch shuts the moment wave 1
# dies, and wave 2 never does.
#
# `sole_objective_count = 1` is the carve-out, and it counts NAMED Destroy
# targets rather than doctrine entries. A world's `spawn_entity` override
# APPENDS its brief to the template's standing orders — doctrine reconciles by
# `id`, and an instance override may not remove what the template authored — so
# combat_test's raid cruisers carry their template's untargeted
# `destroy-hostiles` alongside the `assault-starbase` the world hands them: two
# entries, one named target, one engagement they will not outlive. Those spend
# freely. A hull whose brief names no target reads 0 and paces — which is the
# player's destroyer, the ship #943 was filed about.
[torpedoes.ai]
param = { min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5, sole_objective_count = 1.0 }

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_magazine_grant"
when = "true"
verb = "grant_torpedo_round"

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_conservation"
when = "fact(targeted_objective_count) == param(sole_objective_count) or fact(rounds_per_threat) >= param(min_rounds_per_threat)"
verb = "release_torpedo"

# ── Doctrine tuning: parameters only (issue #875 AC1) ────────────────────────
#
# The whole specialisation of a shared class doctrine, and the entire authoring
# interface a hull has to it. No rule, state or transition is restated here: the
# `param` table is an ordinary TOML table and deep-merges, so naming one key
# retunes that threshold and leaves the machine alone.
#
# `commit_range` is restated on all three axes because they are three
# INDEPENDENT copies of one machine that agree by reading the same facts — a copy
# left on the fragment's default would reach `inbound` at a different range from
# the other two and the axes would disagree about which leg they are flying.
#
# This hull is tuned DEFENSIVE relative to the class default: it commits later
# (120 rather than 150 — its longest direct-fire bank reaches 35, so a long run-in
# is time spent unable to shoot back) and it shadows a little tighter (45 rather
# than 60 units beyond the target's own reach, which is what keeps a 15-unit hull
# from losing contact altogether while the alert is down).
[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
commit_range = 120.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
commit_range = 120.0
safe_range_margin = 45.0

[helm_console.boost_ai.param]
commit_range = 120.0

# ── AI sensing horizon ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Authored, not defaulted. `AiProfile.sensor_range` is what `ai::lod::evaluate_lod`
# measures an NPC copy of this hull against: a ship further than
# `sensor_range * 1.2` from the player for `LOD_DWELL_SECS` loses
# `AiHighFidelity`, and with it every helm/captain/weapons decider it carries.
# `simulate_low_lod_ships` then dead-reckons it on its LAST heading and speed
# for ever — a hull demoted mid-manoeuvre at speed simply leaves the scenario
# and never comes back.
#
# Every Harrow hull has always authored this (`ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`
# 400, `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` 350). No Alliance hull did, so an Alliance
# hull spawned as an NPC fell to the 100.0 Rust fallback in
# `entities::spawner` — INSIDE its own authored doctrine envelope, whose
# `commit_range`/`safe_range_margin` legs work out past 120 units. The value
# below is sized to the doctrine this hull flies, so the ship stays decided-for
# across its own manoeuvre.
[ai_profile]
aggression = 1.0
sensor_range = 400.0

# ── Coupling terms (issue #1164 S11a) ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The authored terms for the tractor, umbilical and dock systems declared above,
# and the whole of what the retired `[[operations.capability]]` blocks (transfer,
# field_repair, tow, stabilise) became. Falling Skyway's own migration onto these
# systems is a following slice (#1165 S11b); this hull carries every replacement
# system that scenario will need before it starts.
#
# The mapping — four capabilities onto three systems:
#   tow + stabilise -> the TRACTOR. Both were "take the strain off a crippled
#                      craft and hold it": one beam that couples a locked target
#                      and holds it does both. `[tractor.tow_load]` is the
#                      held-load helm penalty (#1157) the old verbs never had.
#   transfer        -> the UMBILICAL, run over the DOCK. A transfer stood up at a
#                      structure is now Helm achieving a dock and Engineering
#                      flowing a capacity across it (#1159/#1160).
#   field_repair    -> `[repair.external_dispatch]`, authored up with `[repair]`.

# TRACTOR — the coupling reach, where a held load rides, the lowest powered rung,
# and the mass -> helm-penalty curve. [ai] Unratified.
#
# `range = 500` is the destroyer's OWN longest authored coupling reach, carried
# from the old `stabilise` (stand-off work off a shedding head); it comfortably
# covers the old `tow`'s 300-unit close work in the one beam. `coupling_offset`
# is the old `tow`'s `tow_offset` verbatim — the load rides 90 units astern in
# the destroyer's own frame, so turning the ship swings it round rather than
# dragging it sideways. `[tractor.tow_load]` adopts the fleet curve the tug and
# the tractor probe author (half-penalty at #1154's default entity mass, a 0.8
# ceiling a laden hulk approaches but never reaches).
[tractor]
range = 500.0
coupling_offset = [ 0.0, 0.0, -90.0 ]
min_power_level = 2

[tractor.tow_load]
half_penalty_mass = 10000.0
max_penalty = 0.8

# DOCK — the approach terms the umbilical's flow gates on (a transfer waits on
# Helm having achieved the dock, #1159). The values are the shipped dock
# vocabulary (`alliance_tender.toml`, `dock_probe`): the reach the control
# appears within and a held dock parts past, the close-in engage distance, the
# low approach speed, the mate tolerance, how far undock backs clear, and the
# lowest powered rung. The dock MARKERS themselves are authored in the rig
# sidecar (`alliance_destroyer_recreated.model.toml`), not here.
[dock]
range = 200.0
engage_distance = 400.0
approach_speed = 60.0
mate_tolerance = 4.0
undock_clear_distance = 120.0
min_power_level = 2

# UMBILICAL — what the transfer moves, how fast, which way, and the lowest
# powered rung. The capacity id both docked ends must carry is `reserve_fuel`,
# the shipped resupply ledger (`alliance_tender.toml`, `umbilical_probe`);
# `direction = "deliver"` sends the operator's capacity to the docked partner,
# which is a crew pumping load INTO a depot's demand rows the way Falling
# Skyway's transfer berths are authored. `rate = 20` is the shipped flow rate.
# [ai] Unratified.
#
# This hull authors NO `[infrastructure]` ledger of its own — deliberately, for
# the reason the old operations note carried: a condition/capacity track on the
# crew's own hull would fold into every world it flies. Until #1165 gives the
# transfer an end to draw from, the flow refuses `NoCapacity` — inert in
# combat_test and patrol, where the destroyer never docks, and re-homed by the
# Falling Skyway slice that follows.
[umbilical]
capacity = "reserve_fuel"
rate = 20.0
direction = "deliver"
min_power_level = 2

# TRANSPORTER (issue #1348) — the reach a discovered rescue contact must sit
# within, how long recovering one civilian takes, and the lowest powered rung.
# `range = 500` matches the tractor's reach: a rescue is a close-in act like a
# tow. `seconds_per_civilian = 2` gives a full hold's worth of a dozen souls a
# tuneable half-minute so the crew watch the recovery advance and can be pulled
# off it by range, power or a more urgent tractor hold. [ai] Unratified.
[transporter]
range = 500.0
seconds_per_civilian = 2.0
min_power_level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/alliance_tender.toml:
# Alliance Tender (issue #1163) — an ALLIED, fully AI-crewed hull that docks with
# a stranded ship and transfers a capacity to it across the umbilical, with NO
# player involvement.
#
# ── The point of this hull (PRD #1143 / issue #1163) ──────────────────────────
#
# The NPC side of the resupply chain (issues #1159-#1160). It owns the SAME
# admission-gated `[[system]] kind = "dock"` (Helm) and `kind = "umbilical"`
# (Engineering) a crewed hull does, and runs them through the SAME backfill hosts
# — `operate_dock_ai` then `operate_umbilical_ai` (#1162) — on the shared AI
# cadence. There is NO NPC-vs-player branch: the hosts emit the byte-identical
# `Dock` / `StartTransfer` a human crew would, through `emit_ai_command`.
#
# Resupply is a chain no single seat completes: the umbilical waits on the dock
# the dock host achieves (`DockControl::docked_partner`), exactly as a human
# Engineering officer waits for Helm to call the dock made. Handing this hull one
# `Transfer` directive drives BOTH seats — Helm docks once the ordered hull is in
# range, then Engineering flows the capacity.
#
# ── How it is DIRECTED ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# World-agnostic on purpose: this template authors only a HOLD default doctrine
# (attaching a `BehaviourSection` and satisfying strict AI-declaration mode). A
# world hands it the job by OVERRIDING `behaviour.doctrine` on the spawn with a
# `Transfer` directive whose `directive_operate_target` names the stranded ship.
# See `assets/worlds/probe_npc_resupply.toml`.
#
# It carries a FULL `reserve_fuel` ledger and delivers across the umbilical, so it
# is the SOURCE; the stranded ship carries the empty receiving ledger. It is NOT a
# shipped combat hull and flies in no scenario.

includes = ["fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml", "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml"]

class = "courier"  # picker badge / scan subtitle — a light support hull
tags = ["ship", "npc"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"  # Alliance — allied to the player
# Authored mass (issue #1154).
mass = 11000.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 0.8
length = 2.0
# A flyable hull (it authors `[helm_console]`), so per the movable/helm invariant
# it must be movable. The dock manoeuvre drives the actual berthing.
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.3, 0.8, 0.9]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

[mesh]
# Shares the courier silhouette but reads its DOCK-MARKER rig from the dedicated
# `dock_probe` variant sidecar — the same markers the dock probe mates on.
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
variant = "dock_probe"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[helm_console]
max_speed = 14.0
max_reverse_speed = 5.0
impulse_speed_multiplier = 4.0
acceleration = 4.0
deceleration = 10.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.2
max_bank_deg = 8.0

[ai_profile]
aggression = 0.0
sensor_range = 800.0

# ── High-fidelity bubble ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A `LodBubble` carrier is itself ALWAYS full-fidelity. Without it, a tender
# operating far from the player would sit in the low-LOD path and never run its
# own dock/umbilical procedure. Small radius: it self-promotes the tender (and the
# stranded ship inside it).
[lod_bubble]
radius = 300.0

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# HOLD default only — a world overrides `behaviour.doctrine` with the Transfer
# order (see the header). No Destroy doctrine — a tender does not fight.
[behaviour]

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "hold-station"
directive_kind = "None"
base_priority = 5.0
target_speed  = 0.0

# ── Systems: every one ownerless + `ai_only`, so the NPC spawn path puts each
# under `ControlSource::Ai` and the #1162 hosts' `operate_ai` gate holds.

# Per-axis helm — a flyable hull.
[[system]]
id = "helm-thrust"
kind = "helm_thrust"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-steering"
kind = "helm_steering"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-impulse"
kind = "helm_impulse"
ai_only = true

# Fine power (reactor + battery).
[[system]]
id = "power-reactor"
kind = "power_reactor"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "power-battery"
kind = "power_battery"
ai_only = true

# ── The dock and umbilical systems ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Helm owns the dock, Engineering the umbilical. Both draw from the dedicated
# `ops` power bus. This hull composes `fleet_baseline.toml`, whose
# `[power.ai_policy]` manages the `helm` and `weapons` channels — so those groups
# are authored below (a `[power_groups.*]` block replaces the canonical defaults
# wholesale, so the policy's channels must be re-declared) — and `ops` is added
# beside them for the resupply systems. It rests at its seeded level 2, at or
# above each `min_power_level`.
[[system]]
id = "dock"
kind = "dock"
ai_only = true
power_group = "ops"

[[system]]
id = "umbilical"
kind = "umbilical"
ai_only = true
power_group = "ops"

# ── Power groups ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `helm` + `weapons` re-declare the canonical groups `fleet_baseline`'s power
# policy manages; `ops` is the resupply systems' own bus. All seeded at level 2.
[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.alliance_tender.power_groups.helm.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.alliance_tender.power_groups.weapons.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.ops]
label = "entity.alliance_tender.power_groups.ops.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── The transferable capacity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Starts FULL and DELIVERS across the umbilical. An inert condition track (no
# decay, no hull share) — used only as a capacity ledger, not a degrading
# structure, so damaging a system never touches the fuel.
[infrastructure]
condition_max = 100.0
decay_per_sec = 0.0
hull_damage_share = 0.0

[[infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "reserve_fuel"
amount = 100
ceiling = 100

# ── The dock terms ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[dock]
range = 200.0
engage_distance = 400.0
approach_speed = 60.0
mate_tolerance = 4.0
undock_clear_distance = 120.0
min_power_level = 2

# ── The umbilical terms (all authored — AGENTS.md rule 11) ────────────────────
# Deliver = operator → docked partner.
[umbilical]
capacity = "reserve_fuel"
rate = 20.0
direction = "deliver"
min_power_level = 2

# ── Per-system hull ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "core"
max_hp = 24
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.10

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "dock"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "umbilical"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "helm-thrust"
max_hp = 20
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.20

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "helm-steering"
max_hp = 20
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.20

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "helm-impulse"
max_hp = 20
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75

debuff_magnitude = 0.20

[[hull.system_hull]]

max_hp = 20

base_files.assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml:
# Orbital transfer depot — the first piece of authored world furniture to carry
# an [infrastructure] condition track (issue #1025).
#
# It is deliberately generic rather than Falling-Skyway-specific: a depot is
# something a scenario places, degrades, repairs and asks capacity questions of,
# and the whole point of putting condition and capacity on the ENTITY is that
# the next mission that needs one does not re-derive the bookkeeping.
#
# Two health tracks, and they are not the same thing:
#
#   [hull]           what weapons destroy. At zero the depot is despawned.
#   [infrastructure] what a storm, a decade of deferred maintenance and a repair
#                    team move. At zero the depot is still there — it just
#                    cannot do anything.
#
# `hull_damage_share = 0.5` is the coupling between them: a depot that takes a
# torpedo is structurally worse off, at half a condition point per hull point,
# without hull damage BEING condition damage.

name = "entity.depot_transfer.name"
tags = ["station", "infrastructure"]
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the structure's other stats. [ai] Unratified — a smaller
# freestanding depot, lighter than the tethered skyhook head.
mass = 180000.0

[target]
tags = ["station"]
threat_level = "none"
description = "entity.depot_transfer.target.description"

[hull]
hull_integrity = 400.0

[collider]
# Matched to the visible hull, at John's request. The recreated research outpost
# preserves the original rendered dimensions, baked into its GLB with an identity
# sidecar: 7.56 x 3.37 x 7.59 — a max half-extent of 3.80. The 10 here was
# two and a half times that: a ship "collided" with this depot while still nearly
# six units clear of anything on screen.
#
# A Cylinder, per `station_axiom.toml` — this hull is a disc too, and a flatter
# one than the starbase: 7.59 across against 3.37 tall, so a sphere at the max
# half-extent covered more than twice the height the model has. `half_height`
# is 1.68, half the sidecar's drawn 3.366.
#
# The radius is very nearly exact here, unlike the starbase's: 7.5619 across X
# and 7.5944 across Z put the two half-extents at 3.781 and 3.797, so a single
# 3.80 fits both to within two hundredths of a unit.
shape = "Cylinder"
radius = 3.8
half_height = 1.68
length = 0.0

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.72, 0.62, 0.32]
size = 10.0
icon = "station"

[mesh]
# Shares the Alliance research-outpost hull with the other stations; the torus
# is the streaming/flat-render fallback, as on station_outpost.
model = "assets/models/alliance_research_outpost_recreated.glb"
# Sized off the same measurement the collider is, and render-only the same way
# (see `station_axiom.toml` for why the stand-in is derived from the sidecar's
# extents at all, and for the `Torus` envelope arithmetic).
# `alliance_research_outpost_recreated.model.toml` records the drawn hull at
# 7.56 x 3.37 x 7.59 in its `[extents].size`, already through that sidecar's
# `[base].scale` of [4, 4, 4]:
#
#   minor = 3.37 / 2                      = 1.68   (half the measured height)
#   major = 7.59 / 2 - 1.68 = 3.80 - 1.68 = 2.12
#
# The 10.0 / 2.5 this replaces drew a 25-unit ring for a 7.6-unit depot — over
# three times too wide, and stale in exactly the way the 10-unit collider above
# was before it was corrected to 3.80.
shape = "torus"
radius = 2.12
minor_radius = 1.68
colour = [0.72, 0.62, 0.32]

[comms]
range = 900.0

[infrastructure]
# 100 condition points, intact on arrival unless a world overrides it.
condition_max = 100.0
# Half a condition point per hull point taken.
hull_damage_share = 0.5

# What a consumer asks instead of restating the number: how much this depot
# moves in one transfer window.
[[infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "depot_transfer_throughput"
amount = 40

# Below 40 % condition the transfer arm is out of tolerance and the depot stops
# being able to move anything. It comes back at 45 % — `fails_below` plus the
# default hysteresis band — so a depot hovering on the line does not flap.
[[infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "depot_transfer_capable"
fails_below = 0.4
base_files.assets/entities/dock_berth.toml:
# Dock berth — the passive dockable structure for issue #1159.
#
# A hull that can be DOCKED WITH but does not dock: it authors a `[dock]` table
# (whose presence opts it in and triggers the one spawn-time read of its rig
# sidecar for dock markers) and declares its dock markers in the `dock_probe`
# variant sidecar, but carries no `[[system]] kind = "dock"`, so it gets a
# `DockMarkers` component and no `DockControl`. Its `[dock]` terms are inert — a
# passive berth runs no manoeuvre — but present because the table is the opt-in.
# It never moves: only the docker's own ship is flown onto the mate.

tags = ["structure"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
variant = "dock_probe"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.9, 0.7, 0.2]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

# The opt-in. A passive berth runs no manoeuvre, so these numbers are inert; they
# are authored because the `[dock]` table's presence is what reads the sidecar
# for this hull's dock markers.
[dock]
range = 200.0
engage_distance = 400.0
approach_speed = 60.0
mate_tolerance = 4.0
undock_clear_distance = 120.0
min_power_level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/dock_probe.toml:
# Dock probe — the helm-docking operator for issue #1159.
#
# A deliberately lean hull that exercises ONE mechanism end to end: a helm-owned
# `[[system]] kind = "dock"`, its own `[power_groups.dock]` power group, a damage
# entry so it can be knocked out, a `[dock]` table carrying the approach terms,
# and dock markers declared in its rig sidecar (the `dock_probe` variant). It is
# NOT a shipped combat hull and is flown in no scenario — it is the fixture
# `assets/worlds/probe_dock.toml` puts a dock control on, kept out of
# `alliance_destroyer.toml` on purpose so no shipped hull's folded system-hull
# (and therefore no committed world's digest) moves for this slice. The demo
# destroyer gains docking in a later integration (#1164 S11a), not here.
#
# It flies nothing of its own: the dock manoeuvre moves the own ship onto its
# mate, so the probe needs no helm axes — the helm station exists only to OWN the
# dock system and give the Dock/Undock commands a seat to be admitted against.

tags = ["ship"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"

[mesh]
# Shares the courier silhouette but reads its DOCK-MARKER rig from the dedicated
# `dock_probe` variant sidecar — a bespoke .glb would buy the probe nothing.
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
variant = "dock_probe"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 0.6
length = 1.5
# The dock manoeuvre writes the own ship's position directly (it is the own-ship
# analogue of the tractor rig), so like the tug this stays the static-terrain
# default rather than claiming a flyable helm.
movable = false

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.2, 0.9, 0.6]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

# Power: no `[power]` block, so the reactor takes the default profile. The one
# small dock group draws well under it and rests at its nominal level.
[power_groups.dock]
label = "entity.dock_probe.power_groups.dock.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── The dock's damage entry ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# So the dock can be damaged to Disabled — the interruption the probe drives by
# knocking this system down.
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "dock"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

# ── Helm owns the dock ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[station]]
id = "helm"
name = "Helm"
description = "entity.dock_probe.station.helm.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "HLM"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

# ── The dock system ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First-class, helm-owned, power-grouped: the admitted target for Dock / Undock,
# admission-gated exactly like any other station-owned system.
[[system]]
id = "dock"
kind = "dock"
station = "helm"
power_group = "dock"

# ── The dock terms ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# All authored (AGENTS.md rule 11): the reach the control appears within and a
# forming/held dock parts past, the distance the close-in manoeuvre engages
# within, the low approach speed, the mate tolerance, how far undock backs clear,
# and the lowest power-group level the dock runs at. The dock MARKERS themselves
# are authored in the rig sidecar, not here.
[dock]
range = 200.0
engage_distance = 400.0
approach_speed = 60.0
mate_tolerance = 4.0
undock_clear_distance = 120.0
min_power_level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/ai/captain_all:
# The ALLIANCE Captain doctrine, as a reusable library fragment (issue #875).
#
# A FRAGMENT, not a hull — see the header of
# `fragments/ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml` for what that means. It lives
# outside `assets/entities/` because everything directly in that directory is
# scanned as a shipped hull.
#
# ── What this owns ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The WHOLE `[captain_console.ai]` policy block, and nothing else. That
# granularity is not a style choice: since issue #911 a keyed array extends by
# `id`, but an array with no identity — and `*.ai.rule` is one — still replaces
# wholesale, so two fragments cannot each contribute a rule to the same policy.
# One fragment owns one policy block; specialisation runs through `param`, which
# is an ordinary table and deep-merges.
#
# ── The parameter surface ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
