# * `combat_window_secs`     — how long after the last shot the alert stays up.
# * `alert_on_hostile_within` — the AGGRESSION knob. How close a faction-hostile
#   has to come before this captain opens an engagement. Raise it for a nervous
#   hull, lower it for a patient one, set it below any reachable range for a
#   captain that only ever returns fire.
#
# A hull tunes either without restating a rule:
#
#     [captain_console.ai.param]
#     alert_on_hostile_within = 220.0
#
# ── What a Harrow does instead ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Harrow hulls author the first rule and NOT the first-contact one, so they do
# not include this fragment. Their guns author `min_alert_to_fire = 0` and are
# always armed, so first contact is not their captain's decision to make — see
# the note on `BESPOKE_DOCTRINES` in `src/entities/authored_ai_pins.rs`.

# Raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within `combat_window_secs`,
# otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so a designer retunes the
# ship's nerve without recompiling.
[captain_console.ai]
param = { combat_window_secs = 10.0, alert_on_hostile_within = 150.0 }

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(secs_since_combat) < param(combat_window_secs)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

# First contact (issue #912). `secs_since_combat` starts only on damage taken,
# hostile fire taken, or own weapon fired — and since #872 an Alliance hull's
# guns hold until Red Alert — so the rule above ALONE can only ever return fire:
# a fully backfilled Alliance hull could not open an engagement at all. This rule
# is the other half. A faction-hostile inside `alert_on_hostile_within` is enough
# to call the alert, and that range is a named parameter, so a designer authors a
# nervous hull or a patient one without recompiling.
#
# `hostile_range` reads 0.0 when there is NO contact — both readings are ALWAYS
# seeded, so a guard reads "clear" rather than "absent" — which is why this guard
# pairs it with `hostile_contact`. The presence clause is load-bearing, not
# decoration.
#
# Since #875 this rule is also what drives the movement `posture` fact, and so
# the aggressive half of every class movement doctrine: `posture` is derived from
# this ship's red-alert state, and a backfilled hull whose captain never raised
# the alert would shadow at standoff for ever.
[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 5
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(hostile_contact) > 0 and fact(hostile_range) < param(alert_on_hostile_within)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/ai/captain_red:
# Reusable Captain fine-system AI policy (issue #869 composition fixture).
#
# A FRAGMENT, not a hull. It is not a valid entity on its own and is never
# parsed alone — `include_resolve` merges it into a declaring template and only
# the resolved document is validated and spawned. It lives outside
# `assets/entities/` for exactly that reason: everything directly in that
# directory is scanned as a shipped hull.
#
# What it demonstrates: a generic AI behaviour authored ONCE and shared, while
# every resolved hull still declares the policy inline as PRD #774 requires.
# Composition is an authoring-time convenience; the runtime never sees a
# fragment.
#
# Deliberately unconditional (`when = "true"`), so a hull that composes it is
# observably driven by THIS policy rather than by the Rust-side synthesised
# default, which stands down without combat facts.

[captain_console]

[captain_console.ai]

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/ai/fleet_basel:
# The fleet-baseline AI declarations, as a reusable fragment (issue #885b
# stage 5d).
#
# Every AI-capable fine system must declare a policy or an explicit idle state
# (PRD #774 US7), and since stage 5d strict AI-declaration mode makes omitting
# one a LOAD ERROR — there is no Rust-side synthesiser left to fill the gap.
# This fragment carries the fifteen ship-level declarations a small NPC hull
# owes but has no reason to specialise — TEN AI policies (the six helm axes,
# Shields, Power, Comms, and the weapons doctrine issue #956 added) and the FIVE
# target selectors — transcribed verbatim from `alliance_battleship.toml`. That
# is the count every other comment in the tree quotes; it is the number of
# `[…_ai]` / `[….ai_policy]` / `[….selector]` blocks in this file and nothing
# else.
#
# Deliberately does NOT carry `[captain_console.ai]`: the composition fixture
# gets that from `ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml`, whose whole point is
# that a hull can take one declaration from one fragment and the rest from
# another. Nor the per-weapon ones — a hull without weapons owes none, and a
# hull with them owes one per bank and tube.
#
# ── Promoted from fixture to SHIPPED library spine (issue #875) ──────────────
#
# This was a #869/#885b mechanism fixture. It is now the ship-level spine of the
# backfill fragment library. `assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml` — the
# first composed shipped hull — takes TWELVE of those fifteen from here: all
# but the three travel axes, which `ai/movement_attack_pass.toml` replaces
# wholesale (see the contract below).
#
# Issue #876 added the other two player hulls. `alliance_battleship.toml` takes
# twelve — all but Engines, Steering and Impulse, which
# `ai/movement_artillery.toml` replaces — and `alliance_cruiser.toml` takes all
# FIFTEEN, because it composes no class movement fragment at all (see the note
# on `includes` in that hull). Nothing about the file changed; what changed is
# that three shipped hulls now depend on it, so a retune here retunes all three.
# #878 moves the rest of the fleet onto it.
#
# ── The three travel axes below are REPLACEABLE, and the contract for it ─────
#
# `engines_ai`, `steering_ai` and `boost_ai` are the fleet's stateless defaults:
# actuate on every axis, and take no AI boost action at all. A hull with a class
# movement doctrine — see `ai/movement_attack_pass.toml` and
# `ai/movement_artillery.toml` — includes this file and then a movement fragment
# that REPLACES the axes it supplies a machine for, which it must do explicitly:
#
#   * `rule = []` on Engines and Steering, because a policy carrying both
#     top-level rules and states is rejected at load. EVERY movement fragment
#     owes these two: a class doctrine is a machine on both travel axes or it is
#     not a class doctrine.
#   * `idle = false` on Boost, but ONLY from a fragment that supplies a boost
#     machine, because `idle` is mutually exclusive with `state` and deep-merges
#     as a plain scalar — a fragment with boost states that forgot this line
#     would compose into a hull that validates, spawns, and never boosts. A
#     doctrine with no boost leg — a gun line, say, where lighting a drive
#     abandons the firing position — says so by leaving this block alone, and
#     the hull keeps a Boost policy that honestly declares it takes no AI boost
#     action.
#
# `impulse_ai` is on the same footing as Boost, from the other direction:
# `ai/movement_artillery.toml` REPLACES it with an explicit idle (`idle = true`
# AND `rule = []`, because the inherited permit below would otherwise be the same
# rejected contradiction), since an artillery hold band sits inside the impulse
# drive's cruise window and an engaged drive overrides commanded throttle.
#
# The rest of this file — the selectors, Shields, Power, Comms and the remaining
# secondary helm axes — is not specialised by any class doctrine, which is why
# they sit here rather than in the movement fragments.
#
# Still deliberately no `[power]`-less split: the reactor block below exists so
# `[power.ai_policy]` has a table to sit in, and a hull that authors its own
# reactor overrides it whole (the includer wins).

[helm_console.engines_ai]

[[helm_console.engines_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "longitudinal"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

# Helm yaw — the mirror of `engines_ai` on the facing axis: always actuate the
# planner's desired facing.
#
# STATELESS, and therefore always yielding to a channel-3 `ArcBearingRequest`
# (issue #918): a hull flying this baseline has no doctrine leg and so no chosen
# heading to defend, and it turns to bring a weapon family that cannot bear onto
# its target exactly as it has since #673-#684. Declining is a property of an
# authored LEG — `yields_to_arc_requests = false` on a `[[...state]]` — so it is
# a class movement fragment's decision to make, never the baseline's.

[helm_console.steering_ai]

[[helm_console.steering_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "yaw"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

# Helm lateral — always actuate. The dodge (and the docking translation) run off
# the shared hazard surface, so again only the decision is authored here.

[helm_console.lateral_ai]

[[helm_console.lateral_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "lateral"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_lateral_thrust"

# Helm vertical — always actuate. `VerticalMovementMode` stays a host-side
# CAPABILITY gate rather than a policy scalar, so a Planar hull still takes no
# vertical component no matter what this rule says.

[helm_console.vertical_ai]

[[helm_console.vertical_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "vertical"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_vertical_thrust"

# Helm impulse — always PERMIT the manoeuvre. The engage-vs-cancel decision is
# still made host-side from the doctrine's `use_impulse` fact and the
# `decide_impulse` geometry; this rule is the authored gate layered over it, and
# `ship_harrow_warhawk.toml` is the worked example of closing it.

[helm_console.impulse_ai]

[[helm_console.impulse_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "impulse"
when = "true"
verb = "engage_impulse"

# Helm boost — an explicit IDLE declaration, and the only one in the set. No AI
# on this hull engages the boost drive, so the honest declaration is "takes no
# AI boost action" rather than a rule that never fires. `idle = true` is a legal
# declaration distinct from silence; an empty block is rejected at load. A hull
# opts in by replacing this with a rule on the `boost` channel —
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml` is the worked example.

[helm_console.boost_ai]
idle = true

# Torpedo magazine — always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The
# offline + non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this policy is the
# authored arbiter layered on top, which is where a hull would ration rounds
# between tubes.

[shields_console.ai_policy.param]
damage_window_secs = 4.0
min_damage_window_secs = 1.0
damage_pct_threshold = 50.0
health_ratio_threshold = 50.0

[[shields_console.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "shield_focus"
when = "fact(recent_damage_pct_max) >= param(damage_pct_threshold)"
verb = "focus_shield_arc"

[[shields_console.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "shield_focus"
when = "true"
verb = "focus_shield_arc"

# Comms dialogue response — answer an open hail with its FIRST response. Guarded
# twice, and both guards matter: an unguarded rule would re-emit a response the
# router refuses, every tick, for as long as the dialogue stays open.
#   * `comms_available` — a Disabled or Destroyed Comms system stops the ship
#     answering as well as hailing.
#   * `sender_in_range` — the router refuses a response whose sender has left
#     comms range, so without this the officer's rejection re-flashes forever.
# WHICH message is being answered comes from the host; only the response INDEX
# rides the verb. A ship that should answer nothing declares `idle = true`.

# The reactor itself, so `[power.ai_policy]` has a `[power]` table to sit in —
# `capacity` / `rates` / `emergency_threshold` have no parse-time defaults.
[power]
capacity = 90
rates = [ 5, 4, 3, 2, -2, -5 ]
emergency_threshold = 22

# ── The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003) ──────────────────────────────
#
# The four `min_*` numbers below are not four unrelated brownout guards; read
# together with the six rules that follow they are ONE staircase, and the
# staircase is what keeps a red-alert fight off the reactor's exhaustion lock.
# Each channel authors three rules — HOLD (priority 15), ELEVATE (10) and the
# BASELINE (0) — and when neither of the first two fires that channel falls to
# its baseline at level 2. That fallback IS the shed: the policy authors no
# demote rule and needs none.
#
# Each channel has TWO battery numbers, not one, and the gap between them is the
# point:
#
#   min_reserve_*  the SHED floor. Below it the channel gives its point back.
#   min_restore_*  the RESTORE floor, always the higher of the two. A channel
#                  that has already shed may not rise again until the charge is
#                  back up here.
#
# A single threshold per channel would be both the shed floor and the
# re-elevate floor, and the AI would then flip that channel every tick the
# charge sat on it: shed at the floor drops the total, the lower total recharges
# the battery back over the floor within one tick (a destroyer moves ±0.095
# battery-percent per 30 Hz tick), the channel re-elevates, the higher total
# drains it back under. That is a `SetPowerGroupAllocation`, a Power log line
# and a ×1.25/×1.0 modifier swing at TICK RATE. The gap makes the traversal ten
# battery-percent wide instead — seconds, and visible as a decision rather than
# as a strobe. `fact(power_<group>)` (the channel's CURRENT level, seeded by
# `ship::power::seed_power_facts`) is what the HOLD rule reads to know which
# side of the gap it is on, so the hysteresis needs no policy state.
#
# THE THRUST AXIS NEEDS THE SAME PAIR, and for the same reason. Helm's trigger
# is not a latch like the alert — `thrust` is a CONTINUOUS value, and
# `plan_helm_travel` hands out analogue throttles: the decel ramps in
# `helm_destroy` / `helm_navigate_to` sweep smoothly through the whole range,
# and avoidance steering dithers whatever they produce. A single
# `thrust_threshold` read by BOTH the HOLD and the ELEVATE is therefore the
# same strobe the battery pair exists to prevent, one axis over — and unlike
# the battery it has no ratchet to fall back on, because above the restore
# floor the ELEVATE is satisfiable again on the very next arm. A hull whose
# throttle DWELLS near the threshold flips helm 3<->2 on consecutive AI
# decision arms, i.e. at 30 Hz, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 `MaxSpeed` swing. That
# is a ship visibly thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn.
#
# So helm gets a pair here too:
#
#   thrust_threshold          the ELEVATE floor. Reached from below.
#   thrust_release_threshold  the RELEASE floor, always the LOWER of the two. A
#                             channel already up holds until the throttle falls
#                             past this, not merely past the elevate floor.
#
# Measured, not reasoned: before this pair, `rng_coverage`'s lancer_alpha flipped
# helm 18 times in a 1800-tick run — sixteen of them inside 38 ticks, throttle
# dithering across 0.70 (0.677 .. 0.750) with the battery at 57-59, nowhere near
# its 50 shed floor. This was dormant until `5672b09a` seeded the `thrust` fact
# from the real throttle: before it the fact read 0.0 on every NPC, so the rule
# never fired and helm was pinned at 2 for the whole fleet.
#
# The ALERT half of the trigger keeps the old treatment and needs no band: it is
# a boolean that already hysteresises upstream (`combat_window_secs`), so one
# tick with it false sheds to baseline and the battery ratchet then holds the
# channel down until the reserve is back over the restore floor. Elevated
# posture belongs to combat stations, not to an alert that blinked.
#
# There is likewise no ship-wide "total" rule anywhere in this file. The total
# is EMERGENT from the per-channel bids (`shields` never bids at all, so
# `plan_allocation` reserves it at its commanded 2). At combat stations under
# thrust — BOTH elevate guards' non-battery halves true, which for helm means
# red alert AND `thrust >= thrust_threshold` — a falling battery walks:
#
#   battery_pct        helm  weapons  shields  total   what the reactor does
#   >= 50               3       3        2       8     steepest authored drain
#   25 ..< 50           2       3        2       7     slow drain
#   < 25                2       2        2       6     RECHARGES (positive rate)
#
# and a RISING battery walks the same steps at 35 (weapons) and 60 (helm).
# Away from combat stations the ship simply rests at total 6.
#
# Below 25 the reserve refills, weapons re-elevates once it is back over 35, and
# the charge oscillates across that 25–35 band — a long way above 0. 0 is the
# number that matters: `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to
# `GROUP_LEVEL_MIN` and LOCKS the reactor the instant the charge reaches it, and
# nothing unlocks it until the charge climbs back to `emergency_threshold`
# above. A ship WITH A WORKING REACTOR must not be able to fight its way into
# that on its own AI's decisions, and with this ladder it cannot: the
# sustainable total is reached while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand.
#
# The floors are AI-SHED ONLY, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight
# in the human/AI command symmetry (AGENTS.md rule #6). The symmetry lives at
# the admitted-command seam — both sides emit the same
# `SetPowerGroupAllocation` and both are applied by the same
# `ship::power::handle_power_messages` — and these guards live upstream of it,
# in the AI's bid stage. `handle_power_messages` never reads `battery_pct`, so a
# human Power officer who wants weapons at 3 on a flat battery gets weapons at 3
# and the consequences that follow.
#
# One case the ladder does NOT cover, deliberately: a Disabled or Destroyed
# power reactor. `ControlSourceResolver::policy_for` rates an offline system
# `operate_ai = false`, so `ai_power_allocation` skips the ship entirely while
# the reactor's own integration carries on at whatever total was last
# commanded. A hull knocked out at total 8 therefore flattens its battery and
# locks, and no shed floor can prevent it — that is a damage outcome for the
# repair seam to answer, not a tuning question for this staircase.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair (see the note above), the mirror of the battery pair one
# axis over: elevate at 0.7, release at 0.6. [ai] The RATIFIABLE QUANTITY IS THE
# BAND WIDTH (0.1 here), not either endpoint — it has to be wider than the
# throttle's own dither around a doctrine speed and narrower than the gap
# between two authored `target_speed`s, so that a real change of travel
# intention still moves the channel. 0.7/0.6 clears the measured dither (±0.04)
# with room and still separates the fleet's 0.8 Destroy from its 0.5/0.6 cruise.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's pair. The shed at half a battery is the first point the ship gives
# back; the restore ten points higher is what stops the two decisions chattering
# into each other.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair, and the lower step of the ladder. 25 sheds to the sustainable
# total while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand — on the destroyer's
# 70-point battery that is a comfortable margin, where the 10 this shipped with
# before issue #1003 left barely three seconds of it.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm: elevate to 3 under sustained thrust with a healthy battery, AT RED
# ALERT, else hold 2.
#
# The `red_alert` guard is load-bearing, not decoration. `plan_helm_travel`
# commands near-max throttle for any ordinary transit — Patrol travel and a
# Destroy directive's `target_speed` (default 0.8) both clear
# `thrust_threshold` — so without this guard a cruising, non-combat ship holds
# helm at 3 essentially the whole time it is under way, resting the ship-wide
# total at 7 rather than the sustainable 6 the budget note above assumes.
# Three of the four Alliance reactors' `rates` are negative at total 7 (see
# each hull's own `[power] rates`), so that reads as the battery browning out
# continuously while the ship is simply flying somewhere, with no combat
# involved at all. Gating on red alert confines the elevation to the "combat
# stations" burst the budget note actually measured (`probe_duel` runs fight
# with the alert up), leaving ordinary cruise at the sustainable resting total.
#
# Helm is the UPPER step of the shed ladder (see the param note): the first
# point the ship gives back, at half a battery, because a combat manoeuvre is
# the cheaper thing to lose and dropping to total 7 slows the drain enough to
# make the second step's timing comfortable. It comes back at 60, not at 50.
#
# HOLD, at the higher priority: helm is ALREADY at 3 (`fact(power_helm)`, the
# level seeded from the reactor's current allocation) and the charge is still
# above the shed floor, so keep it. Same trigger clauses as the elevate below,
# except that the throttle is read against the RELEASE floor rather than the
# elevate one — a hold is not a licence to ignore the alert or the throttle, but
# it is the wider half of the thrust band (see the note at the top of this
# block, and the battery pair it mirrors).
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

# ELEVATE: the RISING edge, at the restore floor. Reached only from below (the
# hold above wins whenever helm is already up), so this is the rule that decides
# how much charge the ship insists on having before it spends again.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons: elevate to 3 on red alert with a healthy battery, else hold 2. Level
# 3 is ×1.25 on `ModifierSlot::PhaserDamage` — the beam hurts more, it does not
# carry further (#955). This is the point #923 spent on `sensors`; it is back.
#
# Weapons is the LOWER step of the shed ladder (see the param note): the last
# elevation the ship gives up, because giving it up drops the total to the
# sustainable 6 and turns the battery around. Losing it costs damage output, not
# the ability to shoot — the fire gate is red alert, which these rules read but
# do not own.
#
# HOLD, at the higher priority: weapons is already at 3 and the charge is still
# above the shed floor. This is the rung the battery actually oscillates on, so
# it is the one the hysteresis earns its keep on.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

# ELEVATE: the RISING edge, at the restore floor — ten points of charge above
# the shed, which at the total-6 recharge rate is seconds of recovery rather
# than one tick's worth.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

[comms_console.ai]

# THE FALLBACK, and only the fallback, since #1343. Answering by INDEX is the
# right thing for a hail acknowledgement and the wrong thing for a decision:
# the option a person reaches for while they think goes first, so a rule that
# always picks index 0 stands by for ever on a conversation that was asking for
# an answer. A node whose responses author `ai_weight` is therefore decided by
# the weighted picker instead (`comms::ai_choice`) and never reaches this rule;
# a node that authors none — which is every conversation but Falling Skyway's
# lift band — keeps exactly the behaviour it has always had.
#
# This block still has to be here for BOTH mechanisms: strict AI declaration
# (#885) means a fine system with no `[comms_console.ai]` at all takes no action
# of any kind, weighted or otherwise.
[[comms_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "comms_respond"
when = "fact(comms_available) > 0 and fact(sender_in_range) > 0"
verb = "respond_to_message"
response_index = 0

[sensors_console.selector]
sources = ["combat-lock", "objective-destroy", "radar-contacts", "debris-assessment"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
# The `source_debris_assess` disjunct (issue #1347) is what lets a NON-hostile
# contact reach this seat at all. Everything else here is something the ship
# means to shoot, and is gated on `hostile`; a rock has no faction and no
# opinion, so that test refuses it. The honest reason it is eligible is not that
# it is an enemy but that it is a thing this instrument can still learn something
# about, and the marker says exactly that.
eligibility = "candidate_fact(detectable) > 0 and (candidate_fact(hostile) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_debris_assess) > 0)"

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_combat_lock) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0"
weight = 100.0

# ── WORKING DOWN A DEBRIS FIELD (issue #1347) ────────────────────────────────
#
# The mission's own ladder is "objective-critical scans, then possible
# collisions, then keep assessing", and these three terms are the last two rungs
# of it. A hazard outranks an incidental radar hostile (1) — a rock about to
# land on a depot is worth more of this seat's attention than the nearest
# unfriendly ship — but never a named objective (100), which is the mission
# telling the crew what matters more.
#
# The `debris_unassessed` bonus is the part that makes the seat WORK: an unread
# rock scores 40, a rock already read scores 10, so the instrument goes to the
# next unknown rather than admiring the one it just finished. Once a contact's
# authored `reassess_secs` elapses it re-enters the top tier by itself and the
# plot Tactical is prioritising on gets refreshed.
#
# `debris_confirmed` adds a little back to a rock already known to be on course,
# so between two contacts both wanting a re-read the seat refreshes the one that
# is actually going to hit something first. It is small on purpose: it must not
# add up past an unread contact, because an unknown rock is a worse thing to
# have than a known one. 10 + 15 = 25 < 40.
[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_debris_assess) > 0"
weight = 10.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_unassessed) > 0"
weight = 30.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_confirmed) > 0"
weight = 15.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_radar) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# ── The WEAPONS DOCTRINE: which gun the ship turns to present (issue #956) ────
#
# Weapons asks Helm to turn — a channel-3 `ArcBearingRequest` — when the target
# is in reach of a weapon family but outside every one of that family's arcs.
# Exactly one such request may be active, so *which* family is worth turning for
# has to be decided, and until #956 that decision was a Rust array in
# `tick_weapons_arc_request`: `[Phasers, Blasters, Torpedoes]`, with a doc
# comment calling it "structural, not a gameplay value". It is nothing of the
# kind. Which gun a ship manoeuvres to present is the shape of the fight it
# intends to have, and a fleet that always turns for its beams can never fly a
# doctrine built on fixed bow tubes.
#
# The CHANNEL is the rank and the VERB is the family. Three ranks, each an
# ordinary channel decision with its own guards, so a hull can reorder itself
# mid-engagement; the host resolves them in order, drops repeats, and walks the
# result until a family actually qualifies. A rank nobody authors simply
# shortens the order — there is no Rust default behind it.
#
# This block is the FLEET BASELINE and it is deliberately unconditional: beams
# first, then blasters, then tubes — byte for byte the behaviour the deleted
# array gave, so nothing about how the fleet flies changed on the day the
# decision became content. A hull that wants something else says so on top of
# it; `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` is the worked example, and it is the issue's
# own: it leads with its tubes while the target's striking arc is down.
#
# Note what the ranks do NOT decide: whether a family is capable at all. Its
# emitters' arcs, ranges, ammunition and online state are host readings taken
# after this order comes back, because a policy that could contradict the
# geometry would ask Helm to turn for a gun that is not there.

[weapons_console.ai]

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_first"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_phasers_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_second"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_blasters_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_third"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_torpedoes_to_bear"

# Tactical — the ship's firing target. `combat-lock` is deliberately ABSENT from
# the sources: it is Tactical's own output, so unioning it would be circular.
# The current lock reaches the ranking as the host-pushed `source_retained`
# retention candidate, which is why that marker appears in the guards but in no
# source list.
#
# PRECEDENCE INVARIANT — terms are additive and one candidate can carry several
# markers at once, so the weights are sized to beat the maximum non-objective
# stack by more than `switch_margin`. Two stacks have to clear that bar, because
# no candidate can carry both sets of markers:
#
#   a warship   500 + 200 + 100 +   1                     = 801 < 1000 - 50
#   a rock      500 + 200 + 120 + (60 + 60)               = 940 < 1000 - 50
#
# A named Destroy objective therefore always wins AND survives hysteresis
# retention, while `retained` still exceeds `last_attacker` so an established
# engagement is not broken off by a fresh attacker. Retune against those two
# inequalities, not term by term.
#
# The second stack is debris (issue #1347) and it is a SEPARATE line because a
# rock cannot carry the warship markers: it has no faction, so `source_radar`
# (nearest faction-hostile) never fires on it, and it does not shoot, so
# `source_last_attacker` never fires either. What it can carry is a Sensors
# designation and the retained lock, which is why those two appear in both sums.

[weapons_console.selector]
sources = ["sensors-designation", "objective-destroy", "last-attacker", "radar-contacts", "objective-operate", "confirmed-debris-threat"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 50.0
# The two urgency bands below are read against these, in seconds of dead-reckoned
# time-to-impact. They are doctrine, not physics: how much room THIS fleet thinks
# it needs to solve a firing problem on a drifting mass. Widen them and Tactical
# commits to rocks earlier; narrow them and it holds its lock on the warship
# longer. An inline table rather than a `[weapons_console.selector.param]`
# header, because a sub-table opened here would swallow every sibling key below
# it — `eligibility` included — and the selector would parse as paramless.
#
# [ai] Both numbers are unratified.
param = { debris_pressing_secs = 60.0, debris_urgent_secs = 25.0 }
# Independent revalidation: `detectable` is required of everything, and beyond
# that a candidate is engageable either because the host already vetted it
# (objective order / last attacker / retained lock) OR because it is
# independently hostile. That disjunction honours a mission naming a factionless
# target while refusing a FRIENDLY Sensors designation, which carries only
# `source_sensors_designation`.
#
# The final `source_operate` disjunct (issue #1162) is DIRECTIVE-GATED: the
# `objective-operate` source injects a candidate ONLY when an active per-verb
# operate directive (Tow/Stabilise/Escort/FieldRepair) names that target, so the
# tractor and external-repair dispatch can reach a NON-hostile lock the ship was
# ordered to work. The term is inert when no operate directive is active — no
# candidate carries `source_operate` — so combat auto-lock is unchanged and
# radar/scan auto-lock stays hostile-gated (`source_radar` still requires
# `hostile`, unaffected here).
#
# The `source_debris_threat` disjunct (issue #1347) is ASSESSMENT-GATED at the
# host: that marker is only ever attached to a contact whose threat state a scan
# taken through the ordinary lifecycle actually raised. So a rock nobody has read
# fails this guard at any distance and on any course, and Backfill cannot open
# fire on something the crew were never told about. A human Tactical is
# untouched — this selector does not run at all while the seat is crewed.
eligibility = "candidate_fact(detectable) > 0 and (candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_last_attacker) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_retained) > 0 or candidate_fact(hostile) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_operate) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_debris_threat) > 0)"

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_sensors_designation) > 0"
weight = 500.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_retained) > 0"
weight = 200.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_last_attacker) > 0"
weight = 100.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_radar) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# An active operate order (issue #1162) is an explicit command decision, the
# same tier as a named Destroy objective, so it carries the same 1000 weight:
# the target the crew were ordered to tow / stabilise / field-repair wins the
# lock over any incidental radar contact. It never stacks with `source_objective`
# in practice (one names a hostile to destroy, the other a non-hostile to
# operate on), so the precedence invariant above is unchanged.
[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_operate) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

# ── CONFIRMED DEBRIS, RANKED BY DEADLINE (issue #1347) ───────────────────────
#
# Three additive terms, and the split is the doctrine. The FIRST says a confirmed
# rock outranks the ordinary fight: 120 beats `last_attacker` (100) and any
# incidental radar hostile (1), which is the mission's own priority ladder —
# confirmed threats to a protected asset first, then threats to the ship, then
# ordinary hostiles. It does NOT beat a named Destroy objective, so a mission
# that has ordered a specific kill keeps it.
#
# The other two rank several confirmed rocks AGAINST EACH OTHER, which is the
# part that actually matters once the corridor comes down: with three contacts
# eligible at once, the one arriving soonest carries both bands and wins by 120,
# far outside the 50-point hysteresis margin, so Tactical works the queue
# earliest-deadline-first instead of holding whichever rock it happened to see
# first. The bands stack deliberately — inside `debris_urgent_secs` is also
# inside `debris_pressing_secs`.
#
# `impact_secs` is the CREW's number: dead-reckoned forward from the last
# assessment Sensors actually took, not the simulation's private truth. A stale
# assessment therefore produces a stale priority, which is what makes going back
# and re-reading a rock worth a seat's time.
#
# Both bands are additionally guarded on `debris_deadline_known`, and that guard
# is load-bearing rather than decorative. An absent fact reads as 0, and 0 is a
# real reading here — "arriving now" — so the two cases have to be told apart by
# something other than the number. A contact CONFIRMED earlier and since shoved
# off course keeps its confirmation (that is a thing that happened) but has no
# arrival any more, and without this guard its missing deadline would read as
# zero seconds and rank it above every rock that really is about to land.
[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_debris_threat) > 0"
weight = 120.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_deadline_known) > 0 and candidate_fact(impact_secs) < param(debris_pressing_secs)"
weight = 60.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_deadline_known) > 0 and candidate_fact(impact_secs) < param(debris_urgent_secs)"
weight = 60.0

# Navigation — rank destinations into the shared Waypoint. Only the objective
# source marks its resolved destination `reachable`, so this policy drives the
# AI waypoint from objectives alone; `chart-contacts` is surfaced so an author
# can widen the eligibility, and by default only ENRICHES a coincident objective
# destination rather than independently steering the ship.

[navigation_console.selector]
sources = ["navigation-objectives", "chart-contacts"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(reachable) > 0"

[[navigation_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_nav_objective) > 0"
weight = 100.0

[[navigation_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_chart_contact) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# Repair — rank this ship's damaged stations for the next free team. Two
# additive ladders whose tier rungs STRICTLY dominate the deficit rungs
# (3 x 100 = 300 < 1000), reproducing the retired `(tier desc, deficit desc)`
# comparator. `assigned < 1` is what makes N free teams pick N DISTINCT
# stations. `tier_ordinal` is the DamageTier discriminant (Operational 0,
# Damaged 1, Disabled 2, Destroyed 3) — a structural enum ordinal, which is why
# its lower bound is a literal rather than a param. The Destroyed rung (3) is
# REACHABLE: since issue #1013 an on-site team repairs a destroyed system like
# any other — `SystemHull::restore` has no tier gate and the first restored HP
# un-latches it — so a destroyed station is real repair work and the eligibility
# must not refuse it. The only tier excluded is Operational (0), which has
# nothing to repair.
#
# Authored on every hull whether or not it crews repair teams: the teams gate
# dispatch, so a ship that gains them later already has its ranking.

[repair.selector]
sources = ["damaged-stations", "core-bucket"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(source_repair_request) > 0 and candidate_fact(assigned) < 1 and candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) > 0"

# The bands sit INSIDE the urgent range and deliberately NOT at the DamageTier
# thresholds — because tier strictly dominates, the deficit ladder only ever
# discriminates within one tier, so bands at the tier boundaries would all fire
# together for every Disabled station and discriminate nothing.
[repair.selector.param]
deficit_band_low = 0.80
deficit_band_mid = 0.90
deficit_band_high = 0.95

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 1"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 2"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 3"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_low)"
weight = 100.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_mid)"
weight = 100.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_high)"
weight = 100.0

# Comms hail — rank who to hail. The most gated of the five, and the only one
# whose eligibility reads a `self_fact`: `comms_available`, so a Disabled or
# Destroyed Comms system stops the ship hailing at all. `source_hail_objective`
# keeps the baseline — only targets an active Hail directive actually names are
# ranked. `has_open_hail_thread < 1` is the anti-respam gate and it TERMINATES:
# a hail arms it even when it fires no `on_hailed` template, and it re-arms on a
# human `ClearComms` or on the target ceasing to be a live candidate, which is
# what an unmanned ship relies on. `switch_margin` is 0 and the host passes no
# current target: a hail is a ONE-SHOT event, so there is nothing to retain.

[comms_console.selector]
sources = ["hail-objectives", "comms-contacts"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(source_hail_objective) > 0 and candidate_fact(in_range) > 0 and candidate_fact(objective_score) > 0 and candidate_fact(has_open_hail_thread) < 1 and self_fact(comms_available) > 0"

# The bands straddle the `base_priority` values the shipped content actually
# authors (20 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 80 / 100), splitting them four ways.
# Bands outside that range would fire for all or none and collapse the ranking
# onto the smallest-UUID tie-break.
[comms_console.selector.param]
score_band_low = 25.0
score_band_mid = 45.0
score_band_high = 75.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_low)"
weight = 100.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_mid)"
weight = 100.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_high)"
weight = 100.0

# ── AI fine-system policies (PRD #774 US7, issue #885b) ───────────────────────
#
# The ship-level AI policies, AUTHORED rather than synthesised. Each answers
# "which verb does this fine system emit on which channel?" for whoever operates
# the station, and each reproduces exactly what the matching
# `default_*_ai_config()` in `src/entities/config.rs` used to invent at spawn.
# The reasoning behind every rule lives on those functions;
# `default_ai_policy_pins` spawns every shipped hull and compares the two, so a
# transcription slip fails the build rather than quietly changing how this ship
# behaves.
#
# Like the selectors above, these attach on `[behaviour]` ALONE, not on the
# console section they name — so a hull owes them whether or not it declares
# `[captain_console]`, `[shields_console]` or `[power]`. Authoring them is what
# brings those sections into existence on hulls that carried none.
#
# A rule's `when` is a guard, not a capability check: the host keeps every
# availability, cooldown, range and arc gate it had. `idle = true` (see Boost) is
# a first-class declaration meaning "this system deliberately takes no AI
# action" — it is NOT the same as an empty block, which validation rejects.

# Captain — raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within
# `combat_window_secs`, otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so
# a designer retunes the ship's nerve without recompiling.
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/ai/movement_ar:
# The ARTILLERY class movement doctrine, as a reusable library fragment
# (issue #876).
#
# A FRAGMENT, not a hull — see the header of
# `fragments/ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml`. It is never parsed alone;
# `include_resolve` merges it into a declaring template and only the resolved
# document is validated and spawned.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What a hull writes to use this
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
#     includes = [
#       "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
#       "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml",
#       "fragments/ai/movement_artillery.toml",
#     ]
#
#     [helm_console.steering_ai.param]
#     max_artillery_range = 50.0
#     artillery_hold_range = 45.0
#
# …and nothing else. Order matters: this fragment REPLACES the fleet baseline's
# two travel axes and its Impulse policy, so it must be listed after it (a
# template's includes merge in declared order, and the declaring template itself
# merges last).
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What this owns, and what it deliberately leaves alone
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# The WHOLE of `[helm_console.engines_ai]` and `[helm_console.steering_ai]` —
# two independent copies of ONE machine, which agree by reading the same
# host-seeded facts rather than by sharing state. They ship together because a
# copy that disagreed with the other about a threshold would reach a different
# leg on the same tick, which is a silent failure with no test that could name
# it.
#
# …and the WHOLE of `[helm_console.impulse_ai]`, as an explicit IDLE. That is not
# a hull's quirk smuggled into a shared file, it is the doctrine: an artillery
# platform that lights an engine is leaving the firing position it just took up.
# It is also load-bearing rather than decorative — see the next section.
#
# NOT `[helm_console.boost_ai]`. No leg of a gun line engages the drive either,
# so the fleet baseline's `idle = true` is exactly the right declaration and this
# fragment leaves it standing. `movement_attack_pass.toml` owes `idle = false`
# because it SUPPLIES a boost machine; a movement fragment that supplies none
# owes nothing.
#
# One fragment owns entire policy blocks because since #911 an array with no
# stable identity — and `*.ai.rule` and `*_ai.state[].transition` are both — still
# REPLACES wholesale on compose. Two fragments cannot each contribute a rule to
# the same policy; the second would wipe the first. Specialisation therefore runs
# entirely through `param`, an ordinary table that deep-merges.
#
# `rule = []` appears three times, on Engines, on Steering and on Impulse, and it
# is load-bearing on all three. On the two travel axes it clears the rules
# `fleet_baseline.toml` authors, because a policy carrying BOTH top-level rules
# and states is rejected at load (`validate_fine_system_ai_policy`). On Impulse it
# clears the baseline's unconditional permit, because `idle` deep-merges as a
# plain scalar and an idle declaration carrying an inherited rule is the same
# rejected contradiction from the other side.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Why the impulse drive has to be switched off HERE
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# `entities::spawner` attaches an `ImpulseConfigResource` to every hull that
# declares a `[helm_console]`, taking the parse defaults — engage at 200 units,
# cancel at 40. An artillery hold band lives inside that window on every hull
# small enough to want one, so without this idle the hull would fly its run-in,
# engage impulse somewhere around 200 with its bow lined up, reach the hold range
# and command `SetThrust{0.0}` every tick — and be ignored, because the impulse
# autopilot in `integrate_ship_physics` hard-OVERRIDES commanded throttle with
# `thrust = 1.0` for as long as the drive is engaged. The hull sails through its
# own gun line at max speed and stops at the drive's own release range, and the
# authored `max_yaw_rate` goes with it, since the same autopilot scales steering
# by the impulse multiplier. That is issue #792's finding on
# `ship_harrow_warhawk.toml`, the hand-authored ancestor of this fragment.
#
# ## Why an `impulse_ai` idle and not `use_impulse = false`
#
# `[[behaviour.doctrine]] use_impulse = false` reads like the obvious lever and is
# the wrong one, because doctrine is the part of a hull a SCENARIO replaces.
# Shipped worlds hand hulls a doctrine list of their own and do not author
# `use_impulse`, and `effective_use_impulse()` defaults to TRUE for every
# non-Patrol directive — so each of them would silently switch the drive back on
# in exactly the scenarios the hull is fought in. A tightened
# `impulse_engage_distance` has the same shape of problem from the other end: it
# is a geometry that has to stay correct against a band a designer retunes.
#
# The `impulse` fine system's own policy is not doctrine and no shipped scenario
# overrides it. An explicit `idle` is a legal, distinct-from-silence declaration:
# `ai_helm_impulse` resolves the channel to nothing and emits neither
# `StartImpulseCharge` nor `CancelImpulse`, whatever geometry or doctrine it is
# handed.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The doctrine
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# A gun line with a posture gate over it.
#
#   shadow     → the DEFENSIVE resting leg. HOLDS POSITION AT RANGE: a wide,
#                slow ring around the target at
#                `target_direct_fire_range + safe_range_margin`, outside the
#                other ship's guns by an authored margin, and it never closes.
#                This is where a hull sits whenever its captain has not called
#                red alert.
#   acquire    → a target has appeared. Decides in one tick whether it is already
#                inside the band or has to be closed on.
#   reposition → the run-in. Tracks the target and lets ordinary doctrine travel
#                carry the hull in (this fragment authors no pass throttles, so
#                the planner's fallback pass arm is not published at all). The bow
#                is on the TARGET rather than on a lead solution, which is
#                correct: nothing is being fired at this range, and a run-in aimed
#                at an intercept would arrive off to one side of it.
#   hold       → THE PREDICTIVE FIRING POSITION, and what the posture gate buys.
#                Translational station on the authored `artillery_hold_speed`
#                while the bow pivots onto where the target WILL BE when this
#                hull's own bolt arrives — not where it is now.
#
# ── The band, and why it is two numbers ──────────────────────────────────────
#
# `artillery_hold_range` is the INNER edge: the run-in ends there and the firing
# position is taken. `max_artillery_range` is the OUTER edge: the hold ends there
# and the hull repositions. The gap between them is the hysteresis — one threshold
# would have the hull chattering between closing and holding every time the target
# drifted across it.
#
# Note what is ABSENT from the hold's exits: nothing fires when the range SHRINKS.
# A ship closing on an artillery platform cannot make it give ground.
#
# ── The posture gate (issue #876) ────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `posture` is host-seeded on every helm policy host from this ship's own red
# alert: 0 DEFENSIVE, 1 PRESSED. Every leg of the aggressive half carries a
# transition back to `shadow` on `fact(posture) < param(press_posture)` at the
# HIGHEST priority in the state — nothing in a gun line is a commitment that
# outranks the captain standing the alert down.
#
# It is compared against an authored `press_posture` rather than a literal so a
# future intermediate rung on the posture ladder does not have to touch a guard.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The parameter surface
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# ENVELOPE    `max_artillery_range` / `artillery_hold_range` — the outer and inner
#             edges of the gun line. THE knobs: they belong to the including
#             hull's artillery piece and nothing else, so a hull whose bow gun
#             reaches 50 units and one whose reaches 200 differ here and nowhere.
#             `artillery_hold_speed` is the throttle held there.
# SAFE RANGE  `safe_range_margin` — world units of daylight wanted BEYOND the
#             target's own longest direct-fire reach, plus `orbit_speed`,
#             `orbit_spiral_gain`, `safe_ring_tolerance`,
#             `safe_distance_window_ticks` and `reengage_speed` shaping how the
#             defensive ring is held.
# POSTURE     `press_posture` — the rung at which the aggressive half unlocks.
# FIRE GATE   NOT here: it is `min_alert_to_fire` on each `*.ai` block inside the
#             hull's own `[[weapons_console.*_banks]]` / `[[torpedoes.tubes]]`
#             entries. Those arrays merge by `id`, so a shared fragment could
#             only name bank ids it cannot know, and an unmatched id APPENDS a
#             bank with no geometry. The fire gate is one authored predicate
#             repeated per weapon, by design (issue #872).
#
# The LEAD the hold predicts with is NOT authored anywhere: `artillery_lead_speed`
# is read host-side off the including hull's own blaster banks, because it is a
# reading of the armament rather than a decision about the manoeuvre. A hull with
# no bank publishes zero, which is exactly when there is no flight time to lead by.
#
# Every value below is a DEFAULT for the class, and every one is authored: there
# is no Rust fallback for any of them. The host gates each leg on its OWN complete
# scalar set and declines the whole arm on a missing name rather than flying at an
# invented number:
#
#   * `max_artillery_range` / `artillery_hold_range` / `artillery_hold_speed`
#     gate the firing position (`ARTILLERY_PARAMS`);
#   * the SIX recovery scalars gate the defensive ring (`RECOVERY_PARAMS`), and
#     they gate as one unit. `reengage_speed` names the throttle of a pivot leg
#     this doctrine never flies; it is authored anyway because omitting it
#     declines the standoff ring `shadow` is entirely made of.
#
# The shared thresholds are restated on each axis because content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`, and because these are two independent
# machines rather than one machine with two readers.

# ── Engines (longitudinal) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The throttle axis. Every state authors the same unconditional "actuate the
# planner's desired travel": which THROTTLE that resolves to is the Steering
# axis's verb's business (`artillery_hold_speed` on the gun line, `orbit_speed` on
# the defensive ring, ordinary doctrine travel while closing), so this axis needs
# no knowledge of which leg it is flying.
[helm_console.engines_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
rule = []

[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
# Restated on this axis because its OWN guards reference them; content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`. Engines runs an independent copy of the
# machine from the SAME shared fact snapshot, so it reaches each leg on its own
# reading rather than by consulting Steering's state — the two axes are separate
# fine systems and neither may read the other's memory.
max_artillery_range = 200.0
artillery_hold_range = 180.0
# The posture rung at which the aggressive half of the doctrine unlocks.
press_posture = 1.0

# Host-written private memory (issue #882: the host writes, the policy reads —
# there is no authored write verb). `min_range_seen` starts effectively infinite
# so the first folded range always wins the minimum.
[helm_console.engines_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # A target that appears ALREADY inside the band is not something to close on.
  # Higher priority than the reposition arm below so the two cannot both fire on
  # the tick a target resolves inside it.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "hold"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(artillery_hold_range)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reposition"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) > param(artillery_hold_range)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "reposition"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # Losing the target outranks the run-in: there is no position to take up against
  # nothing.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

  # The run-in ends at the INNER edge of the band, never at the outer one — see
  # the header for why the two are different numbers.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "hold"
  when = "fact(range_to_target) <= param(artillery_hold_range)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "hold"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

  # The ONLY way out of the hold that does not involve losing the target or the
  # alert. Note what is absent: nothing here fires when the range SHRINKS.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reposition"
  when = "fact(range_to_target) > param(max_artillery_range)"

# ── Steering (yaw) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The axis that carries the manoeuvre, because the host reads WHICH leg is being
# flown off this axis's verb — never off a state's name, so these states could be
# called anything.
#
#   hold_recovery_orbit      → hold a wide ring derived from the target's own
#                              reach plus this hull's authored margin: the
#                              defensive leg
#   actuate_desired_facing   → re-solve against the moving target every tick
#   hold_artillery_position  → neither "track the target" nor "hold a ring" but
#                              "point at where it WILL BE when my bolt gets
#                              there", with translational station held on the
#                              authored throttle
[helm_console.steering_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
rule = []

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
press_posture = 1.0
# ── The three scalars the HOST reads off this axis to fly the GUN LINE ────────
# Steering owns them because Steering's yaw verb is what tells the host which leg
# is being flown. Omit ANY ONE and the host declines the artillery arm outright —
# the hull falls back to ordinary doctrine travel rather than holding a position
# at an invented range or an invented throttle.
#
# The outer edge of the envelope, world units. Authored separately from the bow
# bank's own `range` on purpose: `range` is where a bolt stops existing, this is
# where a designer decided the gun line stops being worth holding.
max_artillery_range = 200.0
# The inner edge — ninety per cent of the outer one at the class default, authored
# as a real value because a designer tunes the band and not a ratio buried in
# Rust. Repositioning stops here.
artillery_hold_range = 180.0
# Throttle fraction flown while the position is held. Authored ZERO: an artillery
# platform that keeps closing is not an artillery platform. It needs a name of its
# own rather than borrowing another leg's throttle because an unauthored param and
# an authored 0.0 are the same number and opposite intents, so the host gates on
# the NAME being present.
artillery_hold_speed = 0.0
# Steering response. A tight deadband because the whole of the hold's output is
# yaw: a lead solution the hull declines to chase inside 0.03 rad is a lead
# solution several units wide at artillery range, which is most of a ship. The
# saturation angle is wide, because a heavy hull correcting a small lead error at
# full steering authority would oscillate around the solution rather than settle
# on it.
tracking_deadband_rad = 0.03
tracking_full_steer_rad = 0.6
# ── The six scalars the HOST reads off this axis to fly the DEFENSIVE ring ────
# Gated as one unit (`RECOVERY_PARAMS`): omit any one and the host declines the
# standoff arm outright, which would leave `shadow` — the leg this doctrine rests
# in whenever the alert is down — flying nothing at all.
#
# World units added to the TARGET's own longest usable direct-fire range to get
# the ring. The ring is therefore a property of the fight, not of this file: all a
# hull authors is how much daylight it wants beyond the other ship's guns. THE
# safe-range knob, and the counterpart of `artillery_hold_range`, which is a
# property of the hull's own gun instead.
safe_range_margin = 70.0
# Throttle fraction flown on the defensive ring. Deliberately LOW — this is a hull
# holding position at range, not patrolling one — but not zero: a ship parked
# inside a hostile's reach is not standing off from it, it is a target.
orbit_speed = 0.35
# Radians of heading offset per unit of FRACTIONAL radial error. Fractional so the
# same gain behaves identically on a 100-unit ring and a 400-unit one, and gentle
# because a slow hull hunting a wide ring is the failure mode here.
orbit_spiral_gain = 1.2
# World units inside the ring that still count as "at safe distance" when the
# distance history is folded. Absorbs the spiral's own overshoot, so a converging
# orbit is not read as a breach.
safe_ring_tolerance = 20.0
# Length of the bounded distance history, in shared AI ticks. At the default 30 Hz
# helm cadence this is two seconds of held standoff — the "maintained" in
# "maintained safe distance".
safe_distance_window_ticks = 60.0
# Throttle flown on the re-entry pivot. This doctrine authors no leg that flies
# it — there is no shield-recovery arm here — but the six gate as ONE unit, so
# omitting it would decline the defensive ring along with it. Authored ZERO, which
# is the same statement `artillery_hold_speed` makes: if a future leg ever reaches
# for it, a cold turn is what it should get.
reengage_speed = 0.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0
# Host-written on the tick the defensive ring is entered, from the seeded
# composite key. Declared here so its pre-engagement value is authored rather than
# implicit; no guard reads it — the host does, when it publishes the pass surface.
# The gun line itself never circles anything, so this slot belongs to `shadow`
# alone.
orbit_direction = 1.0

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"
# THE STANDOFF RING NEEDS THE SAME PROTECTION THE FIGHTING DOCTRINES' RINGS DO
# (issue #918 followed up) — see `movement_broadside_orbit.toml`'s `shadow`
# state for the full reasoning. `actuate_desired_facing` (priority 0) only
# runs on the tick `fact(target_valid) < 1`, and that is verified — against
# `tick_weapons_arc_request` in `src/console/weapons/mod.rs`, not assumed —
# to be exactly the tick no request against THIS ship's own combat lock can
# stand: `helm_shared_target_view` folds a resolvable lock's target into the
# merged view unconditionally, which is what makes `target_valid` true in the
# first place (issue #702).
yields_to_arc_requests = false

  # The defensive ring — but only against something to hold a ring AROUND. With
  # no target the standoff has no centre and the host has no reach to derive one
  # from, so the fallback hands the axis back to ordinary doctrine travel and the
  # hull flies its `[behaviour]` doctrine (patrol, hold station, a Navigation
  # waypoint) exactly as an unbackfilled one would. Without this second rule the
  # channel would resolve to "hold" and a targetless hull would coast on its last
  # steering input for ever.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 10
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0"
  verb = "hold_recovery_orbit"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "hold"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(artillery_hold_range)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reposition"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) > param(artillery_hold_range)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "reposition"

  # Ordinary target tracking on the way in. The bow is on the target rather than
  # on a lead solution, which is correct: nothing is being fired at this range, and
  # a run-in aimed at an intercept would arrive off to one side of it.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "hold"
  when = "fact(range_to_target) <= param(artillery_hold_range)"

# THE PREDICTIVE FIRING POSITION.
[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "hold"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "hold_artillery_position"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reposition"
  when = "fact(range_to_target) > param(max_artillery_range)"

# ── Impulse ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Switched OFF, and see the header for why it is switched off here rather than in
# `[[behaviour.doctrine]]`. `rule = []` clears the fleet baseline's unconditional
# permit — `idle` deep-merges as a plain scalar, and an idle declaration carrying
# an inherited rule is a contradiction content validation rejects.
[helm_console.impulse_ai]
idle = true
rule = []
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/ai/movement_at:
# The ATTACK-PASS class movement doctrine, as a reusable library fragment
# (issue #875).
#
# A FRAGMENT, not a hull — see the header of
# `fragments/ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml`. It is never parsed alone;
# `include_resolve` merges it into a declaring template and only the resolved
# document is validated and spawned.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What a hull writes to use this
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
#     includes = [
#       "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
#       "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml",
#       "fragments/ai/movement_attack_pass.toml",
#     ]
#
#     [helm_console.engines_ai.param]
#     commit_range = 150.0
#
# …and nothing else. Order matters: this fragment REPLACES the fleet baseline's
# three travel axes, so it must be listed after it (a template's includes merge
# in declared order, and the declaring template itself merges last).
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What this owns, and why it is one file rather than three
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# The WHOLE of `[helm_console.engines_ai]`, `[helm_console.steering_ai]` and
# `[helm_console.boost_ai]` — three independent copies of ONE machine, which
# agree by reading the same host-seeded facts rather than by sharing state. They
# ship together because a copy that disagreed with the other two about a
# threshold would reach a different leg on the same tick, which is a silent
# failure with no test that could name it.
#
# One fragment owns entire policy blocks because since #911 an array with no
# stable identity — and `*.ai.rule` and `*_ai.state[].transition` are both — still
# REPLACES wholesale on compose. Two fragments cannot each contribute a rule to
# the same policy; the second would wipe the first. Specialisation therefore runs
# entirely through `param`, an ordinary table that deep-merges.
#
# ── The two overrides this fragment has to make explicit ─────────────────────
#
# `rule = []` on Engines and Steering, and `idle = false` on Boost, clear what
# `fleet_baseline.toml` authors for those axes. Both are load-bearing, not
# tidiness:
#
#   * a policy that carries BOTH top-level rules and states is rejected at load
#     (`validate_fine_system_ai_policy`) — a machine resolves only inside its
#     current state, so the inherited rules would be dead code;
#   * `idle = true` is mutually exclusive with `state`, so an inherited idle
#     Boost would reject this machine outright.
#
# Any future class movement fragment owes the same two lines. That is the stated
# contract of a movement fragment: it replaces the baseline's travel axes whole.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The doctrine
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# A fly-through attack pass with a posture gate over it.
#
#   shadow  → the DEFENSIVE resting leg. Holds a standoff ring around the target
#             at `target_direct_fire_range + safe_range_margin` — outside the
#             other ship's guns by an authored margin — and never closes. This is
#             where a hull sits whenever its captain has not called red alert.
#   acquire → lining up. Tracks the target continuously.
#   inbound → closing at `approach_speed`.
#   escape  → the commitment. Steering switches to `hold_committed_heading`: fly
#             the frozen heading and stop looking at the target. NOTHING about
#             the target may cut this dwell short — that is what "commits to the
#             outward heading" means — and the posture check is deliberately at
#             the END of the dwell for the same reason.
#   recover → the pass cost too much; hold the standoff ring until the shields
#             come back.
#   reenter → cut-thrust pivot back onto the target.
#   pressed_pivot / pressed_pass
#           → the OPT-IN half of the doctrine (issue #789, generalised here by
#             #878). What a hull does when the recovery above is not on offer
#             because the other ship simply follows it out: it stops trying to
#             leave and fights at the range it is stuck at. Off by default —
#             see `pressed_min_progress` below.
#
# `escape` is entered by a CLOSEST-APPROACH detector, three conjuncts each doing
# distinct work: the target is visible; the gap has started opening
# (`closing_rate` below a slightly-negative epsilon, so sensor jitter at the
# merge cannot flip the test); and it has opened FAR ENOUGH to be real, measured
# against the running minimum the host keeps in private memory.
#
# ── The posture gate (AC2) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `posture` is host-seeded on every helm policy host from this ship's own red
# alert: 0 DEFENSIVE, 1 PRESSED. Every leg of the aggressive half carries a
# transition back to `shadow` on `fact(posture) < param(press_posture)`, so a
# captain standing the alert down breaks the ship off at the next tick the
# doctrine's own commitment allows.
#
# It is compared against an authored `press_posture` rather than a literal so a
# future intermediate rung on the posture ladder does not have to touch a guard.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The parameter surface (AC1)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# AGGRESSION  `commit_range` — how close before the hull commits to a run;
#             `approach_speed` / `escape_speed` — the two throttles;
#             `escape_duration_secs` — how long it flies out before turning back;
#             `press_posture` (below) at the LOWEST rung, for a hull that is
#             always pressed.
# PRESSED     `pressed_min_progress` — THE switch. World units of separation the
#             escape must have GAINED across the host's `pressed_window_ticks`
#             history for it to count as working; below it, and still inside the
#             target's reach with the shields spent, the hull abandons the
#             standoff ring for the short-pass loop. Authored here at a value no
#             separation reading can fall below, so the class default is OFF and
#             an including hull opts IN by authoring a real threshold — the same
#             "a threshold outside the fact's range is a switch" idiom
#             `min_alert_to_fire = 0` uses on the weapons. `pressed_pivot_secs`
#             and `pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis` shape the loop once it is
#             on and are inert while it is off.
#             The FOURTH pressed scalar, `pressed_window_ticks`, is deliberately
#             NOT authored here: no guard in this file names it, the HOST reads it
#             (with the other three) to publish the pressed arm at all, and a hull
#             that has not authored it gets the arm declined outright. So the loop
#             takes two independent opt-ins — the threshold above and that name —
#             and a hull that wants neither is untouched by either.
# SAFE RANGE  `safe_range_margin` — world units of daylight wanted BEYOND the
#             target's own longest direct-fire reach. The ring is a property of
#             the fight, not of the hull, so this is all a hull authors;
#             `safe_ring_tolerance`, `safe_distance_window_ticks`, `orbit_speed`,
#             `orbit_spiral_gain` shape how it is held.
# POSTURE     `press_posture` — the rung at which the aggressive half unlocks.
# FIRE GATE   NOT here: it is `min_alert_to_fire` on each `*.ai` block inside the
#             hull's own `[[weapons_console.*_banks]]` / `[[torpedoes.tubes]]`
#             entries. Those arrays merge by `id`, so a shared fragment could
#             only name bank ids it cannot know, and an unmatched id APPENDS a
#             bank with no geometry. The fire gate is one authored predicate
#             repeated per weapon, by design (issue #872).
#
# Every value below is a DEFAULT for the class, and every one is authored: there
# is no Rust fallback for any of them. Omit one of the six recovery scalars the
# host reads off the Steering axis by name — `safe_range_margin`, `orbit_speed`,
# `orbit_spiral_gain`, `safe_ring_tolerance`, `safe_distance_window_ticks`,
# `reengage_speed` — and the host DECLINES the standoff arm outright rather than
# orbiting at an invented radius.
#
# The shared thresholds are restated on each axis because content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`, and because these are three independent
# machines rather than one machine with three readers. A hull retuning a shared
# threshold retunes it on every axis that guards on it — which is exactly what
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`, the hand-authored ancestor of this fragment,
# does.

# ── Engines (longitudinal) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The throttle axis. Every state authors the same unconditional "actuate the
# planner's desired travel": which THROTTLE that resolves to is the Steering
# axis's verb's business (`approach_speed` inbound, `escape_speed` outbound,
# `orbit_speed` on the ring, `reengage_speed` on the pivot), so this axis needs no
# knowledge of which leg it is flying. A pass never coasts.
[helm_console.engines_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
rule = []

[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
# Throttle fraction flown while closing. "Normal speed" — not flat out, so the
# escape reads as a distinct change of pace.
approach_speed = 0.85
# Throttle fraction flown outbound.
escape_speed = 1.0
# The hull only commits to a run once the target is this close; further out it is
# still lining up. THE aggression knob.
commit_range = 150.0
# Closing rate (world units/s) below which the range counts as OPENING. Slightly
# negative rather than zero so sensor jitter at the merge cannot flip the test.
closing_rate_epsilon = -0.5
# How far (world units) the range must re-open above the minimum seen this state
# before closest approach is called. The confirmation half of the detector: it
# rejects a momentary negative blip that has not actually opened any distance.
closest_approach_hysteresis = 6.0
# How long (seconds) the escape leg runs before the hull turns back for another
# pass — or, if the posture has dropped, back to the standoff ring.
escape_duration_secs = 6.0
# Own-shield fraction at or below which the pass has cost too much to repeat: the
# escape hands off to the standoff ring instead of turning back in.
recover_shield_fraction = 0.35
# Own-shield fraction the ring must restore before re-entry is even considered.
# The other half of that gate is `fact(safe_distance_held)`; both are required.
reentry_shield_fraction = 0.85
# How long (seconds) the cut-thrust pivot runs before the next pass begins.
reenter_pivot_secs = 1.5
# The posture rung at which the aggressive half of the doctrine unlocks.
press_posture = 1.0
# ── The pressed short-pass loop (issue #789, generalised by #878) ─────────────
# OFF at the class default: `separation_progress` is a world-unit reading of how
# much ground the escape gained, so a threshold a million units below zero is one
# no escape can ever fall under and the branch below can never fire. A hull that
# wants the loop authors a real number here (and `pressed_window_ticks` on
# Steering, which is what makes the HOST publish the arm).
pressed_min_progress = -1000000.0
# How long (seconds) the boosted, thrust-cut pivot runs before the short pass.
# Short: the whole point is that it is faster than the ordinary
# `reenter_pivot_secs` turn, because the drive is lit for it.
pressed_pivot_secs = 1.2
# The SHORT pass's own closest-approach hysteresis, in world units of re-opened
# range. A fraction of the ordinary `closest_approach_hysteresis`, which is what
# makes the pressed pass a jab rather than a second full run-in.
pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis = 2.0

# Host-written private memory (issue #882: the host writes, the policy reads —
# there is no authored write verb). `min_range_seen` starts effectively infinite
# so the first folded range always wins the minimum.
[helm_console.engines_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"
