  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "inbound"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(commit_range)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "inbound"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  # The alert going down mid-run outranks the merge: an unmanned ship whose
  # captain has stood down must not press home a run it is no longer licensed to
  # make. This is the ONE leg of the pass that a posture drop interrupts
  # mid-flight, and it is safe to interrupt precisely because the hull is still
  # tracking rather than committed.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # CLOSEST APPROACH. Three conjuncts, each doing distinct work:
  #   target_valid          — never call a merge against a target we cannot see
  #   closing_rate < eps    — the gap has started opening (the + to − crossing)
  #   range_above_min_seen  — and it has opened far enough to be real, measured
  #                           against the running minimum in private memory
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "escape"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon) and fact(range_above_min_seen) > param(closest_approach_hysteresis) and memory(min_range_seen) < param(commit_range)"

  # Target lost mid-run: abandon the pass rather than merging on a ghost.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "escape"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  # Only the authored dwell ends the escape. Nothing about the target may cut it
  # short — that is what "commits to the outward heading" means. What the dwell
  # ends INTO is a decision, and all three branches share the `state_time`
  # conjunct so none of them can shorten the commitment:
  #   posture dropped  → back to the defensive ring
  #   shields spent    → the recovery ring
  #   otherwise        → line up for another pass
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # PRESSED (issue #789) outranks recovery because it answers a question recovery
  # has already assumed the answer to: recovery is a plan that begins "get away
  # from them", and this conjunct is the check that getting away is possible at
  # all. It shares the shield conjunct — a hull with its shields up has nothing to
  # recover — and deliberately carries no distance-held or shield-threshold
  # conjunct of its own, because both are things the ordinary doctrine WAITS for
  # and the whole finding is that waiting is not available.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 15
  to = "pressed_pivot"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(shield_fraction) <= param(recover_shield_fraction) and fact(inside_threat_range) > 0 and fact(separation_progress) < param(pressed_min_progress)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "recover"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(shield_fraction) <= param(recover_shield_fraction)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "acquire"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs)"

# The standoff ring, entered because the pass cost too much. Engines simply
# actuate the planner's desired travel here as everywhere else — the ring
# throttle (`orbit_speed`) is one of the authored scalars the host publishes on
# the pass surface.
[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "recover"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # BOTH halves, and neither alone. `safe_distance_held` is the bounded history
  # window's verdict — every sample across the whole window at or beyond the safe
  # ring — not a single-tick range reading.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reenter"
  when = "fact(shield_fraction) >= param(reentry_shield_fraction) and fact(safe_distance_held) > 0"

# The cut-thrust pivot. `reengage_speed = 0` on the Steering axis is what makes
# "actuate the planner's desired travel" mean zero throttle here.
[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "reenter"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "acquire"
  when = "state_time >= param(reenter_pivot_secs)"

# ── The pressed short-pass loop, on the travel axis ──────────────────────────
#
# Engines actuates the planner's desired travel in both states exactly as it does
# everywhere else; which throttle that resolves to is the Steering axis's yaw
# verb's business (`reengage_speed` for the pivot, `approach_speed` for the pass),
# so this axis needs no knowledge that it is jabbing rather than closing.
[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "pressed_pivot"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "pressed_pass"
  when = "state_time >= param(pressed_pivot_secs)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "pressed_pass"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # The same closest-approach detector the ordinary inbound leg uses, on the same
  # three conjuncts, differing in ONE authored scalar: the shorter
  # `pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis`. That single substitution is what makes
  # this a jab, and it is why the pressed pass needs no new host geometry at all.
  #
  # It ends in `escape` — the ordinary one — so every short pass is another real
  # attempt to get out, and the escape's own end-of-dwell question decides whether
  # the next thing is another jab or the recovery doctrine.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "escape"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon) and fact(range_above_min_seen) > param(pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis) and memory(min_range_seen) < param(commit_range)"

  # Target lost mid-jab: back to the ordinary acquire cycle. There is nothing left
  # to be pressed BY.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

# ── Steering (yaw) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The axis that carries the actual difference between the legs, because the host
# reads WHICH leg is being flown off this axis's verb — never off a state's name,
# so these states could be called anything.
#
#   actuate_desired_facing → re-solve against the moving target every tick
#   hold_committed_heading → fly the heading frozen at the merge instant, and
#                            stop looking at the target at all. NOT the same as
#                            letting the yaw channel resolve to "hold": a hold
#                            holds the last steering COMMAND, and a non-zero yaw
#                            at the merge would curl the hull straight back into
#                            the target it just passed.
#   hold_recovery_orbit    → hold a ring around the target
#   pivot_to_reengage      → track the target, but paired host-side with the
#                            authored `reengage_speed` instead of the approach
#                            throttle. That pairing is the whole difference.
[helm_console.steering_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
rule = []

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
commit_range = 150.0
closing_rate_epsilon = -0.5
closest_approach_hysteresis = 6.0
escape_duration_secs = 6.0
press_posture = 1.0
# Steering response. The deadband stops the hull hunting around a solved bearing
# at the merge; the saturation angle is what makes it turn hard onto a tracking
# solution rather than easing onto it. Both are read unconditionally by the host
# — omit either and no leg is flown at all.
tracking_deadband_rad = 0.02
tracking_full_steer_rad = 0.5
# Restated because this axis's own guards reference them; content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`.
recover_shield_fraction = 0.35
reentry_shield_fraction = 0.85
reenter_pivot_secs = 1.5
# ── The six scalars the HOST reads off this axis BY NAME to fly a ring ────────
# Steering owns them because Steering's yaw verb is what tells the host which leg
# is being flown; omit any one and the host declines the arm outright rather than
# orbiting at an invented radius.
#
# World units added to the TARGET's own longest usable direct-fire range to get
# the ring. The ring is therefore a property of the fight, not of this file: all a
# hull authors is how much daylight it wants beyond the other ship's guns. THE
# safe-range knob.
safe_range_margin = 60.0
# Throttle fraction flown on the ring. Not zero: a hull parked inside a hostile's
# reach is not shadowing it, it is a target.
orbit_speed = 0.6
# Radians of heading offset per unit of FRACTIONAL radial error. Fractional so the
# same gain behaves identically on an 80-unit ring and an 800-unit one.
orbit_spiral_gain = 1.2
# World units inside the ring that still count as "at safe distance" when the
# distance history is folded. Absorbs the spiral's own overshoot, so a converging
# orbit is not read as a breach.
safe_ring_tolerance = 20.0
# Length of the bounded distance history, in shared AI ticks. At the default 30 Hz
# helm cadence this is two seconds of held standoff — the "maintained" in
# "maintained safe distance".
safe_distance_window_ticks = 60.0
# Throttle flown on the re-entry pivot. ZERO: the hull cuts thrust and turns cold
# before it commits to the next run. The pressed pivot reuses this same throttle —
# a stationary pivot is a stationary pivot — and differs only in having the boost
# drive lit for it.
reengage_speed = 0.0
# ── The pressed short-pass loop (issue #789, generalised by #878) ─────────────
# Restated on this axis because its own guards reference them; content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`. See the Engines copy for why the class
# default is OFF.
pressed_min_progress = -1000000.0
pressed_pivot_secs = 1.2
pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis = 2.0
# `pressed_window_ticks` is the fourth scalar the HOST reads off this axis by name
# to publish the pressed arm at all, and it is DELIBERATELY absent: no guard reads
# it, so a hull that has not asked for the loop gets the arm declined outright.
# Authoring it here would publish the arm for every hull in the class.

[helm_console.steering_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0
# Host-written on the tick a ring is entered, from the seeded composite key.
# Declared here so its pre-ring value is authored rather than implicit; no guard
# reads it — the host does, when it publishes the pass surface.
orbit_direction = 1.0

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"
# THE STANDOFF RING NEEDS THE SAME PROTECTION AS THE FIGHTING LEG BELOW (issue
# #918 followed up) — see `movement_broadside_orbit.toml`'s `shadow` state for
# the full reasoning behind declining the WHOLE state rather than only the
# `hold_recovery_orbit` rule. The short version: this leg's other rule,
# `actuate_desired_facing` (priority 0), only runs on the tick
# `fact(target_valid) < 1`, and that is verified — against
# `tick_weapons_arc_request` in `src/console/weapons/mod.rs`, not assumed — to
# be exactly the tick no request against THIS ship's own combat lock can
# stand: `helm_shared_target_view` folds a resolvable lock's target into the
# merged view unconditionally, which is what makes `target_valid` true in the
# first place (issue #702).
yields_to_arc_requests = false

  # The defensive ring — but only against something to hold a ring AROUND. With
  # no target the standoff has no centre and the host has no reach to derive one
  # from, so the fallback hands the axis back to ordinary doctrine travel and the
  # hull flies its `[behaviour]` doctrine (patrol, hold station, a Navigation
  # waypoint) exactly as an unbackfilled one would. Without this second rule the
  # channel would resolve to "hold" and a targetless hull would coast on its last
  # steering input for ever.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 10
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0"
  verb = "hold_recovery_orbit"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "inbound"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(commit_range)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "inbound"

  # Continuous tracking of a MOVING target: the facing is re-solved from the
  # target's current position on every gated tick.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "escape"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon) and fact(range_above_min_seen) > param(closest_approach_hysteresis) and memory(min_range_seen) < param(commit_range)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "escape"
# THE COMMITMENT IS THE LEG, so the leg keeps the facing (issue #918). "Nothing
# about the target may cut this dwell short" was written into this doctrine from
# the start and nothing enforced it: a channel-3 `ArcBearingRequest` overwrote
# the frozen heading with a bow-on tracking solution for any family that could
# not bear — which, on a hull flying away from the ship it has just passed, is
# most of them — and hauled the destroyer straight back into the guns it had
# just flown through. Declining the request is the enforcement.
#
# The declaration sits on THIS leg alone. `acquire` and `inbound` track the
# target anyway and leave the default standing, so a destroyer still turns to
# bring a family to bear on its way in, exactly as a hull with no doctrine does.
yields_to_arc_requests = false

  # THE commitment. The heading was frozen by the host at the instant this
  # transition committed; hazard avoidance may still bend it, the target may not,
  # and since #918 neither may a weapon that cannot bear.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "hold_committed_heading"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # See the Engines copy for why the pressed branch outranks recovery.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 15
  to = "pressed_pivot"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(shield_fraction) <= param(recover_shield_fraction) and fact(inside_threat_range) > 0 and fact(separation_progress) < param(pressed_min_progress)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "recover"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(shield_fraction) <= param(recover_shield_fraction)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "acquire"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "recover"
# THE RING NEEDS PROTECTING HERE TOO (issue #918 followed up): this leg flies
# the same `plan_recovery_orbit` tangent solver as the fighting ring and the
# `shadow` standoff above, so it is exactly as vulnerable to Channel 3's
# bow-on overwrite. Unlike `shadow` this state has only the one yaw rule
# (unconditional `hold_recovery_orbit`), so the decline is unconditional too.
yields_to_arc_requests = false

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "hold_recovery_orbit"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reenter"
  when = "fact(shield_fraction) >= param(reentry_shield_fraction) and fact(safe_distance_held) > 0"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "reenter"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "pivot_to_reengage"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "acquire"
  when = "state_time >= param(reenter_pivot_secs)"

# ── The pressed short-pass loop, on the axis that carries it ─────────────────
#
# NO fifth yaw verb, and that is the finding rather than a shortcut. The pressed
# pivot is a thrust-cut turn onto the target, which is exactly what
# `pivot_to_reengage` already means — the host pairs it with `reengage_speed`,
# authored at zero — and the short pass is a normal-speed run at a moving target,
# which is exactly what `actuate_desired_facing` already means. What makes these
# states PRESSED is the boost rule on the Boost axis and the shorter hysteresis on
# the way out, not a different way of steering.
#
# Both legs track the target, so both leave the channel-3 default standing and
# still turn to bring a family that cannot bear onto it (issue #918).
[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "pressed_pivot"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "pivot_to_reengage"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "pressed_pass"
  when = "state_time >= param(pressed_pivot_secs)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "pressed_pass"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "escape"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon) and fact(range_above_min_seen) > param(pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis) and memory(min_range_seen) < param(commit_range)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

# ── Boost ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A third independent copy of the same machine. It transitions on the same
# host-seeded facts as the other two, so it reaches `escape` on the same tick —
# by agreeing about the world, not by reading a shared pass state. Only `escape`
# authors a boost rule at all, so the channel holds and the drive stays cold
# through the shadow, approach and ring legs.
#
# `idle = false` is what clears the fleet baseline's explicit idle Boost — see
# the header. A hull that includes this fragment and wants no AI boost after all
# authors `[helm_console.boost_ai] idle = true`, which is rejected against these
# states, so it must drop the fragment instead: the doctrine is a package.
[helm_console.boost_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
idle = false
rule = []

[helm_console.boost_ai.param]
commit_range = 150.0
closing_rate_epsilon = -0.5
closest_approach_hysteresis = 6.0
escape_duration_secs = 6.0
press_posture = 1.0
recover_shield_fraction = 0.35
reentry_shield_fraction = 0.85
reenter_pivot_secs = 1.5
# How long into the escape leg the drive burns. Shorter than the escape itself,
# so the hull coasts the last stretch and the drive is recharging before it turns
# back in.
escape_boost_secs = 3.5
# Do not light the drive from near-standstill (e.g. straight after a collision
# scrub); boost is an escape accelerant, not a launch assist.
boost_min_speed_fraction = 0.3
# ── The pressed short-pass loop (issue #789, generalised by #878) ─────────────
# Restated so this axis reaches the same legs from the same facts — it is a third
# independent copy of the machine, not a reader of the other two. See the Engines
# copy for why the class default is OFF.
pressed_min_progress = -1000000.0
pressed_pivot_secs = 1.2
pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis = 2.0

[helm_console.boost_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0

[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "inbound"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(commit_range)"

[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "inbound"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "escape"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon) and fact(range_above_min_seen) > param(closest_approach_hysteresis) and memory(min_range_seen) < param(commit_range)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "escape"

  # The one rule on this axis. `boost_available` is the host's own capability
  # reading (the drive exists, is enabled and is charged); `speed_fraction` is the
  # anti-launch-assist gate; `state_time` is the burn budget.
  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "boost"
  when = "state_time < param(escape_boost_secs) and fact(boost_available) > 0 and fact(speed_fraction) >= param(boost_min_speed_fraction)"
  verb = "engage_boost"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "shadow"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # See the Engines copy for why the pressed branch outranks recovery. This is a
  # third independent copy of the machine over the same host-seeded facts, so it
  # reaches the same leg on the same tick without reading either sibling.
  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 15
  to = "pressed_pivot"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(shield_fraction) <= param(recover_shield_fraction) and fact(inside_threat_range) > 0 and fact(separation_progress) < param(pressed_min_progress)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "recover"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs) and fact(shield_fraction) <= param(recover_shield_fraction)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "acquire"
  when = "state_time >= param(escape_duration_secs)"

[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "recover"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "reenter"
  when = "fact(shield_fraction) >= param(reentry_shield_fraction) and fact(safe_distance_held) > 0"

[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "reenter"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "acquire"
  when = "state_time >= param(reenter_pivot_secs)"

# ── The pressed short-pass loop, on the drive ────────────────────────────────
#
# The ONE state in the whole doctrine that lights the drive for something other
# than running away. Boost multiplies `max_yaw_rate` as well as speed, and this
# pivot is flown on cut thrust, so every drop of it goes into how fast the bow
# comes round — which is the only resource a pinned hull is actually short of.
[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "pressed_pivot"

  # NO `speed_fraction` conjunct, unlike the escape's rule above, and the omission
  # is the point: this pivot is deliberately flown at zero throttle, so the
  # escape's "do not light the drive from a standstill" guard would refuse exactly
  # the case this state exists for. The reason that guard exists — boost as a
  # launch assist is wasted — does not apply when the drive is being spent on yaw
  # rather than on speed.
  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "boost"
  when = "fact(boost_available) > 0"
  verb = "engage_boost"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "pressed_pass"
  when = "state_time >= param(pressed_pivot_secs)"

# The CANCEL. Like `recover` and `reenter`, this state authors no boost rule at
# all: the channel holds, `ai_helm_boost`'s on-change release fires the tick the
# pivot's rule stops firing, and the short pass runs in at normal speed with the
# drive cold and recharging for the escape at the end of it.
[[helm_console.boost_ai.state]]
id = "pressed_pass"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "escape"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon) and fact(range_above_min_seen) > param(pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis) and memory(min_range_seen) < param(commit_range)"

  [[helm_console.boost_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"
