# The BROADSIDE-ORBIT class movement doctrine, as a reusable library fragment
# (issue #876 AC1).
#
# A FRAGMENT, not a hull — see the header of
# `fragments/ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml`. It is never parsed alone;
# `include_resolve` merges it into a declaring template and only the resolved
# document is validated and spawned.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What a hull writes to use this
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
#     includes = [
#       "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
#       "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml",
#       "fragments/ai/movement_broadside_orbit.toml",
#     ]
#
#     [helm_console.engines_ai.param]
#     torpedo_run_range = 35.0
#
#     [helm_console.steering_ai.param]
#     combat_orbit_range = 32.0
#     combat_orbit_speed = 0.6
#     torpedo_run_range = 35.0
#
# Order matters: this fragment REPLACES the fleet baseline's two travel axes, so
# it must be listed after it (a template's includes merge in declared order, and
# the declaring template itself merges last).
#
# `combat_orbit_range` alone is NOT enough, and the two extra names are not
# decoration:
#
# * `torpedo_run_range` must be restated on BOTH axes, sized to the including
#   hull's own envelope — see "The range gate, and why the leg needs one" below.
#   Left at the class default of 50 a tighter hull enters the bow hold, which is
#   flown at `torpedo_bearing_speed = 0`, from outside its own guns and parks
#   there dealing nothing. Engines and Steering are two independent copies of one
#   machine, so tuning one and not the other has them break their ring at
#   different ranges and disagree about which leg they are flying.
# * `combat_orbit_speed` is left to this file's default only by a hull that has
#   MEASURED that the default suits it. It is a throttle held on a ring of the
#   hull's own radius, and the sustained yaw it demands is `v / r` against that
#   hull's `max_yaw_rate` — a number the class default cannot know.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# What this owns, and what it deliberately leaves alone
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# The WHOLE of `[helm_console.engines_ai]` and `[helm_console.steering_ai]` —
# two independent copies of ONE machine, which agree by reading the same
# host-seeded facts rather than by sharing state. They ship together because a
# copy that disagreed with the other about a threshold would reach a different
# leg on the same tick, which is a silent failure with no test that could name
# it.
#
# NOT `[helm_console.boost_ai]`. No leg of a broadside orbit engages the drive —
# a ring is flown at a steady authored throttle and a boost would only widen it —
# so the fleet baseline's `idle = true` is exactly the right declaration and this
# fragment leaves it standing. `movement_attack_pass.toml` owes `idle = false`
# because it SUPPLIES a boost machine; a movement fragment that supplies none
# owes nothing. This is the same reading `movement_artillery.toml` takes.
#
# NOT `[helm_console.impulse_ai]` either, and that is a REAL difference from
# `movement_artillery.toml` rather than an oversight. The artillery fragment has
# to idle the drive because its hold band (180 units at the class default) sits
# INSIDE the impulse autopilot's default cruise window — engage at 200, cancel at
# 40 — so the drive would still be engaged, hard-overriding commanded throttle,
# at the very range the gun line is supposed to be held at. A fighting ring is
# the opposite geometry: it is tens of units across, comfortably INSIDE the
# drive's own 40-unit cancel radius, so the autopilot releases before the ring
# begins and the doctrine's throttle is the one that flies. `movement_attack_pass.toml`
# leaves impulse alone for the same reason, and both fragments' hulls keep the
# baseline's permit — which is what keeps the impulse baseline unanimous across
# the fleet.
#
# One fragment owns entire policy blocks because since #911 an array with no
# stable identity — and `*.ai.rule` and `*_ai.state[].transition` are both — still
# REPLACES wholesale on compose. Two fragments cannot each contribute a rule to
# the same policy; the second would wipe the first. Specialisation therefore runs
# entirely through `param`, an ordinary table that deep-merges.
#
# `rule = []` appears twice, on Engines and on Steering, and it is load-bearing
# on both: it clears the rules `fleet_baseline.toml` authors, because a policy
# carrying BOTH top-level rules and states is rejected at load
# (`validate_fine_system_ai_policy`).
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The doctrine
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# A fighting ring with a torpedo run cut into it, under a posture gate.
#
#   shadow      → the DEFENSIVE resting leg. Holds a wide standoff ring around
#                 the target at `target_direct_fire_range + safe_range_margin`,
#                 outside the other ship's guns by an authored margin, and it
#                 never closes. This is where a hull sits whenever its captain
#                 has not called red alert.
#   acquire     → a target has appeared but is not yet inside `engage_range`.
#                 Tracks it continuously and lets ordinary doctrine travel carry
#                 the hull in.
#   orbit       → THE MANOEUVRE, and what the posture gate buys. Circles the
#                 target at the hull's own `combat_orbit_range` so the broadsides
#                 bear for the whole ring rather than only where it grazes
#                 weapons range.
#   torpedo_run → the ring BREAKS and the bow comes onto the target, for as long
#                 as there is a salvo to put into it. Then the ring resumes.
#
# ── Why a ring needs a torpedo run at all, and why the doctrine owns it ───────
#
# This is the load-bearing paragraph of the file. A settled ring holds the target
# at EXACTLY 90 degrees — a circular path makes the hull's heading the tangent,
# so the bearing is the beam by construction rather than merely near it. Every
# fixed forward tube in the fleet is therefore permanently out of arc for as long
# as the ring is flown, and a hull that only ever orbits never launches anything.
#
# That is not just a damage cost; left alone it stops the ring being flown at
# all. Weapons raises a channel-3 `ArcBearingRequest` for the first family that
# has the target in reach and cannot bear (`tick_weapons_arc_request` in
# `src/console/weapons/mod.rs`), and a torpedo's reach is `speed * lifespan` —
# hundreds of units, so it is effectively never out of reach. On the receiving
# side `apply_arc_bearing_request` (`src/ship/helm_ai.rs`) does not bias the
# doctrine's facing, it OVERWRITES the steering command with a full bow-on
# tracking solution AFTER the planner has already solved the ring tangent —
# which it did for every yaw verb, `hold_combat_orbit` included, until issue #918
# gave a leg the right to decline. A ring with loaded tubes and no torpedo leg
# got dragged bow-on by Channel 3, snapped back to the tangent when a tube bore,
# and was dragged bow-on again — a sawtooth that walked the hull tens of units in
# and out of its authored radius, through whatever envelope the other ship was
# shooting from.
#
# So the bow-on phase is authored HERE, as a leg of the doctrine, rather than
# left to arrive from Channel 3. `evaluate_family_arc_request` emits nothing for
# a family in which some emitter is READY — in range and in arc — so a hull that
# points its own bow when it has a salvo ready satisfies the request by flying
# its own doctrine, and the ring it returns to is the ring the planner solved.
# The two halves are the same manoeuvre described once.

# ── What this leg absorbs, and what closes the rest (issue #918) ─────────────
#
# The torpedo leg absorbs the request; it does not remove it. The two conditions
# are not the same shape: the request fires while a loaded tube cannot bear, and
# this leg opens while a loaded salvo is worth pointing at. Between them sits
# every tick where the hull is on its ring with tubes it has no run-range for — a
# reloading hull just outside `torpedo_run_range`, most obviously — and on those
# ticks Channel 3 used to overwrite the steering anyway.
#
# Nothing a doctrine could author closed that gap, because closing it meant
# pretending an opportunity existed in order to satisfy a request. #918 closed it
# from the other end instead: the `orbit` state below declares
# `yields_to_arc_requests = false`, and the host asks the leg the helm is
# CURRENTLY flying whether a request may take its facing. The ring says no; the
# hull's travelling legs say nothing and therefore yes, so a cruiser that is not
# yet on its ring still turns to bring a family to bear exactly as it always did.
# It is a property of the leg, never of who asked — a human Tactical officer's
# request and an AI seat's are the same request by the time the helm sees it
# (AGENTS.md #6). #918's other half is the destroyer's `escape` leg in
# `movement_attack_pass.toml`, whose frozen heading had the identical problem and
# no torpedo run to hide behind; it carries the identical declaration.
#
# The torpedo leg is not made redundant by any of this and is not folded away: a
# ring that declines a request still cannot fire a fore tube, and pointing the
# bow when a salvo is worth pointing it is a manoeuvre the doctrine wants for its
# own sake.
#
# What the ring's remaining cost is, is a THROTTLE decision rather than a facing
# one — see `combat_orbit_speed` below, which is the knob an including hull sizes
# against it.
#
# ── The entry condition: what "a torpedo shot is available" reads as ─────────
#
# It is genuinely readable at the helm, which is not obvious and is worth stating
# plainly: `seed_torpedo_opportunity_facts` runs on every ship every shared tick,
# unconditionally, and seeds `tubes_full`, `tubes_fillable`, `torpedoes_in_flight`
# and `target_facing_shield_down` whatever the hull's doctrine asks for. They are
# TRANSITION-scope facts — the per-axis actuator hosts resolve rule guards from
# their own snapshot — which is why every guard below that reads one is a
# transition and every RULE in this file is unconditional.
#
# The entry takes three readings:
#
# * `tubes_full` — is a WHOLE salvo loaded RIGHT NOW? The launcher's own
#   question, computed helm-side by exactly the expression `ai_torpedo_auto_fire`
#   uses to seed the launch channel's fact of the same name, so the manoeuvre
#   that spends a firing geometry and the launcher that uses it ask one question
#   and not two.
# * `tubes_fillable` — is a whole salvo still REACHABLE at all? Slower and
#   quieter: no tube and not the magazine has been shot out, and enough rounds
#   remain to top every tube up. It catches what `tubes_full` structurally
#   cannot, a tube that is loaded but destroyed, so the pair reads "a salvo is
#   loaded, and the battery that will fire it is intact".
# * `range_to_target <= torpedo_run_range` — see below. Without it the leg is not
#   a manoeuvre, it is a handbrake.
#
# ── Why the target's SHIELD FACING is deliberately not one of them ───────────
#
# `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml`, the hand-authored ancestor of this fragment, adds
# `target_facing_shield_down` to its own entry, and on THAT hull the launcher
# really does refuse every shot while the striking arc is up. So the tighter
# guard is not wrong about the shot. It is wrong about the JOB.
#
# Two corrections to how this paragraph used to put it, both owed to issue #929.
# The refusal is no longer a RUST fact and has not been since issue #956:
# `auto_fire_torpedo` (`src/console_ai/core.rs`) is a pure candidate filter now
# — target locked, tube loaded, tube in arc — and does NOT return an empty list
# on `target_facing_shields > 0`; the hold is each tube's own authored
# `torpedo_launch` guard. And it is consequently no longer true "for every hull,
# player and NPC alike" — though as of #929's second pass it is true again:
# `alliance_cruiser.toml` briefly authored a `max_striking_shield_hp` threshold
# past any arc reading and held for nothing, and is now back on the fleet's
# literal `<= 0` with every other armed hull.
#
# What this leg exists to own is the channel-3 `ArcBearingRequest`, and that
# request fires on a strictly WEAKER condition than "the launcher would fire now":
# `evaluate_family_arc_request` emits whenever some loaded tube has the target in
# reach and NO tube of the family bears. Loaded and unable to point is enough. A
# doctrine that only breaks its ring when the shot is already takeable therefore
# leaves the request firing across the whole rest of the engagement, and Channel 3
# flies the ship instead of the planner — which is the exact failure the leg was
# added to end.
#
# It is measured rather than argued. On `alliance_cruiser.toml` in
# `assets/worlds/probe_aggressor.toml`, with `target_facing_shield_down` on the
# entry, the run opened on 0 of 901 ticks: the hull's beams average about 1 damage
# per second into an 80-point arc regenerating 6.5, so the window it was waiting
# for never came. The ring meanwhile sawtoothed from its authored 22 units down to
# 7.8, and the engagement went 101 dealt against 370 taken. With the conjunct
# dropped, the same run holds 24.5-25.6 units with no sawtooth at all and goes 62
# dealt against 0 taken.
#
# The "about 1 damage per second" there is the cruiser at
# `beam_damage_per_sec = 4` on one bearing bank, which is what it carried until
# issue #929 took it to 32 across two (`auto_arc_deg = 270`) so its own launcher
# gate could be satisfiable. The GEOMETRY
# argument is what this paragraph is for and it does not depend on that number:
# the request fires on loaded-and-unable-to-point, so a doctrine that breaks its
# ring only when the shot is already takeable leaves Channel 3 flying the ship
# for the rest of the engagement however hard the beams hit.
#
# The Harrow's reading is right for the Harrow because a shield gap is the only
# thing its bow hold can be FOR: its rounds author `damage_shields = 0`, and its
# beams are a 270-degree pair it works from the beam, so bow-on it can neither
# strip the arc nor use the rounds. Waiting bow-on for a window it is not creating
# would be a deadlock. The shared intent is "only point the bow when pointing it
# accomplishes something"; the literals differ because the hulls differ.
#
# ── WITHDRAWN, and it is the whole of issue #929 ──────────────────────────────
#
# This paragraph used to end: "A hull whose forward bank bears on its own bow can
# strip the arc it is about to shoot through, so the same bow hold is
# SELF-COMPLETING." That was false when it was written, and it is the precise
# false premise that let the permissive reading ship next to a strict launcher.
#
# A bow hold is self-completing only if the hull can open the gap FASTER than the
# target closes it. `alliance_cruiser.toml` could not. Its two banks then authored
# `auto_arc_deg = 180`, abutting on the beam line, so bow-on it worked ONE of them
# — and at its then-authored `beam_damage_per_sec = 4` that was about 1 dmg/s into
# the arc, instrumented — while the target's own Shields AI focuses that arc on
# the fleet baseline: `focus_bonus_regen = 4` over `regen_per_sec = 2.5` is
# 6.5 hp/s, and `focus_focused_damage_multiplier` halves what lands. The hold
# therefore never completed, and because this leg's only armament exits
# (`tubes_full`, `tubes_fillable`) both need a round to have LEFT a tube, a
# launcher that never fires makes the leg ABSORBING: measured on
# `probe_aggressor`, 86.9 s of a 90 s run parked at `torpedo_bearing_speed = 0.0`
# with nothing launched.
#
# THE RULE THAT SURVIVES IT. A permissive `torpedo_run_shield_gap` is only safe
# beside a launcher that will actually fire on the window it opens — and there
# are exactly two ways to owe that, one static and one dynamic:
#
#   * STATICALLY, by making the launcher's guard no stricter than the leg's
#     entry. No shipped hull does this.
#   * DYNAMICALLY, by carrying guns that open the arc the launcher is waiting
#     for. `alliance_battleship`, `alliance_destroyer` and
#     `ship_harrow_warhawk` have always escaped this way, and since #929
#     `alliance_cruiser` does too: `beam_damage_per_sec = 32` on two banks that
#     both bear (`auto_arc_deg = 270`), which its own file justifies against a
#     swept ladder rather than against the arithmetic above — the two-bank case
#     does NOT halve the single-bank break-even, and that file says why.
#
# `authored_ai_pins::a_bow_hold_a_hull_can_reach_and_a_launcher_that_can_answer_it`
# censuses the fleet so a hull with neither escape cannot be composed in silence.
# It reads the STATIC half only — a static answer is provable from the authored
# text, a dynamic one is a balance claim that only a seeded run can make — so a
# hull in the dynamic bucket owes its evidence in its own file, and
# `alliance_cruiser.toml` carries the sweep that pays for it.
#
# #929's first pass took a third route and it is worth naming as a road not
# taken: it authored `max_striking_shield_hp = 1000000.0` on the cruiser's tubes,
# a threshold past any arc reading, which made the launcher unconditional. That
# is gone. It could only be argued for while `damage_hull` bypassed shields
# outright — with a round that no longer does, holding it for a downed arc is
# worth ten times spending it into a live one, and the gate is the point of the
# leg rather than an obstacle to it.
#
# So it is a PARAMETER rather than a fork (issue #878, moving
# `ship_harrow_cruiser.toml` onto this file). `torpedo_run_shield_gap` is the
# minimum `target_facing_shield_down` reading the run demands, and the fact is a
# boolean 0/1:
#
#   * `0.0` (the class default) — "any reading will do". `>= 0` admits both, so
#     the entry below is exactly the range-and-readiness guard the measurements
#     above chose for the player cruiser, and the extra exit is dead (`< 0` is
#     unreachable). Nothing about a hull that leaves this alone changes.
#   * `1.0` — the Harrow's reading. The run opens only on a struck-down arc and
#     ENDS when the arc comes back, which is the exit the stricter entry owes:
#     a hull that kept its bow on a recovered shield would be giving away the
#     broadside for nothing.
#
# The launcher's own gate is a separate and stricter thing again, and stays on the
# TUBES where the loadout lives (`fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0` on both Harrow
# tubes): this parameter decides when the MANOEUVRE is worth flying, not when the
# shot is takeable.
#
# ── The range gate, and why the leg needs one ────────────────────────────────
#
# `torpedo_run_range` is what stops the leg opening during the RUN-IN. The bow
# hold is flown at `torpedo_bearing_speed`, which is authored ZERO, so entering it
# does not merely change the facing — it cuts thrust and stops the hull wherever
# it happens to be. A hull whose tubes finish loading while it is still closing
# would freeze at that range and stay there, and if that range is outside its own
# weapons envelope it will sit and do nothing for the rest of the engagement.
# Measured on the player cruiser with no gate: parked at 26.7 units, three
# hundredths of a unit outside its own effective beam reach, for 810 of 901 ticks,
# dealing nothing. (That measurement predates issue #955, when a bank's reach was
# `beam_range × ModifierSlot::RadarRange` and the cruiser's 40-unit banks reached
# only 26.7. Reach is now the authored `beam_range`, so the cruiser's own gate has
# a wider margin than it was sized for — the FAILURE MODE is unchanged, and an
# including hull whose gate sits outside its envelope still freezes and does
# nothing.)
#
# So an including hull authors this as the range inside which pointing the bow
# still leaves its own guns on the target — a property of that hull's envelope,
# like `combat_orbit_range` and unlike `safe_range_margin`. It belongs just
# outside the radius the ring settles at, so the leg opens from the ring and not
# before it.
#
# ── The three ways back to the ring ──────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `torpedoes_in_flight` is a conjunct on both armament exits and means the same
# thing on both: a hull does not turn away from rounds it has committed, airborne
# or still owed to a burst. Firing makes `tubes_full` false immediately, so
# without that conjunct the first guard would release the ship on the very tick
# it launched.
#
#   * THE SALVO IS SPENT (`tubes_full`) — the ordinary case, and the BOUND. Entry
#     required a full salvo; firing empties the tubes; the reload is what puts
#     the hull back on its ring. This bound is drawn on the hull's OWN armament
#     and so does not depend on the target doing anything — which matters,
#     because `target_facing_shield_down` reads `1.0` permanently against a
#     target that carries no `[shields]` block at all.
#   * THE BATTERY IS GONE (`tubes_fillable`) — what a rounds-in-the-tube reading
#     structurally cannot see. A tube destroyed AFTER the run opened leaves
#     `tubes_full` true (the rounds are still sitting in the dead tube) and would
#     shut every other exit; this is the guard that catches it.
#   * THE TARGET IS GONE (`target_valid`) — there is no bow to hold on nothing,
#     and this one lands in `acquire` rather than `orbit` because there is no
#     ring to hold either.
#
# Priorities are authored explicitly on every exit because content validation
# refuses equal-priority transitions out of one state: an authored tie would
# resolve by file order, which is a decision the file should be making out loud.
#
# ── The posture gate (issue #876) ────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `posture` is host-seeded on every helm policy host from this ship's own red
# alert: 0 DEFENSIVE, 1 PRESSED. Every leg of the aggressive half carries a
# transition back to `shadow` on `fact(posture) < param(press_posture)` at the
# HIGHEST priority in the state — nothing in a ring is a commitment that outranks
# the captain standing the alert down, and unlike an attack pass's escape leg
# there is no frozen heading to protect.
#
# It is compared against an authored `press_posture` rather than a literal so a
# future intermediate rung on the posture ladder does not have to touch a guard.
#
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# The parameter surface
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# RING        `combat_orbit_range` — THE knob. The fighting radius, and a
#             property of the including hull's OWN guns rather than of the enemy:
#             it belongs inside the banks' `beam_range` by a real margin so the
#             target stays under the broadsides for the whole ring instead of
#             only where it grazes weapons range. `combat_orbit_speed` is the
#             throttle held there and `combat_orbit_spiral_gain` how hard the
#             radial error is corrected.
# AGGRESSION  `engage_range` — how close before the ring is joined at all.
# TORPEDO RUN `torpedo_run_range` — how close before a loaded salvo is worth
#             breaking the ring for, and the guard that stops the leg freezing the
#             run-in; `torpedo_bearing_speed` — the throttle flown with the bow on
#             the target; `torpedo_run_shield_gap` — whether the run also demands
#             a struck-down striking arc (see above; 0 = no, 1 = yes).
# SAFE RANGE  `safe_range_margin` — world units of daylight wanted BEYOND the
#             target's own longest direct-fire reach, plus `orbit_speed`,
#             `orbit_spiral_gain`, `safe_ring_tolerance`,
#             `safe_distance_window_ticks` and `reengage_speed` shaping how the
#             defensive ring is held.
# POSTURE     `press_posture` — the rung at which the aggressive half unlocks.
# FIRE GATE   NOT here: it is `min_alert_to_fire` on each `*.ai` block inside the
#             hull's own `[[weapons_console.*_banks]]` / `[[torpedoes.tubes]]`
#             entries. Those arrays merge by `id`, so a shared fragment could
#             only name bank ids it cannot know, and an unmatched id APPENDS a
#             bank with no geometry. The fire gate is one authored predicate
#             repeated per weapon, by design (issue #872).
#
# Every value below is a DEFAULT for the class, and every one is authored: there
# is no Rust fallback for any of them. The host gates each leg on its OWN
# complete scalar set and declines the whole arm on a missing name rather than
# flying at an invented number:
#
#   * `combat_orbit_range` / `combat_orbit_speed` / `combat_orbit_spiral_gain`
#     gate the fighting ring (`COMBAT_ORBIT_PARAMS`), and they gate as one unit —
#     "one authoring the throttle but not the range would fly a tangent of a ring
#     of radius zero, which is a spiral straight into the target";
#   * `torpedo_bearing_speed` gates the bow hold (`TORPEDO_BEARING_PARAMS`) on
#     its own, because the value a hull most often wants is `0.0`, which is
#     indistinguishable from unauthored unless the gate asks for the NAME.
#     `torpedo_run_range` is NOT one of the host's gates — no Rust reads it — it
#     is read only by this file's own entry guard, on both axes;
#   * the SIX recovery scalars gate the defensive ring (`RECOVERY_PARAMS`), and
#     they gate as one unit. `reengage_speed` names the throttle of a pivot leg
#     this doctrine never flies; it is authored anyway because omitting it
#     declines the standoff ring `shadow` is entirely made of.
#
# The shared thresholds are restated on each axis because content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`, and because these are two independent
# machines rather than one machine with two readers.

# ── Engines (longitudinal) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The throttle axis. Every state authors the same unconditional "actuate the
# planner's desired travel": which THROTTLE that resolves to is the Steering
# axis's verb's business (`combat_orbit_speed` on the fighting ring,
# `torpedo_bearing_speed` on the bow hold, `orbit_speed` on the defensive ring,
# ordinary doctrine travel while closing), so this axis needs no knowledge of
# which leg it is flying.
[helm_console.engines_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
rule = []

[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
# Restated on this axis because its OWN guards reference them; content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`. Engines runs an independent copy of the
# machine from the SAME shared fact snapshot, so it reaches each leg on its own
# reading rather than by consulting Steering's state — the two axes are separate
# fine systems and neither may read the other's memory.
engage_range = 220.0
torpedo_run_range = 50.0
# Minimum `target_facing_shield_down` reading the bow hold demands. 0.0 = any —
# see the header. A hull that wants the Harrow's stricter reading authors 1.0.
torpedo_run_shield_gap = 0.0
# The posture rung at which the aggressive half of the doctrine unlocks.
press_posture = 1.0

# Host-written private memory (issue #882: the host writes, the policy reads —
# there is no authored write verb). `min_range_seen` starts effectively infinite
# so the first folded range always wins the minimum.
[helm_console.engines_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(engage_range)"

[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "orbit"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # THE TORPEDO OPPORTUNITY. Engines runs its OWN copy of the machine from the
  # SAME shared fact snapshot, so it reaches the run on its own reading rather
  # than by consulting Steering's state — the two axes are independent fine
  # systems and neither may read the other's memory.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "torpedo_run"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(torpedo_run_range) and fact(tubes_full) > 0 and fact(tubes_fillable) > 0 and fact(target_facing_shield_down) >= param(torpedo_run_shield_gap)"

  # A transition guarded on hazard urgency here would drop the hull out of the
  # ring for the duration of a detour it is already handling additively, and
  # re-entering would re-draw the circulation direction — so a debris field would
  # randomise which way the ship circles. Losing the target is the one thing that
  # genuinely ends an engagement.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

# The torpedo run, on the travel axis. The rule is the same unconditional
# "actuate the planner's desired travel" every other state authors, and it has to
# be: the run's throttle is `torpedo_bearing_speed`, which the HOST reads off the
# Steering axis and folds into the planner solution. This axis never learns which
# leg it is flying, exactly as it never learns it is orbiting.
[[helm_console.engines_ai.state]]
id = "torpedo_run"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "longitudinal"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

  # THE WINDOW CLOSED — dead unless the hull demanded one (`torpedo_run_shield_gap
  # = 0.0` makes `< 0` unreachable). See the header.
  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 15
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(target_facing_shield_down) < param(torpedo_run_shield_gap) and fact(torpedoes_in_flight) < 1"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(tubes_full) < 1 and fact(torpedoes_in_flight) < 1"

  [[helm_console.engines_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(tubes_fillable) < 1 and fact(torpedoes_in_flight) < 1"

# ── Steering (yaw) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The axis that carries the manoeuvre, because the host reads WHICH leg is being
# flown off this axis's verb — never off a state's name, so these states could be
# called anything.
#
#   hold_recovery_orbit    → hold a wide ring derived from the target's own reach
#                            plus this hull's authored margin: the defensive leg
#   actuate_desired_facing → re-solve against the moving target every tick
#   hold_combat_orbit      → neither of those: hold a ring around the target at
#                            MY OWN fighting range, with the broadsides bearing
#   hold_torpedo_bearing   → "point my bow at where the target is RIGHT NOW" — a
#                            live tracking solution, re-solved every tick, because
#                            a target that jinks while a fixed tube is lining up
#                            is the case the leg exists to handle. It is not
#                            `pivot_to_reengage`, whose geometry is identical:
#                            that verb is one leg of the shield-RECOVERY doctrine
#                            and is paired host-side with `reengage_speed`, one of
#                            six scalars all about a ring derived from the
#                            TARGET's reach.
[helm_console.steering_ai]
initial_state = "shadow"
rule = []

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
press_posture = 1.0
# The hull commits to the ring once the target is this close. Comfortably outside
# `combat_orbit_range` so the approach and the ring are distinct phases and the
# spiral-in is visible rather than instantaneous.
engage_range = 220.0
# Steering response. A wide deadband because an orbit is a sustained turn against
# a continuously moving solution and a tight one would have the hull hunting
# either side of the tangent every tick. The saturation angle is TIGHT because it
# is half of what sets the ring's steady-state radius — see
# `combat_orbit_spiral_gain`.
tracking_deadband_rad = 0.05
tracking_full_steer_rad = 0.3
# ── The three scalars the HOST reads off this axis to fly the FIGHTING ring ───
# Steering owns them because Steering's yaw verb is what tells the host which leg
# is being flown. Omit ANY ONE and the host declines the combat-orbit arm
# outright — the hull falls back to ordinary doctrine travel rather than circling
# at an invented radius or at zero throttle.
#
# The fighting radius, world units, and THE knob every including hull retunes: it
# is an authored property of that hull's own guns and is not derived from the
# target. It belongs inside the banks' `beam_range` by a real margin.
combat_orbit_range = 42.0
# Throttle fraction flown on the ring. Not zero and not flat out: the ring has to
# hold its angular rate against `max_yaw_rate`, and a hull at full throttle on a
# tight ring would need more turn authority than it has.
#
# It is also the doctrine's exposure to the residual described in the header, and
# an including hull should size it with that in mind. While the tubes are loaded
# and out of arc, `apply_arc_bearing_request` overwrites the STEERING and leaves
# this THROTTLE alone, so whatever fraction of the ring Channel 3 is flying is
# flown bow-on at this speed — straight at the thing being circled. A ring that is
# too fast for its radius does not wobble, it closes.
combat_orbit_speed = 0.6
# Radians of heading offset per unit of FRACTIONAL radial error. Fractional so
# the same gain behaves identically on a 42-unit ring and a 400-unit one.
#
# Much higher than the defensive ring's gain below, and the reason is the control
# law rather than taste. The correction is PROPORTIONAL — heading offset against
# radial error, with no integral term — so the ring settles at the radius where
# the offset it commands is exactly the offset needed to sustain the turn, which
# is always a little OUTSIDE the authored radius. That equilibrium solves to
# `r(r - R) = v * R * tracking_full_steer_rad / (max_yaw_rate * gain)`. A gentle
# gain is fine for a standoff ring hundreds of units out, where a few per cent is
# noise; on a fighting ring it would settle most of the way to the edge of the
# weapons envelope. Raising the gain and tightening `tracking_full_steer_rad`
# together is what pulls it back in.
combat_orbit_spiral_gain = 4.0
# ── The scalar the HOST reads off this axis to fly the TORPEDO RUN ────────────
# Throttle fraction flown while the bow is held on the target. Authored ZERO: the
# leg exists to stop the hull swinging and let a fixed forward tube settle on the
# target, and thrust on a tight ring is what makes the bearing move.
#
# Zero is exactly why this needs a name of its own. An unauthored param and an
# authored 0.0 are the same number and opposite intents, so the host gates on the
# NAME being present: omit it and the whole bow-hold arm is declined and the hull
# keeps orbiting, rather than coasting to a halt in front of an enemy on a value
# nobody chose.
torpedo_bearing_speed = 0.0
torpedo_run_range = 50.0
# Restated on this axis because its OWN guards reference it; content validation
# rejects an undeclared `param(...)`. See the header.
torpedo_run_shield_gap = 0.0
# ── The six scalars the HOST reads off this axis to fly the DEFENSIVE ring ────
# Gated as one unit (`RECOVERY_PARAMS`): omit any one and the host declines the
# standoff arm outright, which would leave `shadow` — the leg this doctrine rests
# in whenever the alert is down — flying nothing at all.
#
# World units added to the TARGET's own longest usable direct-fire range to get
# the ring. The ring is therefore a property of the fight, not of this file: all a
# hull authors is how much daylight it wants beyond the other ship's guns. THE
# safe-range knob, and the counterpart of `combat_orbit_range`, which is a
# property of the hull's own guns instead.
safe_range_margin = 60.0
# Throttle fraction flown on the defensive ring. Deliberately LOW — this is a hull
# standing off, not patrolling — but not zero: a ship parked inside a hostile's
# reach is not standing off from it, it is a target.
orbit_speed = 0.5
# Radians of heading offset per unit of FRACTIONAL radial error, and gentle
# because a slow hull hunting a wide ring is the failure mode here.
orbit_spiral_gain = 1.2
# World units inside the ring that still count as "at safe distance" when the
# distance history is folded. Absorbs the spiral's own overshoot, so a converging
# orbit is not read as a breach.
safe_ring_tolerance = 20.0
# Length of the bounded distance history, in shared AI ticks. At the default 30 Hz
# helm cadence this is two seconds of held standoff — the "maintained" in
# "maintained safe distance".
safe_distance_window_ticks = 60.0
# Throttle flown on the re-entry pivot. This doctrine authors no leg that flies
# it — there is no shield-recovery arm here — but the six gate as ONE unit, so
# omitting it would decline the defensive ring along with it. Authored ZERO, which
# is the same statement `torpedo_bearing_speed` makes: if a future leg ever
# reaches for it, a cold turn is what it should get.
reengage_speed = 0.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.memory]
min_range_seen = 1000000.0
escape_heading_rad = 0.0
# Host-written on the tick a ring is entered, from the seeded composite key.
# Declared here so its pre-engagement value is authored rather than implicit; no
# guard reads it — the host does, when it publishes the pass surface. Both rings
# share the slot, because a ship circles one way at a time.
orbit_direction = 1.0

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "shadow"
# THE STANDOFF RING NEEDS THE SAME PROTECTION AS THE FIGHTING RING (issue #918
# followed up). This leg's `hold_recovery_orbit` rule flies the identical
# `plan_recovery_orbit` tangent solver `orbit`'s `hold_combat_orbit` does
# (`src/ai/core.rs`), so it is exactly as vulnerable to Channel 3's bow-on
# overwrite: a standoff ring that yielded would sawtooth in and out of its
# own radius precisely as an undeclined fighting ring did.
#
# Declined on the WHOLE state rather than only the `hold_recovery_orbit`
# rule — `yields_to_arc_requests` is a state-level field, so a per-rule
# decline cannot be authored. The coarser grain costs nothing here: the
# state's other rule, `actuate_desired_facing` (priority 0), fires only on
# the tick `fact(target_valid) < 1` — exactly when the ring rule's own guard
# fails and THIS ship has no resolvable target of its own. Verified against
# `tick_weapons_arc_request` (`src/console/weapons/mod.rs`) rather than
# assumed: a request can exist only once this ship's own frozen combat lock
# resolves to a live position (`live_entity_xz`), and `helm_shared_target_view`
# folds that same lock's target into the Helm's merged view unconditionally —
# regardless of this ship's own radar range — precisely so Helm and Weapons
# never disagree about it (issue #702). So on every tick a request against
# this ship's own lock could stand, `target_valid` is already true and the
# ring rule is the one flying, not the fallback — the decline never has a
# live request to refuse while `actuate_desired_facing` is the one running.
yields_to_arc_requests = false

  # The defensive ring — but only against something to hold a ring AROUND. With
  # no target the standoff has no centre and the host has no reach to derive one
  # from, so the fallback hands the axis back to ordinary doctrine travel and the
  # hull flies its `[behaviour]` doctrine (patrol, hold station, a Navigation
  # waypoint) exactly as an unbackfilled one would. Without this second rule the
  # channel would resolve to "hold" and a targetless hull would coast on its last
  # steering input for ever.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 10
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0"
  verb = "hold_recovery_orbit"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)"

[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "acquire"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(engage_range)"

# THE MANOEUVRE.
[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "orbit"
# THE RING IS THE MANOEUVRE, so the ring keeps the facing (issue #918). A settled
# ring holds the target on the beam by construction, which is a bearing no fixed
# fore tube can ever satisfy, so Channel 3 raises a request for the tube family
# on every tick this leg is flown. Declining it is what makes the ring flyable:
# a leg that yielded here would be overwritten by a bow-on tracking solution
# after the planner had already solved the tangent, and the hull would sawtooth
# between the two facings for as long as it fought.
#
# Only THIS leg declines, and it declines only while it is the current one. The
# hull's travelling legs (`acquire`, and `shadow` with nothing to stand off from)
# leave the default standing and turn to bring a family onto its target exactly
# as a hull with no doctrine does.
yields_to_arc_requests = false

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "hold_combat_orbit"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  # THE TORPEDO OPPORTUNITY — see the header for why this leg exists and why its
  # entry is the hull's OWN readiness rather than the target's shield facing.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "torpedo_run"
  when = "fact(target_valid) > 0 and fact(range_to_target) <= param(torpedo_run_range) and fact(tubes_full) > 0 and fact(tubes_fillable) > 0 and fact(target_facing_shield_down) >= param(torpedo_run_shield_gap)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

# THE TORPEDO RUN, on the axis that carries it: the ring stops and the bow comes
# onto the target for as long as there is a salvo to put into it.
[[helm_console.steering_ai.state]]
id = "torpedo_run"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "yaw"
  when = "true"
  verb = "hold_torpedo_bearing"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 30
  to = "shadow"
  when = "fact(posture) < param(press_posture)"

  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 20
  to = "acquire"
  when = "fact(target_valid) < 1"

  # THE WINDOW CLOSED — dead unless the hull demanded one (`torpedo_run_shield_gap
  # = 0.0` makes `< 0` unreachable). `torpedoes_in_flight` is the same conjunct
  # the other two exits carry and means the same thing: a hull does not turn away
  # from rounds it has committed, so a recovering arc cannot release it mid-salvo.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 15
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(target_facing_shield_down) < param(torpedo_run_shield_gap) and fact(torpedoes_in_flight) < 1"

  # THE SALVO IS SPENT, and re-entering `orbit` here is what re-draws the
  # circulation direction — so the ring resumed after a torpedo run is not
  # necessarily the one that preceded it.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 10
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(tubes_full) < 1 and fact(torpedoes_in_flight) < 1"

  # THE BATTERY IS GONE — see the header. `tubes_full` is a statement about the
  # rounds, not about the tubes, so shooting a tube out mid-run leaves the guard
  # above shut with the rounds still sitting in the dead tube.
  [[helm_console.steering_ai.state.transition]]
  priority = 0
  to = "orbit"
  when = "fact(tubes_fillable) < 1 and fact(torpedoes_in_flight) < 1"
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/composed_escor:
# A hull composed entirely from fragments (issue #869 composition fixture).
#
# Declares almost nothing itself: the systems, helm envelope and doctrine come
# from `npc_escort_core.toml`, and the Captain AI policy comes from the fragment
# THAT includes. What this file adds is a specialisation — it raises the shared
# doctrine's `base_priority` by id, which proves the includer wins while the
# keys it never mentions (`directive_kind`, `target_speed`, `maintain_range`)
# still come from the fragment.
#
# This is a mechanism fixture. Shipped hulls are NOT composed yet; migrating
# them is issues #878 / #875.

includes = ["npc_escort_core.toml"]

class = "escort"
hull_id = "FIXTURE-869"

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.9, 0.3, 0.1]
size = 10.0
icon = "destroyer"

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id = "destroy-hostiles"
base_priority = 90.0
base_files.assets/entities/fragments/npc_escort_cor:
# Shared NPC escort core (issue #869 composition fixture).
#
# A FRAGMENT, not a hull — see the header of
# `fragments/ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml`.
#
# Carries the parts every small AI-driven escort repeats: the ownerless
# `ai_only` system suite, a helm envelope, and a Destroy doctrine. It in turn
# includes the reusable Captain policy, so resolving a hull that includes THIS
# file exercises a nested include and a path relative to this file's own
# directory (`ai/...`, not `fragments/ai/...`).
#
# It also includes `ai/fleet_baseline.toml`, which carries the other fifteen
# ship-level AI declarations. Since #885b stage 5d strict AI-declaration mode is
# the default and there is no Rust-side synthesiser behind them, so a hull with
# `[behaviour]` that omits one does not load at all.

includes = ["ai/captain_red_alert_aggressive.toml", "ai/fleet_baseline.toml"]

tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"]

[hull]
hull_integrity = 400.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 4.0
length = 10.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static terrain
# omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
#
# Authored HERE, on a fragment, because this file carries a `[helm_console]`
# and a helm system suite: anything composing from it is by construction a
# hull, and without the field the composed escort resolves to a ship that
# publishes itself as static terrain — over-avoided by everything else, and
# contributing neither vertical repulsion (#780) nor moving-hazard urgency
# (#744) itself. Note that
# `config::tests::shipped_hulls_are_mobile_and_shipped_terrain_is_not` skips
# `fragments/`, because nothing here is spawnable, so this line rests on the
# convention above rather than on that guard.
movable = true

[helm_console]
max_speed = 10.0
max_reverse_speed = 5.0
acceleration = 4.0
deceleration = 10.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.2
max_bank_deg = 5.0

[ai_profile]
aggression = 1.0
sensor_range = 200.0

[behaviour]

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id = "destroy-hostiles"
directive_kind = "Destroy"
base_priority = 40.0
target_speed = 0.9
maintain_range = 40.0

# No stations: every system is ownerless and `ai_only`, so the NPC spawn path
# puts each one under `ControlSource::Ai`. The Red Alert system the Captain
# policy above drives is synthesised by `EntityConfig::from_toml` for any hull
# with a `[behaviour]` block, so it is deliberately not listed here.
[[system]]
id = "helm-thrust"
kind = "helm_thrust"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-steering"
kind = "helm_steering"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-impulse"
kind = "helm_impulse"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "power-reactor"
kind = "power_reactor"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "power-battery"
kind = "power_battery"
ai_only = true
base_files.assets/entities/lifecycle_tender.toml:
# Lifecycle tender — the probe-world operator for the continuous-task lifecycle
# (issue #1341, PRD #1337).
#
# `tractor_tug.toml` proves one mechanism; this hull exists to prove that TWO
# unrelated continuous workflows record the same lifecycle. It is the tug plus a
# survey suite: an engineering-owned `kind = "tractor"` system with its own power
# group and coupling terms, AND a `kind = "sensors"` system with its own power
# group and `[scan]` ladder, so one hull can hold a hulk and read a structure at
# the same moment — which is what makes "simultaneous tasks stay separately
# identifiable" testable at all.
#
# Kept OUT of `tractor_tug.toml` and out of every shipped combat hull on purpose:
# adding a survey suite to a hull a committed world flies would move that world's
# content digest for a slice that changes no gameplay. Nothing here is new
# mechanism — every table is one the tug or the destroyer already authors.
#
# It flies nothing: the probe drives the operator's position and its Tactical
# lock from the test, and both workflows through the ordinary admitted-command
# path, so the tender needs no helm, weapons or AI policy of its own.

tags = ["ship"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"
mass = 12000.0

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 0.6
length = 1.5
# No helm capability, so per the movable/helm invariant this stays the
# static-terrain default rather than claiming to be a flyable hull.
movable = false

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.2, 0.8, 0.9]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

# ── Power ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# No `[power]` block, so the reactor takes the default 100-unit capacity /
# resting-total-6 profile. The two small groups below draw 4 between them, well
# under it, so both rest at nominal without the probe having to nurse them.

[power_groups.tractor]
label = "entity.lifecycle_tender.power_groups.tractor.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.survey]
label = "entity.lifecycle_tender.power_groups.survey.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── Damage entries ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# So either system can be knocked out — the interruption the probe drives by
# damaging one of them.
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "tractor"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "sensors"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

# ── One station owns both systems ────────────────────────────────────────────
# A lean fixture, not a crewing statement: what matters to the lifecycle is that
# each system RESOLVES a station, so a task's start beat can name the station a
# human would be sitting at.
[[station]]
id = "engineering"
name = "Engineering"
description = "entity.lifecycle_tender.station.engineering.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "ENG"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[system]]
id = "tractor"
kind = "tractor"
station = "engineering"
power_group = "tractor"

[[system]]
id = "sensors"
kind = "sensors"
station = "engineering"
power_group = "survey"

# ── The coupling terms ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[tractor]
range = 600.0
coupling_offset = [0.0, 0.0, -120.0]
min_power_level = 2

[tractor.tow_load]
half_penalty_mass = 10000.0
max_penalty = 0.8

# ── The survey suite ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The scan bus rides its own `survey` group so the probe can starve the suite
# without touching the beam, and vice versa — two workflows whose failures are
# genuinely independent.
[scan]
power_group = "survey"
min_power_level = 2

[[scan.band]]
id = "detailed"
label = "entity.lifecycle_tender.scan.band.detailed.label"
max_range = 200.0
condition_step = 0.01

[[scan.band]]
id = "coarse"
label = "entity.lifecycle_tender.scan.band.coarse.label"
max_range = 400.0
condition_step = 0.25
report_capacities = false

base_files.assets/entities/region_kaleth_nebula.tom:
# The Kaleth nebula — the region template that composes the most effects at
# once, and the one `region_radiation_band.toml`'s header names as the shape it
# was written in. Light continuous damage, a shrunken radar picture, stale
# readings, no comms, and a fog the viewscreen draws.
#
# NO WORLD SPAWNS THIS TODAY. `before_the_fire` was the scenario that placed it
# and that tree has been deleted; the template is kept because the composition
# is the reference one and because `docs/prd/before-the-fire-scenario.md` and
# `editor/tests/canvas-region.test.js` both still describe it. That is why the
# fix below moves no digest: a template nothing spawns folds nothing.

tags = ["region", "nebula"]

[radar_appearance]
region_colour = [0.6, 0.4, 1.0]

[shape]
type = "sphere"
radius = 220.0

[effects]

[effects.damage_zone]
damage_per_second = 3.0
shield_pierce = 0.25

# The picture shrinks to TWO FIFTHS — the figure
# `docs/prd/before-the-fire-scenario.md` records as this nebula's acceptance
# criterion ("`radar_dampening` (0.4x multiplier)").
#
# NEGATIVE, and that is not a typo. `range_modifier` is a signed BONUS on
# `ModifierSlot::RadarRange` (`modifiers::coordination::apply_region_effects`),
# not a multiplier, and it reaches the radar through PRD #117's two-sided
# formula in `modifiers::cache::ShipModifiers::rebuild_cache`:
#
#     bonus >= 0  ->  multiplier = 1 + bonus
#     bonus <  0  ->  multiplier = 1 / (1 + |bonus|)
#
# So "two fifths of the scope" is the bonus that solves `1 / (1 + |b|) = 0.4`:
#
#     1 + |b| = 1 / 0.4 = 2.5   ->   |b| = 1.5   ->   range_modifier = -1.5
#
# On the Alliance cruiser that is a weapons horizon of `50 x 0.4 = 20` units and
# a helm scope of `93.75 x 0.4 = 37.5` — inside a 220-unit sphere, a crew who
# cannot see out of the cloud they are in.
#
# THIS FILE SHIPPED WITH `0.4` UNTIL THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THIS COMMENT (found
# in #1037). Read as a multiplier it matches the PRD exactly; read as the signed
# bonus the engine actually applies it said `1 + 0.4`, and a nebula made the
# radar reach FORTY PERCENT FURTHER — the opposite of every other effect in this
# file. A positive number on a DAMPENING effect is always wrong, and
# `regions::effects`'s shipped-asset test now says so.
#
# [ai] `-1.5` is the value that reproduces the PRD's 0.4x under the real
# formula. It is a correction, not a new tuning call, and the tuning itself is
# unratified.
[effects.radar_dampening]
range_modifier = -1.5

[effects.sensor_blind]

[effects.comms_jammed]

[effects.nebula_fog]
color = [0.25, 0.08, 0.32]
density = 0.015

base_files.assets/entities/region_radiation_band.to:
# Radiation band — one band of a sweeping storm (issue #1037).
#
# The Falling Skyway storm is authored as REGION TEMPLATES spawned and retired on
# a schedule, not as new hazard code. This is the whole band: everything a
# radiation front does to a crew, composed out of effects that already existed,
# in the shape `region_kaleth_nebula.toml` set. Nothing in Rust knows this file
# is a storm.
#
# WHY IT IS NOT `region_storm_band.toml`. That template is #1027's, and its own
# header makes a point of carrying NO `damage_zone`: it is the slow-only band the
# operations probe measures a rate against, and putting damage on it would make
# every test of the slow rule also a test of the damage rule. This is the other
# band — the one a scenario places when it wants the storm to cost hull as well
# as time — and the two are separate templates so each stays the single thing it
# claims to be.
#
# ── The five effects, and what each one is for ───────────────────────────────
#
#   damage_zone       the hull cost. LIGHT and continuous: being caught is never
#                     instant death, and lingering is what kills.
#   radar_dampening   the crew's picture shrinks. This is the effect that makes
#                     the storm a PLANNING problem — a band you cannot see past
#                     is a band you have to have routed around already.
#   sensor_blind      … and the readings they do have go stale.
#   comms_jammed      … and they cannot ask anyone about it. Every party in the
#                     corridor is behind a channel that stops working exactly
#                     when the crew most want it.
#   slow_zone         the ship-movement penalty (thrust/yaw), authored at
#                     `[effects.slow_zone]` below. It was ALSO the marker an
#                     operation's `[[operations.capability.interrupt]]` read with
#                     `region_effect = "slow_zone"` to stretch external work — but
#                     since issue #1164 no shipped hull authors an operations
#                     capability, so the storm no longer THROTTLES a crew's
#                     external work. It reaches the destroyer's coupling systems
#                     (tractor/umbilical/dock) the way it reaches any system now:
#                     through `damage_zone` above, which disables them. The
#                     interrupt vocabulary still exists (retired in #1166), so
#                     this slow_zone stays a valid presence marker with no shipped
#                     consumer; here it is purely the movement tax.
#
# ── The tuning, and what it is tuned FOR ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The target the scenario is written against: a ship caught by a band survives
# the crossing; a ship that loiters in one does not. Both halves are the same
# two numbers.
#
# `shield_pierce = 0.5` splits the damage in half. The pierced half goes straight
# to the hull; the absorbed half is spread uniformly across the shield facings,
# which for a per-tick slice this small rounds away — so 5 points a second of
# radiation is TWO AND A HALF points a second of hull, and the arithmetic below
# is written against that effective figure rather than against the nominal one.
#
# EVERY CROSSING TIME BELOW IS AN IN-BAND SPEED, and until the slow-zone sign
# fix none of them was. This table was first written at each hull's authored
# `max_speed` — the destroyer's 18, the hauler's 12 — as though `slow_zone` did
# not exist, which while `slow_zone` made ships FASTER was wrong in the other
# direction as well. A band that genuinely slows to three fifths means a ship
# inside it makes `0.6 x max_speed`, and a 520-unit crossing costs the time
# below. Corrected with the sign; see `[effects.slow_zone]`.
#
#   Alliance Destroyer, 300 hull points — 18 u/s clear, 10.8 u/s in-band
#     crossing one 520-unit band                 ~48 s   120 pts   survives
#     working the Falling Skyway rescue and
#       then flying for the lee                  ~79 s   198 pts   survives, hurt
#     loitering in the corridor for the whole
#       three-band sweep the mission authors    ~124 s   310 pts   DESTROYED
#
#   Alliance Courier, 200 hull points — 22 u/s clear, 13.2 u/s in-band
#     crossing one 520-unit band                 ~39 s    98 pts   survives
#     loitering                                   80 s of exposure  DESTROYED
#
#   Civilian bulk hauler, 60 hull points — 12 u/s clear, 7.2 u/s in-band
#     loitering                                   24 s of exposure  DESTROYED
#
# Only the CROSSINGS moved. Loitering is a wall-clock cost and the front does
# not care how fast the ship it is cooking would like to be going, so those
# three figures are exactly what they were.
#
# The last line is why Falling Skyway orders its traffic off the lane rather than
# trusting it to fly through: a hauler makes 12 units a second in clear space and
# 7.2 inside a band, so a 520-unit crossing would take it 72 seconds and it is
# dead in 24. It cannot cross a band alive, and traffic has to be routed AROUND a
# sweep, which is the whole point of announcing one. THE FIX MADE THIS CLAIM
# TRUE RATHER THAN LUCKY: at the old positive bonus a hauler was swept along at
# 19.2 u/s and crossed in 27 seconds against the 24 it takes to die, so the
# sentence held by three seconds and would have stopped holding under any
# gentler damage tuning.
#
# [ai] Every number here is unratified. `damage_per_second` and `shield_pierce`
# are the pair the tuning pass (#1044) moves to make "you can be caught, you
# cannot camp" land exactly; `radius` is sized to the Falling Skyway corridor,
# which runs about 2,100 units north to south, so three bands sweep it in three
# legible steps rather than smothering it in one.

name = "entity.region_radiation_band.name"
tags = ["region", "storm", "radiation", "slow_zone"]

[radar_appearance]
# Hot orange, and distinct from `region_storm_band.toml`'s duller amber: the two
# read differently on a radar because one of them hurts.
region_colour = [0.95, 0.45, 0.15]

[target]
tags = ["region"]
threat_level = "none"
description = "entity.region_radiation_band.target.description"

[shape]
type = "sphere"
radius = 260.0

[effects]

# Light, and continuous. See the tuning table above for what these two numbers
# buy against the two hulls the scenario fields.
[effects.damage_zone]
damage_per_second = 5.0
shield_pierce = 0.5

# The picture shrinks to a third. Enough that a crew inside a band are working
# off what they knew a minute ago, not enough that the radar goes dark — a blank
# scope reads as a broken console rather than as weather.
#
# NEGATIVE, and that is not a typo. `range_modifier` is a signed BONUS on
# `ModifierSlot::RadarRange`, not a multiplier, and it goes through PRD #117's
# negative-bonus formula: −2.0 is a range multiplier of 1/(1+2) — one third.
# A POSITIVE number here would make a radiation front improve the radar.
[effects.radar_dampening]
range_modifier = -2.0

[effects.sensor_blind]

[effects.comms_jammed]

# The thrust/yaw numbers are the region system's own — flying through a front is
# slower than flying around it. An OPERATION reads only that a slow zone is
# present; what that costs the work is the capability's rate to author, and that
# rate (`rate_percent = 50`, meaning half) is a percentage and was never wrong.
#
# THREE FIFTHS the thrust, seven tenths the turn. The thrust number is the one
# the tuning table at the top of this file is written against: it is what makes
# a 520-unit crossing 48 destroyer-seconds instead of 29, and so it is what
# makes a crossing cost 120 hull points instead of 72. "Flying through a front
# is slower than flying around it" is a claim about the ship, not only about the
# work, and this is the field that has to be true for the sentence to be.
#
# NEGATIVE, and that is not a typo — the same sign trap `[effects.radar_dampening]`
# above documents, on the field pair whose names read even harder as multipliers.
# `thrust_modifier` and `yaw_rate_modifier` are signed BONUSES on
# `ModifierSlot::MaxSpeed` and `ModifierSlot::MaxYawRate`, not multipliers, and
# they go through PRD #117's two-sided formula. The bonus that gives a wanted
# multiplier `m` is `-(1/m - 1)`:
#
#     thrust, m = 0.6   ->   1/0.6 = 5/3    ->   -(5/3 - 1)    = -0.6666667
#     yaw,    m = 0.7   ->   1/0.7 = 10/7   ->   -(10/7 - 1)   = -0.4285714
#
# THIS FILE SHIPPED WITH `0.6` AND `0.7` UNTIL THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THIS
# COMMENT. Read as multipliers they say "three fifths thrust, seven tenths yaw";
# read as the signed bonuses the engine actually applies they said `1 + 0.6` and
# `1 + 0.7`, and a RADIATION FRONT MADE SHIPS 60% FASTER AND 70% MORE AGILE than
# they are in clear space — in a file whose own header, eighty lines up, said
# that flying through a front is slower than flying around it. It is the same
# defect the radar-dampening sign fix corrected on the neighbouring field
# (found in #1037); this band's `radar_dampening` was authored deliberately
# negative in that pass and these two were missed.
#
# [ai] `-0.6666667` and `-0.4285714` are the values that reproduce this file's
# original authoring intent under the real formula. They are a correction, not a
# new tuning call, and the tuning itself is unratified.
[effects.slow_zone]
thrust_modifier = -0.6666667
yaw_rate_modifier = -0.4285714

[radar_appearance]
