base_files.assets/entities/region_storm_band.toml:
# Radiation storm band — a sweeping hazard that makes work take longer
# (issue #1027).
#
# ORPHANED SINCE ISSUE #1164. This slow-only band existed for the operations
# interrupt to read `region_effect = "slow_zone"` and stretch external work. Its
# only consumers were `probe_operations` and `probe_destroy`, both retired in
# #1164 when the destroyer's operations capabilities became first-class systems;
# a storm now reaches those systems through damage, not by throttling an
# operation (see `region_radiation_band.toml`). The template is kept — it is a
# valid, correctly-signed slow zone any future scenario can place — but no world
# ships it today. The operations interrupt vocabulary it was built for is retired
# in #1166.
#
# The Falling Skyway storm is authored as REGION TEMPLATES spawned and retired
# on a schedule rather than as new hazard code, and this is the piece of it that
# external operations read. Deliberately generic: any scenario that wants
# "everything out here is harder" places one.
#
# WHAT IT IS NOT is as load-bearing as what it is. There is no `damage_zone`
# here. A band that hurt the ship as well would make every test of the slow rule
# also a test of the damage rule, and — more to the point — the storm's design
# is a SLOW BURN: an information hazard and a tax on time, with the hull damage
# authored separately where a scenario wants it. A crew flying through this one
# loses minutes, not hull.
#
# `slow_zone` is what an operation's `[[operations.capability.interrupt]]` rule
# names with `region_effect = "slow_zone"`. The rule and the rate live on the
# CAPABILITY, not here: the same band stretches a tow and stops a field-repair
# if that is what the designer authored, because how bad a storm is for a
# particular job is a judgement about the job.
#
# `radar_dampening` rides along because a storm you cannot see through is the
# same storm. It costs an operation nothing unless a capability authors a rule
# naming it. Its sign is not a taste call and is documented at the block itself.

tags = ["region", "storm", "slow_zone"]

[radar_appearance]
region_colour = [0.85, 0.55, 0.2]

[shape]
type = "sphere"
radius = 400.0

[effects]

# The thrust/yaw numbers are the region system's own; an operation reads only
# that a slow zone is PRESENT, because "how much slower does this make the work"
# is the capability's rate to author and not the band's to impose. THE TWO
# MECHANISMS ARE SEPARATE and only one of them was ever wrong: the interrupt's
# `rate_percent = 50` on `probe_operations`' field-repair means half rate and
# always did, because a percentage is a percentage. These two are bonuses.
#
# HALF THE THRUST, and roughly three fifths the turn. Enough that a crew flying
# a band feel the front on the stick — a course change costs real seconds, and a
# job out here is one you committed to before you could see the far side.
#
# NEGATIVE, and that is not a typo — the same sign trap `[effects.radar_dampening]`
# below documents at length, on the field pair whose names read even harder as
# multipliers. `thrust_modifier` and `yaw_rate_modifier` are signed BONUSES on
# `ModifierSlot::MaxSpeed` and `ModifierSlot::MaxYawRate`
# (`modifiers::coordination::apply_region_effects`), not multipliers, and they
# reach the helm through PRD #117's two-sided formula in
# `modifiers::cache::ShipModifiers::rebuild_cache`:
#
#     bonus >= 0  ->  multiplier = 1 + bonus
#     bonus <  0  ->  multiplier = 1 / (1 + |bonus|)
#
# So the bonus that gives a wanted multiplier `m` is `-(1/m - 1)`:
#
#     thrust, m = 0.5   ->   1/0.5 = 2      ->   -(2 - 1)     = -1.0
#     yaw,    m = 0.6   ->   1/0.6 = 5/3    ->   -(5/3 - 1)   = -0.6666667
#
# THIS FILE SHIPPED WITH `0.5` AND `0.6` UNTIL THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THIS
# COMMENT. Read as multipliers they say "half thrust, three fifths yaw"; read as
# the signed bonuses the engine actually applies they said `1 + 0.5` and
# `1 + 0.6`, and a storm band made a ship HALF AGAIN AS FAST and much more
# agile than it is in clear space. A positive number on an effect called a SLOW
# ZONE is always wrong, and `regions::effects` and `regions::server` now each
# carry a guard that says so — one over the data, one through the engine.
#
# [ai] `-1.0` and `-0.6666667` are the values that reproduce this file's
# original authoring intent under the real formula. They are a correction, not a
# new tuning call, and the tuning itself is unratified. This band's job in
# `probe_operations` is unchanged either way: that world gates its packhorse
# field-repair on the slow zone being PRESENT, never on how slow it is — which
# is measurable rather than assumed, and is measured in the commit that made
# this change.
[effects.slow_zone]
thrust_modifier = -1.0
yaw_rate_modifier = -0.6666667

# The picture HALVES. Enough that a crew inside the band are working a smaller
# scope than the one they planned the job on; not enough that the scope goes
# dark, which reads as a broken console rather than as weather.
#
# NEGATIVE, and that is not a typo. `range_modifier` is a signed BONUS on
# `ModifierSlot::RadarRange` (`modifiers::coordination::apply_region_effects`),
# not a multiplier, and it reaches the radar through PRD #117's two-sided
# formula in `modifiers::cache::ShipModifiers::rebuild_cache`:
#
#     bonus >= 0  ->  multiplier = 1 + bonus
#     bonus <  0  ->  multiplier = 1 / (1 + |bonus|)
#
# So "half the scope" is the bonus that solves `1 / (1 + |b|) = 0.5`:
#
#     1 + |b| = 1 / 0.5 = 2   ->   |b| = 1.0   ->   range_modifier = -1.0
#
# On the Alliance cruiser that flies `probe_operations` and `probe_destroy` that
# is a weapons horizon of `50 x 0.5 = 25` units and a helm scope of
# `93.75 x 0.5 = 46.875` — a 400-unit band whose far side a ship inside it
# cannot see, which is the whole claim the header makes.
#
# THIS FILE SHIPPED WITH `0.5` UNTIL THE COMMIT THAT ADDED THIS COMMENT (found
# in #1037). Read as a multiplier it says "halve the radar"; read as the signed
# bonus the engine actually applies it said `1 + 0.5`, and a storm made the
# radar reach FIFTY PERCENT FURTHER. A positive number on a DAMPENING effect is
# always wrong, and `regions::effects`'s shipped-asset test now says so.
#
# [ai] `-1.0` is the value that reproduces this file's original authoring intent
# under the real formula. It is a correction, not a new tuning call, and the
# tuning itself is unratified.
[effects.radar_dampening]
range_modifier = -1.0
base_files.assets/entities/repair_tender.toml:
# Repair tender — the probe-world operator for external repair-team dispatch
# (issue #1161).
#
# A deliberately lean hull that exists to exercise ONE mechanism end to end: a
# `[repair]` block that gives it a single repair team and a
# `[repair.external_dispatch]` table carrying the reach a team can cross and the
# rate it works a target's condition track at. It is NOT a shipped combat hull
# and is not flown in any scenario — it is the fixture
# `assets/worlds/probe_external_repair.toml` puts a dispatch on, kept out of
# `alliance_destroyer.toml` on purpose so no shipped hull's folded state (and
# therefore no committed world's digest) moves for this slice. A shipped hull
# gains external dispatch in a later integration, not here.
#
# It flies nothing: the probe drives the operator's position and its Tactical
# lock from the test, and the dispatch/recall through the ordinary admitted-
# command path, so the tender needs no helm, weapons or AI policy of its own.
# It authors NO `[repair.selector]`, so `operate_repair_ai` never auto-dispatches
# its one team — the test is the only thing that moves it, which is what keeps
# the "own repairs slow" trade observable.

tags = ["ship"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"
mass = 9000.0

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 0.6
length = 1.5
# No helm capability, so per the movable/helm invariant this stays the
# static-terrain default; the probe moves the operator by writing ShipPhysics.
movable = false

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.3, 0.9, 0.5]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

# ── The one repair team + its external-dispatch reach ────────────────────────
# One team so the trade is crisp: dispatch it abroad and the hull's own
# damage-control sweep has nobody left. Travel is short so an internal dispatch
# lands within a tick of the test issuing it. Every number is authored (rule 11).
[repair]
repair_team_count = 1
travel_duration_secs = 0.2
repair_rate_hp_per_sec = 5.0

# The external-dispatch terms: how far a team can cross, and the condition
# points per second it raises the target's own track by while it works there.
[repair.external_dispatch]
range = 600.0
repair_rate = 20.0

# ── Engineering owns the ship-wide repair system ─────────────────────────────
# The `repair` system (engineering-owned like the destroyer's, issue #1013/#830)
# is what `DispatchExternalRepair` / `RecallExternalRepair` target and admission
# gates: backfill-rated, so with nobody at the console it is AI-controlled and
# the probe's `ai:` token is admitted — the same seam #1162's repair AI will use.
[[station]]
id = "engineering"
name = "Engineering"
description = "entity.repair_tender.station.engineering.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "ENG"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[system]]
id = "repair"
kind = "repair"
station = "engineering"

# A single damage entry so the tender carries a non-empty hull; nothing in the
# probe damages it — the "own repairs slow" trade is proved through the team
# availability answer, not through this bar.
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "repair"
max_hp = 100
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15
base_files.assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.tom:
# Civilian bulk hauler — the first hull to carry a `[civilian]` table
# (issue #1028).
#
# Deliberately generic rather than Falling-Skyway-specific: a hauler is
# something a scenario puts on a lane, talks to, and occasionally has to argue
# with, and the whole point of putting the route assignment and the compliance
# disposition on the ENTITY is that the next mission needing traffic does not
# re-derive the bookkeeping.
#
# What makes it civilian is what it does NOT have: no weapons, no Destroy
# doctrine, and a Captain policy that stands DOWN unconditionally rather than
# going to red alert. Its faction is Requiem, which is neutral to everyone, so
# it never becomes a target by accident.
#
# Its travel doctrine is not authored here at all. `[civilian] route` names a
# world `[[route]]`, and `civilian::tick_civilian_traffic` keeps a single
# `civilian-route` doctrine entry pointed at whatever the craft is currently
# trying to do — its lane, an ordered anchor, an ordered berth, or nothing when
# it has been told to hold. That entry is an ordinary authored directive and is
# flown by the ordinary NPC helm.

name = "entity.ship_civilian_hauler.name"
tags = ["ship", "npc", "civilian"]
faction = "dddddddd-4444-4444-8444-dddddddddddd"
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] Unratified — a bulk freighter,
# heavier than a combat courier despite carrying no weapons.
mass = 9000.0

# The fifteen ship-level AI declarations every hull with a `[behaviour]` block
# owes (PRD #774 US7). The Captain one is authored inline below instead, because
# a hauler's is the opposite of the shared fragment's.
includes = ["fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml"]

[target]
tags = ["ship"]
threat_level = "none"
description = "entity.ship_civilian_hauler.target.description"

[hull]
hull_integrity = 60.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 2.0
length = 6.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958).
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.55, 0.75, 0.45]
size = 4.0
icon = "ship"

[mesh]
# Shares the Dynasty courier hull with `ship_requiem_courier`: a civilian hauler
# is the same silhouette at this scale, and a new .glb for it would buy nothing.
model = "assets/models/dynasty_courier_recreated.glb"
shape = "cuboid"
size = [4.0, 1.5, 6.0]
colour = [0.55, 0.75, 0.45]

[comms]
range = 900.0

[helm_console]
# Slow. A hauler under way should be something a crew can catch, hail and argue
# with rather than something that outruns the conversation.
max_speed = 12.0
max_reverse_speed = 4.0
acceleration = 5.0
deceleration = 8.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.35
max_bank_deg = 5.0

[ai_profile]
aggression = 0.0
sensor_range = 200.0

# Reactor + battery, at the fleet baseline's own numbers. Authored HERE rather
# than taken from `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` even though the fragment
# carries an identical block: `capacity` is an authoring surface the spawner
# gates a capability on, and a shared AI-policy fragment must never be the thing
# that supplies one (`every_shipped_template_resolves_to_its_own_bytes`). The
# shed LADDER above it is still the fragment's, unchanged — a hauler manages a
# reactor exactly the way the fleet does.
[power]
capacity = 90
rates = [ 5, 4, 3, 2, -2, -5 ]
emergency_threshold = 22

# Civilian traffic (issue #1028). No `route` here on purpose: which lane a
# hauler flies is a fact about the mission that placed it, so a world authors it
# per instance with `overrides = { civilian = { route = "…" } }`. Everything
# else is the hull's own temperament, and this one is cooperative — a scenario
# that wants a difficult operator authors `[civilian.compliance]` on the
# instance, or on the faction.
[civilian]
route_priority = 60.0

[behaviour]
# No doctrine entries. A civilian's travel objective is installed and maintained
# by the traffic adapter; a standing `Reach` here would compete with it.
waypoint_arrival_radius = 20.0
nav_handoff_speed = 0.9

# Captain — a hauler stands down, always. Authored inline rather than composed,
# because every shared Captain fragment in the library raises alert on contact
# and that is precisely what a civilian does not do. This is a DECLARATION, not
# an omission: US7 asks that automation is never silently synthesised, and "this
# ship deliberately never goes to red alert" is a policy like any other.
[captain_console]

[captain_console.ai]

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false

# Every system is ownerless and `ai_only`, so the NPC spawn path puts each one
# under `ControlSource::Ai`.
[[system]]
id = "helm-thrust"
kind = "helm_thrust"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-steering"
kind = "helm_steering"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-impulse"
kind = "helm_impulse"
ai_only = true

# The navigation system is what makes a `dock` order flyable. A Dock directive
# resolves to a destination through `operate_navigation_ai`, which emits this
# hull's own anchored waypoint as an admitted command — so without a navigation
# system to admit it, the berth would resolve and the hauler would never set
# off. It is `ai_only` because nobody is ever seated here.
[[system]]
id = "navigation"
kind = "navigation"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "power-reactor"
kind = "power_reactor"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "power-battery"
kind = "power_battery"
ai_only = true
base_files.assets/entities/ship_harrow_cruiser.toml:
# Harrow Cruiser (Ironveil class) — the broadside orbit and its one
# interruption (issues #790, #791)
#
# The second hull whose HELM BEHAVIOUR is authored rather than inherited, and
# the opposite manoeuvre to the destroyer's.
#
#   acquire     ──(target visible, inside engage_range)──▶ orbit
#   orbit       ──(target lost)───────────────────────────▶ acquire
#   orbit       ──(arc facing us down AND a salvo LOADED
#                  AND the battery intact)────────────────▶ torpedo_run
#   torpedo_run ──(target lost)───────────────────────────▶ acquire
#   torpedo_run ──(arc back up AND no salvo committed)────▶ orbit
#   torpedo_run ──(tubes not loaded AND no salvo
#                  committed)────────────────────────────▶ orbit
#   torpedo_run ──(battery unusable AND no salvo
#                  committed)────────────────────────────▶ orbit
#
# Three states, and the third is the only thing that stops the circling. This
# hull has no break-off, no re-entry pivot and no escape leg: it circles, and it
# keeps circling for as long as there is something to circle. What makes that a
# fight rather than a stalemate is the ARMAMENT below.
#
# ## The one interruption: a shield opportunity (issue #791)
#
# The broadsides do not kill. They strip. A ship being circled by this hull is
# taking beam fire on whichever arc happens to face the ring, and sooner or later
# that arc collapses — and a collapsed arc passes damage straight through to the
# hull for the few seconds it takes to come back.
#
# That window is what the torpedoes are for, and the geometry of taking it is the
# exact opposite of the orbit's. The tubes are fixed and forward, on a 24-degree
# arc; the orbit deliberately holds the target ABEAM. So the cruiser cannot shoot
# through the gap and keep circling. It has to stop circling, cut thrust, and
# swing its bow onto the target — accepting, for the length of the phase, that it
# is presenting its nose to an enemy instead of raking it.
#
# Five properties of the phase are load-bearing and each is authored below:
#
# * it OPENS on the arc that faces THIS ship being down, resolved through the
#   target's own arc router — the same one the eventual torpedo hit goes through,
#   so the manoeuvre can never commit to an opportunity the shot cannot take;
# * it OPENS ONLY WITH A SALVO ACTUALLY LOADED, and only while the battery that
#   would fire it is intact. Those are two different readings and the doctrine
#   takes both. `tubes_full` is the launcher's own question — every tube at its
#   volley capacity right this second — and it has to be the entry question too,
#   because entering is what spends the broadside geometry the launch depends on;
#   `tubes_fillable` catches the slower failures beside it, a magazine emptied or
#   a tube shot out. The magazine is 8 rounds against a 4-round salvo, so this
#   hull gets two runs and no more, and the 18-second reload between them is time
#   it spends circling rather than pointing. Note where the second of those runs
#   fires from: a round is drawn from the magazine when it STARTS loading, so
#   after the second reload the hold reads zero with a full battery standing
#   ready, and the launcher must fire it anyway — emptiness stops the next load,
#   never the shot already in the tube;
# * it ABORTS the moment that arc comes back, if nothing has launched yet. A
#   cruiser that kept its bow on a recovered shield would be giving away the
#   broadside for nothing;
# * it COMMITS once a salvo is away. `torpedoes_in_flight` holds the phase open
#   even after the shield recovers, because a homing round still in the air is
#   worth tracking to the end, and because turning away mid-salvo is how a hull
#   ends up with its tubes empty and its beams off target at once. "Away" means
#   COMMITTED, not merely airborne: `volley_max = 2` fires as a burst, so half a
#   salvo is still sitting in the tube on `burst_interval_secs` while the first
#   half flies, and a reading that counted only the airborne rounds released the
#   hull between them — the back half then left the tubes in `orbit`, outside
#   their own 24-degree arc;
# * it ENDS ANYWAY, three ways, none of which the enemy has to co-operate with.
#   The tubes going empty and the rounds resolving is the ordinary one; the
#   battery becoming unusable — a tube shot out, which leaves the rounds sitting
#   in it and so is invisible to a loaded-count reading — is the second; losing
#   the target is the third. All three are drawn on the cruiser's own armament or
#   its own sensors rather than on the target's shields, because a target with no
#   shields at all (a station, a probe) never raises the arc that would otherwise
#   release the hull, and a manoeuvre whose only exit is something the ENEMY has
#   to do is not bounded at all.
#
# When the run is over the cruiser re-enters `orbit` — a genuinely re-entered
# state, which is what makes the host RE-DRAW the circulation direction from the
# seeded key. The second orbit is not necessarily the same way round as the
# first, and that is deliberate: a player who learns which way this ship circles
# should have to learn it again after every torpedo run.
#
# ## Why an orbit at all
#
# The shared `plan_helm_travel` Destroy arm (`helm_destroy`) brakes through a
# decel zone, parks at a fraction of weapons range and re-faces the target. That
# is a bow-on gunship posture: it presents the smallest silhouette and brings the
# forward arc to bear. A ship whose guns are on its BEAM wants the exact
# opposite — it wants to be side-on, and it wants to stay side-on while the
# target manoeuvres, which a station-keeper cannot do because "face the target"
# and "show the target your flank" are contradictory instructions.
#
# So Steering answers its channel with `hold_combat_orbit`: the host solves the
# TANGENT of a ring of `combat_orbit_range` around the target, bent toward or
# away from it in proportion to how wrong the current radius is. The result is
# continuous tangential travel (the broadsides stay on) that SPIRALS onto the
# ring from either side — inside it the tangent is rotated outward and the
# cruiser works its way out while still circling; outside it the tangent is
# rotated inward and the cruiser closes while still circling. It never stops and
# it never simply runs.
#
# The circulation direction — clockwise or anticlockwise — is drawn ONCE, on the
# tick the orbit state is entered, from a seeded (world, ship, system,
# transition, occurrence) key. So a replayed seed produces the same fight every
# time, two cruisers entering the same engagement do not mirror one another, and
# a player cannot learn "they always break left".
#
# ## Why the ring radius is AUTHORED and the destroyer's is not
#
# The destroyer's recovery ring is derived from the TARGET's own direct-fire
# reach plus a margin, because a standoff is a statement about the other ship's
# guns. This ring is a statement about THIS ship's guns: the cruiser wants its
# target inside its own beam envelope, which is a property of this file and is
# knowable when the file is written. `combat_orbit_range` is therefore a plain
# authored `param`, deliberately set inside `beam_range` so the target is under
# the broadsides for the whole orbit rather than only at the tangent point.
#
# ## Hazards do not break the orbit
#
# There is no transition anywhere below guarded on hazard urgency, collision
# proximity, or any other avoidance reading — and that absence is load-bearing.
# Avoidance already composes onto this leg two ways, both of them temporary and
# both of them outside the state machine: the shared repulsion steering is summed
# onto the orbit's own tangent inside the pure planner, and an IMMINENT collision
# temporarily overrides desired facing from the shared hazard force. Neither
# touches `memory(orbit_direction)` and neither is a state, so the detour
# evaporates the moment the hazard clears and the cruiser resumes the same
# circulation it was already flying. Adding a "dodging" state would have replaced
# that with a manoeuvre that has to be exited — and an exit is a place to get
# stuck.
#
# ## ARMAMENT: fore and aft, each 270 degrees
#
# Not port and starboard. A pair of 180-degree beam banks covers each side once
# and can only ever fire one of them at a target. This hull mounts its banks on
# the CENTRELINE — one forward, one aft — and gives each a 270-degree arc, so
# each bank's only blind spot is the 90-degree wedge directly behind it. The
# consequence is that everything abeam, to port or to starboard, is inside BOTH
# arcs at once, and a bearing broadside lights two beams rather than one.
#
# That is what makes a circling ship dangerous rather than merely evasive: the
# orbit holds the target abeam by construction, which is precisely where the
# overlap is. It is also why the arcs are 270 and not 360 — a ship that can shoot
# anywhere has no geometry to fly, and the whole doctrine would collapse back
# into station-keeping.
#
# A useful consequence for the torpedo phase (issue #791): 270 degrees means both
# banks still cover DEAD AHEAD, so swinging the bow onto a shield gap costs the
# cruiser none of its beam pressure. The phase gives up the double-broadside
# overlap for a few seconds; it does not give up the guns.

# ── Composed on the shared fragment library (issue #878) ──────────────────────
#
# The ring and its one interruption are no longer authored here. They are
# `fragments/ai/movement_broadside_orbit.toml` — the same file
# `alliance_cruiser.toml` flies — and this hull tunes it with THREE parameters
# (below the boost note). One library, player fleet and Harrow alike; the
# difference between them is a number, not a second copy of the machine.
#
# Order is significant: fragments merge in declared order and this file merges
# last, so the includer always wins. `movement_broadside_orbit.toml` is listed
# AFTER `fleet_baseline.toml` because it REPLACES the baseline's two travel axes.
#
# Still authored below: everything that makes this hull ITSELF — its banks, its
# two narrow bow tubes and their arc-aware launch doctrine, its stations and
# systems — plus the two ship-level declarations a Harrow deliberately does not
# share with the fleet: the stand-down `[captain_console.ai]` (#912) and
# `[power]` + `[power.ai_policy]`, re-authored whole because the baseline's
# `helm` rule gates its elevation on `red_alert` and a Harrow raises the alert
# only around combat, not for the whole transit, so inheriting the guard would
# pin the drive at 2 for exactly the leg that needs it (#923; corrected #955).
# `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` carries the fuller note on both.
includes = [
  "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
  "fragments/ai/movement_broadside_orbit.toml",
]

# ── Doctrine tuning: parameters only (issue #878) ─────────────────────────────
#
# The whole specialisation of the shared broadside-orbit doctrine. No rule, state
# or transition is restated: `param` is an ordinary TOML table and deep-merges,
# so naming one key retunes that threshold and leaves the machine alone. Three
# keys, restated on BOTH axes because Engines and Steering are two independent
# copies of one machine that agree by reading the same facts — a copy left on a
# class default would reach a different leg on the same tick.
#
# `press_posture = 0.0` — THE aggression knob, and the same lever as
# `min_alert_to_fire = 0` on the guns below. `posture` is host-seeded from this
# ship's own red alert (0 DEFENSIVE, 1 PRESSED); at the lowest rung the gate is
# open from the first tick and every break-off guard is unreachable, so the hull
# leaves `shadow` immediately, never returns, and flies exactly the
# acquire → orbit → torpedo_run ring it flew inline before it was composed
# (#790/#791). A Harrow has no bridge crew to call the alert and its captain
# policy (#912) stands it down out of combat, so a hull that waited for one would
# hold a standoff ring outside its own guns for ever. It changes no red-alert
# STATE — see `ship_harrow_warhawk.toml` for the fuller note.
#
# `torpedo_run_shield_gap = 1.0` — the Harrow's reading of when the ring is worth
# breaking, restored as a parameter. The class default (0.0) opens the bow hold
# on range and readiness alone, which is what the player cruiser measured best;
# this hull demands the striking arc actually be DOWN, and gets the matching exit
# when it comes back up, because bow-on it works one 270-degree bank instead of
# two and its rounds author `damage_shields = 0`. The fragment header carries the
# full argument for both readings.
#
# `torpedo_run_range` — NOT overridden any more, so this hull takes the class
# default of 50. It used to author 220, this hull's own `engage_range`, i.e.
# non-binding, and the argument for that is worth keeping because it is the thing
# that was wrong (issue #1243).
#
# The withdrawn reasoning ran: the class gate exists to stop the bow hold —
# flown at `torpedo_bearing_speed = 0.0`, so entering it cuts thrust — freezing
# the RUN-IN at whatever range the tubes happened to finish loading at; on a hull
# whose entry is range-and-readiness alone that is a real hazard and the player
# cruiser authors a tight 25; but on THIS hull the binding gate is
# `torpedo_run_shield_gap = 1.0`, so the run cannot open until the cruiser has
# already stripped the arc facing it, which it can only do from inside its own
# 55-unit beam envelope — the shot is therefore never a hopeful one and the range
# gate has nothing left to protect.
#
# Every step of that holds against a target WITH SHIELDS, and the conclusion
# fails against one without. `target_facing_shield_down` reads 1.0 — permanently
# — for a target that carries no `[shields]` block at all; its own doc says so
# ("a station, a probe, a hull authored without the block… there is genuinely no
# arc in the way and there never will be"). So against such a target the shield
# gate is open from the first tick, nothing had to be stripped, no beam envelope
# was ever entered, and the range gate is the ONLY thing left — set, on that
# reasoning, to 220.
#
# `combat_test.toml`'s Starbase Alpha (`station_axiom.toml`) is exactly that
# target, and the result was a hull frozen solid. It crossed 220 with a loaded
# salvo, opened the bow hold, cut thrust, and coasted to a stop ~211 units out —
# beyond the 200-unit acquisition band that world gives its raid, so it could not
# lock the thing it had stopped to shoot. It never fired; the leg's only armament
# exits (`tubes_full < 1`, `tubes_fillable < 1`) both need a round to have LEFT a
# tube; `press_posture = 0.0` makes the posture exit unreachable; the starbase
# stayed alive so `target_valid` held; and the shield exit (`< 1.0`) can never
# fire against a shieldless hull. Measured: 694 s of an 800 s run in
# `torpedo_run`, `shots_fired: {}`, zero damage in either direction — and one
# such straggler makes that world's `on_all_destroyed("hostiles", …)` victory
# unreachable for the rest of the run.
#
# 50 is the class default and needs no special pleading: the fragment sizes it
# against `combat_orbit_range`, and this hull's ring is 42 and settles at ~43.5,
# so the bow hold opens just outside the ring it is breaking — the same shape
# `alliance_cruiser.toml` authors with 22/25. It is inside every envelope this
# hull has (beams 55, torpedo reach `speed 45` x `lifespan 6` = 270), so a hull
# that stops to shoot can always see what it stopped for.
#
# What this gives up is the "opportunities the hull used to take whenever the
# settled ring sat wide of the number" the old note claimed. Against a shielded
# target those are opportunities from inside the beam envelope anyway, so 50
# covers them; against a shieldless one they were never opportunities, because
# the gap was not something this hull had opened.
[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0
torpedo_run_shield_gap = 1.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0
torpedo_run_shield_gap = 1.0

# ── Weapons ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The pair the whole doctrine exists to point: centreline fore and aft, 270
# degrees each, so their arcs overlap across both beams. See the header.
#
# `auto_arc_deg` matches `fire_arc_deg` deliberately. On hulls where the two
# differ, the narrower auto arc is a "do not open fire at the very edge of the
# envelope" rule; here the edge of the envelope IS the doctrine — the overlap
# region a broadside orbit lives in reaches to 135 degrees off each bank's
# facing, so narrowing the auto arc would switch off exactly the double
# broadside this hull is built around.
[weapons_console]

# ── The BESPOKE weapons doctrine: tubes first into a gap (issue #956) ─────────
#
# The one hull in the fleet that departs from the baseline order in
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`, and it is the issue's own worked example:
# **torpedoes when the target's shields are down.**
#
# `arc_bearing_first` is what Weapons asks Helm to turn for, and it carries TWO
# rules on the same channel rather than one, which is the whole doctrine:
#
# * priority 10 — while the arc a round from this ship would strike is not
#   blocking (`target_facing_shields <= 0`, the same per-arc HP reading the bow
#   tubes' own launch guard is written against), the family worth turning for is
#   the TUBES. They are 24-degree bow cones; nothing but a deliberate turn ever
#   puts them on a target, and a gap in a screen does not stay open.
# * priority 0 — otherwise the fleet baseline: present the beams. Their 270
#   degree arcs almost always bear anyway, so in practice this rank is quiet and
#   the ship keeps flying its ring.
#
# Rank two carries the same pair, one place down: the beams while the gap is
# open, the fleet's blasters otherwise. Rank three is the baseline's, untouched.
# So the order resolves to
#
#     screen down  ⇒  [torpedoes, phasers]      (rank three repeats the tubes,
#                                                and the host drops repeats)
#     screen up    ⇒  [phasers, blasters, torpedoes]   — the fleet baseline,
#                                                exactly, term for term.
#
# That second line is the point of authoring it this way rather than reordering
# the ranks outright: when the gap closes, the hull is flying the fleet's own
# doctrine again, not a third order nobody wrote down.
#
# This pairs with — and does not duplicate — the manoeuvre half in
# `fragments/ai/movement_broadside_orbit.toml`, whose `torpedo_run_shield_gap`
# breaks the ring on the same reading. That leg decides where the HULL goes;
# this decides which gun Weapons asks Helm to present when it cannot bear.

[weapons_console.ai]

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "arc_bearing_first"
when = "fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0"
verb = "bring_torpedoes_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_first"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_phasers_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "arc_bearing_second"
when = "fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0"
verb = "bring_phasers_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_second"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_blasters_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_third"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_torpedoes_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than

  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]

# ── Torpedoes: the shield opportunity (issue #791) ────────────────────────────
#
# #790 shipped this hull with no `[torpedoes]` table at all, on the reasoning
# that "a ship that never presents its bow to the enemy has nothing to launch a
# fixed forward tube at". #791 changes the premise rather than the reasoning: the
# cruiser now DOES present its bow, once, deliberately, for the few seconds an
# arc it has just stripped is down. See the header.
#
# The loadout is authored around that single use and would be poor for anything
# else, which is the point:
#
# * `damage_shields = 0`. These rounds are not a way through a shield, they are
#   what goes through the hole the beams made. A shot that arrives after the arc
#   is back does nothing at all — which is the cost of a phase entered too early,
#   and the reason the abort transition exists.
#
#   That sentence was ASPIRATIONAL when it was written and is now literal
#   (issue #929). Until #929's second pass `damage_hull` bypassed the shield
#   system unconditionally, so a round arriving at a recovered arc still landed
#   all 34 of its points and this bullet described a cost the hull never paid. A
#   round now meets the ONE arc it flew into and that arc's own reading picks the
#   payload: `damage_shields`, i.e. nothing, if the arc is up; `damage_hull = 34`
#   whole on the plating if it is down. Neither number moved and the doctrine
#   around them did not either — the simulation caught up with what this file
#   already claimed.
# * a short `lifespan` and a low `turn_rate_deg_per_sec`. Barely homing: the
#   bow-on line-up is what aims them, not the seeker. It is also what makes
#   "every projectile has hit, missed or EXPIRED" a state the phase actually
#   reaches within a few seconds rather than a theoretical one.
# * `load_time` far longer than the phase. The tubes cannot be refilled inside
#   one opportunity, so the cruiser gets one salvo per shield gap and then goes
#   back to stripping the next arc. That, not a cooldown, is what stops the
#   doctrine collapsing into "hold the bow on and empty the magazine".
[torpedoes]
count = 8
burst_interval_secs = 0.35
damage_hull = 34
damage_shields = 0
speed = 45.0
turn_rate_deg_per_sec = 25.0
lifespan = 6.0
load_time = 9.0
detonation_radius = 4.0

# TWO forward tubes, not one, and that is what makes `fact(tubes_full)` mean
# something: with a single tube "every tube is full" would be indistinguishable
# from "this tube is full" and the salvo doctrine would be untestable content.
#
# The 24-degree arc is the other half of the phase's premise. It is narrow enough
# that the orbit — which holds the target abeam by construction — can never
# satisfy it, so the cruiser genuinely has to break off and point. Widen it and
# the manoeuvre becomes decoration.
[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "bow_port"
facing_deg = 0.0
fire_arc_deg = 24.0
volley_max = 2
ai_target_count = 2

  # The per-tube doctrine (issue #791) — the first hull in the set to author one.
  #
  # LOAD is unconditional: the tubes are kept full between opportunities, because
  # a tube that starts loading when the shield goes down has already missed the
  # window (`load_time` is 9 s; the window is a few).
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  # LAUNCH takes all three of AC2's conditions, continuously, every tick:
  #
  # * `tubes_full` — every tube at its `volley_max`. The whole salvo goes at
  #   once or none of it does; a dribble of single rounds into a gap that is
  #   closing is how the magazine empties for nothing.
  # * `target_facing_shields <= 0` — the striking ARC is not blocking. An HP
  #   reading, not a boolean, and per-arc rather than ship-wide: the host
  #   resolves it through the target's own arc router, so this gate and the
  #   eventual hit agree about which arc is in the way.
  # * `in_arc` — the target is inside THIS tube's 24-degree cone. It is the
  #   Steering phase above that puts it there, and this guard is what makes the
  #   two halves of the manoeuvre one thing rather than two hopeful ones.
  #
  # Any of the three going false holds fire on the next tick without the tube
  # needing to be told the opportunity is over.
  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(tubes_full) > 0 and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0 and fact(in_arc) > 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"

[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "bow_starboard"
facing_deg = 0.0
fire_arc_deg = 24.0
volley_max = 2
ai_target_count = 2

  # Identical doctrine to `bow_port`: the tubes fire as one salvo, so they must
  # answer their channels the same way. Authored per tube rather than shared
  # because a tube's policy is a property of the tube — a later refit that gives
  # one of them a different arc would change its answer and not the other's.
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(tubes_full) > 0 and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0 and fact(in_arc) > 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"

[comms]

[ai_profile]

# Captain — raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within
# `combat_window_secs`, otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so
# a designer retunes the ship's nerve without recompiling.
[captain_console.ai]
param = { combat_window_secs = 10.0 }

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(secs_since_combat) < param(combat_window_secs)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false

# Torpedo magazine — two axes on one authored block.
#
# GRANT: always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The offline +
# non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this rule is the authored arbiter
# layered on top, and it is where a hull would ration rounds between its tubes.
#
# CONSERVATION (issue #943): whether a launch the ship has already authorised may
# SPEND its round here, or should hold it for later in the mission. Resolved
# inside `handle_fire_torpedo`, the one consumer of an admitted `FireTorpedo`, so
# a human Tactical operator and an AI backfill meet this guard identically — the
# per-tube `torpedo_launch` doctrine gates only the AI, and a gate that
# constrains NPCs alone is how a player empties the whole magazine into wave one.
#
# `rounds_per_threat` is a host reading, not an authored number: every round the
# ship still HAS — the magazine PLUS whatever is already parked in the tubes —
# divided by the mission threat still ahead, which the SCENARIO publishes as the
# world counter `mission_threat_remaining`. A world that publishes none leaves
# the ratio unbounded and this rule always fires, because pacing is something a
# mission asks for and never something a hull decides for itself.
#
# `min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5` reads "keep one round for every TWO things still
# coming". Before retuning it, understand what kind of gate it is: a ONE-WAY
# LATCH. `rounds_aboard` only ever FALLS inside a mission, and the threat count
# only falls when something DIES — so a hull that dips under its own reserve
# stops firing, stops killing the thing that would bring the count down, and
# never climbs back over the line. Whatever is authored here is not a soft
# brake. It is a floor the ship must never be pushed below mid-mission.
#
# 0.5 is chosen for the margin it leaves, not for a tidy identity:
#
#   * The middle of the mission stays open. Over every position combat_test can
#     put this hull in while it still carries half its payload or more, the
#     reserve clears at least 4 rounds — two full volleys — against the wave in
#     front of it. A wave that survives one volley is a wave that never dies,
#     and a wave that never dies freezes the threat count and the latch with it.
#   * Nothing is stranded. At the last unit of threat the floor is half a round,
#     so anything still aboard clears the gate and can be spent on the last
#     fight. A reserve measured against the magazine COUNTER rather than the
#     rounds aboard strands the parked volley whatever this number is, because
#     the counter is debited the moment a tube starts loading.
#
# What it trades away is the front of the mission. The floor at eight published
# waves is 4 rounds rather than 8, so an engagement lasting as long as the hull
# is willing to keep shooting may now take 10 of the 12 rounds while the whole
# schedule is still published, where 1.0 capped it at 6. That ceiling is a
# licence rather than a forecast — flown for real the destroyer spends 6 across
# that stretch either way, because the engagement ends before the gate does —
# but it is what 0.5 permits, and it is the price of the margin above.
#
# The tidy identity is what 1.0 bought (issue #943): the reserve came to exactly
# one round at the last unit of threat, so on paper nothing could ever be
# stranded. It shipped with ZERO margin and it broke. Against the old asteroid
# layout the destroyer bottomed out at exactly 7 rounds against 7 remaining
# waves — a ratio of exactly 1.0, the last reading the gate still passes. #946
# reshuffled which rock lands in which cell (same radii, same split), that moved
# the engagement by one round, the ratio fell under, the latch shut, and
# combat_test's wave chain stalled at wave 2 with the hull holding rounds it
# would never fire.
#
# All of it is measured, not asserted by hand.
# `the_shipped_destroyer_spends_its_whole_payload_across_the_eight_wave_mission`
# (`src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs`) walks this doctrine through the real
# torpedo system over the world's whole authored schedule, INCLUDING a wave that
# outlives the engagement fought against it, and states the latch directly on
# the doctrine.
# `combat_test_paces_the_player_magazine_against_the_whole_eight_wave_threat`
# (`tests/headless_runner.rs`) flies it for real and prints the magazine's
# shape bucketed by remaining threat, (entered, lowest) per bucket:
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 2), 6: (2, 2), 5: (2, 2)}. Read a bucket as a STRETCH OF
# THE MISSION rather than as one engagement — since #960 a wave arrives on its
# own clock whether or not the last one is dead, so the top bucket spans wave 1
# and the opening of wave 2, and bottoms lower than the death-gated chain used
# to show. Ten of the twelve rounds go while six or more waves are still
# published; the last two then sit under the floor (2/6 and 2/5 are both below
# 0.5) until the count reaches 4. At 1.0 the same run reads
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 6)} and stops there: the latch shuts the moment wave 1
# dies, and wave 2 never does.
#
# `sole_objective_count = 1` is the carve-out, and it counts NAMED Destroy
# targets rather than doctrine entries. A world's `spawn_entity` override
# APPENDS its brief to the template's standing orders — doctrine reconciles by
# `id`, and an instance override may not remove what the template authored — so
# combat_test's raid cruisers carry their template's untargeted
# `destroy-hostiles` alongside the `assault-starbase` the world hands them: two
# entries, one named target, one engagement they will not outlive. Those spend
# freely. A hull whose brief names no target reads 0 and paces — which is the
# player's destroyer, the ship #943 was filed about.
[torpedoes.ai]
param = { min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5, sole_objective_count = 1.0 }

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_magazine_grant"
when = "true"
verb = "grant_torpedo_round"

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_conservation"
when = "fact(targeted_objective_count) == param(sole_objective_count) or fact(rounds_per_threat) >= param(min_rounds_per_threat)"
verb = "release_torpedo"

# Reactor + battery. Transcribed from `PowerConfig::default()`, which is what
# this hull ran on before it declared the section: authoring
# `[power.ai_policy]` cannot be done without bringing `[power]` into existence,
# and the three fields are required, so they are written out at exactly the
# values the Rust default supplied.
[power]
capacity = 100.0
rates = [ 6, 5, 4, 2, -2, -6 ]
emergency_threshold = 25.0

# The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003), the same numbers the fleet
# baseline authors — see `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`'s param note for the
# full reasoning. Each channel authors three rules: HOLD (priority 15), ELEVATE
# (10), and the `priority = 0` BASELINE at level 2 that takes the channel back
# when neither of the others fires. That fallback IS the shed; there is no
# demote rule and no ship-wide total rule (`shields` never bids, so it is
# reserved at its commanded 2).
#
# Each channel carries TWO floors and the gap between them is the point: the
# channel sheds below `min_reserve_*` and may not rise again until the charge is
# back over the higher `min_restore_*`. With one floor per channel the shed and
# the re-elevate would sit on the same number, and the AI would flip that
# channel on every tick the charge rested there. `fact(power_<group>)` — the
# channel's CURRENT level — is what lets the hold rule tell "already up" from
# "climbing back", so the hysteresis needs no policy state.
#
# A FALLING battery at combat stations under thrust (helm's elevate needs the
# thrust, weapons' needs the alert — a Harrow drops the `red_alert` clause from
# its helm rules, see the note on `includes` at the top of this file):
#
#   >= 50   helm 3 / weapons 3 / shields 2 = 8 — the steepest drain in `rates`
#   25..50  helm sheds  => total 7 — a slow drain (-2/s here)
#   < 25    weapons too => total 6 — POSITIVE (+2/s), so the reserve refills
#
# A RISING one climbs the same steps at 35 (weapons) and 60 (helm), so the
# charge oscillates across the 25–35 band and — with the reactor undamaged —
# never reaches 0, which is where `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to 1 and
# locks the reactor until `emergency_threshold` above is back. Under thrust with
# the alert DOWN a Harrow's ordinary transit rests at total 7 rather than 6, and
# the 50 step turns even that around.
#
# The hold rules carry the SAME trigger clause as the elevate they sit above —
# helm's thrust, weapons' red alert — not only the shed floor, and that is
# deliberate: one tick with the trigger false sheds the channel exactly as a
# battery breach would, and it cannot climb back on the trigger returning alone
# while the charge is under the restore floor — the elevate rule that would
# re-raise it is gated on the RESTORE floor, not the shed one. A one-way
# ratchet on trigger flap for as long as the reserve is in the band — elevated
# posture belongs to combat stations, not to a throttle or an alert that
# blinked for a single tick.
#
# AI-shed only: `handle_power_messages` never reads `battery_pct`, so a human
# Power officer pushes straight past all four floors. Out of scope in the other
# direction: a Disabled or Destroyed reactor rates `operate_ai = false`, so the
# AI stops operating power altogether while the reactor keeps integrating at the
# last commanded total — no floor reaches that case.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair, the mirror of the battery pair one axis over: elevate at
# 0.7, release at 0.6. Without it a throttle DWELLING near the single threshold
# strobes helm 3<->2 at the AI tick rate, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 MaxSpeed swing --
# a ship thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn. [ai] The
# ratifiable quantity is the BAND WIDTH (0.1), not either endpoint. See
# fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml for the full note and the measurement.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's shed/restore pair: the first point the ship gives back, and the higher
# charge it takes the point again at.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair, the lower step of the ladder. 25 sheds to the sustainable total
# while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand; the 10 this shipped with
# before issue #1003 shed with barely a tenth of it left.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm — HOLD (already at 3 and still above the shed floor), then ELEVATE
# (climbing back past the restore floor), then the baseline.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons — the rung the battery actually oscillates on, and the last elevation
# the ship gives up.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/ship_harrow_destroyer.to:
# Harrow Destroyer — the fly-through attack pass (issue #883)
#
# The first hull whose HELM BEHAVIOUR is authored rather than inherited. Every
# other NPC flies the shared `plan_helm_travel` doctrine, whose Destroy arm
# (`helm_destroy`) is a brake-and-orbit station-keeper: close, decelerate
# through a decel zone, park at 80% of weapons range and re-face the target so
# the forward arc bears. That is a perfectly good gunship and a terrible
# interceptor.
#
# This hull does the opposite. It runs a three-state machine on the #882
# stateful policy spine — independently on Engines, on Steering and on Boost —
# that flies a classic strafing pass:
#
#   acquire  ──(target inside commit_range)──▶  inbound
#   inbound  ──(closest approach detected)───▶  escape
#   escape   ──(dwell done, shields intact)──▶  acquire
#   escape   ──(dwell done, shields down, escape WORKED)─▶  recover
#   escape   ──(dwell done, shields down, escape FAILED)─▶  pressed_pivot
#   recover  ──(shields back AND distance held)▶ reenter
#   reenter  ──(pivot complete)──────────────▶  acquire
#   pressed_pivot ──(pivot dwell done)───────▶  pressed_pass
#   pressed_pass  ──(closest approach, short)─▶ escape
#
# * INBOUND is flown at a flat, normal approach throttle, with Steering
#   re-solving the facing against the target's CURRENT position every tick — the
#   target moves, so the tracking must too. Nothing brakes.
# * CLOSEST APPROACH is detected from the closing rate crossing from + to −,
#   confirmed against the running minimum range the host folds into private
#   memory. One tick of retention is exactly what a "the gap stopped shrinking"
#   test needs and exactly what no single-tick fact can express.
# * ESCAPE closes the facing solution: Steering switches to the second yaw mode
#   verb, `hold_committed_heading`, and flies the heading the host froze at the
#   merge. Engines stay on full escape throttle and Boost lights for the
#   authored window. The target can turn, run, or die — the escape does not care.
# * RECOVERY (issue #788) is what the escape hands off to when the pass cost the
#   destroyer its shields. Since #788 a collapsed shield comes back EMPTY and
#   climbs at its authored regen rate, so "my shields are down" is now a state
#   with a duration, and flying a second pass through it is how this hull dies.
#   At the end of the escape dwell the machine therefore asks one question — are
#   my shields effectively gone? — and if so breaks off to a standoff ORBIT
#   instead of turning back in.
#
#   The orbit's radius is NOT authored: it is the TARGET's own longest usable
#   direct-fire range plus `safe_range_margin`. A destroyer standing off a
#   short-ranged blaster boat has no business sitting where it would have to sit
#   against a beam cruiser, and neither number is knowable when this file is
#   written. The circulation direction is drawn once per recovery from a seeded
#   (world, ship, system, transition, occurrence) key, so a replayed seed breaks
#   the same way every time while two destroyers breaking off together do not
#   mirror one another.
#
#   The orbit SPIRALS: the host flies a tangent of the ring bent toward or away
#   from the target in proportion to the radial error, so a destroyer inside the
#   ring works its way out while still circling, and one that has over-run works
#   its way back in rather than running to the edge of the map. It never stops
#   and it never simply retreats.
# * RE-ENTRY needs BOTH halves and will not take one: shields back to
#   `reentry_shield_fraction`, AND the safe distance actually HELD across the
#   whole `safe_distance_window_ticks` history window. One tick at range is not a
#   maintained standoff, and full shields while still being shot at is not a
#   recovery. When both are true the destroyer cuts thrust (`reengage_speed = 0`),
#   pivots onto the target with the drive cold, and starts an ordinary
#   normal-speed pass — no boost, because boost is the escape's accelerant and
#   this is an approach.
# * PRESSED (issue #789) is what happens when the recovery above is not on
#   offer, because the player will not let it be. Standing off needs the
#   destroyer to actually GET away first, and against an aggressive opponent who
#   simply follows it out, the escape leg ends with the hull still inside the
#   other ship's guns and no further from them than when it started. Breaking
#   off then is not a recovery, it is a slow death at a fixed range.
#
#   So at the end of every escape the machine asks a second question after the
#   shield one: did that escape actually WORK? The answer is a trend, not a
#   level — the net separation gained across the `pressed_window_ticks` history
#   window — and it is asked only while still inside the target's own
#   direct-fire reach, because distance that does not matter is not distance
#   worth measuring. Gained less than `pressed_min_progress` while still under
#   the guns, and the destroyer stops trying to leave.
#
#   What it does instead is fight at the range it is stuck at. It abandons the
#   standoff ring and the `reentry_shield_fraction` threshold outright — both
#   are things you wait for, and waiting is what is killing it — and instead
#   BOOSTS a thrust-cut pivot (boost multiplies `max_yaw_rate`, so the drive is
#   spent on turning authority rather than on a run it cannot win), then makes a
#   short normal-speed attack pass. The pass breaks off on its own, smaller
#   `pressed_closest_approach_hysteresis`: it is a jab, not a run-in from range.
#
#   Every short pass ends in the ordinary `escape` state, so every one of them is
#   another honest attempt to get out, and the moment one of them opens real
#   distance the machine drops straight back into the recovery doctrine above.
#   The pressed loop is a response to being pinned, not a mode the hull has to be
#   talked out of.
#
# Shared hazard avoidance still bends the escape (it is a steering force folded
# into the same pure arm), and bending it changes no pass state at all. It bends
# the recovery orbit the same way, for the same reason.
#
# ARMAMENT: forward blasters, and deliberately NO torpedoes. A ship that crosses
# the merge at full throttle has a fraction of a second of firing solution;
# fixed forward blasters are the weapon that suits it, and a torpedo magazine it
# could never bring to bear would be dead tonnage. The absence is load-bearing
# content, pinned by a parse test.

# ── Composed on the shared fragment library (issue #878) ──────────────────────
#
# The three-axis machine described above is no longer authored here. It is
# `fragments/ai/movement_attack_pass.toml` — the same file `alliance_destroyer.toml`
# flies — and this hull tunes it by PARAMETER alone (see "Doctrine tuning"
# below). The fragment was this hull's descendant and is now its source: #875
# lifted the pass out of it, and #878 gave the fragment the pressed short-pass
# loop (#789) as an opt-in leg so the last thing that was only ever authored here
# belongs to the library too.
#
# Order is significant: fragments merge in declared order and this file merges
# last, so the includer always wins. `movement_attack_pass.toml` is listed AFTER
# `fleet_baseline.toml` because it REPLACES the baseline's three travel axes.
#
# Still authored below: everything that makes this hull ITSELF — its blaster
# pair, its mandatory boost drive, its stations and systems, its doctrine — plus
# the two ship-level declarations a Harrow deliberately does not share with the
# fleet: the stand-down `[captain_console.ai]` (#912) and `[power]` +
# `[power.ai_policy]`, re-authored whole because the baseline's `helm` rule
# gates its elevation on `red_alert` and a Harrow raises the alert only around
# combat, not for the whole transit, so inheriting the guard would pin the
# drive at 2 for exactly the leg that needs it (#923; corrected #955).
# `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` carries the fuller note on both.
includes = [
  "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
  "fragments/ai/movement_attack_pass.toml",
]

name = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.name"
display_name = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.display_name"
class = "destroyer"  # [ai] picker badge / scan subtitle
tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"]
faction = "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc"
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] Unratified — a lean destroyer
# weight, tuned for its fly-through attack-pass doctrine.
mass = 13000.0

[target]
tags = ["ship"]
threat_level = "high"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.target.description"

# The lightest hull that still fights the ladder: it trades staying power for
# the speed and turn rate the pass depends on.
#
# 900 -> 200 (#915 tuning pass). 900 was an outlier against this hull's own
# class ladder — patrol 120, warhawk 280, cruiser 420 — and it made the demo's
# mirror duel arithmetically unwinnable: the Alliance destroyer lands ~285 hull
# damage per 120 s, so a 900-point pool needs over three times the sim budget
# to burn through. Five seeds produced five identical draws because of it.
[hull]
hull_integrity = 200.0

# Single omni arc, as on every other NPC hull: NPCs have no `[shields]` station,
# so the auto-generated `[[system]]` entry is ownerless and `ai_only`.
#
# `regen_per_sec` is load-bearing for the recovery doctrine since issue #788: a
# collapsed facing now comes back at ZERO and climbs at this rate, so this is
# what sets how long a broken-off destroyer spends on its standoff ring. At 4/s
# a collapsed 40-point arc reaches the authored 75% re-entry threshold about 7.5
# seconds after the offline delay expires.
[[shield_arc]]
id = "all"
label = "shield_arc.all.label"
center_deg = 0
width_deg = 360
max_hp = 40
regen_per_sec = 4.0
offline_duration = 6.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 3.0
length = 9.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.95, 0.45, 0.1]
size = 9.0
icon = "destroyer"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/dynasty_destroyer_recreated.glb"
shape = "cuboid"
size = [6.0, 2.5, 12.0]
colour = [0.95, 0.45, 0.1]

# Fast and agile. `max_speed` is what the seeded `speed_fraction` fact is
# measured against, and `max_yaw_rate` is what makes continuous target tracking
# on the inbound leg actually converge before the merge.
[helm_console]
max_speed = 16.0
max_reverse_speed = 8.0
impulse_speed_multiplier = 6
acceleration = 9.0
deceleration = 12.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.55
# Low-speed turn trade, the Harrow light-hull figure (x1.3 at rest). Lower
# than the Alliance destroyer's 0.5: the Harrow already out-turns it flat
# out, and matching the bonus would hand it both ends of the trade.
low_speed_turn_boost = 0.3
max_bank_deg = 22.0

[helm_console.engine_pfx]
color = [ 1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 0.68 ]
markers = [ "engine_port", "engine_starboard" ]
trail_lifetime_secs = 0.65

# MANDATORY for this hull, not decoration: the spawner only inserts an ENABLED
# `BoostConfigResource` when `[helm_console.boost]` is authored, and
# `ai_helm_boost` returns immediately without one. The escape leg's boost is the
# whole back half of the doctrine, so omitting this block would silently produce
# a destroyer that makes the pass and then dawdles away from it.
[helm_console.boost]
multiplier = 2.4
# Above 1.0 since issue #789, and load-bearing: the drive multiplies
# `max_yaw_rate` as well as speed, and the pressed doctrine spends it on a
# thrust-cut pivot rather than on a run. A pinned destroyer's scarcest resource
# is how fast it can bring the bow back round, so `1.8 * 0.55 = 0.99 rad/s`
# roughly halves the time that pivot takes. (It also makes the escape leg's own
# hazard avoidance bite harder, which is free — the escape flies a frozen
# heading inside a deadband, so it commands no yaw of its own to amplify.)
steering_multiplier = 1.8
active_duration = 5.0
# The battery drains partially and recharges whenever the drive is cold, so a
# pressed destroyer that spends `pressed_pivot_secs` of it on each pivot and
# recharges through each short pass runs a progressively tighter boost budget
# the longer it stays pinned. That is intended: being pressed should cost.
recharge_duration = 14.0

# ── Doctrine tuning: parameters only (issue #878) ─────────────────────────────
#
# The whole specialisation of the shared attack-pass doctrine, and the entire
# authoring interface this hull has to it. No rule, state or transition is
# restated: `param` is an ordinary TOML table and deep-merges, so naming one key
# retunes that threshold and leaves the machine alone.
#
# Every shared threshold is restated on ALL THREE axes because they are three
# INDEPENDENT copies of one machine that agree by reading the same facts — a copy
# left on a class default would reach `inbound` (or `pressed_pivot`) at a
# different moment from the other two and the axes would disagree about which leg
# they are flying.
#
# ── The aggression override ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `press_posture = 0.0` is THE knob, and the same lever as `min_alert_to_fire =
# 0` on the blasters below. `posture` is host-seeded on every helm policy host
# from this ship's own red alert — 0 DEFENSIVE, 1 PRESSED — and the class
# doctrine rests in `shadow`, a standoff ring outside the target's guns, until it
# reads at least `press_posture`. At the lowest rung `fact(posture) >=
# param(press_posture)` holds from the first tick and every `fact(posture) <
# param(press_posture)` break-off guard is unreachable, so the hull leaves
# `shadow` immediately, never returns, and flies exactly the
# acquire → inbound → escape → (pressed | recover → reenter) pass it flew inline
# before it was composed (#883/#788/#789).
#
# A Harrow has no bridge crew to call red alert and its captain policy (#912)
# stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull that waited for one would hold a
# ring outside its own 60-unit blasters for ever and never start the fight it
# exists to start. Note what the override deliberately does NOT do: it changes no
# red-alert STATE, so every fact, comms, repair and arc-overlay reading keyed on
# the alert is exactly where #912 left it, and the always-armed guard on the guns
# stays the load-bearing one.
#
# ── The pressed short-pass loop (#789) ───────────────────────────────────────
#
# Opted into by parameter, twice over, because the class default is OFF:
# `pressed_min_progress` is authored here at the real threshold (the fragment's
# default is a value no separation reading can fall below), and
# `pressed_window_ticks` is the fourth scalar the HOST gates the whole arm on,
# which the fragment deliberately does not author. This hull is the reason the
# leg exists and it is still the only hull that flies it.
[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0
# THE aggression knob of the pass itself: how close before the hull commits to a
# run. Far longer than the player destroyer's 120 — this hull is an interceptor
# with a 400-unit sensor range, and the run-in is the manoeuvre.
commit_range = 260.0
# A longer outward leg than the class default, to match.
escape_duration_secs = 7.0
# LOW: a scratched destroyer presses the attack and only a COLLAPSED one breaks
# off, where the class default (0.35) breaks off on a dent.
recover_shield_fraction = 0.15
# …and it re-enters sooner, at 75% rather than 85%.
reentry_shield_fraction = 0.75
# The pressed loop, ON. World units of separation the escape must have GAINED
# across `pressed_window_ticks` for it to count as working; deliberately below
# what an unboosted escape covers in that window (26 u/s over 1.467 s is 38.1
# units), so a destroyer that is merely coasting still reads as escaping and only
# one that is being MATCHED falls under it.
pressed_min_progress = 30.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0
commit_range = 260.0
escape_duration_secs = 7.0
recover_shield_fraction = 0.15
reentry_shield_fraction = 0.75
pressed_min_progress = 30.0
# Twice the class default's daylight beyond the target's own reach: a hull that
# breaks off at 26 u/s and re-enters at full throttle needs room to turn round in.
safe_range_margin = 120.0
# A touch faster on the ring, and a touch more slack folding the distance history
# — both because this hull holds a wider ring than the class default assumes.
orbit_speed = 0.7
safe_ring_tolerance = 25.0
# Length of the separation-PROGRESS history, in shared AI ticks, and the fourth
# name the HOST gates the pressed arm on: authoring it here is the second half of
# opting in. The trend is measured between the two ENDS of the window, so 45
# samples span 44 tick intervals — 1.467 seconds at the default 30 Hz helm
# cadence, not 1.5. Its own window with its own length, not a reuse of
# `safe_distance_window_ticks`: that one is tuned for "how long counts as a
# maintained standoff before re-entry", this one for "how long a failing escape
# takes to be obvious".
pressed_window_ticks = 45.0

[helm_console.boost_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0
commit_range = 260.0
escape_duration_secs = 7.0
recover_shield_fraction = 0.15
reentry_shield_fraction = 0.75
pressed_min_progress = 30.0
# Longer than the class default's 3.5, to match the longer escape: the drive
# still cuts before the dwell ends, so the hull coasts the last stretch and the
# battery is recharging before it turns back in.
escape_boost_secs = 4.0

# ── Weapons ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Forward blasters only. Field set copied from `alliance_destroyer.toml`'s
# forward banks, narrowed to a single pair firing dead ahead: a fly-through has
# a firing window measured in fractions of a second, and it happens straight off
# the bow.
[weapons_console]

[[weapons_console.blaster_banks]]
id = "harrow-lance-port"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 45
volley_count = 3
volley_interval_secs = 0.35
cooldown_secs = 4
projectile_speed = 70
collision_radius = 0.8
visual_scale = 0.5
damage = 12
shield_pierce = 0.15
range = 60

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Mirror of the phaser banks on the `blaster_fire`
  # channel: unconditional, with the host still enforcing availability,
  # cooldown, range, arc and target validity before the volley starts.
  [weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "blaster_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_blaster"

[[weapons_console.blaster_banks]]
id = "harrow-lance-starboard"
facing_deg = 0
fire_arc_deg = 45
volley_count = 3
volley_interval_secs = 0.35
cooldown_secs = 4
projectile_speed = 70
collision_radius = 0.8
visual_scale = 0.5
damage = 12
shield_pierce = 0.15
range = 60

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Mirror of the phaser banks on the `blaster_fire`
  # channel: unconditional, with the host still enforcing availability,
  # cooldown, range, arc and target validity before the volley starts.
  [weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "blaster_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_blaster"

# NOTE the deliberate absence: there is no `[torpedoes]` table, no
# `[[torpedoes.tubes]]`, and no torpedo `[[system]]` entry anywhere below. See
# the header. `harrow_destroyer_carries_forward_blasters_and_no_torpedoes` in
# `src/entities/config.rs` pins it, because an absence is exactly the kind of
# content that gets "helpfully" filled back in.

[comms]
range = 800.0

[ai_profile]
aggression = 1.0
# Wide enough that the destroyer sees its target well outside `commit_range` and
# spends real time in `acquire` lining the run up.
sensor_range = 400.0

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Destroy only. The doctrine entry supplies the objective the
# helm surfaces score; the *manoeuvre* is the policy machine's, not this
# section's — `target_speed`/`maintain_range` here only apply on the fallback
# path (no pass target visible), where ordinary doctrine travel resumes.
[behaviour]

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id             = "destroy-hostiles"
text           = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.behaviour.doctrine.destroy_hostiles.text"
directive_kind = "Destroy"
base_priority  = 40.0
target_speed   = 0.9
maintain_range = 40.0

# ── Stations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Crew stations (issue #871), mirroring `alliance_destroyer.toml` — the
# comparable player hull.
#
# THE FULLER NOTE. This lived in `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml` until issue #892 retired
# that hull as a display-name duplicate of this one; the other NPC hulls point
# here for it.
#
# NPC hulls used to declare no stations at all: every system was ownerless +
# `ai_only`, and the spawner set the lot to `ControlSource::Ai` by fiat. That
# made "NPC" a different SHAPE of ship from a player hull rather than the same
# ship with nobody aboard — a human could never be admitted to any of its
# systems, because admission resolves a human token through the station that
# owns the target system and there was no station to resolve to.
#
# Every seat boots on the implicit `Backfill` rating (see
# `ship::rating::seed_boot_ratings`), which automates every system the station
# owns — so an unmanned hull behaves exactly as it did when its systems were
# `ai_only`.
#
# Each seat authors a `console` path (issue #925), chosen by the fine systems it
# owns rather than by hull name. Every seat here owns exactly ONE console family
# (captain→captain, helm→helm, tactical→tactical, engineering→power), so each
# gets the FLAT plain-builder payload and reuses the matching flat
# `gui/battleship/*.html` console: captain, helm, tactical, and power (the
# Engineering seat owns only the power family, so it mounts battleship/power.html;
# the single-family dispatch in gui/console-state.js keys on the owned family, so
# the `engineering` seat id need not equal the family name). tactical mounts
# battleship/tactical.html, which renders this hull's blaster banks. The seat's
# owned families are a subset of its console's families, and the payload shape
# (flat vs system-keyed) must match — this is authored by hand rather than
# machine-checked today: tests/client/npc-hull-console-coverage.test.js, which
# used to assert it against the gui/console-families.js spec map, was deleted
# (642f544f) as content validation better suited to a load-time check than a
# vitest suite, and no such load-time check has replaced it yet. `manual_overview`
# is still omitted — the ship manual is published for the player's own hull.
#
# Only the AUTO-GENERATED systems stay ownerless + `ai_only`: the
# `shield-arc-all` system synthesised from `[[shield_arc]]` above (no shields
# station on this hull), which is the case `ai_only` exists for.

[[station]]
id = "captain"
name = "Captain"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.station.captain.description"
rank = "Cpt."
short_code = "CPT"
console = "gui/battleship/captain.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[station]]
id = "helm"
name = "Helm"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.station.helm.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "HLM"
console = "gui/battleship/helm.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[station]]
id = "tactical"
name = "Tactical"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.station.tactical.description"
rank = "Lt. Cmdr."
short_code = "TAC"
console = "gui/battleship/tactical.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[station]]
id = "engineering"
name = "Engineering"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_destroyer.station.engineering.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "ENG"
console = "gui/battleship/power.html"

[[station.rating]]

# ── Systems ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Red Alert authored explicitly (issue #871) rather than left to the #749
# ownerless provision, so the Captain seat owns it. Control source is unchanged:
# Backfill automates it.
[[system]]
id = "red-alert"
kind = "red_alert"
station = "captain"

[[system]]
id = "helm-thrust"
kind = "helm_thrust"

[[system]]
id = "helm-steering"
kind = "helm_steering"
station = "helm"

[[system]]
id = "helm-impulse"
kind = "helm_impulse"
station = "helm"

# Declared because the doctrine's escape leg engages it. `ai_helm_boost` gates on
# this system's control source AND on the `[helm_console.boost]` block above.
[[system]]
id = "helm-boost"
kind = "helm_boost"
station = "helm"

[[system]]
id = "helm-lateral-thrust"
kind = "lateral_thrust"
station = "helm"

# The Tactical radar (issue #871) — the system every player hull declares and no
# NPC hull did, which is what blocked #887 from routing AI target selection
# through admission.
[[system]]
id = "tactical-radar"
kind = "tactical_radar"
station = "tactical"

[[system]]
id = "blaster-harrow-lance-port"

[[system]]

[[system]]

[[system]]
