# Captain — raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within
# `combat_window_secs`, otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so
# a designer retunes the ship's nerve without recompiling.
[captain_console.ai]
param = { combat_window_secs = 10.0 }

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(secs_since_combat) < param(combat_window_secs)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false

# Reactor + battery. Transcribed from `PowerConfig::default()`, which is what
# this hull ran on before it declared the section: authoring
# `[power.ai_policy]` cannot be done without bringing `[power]` into existence,
# and the three fields are required, so they are written out at exactly the
# values the Rust default supplied.
[power]
capacity = 100.0
rates = [ 6, 5, 4, 2, -2, -6 ]
emergency_threshold = 25.0

# The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003), the same numbers the fleet
# baseline authors — see `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`'s param note for the
# full reasoning. Each channel authors three rules: HOLD (priority 15), ELEVATE
# (10), and the `priority = 0` BASELINE at level 2 that takes the channel back
# when neither of the others fires. That fallback IS the shed; there is no
# demote rule and no ship-wide total rule (`shields` never bids, so it is
# reserved at its commanded 2).
#
# Each channel carries TWO floors and the gap between them is the point: the
# channel sheds below `min_reserve_*` and may not rise again until the charge is
# back over the higher `min_restore_*`. With one floor per channel the shed and
# the re-elevate would sit on the same number, and the AI would flip that
# channel on every tick the charge rested there. `fact(power_<group>)` — the
# channel's CURRENT level — is what lets the hold rule tell "already up" from
# "climbing back", so the hysteresis needs no policy state.
#
# A FALLING battery at combat stations under thrust (helm's elevate needs the
# thrust, weapons' needs the alert — a Harrow drops the `red_alert` clause from
# its helm rules, see the note on `includes` at the top of this file):
#
#   >= 50   helm 3 / weapons 3 / shields 2 = 8 — the steepest drain in `rates`
#   25..50  helm sheds  => total 7 — a slow drain (-2/s here)
#   < 25    weapons too => total 6 — POSITIVE (+2/s), so the reserve refills
#
# A RISING one climbs the same steps at 35 (weapons) and 60 (helm), so the
# charge oscillates across the 25–35 band and — with the reactor undamaged —
# never reaches 0, which is where `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to 1 and
# locks the reactor until `emergency_threshold` above is back. Under thrust with
# the alert DOWN a Harrow's ordinary transit rests at total 7 rather than 6, and
# the 50 step turns even that around.
#
# The hold rules carry the SAME trigger clause as the elevate they sit above —
# helm's thrust, weapons' red alert — not only the shed floor, and that is
# deliberate: one tick with the trigger false sheds the channel exactly as a
# battery breach would, and it cannot climb back on the trigger returning alone
# while the charge is under the restore floor — the elevate rule that would
# re-raise it is gated on the RESTORE floor, not the shed one. A one-way
# ratchet on trigger flap for as long as the reserve is in the band — elevated
# posture belongs to combat stations, not to a throttle or an alert that
# blinked for a single tick.
#
# AI-shed only: `handle_power_messages` never reads `battery_pct`, so a human
# Power officer pushes straight past all four floors. Out of scope in the other
# direction: a Disabled or Destroyed reactor rates `operate_ai = false`, so the
# AI stops operating power altogether while the reactor keeps integrating at the
# last commanded total — no floor reaches that case.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair, the mirror of the battery pair one axis over: elevate at
# 0.7, release at 0.6. Without it a throttle DWELLING near the single threshold
# strobes helm 3<->2 at the AI tick rate, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 MaxSpeed swing --
# a ship thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn. [ai] The
# ratifiable quantity is the BAND WIDTH (0.1), not either endpoint. See
# fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml for the full note and the measurement.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's shed/restore pair: the first point the ship gives back, and the higher
# charge it takes the point again at.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair, the lower step of the ladder. 25 sheds to the sustainable total
# while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand; the 10 this shipped with
# before issue #1003 shed with barely a tenth of it left.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm — HOLD (already at 3 and still above the shed floor), then ELEVATE
# (climbing back past the restore floor), then the baseline.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons — the rung the battery actually oscillates on, and the last elevation
# the ship gives up.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml:
# Harrow Patrol Cruiser (Ironveil class)
#
# Medium-weight cruiser. Two phaser banks (port + starboard), shielded,
# fights to the death. (#790) Renamed from the bare "Harrow Cruiser":
# `ship_harrow_cruiser` now flies alongside it in the combat-test waves,
# and two hulls sharing a name on radar and target readouts is unreadable. (#474) Rebalanced for the combat-test scenario
# (#475) — gained weapons (previously had a `[behaviour]` block declaring
# `attacking` state but no `[weapons_console]`, so could not fire),
# gained `on_attacked → pursue` transition (mirrors the destroyer),
# gained a `[shields]` block, removed flee/warp_out from combat.

# ── Composed on the shared fragment library (issue #878) ──────────────────────
#
# This hull flies NO manoeuvre of its own — its Engines and Steering axes were
# byte-identical to the fleet's stateless defaults — so the whole of its
# ship-level AI declaration now comes from `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`:
# the six helm axes, Shields, Comms and the five target selectors. What is still
# authored below is only what makes this hull ITSELF: its guns, its stations and
# systems, its doctrine, and the two declarations a Harrow deliberately does not
# share with the fleet (see `BESPOKE_DOCTRINES` in
# `src/entities/authored_ai_pins.rs`):
#
#   * `[captain_console.ai]` — the stand-down captain (#912). A Harrow needs no
#     captain's permission to shoot, so it authors no first-contact rule. The
#     baseline deliberately carries no Captain policy at all, so nothing here is
#     an override.
#   * `[power]` + `[power.ai_policy]` — RE-AUTHORED WHOLE, and that is
#     load-bearing. The baseline gates its `helm` elevation on `red_alert`
#     because an Alliance hull cruises with the alert DOWN and its captain
#     raises it on first contact, so the guard confines the elevation to combat
#     without ever costing the drive a point in a fight.
#     That does not hold here, and the reason is this hull's own captain policy
#     below: it raises the alert ONLY inside `combat_window_secs` of the last
#     exchange of fire and stands it down otherwise. A patrol spends almost all
#     of its life in transit with the alert down, so inheriting the baseline's
#     guard would pin the drive at 2 for exactly the leg that needs it and
#     release it only once the shooting had already started. A rules array has
#     no stable identity and so replaces the baseline's wholesale; the reactor
#     scalars are re-authored beside it.
#     (#923 briefly gave the baseline a `sensors` channel, on the theory that
#     sensor power was weapon reach; #955 removed the range coupling instead, so
#     that channel and its `min_reserve_sensors` param are gone from the baseline
#     and nothing here has to work around them. #952 then retired the `sensors`
#     power group outright in favour of `shields`, which the baseline also gives
#     no channel — so the re-authored rules below still cover every channel the
#     fragment declares.)
includes = ["fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml"]

name = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.name"
display_name = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.display_name"
# [ai] Ironveil-class patrol cruiser — classed as a cruiser for the picker badge
# and scan subtitle.
class = "cruiser"
tags = ["ship", "npc", "comms_contact"]
faction = "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc"
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] Unratified — a medium-weight
# patrol cruiser, lighter than the combat-tuned Ironveil cruiser.
mass = 18000.0

[target]
tags = ["ship"]
threat_level = "medium"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.target.description"

# 120 -> 300 (#915 tuning pass), joining the cruiser on the ladder's middle
# rung. This roughly doubles the patrol's staying power and is the opposite
# direction to the blaster nerf that softened the same duel — the two are
# deliberate and the batch measures the net.
[hull]
hull_integrity = 300.0

# Single omni shield arc (issue #514). NPCs have no `[shields]` station so
# the auto-generated `[[system]]` entry is `ai_only = true` and ownerless.
[[shield_arc]]
id = "all"
label = "shield_arc.all.label"
center_deg = 0
width_deg = 360
max_hp = 60
regen_per_sec = 1.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 3.0
length = 7.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.8, 0.3, 0.1]
size = 7.0
icon = "cruiser"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/dynasty_cruiser_recreated.glb"
shape = "cuboid"
size = [6.0, 2.0, 10.0]
colour = [0.8, 0.3, 0.1]

[helm_console]
max_speed = 12.0
max_reverse_speed = 6.25
impulse_speed_multiplier = 6
acceleration = 4.1665
deceleration = 12.5
max_yaw_rate = 0.196
# Mid-weight Harrow: the smallest non-zero trade (x1.1 at rest).
low_speed_turn_boost = 0.1
max_bank_deg = 10.0

[helm_console.engine_pfx]
color = [ 1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 0.68 ]
markers = [ "engine_port", "engine_starboard" ]
trail_lifetime_secs = 0.55

[weapons_console]

# Port bank: facing -90° (left side), wide auto-arc so the cruiser can
# fire one bank or the other depending on relative bearing without
# perfect alignment.
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "port"
facing_deg = -90.0
fire_arc_deg = 180.0
auto_arc_deg = 180.0
beam_range = 50.0
beam_damage_per_sec = 8.0
beam_duration_secs = 5.0
cooldown_secs = 4.0
shield_pierce = 0.1
beam_color = [1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 1.0]
marker = "phasers_port"

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

# Starboard bank: facing +90° (right side).
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "starboard"
facing_deg = 90.0
fire_arc_deg = 180.0
auto_arc_deg = 180.0
beam_range = 50.0
beam_damage_per_sec = 8.0
beam_duration_secs = 5.0
cooldown_secs = 4.0
shield_pierce = 0.1
beam_color = [1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 1.0]
marker = "phasers_starboard"

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

[comms]
range = 600.0

[ai_profile]
aggression = 0.7
sensor_range = 110.0

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# (#572) Doctrine-based behaviour (FSM dissolved). Destroy outscores Patrol so
# the cruiser engages any hostile it can see; falls back to its route when no
# target is visible.
#
# (#892) THE ROUTE IS A PICKET, NOT A SWEEP. This is the hull the Harrow fields
# as a standing presence — the one that is already there when a scenario starts,
# as against the destroyer and the cruiser, which arrive on a schedule. Three
# authored changes carry that:
#
#   * The Patrol entry paces its two stations at a third of maximum rather than
#     half, and scores 30 rather than 20 with a further +15 while nothing has
#     shot at it. A picket that is not being shot at is worth more on station
#     than a roving patrol ever was.
#   * The Destroy entry fights at 60 units rather than 45 and closes at 0.6
#     rather than 0.9. A picket does not tail-chase: it comes off station
#     grudgingly, holds a standoff, and is back on its line quickly.
#   * The Destroy entry gains +25 while `attacked`. Shot at, the picket stops
#     being a picket and commits — 63 against the Patrol entry's 30.
#
# The ordering that results is the whole point, and is worth reading twice:
# undisturbed, the picket HOLDS (45 > 38) even with a hostile on its scope;
# shot at, it fights (63 > 30). That is the inversion of the old numbers, and it
# is what makes a picket a picket — the raid comes to it, not the other way
# round. The hull's own `[ai_profile] sensor_range = 110` bounds the radius it
# can see into at all, so the line it holds is a real one.
#
# Blast radius: `default.toml`, `patrol.toml` and `reinforcements.toml` all
# field this hull as the ambient patrol the player goes looking for, which is
# exactly the posture above. `duel.toml` and the
# probe worlds field it as a combatant, and are unaffected for a different
# reason: `duel.toml` injects its own `{ id = "kill", base_priority = 80 }`
# Destroy entry into the slot override, and the by-id doctrine merge
# (`entity_override.rs:46-55`) reconciles it against this hull's `destroy-hostiles`
# entry by that shared id rather than appending a second Destroy — so the
# injected 80 dominates in every state, attacked or not, and this hull's own
# 30/38/63 ordering never gets a turn to matter there.

[behaviour]

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "patrol-ironveil"
text          = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.behaviour.doctrine.patrol_ironveil.text"
directive_kind    = "Patrol"
directive_anchors = ["ironveil_patrol_a", "ironveil_patrol_b"]
directive_loop    = true
base_priority     = 30.0
target_speed      = 0.3
modifiers         = [{ condition = "not_attacked", weight = 15.0 }]

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "destroy-hostiles"
text          = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.behaviour.doctrine.destroy_hostiles.text"
directive_kind = "Destroy"
base_priority  = 38.0
target_speed   = 0.6
maintain_range = 60.0
modifiers      = [{ condition = "attacked", weight = 25.0 }]

# ── Stations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Crew stations (issue #871), mirroring `alliance_destroyer.toml` — the
# comparable player hull for this patrol escort. See the fuller note in
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`: every seat boots on the implicit `Backfill` rating, which
# automates every system the station owns, so an unmanned hull behaves exactly as
# it did when its systems were ownerless + `ai_only`.
#
# The auto-generated `shield-arc-all` system is the only thing left ownerless.

[[station]]
id = "captain"
name = "Captain"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.station.captain.description"
rank = "Cpt."
short_code = "CPT"
console = "gui/battleship/captain.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[station]]
id = "helm"
name = "Helm"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.station.helm.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "HLM"
console = "gui/battleship/helm.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[station]]
id = "tactical"
name = "Tactical"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.station.tactical.description"
rank = "Lt. Cmdr."
short_code = "TAC"
console = "gui/battleship/tactical.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

[[station]]
id = "engineering"
name = "Engineering"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.station.engineering.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "ENG"
console = "gui/battleship/power.html"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

# ── Systems ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Red Alert authored explicitly (issue #871) rather than left to the #749
# ownerless provision, so the Captain seat owns it. Control source is unchanged:
# Backfill automates it.
[[system]]
id = "red-alert"
kind = "red_alert"
station = "captain"

# Per-axis helm systems (issues #701/#703, declared in #800 and #704), owned by
# the Helm seat.
#
# #800 declared thrust + steering. #704 adds impulse + lateral-thrust, which the
# deleted `operate_helm_ai` monolith used to drive on this hull's behalf: an
# undeclared system resolves to ControlSource::Human (`operate_ai = false`), so
# the monolith never stood down from those two axes here. Declaring them hands
# both to `ai_helm_impulse` / `ai_helm_lateral_thrust`, which was what made the
# delete behaviour-preserving. (Since #803 both systems decide on the shared
# AI-helm sim tick — `[global] ai_helm_tick_hz`, default 30 Hz — rather than
# once per rendered frame as the monolith did.)
[[system]]
id = "helm-thrust"
kind = "helm_thrust"
station = "helm"

[[system]]
id = "helm-steering"
kind = "helm_steering"
station = "helm"

[[system]]
id = "helm-impulse"
kind = "helm_impulse"
station = "helm"

# Boost drive axis (issue #801), declared for hull-uniformity with the player
# ships: every helm axis is a declared system on every hull. No AI drives
# boost, so the declaration gives the axis the standard damage/repair surface
# plus a lever for a human at the Helm seat.
[[system]]
id = "helm-boost"
kind = "helm_boost"
station = "helm"

[[system]]
id = "helm-lateral-thrust"
kind = "lateral_thrust"
station = "helm"

# The Tactical radar (issue #871) — the system every player hull declares and no
# NPC hull did, which is what blocked #887 from routing AI target selection
# through admission.
[[system]]
id = "tactical-radar"
kind = "tactical_radar"
station = "tactical"

# Fine Tactical systems (issue #512): port + starboard phaser banks. No torpedoes.
# `phaser_bank_system_id("port")` resolves to `SystemId("phaser-port")` via
# the `phaser-<id>` naming convention, and the resolver has that id from the
# [[system]] block below, so per-bank gating (system_is_registered + own
# fine-system policy) is used for firing.
[[system]]
id = "phaser-port"
kind = "phaser_bank"
station = "tactical"
power_group = "weapons"

# Ship-wide phaser settings (issue #801): firing mode + emitter frequency.
# One declared system (NOT per-bank) so SetPhaserMode/SetPhaserFrequency
# admission gates on a real system instead of the deleted coarse `tactical`.
[[system]]
id = "phaser-control"
kind = "phaser_control"
station = "tactical"

[[system]]
id = "phaser-starboard"
kind = "phaser_bank"
station = "tactical"
power_group = "weapons"

# Fine Power systems (issue #513): reactor + battery for per-instance damage.
# The reactor and the battery are not ON a power group — they ARE the reactor —
# so `power_group` is omitted here. The gun line above declares one; see the
# `[power_groups.*]` block below for why this hull grew one at all.
[[system]]
id = "power-reactor"
kind = "power_reactor"
station = "engineering"

[[system]]
id = "power-battery"
kind = "power_battery"
station = "engineering"

# Captain — raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within
# `combat_window_secs`, otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so
# a designer retunes the ship's nerve without recompiling.
[captain_console.ai]
param = { combat_window_secs = 10.0 }

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(secs_since_combat) < param(combat_window_secs)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false

# ── Power groups (issue #1398) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# THE FIRST NPC HULL THAT MAY BE TAKEN COLD, and it declares a
# `[power_groups.*]` block for one reason: restraint. (`ship_harrow_tug.toml`
# already declares one, for its tractor bus; what is new here is
# `min_level = 0` on weapons.) Issue #1398 retired the captain's hidden weapons
# hold, so `ctx.effects.hold_fire(name)` is now a POWER order on this ship's
# `weapons` group — and a group can only be commanded cold if its own hull says
# so. Three worlds order this hull to hold: `probe_restraint.toml`,
# `probe_picket.toml` and Falling Skyway's Havelock enforcer. Without
# `min_level = 0` here every one of them would issue an order the reactor
# clamps back to 1, and the enforcer would go on shooting.
#
# Authoring a `[power_groups.*]` block replaces the canonical default seeding
# wholesale (`ship::power::authored_power_group_seed`), so all three groups are
# written out — at exactly the levels the default seeding gave them, which is why
# this block changes nothing about how the hull flies. `default_level = 2` is the
# level each group booted at before; `max_level = 4` is the API ceiling; and the
# only value that is not a transcription of the old behaviour is the weapons
# floor.
#
# The gun line's `[[system]]` entries name `weapons` above. Nothing else on this
# hull does: `helm` and `shields` are declared because the reactor's budget and
# the `[power.ai_policy]` channels below are written in terms of them, not
# because a system reads them for a gate.
[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.power_groups.helm.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.power_groups.weapons.label"
# `min_level = 0`: this group may be taken COLD. The same statement the
# destroyer and the cruiser make (issue #1395), on the hull a scenario actually
# silences. Weapons is the one group here that can be switched off outright:
# cutting a patrol boat's drive or its shields to nothing is a way to lose it,
# while its guns at 0 cost it its guns and nothing else.
default_level = 2
min_level = 0
max_level = 4

[power_groups.shields]
label = "entity.ship_harrow_patrol.power_groups.shields.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# Reactor + battery. Transcribed from `PowerConfig::default()`, which is what
# this hull ran on before it declared the section: authoring
# `[power.ai_policy]` cannot be done without bringing `[power]` into existence,
# and the three fields are required, so they are written out at exactly the
# values the Rust default supplied.
[power]
capacity = 100.0
rates = [ 6, 5, 4, 2, -2, -6 ]
emergency_threshold = 25.0

# The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003), the same numbers the fleet
# baseline authors — see `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`'s param note for the
# full reasoning. Each channel authors three rules: HOLD (priority 15), ELEVATE
# (10), and the `priority = 0` BASELINE at level 2 that takes the channel back
# when neither of the others fires. That fallback IS the shed; there is no
# demote rule and no ship-wide total rule (`shields` never bids, so it is
# reserved at its commanded 2).
#
# Each channel carries TWO floors and the gap between them is the point: the
# channel sheds below `min_reserve_*` and may not rise again until the charge is
# back over the higher `min_restore_*`. With one floor per channel the shed and
# the re-elevate would sit on the same number, and the AI would flip that
# channel on every tick the charge rested there. `fact(power_<group>)` — the
# channel's CURRENT level — is what lets the hold rule tell "already up" from
# "climbing back", so the hysteresis needs no policy state.
#
# A FALLING battery at combat stations under thrust (helm's elevate needs the
# thrust, weapons' needs the alert — this hull drops the `red_alert` clause from
# its helm rules, see the fuller note at the top of this file):
#
#   >= 50   helm 3 / weapons 3 / shields 2 = 8 — the steepest drain in `rates`
#   25..50  helm sheds  => total 7 — a slow drain (-2/s here)
#   < 25    weapons too => total 6 — POSITIVE (+2/s), so the reserve refills
#
# A RISING one climbs the same steps at 35 (weapons) and 60 (helm), so the
# charge oscillates across the 25–35 band and — with the reactor undamaged —
# never reaches 0, which is where `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to 1 and
# locks the reactor until `emergency_threshold` above is back. Under thrust with
# the alert DOWN this hull's ordinary transit rests at total 7 rather than 6,
# and the 50 step turns even that around.
#
# The hold rules carry the SAME trigger clause as the elevate they sit above —
# helm's thrust, weapons' red alert — not only the shed floor, and that is
# deliberate: one tick with the trigger false sheds the channel exactly as a
# battery breach would, and it cannot climb back on the trigger returning alone
# while the charge is under the restore floor — the elevate rule that would
# re-raise it is gated on the RESTORE floor, not the shed one. A one-way
# ratchet on trigger flap for as long as the reserve is in the band — elevated
# posture belongs to combat stations, not to a throttle or an alert that
# blinked for a single tick.
#
# AI-shed only: `handle_power_messages` never reads `battery_pct`, so a human
# Power officer pushes straight past all four floors. Out of scope in the other
# direction: a Disabled or Destroyed reactor rates `operate_ai = false`, so the
# AI stops operating power altogether while the reactor keeps integrating at the
# last commanded total — no floor reaches that case.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair, the mirror of the battery pair one axis over: elevate at
# 0.7, release at 0.6. Without it a throttle DWELLING near the single threshold
# strobes helm 3<->2 at the AI tick rate, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 MaxSpeed swing --
# a ship thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn. [ai] The
# ratifiable quantity is the BAND WIDTH (0.1), not either endpoint. See
# fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml for the full note and the measurement.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's shed/restore pair: the first point the ship gives back, and the higher
# charge it takes the point again at.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair, the lower step of the ladder. 25 sheds to the sustainable total
# while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand; the 10 this shipped with
# before issue #1003 shed with barely a tenth of it left.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm — HOLD (already at 3 and still above the shed floor), then ELEVATE
# (climbing back past the restore floor), then the baseline.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons — the rung the battery actually oscillates on, and the last elevation
# the ship gives up.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/ship_harrow_tug.toml:
# Harrow Salvage Tug (issue #1163) — a HOSTILE, fully AI-crewed tug that locks a
# disabled craft, engages its tractor and hauls the prize off, with NO player
# involvement.
#
# ── The point of this hull (PRD #1143 / issue #1163) ──────────────────────────
#
# The world acts on the crew with the same verbs the crew act with. This hull is
# the NPC side of the tractor family (issues #1156-#1158): it owns exactly the
# same admission-gated `[[system]] kind = "tractor"` a crewed hull does, and it
# runs it through the SAME backfill hosts (`operate_tractor_ai`, #1162) on the
# shared AI cadence — there is NO NPC-vs-player branch anywhere. An NPC "runs the
# same procedure" purely by owning the system and being handed a `Tow` directive
# that names its target; the host emits the byte-identical `EngageTractor` a human
# Engineering officer would, through `emit_ai_command` → `validate_and_admit`.
#
# ── How it is DIRECTED ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# World-agnostic on purpose: this template authors only a HOLD default doctrine,
# so it attaches a `BehaviourSection` (which satisfies strict AI-declaration mode
# and lets `aggregate_doctrine_blackboards` publish its scored objectives) and
# sits still until ordered. A world hands it the actual job by OVERRIDING
# `behaviour.doctrine` on the spawn (by-id merge) with:
#
#   * a `Tow` directive whose `directive_operate_target` names the prize — the
#     Engineering tractor host engages the beam once the ship's one Tactical lock
#     is on that target, and
#   * a `Retreat` (or `Reach`) directive naming a haven anchor — the Helm flies
#     there, and the coupling drags the prize along at the authored offset.
#
# The lock itself is reached by the widened weapons selector's `objective-operate`
# source (issue #1162 D2), composed from `fleet_baseline.toml`: a per-verb operate
# directive naming a target injects a NON-hostile candidate, so the tug reaches a
# lock on the disabled craft it was ordered to tow without the target ever being
# hostile. See `assets/worlds/probe_npc_tow.toml` for the driving world.
#
# It is NOT a shipped combat hull and flies in no scenario — it is the NPC content
# the #1163 headless tests put a beam on. Kept out of every shipped hull so no
# committed world's digest moves for this slice.

includes = ["fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml", "fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml"]

class = "courier"  # picker badge / scan subtitle — a light salvage hull
tags = ["ship", "npc"]
faction = "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc"  # Harrow — hostile to the Alliance
# Authored mass (issue #1154): a light, powerful little tug. Read by the tow-load
# helm penalty (#1157) as the operator's own mass; the prize's mass is what
# actually loads the drive.
mass = 9000.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 0.8
length = 2.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact (issue #958); it flies its Retreat leg under power.
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.9, 0.5, 0.2]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

[mesh]
# Shares the courier silhouette; a bespoke .glb would buy the probe nothing.
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

# A modest drive — enough to haul a laden prize off the field, not enough to run
# down a warship.
[helm_console]
max_speed = 16.0
max_reverse_speed = 5.0
impulse_speed_multiplier = 4.0
acceleration = 4.0
deceleration = 10.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.2
max_bank_deg = 8.0

[ai_profile]
aggression = 0.2
# Wide enough to keep the tug high-fidelity across the whole of the tractor's
# own reach. The `objective-operate` candidate itself is bounded by the installed
# tractor's authored executable reach, not this LOD horizon.
sensor_range = 800.0

# ── High-fidelity bubble ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A `LodBubble` carrier is itself ALWAYS full-fidelity (see `LodBubble`). Without
# it, a tug operating far from the player would sit in the cheap dead-reckoned
# low-LOD path and never fly its own helm doctrine — the tow would form but the
# tug would never haul the prize off. Small radius: it self-promotes the tug (and
# the prize inside it), not the whole map.
[lod_bubble]
radius = 300.0

# ── Behaviour ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Only a HOLD default: this makes `spawn_entity`/game-start attach the
# `BehaviourSection` and satisfies strict AI-declaration mode, but leaves the tug
# idle until a world overrides `behaviour.doctrine` with the actual Tow + Retreat
# order (see the header). No Destroy doctrine — a salvage tug does not go hunting.
[behaviour]

[[behaviour.doctrine]]
id            = "hold-station"
directive_kind = "None"
base_priority = 5.0
target_speed  = 0.0

# ── Systems: every one ownerless + `ai_only`, so the NPC spawn path puts each
# under `ControlSource::Ai` and the #1162 hosts' `operate_ai` gate holds. The
# Red Alert system the captain policy drives is synthesised for any hull with a
# `[behaviour]` block, so it is not listed here.

# Per-axis helm (the tug flies its Retreat leg).
[[system]]
id = "helm-thrust"
kind = "helm_thrust"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-steering"
kind = "helm_steering"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "helm-impulse"
kind = "helm_impulse"
ai_only = true

# Tactical radar — the surface the weapons selector's `objective-operate` source
# resolves the tow target's lock onto.
[[system]]
id = "tactical-radar"
kind = "tactical_radar"
ai_only = true

# Fine power (reactor + battery) for per-instance damage and the group allocator.
[[system]]
id = "power-reactor"
kind = "power_reactor"
ai_only = true

[[system]]
id = "power-battery"
kind = "power_battery"
ai_only = true

# ── The tractor system ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First-class, ownerless + `ai_only`, power-grouped: the admitted target for
# EngageTractor / ReleaseTractor, admission-gated exactly like a crewed hull's.
#
# It draws from the dedicated `ops` power bus. This hull composes
# `fleet_baseline.toml`, whose `[power.ai_policy]` manages the `helm` and
# `weapons` channels — so those groups are authored below (a `[power_groups.*]`
# block replaces the canonical defaults wholesale, per `authored_power_group_seed`,
# so the policy's channels must be re-declared) — and `ops` is added beside them
# for the tractor. It rests at its seeded level 2, at or above the
# `min_power_level` below.
[[system]]
id = "tractor"
kind = "tractor"
ai_only = true
power_group = "ops"

# ── Power groups ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `helm` + `weapons` re-declare the canonical groups `fleet_baseline`'s power
# policy manages (authoring any group replaces the defaults, so these must be
# restated); `ops` is the tractor's own bus. All seeded at level 2 by
# `authored_power_group_seed`.
[power_groups.helm]
label = "entity.ship_harrow_tug.power_groups.helm.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.weapons]
label = "entity.ship_harrow_tug.power_groups.weapons.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

[power_groups.ops]
label = "entity.ship_harrow_tug.power_groups.ops.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── The coupling terms (all authored — AGENTS.md rule 11) ─────────────────────
[tractor]
range = 600.0
coupling_offset = [0.0, 0.0, -100.0]
min_power_level = 2

# The mass → helm-penalty curve (issue #1157): a laden prize slows the tug.
[tractor.tow_load]
half_penalty_mass = 10000.0
max_penalty = 0.8

# ── Per-system hull ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# So the tractor can be knocked out (the "tractor destroyed" interruption) and the
# tug can be killed. "core" is the ownerless bucket RepairTarget::Core dispatches
# to. Radar carries no hull, matching fleet convention.
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "core"
max_hp = 24
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.10

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "tractor"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "helm-thrust"
max_hp = 20
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.20

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "helm-steering"
max_hp = 20
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.25
debuff_magnitude = 0.20

[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "helm-impulse"
max_hp = 20
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.75

[[hull.system_hull]]

[[hull.system_hull]]

base_files.assets/entities/ship_harrow_warhawk.toml:
# Harrow Battleship (Warhawk class) — the artillery platform (issue #792)
#
# Heavy capital ship. Two long-range phaser banks (port + starboard), heavy
# shielding, slow but devastating. (#474) Rebalanced for the combat-test scenario
# (#475) — gained a full behaviour tree (previously only had
# `initial_state = "idle"` and a stub `attacking` state with no transitions, so
# the ship spawned and sat there), gained weapons (no `[weapons_console]` block
# before), gained shields, slowed down.
#
# #792 is the first issue to give this hull a HELM DOCTRINE of its own. Until now
# it fell back to the shared `plan_helm_travel` Destroy arm — a station-keeper
# that closes to a fraction of weapons range and re-faces the target — which is
# the same manoeuvre every undoctrined hull flies. The third of the three Harrow
# hulls to be authored, and the opposite of both its siblings:
#
#   acquire     ──(target visible, inside artillery_hold_range)─▶ hold
#   acquire     ──(target visible, beyond it)────────────────────▶ reposition
#   reposition  ──(range <= artillery_hold_range)────────────────▶ hold
#   reposition  ──(target lost)──────────────────────────────────▶ acquire
#   hold        ──(range >  max_artillery_range)─────────────────▶ reposition
#   hold        ──(target lost)──────────────────────────────────▶ acquire
#
# The destroyer flies THROUGH its target and runs; the cruiser circles it. This
# hull does neither. It closes once, stops, and then does not move again for the
# rest of the engagement — the whole doctrine is two states and a range band.
#
# ## The range band, and why it is TWO numbers
#
# `max_artillery_range` (200) is the outer edge of the envelope: past it the gun
# line is not worth holding and the hull starts closing again. `artillery_hold_range`
# (180 — ninety per cent of it, authored as a real value rather than computed in
# Rust) is where the closing STOPS.
#
# The twenty units between them are not slack, they are the hysteresis. A single
# threshold would put the entry and the exit on the same number, so a target
# drifting either side of 200 would flip the battleship between "close" and
# "hold" every few ticks — accelerating and braking a 280-hull capital ship
# against a boundary it is always sitting on. With the band, entering costs a
# 20-unit run-in and leaving costs the target 20 units of real separation, and
# neither can chatter.
#
# ## What "holds position" means, and what it deliberately does not
#
# `artillery_hold_speed` is authored ZERO. Inside the band the hull commands no
# translational thrust at all and coasts to a stop; the only thing it keeps doing
# is TURNING. That is the whole of AC5: there is no transition anywhere below
# guarded on the target getting CLOSER, so a player who charges the battleship
# does not push it backwards. It stops shooting artillery at knife range and
# starts shooting phasers, which is what the 75-unit beam banks are for.
#
# Zero is also exactly why the throttle needs a name of its own rather than
# borrowing the cruiser's `torpedo_bearing_speed` or the destroyer's
# `reengage_speed`. An unauthored param and an authored 0.0 are the same number
# and opposite intents, so the host gates on the NAME being present: omit it and
# the whole arm is declined and the battleship flies ordinary doctrine travel,
# rather than parking at an invented standstill in front of an enemy.
#
# ## Why the yaw verb is its own, and what it solves for
#
# Steering answers the hold with `hold_artillery_position`, the SEVENTH yaw mode
# verb. It is not `pivot_to_reengage`: that verb is one leg of the shield-RECOVERY
# doctrine and the host only publishes it for a hull that authors all six standoff
# scalars, every one of them a statement about a ring derived from the TARGET's
# reach — which an artillery platform has no business inventing in order to borrow
# a turn. It is not `hold_torpedo_bearing` either, and that one is the more
# interesting refusal: the cruiser's bow hold points at where the target IS, with
# no lead at all, which is right for a fixed tube settling on a shield gap forty
# units away and wrong here. This hull's bolt takes five and a half seconds to
# cross its own envelope. At that flight time "where it is" and "where it will be"
# are different bearings, and a battleship that aimed at the first would miss
# every moving target it ever fired at.
#
# So the host solves a PREDICTIVE intercept: the target's velocity is
# reconstructed from its heading and speed, and the bow goes onto the point the
# bolt and the target both arrive at — through the same
# `predict_intercept_heading` the blaster itself launches on, at the same lead
# speed, so the AI's aim cannot drift from its own ballistics. The lead speed is
# READ off the bank below rather than authored twice; a second copy of a weapon's
# flight speed is a number that can silently disagree with the weapon.
#
# ## Hazards may move the gun line; they may not make it an orbit
#
# There is no transition below guarded on hazard urgency, collision proximity, or
# any other avoidance reading, and that absence is load-bearing — the same posture
# the cruiser's header sets out. Avoidance composes onto this leg three ways, all
# of them temporary and all of them outside the state machine: the shared
# repulsion steering is summed onto the solved intercept facing inside the pure
# planner; `ai_helm_lateral_thrust` nudges the hull sideways off its held point
# without touching Engines or Steering at all (which IS "limited hazard avoidance
# may relocate the firing position"); and an IMMINENT collision temporarily
# overrides desired facing from the shared hazard force. None of the three is a
# state, so a detour evaporates the moment the hazard clears and the battleship
# resumes the gun line it was already holding. Adding a "dodging" state would have
# turned an artillery platform into an orbiting one — a manoeuvre with an exit is
# a place to get stuck.
#
# ## Close defence (issue #793), and why it is entirely a WEAPONS story
#
# #792 left the hull with one answer to a player who closes: keep holding, and let
# the beams do the work at 75 units. #793 completes it. Nothing below adds a state,
# a transition, a steering verb or a helm param — the doctrine above is untouched,
# and that is the design rather than an economy. The close-defence armament is
# opportunistic: it takes the shots the gun line happens to offer and never asks
# for one.
#
# ### The beams: 270 degrees, not 180
#
# The two banks were authored at `fire_arc_deg = 180` on ±90 facings. That covers
# the full circle with no dead zone, which is where #792 left it — but the two
# half-planes only touch, they do not overlap, so at any real bearing exactly ONE
# bank could ever fire and the hull's close-in output was 12 damage/s however it
# was engaged. Worse, the seam between them lies dead ahead, which is precisely
# where the hold puts the target: an artillery platform pivoting onto its lead
# solution spends the whole engagement with the enemy sitting on the one bearing
# its battery is split across.
#
# At 270 each the arcs overlap through the bow and through the stern (±45 of
# either), so both banks bear on anything within 45 degrees of the centreline —
# 24 damage/s, double, in exactly the cone the doctrine holds a closing player in
# — while the beams keep the single-bank cover they already had and no bearing
# loses coverage. `auto_arc_deg` matches `fire_arc_deg` for the same reason the
# cruiser's does: the overlap region reaches to 135 degrees off each bank's
# facing, and a narrower auto arc would switch off the very cover this widening
# exists to create.
#
# ### The launchers: fore and aft, independent, and silent about steering
#
# Two tubes on opposite facings, each deciding entirely for itself. A tube fires
# when it is loaded, the target is already inside ITS cone, and the shield arc the
# round would strike is down — and at no point does any of that reach the helm.
# There is no torpedo state on either travel axis, no `torpedo_bearing_speed`, and
# no yaw verb but the artillery hold's: the tubes take the bearing the gun line
# gives them, and when it gives them nothing they hold their rounds. A battleship
# that swung its bow to line up a torpedo would be abandoning the predictive
# intercept its main gun is aimed by, which is the whole hull.
#
# That is also why the AFT tube exists and is the interesting one. The hull turns
# at 0.20 rad/s. A player circling at knife range crosses in bearing several times
# faster than that, so the battleship cannot keep its nose on them — they sweep
# through the stern cone on every lap, and the aft launcher is what makes getting
# behind this ship stop being free. The fore tube covers the opposite case, the
# player who closes straight down the gun line.
#
# Per-tube independence is a real requirement and not a phrasing, and it is the
# HOST that delivers it: `auto_fire_torpedo` admits candidates tube by tube on
# their own `loaded` and their own `in_arc`. What the authored launch guards below
# contribute is a refusal — they never conjoin the ship-wide `tubes_full` the
# cruiser's committed salvo gates on. On this hull `tubes_full` would mean a loaded
# fore tube bearing on a collapsed arc refuses the shot because the aft tube is
# still on its reload — which is the opposite of opportunistic.

# ── Composed on the shared fragment library (issue #878) ──────────────────────
#
# The gun line above is no longer authored here. It is
# `fragments/ai/movement_artillery.toml` — the same file `alliance_battleship.toml`
# flies — and this hull tunes it with ONE parameter (`press_posture`, below).
# That is the whole point of the migration: one library serves the player fleet
# and the Harrow, and "aggressive" is a number rather than a second copy of the
# machine.
#
# Order is significant: fragments merge in declared order and this file merges
# last, so the includer always wins. `movement_artillery.toml` is listed AFTER
# `fleet_baseline.toml` because it REPLACES the baseline's two travel axes and
# its Impulse policy.
#
# What is still authored below is what makes this hull ITSELF — its guns, its
# tubes, its stations and systems, its doctrine — plus the two ship-level
# declarations a Harrow deliberately does not share with the fleet: the
# stand-down `[captain_console.ai]` (#912) and `[power]` + `[power.ai_policy]`,
# re-authored whole because the baseline's `helm` rule gates its elevation on
# `red_alert` and a Harrow raises the alert only around combat, not for the
# whole transit, so inheriting the guard would pin the drive at 2 for exactly
# the leg that needs it (#923; corrected #955). `ship_harrow_patrol.toml`
# carries the fuller note on both.
includes = [
  "fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml",
  "fragments/ai/movement_artillery.toml",
]

name = "entity.ship_harrow_warhawk.name"
display_name = "entity.ship_harrow_warhawk.display_name"
# [ai] Warhawk-class capital ship ("Harrow Battleship" in the header) — classed
# as a battleship for the picker badge and scan subtitle.
class = "battleship"
tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"]
faction = "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc"
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the hull's other stats. [ai] Unratified — a capital-ship
# weight, close to the Alliance battleship's.
mass = 52000.0

[target]
tags = ["ship"]
threat_level = "high"
description = "entity.ship_harrow_warhawk.target.description"

# 280 -> 400 (#915 tuning pass). The heaviest Dynasty hull was outweighed by
# both the cruiser and the destroyer; it now tops the ladder as intended.
[hull]
hull_integrity = 400.0

# Single omni shield arc (issue #514). NPCs have no `[shields]` station so
# the auto-generated `[[system]]` entry is `ai_only = true` and ownerless.
[[shield_arc]]
id = "all"
label = "shield_arc.all.label"
center_deg = 0
width_deg = 360
max_hp = 120
regen_per_sec = 1.5

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 5.0
length = 12.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.9, 0.2, 0.05]
size = 12.0
icon = "battleship"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/dynasty_battleship.glb"
shape = "cuboid"
size = [10.0, 3.0, 16.0]
colour = [0.9, 0.2, 0.05]

# Slower than the cruiser; the battleship is a deliberate threat the
# player must engage, not a kiteable nuisance.
#
# `max_yaw_rate` is the one figure #792 moved (0.12 → 0.20), and it is the
# doctrine's own requirement rather than a rebalance. The hold turns and does
# nothing else, and the angular rate it has to sustain is the target's crossing
# speed over the holding radius: the fastest hull the game ships crosses at 22
# units/s, which at 180 units is 0.145 rad/s, and a boosted one is faster still.
# At 0.12 the battleship could not follow its own
# intercept solution round, so the bow would lag every crosser and the artillery
# would be aimed at where the solution used to be. Still the slowest hull in the
# set by a wide margin — the cruiser turns at 0.30 — and still far too slow to
# fly anything but a gun line.
[helm_console]
max_speed = 8.0
max_reverse_speed = 4.5
impulse_speed_multiplier = 6
acceleration = 3.0
deceleration = 9.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.20
# Capital hull: no low-speed turn trade. Authored explicitly so the zero
# reads as a decision.
low_speed_turn_boost = 0.0
max_bank_deg = 5.0

[helm_console.engine_pfx]
color = [ 1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 0.68 ]
markers = [ "engine_port", "engine_starboard" ]
trail_lifetime_secs = 0.65

# NOTE the deliberate absences, both pinned by a parse test because both are
# exactly the kind of content that gets helpfully filled in: there is no
# `[helm_console.boost]` block and no `[helm_console.boost_ai]` machine (no state
# in this doctrine engages the drive — an artillery platform that lit a boost
# would be leaving its own firing position), and no `[helm_console.radar]` block
# (an unauthored radar range means UNLIMITED helm visibility, which is what lets
# a 200-unit envelope resolve a target at all).

# ── Doctrine tuning: parameters only (issue #878) ─────────────────────────────
#
# The whole specialisation of the shared artillery doctrine, and the entire
# authoring interface this hull has to it. No rule, state or transition is
# restated: `param` is an ordinary TOML table and deep-merges, so naming one key
# retunes that threshold and leaves the machine alone.
#
# ONE key, and it is the aggression knob. `press_posture` is the rung of the
# host-seeded `posture` fact at which the class doctrine's aggressive half
# unlocks — 0 DEFENSIVE, 1 PRESSED, seeded from this ship's own red alert. The
# Alliance hulls leave it at the class default of 1 and rest on a standoff ring
# until their captain calls the alert. A HARROW IS ALWAYS PRESSED, and this is
# where that is said: at the lowest rung `fact(posture) >= param(press_posture)`
# holds from the first tick and every `fact(posture) < param(press_posture)`
# break-off guard is unreachable, so the machine leaves `shadow` immediately and
# never returns to it. What is left is exactly the acquire → reposition → hold
# gun line this hull flew inline before it was composed (#792).
#
# It is the SAME lever as `min_alert_to_fire = 0` on the banks below and it is
# there for the same reason: a Harrow has no bridge crew to call red alert, and
# its captain policy (#912) stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull that
# waited for one would sit on a standoff ring outside its own guns for ever and
# never start the fight it exists to start. Note what it deliberately does NOT
# do: it changes no red-alert STATE, so every fact, comms, repair and arc-overlay
# reading keyed on the alert is exactly where #912 left it.
#
# Everything else — the 200/180 band, the zero hold throttle, the 0.03/0.6
# steering response — is the artillery class default and is authored once in
# `fragments/ai/movement_artillery.toml`. The fragment also supplies the
# `[helm_console.impulse_ai]` idle this hull used to author inline: an artillery
# hold band lies inside the impulse drive's default cruise window on every hull
# small enough to want one, and an engaged drive hard-overrides commanded
# throttle, so switching the drive off is a property of the DOCTRINE and now
# lives with it.
[helm_console.engines_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0

[helm_console.steering_ai.param]
press_posture = 0.0

[weapons_console]

# ── The close-defence battery (retuned by issue #793) ─────────────────────────
#
# Both banks widened from 180 degrees to 270. See the header for the argument;
# the short of it is that two 180-degree half-planes on ±90 facings cover the
# circle without ever OVERLAPPING, so the hull could only bring one bank to bear
# at a time and the seam between them sat dead ahead — the one bearing an
# artillery platform holding a lead solution keeps its target on. At 270 the arcs
# overlap through the bow and the stern, so a player inside 45 degrees of the
# centreline is engaged by both.
#
# `auto_arc_deg` tracks `fire_arc_deg` deliberately, exactly as on the cruiser. On
# hulls where the two differ, the narrower auto arc is a "do not open fire at the
# very edge of the envelope" rule; here the edge IS the point, because the overlap
# reaches 135 degrees off each bank's facing and a narrower auto arc would switch
# off the double cover this widening exists to create.
#
# Port heavy bank.
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "port"
facing_deg = -90.0
fire_arc_deg = 270.0
auto_arc_deg = 270.0
beam_range = 75.0
beam_damage_per_sec = 12.0
beam_duration_secs = 8.0
cooldown_secs = 4.0
shield_pierce = 0.1
beam_color = [1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 1.0]

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

# Starboard heavy bank.
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "starboard"
facing_deg = 90.0
fire_arc_deg = 270.0
auto_arc_deg = 270.0
beam_range = 75.0
beam_damage_per_sec = 12.0
beam_duration_secs = 8.0
cooldown_secs = 4.0
shield_pierce = 0.1
beam_color = [1.0, 0.22, 0.08, 1.0]

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

# ── The bow artillery piece (issue #792) ──────────────────────────────────────
#
# ONE bank, and everything about it is authored around the gun line the doctrine
# above holds. A blaster rather than a beam or a torpedo because a blaster bolt is
# already exactly the projectile this issue needs and needs no new mechanics: the
# launch heading is solved ONCE, at fire time, through `predict_intercept_heading`
# against the target's velocity, and the bolt then flies that fixed heading in a
# straight line with no reference to the target ever again. Ballistic,
# launch-time predictive, and non-homing, all of it already built.
#
# * `damage = 60` — POWERFUL. Five times a shipped blaster's default, and more
#   than either phaser bank lands in a whole 8-second beam. One bolt is the point:
#   at this range the battleship gets one shot every twelve seconds and it has to
#   be worth waiting for.
# * `projectile_speed = 35` — SLOW, and the slowest bolt in the set (the
#   RNG-coverage escort's test-only `spike` is 60, the default 40). This is the
#   number the whole issue turns on. It is what makes the flight time across the
#   envelope five and a half seconds, which is what makes the intercept
#   prediction necessary; and because the heading is frozen at launch, it is
#   also what makes a course change AFTER the bolt is away pay off. A player
#   who holds a constant heading is hit by a shot aimed where they were going.
#   A player who turns is not.
# * `range = 200` — the envelope the doctrine's `max_artillery_range` names, and
#   nearly three times the 75-unit beam banks. Inside 75 this hull is an ordinary
#   gunship; the artillery is what it does at a distance nothing else of its
#   generation can reach.
# * `cooldown_secs = 12` — a bombardment cadence, not a rate of fire. Sustained
#   it is 5 damage per second, well under the beams' combined output. The bolt is
#   a punishment for flying predictably, not a DPS race.
# * `fire_arc_deg = 90` — a bow mount, and the reason the pivot is load-bearing
#   rather than decorative. The host's fire gate asks whether the target is inside
#   this cone; a battleship that did not put its nose on the solution would simply
#   never be allowed to shoot. Ninety rather than something tighter because the
#   gate reads the target's CURRENT bearing while the hull is pointed at the LEAD,
#   and the angle between those two is real. The exact square-on lead is
#   asin(v/c), not atan(v/c) — the bolt has to cover the hypotenuse, not the
#   opposite side — so the fastest hull the game ships, CRUISING at 22 units/s
#   against a 35-unit/s bolt, wants about 39 degrees. That is inside this
#   45-degree half-arc, so every shipped hull is admitted at square-on cruise.
#   The pinning test derives this rather than trusting this comment.
#
#   Any radial component shortens the lead back inside the cone, so this only
#   bites dead-square crossings. The boosted case is not a cone question at all:
#   the destroyer authors a 2.4x boost, and 38.4 units/s exceeds the bolt's own
#   35 — there is no intercept to aim at, at any cone width.
#
# No `[weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai]` policy is authored, so the canonical
# unconditional-fire policy is synthesised at spawn: the bank fires whenever the
# host's own readiness gates (lock, cooldown, range, arc) are all satisfied. That
# is the whole doctrine this weapon needs — WHERE to be and WHICH WAY to point is
# the helm's job, and it is the interesting half.
[[weapons_console.blaster_banks]]
id = "bow_artillery"
facing_deg = 0.0
fire_arc_deg = 90.0
volley_count = 1
volley_interval_secs = 0.0
cooldown_secs = 12.0
projectile_speed = 35.0
collision_radius = 3.0
visual_scale = 2.5
damage = 60
shield_pierce = 0.15
range = 200.0

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Mirror of the phaser banks on the `blaster_fire`
  # channel: unconditional, with the host still enforcing availability,
  # cooldown, range, arc and target validity before the volley starts.
  [weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "blaster_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_blaster"

# ── The close-defence launchers (issue #793) ──────────────────────────────────
#
# Two tubes, opposed, each answering for itself. The hull carried no `[torpedoes]`
# table before this issue. See the header for why they are opportunistic and why
# neither of them may ever ask the helm for a bearing.
#
# The loadout is authored around "the round that goes through a hole somebody else
# made", which is the same premise as the cruiser's and a different weapon:
#
# * `damage_shields = 0`, so every one of the 30 points is hull damage AND every
#   one of them is conditional. WITHDRAWN, issue #929: this bullet used to read
#   "`damage_hull` always hits hull by design, and the detonation path only enters
#   the shield branch when `damage_shields > 0` — so a round arriving at a
#   RECOVERED arc still lands its full payload. The shield gate on the launcher
#   below is therefore doctrine, not damage arithmetic." Both halves are now
#   false. A round meets the ONE arc it flew into and that arc's own reading picks
#   the payload — `damage_shields` (nothing, on this hull) into a live screen, or
#   `damage_hull = 30` whole onto bare plating — so a round arriving at a
#   recovered arc lands NOTHING, and the launcher's shield gate is damage
#   arithmetic as well as doctrine. The doctrinal reason still stands beside it
#   and is the reason the number does not move: twelve rounds is a small magazine,
#   and a battleship holding station spends them on the opening somebody else made
#   rather than on a target that is still covered.
#
#   The bullet below on flight time is what this now costs. A four-second shot at
#   the edge of the envelope is a bet on the arc still being down when it arrives,
#   and losing that bet used to cost 0 points of 30; it now costs all 30.
# * `speed * lifespan = 200`, the artillery envelope to the unit. Reach is the
#   only lever there is: no launch guard can read a range, because the host seeds
#   `in_range` as a constant `true` for every candidate and applies no range gate
#   of its own. So `lifespan` alone decides how far out a shot may be taken from,
#   and a shorter one would silently decline opportunities the gun line can still
#   see — hence the match.
#
#   What that argument does NOT establish is that a shot at the far edge is a
#   GOOD one, and it should not be read as if it did. 200 units at 50 units/s is
#   four seconds of flight, and the striking-arc reading the guard launched on is
#   four seconds old by the time the round arrives: the target has manoeuvred, the
#   seeker has turned to follow, and the arc the round is nose-on to when it goes
#   off is resolved at impact, not at launch — and it need not be the arc the
#   doctrine looked at. Flight time, not reach, is what makes a long shot a
#   bet — matching the envelope bounds where a round can be spent from, and
#   promises nothing about where it lands.
# * `turn_rate_deg_per_sec = 60` — genuinely homing, unlike the cruiser's barely
#   -steering salvo. A fixed tube on a hull that turns at 0.20 rad/s cannot lead a
#   crossing player, so the seeker has to be what closes the last of the distance.
# * `volley_max = 1` and a `load_time` of 8 seconds. ONE round per launcher per
#   opportunity, and then that launcher is out of the fight for eight seconds
#   while the other one is not. This is the cruiser's exact opposite: there the
#   whole battery commits to one window, here each tube spends its own round on
#   its own window and the two are never coupled.
[torpedoes]
count = 12
damage_hull = 30
damage_shields = 0
speed = 50.0
turn_rate_deg_per_sec = 60.0
lifespan = 4.0
load_time = 8.0
detonation_radius = 4.0

# No `burst_interval_secs`: with `volley_max = 1` there is no burst to space out.
# The parse default stands and nothing reads it.

# The FORE launcher — the player who closes straight down the gun line.
#
# A 90-degree cone, so ±45 off the bow. Wide enough that the hold's own lead angle
# (see the artillery bank above, which is sized on the same 45 degrees) does not
# routinely carry the target out of it, and narrow enough that
# it and the aft cone leave a real 90-degree gap on each beam. The gap is not an
# oversight: an armament that covered every bearing would not be opportunistic, it
# would be a turret, and the whole point is that these tubes take what the gun line
# gives them.
[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "fore"
facing_deg = 0.0
fire_arc_deg = 90.0
volley_max = 1
ai_target_count = 1

  # LOAD is unconditional: a tube that starts loading when the opportunity opens
  # has already missed it (`load_time` is 8 s and a shield arc is back in a few),
  # so the launcher is kept ready between windows and the reload is the cost of
  # having taken a shot rather than a cost of taking one.
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  # LAUNCH. Read what the HOST has already decided before this guard is
  # consulted, because it is most of the decision:
  #
  # `auto_fire_torpedo` refuses the whole ship's launch unless the target is
  # locked and `target_facing_shields <= 0`, then hands on only the tubes passing
  # `loaded && in_arc` — PER TUBE. That filter, not this line, is what delivers
  # the per-tube independence the doctrine is built on. `ai_torpedo_auto_fire`
  # then seeds this snapshot for each surviving candidate with `loaded`,
  # `target_valid`, `in_range` and `in_arc` as literal `true` — they all passed
  # already — so the only facts here carrying a live reading are
  # `target_facing_shields` (which the host has also already gated) and
  # `tubes_full`.
  #
  # So be honest about what this line adds: behaviourally it is the same as the
  # unconditional launch policy synthesised for a tube that authors none. Its
  # content is NEGATIVE and it is deliberate — the one live fact this guard could
  # have gated on, and does not, is `tubes_full`:
  #
  # * `tubes_full` is SHIP-WIDE: every tube on the hull at its volley capacity.
  #   It is right for the cruiser's committed salvo and catastrophic here — a
  #   loaded fore tube bearing on a collapsed arc would refuse the shot because
  #   the aft tube is eight seconds into a reload, and the two launchers would
  #   degrade into one. Its absence is the whole authored decision.
  #
  # The conjuncts that ARE written out are written for two reasons, neither of
  # them "the host might not check":
  #
  # * `loaded` and `in_arc` each NAME a real host filter, so this line states at
  #   the tube what its doctrine depends on: per-tube readiness (`loaded_count >
  #   0`, never the ship-wide reading) and a bearing nobody supplies — the bow is
  #   aimed by the artillery's intercept solution and the stern by wherever that
  #   leaves it. This guard is the whole of the "opportunistic": a question about
  #   the world, never a request to change it.
  # * Writing them out pins the fact NAMES. An unseeded or misspelled `fact(...)`
  #   parses, validates, and then reads absent for ever (the #779 failure mode) —
  #   invisible through the host path, which would fire anyway. The unit test
  #   drives `seed_torpedo_tube_launch_facts` against this policy directly and
  #   switches each conjunct off in isolation, so a typo here fails a test.
  #
  # `in_range` is omitted for a reason that does NOT apply to those two: there is
  # no range gate anywhere on this path. The fact is seeded `true` with nothing
  # behind it, so naming it would pin a condition no host enforces.
  #
  # `target_facing_shields <= 0` restates the host's own ship-wide gate at the
  # tube, and is worth restating because of WHAT it reads: an HP number, not a
  # boolean, resolved per-arc through the target's own arc router, so this gate
  # and the eventual hit agree about which arc is in the way.
  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(loaded) > 0 and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0 and fact(in_arc) > 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"

# The AFT launcher — the player who gets behind a ship that cannot turn.
#
# Identical policy to `fore`, and authored out in full rather than shared, because
# a tube's policy is a property of the tube: these two answer the same words about
# DIFFERENT arcs and different reloads, and that is exactly the independence the
# doctrine is built on. A later refit that changed one cone must change one policy.
[[torpedoes.tubes]]
id = "aft"
facing_deg = 180.0
fire_arc_deg = 90.0
volley_max = 1
ai_target_count = 1

  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"
  when = "true"
  verb = "load_torpedo"

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_launch"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire) and fact(loaded) > 0 and fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0 and fact(in_arc) > 0"
  verb = "launch_torpedo"
