# Torpedo magazine — two axes on one authored block.
#
# GRANT: always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The offline +
# non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this rule is the authored arbiter
# layered on top, and it is where a hull would ration rounds between its tubes.
#
# CONSERVATION (issue #943): whether a launch the ship has already authorised may
# SPEND its round here, or should hold it for later in the mission. Resolved
# inside `handle_fire_torpedo`, the one consumer of an admitted `FireTorpedo`, so
# a human Tactical operator and an AI backfill meet this guard identically — the
# per-tube `torpedo_launch` doctrine gates only the AI, and a gate that
# constrains NPCs alone is how a player empties the whole magazine into wave one.
#
# `rounds_per_threat` is a host reading, not an authored number: every round the
# ship still HAS — the magazine PLUS whatever is already parked in the tubes —
# divided by the mission threat still ahead, which the SCENARIO publishes as the
# world counter `mission_threat_remaining`. A world that publishes none leaves
# the ratio unbounded and this rule always fires, because pacing is something a
# mission asks for and never something a hull decides for itself.
#
# `min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5` reads "keep one round for every TWO things still
# coming". Before retuning it, understand what kind of gate it is: a ONE-WAY
# LATCH. `rounds_aboard` only ever FALLS inside a mission, and the threat count
# only falls when something DIES — so a hull that dips under its own reserve
# stops firing, stops killing the thing that would bring the count down, and
# never climbs back over the line. Whatever is authored here is not a soft
# brake. It is a floor the ship must never be pushed below mid-mission.
#
# 0.5 is chosen for the margin it leaves, not for a tidy identity:
#
#   * The middle of the mission stays open. Over every position combat_test can
#     put this hull in while it still carries half its payload or more, the
#     reserve clears at least 4 rounds — two full volleys — against the wave in
#     front of it. A wave that survives one volley is a wave that never dies,
#     and a wave that never dies freezes the threat count and the latch with it.
#   * Nothing is stranded. At the last unit of threat the floor is half a round,
#     so anything still aboard clears the gate and can be spent on the last
#     fight. A reserve measured against the magazine COUNTER rather than the
#     rounds aboard strands the parked volley whatever this number is, because
#     the counter is debited the moment a tube starts loading.
#
# What it trades away is the front of the mission. The floor at eight published
# waves is 4 rounds rather than 8, so an engagement lasting as long as the hull
# is willing to keep shooting may now take 10 of the 12 rounds while the whole
# schedule is still published, where 1.0 capped it at 6. That ceiling is a
# licence rather than a forecast — flown for real the destroyer spends 6 across
# that stretch either way, because the engagement ends before the gate does —
# but it is what 0.5 permits, and it is the price of the margin above.
#
# The tidy identity is what 1.0 bought (issue #943): the reserve came to exactly
# one round at the last unit of threat, so on paper nothing could ever be
# stranded. It shipped with ZERO margin and it broke. Against the old asteroid
# layout the destroyer bottomed out at exactly 7 rounds against 7 remaining
# waves — a ratio of exactly 1.0, the last reading the gate still passes. #946
# reshuffled which rock lands in which cell (same radii, same split), that moved
# the engagement by one round, the ratio fell under, the latch shut, and
# combat_test's wave chain stalled at wave 2 with the hull holding rounds it
# would never fire.
#
# All of it is measured, not asserted by hand.
# `the_shipped_destroyer_spends_its_whole_payload_across_the_eight_wave_mission`
# (`src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs`) walks this doctrine through the real
# torpedo system over the world's whole authored schedule, INCLUDING a wave that
# outlives the engagement fought against it, and states the latch directly on
# the doctrine.
# `combat_test_paces_the_player_magazine_against_the_whole_eight_wave_threat`
# (`tests/headless_runner.rs`) flies it for real and prints the magazine's
# shape bucketed by remaining threat, (entered, lowest) per bucket:
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 2), 6: (2, 2), 5: (2, 2)}. Read a bucket as a STRETCH OF
# THE MISSION rather than as one engagement — since #960 a wave arrives on its
# own clock whether or not the last one is dead, so the top bucket spans wave 1
# and the opening of wave 2, and bottoms lower than the death-gated chain used
# to show. Ten of the twelve rounds go while six or more waves are still
# published; the last two then sit under the floor (2/6 and 2/5 are both below
# 0.5) until the count reaches 4. At 1.0 the same run reads
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 6)} and stops there: the latch shuts the moment wave 1
# dies, and wave 2 never does.
#
# `sole_objective_count = 1` is the carve-out, and it counts NAMED Destroy
# targets rather than doctrine entries. A world's `spawn_entity` override
# APPENDS its brief to the template's standing orders — doctrine reconciles by
# `id`, and an instance override may not remove what the template authored — so
# combat_test's raid cruisers carry their template's untargeted
# `destroy-hostiles` alongside the `assault-starbase` the world hands them: two
# entries, one named target, one engagement they will not outlive. Those spend
# freely. A hull whose brief names no target reads 0 and paces — which is the
# player's destroyer, the ship #943 was filed about.
[torpedoes.ai]
param = { min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5, sole_objective_count = 1.0 }

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_magazine_grant"
when = "true"
verb = "grant_torpedo_round"

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_conservation"
when = "fact(targeted_objective_count) == param(sole_objective_count) or fact(rounds_per_threat) >= param(min_rounds_per_threat)"
verb = "release_torpedo"

# Reactor + battery. Transcribed from `PowerConfig::default()`, which is what
# this hull ran on before it declared the section: authoring
# `[power.ai_policy]` cannot be done without bringing `[power]` into existence,
# and the three fields are required, so they are written out at exactly the
# values the Rust default supplied.
[power]
capacity = 100.0
rates = [ 6, 5, 4, 2, -2, -6 ]
emergency_threshold = 25.0

# The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003), the same numbers the fleet
# baseline authors — see `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`'s param note for the
# full reasoning. Each channel authors three rules: HOLD (priority 15), ELEVATE
# (10), and the `priority = 0` BASELINE at level 2 that takes the channel back
# when neither of the others fires. That fallback IS the shed; there is no
# demote rule and no ship-wide total rule (`shields` never bids, so it is
# reserved at its commanded 2).
#
# Each channel carries TWO floors and the gap between them is the point: the
# channel sheds below `min_reserve_*` and may not rise again until the charge is
# back over the higher `min_restore_*`. With one floor per channel the shed and
# the re-elevate would sit on the same number, and the AI would flip that
# channel on every tick the charge rested there. `fact(power_<group>)` — the
# channel's CURRENT level — is what lets the hold rule tell "already up" from
# "climbing back", so the hysteresis needs no policy state.
#
# A FALLING battery at combat stations under thrust (helm's elevate needs the
# thrust, weapons' needs the alert — a Harrow drops the `red_alert` clause from
# its helm rules, see the note on `includes` at the top of this file):
#
#   >= 50   helm 3 / weapons 3 / shields 2 = 8 — the steepest drain in `rates`
#   25..50  helm sheds  => total 7 — a slow drain (-2/s here)
#   < 25    weapons too => total 6 — POSITIVE (+2/s), so the reserve refills
#
# A RISING one climbs the same steps at 35 (weapons) and 60 (helm), so the
# charge oscillates across the 25–35 band and — with the reactor undamaged —
# never reaches 0, which is where `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to 1 and
# locks the reactor until `emergency_threshold` above is back. Under thrust with
# the alert DOWN a Harrow's ordinary transit rests at total 7 rather than 6, and
# the 50 step turns even that around.
#
# The hold rules carry the SAME trigger clause as the elevate they sit above —
# helm's thrust, weapons' red alert — not only the shed floor, and that is
# deliberate: one tick with the trigger false sheds the channel exactly as a
# battery breach would, and it cannot climb back on the trigger returning alone
# while the charge is under the restore floor — the elevate rule that would
# re-raise it is gated on the RESTORE floor, not the shed one. A one-way
# ratchet on trigger flap for as long as the reserve is in the band — elevated
# posture belongs to combat stations, not to a throttle or an alert that
# blinked for a single tick.
#
# AI-shed only: `handle_power_messages` never reads `battery_pct`, so a human
# Power officer pushes straight past all four floors. Out of scope in the other
# direction: a Disabled or Destroyed reactor rates `operate_ai = false`, so the
# AI stops operating power altogether while the reactor keeps integrating at the
# last commanded total — no floor reaches that case.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair, the mirror of the battery pair one axis over: elevate at
# 0.7, release at 0.6. Without it a throttle DWELLING near the single threshold
# strobes helm 3<->2 at the AI tick rate, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 MaxSpeed swing --
# a ship thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn. [ai] The
# ratifiable quantity is the BAND WIDTH (0.1), not either endpoint. See
# fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml for the full note and the measurement.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's shed/restore pair: the first point the ship gives back, and the higher
# charge it takes the point again at.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair, the lower step of the ladder. 25 sheds to the sustainable total
# while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand; the 10 this shipped with
# before issue #1003 shed with barely a tenth of it left.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm — HOLD (already at 3 and still above the shed floor), then ELEVATE
# (climbing back past the restore floor), then the baseline.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons — the rung the battery actually oscillates on, and the last elevation
# the ship gives up.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# `Reach` reads the SINGULAR `directive_anchor`; `directive_anchors` (plural) is

# ── Stations ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Crew stations (issue #871), mirroring `alliance_courier.toml` — the comparable
# player hull. That hull is a two-seat runabout whose Tactical seat is the
# pilot-and-gunner position (it owns every helm axis) while the Captain seat owns
# command and the support systems; this courier has the same shape minus the
# blaster, so it takes the same two seats.
#
# See the fuller note in `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`: both seats boot on the implicit
# `Backfill` rating, which automates every system the station owns, so an
# unmanned courier behaves exactly as it did when its systems were ownerless +
# `ai_only`. This hull declares no `[[shield_arc]]`, so after the restructure it
# has NO ownerless systems left at all.

[[station]]
id = "captain"
name = "Captain"
description = "entity.ship_requiem_courier.station.captain.description"
rank = "Cmdr."
short_code = "CPT"
console = "gui/courier/captain.html"

[[station.rating]]

[[station]]
id = "tactical"

# ── AI target selectors (PRD #774 US7, issue #885b) ───────────────────────────
#
# The five per-system target selectors, AUTHORED rather than synthesised. Each
# answers "which entity is this system's target?" for whoever operates the
# station, and each reproduces exactly what the matching
# `default_*_target_selector_config()` in `src/entities/config.rs` used to
# invent at spawn. The reasoning behind every number lives on those functions
# and on the constant blocks above them; `default_ai_policy_pins` spawns every
# shipped hull and compares the two, so a transcription slip fails the build
# rather than quietly changing how this ship picks targets.
#
# All five attach on `[behaviour]` ALONE, not on the console section they name,
# so a hull owes all five whether or not it declares `[sensors_console]`,
# `[navigation_console]`, `[repair]` or `[comms_console]`.
#
# `horizon` is a static outer bound, NOT the live range gate — each host owns
# its own (Sensors' damage-scaled radar reach, Comms' authored `[comms].range`).
# Do not "helpfully" tighten it to look like a range.
#
# A score term's magnitude is its own `weight` field. A `param` entry exists
# only where a `when` guard names one: Repair's `deficit_band_*` and Comms'
# `score_band_*` are the whole set.

# Sensors — rank detectable hostiles by which SOURCE surfaced them:
# combat-lock >> objective >> radar. `switch_margin` is 0 because the gaps
# between the tiers ARE the anti-thrash mechanism.
[sensors_console.selector]
sources = ["combat-lock", "objective-destroy", "radar-contacts", "debris-assessment"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
# The `source_debris_assess` disjunct (issue #1347) is what lets a NON-hostile
# contact reach this seat at all: a moving hazard has no faction, so the
# `hostile` test that gates every other source refuses it. Kept byte-for-byte
# identical to the shared `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` selector, which is
# where the reasoning lives (this hull authors it inline).
#
# INERT ON THIS HULL AS IT STANDS, and deliberately left declared. This ship
# authors no `[scan]` table, and `operate_sensors_ai` offers the debris source
# no contact a hull's own suite could not take a reading of - so the terms below
# score nothing here until somebody gives it an instrument, at which point they
# start working with no further edit. Diverging this block from the shared
# fragment to say so would cost that, and would put a second, subtly different
# Sensors doctrine in the fleet.
eligibility = "candidate_fact(detectable) > 0 and (candidate_fact(hostile) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_debris_assess) > 0)"

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_combat_lock) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0"
weight = 100.0

# Working down a debris field (issue #1347): a hazard outranks an incidental
# radar hostile but never a named objective, and the unread bonus is what makes
# the seat go to the next unknown rather than admire the rock it just read.
# 10 + 15 = 25 < 40, so a confirmed-but-read contact never displaces an unread
# one. See `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`.
[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_debris_assess) > 0"
weight = 10.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_unassessed) > 0"
weight = 30.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_confirmed) > 0"
weight = 15.0

[[sensors_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_radar) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# ── The WEAPONS DOCTRINE: which gun the ship turns to present (issue #956) ────
#
# The fleet baseline, authored inline because this hull composes no fragments.
# The CHANNEL is the rank and the VERB is the family: beams first, then
# blasters, then tubes — the order that used to be a Rust array in
# `tick_weapons_arc_request`. The full reasoning lives in
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`.
#
# This courier is UNARMED, and it still declares the order rather than
# `idle = true`, deliberately: an unarmed hull carries no emitters, so no rank
# can ever qualify and the declaration costs it nothing — while a refit that
# bolts a bank on inherits the fleet's doctrine instead of silently turning for
# nothing. `idle = true` is the honest answer for a hull that must NOT turn for
# its guns, which is a different claim.

[weapons_console.ai]

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_first"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_phasers_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_second"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_blasters_to_bear"

[[weapons_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "arc_bearing_third"
when = "true"
verb = "bring_torpedoes_to_bear"

# Tactical — the ship's firing target. `combat-lock` is deliberately ABSENT from
# the sources: it is Tactical's own output, so unioning it would be circular.
# The current lock reaches the ranking as the host-pushed `source_retained`
# retention candidate, which is why that marker appears in the guards but in no
# source list.
#
# PRECEDENCE INVARIANT — terms are additive and one candidate can carry several
# markers at once, so the weights are sized to beat the maximum non-objective
# stack by more than `switch_margin`: 500 + 200 + 100 + 1 = 801 < 1000 - 50.
# A named Destroy objective therefore always wins AND survives hysteresis
# retention, while `retained` still exceeds `last_attacker` so an established
# engagement is not broken off by a fresh attacker. Retune against that
# inequality, not term by term.
[weapons_console.selector]
sources = ["sensors-designation", "objective-destroy", "last-attacker", "radar-contacts", "objective-operate", "confirmed-debris-threat"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 50.0
# The two urgency bands are read against these, in seconds of dead-reckoned
# time-to-impact (issue #1347). An inline table because a sub-table header here
# would swallow every sibling key below it, `eligibility` included. Kept in step
# with `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`, where the reasoning lives.
param = { debris_pressing_secs = 60.0, debris_urgent_secs = 25.0 }
# Independent revalidation: `detectable` is required of everything, and beyond
# that a candidate is engageable either because the host already vetted it
# (objective order / last attacker / retained lock) OR because it is
# independently hostile. That disjunction honours a mission naming a factionless
# target while refusing a FRIENDLY Sensors designation, which carries only
# `source_sensors_designation`.
#
# The final `source_operate` disjunct (issue #1162) is DIRECTIVE-GATED: it
# injects a candidate ONLY when an active per-verb operate directive names that
# target, so the tractor / external-repair dispatch reach a NON-hostile lock;
# inert otherwise. Kept byte-for-byte identical to the shared
# `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` selector (this hull authors it inline).
#
# The `source_debris_threat` disjunct (issue #1347) is ASSESSMENT-GATED at the
# host: the marker is only ever attached to a contact whose threat state a scan
# actually raised, so Backfill cannot fire on a rock the crew were never told
# about.
eligibility = "candidate_fact(detectable) > 0 and (candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_last_attacker) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_retained) > 0 or candidate_fact(hostile) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_operate) > 0 or candidate_fact(source_debris_threat) > 0)"

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_objective) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_sensors_designation) > 0"
weight = 500.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_retained) > 0"
weight = 200.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_last_attacker) > 0"
weight = 100.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_radar) > 0"
weight = 1.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_operate) > 0"
weight = 1000.0

# Confirmed debris, ranked by deadline (issue #1347). 120 puts a confirmed rock
# above the ordinary fight and below a named Destroy objective; the two bands
# rank several rocks against each other so Tactical works the queue
# earliest-deadline-first. Both bands are guarded on `debris_deadline_known`
# because an ABSENT `impact_secs` reads as 0, and 0 is a real answer here.
# See `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` for the precedence invariant.
[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_debris_threat) > 0"
weight = 120.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_deadline_known) > 0 and candidate_fact(impact_secs) < param(debris_pressing_secs)"
weight = 60.0

[[weapons_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(debris_deadline_known) > 0 and candidate_fact(impact_secs) < param(debris_urgent_secs)"
weight = 60.0

# Navigation — rank destinations into the shared Waypoint. Only the objective
# source marks its resolved destination `reachable`, so this policy drives the
# AI waypoint from objectives alone; `chart-contacts` is surfaced so an author
# can widen the eligibility, and by default only ENRICHES a coincident objective
# destination rather than independently steering the ship.
[navigation_console.selector]
sources = ["navigation-objectives", "chart-contacts"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(reachable) > 0"

[[navigation_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_nav_objective) > 0"
weight = 100.0

[[navigation_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(source_chart_contact) > 0"
weight = 1.0

# Repair — rank this ship's damaged stations for the next free team. Two
# additive ladders whose tier rungs STRICTLY dominate the deficit rungs
# (3 x 100 = 300 < 1000), reproducing the retired `(tier desc, deficit desc)`
# comparator. `assigned < 1` is what makes N free teams pick N DISTINCT
# stations. `tier_ordinal` is the DamageTier discriminant (Operational 0,
# Damaged 1, Disabled 2, Destroyed 3) — a structural enum ordinal, which is why
# its lower bound is a literal rather than a param. The Destroyed rung (3) is
# REACHABLE: since issue #1013 an on-site team repairs a destroyed system like
# any other — `SystemHull::restore` has no tier gate and the first restored HP
# un-latches it — so a destroyed station is real repair work and the eligibility
# must not refuse it. The only tier excluded is Operational (0), which has
# nothing to repair.
#
# Authored on every hull whether or not it crews repair teams: the teams gate
# dispatch, so a ship that gains them later already has its ranking.
[repair.selector]
sources = ["damaged-stations", "core-bucket"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(source_repair_request) > 0 and candidate_fact(assigned) < 1 and candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) > 0"

# The bands sit INSIDE the urgent range and deliberately NOT at the DamageTier
# thresholds — because tier strictly dominates, the deficit ladder only ever
# discriminates within one tier, so bands at the tier boundaries would all fire
# together for every Disabled station and discriminate nothing.
[repair.selector.param]
deficit_band_low = 0.80
deficit_band_mid = 0.90
deficit_band_high = 0.95

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 1"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 2"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(tier_ordinal) >= 3"
weight = 1000.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_low)"
weight = 100.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_mid)"
weight = 100.0

[[repair.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(damage_fraction) >= param(deficit_band_high)"
weight = 100.0

# Comms hail — rank who to hail. The most gated of the five, and the only one
# whose eligibility reads a `self_fact`: `comms_available`, so a Disabled or
# Destroyed Comms system stops the ship hailing at all. `source_hail_objective`
# keeps the baseline — only targets an active Hail directive actually names are
# ranked. `has_open_hail_thread < 1` is the anti-respam gate and it TERMINATES:
# a hail arms it even when it fires no `on_hailed` template, and it re-arms on a
# human `ClearComms` or on the target ceasing to be a live candidate, which is
# what an unmanned ship relies on. `switch_margin` is 0 and the host passes no
# current target: a hail is a ONE-SHOT event, so there is nothing to retain.
[comms_console.selector]
sources = ["hail-objectives", "comms-contacts"]
horizon = 1e9
switch_margin = 0.0
eligibility = "candidate_fact(source_hail_objective) > 0 and candidate_fact(in_range) > 0 and candidate_fact(objective_score) > 0 and candidate_fact(has_open_hail_thread) < 1 and self_fact(comms_available) > 0"

# The bands straddle the `base_priority` values the shipped content actually
# authors (20 / 30 / 35 / 40 / 45 / 50 / 80 / 100), splitting them four ways.
# Bands outside that range would fire for all or none and collapse the ranking
# onto the smallest-UUID tie-break.
[comms_console.selector.param]
score_band_low = 25.0
score_band_mid = 45.0
score_band_high = 75.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_low)"
weight = 100.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_mid)"
weight = 100.0

[[comms_console.selector.score]]
when = "candidate_fact(objective_score) >= param(score_band_high)"
weight = 100.0

# ── AI fine-system policies (PRD #774 US7, issue #885b) ───────────────────────
#
# The ship-level AI policies, AUTHORED rather than synthesised. Each answers
# "which verb does this fine system emit on which channel?" for whoever operates
# the station, and each reproduces exactly what the matching
# `default_*_ai_config()` in `src/entities/config.rs` used to invent at spawn.
# The reasoning behind every rule lives on those functions;
# `default_ai_policy_pins` spawns every shipped hull and compares the two, so a
# transcription slip fails the build rather than quietly changing how this ship
# behaves.
#
# Like the selectors above, these attach on `[behaviour]` ALONE, not on the
# console section they name — so a hull owes them whether or not it declares
# `[captain_console]`, `[shields_console]` or `[power]`. Authoring them is what
# brings those sections into existence on hulls that carried none.
#
# A rule's `when` is a guard, not a capability check: the host keeps every
# availability, cooldown, range and arc gate it had. `idle = true` (see Boost) is
# a first-class declaration meaning "this system deliberately takes no AI
# action" — it is NOT the same as an empty block, which validation rejects.

# Captain — raise Red Alert while the ship has been in combat within
# `combat_window_secs`, otherwise stand down. The window is a named parameter so
# a designer retunes the ship's nerve without recompiling.
[captain_console.ai]
param = { combat_window_secs = 10.0 }

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "red_alert"
when = "fact(secs_since_combat) < param(combat_window_secs)"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = true

[[captain_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "red_alert"
when = "true"
verb = "set_red_alert"
value = false

# Helm longitudinal — always actuate the planner's desired travel. The
# continuous magnitude comes from `DesiredMotion`, so no thrust number is pinned
# here; this rule is only the DECISION to actuate, which a designer can gate.
[helm_console.engines_ai]

[[helm_console.engines_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "longitudinal"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_desired_travel"

# Helm yaw — the mirror of `engines_ai` on the facing axis: always actuate the
# planner's desired facing.
[helm_console.steering_ai]

[[helm_console.steering_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "yaw"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_desired_facing"

# Helm lateral — always actuate. The dodge (and the docking translation) run off
# the shared hazard surface, so again only the decision is authored here.
[helm_console.lateral_ai]

[[helm_console.lateral_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "lateral"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_lateral_thrust"

# Helm vertical — always actuate. `VerticalMovementMode` stays a host-side
# CAPABILITY gate rather than a policy scalar, so a Planar hull still takes no
# vertical component no matter what this rule says.
[helm_console.vertical_ai]

[[helm_console.vertical_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "vertical"
when = "true"
verb = "actuate_vertical_thrust"

# Helm impulse — always PERMIT the manoeuvre. The engage-vs-cancel decision is
# still made host-side from the doctrine's `use_impulse` fact and the
# `decide_impulse` geometry; this rule is the authored gate layered over it, and
# `ship_harrow_warhawk.toml` is the worked example of closing it.
[helm_console.impulse_ai]

[[helm_console.impulse_ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "impulse"
when = "true"
verb = "engage_impulse"

# Helm boost — an explicit IDLE declaration, and the only one in the set. No AI
# on this hull engages the boost drive, so the honest declaration is "takes no
# AI boost action" rather than a rule that never fires. `idle = true` is a legal
# declaration distinct from silence; an empty block is rejected at load. A hull
# opts in by replacing this with a rule on the `boost` channel —
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml` is the worked example.
[helm_console.boost_ai]
idle = true

# Shields focus — two rules on one channel, both emitting the value-less
# `focus_shield_arc`. WHICH of the four arcs is focused is not in the policy: it
# comes from the retained ranking kernel, which reads the four params below
# directly out of `param`. `damage_window_secs`, `min_damage_window_secs` and
# `health_ratio_threshold` are therefore live tunables even though no `when`
# names them — do not delete them for looking unreferenced.
#
# The priority-10 damage rule and the priority-0 fallback emit the same verb and
# the fallback is unconditional, so today the channel resolves identically
# whatever `recent_damage_pct_max` reads. The rule is transcribed as-is because
# this migration changes no behaviour; the redundancy is recorded on #885.
[shields_console.ai_policy.param]
damage_window_secs = 4.0
min_damage_window_secs = 1.0
damage_pct_threshold = 50.0
health_ratio_threshold = 50.0

[[shields_console.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "shield_focus"
when = "fact(recent_damage_pct_max) >= param(damage_pct_threshold)"
verb = "focus_shield_arc"

[[shields_console.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "shield_focus"
when = "true"
verb = "focus_shield_arc"

# Reactor + battery. Transcribed from `PowerConfig::default()`, which is what
# this hull ran on before it declared the section: authoring
# `[power.ai_policy]` cannot be done without bringing `[power]` into existence,
# and the three fields are required, so they are written out at exactly the
# values the Rust default supplied.
[power]
capacity = 100.0
rates = [ 6, 5, 4, 2, -2, -6 ]
emergency_threshold = 25.0

# The AI's two-step SHED LADDER (issue #1003), the same numbers the fleet
# baseline authors — see `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`'s param note for the
# full reasoning. Each channel authors three rules: HOLD (priority 15), ELEVATE
# (10), and the `priority = 0` BASELINE at level 2 that takes the channel back
# when neither of the others fires. That fallback IS the shed; there is no
# demote rule and no ship-wide total rule (`shields` never bids, so it is
# reserved at its commanded 2).
#
# Each channel carries TWO floors and the gap between them is the point: the
# channel sheds below `min_reserve_*` and may not rise again until the charge is
# back over the higher `min_restore_*`. With one floor per channel the shed and
# the re-elevate would sit on the same number, and the AI would flip that
# channel on every tick the charge rested there. `fact(power_<group>)` — the
# channel's CURRENT level — is what lets the hold rule tell "already up" from
# "climbing back", so the hysteresis needs no policy state.
#
# A FALLING battery at combat stations under thrust (helm's elevate needs the
# thrust, weapons' needs the alert — this hull's helm rules carry no `red_alert`
# clause):
#
#   >= 50   helm 3 / weapons 3 / shields 2 = 8 — the steepest drain in `rates`
#   25..50  helm sheds  => total 7 — a slow drain (-2/s here)
#   < 25    weapons too => total 6 — POSITIVE (+2/s), so the reserve refills
#
# A RISING one climbs the same steps at 35 (weapons) and 60 (helm), so the
# charge oscillates across the 25–35 band and — with the reactor undamaged —
# never reaches 0, which is where `PowerSystem::tick` slams every group to 1 and
# locks the reactor until `emergency_threshold` above is back. Under thrust with
# the alert DOWN this hull's ordinary transit rests at total 7 rather than 6,
# and the 50 step turns even that around.
#
# The hold rules carry the SAME trigger clause as the elevate they sit above —
# helm's thrust, weapons' red alert — not only the shed floor, and that is
# deliberate: one tick with the trigger false sheds the channel exactly as a
# battery breach would, and it cannot climb back on the trigger returning alone
# while the charge is under the restore floor — the elevate rule that would
# re-raise it is gated on the RESTORE floor, not the shed one. A one-way
# ratchet on trigger flap for as long as the reserve is in the band — elevated
# posture belongs to combat stations, not to a throttle or an alert that
# blinked for a single tick.
#
# AI-shed only: `handle_power_messages` never reads `battery_pct`, so a human
# Power officer pushes straight past all four floors. Out of scope in the other
# direction: a Disabled or Destroyed reactor rates `operate_ai = false`, so the
# AI stops operating power altogether while the reactor keeps integrating at the
# last commanded total — no floor reaches that case.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# Helm's THRUST pair, the mirror of the battery pair one axis over: elevate at
# 0.7, release at 0.6. Without it a throttle DWELLING near the single threshold
# strobes helm 3<->2 at the AI tick rate, each flip a ×1.25/×1.0 MaxSpeed swing --
# a ship thrusting in bursts instead of holding a constant burn. [ai] The
# ratifiable quantity is the BAND WIDTH (0.1), not either endpoint. See
# fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml for the full note and the measurement.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
# Helm's shed/restore pair: the first point the ship gives back, and the higher
# charge it takes the point again at.
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_restore_helm = 60.0
# Weapons' pair, the lower step of the ladder. 25 sheds to the sustainable total
# while a quarter of the reserve is still in hand; the 10 this shipped with
# before issue #1003 shed with barely a tenth of it left.
min_reserve_weapons = 25.0
min_restore_weapons = 35.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# helm — HOLD (already at 3 and still above the shed floor), then ELEVATE
# (climbing back past the restore floor), then the baseline.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# weapons — the rung the battery actually oscillates on, and the last elevation
# the ship gives up.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(power_weapons) >= 3 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_restore_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

# Comms dialogue response — answer an open hail with its FIRST response. Guarded
# twice, and both guards matter: an unguarded rule would re-emit a response the
# router refuses, every tick, for as long as the dialogue stays open.
#   * `comms_available` — a Disabled or Destroyed Comms system stops the ship
#     answering as well as hailing.
#   * `sender_in_range` — the router refuses a response whose sender has left
#     comms range, so without this the officer's rejection re-flashes forever.
# WHICH message is being answered comes from the host; only the response INDEX
# rides the verb. A ship that should answer nothing declares `idle = true`.
[comms_console.ai]

[[comms_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "comms_respond"
when = "fact(comms_available) > 0 and fact(sender_in_range) > 0"
verb = "respond_to_message"
response_index = 0
base_files.assets/entities/skyhook.toml:
# Orbital skyhook head — the structure Falling Skyway is named after (issue
# #1034, parent #852).
#
# A skyhook is a tether anchored to the world below and a transfer head in orbit
# above it. Only the head is an entity: the ribbon is scenery, the climbers are
# traffic, and what a crew can actually DO to a skyhook — read its condition,
# stabilise it, watch its lift tolerance go — all happens at this end of it.
#
# It is authored as its own template rather than as a dressed-up
# `depot_transfer.toml` because the two structures answer different questions. A
# depot is asked "how much can you move this window"; a skyhook is asked "how
# many can you lift, and are you still safe to lift them". Those are different
# capacities and different thresholds, and folding them onto one template would
# have every future world that places a depot inherit a tether-stability flag it
# has no tether for.
#
# Two health tracks, exactly as on `depot_transfer.toml`:
#
#   [hull]           what weapons destroy. At zero the head is despawned.
#   [infrastructure] what neglect, a storm and a repair team move. At zero the
#                    head is still there — it simply cannot lift anything.
#
# `hull_damage_share = 0.5` couples them: a head that takes a torpedo is
# structurally worse off at half a condition point per hull point, without hull
# damage BEING condition damage.
#
# THE THRESHOLDS ARE A LADDER, not a set of alternatives. The top one is an
# operational limit a crew can trade against — below it the head stops being
# certified to lift, and the mission's transfer window is in trouble. The bottom
# one is structural, and it is the one #1040 hangs the collapse off. A world that
# wants the collapse authors the condition low enough to reach it; nothing here
# decides that.
#
# THE THREE RUNGS BETWEEN THEM ARE THE WARNING LADDER (issue #1040), and they
# are on the template rather than in the world for one reason: a skyhook that
# falls without telling anybody first is bad design in EVERY scenario, not just
# in Falling Skyway. Each rung is a distinct physical failure with its own name,
# so a crew reading an operations panel can see which one they are on and a
# scenario hanging `on_flag_cleared` off one is hanging it off a fact rather than
# off an arbitrary percentage:
#
#   45 %  lift tolerance     not certified to run a climber
#   37 %  load bearing       cannot carry the traffic already on it; trim going
#   31 %  tether tension     the ribbon's tension control is failing
#   25 %  station holding    the head can no longer hold its own station
#   20 %  STRUCTURAL         the tether is coming apart — the floor
#
# THE SPACING IS THE WARNING WINDOW. Six condition points between each warning
# rung and five between the last rung and the floor, so a scenario driving the
# head down at a constant rate gets evenly-spaced warnings and a final window it
# can compute from its own decay rate rather than from a number invented here.
# Falling Skyway's Act-3 header does that arithmetic out loud. [ai] Every
# fraction below is unratified.

name = "entity.skyhook.name"
tags = ["station", "infrastructure"]
# Authored mass (issue #1154), the game's own mass unit — the deterministic
# input a mass-driven mechanic (the tow/tractor helm penalty) reads instead of
# guessing from the structure's other stats. [ai] Unratified — a tethered
# orbital structure, far heavier than any hull that could work it.
mass = 250000.0

[target]
tags = ["station"]
threat_level = "none"
description = "entity.skyhook.target.description"

[hull]
# Sturdier than a depot: this is the biggest thing in the sky over the city, and
# a scenario that wants it gone should have to take its CONDITION down rather
# than shoot the head off in a pass.
hull_integrity = 1200.0

[collider]
# Matched to the visible hull, at John's request. This structure draws the SAME
# `alliance_starbase_recreated.glb` as `station_axiom`, through the same identity
# sidecar and baked original rig dimensions, so it is the same size on screen:
# 28.46 x 14.33 x 34.08, a max half-extent of 17.04. It cannot have a different
# collider from the axiom station while sharing its mesh, and it had one — 26,
# half again too big, an invisible wall nine units out from the visible surface.
#
# Nothing about "the biggest thing in the sky over the city" is lost here: the
# head is still the largest silhouette in the library, because the axiom station
# is that silhouette too. The 26 was never drawn — only flown into.
#
# Sharing the mesh means sharing the shape as well as the size: a Cylinder of
# radius 17.04 and half_height 7.16 (half the drawn 14.325), exactly as
# `station_axiom.toml` authors it, and for the reasons set out there. The head
# is the structure that most wanted this — traffic in this world passes OVER it
# on the way down the skyway, which is the one approach a Ball got wrong by ten
# units.
shape = "Cylinder"
radius = 17.04
half_height = 7.16
length = 0.0

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.85, 0.74, 0.45]
size = 22.0
icon = "station"

[mesh]
# The starbase hull — the largest station silhouette in the library, and the
# only one that reads as a transfer head rather than as an outpost. The torus is
# the streaming/flat-render fallback, as on every other station.
model = "assets/models/alliance_starbase_recreated.glb"
# Same hull as `station_axiom`, through the same sidecar and the same
# `[base].scale`, so it draws at the same size and takes the same stand-in:
# 28.46 x 14.33 x 34.08 measured, minor = 7.16 and major = 9.88 derived from it.
# See `station_axiom.toml` for the arithmetic.
#
# The 26.0 / 6.0 this replaces was the render twin of the 26-unit collider the
# block above corrected: 64 units across against a hull that is 34, so the
# placeholder was nearly twice the width of the thing it stood in for. Same
# staleness, and it could no more keep a different size from the axiom station's
# fallback than it could keep a different collider while sharing its mesh.
shape = "torus"
radius = 9.88
minor_radius = 7.16
colour = [0.85, 0.74, 0.45]

[comms]
# Long-range: the head talks to the whole corridor, and a crew that has to close
# to hailing range before they can ask it anything would spend Act 1 flying.
range = 1600.0

[infrastructure]
# 100 condition points, intact on arrival unless a world overrides it — and
# every world that fields this structure in Falling Skyway does, because the
# mission opens on a head that is already in trouble.
condition_max = 100.0
hull_damage_share = 0.5

# No `decay_per_sec`, deliberately. Condition ticks from the moment the entity
# spawns, which for a `spawn_on = "immediate"` structure is world LOAD — i.e.
# during the lobby, before the mission clock exists. An authored decay would
# therefore charge a scenario for how long its crew spent picking seats, and a
# skyhook's deterioration is a mission beat rather than a lobby tax. A world
# that wants the head to fall on a schedule authors a `[[deadline]]` and spends
# condition from its handler, which is anchored on the mission's first tick.

# How many claimants the head can put through one transfer window. THE NUMBER IS
# THE SCENARIO'S CENTRAL PRESSURE and belongs on the structure rather than in a
# script: Falling Skyway fields three parties who each need to be on it.
[[infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "skyhook_transfer_berths"
amount = 2
label = "entity.skyhook.capacity.transfer_berths.label"

# What one climber carries. Published and labelled so the crew can do the
# arithmetic themselves rather than being told the answer.
[[infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "skyhook_climber_load"
amount = 180
label = "entity.skyhook.capacity.climber_load.label"

# The operational limit. Below 45 % the head is out of lift tolerance and stops
# being certified to run a climber; it comes back at 50 % — `fails_below` plus
# the default hysteresis band — so a head hovering on the line does not flap.
[[infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyhook_lift_capable"
fails_below = 0.45
label = "entity.skyhook.threshold.lift_capable.label"

# WARNING ONE. The head can no longer carry the traffic already on it: ballast
# trim starts going and the transfer schedule has to be shed. First rung a
# scenario can say "this is going to fall" from.
[[infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyhook_load_bearing"
fails_below = 0.37
label = "entity.skyhook.threshold.load_bearing.label"

# WARNING TWO. Tension control on the ribbon is failing and the head has begun
# to oscillate on it. Worse than the first in a way anybody on the structure can
# feel, which is what makes it worth a second, louder beat.
[[infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyhook_tether_tensioned"
fails_below = 0.31
label = "entity.skyhook.threshold.tether_tensioned.label"

# WARNING THREE — the last one. The head can no longer hold its own station and
# is riding down the ribbon. Everything past here is the floor.
[[infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyhook_station_holding"
fails_below = 0.25
label = "entity.skyhook.threshold.station_holding.label"

# The structural one — THE FLOOR. Nothing in the skeleton scenario reached it;
# #1040's Act 3 does, and a world whose condition crosses this line is a world
# whose skyhook comes apart. It is a line to cross rather than a number invented
# at the point of use, which is what lets a scenario hang `destroy_entity` off an
# `on_flag_cleared` and nothing else.
[[infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyhook_tether_stable"
fails_below = 0.2
label = "entity.skyhook.threshold.tether_stable.label"
base_files.assets/entities/skyway_castaway_lifeboat:
# A castaway lifeboat adrift in the Falling Skyway corridor — a scannable derelict
# carrying trapped civilians (issue #1348 mechanism, placed for the T2 refinement).
#
# It is the mirror of the transporter on the rescuing hull: the destroyer authors a
# `[transporter]` table saying what it can do the rescuing WITH, and this entity
# authors a `[civilian_rescue]` table saying who is aboard to be rescued. The life
# signs are DISCOVERED, not given: the count is authored here, but a crew learns it
# only after Sensors complete a scan — the `[infrastructure]` condition track below
# is what makes the lifeboat scannable at all (issue #1032's rule).
#
# It carries a `[hull]` so weapons CAN destroy it: a human Tactical operator who
# fires on it registers the casualty, exactly as the probe lighter does. Backfill
# Tactical never fires on a civilian-carrying contact, so the AI cannot cause that.
#
# This is a Falling-Skyway-specific contact, so it names itself under
# `world.falling_skyway.*` rather than reusing the probe world's lighter — the two
# are the same mechanic, not the same craft.

name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.castaway_lifeboat.name"
tags = ["civilian", "infrastructure"]
mass = 60000.0

[target]
tags = ["civilian"]
threat_level = "none"
description = "world.falling_skyway.entity.castaway_lifeboat.name"

# A soft hull — a lifeboat is not a warship — so a Tactical operator who chooses to
# fire on it can, and the destruction is what the casualty attribution hangs off.
[hull]
hull_integrity = 60.0

[collider]
shape = "Cylinder"
radius = 3.0
half_height = 1.5
length = 0.0

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.4, 0.7, 0.85]
size = 8.0
icon = "station"

# The condition track that makes the lifeboat scannable (issue #1032). A scan of a
# hull with no readable condition is refused, so without this the life signs could
# never be discovered — `[infrastructure]` is the door the scan reads through, and
# `[civilian_rescue]` is what the discovery beat announces once that reading lands.
[infrastructure]
condition_max = 100.0
condition = 55.0

# The Alliance (issue #936). This station is tagged `allied` in every world
# that fields it, and until now it belonged to nobody: a factionless entity is
# never `hostile` to anything and never `friendly` to anything either, so
# "Starbase Alpha" in `assets/worlds/combat_test.toml` was a defence objective
# the defenders had no relationship with. Authoring the faction here rather than
# as a per-world override is deliberate — an allied station is allied in both
# worlds that spawn it (`combat_test`, `default`), and the Harrow are neutral to
# the Alliance in the other one, so nothing outside the combat scenario changes
# hostility as a result.
#
# Since issue #1011, this DOES make the station auto-acquirable as an enemy
# target: `ai_target_selection`'s `hostile_scan_q` reads faction off
# `Or<(With<Ship>, With<StaticPointDefence>)>`, and this station is a
# `StaticPointDefence` combatant (see below), so a hostile raider's untargeted
# "nearest hostile" doctrine can lock it same as any ship. A raider can also
# still reach it through a named `Destroy` directive, which is what
# combat_test's `assault-starbase` override authors — the two routes are
# independent, not alternatives.
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"

# High-fidelity bubble. LOD promotion (`lod_ai_ships`) only runs the weapons /
# target-selection AI (`ai_target_selection`, `ai_phaser_auto_fire`) for hulls
# inside a bubble; a `LodBubble` carrier anchors its own zone and is itself always
# full-fidelity. Without this the station spends most of a fight demoted to
# low-LOD (the player roams to hunt, taking the only other bubble with them),
# where its phaser never runs and it is a sitting duck the raid grinds down for
# zero return — it dealt ZERO damage and died in the combat_test pacing run. The
# 250-unit radius also keeps the raiders SIEGING the station promoted while the
# player is elsewhere, so the defence — theirs and the station's — actually
# happens instead of being dead-reckoned. Smaller than a player hull's bubble on
# purpose: it covers the station's own airspace, not the whole map — the player's
# own 600-unit bubble already promotes the running fight it is flying through.
[lod_bubble]
radius = 250.0

# Autonomous point defence. The station is an AI-operated static combatant: it
# carries only the Tactical systems needed to acquire and fire, never Helm or
# player stations. Its omni phaser covers the immediate defence perimeter,
# buying the defenders time to meet the clocked Harrow raid rather than
# replacing them.

[collider]
# Sized to the hull this station actually draws, at John's request: collision has
# to match visible size.
#
# The recreated starbase preserves the original rig's rendered dimensions,
# baked into its GLB with an identity sidecar: 28.46 x 14.33 x 34.08 on
# screen — a max half-extent of 17.04. The 12 here was seven-tenths of that, so
# the outer five units of the ring carried no collision and ships flew THROUGH
# the visible structure.
#
# A CYLINDER, which is the shape a station is. The Ball this replaced was the
# best of a bad set — `ColliderShape` offered only Ball and Capsule, and
# `Collider::capsule_y` is a cylinder with hemispherical caps, so it can only
# ever be taller than it is wide, which a disc 34 across and 14 tall is not. A
# Ball at the max half-extent was right in the wide axis and over-covered the
# short one by ten units, so a ship crossing directly over the hub stopped dead
# in clear sky. That was the honest cost of having no cylinder; the cylinder now
# exists, so it is not a cost worth paying.
#
# `half_height = 7.16` is HALF the drawn height, 14.325 / 2 — the sidecar's own
# `[extents].size`, not a guess. `radius` stays the max half-extent: a Y-axis
# cylinder has one radius for two horizontal axes, and this hull is 28.46 across
# X against 34.08 across Z, so 17.04 fits Z exactly and stands 2.81 proud of X.
# That residual is deliberate and it is the LAST of it — collision still errs
# outward rather than inward, so the error keeps ships outside a hull rather
# than letting them through one, and it is now confined to a single axis
# instead of two.
shape = "Cylinder"
radius = 17.04
half_height = 7.16
length = 0

[radar_appearance]
colour = [ 0.3, 0.8, 0.6 ]
size = 18
icon = "station"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_starbase_recreated.glb"
# The torus is the procedural stand-in, drawn only while the GLB above is still
# streaming or when it is missing entirely. RENDER-ONLY — the simulation reads
# none of it (the `[collider]` above is the only thing anything collides with),
# so correcting it moves no digest.
#
# Sized off the same measurement the collider is. `alliance_starbase_recreated.model.toml`
# records the drawn hull at 28.46 x 14.33 x 34.08 in its `[extents].size` —
# already through that sidecar's `[base].scale` of [15, 18, 18] — so the stand-in
# wants a 34.08-wide, 14.33-tall envelope. A Bevy `Torus` spans
# `(major_radius + minor_radius) * 2` across and `minor_radius * 2` tall, which
# pins both numbers:
#
#   minor = 14.33 / 2                       = 7.16   (half the measured height)
#   major = 34.08 / 2 - 7.16 = 17.04 - 7.16 = 9.88
#
# The 18 / 4.5 this replaces belonged to the pre-correction era: 45 units across
# and 9 tall, a third wider than the hull and well under its height. It is the
# render half of the same staleness the collider block above fixed — and a
# fallback that size meant the station visibly shrank the moment its GLB
# finished loading.
shape = "torus"
radius = 9.88
minor_radius = 7.16
colour = [ 0.3, 0.8, 0.6 ]

[comms]
range = 800
# On the hail roster (issue #985). Until #984 converted `default.toml` to
# `[script]`, this station reached the roster only as a `[[comms]] from`
# reference id. `hailable` is the replacement — and since #985 deleted the

#
# No `display_name`: the contact label falls through to the entity's
# `EntityName`, which for a world-declared `[[entity]]` is its `name` reference
# id — the SAME string the deleted `[[comms]] from` supplied.
hailable = true

base_files.assets/entities/test/rng_coverage_lancer:
# RNG-coverage escort — A TEST FIXTURE, NOT A SHIPPED HULL (issue #954)
#
# ## Why it lives under `assets/entities/test/` rather than beside the fleet
#
# It carries all three weapon kinds — phasers, blasters and torpedoes — which no
# hull the game actually ships does. `assets/worlds/rng_coverage.toml` fields two
# of them so `tests/rng_determinism.rs`'s determinism guard covers every RNG site
# rather than just the beam one (issue #837), and that is the ONLY thing it is
# for. It was previously `assets/entities/ship_harrow_lancer.toml` — a Harrow
# Escort (Lancer class) sitting in the shipped fleet, on the balance ladder and
# in every "the whole fleet does X" walk, purely to serve one test world.
#
# Every shipped-fleet walk reads `assets/entities/*.toml` at the TOP LEVEL only
# (`include_resolve::tests::shipped_tree::shipped_templates`,
# `authored_ai_pins::entity_stems`, `ai_declaration_manifest::hull_files`,
# `ship::power`'s and `modifiers::coordination`'s fleet walks, the strict-parse
# and torpedo-tube gates in `entities::config`, and `perf::assets::inventory`),
# exactly as they all skip `assets/entities/fragments/`. Sitting one directory
# down is therefore what makes this NOT a fleet hull, and it is why the fleet
# totals those walks pin came down by one hull when it moved.
#
# It is still loaded through the real path: a world names it by `template_path`,
# and on native `WasmTemplateLoader` falls back to
# `entity_includes::resolve_from_disk`, so include composition and the strict
# `deny_unknown_fields` schema apply to it exactly as to a shipped hull.
# `rng_determinism` spawning it every run is what keeps it from rotting.
#
# ## The ids are load-bearing
#
# The bank and tube ids ("lash", "spike", "lance") are deliberately unique
# across the whole asset set: balance events name the weapon by bank/tube id
# alone, so the test classifies a hit as beam / blaster / torpedo by that id.
# Reusing an id another hull already carries would make the classification lie —
# and worse, it would still PASS, having attributed one chokepoint's damage to
# another. Do not rename them.
#
# Tuned to hurt without killing: short ranges and modest damage so a hostile
# escort degrades the player's systems over a minute rather than ending the
# run in ten seconds.

# ── Composed on the shared fragment library (issue #878) ──────────────────────
#
# Like `ship_harrow_patrol.toml`, this hull flies no manoeuvre of its own — its
# Engines and Steering axes were byte-identical to the fleet's stateless
# defaults — so its six helm axes, Shields, Comms and all five target selectors
# come from `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. See that hull's header for the
# full note on the two declarations still authored below (`[captain_console.ai]`,
# the stand-down captain of #912; and `[power]` + `[power.ai_policy]`,
# re-authored whole because the baseline's `helm` rule gates its elevation on
# `red_alert` and a Harrow raises the alert only around combat, not for the
# whole transit, so inheriting the guard would pin the drive at 2 for exactly
# the leg that needs it — issue #923; corrected #955).
#
# The `../` is not decoration: an `includes` reference resolves relative to the
# DECLARING file's directory (`include_resolve::canonical_include_path`), so from
# this subdirectory the fragment library is one level up.
#
# `[torpedoes.ai]` stays authored here too: the baseline carries no per-weapon
# declaration, because a hull without weapons owes none and a hull with them owes
# one per magazine, bank and tube.
includes = ["../fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml"]

name = "entity.rng_coverage_lancer.name"
tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"]
faction = "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc"

[target]
tags = ["ship"]
threat_level = "medium"
description = "entity.rng_coverage_lancer.target.description"

# Deliberately tanky. The observable torpedo damage in this scenario is THIS
# hull's torpedoes landing on the shieldless player (see the player-ship shield
# override in the world file) — torpedo damage dealt to an NPC is invisible to
# the report. For that the two escorts have to stay alive and keep firing across
# the whole run, so their hull outlasts the player's return fire.
#
# 2000 -> 800 (#915 tuning pass). 800 is an INSTRUMENTATION number, not a
# balance one, and since #954 it is not on the fleet's class ladder at all —
# that was the audit finding this hull's relocation settles. It is sized so the
# escort survives long enough to fire all three weapon kinds: a light hull dies
# before it has, and the coverage world stops covering.
[hull]
hull_integrity = 800.0

# Single omni arc, as on every other NPC hull: NPCs have no `[shields]`
# station, so the auto-generated `[[system]]` entry is ownerless and `ai_only`.
[[shield_arc]]
id = "all"
label = "shield_arc.all.label"
center_deg = 0
width_deg = 360
max_hp = 5
regen_per_sec = 0.0

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 4.0
length = 10.0
# A ship is a MOBILE contact, so another hull's authored
# `hazard_ignore_size_ratio` may size-ignore it (issue #958). Static
# terrain omits this field and is avoided at any relative size.
movable = true

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.9, 0.3, 0.1]
size = 10.0
icon = "destroyer"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/dynasty_battleship.glb"
shape = "cuboid"
size = [8.0, 3.0, 14.0]
colour = [0.9, 0.3, 0.1]

[helm_console]
max_speed = 10.0
max_reverse_speed = 5.0
acceleration = 4.0
deceleration = 10.0
max_yaw_rate = 0.2
# Escort hull, so it takes the Harrow light-hull low-speed turn trade.
low_speed_turn_boost = 0.3
max_bank_deg = 5.0

[weapons_console]

# Omni phaser. 360° so the beam site fires without waiting on a facing
# solution — this hull exists to make damage happen, not to be tactically
# interesting.
[[weapons_console.phaser_banks]]
id = "lash"
facing_deg = 0.0
fire_arc_deg = 360.0
auto_arc_deg = 360.0
beam_range = 90.0
beam_damage_per_sec = 1.5
beam_duration_secs = 6.0
cooldown_secs = 3.0
# No pierce: the beam's job here is to strip the player's shields, because
# NPC torpedo auto-fire only unlocks once the target's online shield facings
# are at zero. A high-pierce beam would bypass the shields, leave them up, and
# the torpedo chokepoint would never fire.
shield_pierce = 0.0
beam_color = [1.0, 0.3, 0.1, 1.0]

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). One unconditional rule: when the host offers the bank a
  # decision it fires. Every readiness gate — availability, cooldown, range,
  # arc, target validity — is the host's and is unchanged; the policy is the
  # authored DECISION layered on top, and `idle = true` is how a bank opts out.
  [weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.phaser_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "phaser_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_phaser"

# Omni blaster bank, matched to the phaser's engagement envelope so the
# blaster chokepoint fires whenever the beam one does.
[[weapons_console.blaster_banks]]
id = "spike"
facing_deg = 0.0
fire_arc_deg = 360.0
volley_count = 2
volley_interval_secs = 0.5
cooldown_secs = 3.0
projectile_speed = 60.0
collision_radius = 1.0
visual_scale = 0.5
damage = 2
shield_pierce = 0.3
range = 80.0

  # Open-fire policy for this bank (issue #781), AUTHORED rather than
  # synthesised (#885b). Mirror of the phaser banks on the `blaster_fire`
  # channel: unconditional, with the host still enforcing availability,
  # cooldown, range, arc and target validity before the volley starts.
  [weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[weapons_console.blaster_banks.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "blaster_fire"
  when = "fact(red_alert) >= param(min_alert_to_fire)"
  verb = "fire_blaster"

# Why this fixture still reaches the torpedo damage chokepoint under the
# shields-aware impact model (issue #929). A round now delivers `damage_shields`
# into a live arc and `damage_hull` into a downed one, and this hull authors
# `damage_shields = 0` — so a round spent on a screened target would land
# nothing, never take the `hull_damage > 0` branch, and draw no
# `SimStream::TorpedoDamage`. That is not what happens here:
# `rng_determinism.rs::strip_local_ship_shields` zeroes every facing on the
# player before the window it measures, precisely so the tube's own
# `fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0` guard will open. A zeroed facing reads 0,
# the round takes the shields-down branch, and all 3 points land on hull exactly
# as they did when `damage_hull` bypassed the shield system unconditionally.
# Keep those two halves together: raise `damage_shields` here and the fixture
# still works; drop the shield-stripping there and the chokepoint goes quiet.
[torpedoes]
count = 40
burst_interval_secs = 0.4
damage_hull = 3
damage_shields = 0
speed = 30.0
turn_rate_deg_per_sec = 120.0
lifespan = 12.0

  # Load + launch policy for this tube (issue #782), AUTHORED rather than

  # the round would strike is down (issue #956 moved that second clause out of
  # `auto_fire_torpedo` and into the tube's own guard). Loaded state, magazine
  # stock, target validity, range and arc stay host-side gates.
  [torpedoes.tubes.ai]
  # The RED-ALERT fire gate (issue #872), the same guard text every armed hull
  # authors. A Harrow is ALWAYS ARMED — threshold 0, which `fact(red_alert)`
  # clears whether the alert is up or not. It has no bridge crew to call red
  # alert, and its captain policy stands the alert down out of combat, so a hull
  # that waited for one would never open fire and never start the fight it
  # exists to start.
  param = { min_alert_to_fire = 0.0 }

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]
  priority = 0
  channel = "torpedo_load"

  verb = "load_torpedo"

  [[torpedoes.tubes.ai.rule]]

  channel = "torpedo_launch"
