# Torpedo magazine — two axes on one authored block.
#
# GRANT: always grant a claim the host has already found legal. The offline +
# non-empty gates remain the hard authority; this rule is the authored arbiter
# layered on top, and it is where a hull would ration rounds between its tubes.
#
# CONSERVATION (issue #943): whether a launch the ship has already authorised may
# SPEND its round here, or should hold it for later in the mission. Resolved
# inside `handle_fire_torpedo`, the one consumer of an admitted `FireTorpedo`, so
# a human Tactical operator and an AI backfill meet this guard identically — the
# per-tube `torpedo_launch` doctrine gates only the AI, and a gate that
# constrains NPCs alone is how a player empties the whole magazine into wave one.
#
# `rounds_per_threat` is a host reading, not an authored number: every round the
# ship still HAS — the magazine PLUS whatever is already parked in the tubes —
# divided by the mission threat still ahead, which the SCENARIO publishes as the
# world counter `mission_threat_remaining`. A world that publishes none leaves
# the ratio unbounded and this rule always fires, because pacing is something a
# mission asks for and never something a hull decides for itself.
#
# `min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5` reads "keep one round for every TWO things still
# coming". Before retuning it, understand what kind of gate it is: a ONE-WAY
# LATCH. `rounds_aboard` only ever FALLS inside a mission, and the threat count
# only falls when something DIES — so a hull that dips under its own reserve
# stops firing, stops killing the thing that would bring the count down, and
# never climbs back over the line. Whatever is authored here is not a soft
# brake. It is a floor the ship must never be pushed below mid-mission.
#
# 0.5 is chosen for the margin it leaves, not for a tidy identity:
#
#   * The middle of the mission stays open. Over every position combat_test can
#     put this hull in while it still carries half its payload or more, the
#     reserve clears at least 4 rounds — two full volleys — against the wave in
#     front of it. A wave that survives one volley is a wave that never dies,
#     and a wave that never dies freezes the threat count and the latch with it.
#   * Nothing is stranded. At the last unit of threat the floor is half a round,
#     so anything still aboard clears the gate and can be spent on the last
#     fight. A reserve measured against the magazine COUNTER rather than the
#     rounds aboard strands the parked volley whatever this number is, because
#     the counter is debited the moment a tube starts loading.
#
# What it trades away is the front of the mission. The floor at eight published
# waves is 4 rounds rather than 8, so an engagement lasting as long as the hull
# is willing to keep shooting may now take 10 of the 12 rounds while the whole
# schedule is still published, where 1.0 capped it at 6. That ceiling is a
# licence rather than a forecast — flown for real the destroyer spends 6 across
# that stretch either way, because the engagement ends before the gate does —
# but it is what 0.5 permits, and it is the price of the margin above.
#
# The tidy identity is what 1.0 bought (issue #943): the reserve came to exactly
# one round at the last unit of threat, so on paper nothing could ever be
# stranded. It shipped with ZERO margin and it broke. Against the old asteroid
# layout the destroyer bottomed out at exactly 7 rounds against 7 remaining
# waves — a ratio of exactly 1.0, the last reading the gate still passes. #946
# reshuffled which rock lands in which cell (same radii, same split), that moved
# the engagement by one round, the ratio fell under, the latch shut, and
# combat_test's wave chain stalled at wave 2 with the hull holding rounds it
# would never fire.
#
# All of it is measured, not asserted by hand.
# `the_shipped_destroyer_spends_its_whole_payload_across_the_eight_wave_mission`
# (`src/console/weapons/server_tests.rs`) walks this doctrine through the real
# torpedo system over the world's whole authored schedule, INCLUDING a wave that
# outlives the engagement fought against it, and states the latch directly on
# the doctrine.
# `combat_test_paces_the_player_magazine_against_the_whole_eight_wave_threat`
# (`tests/headless_runner.rs`) flies it for real and prints the magazine's
# shape bucketed by remaining threat, (entered, lowest) per bucket:
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 2), 6: (2, 2), 5: (2, 2)}. Read a bucket as a STRETCH OF
# THE MISSION rather than as one engagement — since #960 a wave arrives on its
# own clock whether or not the last one is dead, so the top bucket spans wave 1
# and the opening of wave 2, and bottoms lower than the death-gated chain used
# to show. Ten of the twelve rounds go while six or more waves are still
# published; the last two then sit under the floor (2/6 and 2/5 are both below
# 0.5) until the count reaches 4. At 1.0 the same run reads
# {8: (12, 6), 7: (6, 6)} and stops there: the latch shuts the moment wave 1
# dies, and wave 2 never does.
#
# `sole_objective_count = 1` is the carve-out, and it counts NAMED Destroy
# targets rather than doctrine entries. A world's `spawn_entity` override
# APPENDS its brief to the template's standing orders — doctrine reconciles by
# `id`, and an instance override may not remove what the template authored — so
# combat_test's raid cruisers carry their template's untargeted
# `destroy-hostiles` alongside the `assault-starbase` the world hands them: two
# entries, one named target, one engagement they will not outlive. Those spend
# freely. A hull whose brief names no target reads 0 and paces — which is the
# player's destroyer, the ship #943 was filed about.
[torpedoes.ai]
param = { min_rounds_per_threat = 0.5, sole_objective_count = 1.0 }

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_magazine_grant"
when = "true"
verb = "grant_torpedo_round"

[[torpedoes.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "torpedo_conservation"
when = "fact(targeted_objective_count) == param(sole_objective_count) or fact(rounds_per_threat) >= param(min_rounds_per_threat)"
verb = "release_torpedo"

# Reactor + battery. Transcribed from `PowerConfig::default()`, which is what
# this hull ran on before it declared the section: authoring
# `[power.ai_policy]` cannot be done without bringing `[power]` into existence,
# and the three fields are required, so they are written out at exactly the
# values the Rust default supplied.
[power]
capacity = 100.0
rates = [ 6, 5, 4, 2, -2, -6 ]
emergency_threshold = 25.0

# DELIBERATELY the pre-#1003 single-floor shape ON THE BATTERY AXIS: no
# `min_restore_*` pair and `min_reserve_weapons` still at 10. This fixture exists
# for RNG/decode coverage in one test world, it is outside
# `assets/entities/*.toml` (and so outside the fleet-baseline pins), and it never
# fights long enough for a battery shed ladder to matter — so it carries the
# smallest policy that still decodes rather than a copy of the fleet's
# hysteresis. See `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` for the shape every hull the
# fleet actually flies authors. That single-floor battery shape is UNCHANGED and
# is still the exercised one.
#
# THE THRUST AXIS IS A DIFFERENT MATTER, and this hull now carries the fleet's
# band there. The "never long enough to matter" claim above was measured false
# once `5672b09a` seeded the `thrust` fact from the real throttle: lancer_alpha
# flipped helm 18 times in an 1800-tick `rng_coverage` run, sixteen of them
# inside 38 ticks, throttle dithering across 0.70 with the battery at 57-59 —
# nowhere near the 50 floor above. The battery ladder was indeed never reached;
# the strobe was the THRUST threshold with no band, and it is the same defect
# the fleet's hulls carried.
#
# Banding it here rather than keeping the raw shape is a deliberate call. [ai]
# This fixture's purpose is coverage of the five seeded DAMAGE-DRAW sites, not
# coverage of power-allocation chatter: a hull whose speed cap strobes at 30 Hz
# flies a different path every time the tuning next to it moves, which makes the
# draw sites it reaches LESS stable, not more. Nothing here exercises the
# thrust-axis rule shape for its own sake, so there is no coverage to lose. The
# HOLD rule below is the one addition; the elevate and baseline are untouched.
[power.ai_policy.param]
thrust_threshold = 0.7
# [ai] Band width 0.1, matching the fleet. See fleet_baseline for the rationale.
thrust_release_threshold = 0.6
min_reserve_helm = 50.0
min_reserve_weapons = 10.0
min_reserve_baseline = 0.0

# HOLD, above the elevate: helm is already at 3 and the throttle has not yet
# fallen past the RELEASE floor, so keep it. Reads `min_reserve_helm` on the
# battery axis exactly as the elevate does — the single floor is preserved, and
# only the thrust axis carries a band.
[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 15
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(power_helm) >= 3 and fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_release_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(thrust) >= param(thrust_threshold) and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_helm)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "helm"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 10
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(red_alert) > 0 and fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_weapons)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 3

[[power.ai_policy.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "weapons"
when = "fact(battery_pct) >= param(min_reserve_baseline)"
verb = "set_power_group_allocation"
level = 2
base_files.assets/entities/tractor_tug.toml:
# Tractor tug — the probe-world operator for the tractor beam (issue #1156).
#
# A deliberately lean hull that exists to exercise ONE mechanism end to end: an
# engineering-owned `[[system]] kind = "tractor"`, its own `[power_groups.tractor]`
# power group, a damage entry so it can be knocked out, and a `[tractor]` table
# carrying the coupling terms. It is NOT a shipped combat hull and is not flown in
# any scenario — it is the fixture `assets/worlds/probe_tractor.toml` puts a beam
# on, kept out of `alliance_destroyer.toml` on purpose so no shipped hull's folded
# system-hull (and therefore no committed world's digest) moves for this slice.
# The demo destroyer gains the tractor in a later integration, not here.
#
# It flies nothing: the probe drives the operator's position and its Tactical lock
# from the test, and the beam's engage/release through the ordinary admitted-command
# path, so the tug needs no helm, weapons or AI policy of its own.

tags = ["ship"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"
# Authored mass (issue #1154). Read by the later helm-penalty slice (#1157), not
# by this one — the coupling geometry takes transforms and the offset only.
mass = 12000.0

[mesh]
# Shares the courier silhouette; a bespoke .glb would buy the probe nothing.
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[collider]
shape = "Capsule"
radius = 0.6
length = 1.5
# No helm capability (see header), so per the movable/helm invariant this
# stays the static-terrain default rather than claiming to be a flyable hull.
movable = false

[radar_appearance]
colour = [0.2, 0.8, 0.9]
size = 5.0
icon = "ship"

# Power: no `[power]` block, so the reactor takes the default 100-unit capacity /
# resting-total-6 profile. The tug's one small group (tractor, nominal level 2)
# draws well under that, so the battery stays charged and the group rests at its
# nominal level without the probe having to nurse it.

# ── The tractor's own power group ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Declared here rather than shared with helm/weapons/shields: the tractor draws
# its own allocation, and an interruption checks THIS group's level against the
# `[tractor]` min_power_level below.
[power_groups.tractor]
label = "entity.tractor_tug.power_groups.tractor.label"
default_level = 2
min_level = 1
max_level = 4

# ── The tractor's damage entry ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# So the beam can be damaged to Disabled — the interruption the probe drives by
# knocking this system down.
[[hull.system_hull]]
system_id = "tractor"
max_hp = 30
damaged_threshold_pct = 0.5
disabled_threshold_pct = 0.15
debuff_magnitude = 0.15

# ── Engineering owns the tractor ─────────────────────────────────────────────
[[station]]
id = "engineering"
name = "Engineering"
description = "entity.tractor_tug.station.engineering.description"
rank = "Ltn."
short_code = "ENG"

[[station.rating]]
name = "Std"
automated_systems = []

# ── The tractor system ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# First-class, engineering-owned, power-grouped: the admitted target for
# EngageTractor / ReleaseTractor, admission-gated exactly like any other
# station-owned system.
[[system]]
id = "tractor"
kind = "tractor"
station = "engineering"
power_group = "tractor"

# ── The coupling terms ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# All authored (AGENTS.md rule 11): the reach, where the held load rides in the
# operator's own frame (120 units astern), and the lowest power-group level the
# beam holds at.
[tractor]
range = 600.0
coupling_offset = [0.0, 0.0, -120.0]
min_power_level = 2

# ── The tow-load helm penalty curve (issue #1157) ────────────────────────────
# The mass → penalty curve, authored here rather than inlined (AGENTS.md rule
# 11): while the beam holds a target, the operator's top speed AND turn rate are
# cut by `max_penalty * m / (m + half_penalty_mass)` of the held target's own
# authored mass. `half_penalty_mass` is the knee — a load of this mass costs half
# the cap — set at #1154's default entity mass so an unauthored hulk is a
# felt-but-fair tow; `max_penalty` is the ceiling a laden freighter approaches
# but never reaches. A buoy near zero mass is barely felt; a heavy hull is
# severe; both from these two numbers.
[tractor.tow_load]
half_penalty_mass = 10000.0
max_penalty = 0.8
base_files.assets/entities/umbilical_berth.toml:
# Umbilical berth — the passive docked partner for issue #1160.
#
# The far end of the transfer umbilical: a hull that can be DOCKED WITH (it authors
# a `[dock]` table, whose presence opts it in and reads its dock markers from the
# `dock_probe` rig variant sidecar) and carries an `[infrastructure]` ledger with
# the same `reserve_fuel` capacity the operator delivers into — starting empty, with
# headroom up to its ceiling. It runs no dock and no umbilical of its own: only the
# operator docks, and only the operator's umbilical moves the capacity. It never
# moves under its own power.

tags = ["structure"]
faction = "aaaaaaaa-1111-4111-8111-aaaaaaaaaaaa"

[mesh]
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier_recreated_dock_probe.glb"
variant = "dock_probe"
shape = "sphere"
colour = []

[radar_appearance]

mate_tolerance = 4.0
undock_clear_distance = 120.0
min_power_level = 2

[[system]]

[dock]
range = 200.0
engage_distance = 400.0

mate_tolerance = 4.0

# the units-per-second it moves, the direction from the operator's point of view
# (deliver = operator → docked partner), and the lowest power-group level the flow
# runs at.
[umbilical]
capacity = "reserve_fuel"
rate = 20.0
direction = "deliver"
min_power_level = 2

base_files.assets/join/join-codes.toml:
# Authored join-code format data (issue #1111). THIS FILE is the ONE place the
# join-identifier scheme is written down, and the one a designer edits.
#
# assets/join/join-codes.json beside it is a GENERATED artifact, committed
# because three consumers must read the table with no parser and no build step:
# the phone fetches it as plain JSON, tests/client/*.test.js read it from disk,
# and worker-rendezvous/src/registry.js has it bundled into the Cloudflare
# Worker by esbuild. None of those three can parse TOML. `node
# scripts/build-client.mjs` regenerates the JSON from this file, and
# tests/client/join-codes-data.test.js fails if the committed JSON has drifted
# from it — the same discipline as the LOD manifest's `npm run lods:check`.
#
# Design source: docs/gdd/systems/native-network-foundation.md "Join-code
# model" and pasm/spec/design/p2p-design-deltas.yaml decision
# p2p-human-readable-join-namespaces.

# Wire/format revision. gui/join-code.js refuses a table whose format_version
# it does not implement (JOIN_CODE_FORMAT_VERSION), rather than reading fields
# that may have moved.
format_version = 1

[suffix]
# Eight typed letters. The alphabet deliberately EXCLUDES L, because L
# normalises to I — a letter that can never survive canonicalisation must never
# be minted, or the printed code would not round-trip through the very
# normalisation that makes it typeable. O and I stay in: they are the canonical
# forms of 0 and 1. J stays distinct and is minted normally.
#
# WHY EIGHT AND NOT FIVE. The code is the ONLY secret in front of a game: the
# join stamp is public (every host serves it), so anyone holding the code can
# join, open a relay and act as a crew member. Five letters over this alphabet
# is 25^5 ≈ 9.77e6 codes — 23.2 bits — and a native host accepting LAN joins
# directly (issue #1353) was measured answering ~2,340 wrong guesses a second
# to a single machine that reconnected between batches, which walks that
# keyspace in about 35 MINUTES of expected search. Eight letters is 25^8 ≈
# 1.526e11 — 37.15 bits — which is ~377 days of expected search at that same
# unthrottled rate, before the per-source and global attempt limits in
# src/native_host/direct_join.rs take the achievable rate down by another three
# orders of magnitude. The cost is three more letters to read off a viewscreen;
# the QR carries the whole code either way, and both worker and native legs
# inherit the stronger scheme because all three readers read THIS file.
length = 8
alphabet = "ABCDEFGHIJKMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
# Punctuation a player adds while reading a code aloud, dropped before the
# comparison. `_` is here as well as being the separator inside a full code:
# gui/join-code.js decides which shape it is looking at BEFORE stripping.
strip = "-_ \t"

[suffix.normalise]
# The confusable map, applied after upper-casing.
"0" = "O"
"1" = "I"
"L" = "I"

[namespaces]
# Two stable project GUIDs, one per join type, so a suffix typed into the crew
# field can never silently resolve a fleet host. These values are permanent —
# changing one orphans every printed code of that type.
#
# `client` is what a phone/console types; `server` admits ship hosts to a fleet
# (issue #1114 owns joining it; #1111 only needs it to EXIST so a wrong-type
# answer is distinguishable from an unknown one).
client = "2f6b0a11-9c4e-4d7a-8f31-5b90c2d47e18"
server = "8d13c7a4-0e52-49bb-9a6c-4f27ed3b90d1"

[version]
# One version GUID marks a compatible release. Bump it when a release can no
# longer join a host built from the previous one, so the rendezvous can answer
# "version-mismatch" instead of "unknown" for a suffix registered under an
# older build. ADVISORY discovery help only: the authoritative protocol/content
# check is the host's own delivery stamp handshake (src/delivery/stamp.rs,
# delivery::check_join_stamp).
guid = "5c0a3e91-7b18-4f26-8d43-9e61af07c25b"

[limits]
# Registry bounds (issue #1111). The rendezvous registry is an untrusted-facing
# service: every one of these exists to stop one socket costing the Durable
# Object unbounded work or memory. See worker-rendezvous/src/registry.js.
#
# How long a host record survives without its socket being seen again. The
# record normally dies with the socket; this is the sweep for the case where a
# close event never arrives.
record_ttl_seconds = 43200
# Lookups (resolve + join) one socket may make before it is cut off. Codes are
# private, so an unbounded socket could walk the namespace — but note that this
# bound is charged to a SOCKET, which a guesser simply reconnects to reset. It
# is the cheapest way to end one abusive connection, not the rate limit; the
# limits that survive a reconnect are per-SOURCE and global, and they live in
# src/native_host/direct_join.rs (AdmissionBudgets) because they are transport
# plane rather than authored scheme.
max_lookups_per_connection = 60
# Joiners one host record may hold at once, counting only sockets that have
# RESOLVED THE CODE. Sockets that upgraded and never joined have a budget of
# their own (AdmissionBudgets::unjoined_total) so that silence cannot spend the
# room's places.
max_peers_per_record = 32
# How many player-ship slots one fleet may hold, the owner's own included
# (issue #1114). This is a DESIGN number — how big a fleet the game is meant to
# field — and it is deliberately smaller than `max_peers_per_record`, which is
# the service's memory bound on any record and knows nothing about ships. The
# fleet owner refuses a further host with `fleet-full` before the record's own
# cap is ever reached.
max_fleet_hosts = 4
# What one ship host may say about ITSELF in a fleet roster (issue #1114). The
# display name and the hull's template path are the only two fields a member
# writes, and the fleet lead re-broadcasts the whole roster to every admitted
# host on every change — so these are the bounds that stop one member amplifying
# an arbitrary payload across the fleet. Protocol hygiene, not a design number:
# gui/host-mesh.js carries a parse-time default for each so an older table still
# loads. Anything longer is truncated, never refused; a hull path that is not a
# non-empty string reads as "no ship chosen yet".
max_slot_name_length = 48
max_slot_ship_path_length = 160
# Longest accepted code string on a resolve/join frame — comfortably longer
# than PROJECT_GUID_VERSION_GUID_SUFFIX, short enough that parsing is cheap.
# (There is no stamp bound here: no frame carries a delivery stamp. The
# compatibility handshake is in-band, host to phone, and the service stores
# nothing about either build.)
max_code_length = 160
# How long a record survives its host's SIGNALLING SOCKET dying before the
# service drops it for good (issue #1115). A record normally dies with an
# EXPLICIT host-close; this is the window an ORDINARY transient loss — a
# Durable Object hiccup, a phone radio killing a backgrounded tab's socket, a
# brief network blip — has to reclaim the SAME code (by presenting the
# resume secret its own `hosted` frame carried) before it goes cold. Distinct
# from and much shorter than `record_ttl_seconds` above, which is the idle
# sweep for a record whose close event never arrived at all. 120s comfortably
# outlasts several rounds of the host's own reconnect backoff
# (gui/connection-manager.js's nextBackoffDelay: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 30s,
# 30s, …) without holding a dead code open indefinitely.
reclaim_grace_seconds = 120
# The most grace-held records ONE Durable Object instance will carry at once
# (issue #1115). A deliberate leave/host-close drops a host's record on the
# spot, so only a socket that genuinely DIES enters grace — this bounds a flood
# of separate dying sockets, not one looping socket, and over the cap a further
# loss drops its record for good rather than parking it un-hostable for the
# whole window. Defence in depth alongside the per-connection bounds above.
max_grace_records = 256

# ── The WebSocket game relay (issue #1113) ───────────────────────────────────
# When a joiner's direct WebRTC ladder is exhausted, the SAME rendezvous socket
# carries the game's own frames instead. That turns a signalling socket into a
# data path, so it needs bounds of its own: a signalling socket exchanges a
# handful of SDP blobs and then goes quiet, while a relay session carries every
# command and every snapshot for as long as the mission lasts.
#
# Joiners one record may carry over the relay at once, counted separately from
# `max_peers_per_record`. Deliberately much smaller: a relayed crew member
# costs the Durable Object real bandwidth every tick, where a peer that only
# ever signalled costs it two SDP blobs and then nothing.
max_relay_peers_per_record = 8
# Largest single relayed game frame, in bytes. THE SAME NUMBER THE DIRECT PATH
# HAS TO FIT, and that is the whole reason for it: a DataChannel's ceiling is
# the SDP-negotiated `max-message-size`, 262144 bytes between two Chromiums and
# the smallest ceiling any browser pair negotiates in practice (see the note in
# gui/rendezvous-transport.js). A relay ceiling BELOW it would mean a payload
# that crosses a good network perfectly well cannot cross a bad one — a mission
# that works direct and fails relayed, which is the exact failure this fallback
# exists to prevent, and it failed silently.
#
# The two payload classes that scale with content are WorldData (one
# EntitySnapshot per STATIC entity; the largest world in assets/worlds authors
# 17 [[entity]] blocks) and the per-tick snapshot (dynamic entities — hundreds
# of asteroids at worst, a few tens of KB). The SECOND is the one that can
# approach this bound, not the first. tests/relay_frame_budget.rs measures both
# against this number rather than calling them "comfortably" under it.
#
# Still far below anything that would let one socket park megabytes inside the
# Durable Object: the queue depths below are what bound a mailbox's total.
max_relay_frame_bytes = 262144
# Bounded queue depth per relay peer, per delivery class. This is the
# lossy/reliable split made structural: the snapshot queue DROPS its oldest
# entries once full, because a late snapshot is worthless and the next tick
# supersedes it, while the reliable queue may not drop anything at all — a
# silently dropped command would fork the guarantee the game protocol makes
# about its own reliable class. A reliable queue that fills is therefore a dead
# session, closed and said so, rather than a quietly lossy one.
max_relay_queue_reliable = 256
max_relay_queue_snapshot = 32
# The SENDER's half of the same rule, advertised to both ends on `relay-ready`.
# A WebSocket is reliable and ordered, so a relay would silently upgrade the
# snapshot class into a reliable one unless the sender sheds; once its socket's
# own `bufferedAmount` is past this many bytes, a snapshot frame is dropped
# rather than queued behind the backlog. Reliable frames are never shed there —
# the socket buffers them. Browsers and tungstenite both report
# `bufferedAmount`; a Durable Object's WebSocket does not, which is why this
# bound belongs to whoever is sending rather than to the service.
max_relay_send_buffer_bytes = 262144

# ── Deny-list ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Words never minted and never accepted, in ordinary spelling: gui/join-code.js
# canonicalises each entry before comparing, so one row refuses every
# confusable spelling of the word (LOGIN also refuses IOGIN, HELLO also refuses
# HE110).
#
# A word is matched ANYWHERE INSIDE a canonicalised suffix, not only as the
# whole of it. That is what keeps this list meaningful now the suffix is longer
# than the words on it: a code is refused for READING as one of these, and
# `QRAPESVW` reads as one exactly as `RAPES` did. (At five letters the two
# rules were the same rule; nothing about an entry's meaning changed.) The cost
# to minting is negligible — ~36 words × 4 positions / 25^5 ≈ 1.5e-5 of draws
# are redrawn — and the ceiling in mintSuffix bounds it regardless.
#
# Every entry must therefore be no LONGER than `suffix.length` after
# canonicalisation, or it could never match — tests/client/join-code.test.js
# checks that.
#
# `reason` is for the next person reading the list, not for the player: the
# phone only ever says "that is not a code we hand out".

[[deny]]
word = "ADMIN"
reason = "misleading: reads as a privileged account rather than a room code"

[[deny]]

reason = "misleading: reads as a diagnostic mode"

[[deny]]

base_files.assets/models/alliance_courier.dock_prob:
# Dock-probe rig variant for issue #1159 — the docking probe's dock markers.
#
# A dedicated `dock_probe` VARIANT sidecar over the shipped `alliance_courier.glb`
# so the docking probe world can field hulls that DECLARE DOCK MARKERS in the
# ordinary rig-marker vocabulary — the same `[markers.<name>]` blocks that carry
# engines and hardpoints — without touching the courier's own default sidecar or
# the shipped destroyer (whose committed digest must not move; destroyer docking
# is deferred to #1164 S11a). A marker whose name begins with `dock` is a dock
# marker; a hull whose sidecar declares none can never be docked with.
#
# Identity base on purpose: this is a headless test fixture, and an identity rig
# keeps the mate geometry the probe asserts on readable — a marker authored here
# is exactly the ship-local point it reads as. The two dock plates sit on the
# port and starboard beams facing outward, so two hulls drawn up alongside each
# other mate plate-to-plate.

[base]
offset = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
rotation = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
scale = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]

# Port dock plate: 5 units to port (-X), facing outward to port.
[markers.dock_port]
position = [-5.0, 0.0, 0.0]
direction = [-1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Starboard dock plate: 5 units to starboard (+X), facing outward to starboard.
[markers.dock_starboard]
position = [5.0, 0.0, 0.0]
direction = [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The docking fixtures share the courier's simplified geometry (#1239), but
# retain this variant's identity base and authoritative dock markers. Do not
# reuse the default courier billboard: it was captured with a different base.
[[lod]]
max_distance = 15.0
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier.glb"

[[lod]]
max_distance = 100.0
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier_lod1.glb"
tier_rig = "identity"

[[lod]]
model = "assets/models/alliance_courier_lod2.glb"
tier_rig = "identity"
base_files.assets/models/alliance_courier.model.tom:
# Rig for assets/models/alliance_courier.glb (Alliance Courier, the
# single-station player hull).
#
# Raw GLB frame: the hull runs along Z, broad stern at -Z (half-width 0.55),
# tapering to a bow at +Z (half-width 0.08). Same orientation as the
# destroyer, so the same [base].rotation of 180 deg about Y applies: it turns
# the raw +Z bow into ship-local -Z, which is Bevy's forward.
#
# Marker positions are in RAW-GLB space, not post-base space — the base rig
# (offset/rotation/scale) is applied to them at resolve time by
# ModelMarkers::resolve_world_position. So markers here read "backwards":
# engines at raw -Z end up at the ship's stern, and camera_fore at raw +Z ends
# up at the bow. [extents] below, by contrast, ARE post-base (raw * scale +
# offset).

[base]
offset = [ 0, -0.0623404, 0 ]
rotation = [ 0, 3.14, 0 ]
scale = [ 0.4, 0.4, 0.4 ]

base_files.assets/scenarios.demo.toml:
# Demo scenario manifest (issue #917).
#
# A curated alternate to `assets/scenarios.toml`: same `[[scenario]]` schema
# (shared with the mod-pack manifests from #759/#760 — see that file's header
# comment), listing only the scenarios and per-scenario playable hulls the
# public demo build should offer. Loaded INSTEAD OF the base manifest when the
# host is started with `?manifest=assets/scenarios.demo.toml`; dev/default
# launches (no query param) keep fetching the base manifest untouched, so the
# full catalogue is unaffected.
#
# Curation never edits the referenced world TOML: `combat_test.toml` still
# authors all four Alliance hulls in its own `[[available_ships]]` list. The
# optional `ships` field below is an allowlist of `template_path` values —
# the pre-load catalog (`world::manifest::build_catalog`) filters the world's
# ship list down to just these, in the world's own authored order, and
# `wasm_get_scenario_catalog` is what both the host UI and connected phones
# read. The two entries below keep the world's authored order: the Destroyer is
# the first/default card and the Cruiser follows it. Because more than one ship
# survives curation, the pre-load arbiter shows the regular ship picker rather
# than auto-selecting a hull (server.html's ship selection logic, issue #623).
#
# `[content]` (issue #986) mirrors the base manifest's content identity: the
# demo curates the same shipped assets, so a mod pack compatible with the base
# is compatible here too. Keep this in step with `assets/scenarios.toml`.

[content]
id = "phoenix-base"
epoch = 1

[[scenario]]
id = "combat_test"
world = "assets/worlds/combat_test.toml"
ships = ["assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml", "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"]
base_files.assets/scenarios.toml:
# Base scenario manifest (issue #754).
#
# The authoritative list of *selectable root worlds* — the scenarios a host may
# choose before any world is loaded. Each entry references a world TOML under
# `assets/worlds/`. Display metadata (title/description) and the per-scenario
# player-ship list are read from the referenced world's `[global]` and
# `[[available_ships]]` sections, so this manifest stays a thin index and the
# authored data is single-sourced in the world file.
#
# Only regular selectable roots are listed. Composition-only and test-infra
# worlds (patrol, reinforcements, default, the probe_* / duel / rng_coverage test
# worlds) are loaded additively via `extra_worlds`, trigger actions, or the
# headless harness and are deliberately absent here.
#
# This schema is shared with mod-pack scenario manifests (issues #759/#760):
# `[[scenario]]` entries with an `id`, a `world` path, and an optional `label`.
#
# `[content]` (issue #986) declares the host side of the mod-pack compatibility
# contract: the identity + revision an uploaded pack's `[pack.requires]` must
# match to be accepted. Bump `epoch` when shipped content changes in a way that
# would invalidate packs authored against the previous revision.

[content]
id = "phoenix-base"
epoch = 1

[[scenario]]
id = "combat_test"
world = "assets/worlds/combat_test.toml"

# Falling Skyway (issue #1034, parent #852) — the first Thin Margin scenario.
# Selectable from the host panel alongside combat_test; its title, description
# and single playable hull are read from the world's own `[global]` and
# `[[available_ships]]`, so nothing about the mission is restated here.
#
# Deliberately NOT added to `assets/scenarios.demo.toml`: the public demo build
# is combat_test with the Alliance Destroyer and Alliance Cruiser, and what the
# demo curates is a separate decision from what the dev catalogue offers.
[[scenario]]
id = "falling_skyway"
world = "assets/worlds/falling_skyway.toml"
base_files.assets/worlds/combat_test.toml:
# Combat Test Scenario (#475, re-authored for #960 + #936)
#
# An 8-wave defence scenario that exercises the full combat stack:
#   - on_timer wave clock + on_all_destroyed completion/victory (#470, #960)
#   - NPC shields backend + Sensors panel rendering (#471, #473)
#   - Rebalanced Harrow fleet + Axiom Station (#474)
#   - Alliance-Harrow mutual hostility (#472)
#
# Layout: concentric rings centred on the star at the origin.
#   - Star at [0, 0, 0]
#   - Inner asteroid belt: r=200..300 (cover near the playspace centre)
#   - Clear zone: r=300..800 (planet, starbase, and player live here)
#   - Outer asteroid belt: r=800..1000 (forces attackers to fly through
#     asteroids to reach the starbase)
#   - Spawn anchors beyond the outer belt (r > 1000), biased toward
#     the +X hemisphere.
#   - Gas giant + ice moon beyond the outer belt on the -X side (r ~1237),
#     clear of the spawn anchors.
#
# Starbase Alpha sits at [500, 0, 100] — within the clear zone. Player ship
# spawns at [400, 0, 200] (~141u from the starbase) ready to defend.
#
# Ship selection: four Alliance hulls are available in the lobby.
#   Alliance Courier    power_rating = 25   (single-station, solo)
#   Alliance Destroyer  power_rating = 70
#   Alliance Cruiser    power_rating = 90
#   Alliance Battleship power_rating = 120
#
# ── The wave clock (issue #960) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Waves are TIMED, not death-gated. Every wave hangs off its own `on_timer` at a
# fixed offset, so the raid arrives whether or not the last one has been cleared
# and falling behind compounds instead of pausing the mission:
#
#   wave  t (s)  composition                anchors
#   1       0    1x cruiser                 enemy_n_outer
#   2      45    1x destroyer                enemy_se
#   3      90    1x cruiser                 enemy_e
#   4     135    1x destroyer                enemy_ne
#   5     180    2x cruiser                 enemy_ese  + enemy_ene
#   6     225    2x destroyer                enemy_s_outer + enemy_n_outer
#   7     270    1x cruiser + 1x destroyer   enemy_e_far + enemy_e
#   8     315    1x patrol cruiser          enemy_e_far
#
# The interval is a single authored number repeated as each registration's
# offset (45 s), chosen against transit: a Harrow needs roughly 50 s to cross
# the ~700 units from its spawn anchor to the starbase, so at 45 s the next wave
# launches just before the previous one arrives and the player meets a
# continuous stream rather than a queue. Retune by editing the eight
# `on_timer(N, …)` offsets — nothing in Rust knows the cadence.
#
# The ONLY thing still gated on `on_all_destroyed` is the ending window:
# victory's `on_all_destroyed` over `hostiles` (plus its 5 s deferral), and the
# eight per-wave completion registrations that close each objective and pay down
# `mission_threat_remaining`. Nothing spawns off a death any more.
#
# Power-scaled bonus spawns (gated by ship_power counter = player power_rating),
# authored as an `if` inside the wave's own timer handler so a bonus ship rides
# the same group and the same clock:
#   ship_power >= 90 (cruiser or battleship): +1 Harrow destroyer on each odd
#     wave (1, 3, 5, 7).
#   ship_power >= 100 (battleship only): +1 Harrow cruiser on each even wave
#     (2, 4, 6, 8).
#   Bonus ships are named wave_N_bonus. They join `hostiles` and `wave_N`, so
#   they gate victory and their wave's objective. They carry the same assault
#   override every other hull in the wave does.
#
# The DEMO tier (destroyer, power_rating 70) therefore sees exactly the table
# above and nothing else; the fuller catalogue is what the two higher tiers add.
#
# ── The single target story (issues #960, #936) ──────────────────────────────
#
# There are no standing pickets and no patrol circuits left in this world. Every
# Harrow that spawns is committed to Starbase Alpha, and the scenario is the
# race between the raid closing on the station and the player breaking it up.
#
# Starbase Alpha is now a ALLIANCE entity (`assets/entities/station_axiom.toml`
# authors the faction, issue #936). It used to be factionless, which made it a
# thing the enemy could be ordered at but never a thing it owned an opinion
# about; it is now the player's own station, which is what "defend it" is
# supposed to mean.
#
# Every wave — cruiser, destroyer, patrol hull and tier bonus alike — carries the
# same two-entry doctrine override. Before #936 only the cruiser waves had it,
# so the destroyer waves never ran at the station at all:
#
#   * `assault-starbase`  Destroy @50, target `world.entity.starbase_alpha.name`,
#     zero-gated on `not_attacked`. THE TARGET NAME IS THE STRING ID, not the
#     English "Starbase Alpha": `resolve_objective_target_uuid` matches the
#     entity's authored `name`, and this world authors that name as a string id.
#     The old override named the display text, resolved nothing, and every
#     "assault" wave sat on its spawn anchor for the whole run. Shooting one
#     zeroes this entry and the hull turns to fight whoever hit it.
#   * `close-on-starbase` Reach @35, anchor `harrow_assault_point`. The RUN-IN,
#     and the reason the band below does not simply strand the raid: a Destroy
#     directive resolves nothing until Tactical can actually see its target, so
#     outside the acquisition band the hull falls through to this Reach and
#     flies the approach. It sits BELOW the hull's own `destroy-hostiles` entry
#     (38-40) on purpose — a Harrow that has been shot at fights first and only
#     resumes the run once it has nothing to shoot at.
#
#     It is also what makes a wave move at all before it is close enough to be
#     promoted to high-fidelity AI: `simulate_low_lod_ships` steers a low-LOD
#     hull along a Patrol/Reach route and dead-reckons everything else, so a
#     Destroy-only wave spawned 700 units out has no route to fly and drifts at
#     zero speed. The Reach entry is that route.
#
# ── The engagement band: 200 out, 150 back (issue #960) ──────────────────────
#
# Enemies engage only what they can SEE, and in this world they see 200 units.
# Every Harrow spawn overrides `[weapons_console.radar] range = 200`; the hull
# templates author no radar block at all, which `ai_target_selection` reads as
# an UNBOUNDED horizon — a raider that acquires the player from a kilometre away
# is not an engagement, it is a homing missile. Inside 200 the ship acquires
# (the station under its assault order, or the player once its assault order has
# been zeroed by taking fire); outside 200 no candidate survives the host's range
# gate, Tactical drops the lock, and the hull disengages back onto the
# `close-on-starbase` Reach. Leaving the band is a real escape.
#
# The other half of the band is NOT authored here and deliberately so: the
# Alliance captain fragment (`assets/entities/fragments/ai/captain_alliance.toml`)
# calls Red Alert at `alert_on_hostile_within = 150`, and every Alliance gun
# authors `min_alert_to_fire = 1.0`. A Harrow authors `min_alert_to_fire = 0`
# and is always armed. So the ordering across the 200 → 150 band is:
#
#   * 200 u — the Harrow acquires and commits. Its guns were never locked.
#   * 150 u — the player's captain calls the alert and the player's guns unlock.
#
# The enemy is therefore always the one that opens the engagement, and a player
# who wants to shoot first has to either close to 150 or take a hit (damage
# starts `secs_since_combat`, which raises the alert on the other captain rule).
# Both numbers are content: widen the band by raising the 200 here, or make the
# fleet twitchier by raising the 150 there.
#
#   Harrow defaults to neutral so non-combat worlds (Starbase Alpha,
#   Before the Fire) can reuse the same ship templates as ambient
#   patrols. This scenario flips both directions of the Alliance
#   <-> Harrow relationship hostile on `on_world_loaded` via two
#   `add_faction_enemy` effects, *before* the first wave's first
#   acquisition tick — guaranteeing wave 1 engages immediately rather
#   than drifting past the station as a neutral patrol.
#
# Victory: every hostile destroyed → game_over "VICTORY". ONE trigger, not the
#   three per-tier variants this world used to carry. Those enumerated a fixed
#   name list per tier, and an unregistered name in such a list permanently
#   blocks the trigger — which is exactly what happened: no spawn action in this
#   world ever authored `groups`, so the `waves` group was empty and victory was
#   unreachable at every tier (the all-defeat headless baseline recorded on
#   issue #892). Group membership is dynamic, so a single `on_all_destroyed`
#   over `hostiles` covers all three tiers with no name list at all.
#
#   The guard is `counter(waves_spawned) >= 8` rather than a clock, and under a
#   wave CLOCK it matters more than it did under the death-gated chain, not
#   less: a good player can clear every ship on the field with four waves still
#   unspawned, and without the counter that window reads as victory. Each wave
#   increments the counter in the same handler that spawns it, so the counter
#   reaches 8 in the same dispatch batch that registers wave 8.
#
#   It is a TRIGGER-LEVEL `.when(…)`, not an `if` at the top of the handler, and
#   the difference is the whole guard: a `when` that reads false suppresses the
#   firing without CONSUMING the one-shot trigger, so victory stays armed
#   through every window where the field is clear but the clock has waves left.
#   An in-handler test would have spent the trigger on the first such window and
#   made victory unreachable — the same failure, by a different route, that the
#   guard exists to prevent.
# Defeat:  Starbase Alpha destroyed → game_over "DEFEAT".
#          Player ship destroyed → handled by the built-in apply_hull_damage
#          path which sets GamePhase::GameOver directly with reason
#          "All consoles destroyed" — no scenario trigger needed.
#
# ── Pacing: `mission_threat_remaining` under a clock (issue #943) ────────────
#
# This world PUBLISHES how much of itself is still ahead, as the world counter
# `mission_threat_remaining`. It is set to 8 on `on_world_loaded` and paid down
# by one in each wave's own completion handler, so at any moment it reads how
# many waves are still to be FOUGHT. Anything that has to ration a finite
# resource across the whole run reads it instead of guessing — today that is the
# torpedo magazine's `torpedo_conservation` doctrine (see `[torpedoes.ai]` on
# any hull with tubes), which divides the rounds the ship still has ABOARD —
# magazine plus tubes — by this number and holds fire once the quotient falls
# under the reserve the hull authors. Without it a ship — player or NPC — meets
# wave 1 with twelve torpedoes and waves 2-8 with none.
#
# WHAT IT COUNTS, AND WHY THAT IS STILL HONEST UNDER A CLOCK. It counts waves
# NOT YET DESTROYED — which under the death-gated chain was the same set as
# "waves not yet spawned", and under the clock is not. A timed wave 5 that is
# already on the field is still threat the ship has to survive, so counting it
# is exactly right; what would be dishonest is counting waves DOWN as they
# SPAWN, which would read 0 while the last four waves were alive and in the
# player's face. The decrement is therefore kept where it was — beside each
# wave's `complete_objective`, in that wave's own `on_all_destroyed` handler —
# and moved OFF the next wave's spawn trigger, which no longer exists. Waves can now
# also die out of order (a player may focus wave 6 while wave 5 is still alive);
# the counter does not care, because each wave pays its own single decrement.
#
# It stays a SECOND counter rather than arithmetic on `waves_spawned`: that one
# counts waves RELEASED (and is what victory waits for), this one counts waves
# still alive or still to come, and under a clock the two are independent.
#
# Worth knowing before lengthening this schedule: this counter is the
# DENOMINATOR of a ONE-WAY LATCH. It falls only when a wave DIES, and a hull
# that has already dipped under its reserve is not shooting at the wave whose
# death would make it fall. Publishing more threat than the fleet's magazines
# can pace against therefore does not make the ships thriftier — it makes them
# silent. That is exactly what this world did at the fleet's original reserve of
# one round per remaining wave: the destroyer met wave 2 holding five rounds it
# was never cleared to fire.
#
# ── HOLDS at 14942520827746055774 over the thrust-band fix, and why ──────────
#
# The AI-thrust-burst fix added a `thrust_release_threshold` band to the helm
# power rules of eight hulls, two of which this world fields (`ship_harrow_
# cruiser` and `ship_harrow_destroyer`, in the later waves) alongside the player
# cruiser's inherited `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. This digest does not
# move, and that is a claim rather than an oversight.
#
# MEASURED: 0 helm power changes across the 900-tick window, banded or not. The
# band changes WHEN a helm channel gives its point back, so it can only reach a
# digest through a hull that actually resolves the helm HOLD rule — and
# `ai_power_allocation` is `With<AiHighFidelity>`, so a low-LOD NPC never runs it
# at all. The waves here sit outside promotion range for the whole window with
# the player ship AI-backfilled and holding station, so no ship in this world
# ever reaches the rule whose text changed. The two worlds that DO — `duel` and
# `rng_coverage` — carry their own baselines and both moved.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state, and this world's own
# script populates plenty of it: the `mission_threat_remaining`/`ship_power`/
# `waves_spawned` flags above are FlagStore entries, and the eight
# `on_timer`/`on_all_destroyed`/`on_destroyed` triggers are latches — both now
# walked by `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` / `fold_scenario_flags`, neither
# of which happened when 14942520827746055774 was measured. The thrust-band A/B
# is untouched — it is a same-build comparison, and "0 helm power changes" is
# still the finding — but the absolute value predates the fold and does not
# reproduce on a clean tree. Re-measure before treating it as a baseline again.

# [ai] Combat Test's timed waves require a human-hosted Navigation surface to
# retain direct waypoint control. The selector names the hull-agnostic System
# kind; the selected hull resolves it after the lobby locks the ship.
scenario_detail_floor = ["navigation"]

# How long a landed hit keeps a Harrow's `not_attacked` zero-gate closed, i.e.
# how long a raider that the player has shot fights the PLAYER (self-defence via
# the base `destroy_hostiles` arm) before its `assault-starbase` Destroy re-arms
# and it turns back on the station. At the 8 s default a tagged raider slips back
# to the station almost immediately, so the player cannot peel the raid off the
# station faster than it re-commits and the whole fleet grinds the station down.
# A longer reprieve is what "attacked enemies attack the player, not the station,
# unless left alone long enough" means: the player draws hulls onto itself and
# gets time to kill them, and only a raider genuinely left alone resumes the run.

# Verification: distance from world origin to each anchor, computed as
# sqrt(x^2 + z^2). All should be >= 1000.
enemy_e        = [1200.0, 0.0, 100.0]    # 1204
enemy_ne       = [1000.0, 0.0, -400.0]   # 1077
enemy_se       = [1000.0, 0.0, 600.0]    # 1166
enemy_n_outer  = [900.0, 0.0, -600.0]    # 1081
enemy_s_outer  = [900.0, 0.0, 800.0]     # 1204
enemy_ene      = [1100.0, 0.0, -150.0]   # 1110
enemy_ese      = [1100.0, 0.0, 350.0]    # 1154
enemy_e_far    = [1400.0, 0.0, 100.0]    # 1404

# The Harrow run-in point (issue #960). Every wave's `close-on-starbase` Reach
# entry names this anchor: it is 100 units +X of Starbase Alpha, i.e. on the
# approach side the whole raid flies in on, and well inside the 200-unit
# acquisition band from the station itself. A hull that reaches it has the
# starbase on its scope and its `assault-starbase` Destroy entry — which
# outscores this one — takes the fight over from here.
harrow_assault_point = [600.0, 0.0, 100.0]

# The player's own defensive circuit around the object it is defending. This is
# the mission's `obj-defend` Patrol directive (bottom of the file), not an enemy
# route: with the raid coming to the station, a backfilled player that had
# nowhere to be would sit on its spawn point until something wandered inside its
# 50-unit tactical radar. Four stations, ±200 units on each axis.
starbase_patrol_north = [500.0, 0.0, -100.0]   # starbase + [  0, 0, -200]
starbase_patrol_east  = [700.0, 0.0, 100.0]   # starbase + [+200, 0,    0]
starbase_patrol_south = [500.0, 0.0, 300.0]   # starbase + [  0, 0, +200]
starbase_patrol_west  = [300.0, 0.0, 100.0]   # starbase + [-200, 0,    0]

# The picket line is gone, and its two anchors went with it (issue #960).
#
# `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` - the hull wave 8 arrives in - authors a
# `patrol-ironveil` Patrol entry naming `ironveil_patrol_a`/`_b`, and an
# unresolved doctrine anchor fails the world load. That is not a reason to
# declare a route nothing flies: wave 8's spawn override stands the entry DOWN
# instead of restating it at zero priority. `doctrine_anchor_refs` reads the
# EFFECTIVE doctrine, template plus overrides, and asks
# `parse_doctrine_directive` which fields are anchors, so a stood-down entry
# asks for none and the world loads with none declared. Left a Patrol at
# `base_priority = 0`, it would still have been a Patrol, and a Patrol keeps its
# anchors alive.
#
# Standing an entry down means clearing EVERY field its old kind owned, not just
# the anchors. `duel.toml` documents the short form
# (`directive_kind = "None", directive_anchors = []`), which is enough for a
# route that only names anchors; this hull also authors `directive_loop`, and
# `validate_doctrine_directives` rejects a field belonging to another directive
# kind rather than ignoring it, so `directive_loop = false` goes with it. Get
# that wrong and the failure is quiet in the wrong place: `doctrine_anchor_refs`
# treats a merge error as "no anchors to check", so the world would load
# happily and wave 8 would simply never spawn.
#
# There is no `patrol_alpha`/`_beta`/`_gamma` circuit any more (issue #892):
# those three anchors existed solely for the retired `pirate_raider.toml`.
# `warhawk_patrol_a`/`_b` are gone with the Harrow battleship, and there is
# deliberately no `pirate_haven` either.

# ── Script ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Issue #984 (Rhai M6). This world's twenty `[[trigger]]` blocks and its twelve
# `[[comms]]` templates are authored here instead, and with it the last
# declaratively-authored world in the game is gone: every shipped scenario is
# script-authored now.
#
# It is also the world that finished the front-end, because it is the only one
# that authored the three trigger-level shapes nothing had yet needed:
#
#   * a trigger-level `when` — the victory guard. Chained onto the registration
#     (`.when("counter(waves_spawned) >= 8")`) rather than tested inside the
#     handler, and the difference is the whole scenario: a `when` that reads
#     false suppresses the firing WITHOUT consuming the trigger, so victory
#     stays armed through every window where the field is clear but the clock
#     has waves left to release. An `if` at the top of the handler would have
#     spent the trigger on the first such window and made victory unreachable —
#     which is the exact bug the guard was added to fix (issue #892).
#   * a per-ACTION `when` — the two power-tier bonus spawns. Those ARE an `if`
#     in the handler, and correctly so: the declarative form filtered one action
#     out of a firing that happened anyway, which is what a conditional
#     statement inside the handler means.
#   * `on_hull_below` — the station's three integrity reports. The one condition
#     whose own field is a fraction, so it is the one registration that takes a
#     `flt("0.75")` marker instead of an integer.
#
# The delayed action converts to `ctx.schedule.in_seconds(5)`: the victory
# window is the same `DelayedAction` on the same queue, just said by the handler
# that queues it rather than by a `delay_secs` beside the action.
#
# Registration order mirrors the authored order of what it replaces — the twenty
# `[[trigger]]` blocks first, then the twelve `[[comms]]` templates — because
# intra-tick trigger order is part of the authoritative digest, and because the
# declarative comms fired in authored order after the triggers had run. The wave
# reports are deliberately NOT merged into the wave handlers they share a clock
# with: keeping them last keeps the comms queue in the order
# `inject_comms_templates` drained it.
#
# Every player-visible string keeps its `strings.csv` id. A dialogue node's
# `message` reaches the wire as a message body exactly as the declarative
# `message` field did, and each announcement is a node with an EMPTY `responses`
# array — the one-way report all twelve of these always were.
#
# The one thing the conversion CHANGED rather than restated: the assault
# override is now written once and called nineteen times. The declarative file
# restated it per spawn and said so, because a `spawn_entity` action has no
# inheritance mechanism; a Rhai handler does, so `raid_overrides()` is the
# single place to retune the acquisition band or either doctrine entry, and
# `wave_8_overrides()` is the same thing plus the Ironveil stand-down.
[script]
setup = """
// ── Triggers, in authored order ──
on_world_loaded("arm_the_scenario");

on_timer(0, "release_wave_1").gm_controls("release_wave_1", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.1").pauseable();
on_timer(45, "release_wave_2").gm_controls("release_wave_2", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.2").pauseable();
on_timer(90, "release_wave_3").gm_controls("release_wave_3", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.3").pauseable();
on_timer(135, "release_wave_4").gm_controls("release_wave_4", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.4").pauseable();
on_timer(180, "release_wave_5").gm_controls("release_wave_5", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.5").pauseable();
on_timer(225, "release_wave_6").gm_controls("release_wave_6", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.6").pauseable();
on_timer(270, "release_wave_7").gm_controls("release_wave_7", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.7").pauseable();
on_timer(315, "release_wave_8").gm_controls("release_wave_8", "world.combat_test.gm.wave.8").pauseable();

on_all_destroyed("wave_1", "wave_1_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_2", "wave_2_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_3", "wave_3_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_4", "wave_4_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_5", "wave_5_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_6", "wave_6_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_7", "wave_7_cleared");
on_all_destroyed("wave_8", "wave_8_cleared");

on_all_destroyed("hostiles", "on_raid_broken").when("counter(waves_spawned) >= 8");
on_destroyed("world.entity.starbase_alpha.name", "on_starbase_lost");
on_world_loaded("add_standing_mission");

// ── Comms, in authored order ──
on_world_loaded("send_brief");

on_timer(0, "report_wave_1");
on_timer(45, "report_wave_2").gm_controls("report_wave_2", "world.combat_test.gm.report.2").pauseable().skip();
on_timer(90, "report_wave_3");
on_timer(135, "report_wave_4");
on_timer(180, "report_wave_5");
on_timer(225, "report_wave_6");
on_timer(270, "report_wave_7");
on_timer(315, "report_wave_8");

on_hull_below("world.entity.starbase_alpha.name", flt("0.75"), "report_hull_75");
on_hull_below("world.entity.starbase_alpha.name", flt("0.50"), "report_hull_50");
on_hull_below("world.entity.starbase_alpha.name", flt("0.10"), "report_hull_10");

// ── The raid's shared spawn overrides ──
//
// Every Harrow in this world — cruiser, destroyer, patrol hull and tier bonus
// alike — carries the same two things. See the file header for both at length:
// the 200-unit acquisition band (`ai_target_selection` reads an unauthored
// radar block as an UNBOUNDED horizon, which is a homing missile rather than an
// engagement), and the assault/run-in doctrine pair. Retune here, once.

fn acquisition_band() {
    #{ radar: #{ range: 200, shows: ["player", "ship", "station"], selects: ["ship", "station"] } }
}

// Destroy @50 naming the starbase's STRING ID — `resolve_objective_target_uuid`
// matches the entity's authored `name`, and this world authors that name as a
// string id. Zero-gated on `not_attacked`: shooting one of these zeroes the
// entry and the hull turns to fight whoever hit it.
fn assault_entry() {
    #{ id: "assault-starbase", directive_kind: "Destroy",
       directive_target: "world.entity.starbase_alpha.name",
       base_priority: 50, target_speed: flt("0.9"), maintain_range: 25,
       zero_gates: [ #{ condition: "not_attacked" } ] }
}

// Reach @35 — the RUN-IN, and the route `simulate_low_lod_ships` steers a
// far-out hull along. It sits BELOW the hull's own `destroy-hostiles` entry on
// purpose: a Harrow that has been shot at fights first.
fn run_in_entry() {
    #{ id: "close-on-starbase", directive_kind: "Reach",
       directive_anchor: "harrow_assault_point",
       base_priority: 35, target_speed: flt("0.9") }
}

fn raid_overrides(display_name) {
    #{ display_name: display_name, weapons_console: acquisition_band(),
       behaviour: #{ doctrine: [ assault_entry(), run_in_entry() ] } }
}

// Wave 8's hull is the Ironveil-class patrol cruiser, the one wave whose
// template carries a Patrol entry of its own. The override stands
// `patrol-ironveil` DOWN rather than re-pointing or de-prioritising it:
// `directive_kind = "None"` leaves nothing for the Helm to serve, and clearing
// the two Patrol-owned fields with it — `directive_anchors`, `directive_loop` —
// is what frees `ironveil_patrol_a`/`_b` from this world's anchor table AND
// keeps the merge legal (see the anchors section above). `base_priority = 0`
// and the empty `modifiers` keep it out of the scored pool as well, so it
// cannot lead a pool every consumer reads the FIRST entry of.
fn wave_8_overrides(display_name) {
    #{ display_name: display_name, weapons_console: acquisition_band(),
       behaviour: #{ doctrine: [
           #{ id: "patrol-ironveil", directive_kind: "None", directive_anchors: [],
              directive_loop: false, base_priority: 0, modifiers: [] },
           assault_entry(),
           run_in_entry(),
       ] } }
}

// ── World load ──
//
// Make Harrow hostile to the Alliance (and vice versa) for the duration of
// this scenario. The faction TOMLs default both sides to neutral so the same
// Harrow ship templates can appear as ambient patrols in non-combat worlds
// (Starbase Alpha, Before the Fire). Two `add_faction_enemy` effects flip both
// directions of the asymmetric `is_enemy` relationship at world-load time,
// *before* any wave's first acquisition tick — guaranteeing wave 1 engages on
// detection rather than drifting past as a neutral patrol. Idempotent, so
// re-running the handler (e.g. via load_world layering) is a no-op.
//
// Since #960 this handler spawns NOTHING. The two standing pickets it used to
// put on station are gone with the picket line; the only ships in this world
// are the eight timed waves.
//
// `mission_threat_remaining` is how much threat this mission poses, published
// for anything that has to pace itself against the WHOLE run rather than the
// fight in front of it (issue #943). Read today by the torpedo magazine's
// `torpedo_conservation` doctrine — see `[torpedoes.ai]` on any hull with tubes
// — which divides the rounds the ship still has aboard (magazine plus tubes) by
// this number and holds fire once the quotient drops below the reserve the hull
// authors. Eight, because eight waves is what the clock releases: the same
// number the victory guard counts UP to, stated the other way round. An
// absolute write (`flags.x = v`), matching the declarative `set_flag_value` it
// replaces, not the composable `increment` the waves use.
fn arm_the_scenario(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
    ctx.flags.mission_threat_remaining = 8;
}

// ── The wave clock ──
//
// Eight `on_timer` registrations, one per wave, at 45-second intervals. Each
// handler:
//   * spawns its hulls into `hostiles` (victory) and `wave_N` (its objective),
//   * spawns its power-tier bonus hull under a counter guard,
//   * adds the player's `obj-destroy-wave-N` objective,
//   * increments `waves_spawned`.
// None of them defers anything: the registration's own offset IS the schedule,
// and a delay on top of it would only make the authored table lie about when a
// wave arrives.
//
// The bonus guards are the per-action `when` predicates the declarative file
// carried, said as statements: `counter(ship_power) >= 90` reads the same
// counter through the same store, and `ctx.flags.ship_power` is that counter.
// ship_power >= 90 (cruiser or battleship) adds a destroyer to each ODD wave;
// >= 100 (battleship only) adds a cruiser to each EVEN one. The DEMO tier
// (destroyer, power_rating 70) sees neither.

fn release_wave_1(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/ship_harrow_cruiser.toml",
        name: "wave_1", anchor: "enemy_n_outer",
        groups: ["hostiles", "wave_1"], overrides: raid_overrides("world.combat_test.harrow.blood_eagle")
    });
    if ctx.flags.ship_power >= 90 {
        ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
            template_path: "assets/entities/ship_harrow_destroyer.toml",
            name: "wave_1_bonus", position: [900, 0, -560],
            groups: ["hostiles", "wave_1"], overrides: raid_overrides("world.combat_test.harrow.iron_spear")
        });
    }
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-destroy-wave-1",
        text: "world.combat_test.trigger.action.obj_destroy_wave_1.text",
        mandatory: true, targets: [], target: "wave_1",
        directive_kind: "Destroy", base_priority: 80
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("waves_spawned", 1);
}

    ctx.flags.increment("mission_threat_remaining", -1);

// ── Endings ──
//
// Victory: every hostile destroyed — the eight waves and their tier bonuses.
// ONE registration over the dynamic `hostiles` group rather than three per-tier
// name lists, because group membership is dynamic and an unregistered name in
// such a list permanently blocks the trigger (issue #892's actual bug). The
// five-second delay is the game-over WINDOW: the one thing in this world still
// timed off a death rather than off the clock.
fn on_raid_broken(ctx) {
    ctx.schedule.in_seconds(5)
        .game_over("world.combat_test.trigger.action.18.message", "victory");
}

// Defeat: Starbase Alpha destroyed. The player ship dying is handled by the

// with reason "All consoles destroyed" — no scenario trigger needed.
fn on_starbase_lost(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.game_over("world.combat_test.trigger.action.21.message", "defeat");
}

// ── Objectives ──

// and it is the only Patrol left in this world now that the enemy picket line
// is gone. It scores 20, under every `obj-destroy-wave-N` at 80, so it is what
// a backfilled player flies between engagements rather than what it does
// instead of fighting.
fn add_standing_mission(ctx) {

        base_priority: 20,
        directive_kind: "Patrol",
        directive_anchors: ["starbase_patrol_north", "starbase_patrol_east", "starbase_patrol_south", "starbase_patrol_west"],
        directive_loop: true
    });
}

// ── Comms ──

// `station_axiom.toml`'s template-level `[comms] hailable = true` (issue #985)

base_files.assets/worlds/default.toml:
# Default World: Starbase Alpha + initial raider patrol
#
# A "world" file unifies what was previously split between a `map` (anchors,
# global config, entity instances) and a `scenario` (named spawns, triggers,
# comms templates). One file, one fetch, one parse.
#
# Sections:
#   [global]    — seed, world-level constants
#   [anchors]   — named positions for [[entity]] entries to reference
#   [[entity]]  — direct entity instances (Immediate or GameStart spawn);
#                 named entries are trigger / comms eligible
#   [script]    — Rhai: trigger registrations, their handlers, and the comms
#                 dialogue trees those handlers open (issue #984, Rhai M6)

[global]
# Master seed for the simulation RNG (issue #837). `phoenix-headless --seed`
# overrides it; omit the key entirely and a seed is drawn from the OS instead.
# Whichever wins is echoed in the headless exit report, so a run can be replayed.
seed = 42
title = "world.default.global.title"
description = "world.default.global.description"
# Fixed rate (Hz) of the shared AI-helm sim tick: every per-axis AI helm
# system (thrust, steering, lateral thrust, impulse) decides at this cadence,
# independent of the host's frame rate (issue #803). Omitting the key
# defaults to 30.
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[ambient_light]
color      = [0.6, 0.55, 0.5]
brightness = 300.0

# Red-alert audio. `siren` is a one-shot on the false→true edge; `music` loops
# underneath for as long as the alert is active. Every other sound is
# configured on the ship entity instead.
[audio.red_alert]
siren_file   = "assets/sounds/red_alert_siren.ogg"
siren_volume = 0.7
music_file   = "assets/sounds/last_stand_in_space_looped.ogg"
music_volume = 0.35

# Ambient dust motes — a camera-relative velocity field rather than world-space
# particles: speed drives density, brightness and streak length, while the
# ship's true velocity drives direction. Layers, tints and response curves are
# left at the renderer defaults here; see docs/toml-authoring-guide.md for the
# full field list and `combat_test.toml` for a tuned example.
[dust]
enabled = true

# Impulse swaps the ordinary motes out for a dedicated high-speed field.
[dust.warp]
enabled = true

[anchors]
starbase_alpha = [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0]
patrol_alpha   = [600.0, 0.0, -600.0]
patrol_beta    = [500.0, 0.0, -300.0]
patrol_gamma   = [200.0, 0.0, -600.0]
# Where a mauled raider runs to. Referenced by the `retreat-when-hurt` doctrine
# this world authors on `raider_alpha` below; set away from the patrol route and
# the starbase so a retreat visibly breaks off rather than circling the fight.
pirate_haven   = [-800.0, 0.0, -1200.0]

# ── Static map entities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/star_sun.toml"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/planet_earth.toml"
id = "earth"
name = "world.entity.earth.name"
transform = { position = [400.0, 0.0, 400.0] }

# Earth's moon, placed relative to the planet (static — no orbital motion).
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/moon_luna.toml"
id = "luna"
name = "world.entity.luna.name"
transform = { relative_to = "earth", offset = [60.0, 0.0, 30.0] }

# Lava planet in a further-out position (r ~922; the asteroid field spans
# r=300..350 and earth sits at r ~566).
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/planet_lava.toml"
id = "lava-planet"
name = "world.entity.lava_planet.name"
transform = { position = [-700.0, 0.0, -600.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_field_main.toml"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [280.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/region_nebula.toml"
id = "nebula-1"
transform = { position = [600.0, 0.0, -600.0] }

# ── Named entities (trigger / comms-eligible) ────────────────────────────────
#
# `[[entity]] name = "..."` is the unified spawn surface (PRD #337). The
# pipeline assigns a UUID at spawn time and registers it in
# `WorldConfig.name_to_uuid` so triggers and comms can resolve the name.
# Positioning lives under `[entity.transform]` and may use inline `position`,
# `anchor = "..."` (resolved from `[anchors]`), or
# `relative_to = "..." + offset = [x,y,z]`. A `relative_to` names another
# entity in THIS file by its `id` or its `name`, declared before or after this
# one; the target may not itself use `relative_to` (no chains). An
# unresolvable `relative_to` fails world validation (issue #969).

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/station_axiom.toml"
name = "world.entity.starbase_alpha.name"
transform = { anchor = "starbase_alpha" }

# ── Named NPC entities (trigger-eligible) ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# The patrol raider is positioned at the `patrol_alpha` anchor;
# `spawn_world_entities` wires the AI components (BehaviourSection,
# FactionComponent) via the shared `spawn_entity` helper.
#
# (#892) The hull was `pirate_raider.toml`, retired as a duplicate of
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`'s display name. The replacement here is the
# Ironveil-class patrol cruiser rather than the Harrow Destroyer, because this
# spawn is an AMBIENT patrol and the Destroyer authors no Patrol doctrine at
# all — repointing at it would leave a 900-hull interceptor parked on an anchor
# with nothing to do until the player wandered inside its 400-unit sensor range,
# and would silently delete this world's three-waypoint route.
#
# Two overrides carry across what the retired hull did here and the Ironveil
# does not, both merged by doctrine id:
#
#   patrol-ironveil    — retargeted from the Ironveil's own `ironveil_patrol_*`
#                        waypoints (a combat_test circuit this world does not
#                        declare) onto this world's own three.
#   retreat-when-hurt  — appended. `pirate_haven` and the Retreat directive it
#                        feeds were this world's, not the hull's, and after #892
#                        this is the only place in shipped content where a
#                        Retreat directive resolves at all. Losing it would
#                        leave issue #702's whole mechanism unexercised.
#
# Neither override touches `base_priority`, so the #892 picket rebase applies
# here unmodified: this hull now holds its route until fired upon (Patrol 45 >
# Destroy 38 undisturbed; attacked flips it to 63 > 30), superseding the old
# engage-on-sight reading. Flagged for review if engage-on-sight is actually
# wanted for this raider.
#
# `comms = { hailable = true }` (issue #985) is the hail-roster opt-in this
# world's `[[comms]]` block used to supply implicitly: every `[[comms]] from`
# became a `CommsRuntime::contacts` entry, and the M6 conversion below deletes
# that source. Authored HERE rather than on `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` because
# the hull also flies in `combat_test` (wave 8), `patrol`, `probe_huge_rock` and
# `reinforcements`, none of which listed it as a contact — a template-level
# opt-in would put a raider on four other worlds' rosters. The station's opt-in
# IS template-level: see the note in `station_axiom.toml`.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
name          = "world.entity.raider_alpha.name"
transform     = { anchor = "patrol_alpha" }
overrides = { tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"], comms = { hailable = true }, behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "patrol-ironveil", directive_anchors = ["patrol_alpha", "patrol_beta", "patrol_gamma"] },
  { id = "retreat-when-hurt", directive_kind = "Retreat", directive_anchor = "pirate_haven",
    base_priority = 100.0, target_speed = 1.0,
    zero_gates = [{ condition = "hull_below", threshold = 0.3 }] },
] } }

[[available_ships]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
label = "world.default.available_ships.0.label"

[[available_ships]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
label = "world.default.available_ships.1.label"

# ── Script ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Issue #984 (Rhai M6): this world's two `[[trigger]]` blocks and its three
# `[[comms]]` templates are authored here instead. It is the first conversion of
# a world that carries DIALOGUE, so the shape is worth stating once:
#
#   * a trigger registration names a handler fn, exactly as in `patrol.toml`;
#   * a comms template's `trigger =` / `entity =` pair becomes that same
#     registration, and its `message` becomes a DIALOGUE NODE fn — a fn
#     returning `#{ message, responses }` — which the handler opens with
#     `ctx.effects.open_comms(#{ from, node_fn })`;
#   * an announcement (a template with no `[[comms.response]]`) is a node with
#     an EMPTY `responses` array — the one-way broadcast the two distress calls
#     always were;
#   * a response's `[[comms.response.action]]` list becomes its `on_pick` fn,
#     which buffers the same effects through the same `ActionCmd` boundary and
#     returns the follow-up node, or `()` for a terminal response. Both of this
#     world's responses are terminal, so both fns return unit.
#
# Every player-visible string keeps its `strings.csv` id: a dialogue node's
# `message` and a response's `text` reach the wire as message bodies exactly as
# the declarative `message` / `text` fields did (`project_node` →
# `CommsMessage::injected`), so the ids resolve client-side unchanged.
#
# Registration order mirrors the authored order of what it replaces — the two
# `[[trigger]]` blocks first, then the three `[[comms]]` templates — because
# intra-tick trigger order is part of the authoritative digest. The raider's
# on_attacked handler carries BOTH of that event's old reactions: the trigger's
# `load_world` and the comms template's broadcast.
[script]
setup = """
on_destroyed("world.entity.raider_alpha.name", "on_raider_destroyed");
on_attacked("world.entity.raider_alpha.name", "on_raider_attacked");
on_attacked("world.entity.starbase_alpha.name", "on_starbase_attacked");
on_hailed("world.entity.starbase_alpha.name", "on_starbase_hailed");

// ── Trigger handlers ──

fn on_raider_destroyed(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-raider-destroyed",
        text: "world.default.trigger.action.obj_raider_destroyed.text",
        mandatory: false
    });
}

// The reinforcements LAYER is still a layer: `load_world` is the same effect
// the `[[trigger]]` dispatched, so `reinforcements.toml` keeps being loaded as
// a sub-world rather than being inlined here.
fn on_raider_attacked(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.load_world("assets/worlds/reinforcements.toml");
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.entity.raider_alpha.name",
        node_fn: "raider_mayday"
    });
}

fn on_starbase_attacked(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.entity.starbase_alpha.name",
        node_fn: "starbase_mayday"
    });
}

fn on_starbase_hailed(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.entity.starbase_alpha.name",
        node_fn: "starbase_hail"
    });
}

// ── Dialogue nodes ──

// Automatic distress call broadcast when the raider is first attacked.
fn raider_mayday(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.default.comms.0.message", responses: [] }
}

// Automatic distress call broadcast from Starbase Alpha when the station is
// first attacked.
fn starbase_mayday(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.default.comms.1.message", responses: [] }
}

fn starbase_hail(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.default.comms.2.message", responses: [
        #{ text: "world.default.comms.response.0.text", on_pick: "on_survey" },
        #{ text: "world.default.comms.response.1.text", on_pick: "on_dock" },
    ] }
}

// ── Response effects ──

fn on_survey(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-survey",
        text: "world.default.comms.response.action.obj_survey.text"
    });
}

fn on_dock(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-dock",
        text: "world.default.comms.response.action.obj_dock.text",
        mandatory: true
    });
}
