base_files.assets/worlds/duel.toml:
# Duel world for issue #844 — XvY class matchups driven from the CLI.
#
# `phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/duel.toml --side-a cruiser \
#   --side-b destroyer` regenerates the slot roster at the bottom of the
# `[script]` block from those lists, via the PURE
# `headless::duel::apply_duel_sides` transform (which edits this file's raw TOML
# before the script loader reads it — it never touches the file on disk). Up to
# five ships per side. Run without either flag and the authored default roster
# below stands: a 5v5 of couriers against destroyers.
#
# ── BASELINE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# This world had no recorded digest until the AI-thrust-burst fix moved it, which
# is exactly the case a baseline exists for. Measured on a clean tree with the
# debug binary, on the DEFAULT roster (no --side-a/--side-b):
#
#   target/debug/phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/duel.toml \
#     --seed 42 --ticks 900 --record target/duel.ron --digest-every 0
#
# CURRENT VALUE: 14650071985412286067 (0xcb4f82d9f066a673), moved from
# 10785935710004737498 by issue #1164's destroyer coupling systems: the default
# roster fields alliance destroyers on side B, and giving the destroyer its
# tractor/umbilical/dock system-hull entries added three entries to each
# destroyer's damage pool, which moves the per-hull `RegionDamage`/collision
# draw. 10785935710004737498 (0x95af5761c50875da) was itself moved from
# 95852357729946676 by the issue #1053 over-cap bleed. The paragraphs below are
# the history, oldest first; the first number in them is NOT the one to A/B
# against.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state, and this world's
# `on_world_loaded` trigger — the one that makes Alliance and Harrow mutually
# hostile before anything spawns — is a latch on
# `WorldContentRuntime::trigger_states`, now walked by
# `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records`, which did not happen when the CURRENT
# VALUE above was measured. The whole lineage in this section predates the
# fold and none of it reproduces on a clean tree. Re-measure before treating
# any of it as a baseline again.
#
# 95852357729946676 was itself moved from 11542528846502171323 by the
# `thrust_release_threshold` band (the thrust axis's mirror of the battery
# axis's `min_reserve_*`/`min_restore_*` pair). 11542528846502171323 was itself
# only ever measured, never written down here; it is recorded above as the
# lineage rather than as a value this file once claimed.
#
# WHY THIS WORLD AND NOT THE OTHERS. Of the sixteen worlds measured either side
# of that fix, exactly two move: this one and `rng_coverage`. The band changes
# WHEN a helm power channel gives its point back, so it can only reach a digest
# through a world that actually resolves the helm HOLD rule — which needs a
# banded hull at HIGH LOD under a throttle that reaches the band.
# `ai_power_allocation` is `With<AiHighFidelity>`, so a low-LOD NPC never runs it
# at all. This world is a ten-ship close-quarters brawl in which every hull is
# promoted and under way, and its default roster is `alliance_courier` against
# `alliance_destroyer` — the courier authors the banded rule directly and the
# destroyer inherits it from `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. Measured: 24
# helm power changes across the window here, against 0 in combat_test, patrol
# and falling_skyway, all three of which field banded hulls but never promote or
# never reach the band.
#
# MOVED BY ISSUE #1053, to 10785935710004737498 (0x95af5761c50875da). A helm
# power shed used to delete an over-cap velocity in the tick the `MaxSpeed`
# modifier changed; excess is now bled off on the hull's own `deceleration`, so
# a ship coasts down over a few ticks instead of lurching.
#
# THIS WORLD IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE SEVENTEEN THAT MOVES, and a helm shed is
# NOT what decides that — the shed has to land while the hull is ACTUALLY over
# the new cap, which is the one condition the old clamp needed to bite.
# `rng_coverage` is the proof: it sheds helm power four times in its window and
# its digest is untouched, because none of those sheds finds a hull above the
# cap they leave behind. Instrumenting the over-cap branch itself and counting
# the integration steps that take it:
#
#   duel             761        combat_test        0
#   rng_coverage       0        falling_skyway     0
#   probe_destroy      0        probe_storm        0
#
# 761 of them, in three groups, and the middle group is issue #1053's own
# measurement reproduced here: 21 steps at a 54-unit cap with up to 13.50 of
# excess — a hull at 67.5 against a cap of 54, which is the 67.5 -> 54.0 the
# issue reported off `probe_hostile`. The other two are worse rather than
# milder: 12 steps at a 22-unit cap (1.89 of excess) and 728 at an 18-unit cap
# with up to 44.25 — a hull at 62.25 with its cap collapsed to 18, better than
# three times over, previously deleted in a single tick.
#
# The ten-ship brawl is why: every hull is promoted, every hull is under way at
# or near its cap, and the same power deciders that make this the world the
# thrust band moves make it the world where a shed most often finds a ship at
# flank.
#
# ── Why the NPC slots are `spawn_entity` effects, not `[[entity]]` blocks ─────
#
# `on_all_destroyed group = "..."` only tracks membership registered through
# `SpawnEntity` dispatch — a static `[[entity]]` never joins a group (there is
# no groups field on `WorldEntity`, and the game-start spawn path does not
# register groups). So every NPC combatant is spawned by an `on_timer` handler
# at t=0 with `groups = [...]`, exactly like the world-spawned hostile in
# `probe_duel.toml`.
#
# ── Sides, factions, and how the run ends ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# Side A = Alliance (the player's own faction). Side A slot 1 is the PLAYER
#   ship (the LocalShip), set from `--side-a`'s first entry via `--ship`/
#   `PendingShipConfig` — NOT a spawn slot below. Slots `side_a_2`..`side_a_5`
#   are the player's NPC escorts.
# Side B = Harrow. Slots `side_b_1`..`side_b_5` are all NPCs.
#
# VICTORY (side A wins) = every side-B ship destroyed: the `on_all_destroyed
#   group = "side_b"` registration runs `on_side_b_destroyed`, which fires
#   `game_over` outcome = "victory". The transform does NOT EMIT that
#   registration if `--side-b` is empty, so an empty group can't instant-fire a
#   false victory.
# DEFEAT (side A loses) = the PLAYER ship dies. This is the engine's built-in
#   player-death latch (`GamePhase::GameOver`, `Outcome::Defeat`) — there is
#   deliberately NO `on_all_destroyed group = "side_a"` trigger: an empty
#   side_a group (the common player-only case) would fire immediately, and even
#   with escorts the player may still be alive. Escort deaths never end the run;
#   the player's death does. This is a hard engine constraint.
# Neither annihilated nor player dead within the tick budget → the headless
#   runner classifies the run as timeout/draw off the per-side margins (#843).
#
# The doctrine on each slot is an UNTARGETED Destroy (no `directive_target`),
# which licenses the nearest-hostile acquisition tier — the same shape every
# shipped hostile authors and what `probe_duel.toml` uses.

[global]
seed = 844
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

# ── Geometry (AC5 — tune here, no recompile) ──────────────────────────────────
#
# Side A clusters on the origin; side B faces it a short hop away along +X.
# Spacing is kept inside the ~100-unit default AI sensor range so both sides
# acquire and engage immediately (probe worlds prove ~35–55 units engages at
# once; ~500 units never joins the fight). Widen these to stage a longer
# approach, or pull them in for a knife fight.
#
# Every slot spawns on the anchor of its OWN NAME, so this table is also the
# list of slots the harness is allowed to fill: a generated slot whose anchor is
# missing here is rejected (`DuelError::UndeclaredSlotAnchor`) rather than
# spawning nowhere.
[anchors]
player_spawn = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
side_a_2     = [-15.0, 0.0,  30.0]
side_a_3     = [-15.0, 0.0, -30.0]
side_a_4     = [-40.0, 0.0,  30.0]
side_a_5     = [-40.0, 0.0, -30.0]
side_b_1     = [ 55.0, 0.0,   0.0]
side_b_2     = [ 55.0, 0.0,  30.0]
side_b_3     = [ 55.0, 0.0, -30.0]
side_b_4     = [ 80.0, 0.0,  30.0]
side_b_5     = [ 80.0, 0.0, -30.0]

# ── Home routes of substituted hulls (issue #888) ─────────────────────────────
#
# `--side-a`/`--side-b` drop an arbitrary shipped hull into the slots below, and
# a hull arrives carrying its own `[[behaviour.doctrine]]` — including a patrol
# route named after anchors of the scenario it normally fights in. The slot
# overrides add an untargeted Destroy; they do NOT replace the hull's list
# (`merge_id_array` keeps every template entry the override does not name by
# id), so the route comes along and this arena has to say where it goes.
#
# A doctrine anchor no world declares is a goal the ship silently cannot pursue,
# and it is rejected at load rather than resolving to nothing. So a route flown
# in this arena is declared here, on the arena's OWN staging coordinates rather
# than a geography invented for it: `ship_harrow_warhawk.toml` paces the side-B
# line. Nothing changes behaviourally — every slot's Destroy scores 80 against
# the hull's patrol at 20, so the route is never the served directive — but the
# arena now states where the battleship would go instead of leaving it to a
# lookup that misses.
#
# Fielding a hull through `--side-a`/`--side-b` whose route is not declared here
# fails the run before it boots, naming the anchor: `headless::duel::
# apply_duel_sides` re-runs #888's check over every hull it fields
# (`DuelError::UndeclaredDoctrineAnchor`). That is the intended prompt — declare
# the route on this line too, or stand the hull's patrol entry down in the slot

// never drift from this arena's own doctrine. The faction is forced (rather
// than left to the hull's template) so the report buckets each ship on the
// side that fielded it.
fn spawn_slot(ctx, name, template, faction, group) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: template,
        name: name,
        anchor: name,
        groups: [group],
        overrides: #{ faction: faction, behaviour: #{ doctrine: [

# Falling Skyway — the skeleton world and Act 1 (issue #1034, parent #852).
#
# This is the spine every later slice of the scenario hangs content on: the
# PLACE, the TRAFFIC that was already moving before the crew arrived, the CLOCK
# they are working against, and Act 1's triage. It began as a skeleton, and the
# slices that fill it band their own content in below rather than reflowing this
# one: the strike (#1035), the negotiation (#1036), the storm and the rescue
# (#1037), the scan-versus-dossier evidence (#1038), the worker who corroborates
# it (#1039), the restraint lever (#1041), the collapse and its epilogue (#1040),
# the transfer window itself (#1042) and the choice all of them were built for
# (#1043) have landed. The mission is authored whole, and #1131's pacing pass
# now carries it across the ratified 20-30 minute envelope.
#
# ── The place ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# A city world with a skyhook over it and a fuel-depot ladder strung out along
# the corridor beside it. Everything the crew can act on is an entity carrying
# authored data:
#
#   Skyhook Meridian    48/100 condition. Certified to lift above 45 %, so it
#                       is ALREADY three points from being uncertified when the
#                       crew arrive. Two transfer berths.
#   Ladder Depot A      62/100. Pumping. The one that still works.
#   Ladder Depot B      34/100, below its own 40 % line, so it reads as OFF from
#                       the first tick — the triage picture is data, not prose.
#   Skyway Control      the authority. Hailable, Alliance, and where the
#                       survey report goes.
#
# THREE CLAIMANTS, TWO BERTHS. That ratio is the whole scenario, and all three
# parties are in the world from the start because they are part of the place:
#
#   Strike Committee    the workers, moored off Depot B. They know what the
#                       maintenance record actually says (#1038/#1039).
#   Rigger Tacket       one of them, moored with them, who was on the Ladder B
#                       transfer arm the day its file says it was inspected. She
#                       is the second half of the evidence case (#1039), and her
#                       channel opens only for a crew who settled the strike by
#                       talking and went and read the rung.
#   Havelock Cutter     the operator's security, sitting on the same depot.
#   Convoy Meridian     the civilian traffic — sympathetic, and with no
#                       leverage at all.
#
# Their negotiation is #1036's, and it is authored now: the dispute has two ways
# to end, either of which the crew can reach without touching the other.
#
# ── The traffic ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Four civilian craft are on authored lanes at mission start, flying. Not
# spawned by a trigger, not waiting for the player to arrive — the corridor was
# working before the crew got here and it keeps working while they read the
# place, which is the pressure Act 1 is actually made of.
#
# ── The clock ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Five named opening deadlines. The two mission-work clocks are visible; Lark's
# three safety beats are authored but remain Comms pressure rather than extra
# captain-panel countdowns:
#
#   t=160 s `tether_slip`        the head loses six condition points. 48 → 42
#                                takes it under its authored 45 % lift line, the
#                                `skyhook_lift_capable` flag falls, and the
#                                triage priority names itself.
#   t=360 s `skyway_survey_due`  Control wants the assessment. A report filed
#                                after all three structure scans completes the
#                                survey; silence fails it and Control proceeds on
#                                the falsified record already in its hands.
#   t=330 s `lark_first_hail_due` Lark asks whether the throat is safe.
#   t=360 s `lark_final_hail_due` Lark asks again, at Critical priority.
#   t=380 s `lark_collision_due`  without a scan-backed stop order, Lark commits
#                                to the compromised throat and strikes the head.
#
# The opening era owns the first six minutes. Its narrative boundary is authored
# DATA — two `due_secs` numbers — and gates no parallel thread.
#
# ── Act 1's three objectives, and how each one resolves ──────────────────────
#
#   obj-a1-survey    remains the mandatory aggregate. When the tether slips it
#                    gives Helm a non-looping Depot B → Depot A → head patrol,
#                    while three optional visible Scan steps tell Sensors exactly
#                    what to read. Once all three readings exist, a Hail(Control)
#                    report step posts. Filing that response completes the report
#                    and aggregate. Work done before a post remains remembered.
#   obj-a1-corridor  resolves when the lead hauler clears `corridor_gate` — the
#                    lane proving itself, through #1028's route machinery.
#   obj-a1-triage    resolves when the head drops out of lift tolerance, through
#                    #1025's threshold. [ai] IN THE SKELETON THE STRUCTURE NAMES
#                    THE PRIORITY FOR THE CREW. That is a placeholder: once the
#                    strike (#1035) puts a second claim on the repair teams, the
#                    captain makes this call and this handler becomes the beat
#                    that records their choice rather than the one that makes it.
#
# Anything still pending when the survey falls due is FAILED at the act
# boundary, which is what makes partial success readable: the act ends on the
# clock whatever the crew got done, and the objectives list says which.
#
# ── The dispute era's two endings (issue #1036) ──────────────────────────────
#
# The dispute is hailable from the opening tick. Its objectives and incoming
# channels post when the tether slips at t=160, while the survey is still live;
# the survey deadline only advances the narrative era counter. If nobody has
# answered either party, the committee hardens at t=120 and again at t=300.
# Neither ending is behind the other's first pick and no escalation removes it.
#
#   NEGOTIATE  before hardening, the committee settle for two pieces of ground
#              out of three: the
#              captain's word that the corridor is clear in the transfer window,
#              the captain's word that the scan discrepancy and corroborating
#              worker account go to Control unedited, or the crew showing they
#              have already read the file. Both promises
#              go onto the commitments ledger with the workers as the party and
#              stay OPEN — keeping them is #1042's and #1039's business. Once
#              hardened, all three pieces of ground are required.
#   FORCE IT   Havelock clear the picket. Faster, and it costs people, a
#              relationship two campaign flags carry forward, and the worker
#              corroboration route (#1039) — which fails an objective on the
#              crew's own list rather than latching in silence.
#
# The casualty count is READ, not rolled: script has no RNG and should not, so
# the number comes off the workers' mirrored disposition at the moment the order
# is given, with ten minutes' warning as the captain's lever over it. It is
# deterministic per seed by construction and surfaces on a console four ways.
#
# ── The storm era (issue #1037) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The negotiation above opens the act; the RADIATION STORM is its second half,
# and it arrives whatever the crew decided about the strike. Six more visible
# deadlines, three authored region bands sweeping the corridor, the civilian
# traffic ordered off the lane ahead of them, and a stricken hauler in the lane
# that has to be towed clear before the second band. All of it is authored in
# its own banded section further down this file, from the anchors it needs to
# the handlers that run it; `act` now counts 1 → 2 → 3.
#
# ── Act 3, and the two ways the mission ends (issue #1040) ───────────────────
#
# THE SKYHOOK CAN FALL. Act 3 opens on the flag the storm's close writes, puts
# the head back under the corridor's load, and walks its condition down toward
# the structural floor `skyhook.toml` authors. Three escalating warnings on three
# surfaces come first; a crew who stabilise at any of them — including the last —
# keep the structure; a crew who do not watch `destroy_entity` take it out of the
# world mid-mission and the mission BRANCH into a survivor-rescue epilogue. All
# of it is authored in its own banded section further down this file.
#
# ── Act 3's arithmetic (issue #1042) ─────────────────────────────────────────
#
# THE TRANSFER WINDOW OPENS ON A DEADLINE THE CREW HAVE BEEN WATCHING SINCE THE
# FIRST TICK, and what the chain can lift in it does not cover what the three
# claimants have asked for. Demand is authored — three labelled capacity rows on
# Skyway Control's own manifest — and supply is COMPUTED at the moment the
# window opens, from the head's lift certification, each rung's operational line
# and whether the people who staff it are at work. So a crew who settled the
# strike and mended the rung arrive with more to give than a crew who did
# neither, and neither arrives with enough: the ladder's ceiling is 52 against
# 66 of claims, and nothing in the mission can raise it.
#
# THE TWO ACT-3 SECTIONS ARE ONE ACT, and they meet at a NUMBER rather than at a
# name. The head's `skyhook_lift_capable` — the lift certification Act 1 knocked
# it under — is the whole of its contribution to the window's supply, so a tether
# the crew let walk down toward the floor takes the transfer window's lift with
# it on the way past, and a head that comes out of the world takes all of it.
# The window is deliberately priced AFTER the tether's projection falls due, so
# what it publishes is the fate rather than a forecast of it; the two ends of the
# act are read in the order they happen. Nothing in the window's arithmetic names
# anything the collapse slice authors — not a rung of its warning ladder, not one
# of its flags — and it does not need to.
#
# The consequence is a ladder the crew feel rather than are told: let the head
# go and the window has nothing in it; catch it at the last rung and it still
# cannot lift, because a stabilise carries a head back over its FIRST warning and
# not back over its certification; keep it certified and the window is worth
# everything the ladder can give — which is still not enough for three.
#
# The window is authored in its own banded section too: two more visible
# deadlines, one `[entity.overrides.infrastructure]` block on Control, and the
# script that does the sum. The CHOICE is #1043's; what #1042 owns is the ledger
# that choice has to obey.
#
# ── Act 3's choice, and what the mission hands on (issue #1043) ──────────────
#
# THE SCENE THE WHOLE MISSION EXISTS FOR. Three claimants call the ship on three
# channels from three real hulls, the lift covers two of them, and the third
# rides the storm out where the crew can hear it happen. Nothing in that scene
# counts to two: every "take them up" line exists only while #1042's banked
# ledger still covers that claimant's authored claim, and picking it pulls that
# slice's booking seam rather than doing anything itself.
#
# The commitments the earlier acts collected are settled HERE, against facts
# rather than moods — and a captain who gave the workers their word about this
# very window and then left them on the rung hears the terms of it read back by

#

# a quieter one: one mooring on the rung that still works, allocated by giving

# THE STRIKE IS ALREADY HAPPENING WHEN THE CREW ARRIVE. It is authored here
# rather than scripted on tick one for the reason the skyhook's 48 points are
# authored: the situation was under way before anybody sent a destroyer, and a
# world that had to script its own opening state would be describing a change
# nobody was there for.
#
# Two sides, and they are NOT factions. Both parties are Alliance, neither
# will ever fire on the other, and the whole crisis is between them — folding a
# strike into the enemies list would have made "the line is down" mean "the
# depot is hostile" on every console that reads a faction.
#
# `disposition` is what each side makes of the crew, 0..=100. Nothing in the opening era
# branches on it; it is the state the negotiation (#1036) moves and the acts
# after it read. [ai] Both numbers unratified — the workers arrive suspicious
# and the operator arrives correct-but-cold, which is the opening the
# negotiation is written against.

[[workforce]]
id = "skyway_workers"
label = "world.falling_skyway.workforce.skyway_workers.label"
on_strike = true
disposition = 25

[[workforce]]
id = "havelock_operations"
label = "world.falling_skyway.workforce.havelock_operations.label"
disposition = 55

# ── Anchors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The corridor runs north-south past the skyhook; the depot ladder runs out to
# the east of it. Everything a hull steers to is declared here — a doctrine or a
# route leg naming an anchor the composition does not declare is a load error,
# and rightly: an anchor has no runtime source, so a lookup that misses at load
# misses forever.

[anchors]
# The head of the tether, and the origin everything else is placed around.
skyway_head = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Where the destroyer holds station to work the skyway: off the head, out of the
# lane, close enough to hail everything in the corridor.
station_keeping = [180.0, 0.0, 170.0]

# The corridor, north to south. `corridor_gate` is the throat beside the head —
# the point every craft in the lane has to pass, which is why it is the one the
# scenario asks a question about.
corridor_north = [0.0, 0.0, -1100.0]
corridor_gate = [0.0, 0.0, -260.0]
corridor_south = [0.0, 0.0, 1000.0]

# Where a slab of the shed ribbon has come down across the throat and wedged
# (issue #1350). Off the traffic lane and inside the destroyer's Security reach
# from station-keeping, so a team can cross to it to place charges. The Act 3
# controlled-demolition beat clears it.
corridor_obstruction = [80.0, 0.0, -60.0]

# Where a castaway lifeboat has drifted off the corridor throat, out to the east
# flank near the head's latitude (issue #1348 mechanism, T2 refinement). Placed
# CLEAR of the storm lane on purpose: the radiation bands are 260-unit-half-width
# boxes centred on x=0, so a 60-integrity lifeboat sitting inside |x|<260 would be
# scoured by a passing band; at x=340 it is 80 units east of the worst band and
# survives to be found. Still well inside the destroyer's 500-unit transporter
# reach from station-keeping. A discovered contact, not a scripted one — the crew
# have to look. [ai] Unratified.
corridor_castaway = [340.0, 0.0, -120.0]

# The fuel-depot ladder, and the transit leg between its two rungs.
#
# FOUR anchors for two rungs, because a berth and a hull are not the same place
# and this file used to say they were. `depot_a_berth` and `depot_b_berth` were
# BOTH the depots' spawn positions AND `ladder_run`'s first and third legs, so
# the shuttle was commanded to fly to the exact centre of a structure and hold
# there for six seconds.
#
# WHAT SAVED IT WAS NOT THE AUTHORING, and that is the whole reason to fix it.
# A hauler declares `waypoint_arrival_radius = 20`, so `advance_cursor` calls
# the leg reached twenty units out; `TrafficState::cruise_speed` then returns
# 0.0 for the dwell, so the craft coasts down on its own 8.0 deceleration from
# leg 0's 8.4 u/s — about 4.4 units of run-out — and settles some fifteen units
# short of the anchor. Measured rather than reasoned: shrinking the depot's
# collider from 3.8 to 0.01 does not move this world's digest by a bit, so
# nothing was ever in contact. At the depot's PREVIOUS 10-unit collider it was,
# which is why #1043's number moved when that was corrected.
#
# So the bug was latent, not active: three separate accidents of tuning stood
# between a commanded course into a solid object and a craft inside one. Tighten
# an arrival radius, raise a leg speed, grow a collider back, or hand the rung
# to a hull with less drag, and a hauler parks in a depot. A berth that means
# "dock here" should not be relying on the craft being bad at arriving.
#
# So the `_hull` anchors are where the structures ARE, unmoved to the metre, and
# the `_berth` anchors are where a craft ties up alongside one.
depot_a_hull = [620.0, 0.0, -180.0]
depot_b_hull = [1180.0, 0.0, 240.0]

# TWELVE UNITS, along the ladder's own axis, on the side the run comes from.
#
# The number is the clearance the two hulls need, plus room to arrive in. A
# depot's collider is 3.8, a hauler's is 2.0, and `handle_collisions` separates
# to `r + r + 0.05` — so 5.85 is the closest a hauler can sit to a depot centre
# without being pushed off it. Twelve leaves 6.15 on top of that, more than the
# hauler's own four-unit beam, so a craft that overshoots its berth still stops
# clear instead of in contact.
#
# Not larger, because a berth still has to read as "at the depot". Twelve is
# inside the hauler's own 20-unit `waypoint_arrival_radius`, so the leg
# completes where it always did; inside the destroyer's 500-unit tractor and
# 400-unit repair-dispatch reaches (issue #1164, the coupling ranges that replace
# the old `transfer`/`tow`) by two orders of magnitude; and under a tenth of the
# 130-unit gap from Depot B to the nearest mooring (`worker_mooring`, at
# sqrt(70^2 + 110^2) = 130.4), so nothing on that rung has moved relative to
# anything else.
#
# Along X because X is the ladder's axis — the run spans 560 of X against 420 of
# Z — and toward `ladder_transit` because that is the side the shuttle both
# arrives from and departs to on each rung. A berth on the far side would have
# it pass the depot, turn, and come back. [ai] Unratified, like every other
# coordinate in this table.
depot_a_berth = [632.0, 0.0, -180.0]
ladder_transit = [900.0, 0.0, 40.0]
depot_b_berth = [1168.0, 0.0, 240.0]

# Where the two parties sitting on Depot B are moored. Separate anchors rather
# than one, because "they are both at the depot" is the situation and "they are
# alongside each other" is not.
worker_mooring = [1110.0, 0.0, 350.0]
corporate_mooring = [1050.0, 0.0, 340.0]

# Where Havelock's hired picket sits (#1041). Its own anchor rather than the
# mooring beside it, because a picket parked on top of the boat it is guarding
# is not a picket.
corporate_picket = [1330.0, 0.0, 250.0]

# Where traffic gets held when the corridor cannot take it. Nothing in Act 1
# sends anyone here; the storm slice (#1037) does.
holding_arc = [-640.0, 0.0, 520.0]

# ── Act 2's places (issue #1037) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Where the radiation storm goes, and where everything that has to get out of
# its way goes instead. Falling Skyway composes the template band into a box
# with a 260-unit lateral half-width: the three centres are ON the x=0 corridor,
# and the refuges all sit at least 560 units west of it. A shelter inside a band
# would be an authoring bug the end-to-end traffic test now catches against the
# live instance shape.

# The three band centres, stepping down the corridor from the north end to the
# skyhook head. They are 340 units apart while each corridor-long box extends
# 1,100 units north and south, so consecutive bands OVERLAP: the storm reads as
# one front moving south rather than as three separate weather events.
storm_band_north = [0.0, 0.0, -760.0]
storm_band_gate = [0.0, 0.0, -420.0]
storm_band_head = [0.0, 0.0, -80.0]

# Where the Lyra Ascending is adrift — in the corridor, under the first two
# bands and clear of the third. She has been there since before the crew
# arrived, which is why she is an authored `[[entity]]` and not a spawn.
lyra_drift = [60.0, 0.0, -560.0]

# The lee of the storm: west of the corridor, clear of all three bands, and
# where the rescue objective points a helm — human or backfilled.
storm_lee = [-560.0, 0.0, -300.0]

# The traffic's way out. West FIRST, then south to the holding arc: a craft sent
# straight to the arc from the north end of the corridor would fly diagonally
# down the lane and through the sweep, which is the exact mistake the shelter
# run exists to stop.
shelter_west = [-880.0, 0.0, -300.0]

# ── The witness's place (issue #1039) ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Where the rigger's own skiff is tied up: on the picket, with the committee,
# and NOT alongside them — she is one of the people the committee speak for, not
# one of the people speaking. Inside the destroyer's authored 1000-unit comms
# range from the ladder transit leg that #1036's line objective already sends
# helm to, so a crew who did that act's work can answer her without moving
# again. [ai] Unratified, like every other coordinate in this table.
rigger_mooring = [1050.0, 0.0, 430.0]

# ── Act 3's places (issue #1040) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Where the head's own craft end up when it comes apart. Off the head rather than
# at it, because the wreck is where the ribbon was and nobody survives sitting in
# it; and inside the destroyer's authored 500-unit tractor range of
# `station_keeping`, so a crew who were doing their job in Act 3 are already
# close enough to start pulling people out.
head_debris_field = [120.0, 0.0, 140.0]

# The second craft, about a hundred and forty units further out — one tow's
# reposition away, which is what makes the epilogue a triage rather than a queue.
head_debris_drift = [220.0, 0.0, 240.0]

# ── Where the corridor sheds (issue #1347) ───────────────────────────────────
#
# Three contacts come down out of the storm's wake, and the two that matter are
# each authored ON THE AXIS of a working rung — same X as the depot hull they
# are aimed at — so their courses are checkable by eye against the numbers a few
# hundred lines up: a rock at x = 620 drifting +Z is going to Depot A, and one at
# x = 1180 is going to Depot B.
#
# NOTHING here says either of them is a threat. What is authored is a place and a
# drift; that a rock arrives is arithmetic the projection does over these
# coordinates, and re-authoring a start 60 units off its rung's axis makes the
# same code report a miss with no line of copy edited.
#
# The distances are cut against the hull's OWN reach, which is what makes the
# beat work: the survey suite answers to 260 units and the tactical radar
# acquires at 50, so a crew cannot read a rock from the transfer manifold and
# cannot shoot one they have not flown out to. Both start well outside both
# numbers, and going to look is the whole first half of the work.
#
# [ai] Every coordinate here is unratified, like the rest of this table.

# The lead contact: due north of Depot A's hull, 480 units up-track.
debris_lead_start = [620.0, 0.0, -660.0]

# The trailing contact: due north of Depot B's hull, 540 units up-track. Further
# to run and slower, so it arrives well after the lead — which is what gives
# Tactical two live deadlines to rank rather than one to react to.
debris_trail_start = [1180.0, 0.0, -300.0]

# The third contact, and the one aimed at nothing at all. It sits between the
# ship's Act 3 station and the ladder — near enough to be the FIRST thing the
# radar shows and the first thing anybody would reach for, and just outside the
# 260-unit survey reach, so ruling it out still costs a crew the trip. A field
# where every rock is a threat teaches nothing about assessing rocks.
debris_stray_start = [430.0, 0.0, 60.0]

# ── Lanes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The corridor run. Loops, so a craft left alone flies it for the whole mission
# — which is what makes "the lane stopped" an observable event later rather than
# the end of a script.
#
# `corridor_gate` is leg 0 deliberately: it is the waypoint the scenario asks
# about, and a lane that made the crew wait a full circuit before anything
# reached it would be authoring a countdown, not traffic.
[[route]]
id = "skyway_lane"
on_complete = "loop"

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "corridor_gate"
speed = 0.9
# They slow through the throat and hold briefly for clearance. Texture, and a
# reason for the gate to be a place rather than a coordinate.
hold_secs = 4

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "corridor_south"
speed = 0.9

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "corridor_north"
speed = 0.9

# The ladder run: the shuttle working between the two depot rungs. It keeps
# calling at Depot B even though Depot B is not pumping, which is exactly the
# kind of thing a crew notices and asks about.
[[route]]
id = "ladder_run"
on_complete = "loop"

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "depot_a_berth"
speed = 0.7
hold_secs = 6

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "ladder_transit"
speed = 0.8

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "depot_b_berth"
speed = 0.7
hold_secs = 6

# ── The player ship ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# One hull: the Alliance Destroyer, which is the band-A crew hull and the one
# whose four stations (Captain, Helm, Tactical, Engineering) are the small-crew
# set this mission is tuned for. The `[[entity]]` row below is not replaced by
# this list — `spawn_game_start_entities` still needs a game-start "ship" entity
# to anchor position, uuid and tags on, and takes its loadout from the lobby
# selection — so its `template_path` is kept in step with `available_ships[0]`,
# the same rule `combat_test.toml` records at length.

[[available_ships]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
label = "world.falling_skyway.available_ships.0.label"

[player_spawn]
position = [300.0, 0.0, 420.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [300.0, 0.0, 420.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"
# Mission objectives deliberately carry only the cross-hull directive, not one
# hull's travel tuning. The Helm planner resolves that tuning by objective id
# from the selected hull's doctrine. This world therefore restates the
# destroyer's two standing rows and adds one zero-score configuration row for
# the survey route: it never competes as doctrine, but gives Backfill an authored
# cruise fraction for the long, one-shot tour. Impulse is explicitly off: at
# this route's bends a 108 u/s impulse pass overshoots the first berth instead of
# flying the survey. Both fields tune AI execution only; a human Helm keeps the
# same ship, scan ranges and clock.
[entity.overrides.behaviour]
doctrine = [
  { id = "destroy-hostiles", text = "entity.alliance_destroyer.behaviour.doctrine.destroy_hostiles.text", directive_kind = "Destroy", base_priority = 45.0, target_speed = 0.9, maintain_range = 24.0 },
  { id = "hold-station", text = "entity.alliance_destroyer.behaviour.doctrine.hold_station.text", base_priority = 20.0, target_speed = 0.0 },
  { id = "obj-a1-survey", directive_kind = "Patrol", directive_anchors = ["depot_b_berth", "depot_a_berth", "station_keeping"], directive_loop = false, base_priority = 0.0, target_speed = 0.7, use_impulse = false },
]

# Falling Skyway's transfer run-up gives the destroyer a scenario-local load to
# pump into the receiving manifold below. The fleet hull deliberately carries no
# infrastructure ledger in other worlds (#1164); the game-start instance overlay
# is merged onto the lobby-selected hull, so this cargo exists here and nowhere
# else. It is a separate `reserve_fuel` ledger used only by the umbilical. None of
# the window-supply arithmetic reads it, so priming the manifold cannot increase
# the 52-unit lift ceiling or make the three-claimant choice easier.
[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
publish = false
condition_max = 100.0
decay_per_sec = 0.0
hull_damage_share = 0.0

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "reserve_fuel"
amount = 100
ceiling = 100

# ── The world below ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Anonymous scenery: the city the tether is anchored to, and the star it turns
# under. Neither is script-referenceable, because neither is something the
# mission asks a question about.

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/star_sun.toml"
transform = { position = [-4200.0, 0.0, -3400.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/planet_ecumenopolis.toml"
transform = { position = [0.0, -900.0, 0.0] }

# The deterministic receiving end of Act 3's real transfer work. The passive
# berth template supplies dock markers and an empty `reserve_fuel` ledger; this
# instance adds the operational threshold the scenario listens to. Filling it
# to half through the destroyer's landed dock/umbilical path raises
# `skyway_window_transfer_primed` from THIS entity's authoritative state. The
# threshold is an authored fraction of the 100-unit ceiling: at the destroyer's
# authored 20 units/s it takes 2.5 seconds of genuine flow after Helm makes the
# dock. [ai] Unratified, and the threshold is the pace surface.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/umbilical_berth.toml"
id = "window_transfer_manifold"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.window_transfer_manifold.name"
transform = { anchor = "station_keeping" }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition_max = 100.0
decay_per_sec = 0.0
hull_damage_share = 0.0

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "reserve_fuel"
amount = 0
ceiling = 100

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyway_window_transfer_primed"
capacity = "reserve_fuel"
fails_below = 0.5
restores_above = 0.5

# ── The structures ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The skyhook head. 48 of 100 points on arrival: above its 45 % lift line, but
# only just, which is what makes Act 1 triage rather than repair. Everything
# else about it — the ladder of thresholds, the two berths, the labels the
# dossier reads — is on the template.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/skyhook.toml"
id = "skyhook"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name"
transform = { anchor = "skyway_head" }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 48.0
# The head is worked by the people who are out (issue #1035). This records WHO
# staffs the spine; a repair-team dispatch (issue #1161, the replacement for the
# retired `field_repair` operation) can still cross to it and climb, because the
# ship carries its own team. The strike's old mechanical bite — a field-repair
# throttled to an "unassisted" rate while the workers were out — retired with the
# operations table (issue #1164), so this flag is now the negotiation's business
# and the dossier's, not a rate multiplier the crew feel in a work queue.
workforce = "skyway_workers"

# WHAT CATCHING THE TETHER DOES (issue #1165 S11b). The stabilise beat is now the
# TRACTOR (issue #1156) coupling the head and its held-response (#1158) arresting
# the strain while it holds, in place of the retired `stabilise` operation.
# `arrest-decline` recovers the head's condition at the authored rate; the
# recovered condition crosses `skyhook_load_bearing` (the top rung's 42 % restore
# line) by the one system that owns the flag edges, so `on_head_stands_down`
# fires exactly as it did off the old lump payout and the scenario's DETECTION is
# unchanged. The head's decline is a SCRIPTED beat (`tether_strain`, not
# `decay_per_sec`), so the recovery runs NET of the 0.05 pt/s strain: two points
# a second is 1.95 net, carrying it from the third warning's 24.5 over the 42
# line in about ten seconds — inside the 100-second window the last warning
# leaves. The moment it crosses, `on_head_stands_down` stands the watch down and
# the strain stops, so one hold saves it outright.
# [ai] Unratified — the tuning surface of the save margin.
[entity.overrides.held_response]
kind = "arrest-decline"
recover_per_sec = 2.0

# There are people on the head, and Act 3 is them calling the ship (issue #1040).
# The template gives the structure a 1,600-unit `[comms] range` and stops there —
# a range is what a transfer head needs to talk to the corridor, and whether the
# crew may call IT is a scenario's business. Falling Skyway says yes: a captain
# who has just been warned three times that a structure is failing must be able
# to call the people on it back.
[entity.overrides.comms]
hailable = true

# ── WHAT SECURITY CAN DO ON THE HEAD (issue #1346) ───────────────────────────
#
# There are people on the head and the tether is slipping under them. This table
# is the whole of what a boarding party may be sent up there to do, and it is
# authored HERE rather than anywhere in Rust: the engine knows four generic verbs
# and nothing at all about the Falling Skyway, so a compartment on this head and
# a boarding target in some later mission are the same code path with different
# numbers.
#
# ONE action, deliberately. The head is not a place you contain something on —
# the emergency is the structure itself, which is the tractor's job (#1156) and
# the repair dispatch's (#1161). What a Security team adds is the half neither of
# those can do: getting the people off while the structural work goes on. That is
# also why it is authored `life_safety` — the top of the backfill's priority
# order, above anything at Ladder B — so a hull with two teams and both jobs in
# reach sends the first one HERE, and a hull with one team left holds it for here
# rather than spending it on containment.
#
# `outcome_flag` is the ONLY consequence path: raising it is what reaches the
# script (`on_head_evacuation_assisted`), so the scenario hangs its beat off an
# ordinary world flag exactly as the strike settlement hangs off
# `skyway_strike_settled`. Nothing in the engine knows what the flag means.
#
# [ai] All three numbers unratified. 45 seconds against the ~100 the third tether
# warning leaves is the trade the act turns on: a crew who commit a team to the
# head cannot also have that team on the ladder, and a crew who leave it too late
# get the team interrupted by the failure rather than a completion.
[entity.overrides.security_target]

[[entity.overrides.security_target.action]]
action = "assist_evacuation"
duration_secs = 45.0
risk = 0.65
priority = "life_safety"
outcome_flag = "skyway_head_evacuation_assisted"
warning = "world.falling_skyway.security.warning.head_evacuation"

# Ladder Depot A — the rung that still works. Its capacity and threshold tables
# are replaced wholesale by this instance (arrays replace at the instance
# layer), because a flag name and a capacity id are the SCENARIO's namespace:
# two depots sharing `depot_transfer_capable` would be declaring one flag
# between them, and the second would overwrite the first's answer every tick.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "depot_ladder_a"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_a.name"
# The HULL anchor, not the berth. The structure has not moved; the berth beside
# it is a separate place now — see the `[anchors]` table.
transform = { anchor = "depot_a_hull" }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 62.0
# Company people, and they are not the ones who walked out (issue #1035). This
# is why A goes on pumping while B does not, and it is authored on the depot
# rather than implied by which one the mission happens to gate: the rung that
# still works is the rung whose crews are still there.
workforce = "havelock_operations"

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "depot_a_fuel_lift"
amount = 40
label = "world.falling_skyway.capacity.fuel_lift.label"

# ── THE BERTH THAT IS LEFT WHEN THERE IS NO LIFT (issue #1043) ───────────────
#
# ONE mooring on the working rung, and it is the whole of what the corridor can
# offer a crew who reach the transfer window with nothing in it — a head that is
# no longer certified to run a climber, or a head that is no longer there. It is
# not passage. Nobody leaves the rock; somebody sits the weather out alongside a
# structure that still has power on it and a rung that is still pumping.
#
# It is authored on the RUNG rather than on Control's manifest, which is the
# opposite call to the one the window's seven rows make and for the same reason
# they make theirs: the window's figure is a property of the whole CHAIN, and a
# berth is a property of THIS depot. Control publishes what the corridor can
# lift; Ladder A publishes what Ladder A can tie up alongside it.
#
# ONE against three claims, so the smaller scene is short by two exactly as the
# window is short by one — and it is a capacity row rather than a rule in the
# script for the reason the three claims are. "Who gets it" is then arithmetic a
# crew can read off a panel, `shelter_supply` refuses it outright when the rung
# is under its own line or its people have walked out, and a tuning pass that
# authors a second berth changes the ending without touching a handler.
#
# [ai] Unratified, and it is the whole tuning surface of the collapse variant.
[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "depot_a_shelter_berths"
amount = 1
label = "world.falling_skyway.capacity.shelter_berths.label"

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "depot_a_pumping"
fails_below = 0.4
label = "world.falling_skyway.threshold.pumping.label"

# Ladder Depot B — 34 of 100, under its own 40 % line, so `depot_b_pumping` is
# DOWN from the depot's first tick and stays there. The crew do not have to be
# told the ladder is broken; the panel says so before anyone speaks. This is
# also the depot the strike sits on (#1035) and the one whose transfers get
# refused, so it is authored with the same shape as A and a worse number.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "depot_ladder_b"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name"
# The HULL anchor, not the berth — same split as Depot A.
transform = { anchor = "depot_b_hull" }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]

# ── THE WINDOW MANIFEST (issue #1042) ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Control runs the transfer window, so Control keeps the paperwork for it. This
# block is that paperwork, and it is the ONE console surface the whole of Act 3's
# arithmetic lands on: seven labelled rows on the authority's own fact sheet,
# where a crew already goes to ask what the corridor is doing.
#
# It is here rather than on the skyhook head for two reasons and neither is
# fiction. First, the number the crew need is a property of the CHAIN — the head
# and both rungs and the people who staff them — and hanging it off one of the
# three links would say the head decides it. Second, an `[[entity.overrides…]]`
# capacity array REPLACES the template's wholesale at the instance layer (see
# the depots, which restate theirs for exactly that reason), so putting these on
# the head would mean restating `skyhook_transfer_berths` and
# `skyhook_climber_load` in this file — and the head's own template says at
# length that those two numbers belong on the structure.
#
# `station_axiom.toml` authors no `[infrastructure]` at all, so this creates the
# track rather than editing one. That is the whole cost of the choice: Control
# gains a condition bar it did not have. It is authored full and NOTHING in this
# mission moves it — the manifest needed somewhere to live, and a published
# capacity has to hang on a structure that publishes.
#
# ── The three claims: DEMAND IS AUTHORED ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# What each party has asked for, in lift units, filed before the crew arrived.
# These do not move: a claimant does not want less because the ladder is broken.
# Supply is computed from the mission (the Act 3 script does the arithmetic);
# demand is data, and this is the data.
#
# [ai] EVERY NUMBER HERE IS UNRATIFIED, and the three of them together are the
# tuning surface of the whole act. They are sized against what the chain can
# ever deliver — 40 from Ladder A plus 12 from Ladder B is 52, and nothing in
# the mission can raise either — so that:
#
#   any TWO fit          18+22 = 40, 18+26 = 44, 22+26 = 48, all under 52
#   all THREE never do   66 against 52, so the window is short by 14 even for a
#                        crew who did everything right
#
# "Capacity for two" is therefore arithmetic rather than a rule written down
# anywhere, which is what #1043's choice scene needs: it enforces the constraint
# by reading these numbers, not by hard-coding "pick two".
[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]

label = "world.falling_skyway.capacity.claim_committee.label"

# a mission that could only answer them with a beam would be teaching the wrong
# lesson about the Alliance.
#
# TWO actions, and they are genuinely different jobs rather than one job at two
# prices:
#
#   secure_contain   From outside. A team crosses, gets the mounts locked out and
#                    the boat's own crew stood down, and comes home. Shorter and
#                    safer, because nobody has to go through a hatch somebody

#                    anywhere in reach; boarding is what a Security seat does
#                    when it has run out of better things to do, or what a human

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ACT 2 — THE RADIATION STORM AND THE RESCUE (issue #1037)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# Act 1 was a survey. #1036's negotiation opens Act 2 on the dispute; this is the
# act's OTHER half, and it arrives whatever the crew decided about the strike.
# Weather turns a survey into a set of decisions with a clock on them.
#
# ── The storm is not a system ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# It is `region_radiation_band.toml` — an authored region template composing
# `damage_zone`, `radar_dampening`, `sensor_blind`, `comms_jammed` and
# `slow_zone` — spawned on the named deadlines below (#1024) and retired with
# `destroy_entity` (#1033). The retirement is what makes it a SWEEP rather than
# a wall: each band arrives, dwells for forty seconds and goes, and the next one
# is 340 units further south. Nothing in Rust knows a storm exists.
#
# Inside a band the crew's radar range falls to about a third, sensors go blind,
# comms jam, and the hull takes light continuous damage. `region_radiation_band`
# carries the arithmetic; the short form is that the destroyer survives crossing
# a band and does not survive living in one, and a 60-point civilian hauler
# cannot cross one at all.
#
# ── The sweep's clock, and why the traffic goes first ────────────────────────
#
#   t=400  storm_front_due     Control's forecast. Navigation's clearance work
#                              and the Lyra's crisis become the crew's problem.
#   t=580  storm_band_one_due  the first band, over the north corridor. Retires
#                              at t=620, forty seconds later.
#   t=740  storm_band_two_due  the second, over the upper gate. Retires t=780.
#   t=768  lyra_clear_due      THE RESCUE'S CLOCK. She is under control by now
#                              or the band has her.
#   t=900  storm_band_three_due  the third, over the head. Retires t=940.
#   t=1072 storm_passed_due    the corridor is clear. Traffic goes back on the
#                              lane and the act closes.
#
# THREE MINUTES of warning before the first band includes the human work the
# headless arithmetic cannot price: reading the forecast, agreeing an order and
# finding the control. A bulk hauler makes twelve units a second and needs about
# thirty-five of them to get clear once its unchanged authored
# acknowledge-and-decide delay has run. The rest is crew decision time.
#
# ── The rescue, and the two numbers that make it a real decision ─────────────
#
# The payload of the act is a TOW: the Lyra Ascending, a bulk hauler with a dead
# drive, adrift in the corridor with the front coming down on her. The crew take
# her under the destroyer's TRACTOR (issue #1156) and her held-response (#1158,
# authored on her `[entity.overrides.held_response]` above) recovers her while
# the beam holds — the replacement for the retired `tow` operation (issue #1164).
# The recovery is authored to carry her over her line in about thirteen seconds,
# so the crew still make a real decision around the storm: set off early, in
# clear air, and the rescue lands well inside the deadline; wait for the picture
# to improve and the picture is what you lose, because inside a band the radar is
# at a third and the channels are jammed. The old `tow`'s 50 % slow-zone rule is
# gone — the storm no longer THROTTLES external work (issue #1164); it reaches the
# coupling systems as damage and power like any other system — so the deciding is
# about SEEING and about the deadline, not about a rate the band turns down.
#
# HOW A COMPLETED RESCUE IS DETECTED — UNCHANGED. There is no "operation
# completed" trigger; what the work leaves behind IS its payoff. The Lyra authors
# a condition threshold at half of her hundred points and starts at thirty, and
# the tractor's arrest-decline recovery is what carries her over it. The flag
# rising IS the rescue landing, and `on_flag_set` hangs off it like any other
# world flag — the same reading the old lump payout left behind.
# [ai] This is a judgement call about what a condition track means on a stricken
# CRAFT: hers is her drive and her rig, not her plating (`hull_damage_share = 0`
# says so), so "under control" is the reading that moves when somebody takes the
# strain off her — and never moves because the storm scoured her paint.
#
# ── Failing it is a thing that happens, not a thing that vanishes ────────────
#
# At `lyra_clear_due`, if she is not under control, the band has her: the
# objective fails, `destroy_entity` takes her, and the chained `on_destroyed`
# posts the mandatory report objective and writes the campaign flags. One of
# `skyway_lyra_recovered` and `skyway_lyra_lost` is ALWAYS written, so a later
# act — or a later mission — reads a fact rather than an absence.

# ── Act 2's traffic route ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The shelter run. Not a divert-to-anchor, because the anchor a craft is sent to
# matters less than the way it gets there: a hauler at the north end told to
# make for the holding arc would fly diagonally down the corridor and straight
# through the sweep. West first, then south, then hold.
#
# It loops so a craft parked on it stays parked. At `storm_passed_due` the
# scenario marshals survivors back onto `skyway_lane`; that return order is not
# the safety decision, which belongs to Navigation before band one.
[[route]]
id = "storm_shelter_run"
on_complete = "loop"

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "shelter_west"

# ── The stricken craft ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Lyra Ascending. Adrift in the corridor from the first tick of the mission,
# because she has been adrift since before anybody sent a destroyer — an
# `[[entity]]` rather than a spawn, for the reason the strike is authored rather
# than scripted on tick one.
#
# She carries no `[civilian] route`. A craft under tow is not on a lane, and
# giving her one would have the traffic adapter and the tow arguing over where
# she is every tick.
#
# THE THREE AUTHORED FACTS THAT MAKE HER A RESCUE:
#
#   hull_integrity 400   she is a bulk hull, not a shuttle. At the band's
#                        effective two and a half points a second she can sit
#                        through two bands' worth of front without burning up,
#                        which is what makes the DEADLINE the thing that ends
#                        her rather than a damage race the crew cannot see.
#                        [ai] Unratified.
#   hull_damage_share 0  her condition track is her drive and her rig. At the
#                        1.0 default the storm would drag it to zero and the
#                        rescue could not be completed at all — the payout would
#                        land on a track that had already bottomed out.
#   condition 30/100     under her own authored half-way line, so
#                        `skyway_lyra_under_control` is DOWN from her first tick
#                        and its rise is an event. The crew do not need telling
#                        she is in trouble; the panel says so.
#
# `narrative = true` (issue #1338) marks her for the mission timeline. She is
# the one hull in this act whose ARRIVAL and FATE are both story: the timeline
# records her spawn, and `on_lyra_recovered` / `on_lyra_clear_due` state her
# outcome outright rather than letting the engine infer one from a despawn.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
id = "lyra_ascending"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name"
narrative = true
transform = { anchor = "lyra_drift" }

[entity.overrides]
comms = { hailable = true }
hull = { hull_integrity = 400.0 }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 30.0
hull_damage_share = 0.0

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "skyway_lyra_under_control"
fails_below = 0.5
label = "world.falling_skyway.threshold.under_control.label"

# WHAT TAKING THE STRAIN OFF HER DOES (issue #1165 S11b). The rescue is now the
# TRACTOR (issue #1156) coupling her and its held-response (#1158) recovering
# her, in place of the retired `tow` operation. `arrest-decline` is the reading
# the header above argues for: her condition track is her drive and her rig, so
# holding her steady lets it recover, and the recovered condition crosses the
# `skyway_lyra_under_control` line by the one system that owns the flag edges —
# `on_flag_set` still hangs off it exactly as it did off the old payout, so the
# scenario's DETECTION is unchanged. She authors no `decay_per_sec`, so the
# `recover_per_sec` below is her NET rate: two points a second carries her from
# 30 over her 55-point restore line in about thirteen seconds, inside the
# rescue's window with the same room the 24-second tow had.
# [ai] Unratified — the whole tuning surface of the rescue's pace.
[entity.overrides.held_response]
kind = "arrest-decline"
recover_per_sec = 2.0
