# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# ACT 3 — THE HEAD COMES DOWN, OR IT DOES NOT (issue #1040)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#
# THE SKYHOOK CAN FALL. Not as a score penalty at the end of the mission: the
# head's condition walks down to the structural floor its template authors, and
# at that floor `destroy_entity` takes it out of the world mid-mission. Twenty-
# six units of station silhouette stop being on anybody's radar. The mission does
# not end there — it branches into a survivor-rescue epilogue — but the structure
# the scenario is named after is gone, and this is what Act 1's triage was for.
#
# ── What drives it down ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# THE STRAIN. The storm has passed and the corridor is working again, which means
# the head is carrying traffic on a ribbon that has been slipping since before
# the crew arrived. That load costs it [0.5] condition points every [10] seconds,
# for as long as the tether watch is open — a scripted beat that re-arms itself,
# NOT the template's `decay_per_sec`, which the skyhook deliberately does not
# author (its own header says why: decay ticks from world load and would charge
# the mission for the lobby).
#
# This averages 0.05 points a second. The run is deterministic because each
# applied half-point slice is exactly representable and re-arms on fixed ticks;
# every number below is derived from that schedule rather than guessed.
#
# ── The warning ladder, and the window it buys ───────────────────────────────
#
# `skyhook.toml` authors five rungs; Act 3 crosses four of them. The head opens
# the act on 42 points (48 on arrival, six spent by Act 1's `tether_slip`), so
# the strain walks it down half a point at a time:
#
#   t=1072  the storm passes, the watch opens, and its first beat lands with it:
#           the head is on 42 and goes straight to 41.5
#   t=1172  36.5 — under 37 %: `skyhook_load_bearing` falls     WARNING ONE
#   t=1292  30.5 — under 31 %: `skyhook_tether_tensioned` falls WARNING TWO
#   t=1412  24.5 — under 25 %: `skyhook_station_holding` falls  WARNING THREE
#   t=1512  19.5 — under 20 %: `skyhook_tether_stable` falls    THE FLOOR
#
# Those are MEASURED times, off the headless trace, not predicted ones — the
# threshold fires a frame behind the beat that crosses it, and the act's opening
# beat lands on the same tick the watch opens.
#
# The first two warning gaps are two minutes apiece: six condition points at
# 0.05 points a second, discretised by a ten-second beat. The final rung is five
# points above the floor and therefore leaves 100 seconds. Three warnings, each
# louder than the last, and a real last chance before the head comes apart.
#
# ── THE SAVE MARGIN, derived rather than asserted ────────────────────────────
#
# The AC this slice is held to is that a crew who react to the LAST warning can
# still save the structure. The save is now the crew coupling the head with the
# TRACTOR (issue #1156) and its arrest-decline held-response recovering it (issue
# #1158, authored on the head's `[entity.overrides.held_response]` above), in
# place of the retired `stabilise` operation (issue #1164). The arithmetic:
#
#   final warning window           100 s   (24.5 points → 19.5 at 0.05 pt/s)
#   tractor arrest-decline recovery ~10 s  (24.5 -> the 42 line, net of strain)
#   ────────────────────────────────────
#   SLACK FOR GIVING THE ORDER      ~90 s
#
# The recovery arrests the head's decline the moment the beam takes hold and
# recovers it NET of the 0.05 pt/s strain, carrying it from the third warning's
# 24.5 back over the FIRST rung's 42 % restore line — and the moment it crosses, the
# watch stands down and the strain stops, so one hold stands the whole ladder
# down rather than buying another hundred seconds. A crew who react late are
# unambiguously a crew who saved it, with real room to spare.
#
# The travel term is zero on purpose. The tractor is authored at 500 units and
# Act 3's own approach objective puts the ship at `station_keeping`, 247 units
# off the head — so a crew flying the mission's own shape are already in range
# when the first warning lands, and the margin is about DECIDING rather than
# about flying. A crew who wandered off pay their own travel out of it.
#
# `falling_skyway_act_3_a_crew_who_react_to_the_last_warning_save_the_head` is
# the playtest, and it is a playtest rather than an assertion about arithmetic:
# it waits for the third warning to actually fire, engages the tractor then, and
# asserts the head is still in the world after the tick the floor would have been
# crossed on. [ai] The recover rate is unratified — it is the number the tuning
# pass moves to make "you can react to the last warning, but only if you were
# paying attention" land exactly.
#
# ── The three surfaces a warning reaches ─────────────────────────────────────
#
# A first-time crew must not be ambushed, so every rung fires on all three:
#
#   THE OBJECTIVES LIST   each rung posts its own mandatory objective, at a
#                         higher priority than the last, naming what happens
#                         next. And each rung FAILS the previous one — so a crew
#                         who lose the head can read the panel afterwards and see
#                         exactly which warnings went red under them. That is the
#                         `obj-a2-corroborate` device (an objective going red is
#                         the loudest thing this scenario can say without prose)
#                         pointed at the crew's own inattention.
#   THE CAPTAIN'S CLOCK   `skyhook_failure_due` is authored `visible`, so the
#                         countdown to structural failure is on the captain's
#                         panel from the mission's first tick — the same doctrine
#                         Act 2's six deadlines follow. It is CANCELLED the
#                         moment the situation resolves either way, so the panel
#                         never counts down to something that has already
#                         happened.
#   THE CHANNEL           the gang on the head call the ship, from the head's own
#                         hull, three times, each more urgent. They are the
#                         people who will be on it when it goes, and the last
#                         call is them asking to be taken off.
#
# ── The countdown is a PROJECTION, not a fuse ────────────────────────────────
#
# `skyhook_failure_due` is authored at [1528] seconds: sixteen seconds after the
# measured floor crossing above. Nothing about the head's fate is decided by it —
# what takes the head is its CONDITION reaching the floor, and the deadline is
# what that arithmetic says if nobody does anything. A crew who
# neglect it watch the projection come true sixteen seconds early. A crew who
# stabilise beat it, and the deadline firing on a head that is still standing IS
# the act's other ending: the load comes off, the corridor's own structural
# people take over, and she held.
#
# ── What losing it costs ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three things, all on screen and all derived from authored state:
#
#   THE TRANSFER WINDOW   the head carried the only two berths in the corridor
#                         (`skyhook_transfer_berths`), and they leave the world
#                         with it. `skyway_transfer_capacity_lost` is the flag
#                         #1042 reads; the corridor's traffic is put back on the
#                         holding run, because there is nothing to queue for.
#   THE PEOPLE ON IT      counted, never rolled — the same rule #1036's casualty
#                         arithmetic follows. `head_casualties` reads the shift
#                         that was up there (a settled strike means a FULL shift
#                         working the transfer; a rung still stopped means a
#                         skeleton watch), then subtracts what the captain did
#                         about the warnings. Answering the head's channel at all
#                         is worth one; ordering the head cleared at the first or
#                         second warning is worth all of them; ordering it at the
#                         THIRD is too late to get everyone off and the boss says
#                         so. A crew who never picked up the channel lose the
#                         whole shift.
#   THE CAMPAIGN RECORD   exactly one of `skyway_skyhook_lost` and
#                         `skyway_skyhook_held` is ALWAYS written, the invariant
#                         #1037 set for the Lyra, so a later mission reads a fact
#                         rather than an absence.
#
# ── The epilogue ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Losing the skyhook is a worse ending, not a game over. Two craft come off the
# head as it goes — its crew lighter and a work pod — spawned by the collapse
# handler into the debris, adrift, with condition tracks the tractor's
# arrest-decline recovery is sized to cross. That is the Lyra's machinery reused
# exactly: there is no "operation completed" trigger, so what a held tow LEAVES
# BEHIND is the signal, and `on_flag_set` hangs off the threshold it crosses.
#
# The epilogue has [75] seconds, its own two objectives (an approach carrying the
# Reach directive, and the rescue that records the work — split for the reason
# Act 2's rescue is split), and its own resolution: both craft recovered
# completes it, one completes it with the other's loss on the record, neither
# fails it and the debris takes them both.
#
# SHIP DESTRUCTION IS A DIFFERENT PATH ENTIRELY and nothing here touches it. The
# crew's own hull dying is the engine's `GameOver`, with no scenario flag written
# and no epilogue: `skyway_skyhook_lost` and `skyway_skyhook_held` are both
# absent from that run, which is what makes the branches distinguishable rather
# than merely different in tone.

# ── Act 3's clock ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# One deadline, visible, and it is a PROJECTION rather than a fuse — the band
# header above says at length why. [1528] is sixteen seconds past the floor crossing
# the authored strain rate reaches, measured off the headless trace rather than
# guessed at.
[[deadline]]
id = "skyhook_failure_due"
label = "world.falling_skyway.deadline.skyhook_failure.label"
due_secs = 1528
visible = true

# ── Act 3's clock (issue #1042) ──────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# THE TWO DEADLINES THE WHOLE MISSION HAS BEEN WATCHING. Both are authored here,
# beside Act 1's and Act 2's, and both are `visible` — so they are on the
# captain's countdown from the mission's first tick, not posted when the act
# that uses them opens. That is the point: the transfer window is the thing the
# crew are working towards from the moment they arrive, and a deadline that
# appeared at t=1072 would be news rather than a schedule.
#
# The pair reads as ONE window on the panel. Before `skyway_transfer_window`
# fires, its remaining time is how long the crew have to make the chain better.
# After it fires it is spent, and the row beneath it — `skyway_window_closes` —
# is the window's own duration running down. Two named deadlines rather than one
# deadline and a scripted duration, because the panel already renders a
# countdown per deadline and a duration nobody could see coming would be a
# stopwatch the crew are not holding.
#
# THE WINDOW OPENS AFTER THE TETHER'S FATE IS SETTLED, and seventy-two seconds
# is the whole of the gap. `skyhook_failure_due` above falls at 1528 — the projection
# the collapse slice (#1040) either beats or does not — so by 1600 the head has
# either held or come out of the world, and the supply this window is priced at
# is a fact rather than a forecast. Pricing it while the tether was still walking
# down would have published a figure that stopped being true a minute later, and
# the alternative — re-pricing the window mid-flight — would mean a captain could
# book a lift against capacity that evaporated under it.
#
# THAT ORDERING IS THE WHOLE INTERLOCK BETWEEN THE TWO HALVES OF ACT 3. A crew
# who let the head go arrive at a window with nothing in it; a crew who caught it
# late arrive at one that cannot lift, because a stabilise carries the head back
# over its FIRST warning rung and not back over its lift certification; a crew
# who kept it certified arrive with everything the ladder can give. Three
# outcomes, one number, and the window's arithmetic names nothing the collapse
# authors.
#
# #1131 RATIFIES BOTH NUMBERS as the act's pacing surface. 1600 is 72 seconds
# past the projection: long enough that the fate has landed and its consequence
# has been mirrored. 1800 gives the allocation scene 200 seconds — enough to
# read and coordinate, while the authored capacity, not a hidden stopwatch,
# remains what limits the crew to two claims.
[[deadline]]
id = "skyway_transfer_window"
label = "world.falling_skyway.deadline.transfer_window.label"
due_secs = 1600
visible = true

[[deadline]]
id = "skyway_window_closes"
label = "world.falling_skyway.deadline.window_closes.label"
due_secs = 1800
visible = true

# ═══ THE CORRIDOR OBSTRUCTION (issue #1350) ══════════════════════════════════
#
# A slab of the shed ribbon has come down across the throat and wedged. Unlike
# the drifting debris of #1347 — which Tactical breaks up with gunnery — this one
# is lodged, and breaking it up in place with weapons scatters the WORST debris
# pattern of all. The controlled way to clear it is the four-stage act #1350
# names: Tactical dispatches Security to PLACE CHARGES on it, Engineering holds
# the mass with the TRACTOR while the charges are set, Security WITHDRAWS, and
# then Tactical DETONATES.
#
# ── Who owns what ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The ENGINE owns the four stages. `[[security_target.action]] place_charges`
# (issue #1346) is stage one and raises `skyway_obstruction_charges_placed` when
# the team's work completes — which ARMS the detonation, because the
# `[demolition_target]` below reads that same flag as "charges placed". The
# tractor (issue #1156) is stage two, engaged on this mass by Engineering or its
# Backfill. `DetonateCharges` (issue #1350) is stage four, fired through the
# `security` system Tactical owns; the engine decides the OUTCOME from the live
# team and tractor state and raises exactly one of three flags.
#
# THIS FILE owns every consequence, off those flags, exactly as the #1347 debris
# band owns its strikes: nothing below is a special case in Rust.
#
#   SAFE         (charges + team clear + held)  → limited debris, mass cleared.
#   UNSUPPORTED  (charges + team clear + UNHELD) → heavier debris, mass cleared.
#   PREMATURE    (charges + team STILL ON IT)   → casualties, mass cleared.
#   WEAPONS      (no charges — killed by fire)  → worst debris (`on_destroyed`).
#
# Placement completing must NEVER detonate on its own: `place_charges` starts the
# team home, and firing is a separate explicit `DetonateCharges`. That is the
# engine's contract; this file only reacts to the flags it raises.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_large.toml"
id = "corridor_obstruction"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name"
transform = { anchor = "corridor_obstruction" }

# The wedged mass sits still and heavy. A big collider and a still position: it is
# not going anywhere until the charges clear it.
[entity.overrides]
mass = 900.0

# ── WHAT SECURITY CAN DO ON THE OBSTRUCTION (issue #1346) ────────────────────
#
# One action: place charges. It is authored `urgent_objective` so a Backfilled
# Tactical, working its Objective pool, will commit a team to it — but below the
# head's `life_safety`, so the tether emergency still comes first. `outcome_flag`
# is the seam to #1350: raising it is "charges are placed", which is what the
# `[demolition_target]` below reads to arm the detonate control.
#
# [ai] All three numbers unratified. 30 seconds of exposure on an unstable mass,
# against the ~8-second crossing the destroyer's teams take.
[entity.overrides.security_target]

[[entity.overrides.security_target.action]]
action = "place_charges"
duration_secs = 30.0
risk = 0.55
priority = "urgent_objective"
outcome_flag = "skyway_obstruction_charges_placed"
warning = "world.falling_skyway.security.warning.obstruction_charges"

# ── WHAT DETONATING THE CHARGES DOES (issue #1350) ───────────────────────────
#
# Five flag names, nothing else. The engine reads `charges_flag` to know the
# detonate control is armed, raises `detonated_flag` on any shot to mark it spent
# and carry the generic beat, and raises exactly one of the three outcome flags
# the four-outcome decision picks. `stabilization_required` says this mass needs
# the tractor: fire it unheld and the outcome is UNSUPPORTED rather than SAFE.
[entity.overrides.demolition_target]
charges_flag = "skyway_obstruction_charges_placed"
detonated_flag = "skyway_obstruction_detonated"
safe_flag = "skyway_obstruction_cleared_safe"
unsupported_flag = "skyway_obstruction_cleared_unsupported"
premature_flag = "skyway_obstruction_premature"
stabilization_required = true
warning = "world.falling_skyway.demolition.warning.obstruction"

# ── THE CASTAWAY LIFEBOAT (issue #1348 mechanism, T2 refinement) ─────────────
#
# A small craft carrying three civilians, drifted into the corridor throat. The
# whole rescue rides its own template: a `[hull]` so weapons can destroy it, an
# `[infrastructure]` condition track so a scan can read it, and a
# `[civilian_rescue]` count of who is aboard. The world only PLACES it; the id is
# what the discovery and rescue flags key on — `scan.corridor_castaway.taken`,
# `rescue.corridor_castaway.recovered`, `rescue.corridor_castaway.lost` — which
# the castaway band at the end of the script reacts to. Nothing is scripted: the
# crew scan it to discover the life signs, then beam them aboard with Engineering.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/skyway_castaway_lifeboat.toml"
id = "corridor_castaway"
name = "world.falling_skyway.entity.castaway_lifeboat.name"
transform = { anchor = "corridor_castaway" }

# ── Act 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_arrival");

on_deadline("tether_slip", "on_tether_slip");
on_deadline("lark_first_hail_due", "on_lark_first_hail");
on_deadline("skyway_survey_due", "on_survey_due");
on_deadline("lark_final_hail_due", "on_lark_final_hail");
on_deadline("lark_collision_due", "on_lark_collision");
on_flag_set("scan.skyhook.taken", "on_survey_scan");
on_flag_set("scan.depot_ladder_a.taken", "on_survey_scan");
on_flag_set("scan.depot_ladder_b.taken", "on_survey_scan");

// The dispute exists before any era boundary. Each registration is reserved for
// one hardening state, so a crew who hail early, clear the channel and return
// after an escalation still have a crew-initiated way back into both paths.
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name", "on_committee_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_strike_hardening) < 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name", "on_committee_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_strike_hardening) == 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name", "on_committee_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_strike_hardening) > 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name", "on_havelock_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_strike_hardening) < 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name", "on_havelock_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_strike_hardening) == 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name", "on_havelock_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_strike_hardening) > 1");

// A hail trigger is one-shot. Keep a distinct trigger armed for the partial and
// ready states: a false trigger-level `when` does NOT consume it, so a crew who
// checks in early can clear the channel, finish the tour and hail again. The
// third registration provides one post-filing acknowledgement on a fresh hail.
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name", "on_control_survey_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_survey_scans_complete) < 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name", "on_control_survey_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_survey_scans_complete) > 0 and counter(skyway_survey_reported) < 1");
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name", "on_control_survey_hailed")
    .when("counter(skyway_survey_reported) > 0");

// The two events the crew's own objectives resolve on. Neither is a timer: one
// is a structure crossing an authored line, the other is a hull arriving at an
// authored place, and both are single-shot.
on_flag_cleared("skyhook_lift_capable", "on_lift_tolerance_lost");
on_waypoint_reached("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name", "corridor_gate", "on_lane_open");

// THE SETTLEMENT SEAM (#1035). The strike ends here and only here, and it is
// chained off an ordinary world flag rather than wired into a dialogue: the
// negotiation is #1036's and the CONSEQUENCE is this slice's, so whoever sets
// `skyway_strike_settled` — a comms answer, a deadline, a later act — gets the
// same settlement applied in one place. Early dialogue can now set it before
// the objective posts, and the remembered-objective helper preserves that work.
on_flag_set("skyway_strike_settled", "on_strike_settled");

// THE SECURITY SEAM (#1346). A boarding party finishing its authored work at a
// target raises that target's authored `outcome_flag` on the ordinary world
// store, so the consequence arrives here the same way the settlement does — off
// a flag, not off a wire into the Security System. Nothing in the engine knows
// what either flag means; both handlers are this scenario's.
on_flag_set("skyway_head_evacuation_assisted", "on_head_evacuation_assisted");
on_flag_set("depot_b_gallery_contained", "on_gallery_contained");

// The corridor and triage reads are visible on arrival. The survey itself posts
// when the tether slips: its deadline is visible from the opening tick, and the
// structures plus Control are already actionable, so a crew can pre-empt the
// post without shortening the mission's authored schedule.
fn on_arrival(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.act = 1;
    // These are mission-clock timers, scheduled once from world arrival. A
    // response admitted before either one lands raises the engagement memory and
    // both handlers become deterministic no-ops.
    ctx.schedule.after(120, |ctx| { harden_strike(ctx, 1); });
    ctx.schedule.after(300, |ctx| { harden_strike(ctx, 2); });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a1-corridor",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.corridor.text",
        mandatory: true,
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a1-triage",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.triage.text",
        mandatory: true,
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name"],
    });
}

// Generic pre-emption memory for this scenario's late-posting threads. The work
// itself raises `completion_flag` at the place it happens; posting then reads the
// authoritative flag store and resolves immediately when the crew got there
// early. #1135 reuses this for the crowded back-half threads.
fn post_remembered_objective(ctx, spec, completion_flag) {
    let id = spec.id;
    ctx.effects.add_objective(spec);
    if ctx.flags[completion_flag] > 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective(id);
    }
}

fn post_survey_objective(ctx) {

        directive_loop: false,

// AI-addressable by construction (issue #1139): Helm flies one authored tour,
// while each Sensors step names its own subject and is independently visible to
// the crew. B/A/head priorities descend in the same order as the travel route,
// so Backfill retries the next useful reading as the hull reaches it. A scan
// taken before the tether slip is authoritative memory, so its step is skipped
// rather than posted already green.
fn post_survey_scan_objective(ctx, id, text, target, scan_flag, priority) {
    if ctx.flags[scan_flag] > 0 { return; }
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{

        text: text,
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: priority,

        targets: [target],

}

// The slip. Six points off a head sitting at 48 takes it to 42 — under the 45 %

// ── SECURITY (#1346) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The slip is the beat that puts people in danger, so it is the beat that makes
// the boarding party's work visible. Two objectives, both OPTIONAL: the mandatory
// set is #1142's and this slice does not widen it. What they buy is the crew
// being TOLD there is something a team could do, and — because each carries a
// `Secure` directive naming its structure — the backfill Security host being
// told the same thing, so a hull with nobody at the owning console works the same
// list in the same order.
//
// The directive names WHAT to secure and nothing else. Which of the target's
// authored actions gets served is the target's own ranking (`life_safety` on the
// head, `threat_containment` on Ladder B), which is what keeps the mission from
// having to know a structure's internal vocabulary — and what makes the head win
// the tie when both are in reach and only one team is free.
//
// Pre-emption memory, like every other late-posting thread here: a crew who got
// there before the slip see the row post already green rather than being asked to
// do it twice.
fn post_security_objectives(ctx) {
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a1-head-evacuation",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.head_evacuation.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 70,
        directive_kind: "Secure",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name"],
    }, "skyway_head_evacuation_assisted");
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a1-gallery",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.gallery_fire.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 30,
        directive_kind: "Secure",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name"],
    }, "depot_b_gallery_contained");
    // THE PICKET (#1349), and the third `Secure` in this list rather than a
    // fourth kind of thing. The obstruction in the lane is Security work before
    // it is gunnery work, and saying so HERE is what makes it gunnery work last:
    // a `Secure` directive naming the boat promotes its authored containment to
    // the Objective class in the backfill's ranking, while Tactical is handed
    // nothing at all until a captain authorises it on the channel.
    //
    // Priority 40 — under the head's 70 because people on a failing structure
    // outrank a blocked lane, over the gallery's 30 because a lane nothing can
    // move down is what the rest of Act 3 is waiting on.
    //
    // The completion memory is the RESOLUTION COUNTER rather than one outcome
    // flag: five different endings close this row, and a crew who talked the
    // boat off the lane before the slip must see it post already green.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a1-picket",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.picket.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 40,
        directive_kind: "Secure",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name"],
    }, "havelock_enforcer_resolved");
}

// The three successful scan mirrors are the survey's evidence. Any authored
// fidelity band raises the same latched flag in `science::server`; the report
// cares that the crew read each structure, not how close the ship happened to be.
fn survey_ready(ctx) {
    ctx.flags["scan.skyhook.taken"] > 0 &&
    ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_a.taken"] > 0 &&
    ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_b.taken"] > 0
}

fn any_survey_scan(ctx) {
    ctx.flags["scan.skyhook.taken"] > 0 ||
    ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_a.taken"] > 0 ||
    ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_b.taken"] > 0
}

// The trigger predicate grammar deliberately keeps names simple and therefore
// cannot name dotted scan flags directly. Mirror the exact conjunction into one
// scenario flag whenever any constituent arrives; `survey_ready` remains the
// authoritative predicate and the report pickup defensively re-reads it.
fn on_survey_scan(ctx) {
    // Resolve any visible scan steps that have posted. Before the tether slip
    // these calls are harmless; posting later sees the same flags and skips the
    // already-done steps, preserving #1132's pre-emption contract.
    if ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_b.taken"] > 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-survey-scan-depot-b");
    }
    if ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_a.taken"] > 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-survey-scan-depot-a");
    }
    if ctx.flags["scan.skyhook.taken"] > 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-survey-scan-head");
    }
    // The first valid structure scan is the only proof the crew may cite to
    // stop Lark. If it arrives after either check-in, refresh that already-open
    // thread at its current wording and priority so the newly valid response is
    // visible immediately rather than waiting for another hail.
    if ctx.flags.lark_unsafe_response_unlocked == 0 && any_survey_scan(ctx) {
        ctx.flags.lark_unsafe_response_unlocked = 1;
        if ctx.flags.lark_corridor_cancelled == 0 {
            if ctx.flags.lark_final_hail_sent > 0 {
                ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
                    from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name",
                    node_fn: "lark_final_check",
                    thread_id: "falling-skyway-lark-safety",
                    priority: "critical",
                });
            } else if ctx.flags.lark_first_hail_sent > 0 {
                ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
                    from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name",
                    node_fn: "lark_safety_check",
                    thread_id: "falling-skyway-lark-safety",
                    priority: "routine",
                });
            }
        }
    }
    if survey_ready(ctx) {
        ctx.flags.skyway_survey_scans_complete = 1;
        post_survey_report_objective(ctx);
    }
}

fn lark_safety_check(ctx) {
    let responses = [];
    if any_survey_scan(ctx) {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lark_unsafe_response",
            on_pick: "on_lark_unsafe_response",
            important: true,
        });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lark_safety_check", responses: responses }
}

fn lark_final_check(ctx) {
    let node = lark_safety_check(ctx);
    node.message = "world.falling_skyway.comms.lark_final_check";
    node
}

fn lark_holding(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lark_holding", responses: [] }
}

fn lark_collision_report(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lark_collision_report", responses: [] }
}

fn on_lark_first_hail(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.lark_corridor_cancelled > 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.lark_first_hail_sent = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name",
        node_fn: "lark_safety_check",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-lark-safety",
        priority: "routine",
    });
}

fn on_lark_final_hail(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.lark_corridor_cancelled > 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.lark_final_hail_sent = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name",
        node_fn: "lark_final_check",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-lark-safety",
        priority: "critical",
    });
}

fn on_lark_unsafe_response(ctx) {
    // The response was rendered from scan state, but re-read it at the
    // authoritative admitted pickup too. A stale or fabricated submission can
    // never stop the collision.
    if !any_survey_scan(ctx) { return lark_safety_check(ctx); }
    if ctx.flags.lark_corridor_collision_committed > 0 {
        return lark_collision_report(ctx);
    }
    if ctx.flags.lark_corridor_cancelled == 0 {
        ctx.flags.lark_corridor_cancelled = 1;
        if ctx.deadlines.state("lark_collision_due") == "pending" {
            ctx.deadlines.cancel("lark_collision_due");
        }
    }
    lark_holding(ctx)
}

fn on_lark_collision(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.lark_corridor_cancelled > 0 || ctx.flags.lark_corridor_collision_committed > 0 {
        return;
    }
    // Commitment, physical consequence and defeat share the t=380 handler.
    // A late response sees the commitment flag and cannot reverse any of them.
    ctx.flags.lark_corridor_collision_committed = 1;
    ctx.flags.lark_corridor_collision = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name",
        node_fn: "lark_collision_report",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-lark-safety",
        priority: "critical",
    });
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name");
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name");

    // The report a catastrophe still owes (issue #1351, AC5). This ending fires
    // in Act 1/2, long before `write_the_campaign_record` — so left as it was it
    // would reach `game_over` carrying NO rows, and `classify()` would leave it
    // a bare `defeat` with the reasoning thrown away. A catastrophic ending is a
    // REPORTED ending: it still has an account to give of what it cost.
    //
    // Freeze the two facts the collision has just settled — the head is gone and
    // Lark is wreckage in the throat — then write the rows that are knowable at
    // this beat off the frozen flags, using the SAME helpers the clean close
    // does so there is no second copy of the scoring. The destroys above route
    // their own `on_head_lost` / `on_lark_traffic_lost` a tick from now, but a
    // buffered destroy has not run yet, so set the flags the rows read here.
    ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_lost = 1;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_lark == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_lark = 1;
        ctx.flags.increment("a2_traffic_lost", 1);
    }
    survey_report_row(ctx);
    traffic_report_row(ctx);
    skyhook_report_row(ctx);
    ctx.effects.game_over("world.falling_skyway.game_over.lark_collision", "defeat");
}

// Control is an ordinary hailable target. A partial survey can ask, but cannot
// manufacture the report response: the response is built from the live flag
// store each time the crew hail.
fn on_control_survey_hailed(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: "control_survey",
    });
}

fn control_survey(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_survey_reported > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.survey_received", responses: [] };
    }
    if survey_ready(ctx) {
        return #{
            message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.survey_ready",
            responses: [#{
                text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.file_survey",
                on_pick: "on_file_survey",
                important: true,
            }],
        };
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.survey_incomplete", responses: [] }
}

fn on_file_survey(ctx) {
    // Defensive re-read at the authoritative pickup. Scan flags latch, so the
    // normal route cannot regress between rendering and admission, but no stale
    // or hand-built response may file a partial survey either.
    if !survey_ready(ctx) { return control_survey(ctx); }
    ctx.flags.skyway_survey_reported = 1;
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-survey-report");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-survey");
    control_survey(ctx)
}

fn survey_unfiled(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.survey_unfiled", responses: [] }
}

// The survey scoring deadline. A filed survey stays green. Anything else fails
// loudly and records exactly which pieces were missing when the clock landed,
// so the later evidence thread can distinguish silence from a partial attempt.
fn on_survey_due(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_survey_reported == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_survey_unfiled = 1;
        ctx.flags.skyway_survey_missing_report = 1;
        if ctx.flags["scan.skyhook.taken"] == 0 {
            ctx.flags.skyway_survey_missing_skyhook = 1;
            ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-survey-scan-head");
        }
        if ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_a.taken"] == 0 {
            ctx.flags.skyway_survey_missing_depot_a = 1;
            ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-survey-scan-depot-a");
        }
        if ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_b.taken"] == 0 {
            ctx.flags.skyway_survey_missing_depot_b = 1;
            ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-survey-scan-depot-b");
        }
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-survey-report");
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-survey");
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
            node_fn: "survey_unfiled",
            urgent: true,
        });
    }
    if ctx.flags.a1_lane_open == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-corridor");
    }
    if ctx.flags.a1_priority_set == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a1-triage");
    }
    ctx.flags.act1_complete = 1;
    ctx.flags.act = 2;

    // Narrative era counter only. The dispute posted at the tether slip and was
    // hailable before it; nothing is unlocked, closed or re-posted here.
}

// ═══ THE DISPUTE ERA: TWO WAYS THE STRIKE ENDS (#1036/#1133) ════════════════
//
// Both endings are authored whole, both are playable, and both end at the SAME
// lever — `skyway_strike_settled`, which #1035's handler above turns into a
// working rung. What separates them is everything they write on the way there:
// a ledger of promises and a channel that stays open, or two relationship flags,
// a failed objective and people in a sick bay.
//
// ── What the tree branches on ───────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Nothing here is a fixed script. Every node is a function that reads the world
// before it decides what the captain may say:
//
//   the commitments ledger    `ctx.commitments.state(id)` — an option disappears
//                             once the promise behind it is on the books, and
//                             the settlement option appears only when the
//                             committee have enough to take to the floor.
//   the crew's own file       `ctx.dossier.holds(#{ text: … })` — the line about
//                             the maintenance record EXISTS only if the crew
//                             went and got the record. This reads the evidence
//                             log itself rather than a flag set beside the
//                             append, so any route that files the same finding
//                             — including the ones #1038/#1039 have not written
//                             yet — opens the same line.
//   world flags               the force-open latch, and the workers' mirrored
//                             disposition, which is what the casualty risk is
//                             measured against.
//
// ── PATH A: the negotiation ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The committee want two things and, while the dispute is soft, will settle for
// two pieces of ground out of three: promise the corridor is clear in the final
// transfer window, promise the scan discrepancy and corroborating worker account
// go to Control unedited, or show them you have already read the file. Once either
// hardening timer lands they require all three, but every promise, evidence line,
// stall and force option remains available.
//
// The promises stay OPEN in the ledger. Keeping them is the transfer window's
// business (#1042) and the report to Control's (#1039); this beat is where they
// are given.

// One admitted response on either channel is meaningful engagement. Hailing by
// itself is not: an unanswered call must not freeze the dispute in its soft state.
fn engage_strike(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_strike_engaged == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_strike_engaged = 1;
    }
}

fn on_committee_hailed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_committee_channel_opened = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
        node_fn: "committee_hails",
    });
}

fn on_havelock_hailed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_havelock_channel_opened = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
        node_fn: "havelock_hails",
    });
}

// Two authored mission-clock rungs. They are idempotent and stop at the first
// admitted response, not at the first hail. Each rung lowers the workforce's
// live disposition and narrates the change, but neither mutates a response list.
fn harden_strike(ctx, stage) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_strike_engaged > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_strike_hardening >= stage { return; }
    ctx.flags.skyway_strike_hardening = stage;
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", committee_mood(ctx));
    if stage == 1 {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            node_fn: "committee_hardens_one",
            urgent: true,
        });
    } else {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            node_fn: "committee_hardens_two",
            urgent: true,
        });
    }
}

fn committee_hardens_one(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_hardens_one", responses: [] }
}

fn committee_hardens_two(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_hardens_two", responses: [] }
}

fn committee_hails(ctx) {
    // Answered after the picket was cleared over their heads: there is nothing
    // to negotiate and the tree says so rather than silently offering options
    // that no longer mean anything.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 {
        return #{
            message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_no_longer_talking",
            responses: [],
        };
    }
    #{
        message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_hails",
        responses: [
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.listen", on_pick: "on_committee_listen" },
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.dismiss", on_pick: "on_committee_dismiss" },
        ],
    }
}

// What the workers make of the crew, derived in ONE place from what the crew
// have actually done, so two beats cannot disagree about it. Hardening costs ten
// points per timer before promises and evidence are applied. Absolute rather
// than incremental for that reason: `set_workforce_disposition` writes a value,
// and a value computed from the record cannot drift the way a running total of
// `+10`s can.
fn committee_mood(ctx) {
    let mood = 25 - (10 * ctx.flags.skyway_strike_hardening);
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") != "unknown" { mood += 10; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") != "unknown" { mood += 10; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_file_shown > 0 { mood += 15; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_stonewalled > 0 { mood -= 10; }
    mood
}

fn on_committee_listen(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_negotiation_opened", 1);
    committee_terms(ctx)
}

// Talking down to them costs ten points, and those ten points are not
// decoration: they are what the casualty arithmetic on the other path reads.
fn on_committee_dismiss(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_stonewalled", 1);
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", committee_mood(ctx));
    committee_hails(ctx)
}

fn committee_terms(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 {
        return #{
            message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_no_longer_talking",
            responses: [],
        };
    }
    // Read after write inside one call: a promise made by the `on_pick` that
    // called this node is already on the books for it, which is why the option
    // that made it has gone by the time the follow-up node is shown.
    let promised_passage = ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") != "unknown";
    let promised_records = ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") != "unknown";
    let showed_the_file = ctx.flags.skyway_file_shown > 0;

    let ground = 0;
    if promised_passage { ground += 1; }
    if promised_records { ground += 1; }
    if showed_the_file { ground += 1; }

    let responses = [];
    if !promised_passage {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.promise_passage",
            on_pick: "on_promise_passage",
            important: true,
        });
    }
    if !promised_records {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.promise_records",
            on_pick: "on_promise_records",
            important: true,
        });
    }
    // THE EVIDENCE BRANCH. `holds` reads the run's evidence log — what is on the
    // crew's fact sheet — and not a flag mirroring it, so the line appears for
    // any route that filed the finding.
    if !showed_the_file &&
       ctx.dossier.holds(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file" }) {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.show_file",
            on_pick: "on_show_file",
        });
    }
    let vote_ground = 2;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_strike_hardening > 0 { vote_ground = 3; }
    if ground >= vote_ground {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.call_the_vote",
            on_pick: "on_settle",
            important: true,
        });
    }
    // Always last, and never terminal: a captain who needs to go and do
    // something else keeps the channel.
    responses.push(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.stall", on_pick: "on_stall" });

    let body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_terms";
    if ctx.flags.skyway_strike_hardening > 0 {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_terms_hardened";
    }
    if ground >= vote_ground { body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_ready"; }
    #{ message: body, responses: responses }
}

fn on_promise_passage(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    // A passive incoming channel and a crew/Backfill hail can coexist. Both use
    // the same admitted response path, so the authoritative state change — not
    // the actor — makes a repeated pick idempotent.
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") == "unknown" {
        ctx.commitments.record(#{
            id: "skyway_safe_passage",
            made_to: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            terms: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.safe_passage.terms",
            resolves_when: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.safe_passage.resolves",
        });
    }
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", committee_mood(ctx));
    committee_terms(ctx)
}

fn on_promise_records(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") == "unknown" {
        ctx.commitments.record(#{
            id: "skyway_surface_records",
            made_to: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            terms: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.surface_records.terms",
            resolves_when: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.surface_records.resolves",
        });
    }
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", committee_mood(ctx));
    committee_terms(ctx)
}

// The line the crew earned by getting the file. It records nothing on the
// ledger — the captain is not promising anything, they are showing their work —
// and it is worth more than either promise, because it is the only thing in this
// conversation the workers can check.
fn on_show_file(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    ctx.flags.skyway_file_shown = 1;
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", committee_mood(ctx));
    committee_terms(ctx)
}

fn on_stall(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    committee_hails(ctx)
}

// The settlement. It does not end the strike on this tick: the committee put it
// to the floor, and twenty seconds later the rung starts moving. The delay is
// the whole difference in PACE between the two endings — the operator clears a
// picket in six.
fn on_settle(ctx) {
    // Rendering the vote response is not authority. Force, physical settlement
    // or mission finalisation may have landed while the response remained in
    // the inbox, and none of those may be rewritten by a stale pick.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_settles", responses: [] };
    }
    engage_strike(ctx);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation = 1;
        ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", 60);
        ctx.schedule.after(20, |ctx| {
            // The vote is provisional throughout the stand-down. A force order
            // admitted before this callback clears that provisional flag and
            // owns the only remaining settlement callback.
            if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 ||
               ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled > 0 ||
               ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 ||
               ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation == 0 { return; }
            ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled = 1;
        });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_settles", responses: [] }
}

// ── PATH B: the operator clears it ──────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Faster, reachable without saying a word to the workers, and it costs three
// things the negotiation does not: people, a relationship two campaign flags
// carry forward, and the corroboration route.
//
// THE CASUALTY RISK IS RESOLVED FROM STATE, not from a die this engine does not
// give a script. It is read off the workers' mirrored disposition AT THE MOMENT
// THE ORDER IS GIVEN — how dug in they are is what decides how badly it goes —
// and the captain is given one lever over it: ten minutes' warning on the open
// channel costs time and takes a step off the outcome. Deterministic per seed
// by construction, and it surfaces in four places rather than in a flag: the
// cutter reports back on an open channel, the finding lands on the committee's
// fact sheet, the rung takes real condition damage, and the count is a flag a
// later mission reads.

fn havelock_hails(ctx) {
    havelock_offer(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_hails")
}

// One authoritative predicate owns whether a force response can still be
// admitted. The accepted vote is not yet the physical settlement — there is an
// authored twenty-second stand-down in which filing and force can both have
// been rendered, and admission order decides which one wins. Once evidence has
// actually been filed, the strike has physically settled, force has already
// been admitted, or the mission has frozen its ending, that route is spent.
fn force_route_closed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0
}

// The offer, under whichever opening line the caller is answering with.
fn havelock_offer(ctx, body) {
    // Nothing left to sell once the authoritative route is spent. Admission
    // repeats this gate because an already-rendered response can outlive it.
    if force_route_closed(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_stands_off", responses: [] };
    }
    let responses = [];
    // Two checks, and both are needed: `holds` reads the log as it stood when
    // this CALL started, so the flag is what hides the option from the very
    // follow-up node the request returns, and the log is what keeps it hidden
    // once any other route has filed the same finding.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_file_requested == 0 &&
       !ctx.dossier.holds(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file" }) {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.ask_for_file",
            on_pick: "on_request_file",
        });
    }
    // ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, for a reason nothing else in this file has to
    // care about. The destroyer merges `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`, whose
    // Comms policy answers an open thread with its FIRST response while Comms is
    // available and the sender is in range — so on a hull whose Tactical seat is
    // AI-backfilled rather than held by a person, index 0 is what the ship does
    // when nobody is listening. Refusing has to be that answer: an officer who
    // authorised a boarding party because it happened to be listed first would
    // be the loudest possible authoring accident.
    //
    // [ai] The real fix is the console-complexity ladder's human-seeking comms —
    // a system that WANTS a person and says so, instead of a scenario ordering
    // its buttons around a backfill policy. Until then this order is the
    // scenario's own safety catch, and it is the scenario's to hold. Player-ship
    // overrides now compose onto the lobby-selected hull, but switching Comms
    // Backfill off here would also strand every other opening thread on an empty
    // bridge; response order is the narrow per-decision guard this scene needs.
    responses.push(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.refuse_force",
        on_pick: "on_refuse_force",
    });
    responses.push(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.force_warned",
        on_pick: "on_force_warned",
        important: true,
    });
    responses.push(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.force_now",
        on_pick: "on_force_now",
        important: true,
    });
    #{ message: body, responses: responses }
}

// The operator hands over the file that makes the workers trust the crew, which
// is the joke this scenario is built on. `records` provenance: it is a document
// comparison, not a scan and not somebody's word.
fn on_request_file(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file",
        provenance: "records",
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_file_requested", 1);
    havelock_offer(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_sends_file")
}

// Declining does not delete the option — the operator is still sitting on the
// depot with a costed problem. They ask once more, thirty seconds later, and
// only once, so a crew who keep saying no are not nagged for the whole mission.
fn on_refuse_force(ctx) {
    engage_strike(ctx);
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_force_declined", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_force_declined == 1 {
        ctx.schedule.after(30, |ctx| {
            ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
                from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
                node_fn: "havelock_hails",
            });
        });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_stands_off", responses: [] }
}

fn on_force_now(ctx)    { force_the_picket(ctx, false) }
fn on_force_warned(ctx) { force_the_picket(ctx, true) }

fn force_the_picket(ctx, warned) {
    // Re-read the route before ANY mutation. Rendering is not authority: a
    // filing, physical settlement or mission close can all land while an old
    // Havelock response is still visible in the inbox.
    if force_route_closed(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.force_route_closed", responses: [] };
    }
    engage_strike(ctx);
    // READ THE GROUND BEFORE MOVING IT. Everything below drives the workers'
    // disposition to the floor, so the risk has to be measured first — it is
    // what the situation was when the order was given, not what the order made
    // of it. [ai] Thresholds unratified.
    //
    // A crew who negotiated their way up to trust and THEN authorised this get
    // the lowest count, and that is not a reward: the people on that rung were
    // not braced, because the captain had just told them they did not need to
    // be.
    let mood = ctx.flags["workforce.skyway_workers.disposition"];
    let hurt = 1;
    if mood <= 40 { hurt = 2; }
    if mood <= 20 { hurt = 3; }
    if mood <= 10 { hurt = 4; }
    if warned && hurt > 0 { hurt -= 1; }

    // Force admitted during the vote's stand-down wins that admission race.
    // Clear the provisional negotiation before scheduling Havelock's outcome,
    // so the vote callback cannot settle first and the campaign cannot inherit
    // a negotiated+forced hybrid.
    ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation = 0;
    ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_force_casualties = hurt;
    // The campaign flags. `skyway_worker_corroboration_closed` is the route
    // this shuts; the two relationship flags are what a later mission reads to
    // know who the crew are, and they are written as a PAIR because forcing a
    // picket open does not only lose you the workers.
    ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_closed = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_open = 0;
    ctx.flags["relationship.skyway_workers.damaged"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["relationship.havelock_operations.favoured"] = 1;

    // A promise overrun is a promise broken, and the ledger says so in the
    // captain's own record rather than in the narration. Guarded on `open` so
    // a second force-open cannot re-break a settled promise.
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") == "open" {
        ctx.commitments.break_promise("skyway_safe_passage");
    }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") == "open" {
        ctx.commitments.break_promise("skyway_surface_records");
    }

    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", 5);
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("havelock_operations", 70);

    // THE CLOSURE, MADE LEGIBLE. The objective goes red on the list, and the
    // workers say why on the channel they will not answer again.
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-corroborate");
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
        node_fn: "committee_signs_off",
        urgent: true,
    });

    // Ten minutes on the open channel, or now. Both are faster than a vote.
    if warned {
        ctx.schedule.after(12, |ctx| { picket_cleared(ctx); });
    } else {
        ctx.schedule.after(6, |ctx| { picket_cleared(ctx); });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_acknowledges", responses: [] }
}

fn committee_signs_off(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_signs_off", responses: [] }
}

// What it cost, on screen. The count was decided when the order was given and
// banked on a flag, so this handler only reports it — which is also what makes
// it survive a save between the order and the outcome.
fn picket_cleared(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open == 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled > 0 ||
       ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return; }
    let hurt = ctx.flags.skyway_force_casualties;
    // The same lever the negotiation pulls: the rung is working again.
    ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled = 1;

    if hurt > 0 {
        // The rung does not come out of it clean either. Four points a casualty
        // is a real move on a condition track the crew's panels are already
        // showing, which is the difference between a consequence and a sentence
        // about one.
        ctx.effects.damage_infrastructure("world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name", 4 * hurt);
        ctx.dossier.append(#{
            subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.picket_cleared_hurt",
            provenance: "dialogue",
        });
    }

    if hurt >= 2 {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
            node_fn: "force_report_hurt",
            urgent: true,
        });
    } else if hurt == 1 {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
            node_fn: "force_report_one",
            urgent: true,
        });
    } else {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
            node_fn: "force_report_clean",
            urgent: true,
        });
    }
}

fn force_report_clean(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.force_report_clean", responses: [] }
}

fn force_report_one(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.force_report_one", responses: [] }
}

fn force_report_hurt(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.force_report_hurt", responses: [] }
}

// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ACT 2 — the radiation storm and the rescue (issue #1037)
// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//
// The act's data — the band anchors, the shelter route, the Lyra and the six
// deadlines — is authored above this script. What is here is only the wiring
// that turns a clock into a storm.

on_deadline("storm_front_due", "on_storm_front");
on_deadline("storm_band_one_due", "on_storm_band_one");
on_deadline("storm_band_two_due", "on_storm_band_two");
on_deadline("storm_band_three_due", "on_storm_band_three");
on_deadline("lyra_clear_due", "on_lyra_clear_due");
on_deadline("storm_passed_due", "on_storm_passed");
on_flag_set("scan.lyra_ascending.taken", "on_lyra_scanned");

// THE RESCUE'S COMPLETION SIGNAL. The tractor's arrest-decline (issue #1158)
// recovers the towed craft's condition while the beam holds, and the Lyra
// authors a threshold that recovery is sized to cross. There is no "operation
// completed" trigger, and this is the honest substitute: what the work leaves
// behind is its payoff, so a scenario reads the payoff — unchanged from the old
// operation's lump payout it replaces.
on_flag_set("skyway_lyra_under_control", "on_lyra_recovered");

// The consequence, chained off the removal rather than written beside it. A
// scripted destruction chains exactly as a kill does, so whatever takes her —
// this act's own deadline today, something else tomorrow — lands here.
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name", "on_lyra_lost");

// Every craft on a lane. Identity is retained through a thin wrapper so a loss
// is a named ledger fact and an immediate call, not an aggregate discovered at
// the end of the act. Wick remains the canary outside the storm corridor.
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name", "on_meridian_traffic_lost");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name", "on_lark_traffic_lost");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_pell.name", "on_pell_traffic_lost");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.shuttle_wick.name", "on_wick_traffic_lost");

// The forecast. Everything the crew get to plan with arrives in one beat, 180
// seconds before the first band: what is coming, who is in the way, and the
// shelter route Navigation can order each endangered craft onto.
fn on_storm_front(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a2-shelter",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.shelter.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 50,
    });
    // The mandatory row above records the outcome. These three optional rows
    // carry the concrete Navigation work, one target and route per order. A
    // human gets three named instructions; Backfill consumes the same payloads
    // in scored order and emits the same OrderCivilian command.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a2-shelter-meridian",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.shelter_meridian.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 49,
        directive_kind: "Order",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
        route: "storm_shelter_run",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name"],
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a2-shelter-lark",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.shelter_lark.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 49,
        directive_kind: "Order",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name",
        route: "storm_shelter_run",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name"],
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a2-shelter-pell",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.shelter_pell.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 49,
        directive_kind: "Order",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_pell.name",
        route: "storm_shelter_run",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_pell.name"],
    });
    // A craft can be lost before the forecast reaches this handler (combat,
    // collision, or another authored consequence). Its destruction handler has
    // already written the durable named flag, so project that remembered loss
    // onto the objective as soon as the late-posting row exists. Otherwise the
    // row would advertise impossible work against a craft that is already gone.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_meridian > 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-shelter-meridian");
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_lark > 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-shelter-lark");
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_pell > 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-shelter-pell");
    }
    // TWO OPERATIONAL OBJECTIVES FOR ONE RESCUE, and the split is forced by
    // what a Reach directive MEANS: `detect_reached_objective_completion`
    // completes any objective whose Reach anchor an AI-flown helm arrives at.
    // An objective carrying the approach therefore cannot also be the one that
    // records the tow — it would complete the moment the ship got there,
    // whether or not anybody ever put a line on her. Science's optional scan
    // beside them observes the rescue without deciding it.
    //
    // The approach, then, carries the Helm directive, while the rescue carries
    // the Engineering-owned Tow directive below. Both consume the SAME
    // threshold-backed memory: Lyra is actionable from the opening tick, so a
    // crew who got a line on her before Control's forecast must not be handed
    // two newly-active objectives for work the world already records as done.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a2-approach",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.approach.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 70,
        directive_kind: "Reach",
        directive_anchor: "lyra_drift",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name"],
    }, "skyway_lyra_recovered");
    // Science gets its own observable rescue step. It is optional because the
    // tow, not the reading, decides whether Lyra lives; nevertheless it carries
    // the same Scan directive a human Sensors console uses. The Reach objective
    // brings the hull into range, Sensors retries through ordinary admission,
    // and the shared scan applier raises the authored `scan.<id>.taken` memory.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a2-rescue-scan",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.rescue_scan.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 71,
        directive_kind: "Scan",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name"],
    }, "scan.lyra_ascending.taken");
    // The rescue still resolves only from what the crew DID — the tow's own
    // threshold crossing, or the deadline — but the directive makes that work
    // addressable by the same Engineering Backfill host a human shares.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a2-rescue",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.rescue.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 70,
        directive_kind: "Tow",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name"],
    }, "skyway_lyra_recovered");
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a2-storm",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.storm.text",
        mandatory: true,
    });

    ctx.flags.increment("a2_front_warned", 1);
}

// The three bands. Each one spawns at its own anchor and SCHEDULES ITS OWN
// RETIREMENT forty seconds out — the deferred `destroy_entity` #1033 proved.
// The dwell is a property of the band, and a band that spawned without one
// would be a wall. Falling Skyway overrides the template sphere with a narrow,
// corridor-long box: the front physically takes traffic left on the lane while
// the shelter and ladder routes remain laterally clear.
//
// #1142's fixed Backfill sweep completed the mandatory spine in all 20 seeds at
// the shared template's 5 damage/s. The scenario-specific 11.85 damage/s keeps the
// same authored fronts, pierce, movement tax and forty-second dwell, but turns
// their existing SEEDED region-damage distribution into material system
// pressure: most distributions preserve enough propulsion to cross, while a few
// knock it out before the final band clears and trap the destroyer in the hazard
// until hull loss. This is the permitted hardening after AI-first improvements
// made failure impossible; no new randomness or later deadline is introduced.
// Keep the one helper as the single tuning site.
fn storm_band_overrides() {
    #{
        shape: #{ type: "box", half_extents: [flt("260"), flt("260"), flt("1100")] },
        effects: #{ damage_zone: #{ damage_per_second: flt("11.85") } },
    }
}

fn on_storm_band_one(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/region_radiation_band.toml",
        name: "storm_band_one",
        anchor: "storm_band_north",
        groups: ["storm_bands"],
        overrides: storm_band_overrides(),
    });
    ctx.schedule.in_seconds(40).destroy_entity("storm_band_one");
    ctx.flags.increment("a2_band_one", 1);
}

// A returned reading, never objective bookkeeping, is the rescue scan's
// authority. The flag is latched by science::server at the same site that
// produces a human scan result; completing a step here cannot fabricate it.
fn on_lyra_scanned(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-rescue-scan");
}

// The rescue landed. The flag rose because the tractor's recovery carried her
// condition track over its authored line, which is the only thing a held tow
// leaves behind.
fn on_lyra_recovered(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-rescue");
    // Campaign state. One of this and `skyway_lyra_lost` is ALWAYS written, so
    // a later act reads a fact rather than an absence.
    ctx.flags.skyway_lyra_recovered = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a2_lyra_recovered", 1);
    // The story's own record of her fate (issue #1338). Authored rather than
    // inferred, and it also settles the case where a later act removes her hull
    // for tidiness: a marked entity that already has an outcome never has a
    // death invented for it.
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome("world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name", "rescued");
    // SAVING LYRA IS GETTING HER CREW OFF, NOT SAVING HER HULL (John's model, T2
    // refinement). The rescue is complete the moment the crew are recovered, so
    // she WARPS OUT — the same authored `destroy_entity` the loss branch and the
    // epilogue craft use, on the ordinary scripted-removal path, deterministic to
    // the tick her recovery threshold crosses. Because `narrative_outcome`
    // ("rescued") was recorded above (this tick, either order), the removal is
    // read as a warp-out and NOT as a `marked_entity_destroyed`: it is a rescue,
    // not a death. This fixes the t614 contradiction by construction — once she
    // is saved she is gone from the world and can never be "destroyed later" with
    // a stale saved row still standing.
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name");
    // The post-mission report row (issue #1344, re-framed for the T2 refinement).
    // With her crew off she is a CREW-RESCUED outcome — the empty hull warping out
    // is not the verdict, the people are. +6, deliberately felt beside the other
    // rows but not the whole verdict. The hull-with-crew loss (-6) is written by
    // the deadline branch, when she is destroyed with her crew still aboard.
    lyra_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.lyra.crew_saved", "saved", 6);
}

// Both fates write the SAME row id, so whichever happens updates one row in
// place. Two ids would let a run that recovered her and then lost her hull
// report her twice, in two moods, which is exactly the report lying about what
// the crew did.
fn lyra_report_row(ctx, outcome_id, state, score) {
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "lyra",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.lyra.heading",
        outcome: outcome_id,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// The rescue's clock. If she is not under control by now the second band has
// her, and the act says so out loud: the objective fails and the removal
// chains its own consequence.
fn on_lyra_clear_due(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.a2_lyra_recovered == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-rescue");
        // The report row lands HERE and not in `on_lyra_lost`, because this is
        // the tick her fate is decided. `on_lyra_lost` chains off the removal,
        // and a removal that the collision ending or a later act performs for
        // its own reasons must not be able to write a loss row for a hauler the
        // crew had already pulled clear.
        lyra_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.lyra.lost", "lost", -6);
        // The destroy stays the physical fact and the timeline's death beat: the
        // band really did take her, so `marked_entity_destroyed` is the honest
        // outcome and no authored one is recorded to suppress it.
        ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.lyra_ascending.name");
    }
    // The approach beat closes with the window it belonged to. Completed rather
    // than judged: whether the crew got there is not what this act is scoring —
    // the rescue objective beside it is the one that records what they achieved,
    // and an approach left Active for the rest of the mission would be a line on
    // the panel nobody can ever act on.
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-approach");
    // Whatever happened, the crew's own job changes here: the work in the
    // corridor is over and what is left is getting out of the sweep. Posted
    // above the approach's priority so a backfilled helm leaves rather than
    // holding station in a radiation band for another two minutes.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a2-lee",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.lee.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 75,
        directive_kind: "Reach",
        directive_anchor: "storm_lee",
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("a2_rescue_resolved", 1);
}

// Chained off her removal. Guarded on the recovery counter because a craft that
// was pulled clear and came to grief later is not this act's failure — the
// record says what the crew did, not what became of her afterwards.
fn on_lyra_lost(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.a2_lyra_recovered == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_lyra_lost = 1;
        ctx.flags.increment("a2_lyra_lost", 1);
        // The on-screen consequence. Somebody has to tell Control, and it is a
        // MANDATORY objective rather than a line of text so it sits on the
        // panel until the crew have dealt with it.
        ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
            id: "obj-a2-loss-report",
            text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.loss_report.text",
            mandatory: true,
            targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name"],
        });
    }
}

fn record_traffic_loss(ctx, ledger_flag, order_objective, subject, evidence, node_fn) {
    if ctx.flags[ledger_flag] > 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags[ledger_flag] = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a2_traffic_lost", 1);
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-shelter");
    if order_objective != "" { ctx.effects.fail_objective(order_objective); }
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject: subject,
        text: evidence,
        provenance: "scan",
    });
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: node_fn,
        urgent: true,
    });
    if ctx.flags.a2_traffic_lost == 1 {
        ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
            id: "obj-a2-traffic-loss-report",
            text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.traffic_loss_report.text",
            mandatory: true,
            targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name"],
        });
    }
}

// The corridor clears. Marshal surviving traffic back onto its working route;
// this post-sweep reset does not replace Navigation's pre-band shelter orders.
fn on_storm_passed(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name", "skyway_lane");
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name", "skyway_lane");
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_pell.name", "skyway_lane");

    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-storm");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-lee");
    // Completion is per surviving craft. A named loss is durable and must not
    // be painted green merely because the weather later clears.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_meridian == 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-shelter-meridian");
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_lark == 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-shelter-lark");
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_pell == 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-shelter-pell");
    }
    if ctx.flags.a2_traffic_lost == 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-shelter");
    } else {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-shelter");
    }

    ctx.flags.skyway_storm_passed = 1;
    ctx.flags.act2_complete = 1;
    ctx.flags.act = 3;
}
