// ═══ THE SCAN-VERSUS-DOSSIER DIFF (issue #1038) ══════════════════════════════
//
// The Thin Margin arc opens here, and it opens on a contradiction the crew have
// to go and find. It runs alongside Act 1 rather than after it: the rung's file
// is in the crew's hands from the moment they arrive, the rung is scannable from
// the moment they are in range, and nothing in this block waits for an act.
//
// ── The two documents ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// WHAT THE PAPERWORK SAYS is filed below as two BRIEFING entries on Ladder B's
// own dossier — inspected and signed off at the certified load standard,
// transfer arm reinforced and re-rated. They read on the tactical dossier panel
// beside everything else the crew know about the rung, under the provenance that
// says where they came from: somebody handed these to us.
//
// WHAT THE RUNG IS is `depot_b_meets_certified_load`, the threshold authored on
// the depot itself against 0.6 of its ceiling. #1025 mirrors it off the live
// condition track every tick; at an authored 34 points it is down, and a science
// scan (#1032) reads the same published snapshot back at whatever fidelity the
// crew's range and power bought them.
//
// The crew are therefore holding two documents that disagree, and the panel
// shows both. All this block does is notice.
//
// ── Why this is not a scripted reveal ───────────────────────────────────────
//
// `read_the_file_against_the_rung` asks two questions and holds neither answer
// itself. It does not know what the scan SAID; it does not know what the record
// CLAIMS beyond the flag's name. Three consequences, and each one is a thing a
// scripted reveal could not do:
//
//   * Re-author the depot's `condition` above the recorded standard and the
//     flag comes up, the second guard returns, and there is nothing to find —
//     with no line of copy edited, and no handler touched.
//   * A crew who never scan Ladder B never file anything, whatever else they do
//     and however long the mission runs. `probe_scandiff.toml` runs that case as
//     its own rung.
//   * The beat is reachable from EITHER side. `on_flag_set` on the scan is the
//     ordinary route — the crew look at a rung that is already wrong. The
//     `on_flag_cleared` registration is the other one: a crew who read the rung
//     while it still held up, and watched it stop holding up afterwards. Same
//     function, same two questions, no ordering baked in.
//
// ── What it is worth ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The finding is `…evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file` under RECORDS provenance
// — deliberately the SAME entry the operator hands over on Havelock's channel in
// Act 2, because it is the same fact learned two ways, and #1031's store makes
// the second one a silent no-op. So this route feeds the negotiation's evidence
// branch (#1036 reads the log itself rather than a flag, precisely so that any
// route reaching the finding opens the line), and a crew who did the survey work
// settle the strike on one promise instead of two.
//
// Not finding it never blocks anything: both endings stay reachable empty-handed
// and the act boundary does not wait on this. It costs the captain a promise.
//
// `skyway_records_diff_found` is the campaign flag, beside
// `skyway_worker_corroboration_closed` and for its reason: a later mission wants
// to know whether THIS crew were the ones who read the file, and the evidence log
// is scenario state a debrief cannot re-derive.

on_world_loaded("file_the_ladder_b_record");
on_flag_set("scan.depot_ladder_b.taken", "on_ladder_b_read");
on_flag_cleared("depot_b_meets_certified_load", "on_ladder_b_record_fails");

// The operator's file, handed over with the mission. BRIEFING provenance: being
// told is itself a source, and a crew who cannot tell a briefing from a reading
// cannot argue with the briefing.
fn file_the_ladder_b_record(ctx) {
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_record_inspection",
        provenance: "briefing",
    });
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_record_reinforced",
        provenance: "briefing",
    });
}

fn on_ladder_b_read(ctx)         { read_the_file_against_the_rung(ctx) }
fn on_ladder_b_record_fails(ctx) { read_the_file_against_the_rung(ctx) }

// The comparison. Two reads of the world, in either order, and no memory of its
// own — see the block comment above for why that is the whole slice.
fn read_the_file_against_the_rung(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags["scan.depot_ladder_b.taken"] == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.depot_b_meets_certified_load > 0 { return; }

    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file",
        provenance: "records",
    });
    ctx.flags.skyway_records_diff_found = 1;
}

// ═══ THE WORKER WHO WAS ON THE RUNG (issue #1039) ════════════════════════════
//
// #1038 proves a DISCREPANCY: a rung that cannot carry what its own file says it
// was signed off to carry. It does not prove INTENT, and it cannot — an
// instrument reading has nothing to say about who knew. This block is the other
// half of the same case, and it arrives the only way that half ever could:
// somebody who was there says what actually happened.
//
// The finding #1038 files reads "every inspection signed off, none of them by
// anyone who was on the rung that day". Tacket was on the rung that day. That is
// the whole beat, and the copy was written to hand it over a slice early.
//
// ── The two gates, and why each one is the gate it is ───────────────────────
//
// NEITHER is a difficulty knob. Each is a thing the crew did, and each closes a
// different half of the scene:
//
//   THE STRIKE WAS SETTLED BY NEGOTIATION.  `skyway_settled_by_negotiation`, set
//   by #1036's `on_settle` and by nothing else. A crew who had corporate
//   security clear the line over these people's heads do not get one of them on
//   the record afterwards, and that is not a punishment — it is the only thing
//   that could happen. #1036 already writes the closure down where the crew can
//   see it (`obj-a2-corroborate` goes red, the committee say why on the channel
//   they will not answer again, `skyway_worker_corroboration_closed` carries it
//   into the campaign), so this slice deliberately adds NO second announcement:
//   the route it would announce is one the crew were already told they had lost.
//
//   THE CREW READ THE RUNG.  A conversation needs a subject, and the subject is
//   specifically the discrepancy this crew established by scanning Ladder B.
//   Havelock will hand over the same maintenance file on request, but possession
//   is not comparison: only `skyway_records_diff_found`, written by the real scan
//   path above, proves the crew read the file against the structure.
//
// ── Either order, and no memory of its own ──────────────────────────────────
//
// Registered from both sides, exactly as #1038's comparison is: the settlement
// can carry before or after the file lands, and a crew who scan the rung in Act
// 3 reach the same call as a crew who scanned it in Act 1. The single-shot is a
// flag on the OPEN rather than on a trigger, so neither road can double-hail.
on_flag_set("skyway_settled_by_negotiation", "on_the_floor_carries_it");
on_flag_set("skyway_records_diff_found", "on_the_diff_lands");

// The account opens the crew's filing route. It does not itself finish the
// objective: Control must receive both halves through an admitted response on
// its own, range-gated channel.
on_flag_set("skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained", "on_corroboration_obtained");

fn on_the_floor_carries_it(ctx) { call_the_rigger_if_both_halves_hold(ctx) }
fn on_the_diff_lands(ctx)       { call_the_rigger_if_both_halves_hold(ctx) }

fn call_the_rigger_if_both_halves_hold(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_rigger_called > 0 { return; }
    // Belt and braces. `on_settle` is unreachable once the picket has been
    // cleared (#1036's `committee_terms` returns an empty node) and the force is
    // unreachable once the rung is moving, so these two cannot both be true
    // today — but the gate is what this slice IS, and a later slice that finds a
    // third way to end the strike should have to come and read this.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_diff_found == 0 { return; }

    ctx.flags.skyway_rigger_called = 1;
    // From her own hull, never `_self`, for the reason #1036's two threads are:
    // the response router range-gates a pick against the sender's live range
    // flag, and somebody calling is the more honest scene than a voice.
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.rigger_tacket.name",
        node_fn: "rigger_hails",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

// ── The scene ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// INDEX 0 IS THE ASK, and that is the opposite call to the one `havelock_offer`
// makes — deliberately, and off the same underlying fact. The destroyer's
// backfilled Comms policy answers an open thread with its first response, so
// index 0 is what the ship does when nobody is holding Tactical. On Havelock's
// channel that meant index 0 had to be the REFUSAL, because a boarding party
// authorised by a seating accident is the loudest authoring accident there is.
// Here there is nothing to protect the crew from: the two gates above are the
// work, and a crew who negotiated the strike down and went and read the rung
// have earned this whether or not somebody was sitting at the console when she
// called. [ai] The console-complexity ladder's human-seeking comms is still the
// real fix for both trees.
fn rigger_hails(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return rigger_thread_closed(ctx); }
    #{
        message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_hails",
        responses: [
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_ask", on_pick: "on_rigger_ask", important: true },
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_later", on_pick: "on_rigger_later" },
        ],
    }
}

fn rigger_thread_closed(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_stands_by", responses: [] }
}

// Never terminal. A captain in the middle of a tow can put her down and pick her
// back up, and the node she comes back to has the one thing left to say on it.
fn on_rigger_later(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return rigger_thread_closed(ctx); }
    #{
        message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_stands_by",
        responses: [
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_ask", on_pick: "on_rigger_ask", important: true },
        ],
    }
}

// THE CORROBORATION. One append, under DIALOGUE provenance, onto LADDER B's
// sheet — not onto hers.
//
// A finding is filed under what it is ABOUT and not under who said it, which is
// the rule `probe_evidence.toml` was built to state; the subject is therefore
// the same rung #1038's records entry went onto, and the two sit on one panel
// under two provenances. That is the payload of this slice as a crew reads it: a
// fact sheet that says what the structure IS and who KNEW, and that can say
// which of those two it was told and which it worked out.
//
// The append comes BEFORE the flag write — see the trigger registration above.
fn on_rigger_ask(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return rigger_thread_closed(ctx); }
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_worker_account",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    });
    // Campaign state: whether THIS crew got a worker on the record. The mirror
    // of `skyway_worker_corroboration_closed`, so a later mission reads a fact
    // on both branches rather than an absence on one.
    ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained = 1;

    #{
        message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_account",
        responses: [
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_protect", on_pick: "on_rigger_protect", important: true },
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_no_promise", on_pick: "on_rigger_no_promise" },
        ],
    }
}

// She has already said it by the time she asks for this, which is the order a
// person talks in and the reason the promise cannot be a price. It goes on the
// ledger OPEN, made to her rather than to the committee: keeping it is what the
// later confrontation (#1043) has to decide, and a captain who puts her account
// to the operator has to know whose name is on it. Filing the evidence bundle
// with Control does not settle this promise; mission close reads whether the
// crew named her to Havelock.
fn on_rigger_protect(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return rigger_thread_closed(ctx); }
    ctx.commitments.record(#{
        id: "skyway_protect_witness",
        made_to: "world.falling_skyway.entity.rigger_tacket.name",
        terms: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.protect_witness.terms",
        resolves_when: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.protect_witness.resolves",
    });
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_thanks", responses: [] }
}

// Refusing costs the corroboration nothing and is not a trap. It writes a flag
// instead of a promise, because a captain who would not give her cover is a fact
// about this crew that #1043's scene should be able to read.
fn on_rigger_no_promise(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return rigger_thread_closed(ctx); }
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_witness_unprotected", 1);
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.rigger_accepts_risk", responses: [] }
}

// ── What two entries on one sheet unlock ────────────────────────────────────
//
// The rigger's account unlocks TWO things and completes NEITHER of them by
// itself. The first is a sticky Control thread: it remains in the inbox if the
// destroyer is outside Control's range, and the shared response router refuses
// the pick until the ship returns. The response then writes both source entries
// onto Control's own sheet and only that authoritative pickup raises
// `skyway_records_put` and completes `obj-a2-corroborate`.
//
// "Sticky" means range changes and travel do not retire it. The ordinary
// ClearComms command remains an intentional dismissal of the whole inbox and
// its active dialogues; this optional thread is not silently recreated after a
// crew explicitly clears it. The route state stays open until filing, force or
// mission finalisation, so an unfiled dismissal still fails visibly at close.
//
// The second is the existing confrontation lead. Confronting Havelock is a
// separate consequence and never substitutes for filing with Control.
fn on_corroboration_obtained(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_diff_found == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained == 0 { return; }
    if !ctx.dossier.holds(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file",
        provenance: "records",
    }) { return; }
    if !ctx.dossier.holds(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_worker_account",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    }) { return; }

    if ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_opened == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_opened = 1;
        ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_open = 1;
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
            node_fn: "control_evidence_filing",
            thread_id: "falling-skyway-evidence-filing",
        });
    }

    if ctx.flags.skyway_confront_unlocked == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_confront_unlocked = 1;
        ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
            id: "obj-a3-confront",
            text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.confront.text",
            mandatory: false,
            source: "mission",
            base_priority: 20,
            targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name"],
        });
    }
}

fn evidence_filing_ready(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_open > 0 &&
    ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized == 0 &&
    ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open == 0 &&
    ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation > 0 &&
    ctx.flags.skyway_records_diff_found > 0 &&
    ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained > 0 &&
    ctx.dossier.holds(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file",
        provenance: "records",
    }) &&
    ctx.dossier.holds(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_worker_account",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    })
}

fn control_evidence_filing(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.evidence_filed", responses: [] };
    }
    if !evidence_filing_ready(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.evidence_route_closed", responses: [] };
    }
    #{
        message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.evidence_ready",
        responses: [#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.file_evidence",
            on_pick: "on_file_evidence",
            important: true,
        }],
    }
}

fn on_file_evidence(ctx) {
    // Re-read every gate at admission. The thread can outlive range changes and
    // a late force order, so rendering an option is never authority to apply it.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 { return control_evidence_filing(ctx); }
    if !evidence_filing_ready(ctx) { return control_evidence_filing(ctx); }

    // Close the route before buffering any consequences. This is the one
    // authoritative transition from unresolved to filed, shared by every actor;
    // `skyway_records_put` also closes `force_route_closed` before a stale force
    // response can mutate the other branch.
    ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_open = 0;
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file",
        provenance: "records",
    });
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_worker_account",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    });
    ctx.flags.skyway_records_put = 1;
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a2-corroborate");
    control_evidence_filing(ctx)
}

// ── THE PICKET STANDOFF (#1041, completed by #1349) ──────────────────────────
//
// One obstruction, SIX endings, and a different set of campaign flags for each.
// #1041 built two of them — disabled and destroyed — because two is what a
// restraint LEVER needs to be a lever. #1349 builds the rest of the beat around
// it, and the shape it is built to is the issue's own: a standoff a crew can
// resolve without a shot, and a Backfill that will not fire on its own.
//
//   holding       the crew opened the standoff and left the boat standing.
//   contained     a Security team locked its mounts out from outside.
//   boarded       a Security team went aboard and took it.
//   disabled      its guns were shot off and the fight ended there.
//   withdrawing   it left the lane under its own power.
//   destroyed     it did not.
//   unresolved    nobody ever addressed it.
//
// EXACTLY ONE of those is written to the campaign, at finalisation, by
// `write_the_picket_record` — the `campaign.skyway.strike.*` device pointed at a
// second question. Everything below writes the live facts that reading is made
// of, and each of them is a real chain rather than a timer.
//
// THE ONE INVARIANT THIS BAND KEEPS. Nothing here starts a fight. The Harrow are
// neutral until somebody makes them otherwise, the destroyer's own standing
// doctrine only engages what is already hostile, and the ONLY thing that hands
// Tactical Backfill a picket to shoot at is an authorisation a captain gave on
// the channel. A run in which nobody chooses anything reaches none of these
// handlers and is indistinguishable from one with no picket in it.

// THE STANDOFF CHANNEL, and it is REPEATABLE rather than registered once per
// resolution state.
//
// The per-state partition this used to be was wrong, and the way it was wrong is
// worth writing down because the committee channel above is still built that
// way. A single-shot registration is spent by its FIRST firing, and a `when` only
// keeps an UNFIRED one armed — so a partition on the standoff's counters can
// only survive a re-hail if every path through the scene moves one of the keys it
// partitions on. Two do not: warning the picket sets `havelock_enforcer_warned`
// and moves none of `resolved` / `refused` / `left_alone`, and a crew who open
// the channel and dismiss the thread without picking anything move nothing at
// all. Either one left the boat permanently unhailable with the lane still
// blocked — which loses the negotiated withdrawal, the one road the warning
// exists to unlock.
//
// `.repeat()` is the honest answer and it is one line: the boat answers its
// channel for as long as there is a channel to answer. Everything that decides
// whether there is anything left to say already lives in `picket_standoff`,
// which reads `skyway_mission_finalized` and `picket_settled` at the top and
// hands back the closed-channel line — so a settled standoff says so, in words,
// rather than by a hail that silently does nothing.
on_hailed("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "on_picket_hailed").repeat();

// Provocation. Until this fires the Harrow and the Alliance are not enemies
// and the picket does nothing at all — which is what makes what follows a
// CHOICE the crew made rather than an ambush the mission sprang.
on_attacked("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "on_picket_attacked");

// The gunnery outcomes. Both are real chains rather than timers: a condition
// crossing raises and drops its own flag through the infrastructure tick, and a
// kill emits `Destroyed` whether it came from a beam or from a script.
on_flag_cleared("havelock_enforcer_guns_online", "on_picket_disabled");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "on_picket_destroyed");

// THE SECURITY OUTCOMES (#1346's seam, #1349's targets). A boarding party
// finishing its authored work raises that action's authored `outcome_flag` on
// the ordinary world store, so a containment arrives here exactly as the gallery
// fire and the head evacuation do — off a flag, not off a wire into the Security
// System. Nothing in the engine knows what either of these means.
on_flag_set("havelock_enforcer_contained", "on_picket_contained");
on_flag_set("havelock_enforcer_boarded", "on_picket_boarded");

// Havelock's operations staff watching the corridor notice that the destroyer
// has not gone weapons-free. Read off the MIRROR flag, exactly as a condition
// reads `workforce.<id>.on_strike` — the scenario never touches ship state.
//
// Re-keyed from `weapons_hold.own_ship` in issue #1398: restraint is a POWER
// order now, so what the operations staff are actually watching is the crew's
// weapons group at level 0. Same key shape, same handler, same beat.
on_flag_set("weapons_cold.own_ship", "on_crew_holds_fire");

// ── The standoff's shared reads ─────────────────────────────────────────────

// Whether the obstruction has been answered, by any of the five roads out of it.
// Read at the top of every response and by the campaign record, so the beat has
// ONE definition of "settled" rather than five handlers each guessing at it.
fn picket_settled(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_contained > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_boarded > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_disabled > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrawing > 0 ||
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_destroyed > 0
}

// THE CLOSURE EVERY ENDING TAKES, and the half of this beat that makes AC3 true.
//
// `remove_faction_enemy` is the load-bearing call. A picket that shot back is
// hostile, and a hostile contact is exactly what the destroyer's standing
// untargeted `Destroy` doctrine engages — so WITHOUT this, a hull whose Tactical
// seat is backfilled would go on firing at a boat that had already lost its guns
// until there was no boat. Ending the hostility drops the locks the hostility
// licensed (the applier re-validates every AI target on a successful removal,
// issue #710), which is what lets the authored threshold end the engagement
// instead of the hull failing.
//
// The authorisation is withdrawn in the same breath, and the objective it posted
// is completed rather than left open: force was licensed for a job, and the job
// is done. Backfill is back to having nothing it is allowed to shoot.
fn stand_the_picket_down(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("havelock_enforcer_resolved", 1);
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_force_authorized = 0;
    ctx.effects.remove_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.remove_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-picket");
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_force_posted > 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a1-picket-force");
    }
}

// What an ending costs in people. READ, NEVER ROLLED, and decided at the moment
// the ending lands rather than at the epilogue — the `force_the_picket` rule,
// for the same reason: it is what the situation WAS, and it has to survive a
// save between the act and the report.
//
// A crew who said on the channel what they were about to do get the cheaper
// number on every road but one. That is the whole return on hailing first: not
// permission, which nobody needs, but people who were braced.
//
// A HIGH-WATER MARK, NOT AN ASSIGNMENT, and that is load-bearing rather than
// defensive. More than one of these endings can land on a single run, because
// the picket authors `secure_contain` AND `board` on the same target and the
// destroyer musters two teams — so both can be working the boat at once, which
// is what `probe_picket.toml`'s timeline demonstrates. Their finishing order is
// not fixed: a boarding lands 83 s after it is committed (8 s across, 75 s of
// work) and a containment 63 s after its own commit, so a boarding sent first
// and a containment sent half a minute behind it finish in that order.
//
// An assignment would then let the containment overwrite the boarding's casualty
// with its own 0, and the epilogue would print `report.picket.boarded` ("One of
// theirs hurt getting there") over a standoff toll of zero — contradicting its
// own ledger, with the record's sum check agreeing on the wrong number.
//
// Taking the maximum rather than summing is the other half of the same care: a
// boat that was disabled and then destroyed did not hurt its crew twice over,
// and these figures are the same four people counted by the worst thing that
// happened to them.
//
// [ai] Every number unratified.
fn bank_picket_casualties(ctx, base) {
    let hurt = base;
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned > 0 && hurt > 0 { hurt -= 1; }
    if hurt > ctx.flags.skyway_picket_casualties {
        ctx.flags.skyway_picket_casualties = hurt;
    }
    hurt
}

// What an ending costs in GOODWILL, settled the same way and for the same
// reason: more than one ending can land on one run, and a bare assignment would
// let whichever finished LAST decide the number.
//
// It cannot simply take the worst, though, because the two columns answer
// different questions. The casualty ledger counts a run's harm, so the maximum
// is the honest reading of it. The disposition is what Havelock make of the crew
// AT THE END, and the record names exactly ONE ending as what happened — so the
// number the operator is left on has to be that ending's number, or the epilogue
// prints one story over another's arithmetic. A containment finishing half a
// minute behind a boarding is precisely that case: the record says `boarded`,
// and without this the disposition says 55, which is the containment's.
//
// THE RANKS ARE `write_the_picket_record`'s PRECEDENCE, and the two are meant to
// be read together — change one and change the other. They are NOT the order of
// the numbers (a withdrawal is the second-strongest ending and the highest
// goodwill), which is why the rank has to be authored rather than derived.
//
//   5 destroyed   4 withdrawing   3 boarded   2 contained   1 disabled
//
// Nothing else that moves this side's disposition comes through here: being shot
// at, or being met by a destroyer with cold guns, are things the crew did on the
// way to an ending rather than endings, and they stay ordinary assignments.
fn bank_picket_disposition(ctx, rank, value) {
    if rank <= ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_ending_rank { return; }
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_ending_rank = rank;
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("havelock_operations", value);
}

fn on_picket_attacked(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.picket_engaged == 1 {
        return;
    }
    ctx.flags.picket_engaged = 1;
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
    // [ai] Unratified: shooting at the operator's security is worth twelve
    // points of their goodwill. It is a number for #1036's negotiation to argue
    // with, not a balance claim.
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("havelock_operations", 43);
}

// ── The channel ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn on_picket_hailed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_channel_opened = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        node_fn: "picket_standoff",
    });
}

// The standoff node. Four things a captain can say, and their ORDER is a safety
// catch rather than a presentation choice — the same one #1036's force scene
// keeps, for the same reason and with the same note attached.
//
// A headless or short-crewed bridge runs Comms on Backfill, and Backfill takes
// the FIRST response. So the first response here is always "leave them where
// they are": a thread this scene opens on an empty bridge closes benignly,
// having changed nothing, and the destructive end of this beat stays a thing a
// person decided. Switching Comms Backfill off for this hull is not the fix — it
// would strand every other thread in the mission — and until an Objective can
// say "this decision wants a human", response order is the narrow per-decision
// guard the scene needs.
//
// The authorisation is not merely LAST. It is not rendered at all until a
// stand-off request has been made and turned down: force against a neutral
// contract crew is a decision this mission makes the crew earn, not one it
// leaves lying on the list from the opening tick.
fn picket_standoff(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 || picket_settled(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_channel_closed", responses: [] };
    }
    let body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_holds_station";
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_refused > 0 {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_holds_station_refused";
    } else if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned > 0 {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_holds_station_warned";
    }
    picket_node(ctx, body)
}

// The response list, under whatever the boat has just said. Split from
// `picket_standoff` because the CONVERSATION has to stay alive across a pick: a
// refusal that closed the thread would make the authorisation it unlocks
// reachable only by hailing again, and a hail trigger is single-shot. Every pick
// that does not settle the standoff comes back through here with its own body
// and the list rebuilt from the state that pick just wrote — the shape
// `committee_terms` uses on the other channel.
fn picket_node(ctx, body) {
    let responses = [];
    responses.push(#{
        text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_leave_it",
        on_pick: "on_picket_left_alone",
    });
    // Asking twice is asking twice. The request is offered while it has not been
    // refused, and once more after a warning has been delivered — because the
    // warning is the one thing that moves the answer. A third identical ask
    // would be a loop rather than a conversation.
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_refused == 0 ||
       (ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned > 0 && ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_asked_warned == 0) {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_ask_withdraw",
            on_pick: "on_picket_asked_to_withdraw",
        });
    }
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned == 0 {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_warn_boarders",
            on_pick: "on_picket_warned",
        });
    }
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_refused > 0 {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_authorize_force",
            on_pick: "on_picket_force_authorized",
            important: true,
        });
    }
    #{ message: body, responses: responses }
}

// LEAVE IT. Not an outcome and not a refusal — it closes the channel and changes
// nothing, which is exactly what it should do. What makes it READABLE at the
// epilogue is the fact it shares with every other pick on this thread: the
// channel was opened. A crew who talked to the boat and walked away are
// `holding`; a crew who never called are `unresolved`.
fn on_picket_left_alone(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("havelock_enforcer_left_alone", 1);
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_left_alone", responses: [] }
}

// ASK THEM TO GO. Answered against the operator's live disposition, which is a
// number three earlier beats of this mission have already moved: shooting at
// them took it to 43, coming to the depot with cold guns took it to 60, and a
// warning delivered on this channel is worth ten more. Nothing is rolled and
// nothing is hidden — a crew who have been civil can talk the boat off the lane,
// and a crew who opened on it cannot.
//
// [ai] The 60 line and the warning's ten points are unratified. They are chosen
// so the OPENING position (55) is a refusal: the peaceful road exists and it
// still has to be walked.
fn on_picket_asked_to_withdraw(ctx) {
    // Re-read at admission. Rendering is not authority: a containment, a
    // disablement or the mission's close can all land while this response is
    // still sitting in an inbox.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 || picket_settled(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_channel_closed", responses: [] };
    }
    ctx.flags.increment("havelock_enforcer_asked", 1);
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned > 0 {
        ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_asked_warned = 1;
    }
    let mood = ctx.flags["workforce.havelock_operations.disposition"];
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned > 0 { mood += 10; }
    if mood < 60 {
        // REFUSED — and this is the one flag that opens the force option. A
        // captain cannot authorise force against a boat nobody has asked to
        // leave.
        ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_refused = 1;
        // The thread STAYS OPEN under the refusal. It has to: the refusal is
        // what unlocks the authorisation, and a closed thread would make that
        // option reachable only by hailing again — which a single-shot hail
        // trigger cannot promise.
        return picket_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_refuses");
    }
    withdraw_the_picket(ctx);
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_stands_off", responses: [] }
}

// WITHDRAWING. The state is authoritative the instant the boat agrees; the hull
// leaves twelve seconds later, under way rather than in pieces.
//
// The outcome is recorded BEFORE the removal and in the same call, which is the
// engine's own contract for saying a scripted despawn was not a death (see
// `NarrativeKind::MarkedEntityDestroyed`): the authored `escaped` then stands
// alone and no `marked_entity_destroyed` is invented for a boat that flew home.
//
// A crew who shoot it in the back during those twelve seconds have destroyed it,
// and the timeline says so — which is why `on_picket_destroyed` guards on
// `havelock_enforcer_withdrew`, written by the callback, and not on
// `havelock_enforcer_withdrawing`, written here.
fn withdraw_the_picket(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrawing = 1;
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 1;
    bank_picket_casualties(ctx, 0);
    // [ai] Unratified: an operator whose boat came home whole, on their own
    // orders, thinks better of the crew than one whose boat was taken off them.
    bank_picket_disposition(ctx, 4, 65);
    stand_the_picket_down(ctx);
    ctx.schedule.after(12, |ctx| { the_picket_leaves(ctx); });
}

fn the_picket_leaves(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_destroyed > 0 || ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrew > 0 {
        return;
    }
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrew = 1;
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "escaped");
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name");
}

// WARN THEM. The promise this beat can make, and the only one: we are coming
// aboard, and we are not shooting. It is kept by every ending the crew reach
// WITHOUT USING GUNS — talked off the lane, contained, boarded, or left standing
// — and broken by every ending they shoot their way to, the disablement
// included: taking a boat's mounts off it is weapons fire, whatever the boat's
// crew survive. Settled in the ledger at finalisation beside the other three,
// off facts rather than off a mood (`resolve_the_promises`).
fn on_picket_warned(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 || picket_settled(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_channel_closed", responses: [] };
    }
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned > 0 { return picket_standoff(ctx); }
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_warned = 1;
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_picket_restraint") == "unknown" {
        ctx.commitments.record(#{
            id: "skyway_picket_restraint",
            made_to: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
            terms: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.picket_restraint.terms",
            resolves_when: "world.falling_skyway.commitment.picket_restraint.resolves",
        });
    }
    // What they say back is on the record, because the contract they are holding
    // the lane under is the thing #1039's confrontation would want to read.
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.picket_contract",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    });
    picket_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_holds_station_warned")
}

// AUTHORISE FORCE. The scenario-side authorisation, and the ONLY thing in this
// mission that gives Tactical Backfill the picket to work on.
//
// It is a posted `Destroy` objective and nothing else — no new targeting
// vocabulary, no Rust. The objective source is the top tier of the fleet's
// authored weapons selector, so the moment it exists a backfilled Tactical seat
// locks the boat, and the moment `stand_the_picket_down` completes it the lock
// is gone. Authorisation is therefore a thing the crew can SEE on their own
// objective list and a thing the mission can take back, rather than a mood.
//
// PRIORITY 55: under the head evacuation's 70, because getting people off a
// failing structure outranks clearing a lane, and over the gallery fire's 30.
fn on_picket_force_authorized(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 || picket_settled(ctx) {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_channel_closed", responses: [] };
    }
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_refused == 0 {
        return picket_standoff(ctx);
    }
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_force_authorized > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_force_standing", responses: [] };
    }
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_force_authorized = 1;
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_force_posted = 1;
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a1-picket-force",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.picket_force.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 55,
        directive_kind: "Destroy",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name"],
    });
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_force_authorized", responses: [] }
}

// ── The five endings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// CONTAINED. A team crossed, locked the mounts out and came home. Nobody went
// through a hatch, nobody was hurt, and the boat is Havelock's afterwards — the
// cheapest ending this beat has, and the one the Security backfill reaches for
// first because it is the higher-priority of the two actions the picket offers.
fn on_picket_contained(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.hold_fire("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name");
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 1;
    bank_picket_casualties(ctx, 0);
    // [ai] Unratified. Below the withdrawal's 65: their boat was made safe for
    // them rather than by them.
    bank_picket_disposition(ctx, 2, 55);
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "disabled");
    stand_the_picket_down(ctx);
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        node_fn: "picket_contained_report",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

// BOARDED. The same boat, taken rather than talked down. It costs somebody — one
// person, or nobody if the crew said on the channel that they were coming — and
// it costs Havelock more of their goodwill than a containment, because a
// containment leaves them their boat and this does not.
//
// THIS ENDING'S OWN TOLL IS KEPT, separately from the run's ledger, because the
// report row is a sentence about the boarding rather than about the run: the
// ledger takes a maximum across every ending, and the row has to say what THIS
// one cost. A warned crew makes it nought, and the epilogue picks its words off
// this flag rather than asserting a casualty the ledger denies.
fn on_picket_boarded(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.hold_fire("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name");
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 1;
    let toll = bank_picket_casualties(ctx, 1);
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_boarding_toll = toll;
    // [ai] Unratified.
    bank_picket_disposition(ctx, 3, 45);
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "disabled");
    stand_the_picket_down(ctx);
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        node_fn: "picket_boarded_report",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

// DISABLED. The mount is gone, the boat is not: the picket's weapons group is
// taken COLD — the restraint lever #1398 re-pointed at POWER, applied to an NPC
// through the same reactor an Engineering console commands — and everyone aboard
// it lives. Repairable, in principle, which is the difference the flags are
// recording.
//
// AC3 LANDS HERE. Nothing about this handler requires the hull to fail: the
// authored threshold clears its flag at 35 % of the condition track, and
// `stand_the_picket_down` ends the hostility and retracts the authorisation on
// that crossing — so a backfilled Tactical seat stops at a disabled boat rather
// than finishing it.
fn on_picket_disabled(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.hold_fire("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name");
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_disabled = 1;
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 1;
    bank_picket_casualties(ctx, 1);
    // [ai] Unratified: an operator whose people came home is an operator with
    // something left to lose, and the negotiation reads this number.
    bank_picket_disposition(ctx, 1, 50);
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome("world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name", "disabled");
    stand_the_picket_down(ctx);
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_enforcer.name",
        node_fn: "picket_disabled_report",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

// DESTROYED. The same threat removed, and a crew who removed it the other way.
// `restraint_shown` is written by EVERY ending because it is one question with
// two answers, not several unrelated facts — and killing a picket that had
// already been disabled, contained or boarded is still a kill, which is why this
// handler assigns rather than checking what the others wrote.
//
// No authored outcome: this one really is a death, so the automatic
// `marked_entity_destroyed` beat is the honest timeline entry and nothing here
// suppresses it. The guard is for the boat that had already flown home — its
// removal was `the_picket_leaves`, and an `escaped` was recorded for it first.
fn on_picket_destroyed(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrew > 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_destroyed = 1;
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 0;
    bank_picket_casualties(ctx, 3);
    // [ai] Unratified.
    bank_picket_disposition(ctx, 5, 10);
    stand_the_picket_down(ctx);
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
        node_fn: "picket_destroyed_report",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

// WHO REPORTS. Three of the four endings are answered by the BOAT, on the
// channel the crew have been talking to it on: its people are alive and aboard,
// and it is their own ending to describe. Only the kill is the operator's,
// because the one hull that cannot report a destruction is the destroyed one.
//
// That split is also what keeps this beat off the cutter's thread. The cutter is
// the strike negotiation's voice (#1036), and a containment landing mid-parley
// would have put an unrelated report at the bottom of that conversation.
fn picket_contained_report(ctx) { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_contained_report", responses: [] } }
fn picket_boarded_report(ctx)   { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_boarded_report", responses: [] } }
fn picket_disabled_report(ctx)  { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_disabled_report", responses: [] } }
fn picket_destroyed_report(ctx) { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.picket_destroyed_report", responses: [] } }

fn on_crew_holds_fire(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.havelock_saw_restraint = 1;
    // [ai] Unratified: a destroyer that came to the depot with its guns cold is
    // worth five points of the operator's goodwill.
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("havelock_operations", 60);
}

// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ACT 3 — the head comes down, or it does not (issue #1040)
// ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//
// The act's data — the two debris anchors, the projected-failure deadline and the
// head's own hailability — is authored above this script, and the arithmetic that
// ties it together is in that band's header. What is here is only the wiring.

// THE ACT-3 SEAM. Chained off `skyway_storm_passed` rather than written into
// #1037's `on_storm_passed`, deliberately: the storm slice closes its own act
// and this one opens on the flag that closing wrote, so neither slice edits the
// other's handler. It is the `skyway_strike_settled` device pointed at an act
// boundary.
on_flag_set("skyway_storm_passed", "on_head_watch_opens");

// THE WARNING LADDER, and the floor under it — four rungs of the SAME ladder
// `skyhook.toml` authors, read the only way a condition threshold can be read:
// as a named flag falling. Nothing here knows what percentage any of them sits
// at, which is what lets the tuning pass move the ladder without touching a
// handler.
on_flag_cleared("skyhook_load_bearing", "on_head_warning_one");
on_flag_cleared("skyhook_tether_tensioned", "on_head_warning_two");
on_flag_cleared("skyhook_station_holding", "on_head_warning_three");
on_flag_cleared("skyhook_tether_stable", "on_head_gives_way");

// THE SAVE, read off the same ladder from the other side. The tractor's
// arrest-decline recovery carries the condition track's TOP rung back over its
// restore line; the flag rising IS the save landing, exactly as the Lyra's
// rising flag IS her rescue landing. The top rung rather than the bottom one,
// because a crew who react to the FIRST warning never cleared the lower ones and
// would otherwise save the head into silence.
//
// THE `when` IS LOAD-BEARING, and an `if` at the top of the handler cannot do
// its job. A condition track publishes its `initial_flags` on the structure's
// first tick, so `skyhook_load_bearing` goes UP at world load — the head arrives
// on 48 points — and a flag trigger is SINGLE-SHOT. Without a trigger-level
// predicate this registration would be spent in the lobby and the real save, six
// minutes later, would fire nothing. A `when` that reads false suppresses the
// firing WITHOUT consuming the trigger, which is the distinction
// `combat_test.toml` records at length and `probe_stabilise_resume.toml` uses for
// this same "restored after it broke" shape.
on_flag_set("skyhook_load_bearing", "on_head_stands_down")
    .when("counter(skyway_tether_watch) > 0");

// The projection falling due, and the head leaving the world. The second is
// chained off the removal rather than written beside it (#1033's rule): a
// scripted destruction chains exactly as a kill does, so whatever takes the head
// — this act's own floor today, something else tomorrow — lands in one place.
on_deadline("skyhook_failure_due", "on_head_projection_expires");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name", "on_head_lost");

// The epilogue's two completion signals, on the Lyra's pattern and for her
// reason: there is no "operation completed" trigger, so a scenario reads what a
// held tow LEAVES BEHIND — the recovered condition crossing the craft's line.
on_flag_set("skyway_lighter_secured", "on_lighter_recovered");
on_flag_set("skyway_pod_secured", "on_pod_recovered");

// Act 3 opens. The storm has gone and the corridor is working again, which is
// exactly the problem: the head is carrying traffic on a ribbon that has been
// slipping since before anybody sent a destroyer.
fn on_head_watch_opens(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_watch_open", 1);

    // The head can be destroyed before Act 3 opens. Its last published
    // `skyhook_lift_capable` value is then necessarily stale because the
    // structure that owned the threshold no longer ticks. Loss is the earlier,
    // authoritative fate: do not post remembered work or let that fossil turn
    // one destroyed head into both LOST and HELD.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_lost > 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch = 0;
        return;
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch = 1;

    // TWO OBJECTIVES FOR ONE STRUCTURE, split for the reason Act 2's rescue is
    // split: `detect_reached_objective_completion` completes any objective whose
    // Reach anchor an AI-flown helm arrives at, so the one carrying the approach
    // cannot also be the one recording the work. The approach points at
    // `station_keeping` — 247 units off the head, inside the destroyer's authored
    // 500-unit stabilise range — so a backfilled helm parks the ship where the
    // save is possible from.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a3-standoff",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.head_standoff.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 55,
        directive_kind: "Reach",
        directive_anchor: "station_keeping",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name"],
    }, "skyhook_lift_capable");
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a3-head",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.head_watch.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 55,
        directive_kind: "Stabilise",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name"],
    }, "skyhook_lift_capable");

    // THE OBSTRUCTION SHARES THE ONE TRACTOR WITH THE HEAD-SAVE (John's ruling, T2
    // refinement). The corridor obstruction's controlled demolition (#1350) needs
    // the tractor to hold the mass while the charges fire — `demolition_target`
    // authors `stabilization_required = true` — and the ship carries exactly ONE
    // tractor, which Act 3 already needs for the skyhook-head Stabilise above. So
    // the two jobs CONTEND for the one beam, and the intended play is sequential:
    // save the head, release the tractor, then stabilise + fire the obstruction
    // (or the reverse) — achievable only if the crew are quick.
    //
    // base_priority 45 sits BELOW obj-a3-head's 55, so a Backfilled Engineering
    // seat defers to the head-save by default and holds THE HEAD, never the
    // obstruction, while the head is unsaved — the head-save is not regressed, and
    // a crew who ignore the obstruction get exactly the prior Act-3 behaviour. The
    // AI never tries to hold both: the shared operate selector returns one
    // directive for the one seat. A human is free to override the ranking and work
    // the obstruction first — the demolition adapter reads the live tractor state
    // with no objective gate, so a player-driven sequence works either way; this
    // objective's only job is Act-3 visibility and AI-addressability.
    //
    // mandatory: false — this is bonus content layered onto an already-complete
    // Act 3, not a required objective that would fail a crew who never reach it;
    // the demolition report row (below) covers the unattempted case by omission.
    // Completes off `skyway_obstruction_resolved`, which every terminal demolition
    // outcome raises, so a crew who cleared it before Act 3 opens see it remembered.
    // [ai] Unratified: the 45 priority and the sequencing window need a playtest
    // pass (batch mean-fraction target 80-95%). The window is real — the head-save
    // is threshold-driven off `tether_strain`, the obstruction's tractor dwell is
    // an instantaneous check at `DetonateCharges`, and Security's 30s place-charges
    // dispatch can be staged in parallel — but the exact tuning is playtest ground.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a3-obstruction",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.obstruction.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 45,
        directive_kind: "Stabilise",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name"],
    }, "skyway_obstruction_resolved");

    // The head is actionable from Act 1. If the crew already restored its live
    // lift certification after the tether slip, the threshold is the
    // authoritative memory of that work: post the objectives for the record,
    // resolve the watch immediately, and do not start a decline that asks them
    // to repeat a stabilise they have already landed.
    if ctx.flags.skyhook_lift_capable > 0 {
        ctx.flags.increment("a3_stabilised_early", 1);
        head_holds(ctx);
        return;
    }

    // The people on the head, checking in. Not a warning — this is the beat that
    // establishes there ARE people up there, so the three that follow are
    // somebody's voice rather than a console alarm.
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name",
        node_fn: "head_reports_load",
    });

    tether_strain(ctx);
}

// One beat of the load the head is carrying: [0.5] condition points every [10]
// seconds, re-arming itself for as long as the watch is open.
//
// A callback chain rather than the template's `decay_per_sec`, because that
// ticks from world LOAD — i.e. through the lobby — and a skyhook's deterioration
// is a mission beat rather than a lobby tax (the template says so at length).
// And a chain rather than a ladder of `[[deadline]]` blocks because this is the
// act's metronome, not a named thing in the world the crew can see or slip.
//
// It stops on exactly two conditions and both write `skyway_tether_watch`: the
// head is saved, or the head is gone.
fn tether_strain(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.effects.damage_infrastructure("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name", flt("0.5"));
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_strain_beats", 1);
    ctx.schedule.after(10, |ctx| { tether_strain(ctx); });
}

// One rung of the warning ladder, on all three surfaces at once. Factored
// because three rungs that differ only in their strings and their priority
// should differ only in their strings and their priority: the SHAPE of a warning
// — turn the rung they did not act on red, post a louder one, put the boss on
// the channel — is what this slice is actually promising, and it belongs in one
// place where it can be read.
fn head_warning(ctx, supersedes, id, text, priority, node_fn) {
    if supersedes != "" {
        // THE PANEL SAYS WHICH ONE THEY IGNORED. An objective going red is the
        // loudest thing this scenario can say without prose (`obj-a2-corroborate`
        // set the device); here it is pointed at the crew's own inattention.
        ctx.effects.fail_objective(supersedes);
    }
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: id,
        text: text,
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: priority,
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name"],
    });
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name",
        node_fn: node_fn,
        urgent: true,
    });
}

fn on_head_warning_one(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_warning_one", 1);
    head_warning(ctx, "", "obj-a3-tether-1",
                 "world.falling_skyway.objective.tether_one.text", 60, "head_warns_one");
}

fn on_head_warning_two(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_warning_two", 1);
    head_warning(ctx, "obj-a3-tether-1", "obj-a3-tether-2",
                 "world.falling_skyway.objective.tether_two.text", 70, "head_warns_two");
}

// The last one. From here the evacuation cannot be run cleanly — the flag below
// is what `on_head_clear_it` reads to say so out loud rather than quietly
// halving a number nobody was told about.
fn on_head_warning_three(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_warning_three", 1);
    ctx.flags.skyway_head_last_warning = 1;
    head_warning(ctx, "obj-a3-tether-2", "obj-a3-tether-3",
                 "world.falling_skyway.objective.tether_three.text", 80, "head_warns_three");
}

// ── The gang on the head ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Four bodies over one pair of answers, and that is the point: the SITUATION
// escalates and the captain's options do not, because there are only ever two
// things to say to somebody standing on a structure that is failing.
//
// ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, for `havelock_offer`'s reason. A hull whose Tactical
// seat is AI-backfilled answers an open thread with its FIRST response, so index
// 0 has to be the answer an officer who is not there should give: acknowledge,
// commit to nothing, keep the channel. Ordering people off a structure is a
// decision, and a decision belongs to whoever is sitting in the chair.
fn head_reports_load(ctx) { head_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_reports_load") }
fn head_warns_one(ctx)    { head_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_warns_one") }
fn head_warns_two(ctx)    { head_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_warns_two") }
fn head_warns_three(ctx)  { head_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_warns_three") }

fn head_node(ctx, body) {
    // Nothing left to decide once the head is empty.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_head_cleared > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_already_clear", responses: [] };
    }
    #{
        message: body,
        responses: [
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_acknowledge", on_pick: "on_head_acknowledge" },
            #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_clear_it", on_pick: "on_head_clear_it", important: true },
        ],
    }
}

// Being told is worth something, and it is worth something because it is TRUE: a
// gang who have been talking to a destroyer are a gang wearing their rigs and
// standing near the lift when the ribbon goes.
fn on_head_acknowledge(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_head_told = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_head_acknowledged", 1);
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_stays_up", responses: [] }
}

// THE EVACUATION. It costs nothing the crew can feel today and everything in the
// only currency this act has: it takes the shift off the structure, so the
// transfer window the next slice is built around has nobody to work it. The flag
// is the record a later act reads; the count below is what it buys.
fn on_head_clear_it(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_head_cleared = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_head_cleared", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_head_last_warning > 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_head_cleared_late = 1;
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_clearing_late", responses: [] };
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_clearing", responses: [] }
}

// ── The floor ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// One call, and every consequence hangs off the REMOVAL rather than off this
// handler — see `on_head_lost`.
fn on_head_gives_way(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_floor_crossed", 1);
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name");
}

// What was up there when it went. READ, never rolled — #1036's rule and for its
// reason: script has no RNG and should not have one. Every term is a fact the
// crew could have known at the time, and every one of them is a flag something
// else in this act wrote.
//
// [ai] Every number here is unratified.
fn head_casualties(ctx) {
    // A settled strike means a full shift is back on the head working the
    // transfer. That is not a punishment for settling — it is what settling DID,
    // and the captain has a lever over it three warnings long.
    let souls = 6;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled == 0 { souls = 3; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_head_told > 0 { souls -= 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_head_cleared > 0 { souls = 0; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_head_cleared_late > 0 { souls = 2; }
    souls
}

// Chained off the head's own `Destroyed` event. Everything losing the skyhook
// costs is here, in one place, so a later slice that finds another way to take
// the structure gets the same consequences without re-deriving them.
fn on_head_lost(ctx) {
    // The strain has nothing left to strain and the projection nothing left to
    // project. Cancelling is also what keeps `skyhook_failure_due` from firing
    // sixteen seconds later onto a head that is already gone.
    ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch = 0;
    if ctx.deadlines.state("skyhook_failure_due") == "pending" {
        ctx.deadlines.cancel("skyhook_failure_due");
    }

    // THE RECORD. Exactly one of `skyway_skyhook_lost` and `skyway_skyhook_held`
    // is ALWAYS written (#1037's invariant), so a later mission reads a fact
    // rather than an absence.
    ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_lost = 1;
    // The two transfer berths left the world with the structure that carried
    // them, and BOTH halves of that are written here. The named flag is what
    // #1042's transfer window reads; the second line zeroes the capacity's own
    // mirrored counter, which the infrastructure adapter republishes every tick a
    // structure moves and which would otherwise keep saying "two berths" forever
    // — a structure that no longer ticks cannot correct its own last reading, and
    // a script predicate asking `counter(skyhook_transfer_berths)` deserves the
    // truth rather than a fossil.
    ctx.flags.skyway_transfer_capacity_lost = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyhook_transfer_berths"] = 0;
    ctx.flags.skyway_head_casualties = head_casualties(ctx);
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_head_lost", 1);

    // THE PANEL, GOING RED. Blanket rather than tracked: `fail_objective` moves
    // an ACTIVE objective and nothing else, so the rungs the crew already let go
    // stay exactly as they were and only the live one turns over. What is left on
    // the list is the history of the warnings.
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-tether-1");
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-tether-2");
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-tether-3");
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-head");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-standoff");

    // The corridor has nothing to queue for. The same holding run the storm used
    // — west, then south, then hold — pointed at traffic with nowhere to go.
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name", "storm_shelter_run");
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_lark.name", "storm_shelter_run");
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.hauler_pell.name", "storm_shelter_run");

    // Somebody has to tell Control, and it is a MANDATORY objective rather than a
    // line of prose so it sits on the panel until the crew deal with it —
    // #1037's loss report, same device, bigger loss.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-head-report",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.head_report.text",
        mandatory: true,
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name"],
    });
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.head_collapse",
        provenance: "scan",
    });

    // THE BRANCH. Two seconds out, so the craft read as coming OUT of the wreck
    // rather than as replacing the structure on the tick it left.
    ctx.schedule.after(2, |ctx| { head_survivors(ctx); });
}

// ── The epilogue ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Losing the skyhook is a worse ending, not a game over. Two craft come off the
// head as it goes, adrift in the debris with condition tracks the tractor's
// arrest-decline recovery is sized to cross — the Lyra's machinery, reused
// exactly (each carries the same `[held_response]` on its spawn override below).
//
// Spawned with `overrides` rather than authored as `[[entity]]` rows for the
// obvious reason (they do not exist until the head comes apart), and each
// carries its OWN threshold flag, because two entities declaring one flag are
// declaring one flag and would overwrite each other's answer every tick — the
// rule the two ladder depots follow above.
//
// [20] of [100] points each, under their own authored half-way line ([50] %), so
// both flags are DOWN from their first tick and each one's rise is an event. The
// tractor's arrest-decline recovers each over the [55] % restore line with room
// to spare — a survivor craft is a rescue, not a puzzle. `hull_damage_share = 0`
// for the Lyra's reason: what is wrong with a survivor craft is that it has no
// way home, not that its paint is scratched. [ai] All four unratified.
fn head_survivors(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml",
        name: "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_lighter.name",
        anchor: "head_debris_field",
        groups: ["head_survivors"],
        overrides: #{
            comms: #{ hailable: true },
            infrastructure: #{
                condition: 20,
                hull_damage_share: 0,
                threshold: [ #{
                    flag: "skyway_lighter_secured",
                    fails_below: flt("0.5"),
                    label: "world.falling_skyway.threshold.under_tow.label",
                } ],
            },
            // The tow that pulls her clear is now the TRACTOR (issue #1165 S11b):
            // arrest-decline recovers her from 20 over her 55-point line while
            // held, and `on_flag_set("skyway_lighter_secured", …)` reads the
            // crossing exactly as it read the old tow's payout. The Lyra's
            // machinery, reused exactly — same recover rate, same detection.
            held_response: #{ kind: "arrest-decline", recover_per_sec: flt("2.0") },
        },
    });
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml",
        name: "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_pod.name",
        anchor: "head_debris_drift",
        groups: ["head_survivors"],
        overrides: #{
            comms: #{ hailable: true },
            infrastructure: #{
                condition: 20,
                hull_damage_share: 0,
                threshold: [ #{
                    flag: "skyway_pod_secured",
                    fails_below: flt("0.5"),
                    label: "world.falling_skyway.threshold.under_tow.label",
                } ],
            },
            // Towed clear the same way the lighter is (issue #1165 S11b): the
            // tractor's arrest-decline recovers her over her own line, read off
            // `skyway_pod_secured` with no operation-completed trigger.
            held_response: #{ kind: "arrest-decline", recover_per_sec: flt("2.0") },
        },
    });

    // The epilogue's approach and aggregate debt, plus one operate directive per
    // craft. A single Tow directive cannot name both targets, and leaving the
    // first directive active after its threshold rose would make Backfill hold
    // the recovered lighter forever instead of taking the pod next.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-muster",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.muster.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 85,
        directive_kind: "Reach",
        directive_anchor: "head_debris_field",
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-survivors",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.survivors.text",
        mandatory: true,
        targets: [
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_lighter.name",
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_pod.name",
        ],
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-lighter",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.lighter.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 86,
        directive_kind: "Tow",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_lighter.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.head_lighter.name"],
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-pod",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.pod.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 85,
        directive_kind: "Tow",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_pod.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.head_pod.name"],
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_epilogue_open", 1);

    // A second out, so the sender is in `name_to_uuid` before the comms router is
    // asked to range-gate it. A thread opened on the tick its sender spawned
    // would fall through the synthetic-sender escape and read as a message from
    // nowhere.
    ctx.schedule.after(1, |ctx| {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.head_lighter.name",
            node_fn: "lighter_calls",
            urgent: true,
        });
    });

    // The epilogue's clock: [75] seconds, measured from the collapse rather than
    // from the mission start, because WHEN the head fell is a fact about the run
    // and an authored `[[deadline]]` could only ever have been right for one of
    // them.
    ctx.schedule.after(75, |ctx| { head_epilogue_resolves(ctx); });
}

fn lighter_calls(ctx) {
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lighter_calls", responses: [] }
}

fn on_lighter_recovered(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.a3_epilogue_open == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.skyway_lighter_safe = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_survivors_recovered", 1);
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-lighter");
}

fn on_pod_recovered(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.a3_epilogue_open == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.skyway_pod_safe = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_survivors_recovered", 1);
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-pod");
}

// The epilogue's resolution. Three outcomes rather than two, because "we got one
// of them" is what actually happens to a crew who start late.
fn head_epilogue_resolves(ctx) {
    let saved = ctx.flags.a3_survivors_recovered;
    ctx.flags.skyway_survivors_recovered = saved;
    ctx.flags.skyway_survivors_lost = 2 - saved;

    // The civilians row (issue #1351), written HERE — the tick the survivors'
    // fate is decided, the Lyra rule — and never at the close, because a run
    // that held the head never reaches this epilogue and reports no such row.
    civilians_report_row(ctx);

    if saved > 0 {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-survivors");
    } else {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-survivors");
    }
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-muster");

    // What is still adrift when the window closes is taken by the debris. The
    // same `destroy_entity` the head went to, and the same reading: a failure is
    // a thing that happens, not a thing that quietly stops being mentioned.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_lighter_safe == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-lighter");
        ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.head_lighter.name");
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_pod_safe == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-pod");
        ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.head_pod.name");
    }

    ctx.flags.act3_complete = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_epilogue_resolved", 1);
}

// ── The other ending ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The head standing back up. Guarded on the watch for TWO reasons and both
// matter: this flag comes up once at world load, when the condition track is
// first mirrored and the head is sitting on 48 points, and it can come up again
// after the act has already resolved. The watch is what makes this handler mean
// "a crew just saved it" rather than "a number went up".
fn on_head_stands_down(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_stood_down", 1);
    head_holds(ctx);
}

// The projection falling due on a head that is still standing. The load comes
// off, the corridor's own structural people take over, and she held — the act's
// other road to the same ending, walked by a crew who stabilised late enough
// that the ladder never fully stood down but early enough that the floor was
// never crossed.
fn on_head_projection_expires(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch == 0 { return; }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_projection_beaten", 1);
    head_holds(ctx);
}

fn head_holds(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_tether_watch = 0;
    if ctx.deadlines.state("skyhook_failure_due") == "pending" {
        ctx.deadlines.cancel("skyhook_failure_due");
    }
    // The other half of the pair.
    ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_held = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_head_held", 1);

    // Only the LIVE rung turns over: `complete_objective` moves an Active
    // objective and nothing else, so the rungs the crew let go stay red and the
    // panel still says which ones they were. Saving the structure does not
    // un-ignore a warning.
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-tether-1");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-tether-2");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-tether-3");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-head");
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-standoff");

    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyhook.name",
        node_fn: "head_stands_down",
        urgent: true,
    });
    ctx.flags.act3_complete = 1;
}

fn head_stands_down(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_head_cleared > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_holds_empty", responses: [] };
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.head_holds", responses: [] }
}

// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ACT 3 — THE TRANSFER WINDOW, AND THE SUM THAT DOES NOT COME OUT (issue #1042)
// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//
// Act 1 was a survey. Act 2 was weather and a dispute. Act 3's crisis is
// ARITHMETIC, and the arithmetic is the scene: a window opens on a deadline the
// crew have been watching since the first tick, and what the chain can lift in
// it does not cover what the three parties on Control's manifest have asked
// for. Nobody has to work that out. Control says it out loud, and the three
// figures — available, claimed, short by — are rows on Control's own fact sheet
// while the window is open.
//
// ── DEMAND IS AUTHORED, SUPPLY IS COMPUTED ──────────────────────────────────
//
// The asymmetry is the design. What the claimants want is data (three
// `[[infrastructure.capacity]]` rows on Control, filed before the crew arrived,
// and they do not shrink because the ladder is broken). What the corridor can
// deliver is a FUNCTION OF THE MISSION SO FAR, worked out here from live world
// state at the moment the window opens:
//
//   the head       `skyhook_lift_capable` — the 45 % threshold Act 1 knocks it
//                  under, and which a field-repair can put back. Certified, the
//                  head offers its authored berths at its authored climber
//                  load; uncertified, it offers nothing, because a head that is
//                  not signed off to run a climber does not run one.
//   each rung      above its OWN operational line, AND staffed by people who
//                  are at work. One rule, applied twice, and both halves are
//                  needed: repairing Ladder B does not end the strike and
//                  ending the strike does not mend Ladder B (#1035 says so on
//                  the depot itself).
//   the smaller    of what the head can lift and what the ladder can put in it.
//                  A chain delivers what its worst link delivers.
//
// So a crew who settled the strike and mended the rung arrive with more to give
