// than a crew who did neither, and neither arrives with enough. THE CEILING IS
// STRUCTURAL: 40 from Ladder A plus 12 from Ladder B is 52, nothing in this
// mission can raise either capacity — the crew's hull authors no `[transfer]`
// terms and therefore cannot pump anything INTO a rung — and the three claims
// total 66. There is no state of this world in which the window covers all
// three, and the headless test asserts that from the authored numbers rather
// than from a run, because it is a claim about every run.
//
// ── THE SKYHOOK'S FATE IS ALREADY WIRED IN ──────────────────────────────────
//
// `skyhook_lift_capable` is the whole of the head's contribution, and it is a
// threshold on the head's live condition track. Anything that takes the head
// down takes the window's supply with it — the tether slip does it today, a
// field-repair undoes it, and the collapse slice (#1040) will do it for good
// without touching a line of this block. This file deliberately reads the
// EXISTING flag rather than any collapse state, so the two slices meet at a
// number instead of at a name.
//
// ── WHY THE NUMBERS LAND ON A CAPACITY ROW ──────────────────────────────────
//
// [ai] JUDGEMENT CALL, and the honest surface rather than the ideal one.
// Nothing in this engine's crew-facing text can carry a computed number:
// objective text, a comms body and a dossier finding are all `strings.csv` ids
// resolved whole, with no parameter table anywhere on the wire. The only place
// a runtime figure reaches a player is as a labelled `[[infrastructure.capacity]]`
// row on a fact sheet. So the three figures are published as capacity rows on
// Control — which is where a crew already goes to ask what the corridor is
// doing — and the mission COPY states, in words, that the window is short and
// that this makes it a choice. The digits are on the panel; the sentence about
// them is in the dialogue. The real fix is parameterised strings, and it is
// nobody's slice yet.
//
// [ai] SUPERSEDED IN PART, and the paragraph above is kept because it is the
// reason the capacity rows exist rather than a mistake to erase. Parameterised
// strings landed: a text id may now be joined on the wire by a `<field>_params`
// table (`messages::TEXT_PARAMS_SUFFIX`), a script authors it as an optional
// `params` key, and the client's `localiseTree` resolves `t(id, params)` at the
// wire boundary. `window_opens_short` is the first consumer — it reads the three
// banked flags and the copy interpolates them — so the sentence now carries the
// digits it used to point at.
//
// THE CAPACITY ROWS STAY, and that is a decision rather than an oversight. They
// are a standing readout a crew can consult at any point in the window, while
// the dialogue is a single beat that arrives once; and the booking arithmetic
// below moves those rows as lifts are committed and stood down, which no
// sentence spoken at open could track. What changed is that the opening line no
// longer has to say "our manifest carries that figure" instead of the figure.
//
// ── THE CLOSE RULE: ABORT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The window shuts on its deadline whatever is happening. A lift still on the
// ribbon when it does is STOOD DOWN: it does not land, its claimant is not
// served, and its share comes back off the committed row. [ai] Chosen over
// "complete" and over "partial", and for reasons rather than taste.
//
//   COMPLETE would make the closing deadline advisory. A captain who booked at
//   the last second would get a free lift out of the clock, and the pressure the
//   window exists to create would be pressure to dither.
//   PARTIAL has no fiction behind it. Half a climber-load is not half a rescue;
//   the people on it are still on the rock. It is also the call this engine
//   already makes everywhere else — `tow` and `stabilise` pay
//   `condition_on_complete` as a LUMP precisely because a job half-run has moved
//   nobody anywhere.
//
// ── WHO BOOKS A LIFT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Not this slice. The choice is #1043's scene, and what this block owns is the
// LEDGER it has to obey. Each claimant has a seam flag; setting it asks for a
// lift, and the request is granted or refused against the live window state in
// one place, exactly as #1035 put the settlement behind `skyway_strike_settled`
// so that a dialogue pick, a deadline or a later act would all get the same
// consequence applied once. Nothing in this file sets them, so the window
// currently opens, states its shortfall and closes unspent — which is the
// honest state of the act until the choice lands on top of it.

on_flag_set("skyway_storm_passed", "on_act_three_opens");
on_flag_set("skyway_window_transfer_primed", "on_window_transfer_primed");
on_deadline("skyway_transfer_window", "on_transfer_window_opens");
on_deadline("skyway_window_closes", "on_transfer_window_closes");

// The three booking seams. One per claimant rather than one taking a name,
// for the reason this file's other vocabularies are split by verb: a flag store
// cannot carry an argument, and a misspelt claimant would otherwise be a silent
// no-op instead of a seam nobody wired.
//
// ONE ASK PER CLAIMANT, because a trigger is single-shot and this one is never
// re-armed. That is an authored rule rather than a limitation worked around: an
// allocation IS the decision, and a captain who could ask for the same party
// over and over until the ledger happened to allow it would be shopping rather
// than choosing. #1043's tree is expected to gate its options on the ledger
// below — `skyway_window_supply` minus `skyway_window_reserved`, against the
// claim — so a refusal is something the crew are shown BEFORE they can pick it,
// and the two refusal counters here are the backstop for anything that gets
// past that.
on_flag_set("skyway_book_committee", "on_book_committee");
on_flag_set("skyway_book_havelock", "on_book_havelock");
on_flag_set("skyway_book_convoy", "on_book_convoy");

// Act 3 opens on the corridor clearing, chained off the flag `on_storm_passed`
// already writes rather than off the deadline it writes it from — so this block
// is additive to Act 2 rather than an edit of it. The collapse slice (#1040)
// registers a second handler on the SAME flag for the same reason: two slices
// opening one act is two registrations, not an edit of somebody else's function.
fn on_act_three_opens(ctx) {
    // The readiness beat is real two-seat work: Helm docks with the named
    // manifold and Engineering runs the umbilical. The target sits at
    // `station_keeping`, where #1040's standoff Reach already sends the ship.
    // Priority 54, one below that Reach, is load-bearing: Transfer itself is an
    // operate directive rather than a travel directive, so the standoff stays
    // the top Helm destination until the dock is in range; the dock and
    // umbilical hosts still find this directive through their kind filter.
    //
    // The receiving ledger's threshold is the completion memory. A crew may
    // prime it before the storm clears; `post_remembered_objective` then records
    // the objective already green instead of asking them to repeat the work.
    post_remembered_objective(ctx, #{
        id: "obj-a3-window-ready",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.window_ready.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 54,
        directive_kind: "Transfer",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.window_transfer_manifold.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.window_transfer_manifold.name"],
    }, "skyway_window_transfer_worked");
}

// The umbilical work lands. This is a target-side reading, not an operation
// event: capacity physically moved onto the receiving manifold and crossed its
// authored threshold. Latch it separately so completion survives an objective
// that has not posted yet (and any later change to the live capacity).
fn on_window_transfer_primed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_transfer_worked = 1;
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-window-ready");
}

// ── The arithmetic ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// What ONE rung delivers into the window. Two questions, and a rung has to pass
// both: is it above its own operational line, and are the people who work it at
// work. Read from mirrored world counters — a threshold flag (#1025), a
// workforce flag (#1035) and the rung's own published capacity — so a tuning
// pass that moves any of the three moves this without editing it.
fn rung_delivers(ctx, operational_flag, capacity_id, stoppage_flag) {
    if ctx.flags[operational_flag] == 0 { return 0; }
    if ctx.flags[stoppage_flag] > 0 { return 0; }
    ctx.flags[capacity_id]
}

// What the whole chain can put through this window.
fn window_supply(ctx) {
    // The head. Its two published capacities are what it offers when it is
    // certified to offer anything, and this is the first thing in the mission to
    // USE the numbers the skyhook template publishes "so the crew can do the
    // arithmetic themselves".
    let head = 0;
    if ctx.flags.skyhook_lift_capable > 0 {
        head = ctx.flags["skyhook_transfer_berths"] * ctx.flags["skyhook_climber_load"];
    }
    // The ladder. Same rule twice, over the two rungs and the two sides that
    // staff them.
    let ladder =
        rung_delivers(ctx, "depot_a_pumping", "depot_a_fuel_lift",
                      "workforce.havelock_operations.on_strike") +
        rung_delivers(ctx, "depot_b_pumping", "depot_b_fuel_lift",
                      "workforce.skyway_workers.on_strike");
    // A chain delivers what its worst link delivers.
    if head < ladder { head } else { ladder }
}

// WHAT THE CHAIN CAN STILL DELIVER, which is not always what it could deliver
// when the shutters went up (issue #1340).
//
// `skyway_window_supply` is banked at the opening and deliberately never moves:
// a rung that fails while a climber is on the ribbon does not un-book the
// climber, and that is the rule every booked lift is measured against. But a
// claim that has NOT been granted yet is a different question — offering lift
// off a chain that has since stopped delivering is offering something the head
// cannot honour, and this act's whole promise is that a displayed grant is
// executable when it is picked.
//
// So: the lower of the two, never the higher. Re-deriving the chain can only
// ever LOWER what is on offer here, which is the ceiling rule stated as code —
// a rung repaired mid-window does not mint lift the window was not priced for,
// and no correction to this conversation can raise the authored unit supply.
fn window_deliverable(ctx) {
    let banked = ctx.flags.skyway_window_supply;
    let live = window_supply(ctx);
    if live < banked { live } else { banked }
}

// What the three of them have asked for. Read off the manifest rows rather than
// restated here, so the claims are authored data in exactly one place.
fn window_demand(ctx) {
    ctx.flags["skyway_claim_committee"] +
    ctx.flags["skyway_claim_havelock"] +
    ctx.flags["skyway_claim_convoy"]
}

// Publish an absolute figure onto one of Control's manifest rows.
//
// `adjust_capacity` moves a level by a DELTA, so an absolute publish is
// `want - what is there`. That is safe here and would not be everywhere: the
// counter this reads is re-published by the infrastructure tick, so two
// absolute publishes of the same row inside ONE tick would both compute their
// delta from the same stale level. Every caller below either publishes a row
// once (the window opening, the window closing) or moves it by an exact delta
// it worked out itself (a booking, a lift stood down), and exact deltas compose.
fn publish_manifest(ctx, capacity_id, want) {
    let live = ctx.flags[capacity_id];
    if want != live {
        ctx.effects.adjust_capacity(
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
            capacity_id,
            want - live,
        );
    }
}

// THE LIFT ROW, MOVED BY AN EXACT DELTA — the rule the comment above states,
// obeyed by the one row #1340 gave a repeating publisher (issue #1340).
//
// `publish_manifest` is only safe for a row published ONCE, because it derives
// its delta from a mirrored counter the infrastructure tick re-publishes at the
// end of the tick. `skyway_window_available` is not that row any more: a booking
// moves it by an exact delta and `the_board_moved` republishes it whenever the
// chain changes under everybody, and the two can land in one tick — the watch's
// callback runs after the trigger pipeline that booked the lift. The ledger
// flags have moved by then; the mirrored row has not. An absolute publish would
// emit the booking's delta a second time and the panel would lose twice the
// claim.
//
// So this reads a LATCH instead: what the row will read once the queued deltas
// settle, kept by every caller that moves the row. Exact deltas compose, so a
// booking and a republish in one tick land on the right figure in either order —
// and in the ordinary case they agree, the delta is zero and nothing is emitted.
fn publish_window_available(ctx, want) {
    let published = ctx.flags.skyway_window_published;
    if want != published {
        ctx.effects.adjust_capacity(
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
            "skyway_window_available",
            want - published,
        );
        ctx.flags.skyway_window_published = want;
    }
}

// ── The window opens ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn on_transfer_window_opens(ctx) {
    let supply = window_supply(ctx);
    let demand = window_demand(ctx);
    let short = demand - supply;
    if short < 0 { short = 0; }

    // The ledger the bookings are decided against. Banked as flags rather than
    // re-derived per booking, because what a claimant is measured against is
    // what the chain COULD do when the window opened — a rung that fails while a
    // climber is on it does not un-book the climber.
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_open = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_supply = supply;
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_demand_total = demand;
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_shortfall_at_open = short;
    // WHAT THE ROOM HAS ALREADY BEEN TOLD (#1340), as one number: the lift
    // still unspoken for, doubled, plus one if the corridor has already lost
    // the convoy. One mark rather than a flag per term, so every trigger that
    // can move this board — a grant, a rung failing, a hull destroyed, the
    // periodic watch — asks the same question before it announces anything and
    // no two of them announce one movement twice.
    //
    // Computed off the locals the arithmetic above already produced. Nothing is
    // reserved yet on the tick a window opens, so the room and the supply are
    // the same figure and there is no reason to derive it twice.
    let mark = supply * 2;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost > 0 { mark += 1; }
    ctx.flags.skyway_board_marked = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_board_seen = mark;

    // The manifest, on the panel, from this tick. `skyway_window_committed`
    // stays at its authored zero: nothing has been put on the ribbon yet.
    publish_manifest(ctx, "skyway_window_available", supply);
    // …and the lift row is latched from here, because it is the one row this act
    // moves more than once. See `publish_window_available`.
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_published = supply;
    publish_manifest(ctx, "skyway_window_demand", demand);
    publish_manifest(ctx, "skyway_window_shortfall", short);

    // Opening the window is the work's authored boundary, never its completion
    // shortcut. A crew who did not prime the target-side ledger leave the
    // optional run-up red; a timer cannot perform an umbilical transfer.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_transfer_worked == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-window-ready");
    }
    // NO DIRECTIVE, and priority 65 rather than the top of the act. This beat is
    // a DECISION and not a place: there is nowhere to fly to in order to choose
    // who goes up, and an objective carrying a Reach anchor would have a
    // backfilled helm complete the mission's hardest call by arriving somewhere.
    // 65 sits between the tether ladder's first warning (60) and its second
    // (70), which is the honest ordering — the window matters more than a rung
    // nobody has acted on yet, and less than a head that has ignored one.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-window",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.window.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 65,
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name"],
    });

    // THE SHORTFALL, SAID OUT LOUD. Two bodies rather than one, picked by the
    // arithmetic that just ran, because "you have lift for two of them and not
    // for three" and "the head is not lifting anything at all" are different
    // pieces of news and a crew who got one should not be read the other.
    // Terminal — no responses — so the beat cannot be answered by a backfilled
    // Comms policy picking index 0 (this file's other two trees carry that
    // hazard at length).
    //
    // TWO rather than a ladder of severities, and that is a claim about the
    // authored numbers rather than a shrug: any two of the three claims fit
    // inside anything the chain can deliver at all, so "you can take two" is
    // true for every non-zero supply this world can produce. A third body for a
    // case the mission cannot reach would be copy nobody ever hears.
    let node = "window_opens_short";
    if supply <= 0 {
        node = "window_opens_dead";
    }
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: node,
        urgent: true,
    });

    // …and the board is watched from here until the shutters come down (#1340).
    ctx.schedule.after(3, |ctx| { watch_the_manifest(ctx); });
}

// The two bodies. Each is its own node function because `open_comms` names a
// FUNCTION, and both say the same thing at a different volume: the window is
// open, it is short, and that makes it a decision.
//
// THE SHORT BODY NOW CARRIES THE DIGITS. Its `params` map is read off the three
// flags `on_transfer_window_opens` banked a few lines up — the same ledger the
// bookings are decided against, so the sentence and the manifest cannot disagree
// about what the chain could do when the window opened. The copy interpolates
// them as `{available}`, `{claimed}` and `{shortfall}`; see the note above on
// why the numbers used to live only on a capacity row.
//
// The dead body is left as it was, deliberately. It says the lift is nothing at
// all against three standing claims, which is a sentence with no figure in it
// that a number would improve — "short by the whole of it" is the point.
fn window_opens_short(ctx) {
    #{
        message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_opens_short",
        params: #{
            available: ctx.flags.skyway_window_supply,
            claimed: ctx.flags.skyway_window_demand_total,
            shortfall: ctx.flags.skyway_window_shortfall_at_open,
        },
        responses: [],
    }
}
fn window_opens_dead(ctx)  { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_opens_dead", responses: [] } }

// ── Booking a lift ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// `still_there` is `book_berth`'s parameter, on this ledger and for its reason
// (#1340). The pick that pulls one of these seams has ALREADY written
// `skyway_granted_*`, and the seam runs a tick later — so `convoy_standing`
// cannot be re-asked here, because by now it answers "settled" rather than
// "gone". What is left to ask is the half of that question a decision does not
// cover: whether there is still a hull to put on a climber. The convoy is the
// one claimant this corridor can lose; the other two are on the rock and pass
// `true`.
fn on_book_committee(ctx) {
    if book_lift(ctx, "skyway_claim_committee", true) {
        ctx.schedule.after(24, |ctx| {
            land_lift(ctx, "skyway_claim_committee",
                      "skyway_window_served_committee",
                      "skyway_window_stood_down_committee");
        });
    }
}

fn on_book_havelock(ctx) {
    if book_lift(ctx, "skyway_claim_havelock", true) {
        ctx.schedule.after(24, |ctx| {
            land_lift(ctx, "skyway_claim_havelock",
                      "skyway_window_served_havelock",
                      "skyway_window_stood_down_havelock");
        });
    }
}

fn on_book_convoy(ctx) {
    if book_lift(ctx, "skyway_claim_convoy", ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0) {
        ctx.schedule.after(24, |ctx| {
            land_lift(ctx, "skyway_claim_convoy",
                      "skyway_window_served_convoy",
                      "skyway_window_stood_down_convoy");
        });
    }
}

// The one place a request for lift is granted or refused. Three refusals, and
// all three are recorded rather than silent: a captain who asks for something
// the window cannot give is told which of the walls they hit.
fn book_lift(ctx, claim_id, still_there) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 {
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_refused_shut", 1);
        return false;
    }
    // The wall `book_berth` grew for the sibling ledger (#1340), and the same
    // race put it here. `on_lift_convoy` asks `convoy_standing` at PICK time,
    // but the booking it schedules lands a tick later, and the corridor can
    // destroy the hull inside that tick. Spending the window on nobody is the
    // worse half of that bug: the claim is the largest number in the act, the
    // committee and Havelock are repriced out of lift that will never fly, and
    // `got_out` would then report a destroyed convoy as having got off the rock.
    if !still_there {
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_refused_lost", 1);
        return false;
    }
    let need = ctx.flags[claim_id];
    // The ledger, not the panel row: the counter a capacity mirrors onto is
    // re-published by the infrastructure tick, so a second booking in the same
    // tick would read the first one's row before it had moved. These flags land
    // between calls.
    //
    // `window_room` rather than the banked figure since #1340, so the one place
    // a lift is granted asks the SAME question the dialogue asked before it drew
    // the option: what can the chain put through this window right now, less
    // what is already spoken for.
    let left = window_room(ctx);
    if left < need {
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_refused_short", 1);
        return false;
    }
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_reserved", need);
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_lifts_started", 1);
    // The protected human decision resolves its own objective. The close
    // deadline may mark an untouched decision red, but it never turns work
    // green on the crew's behalf.
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-window");
    // Exact deltas, so two bookings landing in one tick both count. The latch
    // moves with the row so a republish in the same tick sees this booking.
    ctx.effects.adjust_capacity(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name", "skyway_window_available", -need);
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_published", -need);
    ctx.effects.adjust_capacity(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name", "skyway_window_committed", need);
    true
}

// A climber reaching the top — or not. THE CLOSE RULE IS THIS BRANCH, and it is
// one `if`: the window's state at the moment the lift would land is what decides
// whether it landed.
fn land_lift(ctx, claim_id, served_flag, stood_down_flag) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open > 0 {
        ctx.flags[served_flag] = 1;
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_lifts_landed", 1);
        return;
    }
    // Stood down at the head. The claimant is not served, and the committed row
    // gives their share back — the manifest at the end of the act says what
    // actually went up, not what was asked for.
    ctx.flags[stood_down_flag] = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_window_lifts_aborted", 1);
    ctx.effects.adjust_capacity(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        "skyway_window_committed",
        -ctx.flags[claim_id],
    );
}

// ── The window closes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn on_transfer_window_closes(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_open = 0;
    ctx.flags.skyway_window_closed = 1;

    // The lift on offer goes with the window: the row reads nothing, because
    // there is nothing left to offer. Through the latch rather than off the
    // banked supply, because since #1340 the chain failing under everybody can
    // lower this row on its own — subtracting a figure derived from what the
    // chain COULD do at the opening would drive the panel below zero on exactly
    // the road where it had already been marked down. It is the row's own last
    // move; nothing raises it again.
    publish_window_available(ctx, 0);

    // Closing the window cannot make the protected allocation decision for the
    // crew. A human booking already resolved this optional good-ending
    // objective at the booking seam; an untouched window stays red, visibly
    // distinct from the mandatory spine.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_lifts_started == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-window");
    }

    // The receiving manifold is mission machinery, not an asset the campaign
    // can inherit. Its job ends with this one window, so close the entity's
    // lifecycle before the terminal snapshot is projected.
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.window_transfer_manifold.name");
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: "window_closes",
    });
}

fn window_closes(ctx) { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_closes", responses: [] } }

// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ACT 3 — WHO GOES UP, WHO STAYS, AND WHAT THE MISSION HANDS ON (issue #1043)
// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
//
// THE SCENE THE WHOLE MISSION EXISTS FOR. Everything above this line is the
// situation: a slipping tether, a rung nobody will work, a storm, a file that
// does not say what it claims to say, and a window whose arithmetic does not
// come out. This band is the captain being asked to decide which of three
// parties is left on the rock, and then being shown what that cost.
//
// ── THE CONSTRAINT IS THE LEDGER, NOT THE DIALOGUE ──────────────────────────
//
// Nothing below counts to two. Every "take them up" line in these trees EXISTS
// only while `window_room` — #1042's banked `skyway_window_supply` minus its
// `skyway_window_reserved` — still covers that claimant's authored claim, and
// picking it pulls that slice's own booking seam rather than doing anything
// itself. So the option disappears when the lift runs out, the seam refuses it
// again on the far side if it somehow got through (#1042 keeps two refusal
// counters for exactly that), and re-authoring the three claims or the ladder's
// throughput changes how many fit with not one line of this band edited. "Pick
// two" is nowhere in this file, in either half of it.
//
// ── THREE CLAIMANTS, THREE CHANNELS ─────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Each party asks for itself, from its own hull, in its own words: the workers
// who know what the record says, the operator's people who will still be
// running the depot chain next time anybody comes through here, and a civilian
// convoy with a bigger claim than either and nothing at all to trade. The three
// threads are independent — none is behind another's answer — and each carries
// the same three shapes of reply: hold, take them up, leave them.
//
// ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, for `havelock_offer`'s reason and `head_node`'s. A hull
// whose Tactical seat is AI-backfilled answers an open thread with its FIRST
// response, so index 0 has to be the answer an officer who is not there should
// give. Here that is HOLD: an empty chair must not be able to decide who rides
// the storm out. A hold is answered with a terminal node and ONE call-back
// twenty-two seconds later, so a backfilled bridge produces at most two
// messages per claimant and then stops asking.
//
// ── THE OPERATOR'S CHANNEL CARRIES THE OTHER CONVERSATION ───────────────────
//
// Havelock's thread is where the confrontation lands, because Havelock are who
// the evidence is about. Filing is not an option on this channel: only Control's
// fixed, range-gated response can put the evidence bundle on its record and keep
// `skyway_surface_records`.
//
//   CONFRONT         available only when `skyway_confront_unlocked` is up: the
//                    record AND somebody who was on the arm. It comes in two
//                    forms, and the difference between them is a promise. A
//                    captain who names Tacket to the operator she works for
//                    leaves `skyway_protect_witness` to break at mission close;
//                    a captain who says "I have a witness and you do not get
//                    their name" leaves it to be kept there.
//
// Both outlive the lift decision — the node re-presents itself after every pick
// — because "are you giving us a berth" and "do you know what your own file
// says" are two different conversations that happen to be on one channel.
//
// ── THE SMALLER, WORSE SCENE (the early collapse) ───────────────────────────
//
// A crew who arrive at the window with no lift in it get a DIFFERENT scene, not
// a quieter version of this one. There is no parley at the ladder, because there
// is nothing at the ladder to parley about and — on the collapse road — the ship
// is in a debris field pulling people out of it at priority 85. What there is
// instead is Ladder A's one mooring, and the captain does not talk to the three
// of them about it: the three of them send one short plea each, delivered
// wherever the ship happens to be, and the ALLOCATION is a name given to Skyway
// Control on Control's own channel. One node, one berth, and the fourth option
// on it is giving it to nobody.
//
// That is the shape the situation actually has. It is shorter, it is colder, it
// costs the captain a conversation they do not get to have, and the difference
// is authored rather than described.
//
// [ai] IT KEYS ON THE NUMBER, NOT ON THE COLLAPSE. `skyway_window_supply <= 0`
// is the seam, so the scene is also what a crew get who kept the head standing
// and let it fall out of lift certification — the head is still there, still
// talking, and still cannot run a climber. Naming `skyway_skyhook_lost` here
// would have made the head's fate the gate; the fate is a separate campaign
// family, and the endings say it separately.
//
// ── WHAT RIDING IT OUT COSTS: READ, NEVER ROLLED ────────────────────────────
//
// `storm_cost` is #1036's casualty rule and #1040's, applied a third time. Every
// term is a fact the crew could have known at the time and every one of them is
// a flag something earlier in this mission wrote — the head's fate, whether the
// rung is moving, how the strike ended, whether the picket is still a hull, and
// whether the corridor's shelter run has already failed once. Nothing is
// randomised, because this script has no RNG and should not have one.
//
// The result reaches the crew on the LEFT-BEHIND PARTY'S OWN CHANNEL, not in a
// closing crawl. A crew who left the workers behind after promising them the
// corridor hear it from the workers, and hear the promise said back to them in
// its own terms.
//
// ── THE ENDING IS COMPOSED, NOT ENUMERATED ──────────────────────────────────
//
// [ai] JUDGEMENT CALL, and the same one `head_casualties` makes. A literal
// cross-product of pair-choice x strike path x evidence state x skyhook fate is
// thirty-six bodies of copy, most of which no run would ever reach, and every
// one of them would have to be re-written by hand when the tuning pass moves a
// number. So the ending is a SEQUENCE of statements, each read off the state
// that produced it and each authored once: the headline says which pair went up,
// the left-behind channels say what that cost and to whom, the fact sheet says
// what became of the record and what became of the captain's word, and #1040's
// own epilogue has already said what became of the structure. Every combination
// produces a distinct set of statements; no combination needs its own string.
//
// ── THE SEVEN FAMILIES THIS MISSION HANDS FORWARD ───────────────────────────
//
// Written in ONE place, `write_the_campaign_record`, under a `campaign.skyway.`
// prefix so a later mission can find them without knowing this file:
//
//   passage      who went up, who was left, who was refused to their face, and
//                how many the window carried
//   strike       negotiated / forced / never resolved — exactly one
//   evidence     none / records / corroborated — exactly one — plus whether it
//                was filed, put to Havelock, and whether a name went with it
//   casualties   the picket, the head and the storm, and their sum
//   skyhook      held / lost, mirroring the pair #1040 guarantees
//   commitments  how many promises were kept and how many broken
//   traffic      the storm's civilian losses, aggregate and per craft
//
// They live in the ordinary `FlagStore`, which is censused and snapshotted
// already, so this slice registers no new authoritative state and adds no Rust.
// `pasm/spec/architecture/world-files.yaml`'s `campaign-flag-handoff-state`
// describes the handoff and names the types that carry it.
//
// ── [ai] THE BAND'S REMAINING TUNABLES, ALL UNRATIFIED ──────────────────────
//
//   [22] s   how long a claimant waits before calling back once, on a window
//            that is 200 seconds long. Long enough that holding is a real
//            decision with a cost, short enough that a captain who put them off
//            to deal with something else gets one more chance.
//   [3] s    the pause before a granted lift reprices the other two screens. It
//            has to clear the seam's own one-tick booking; everything past that
//            is pacing.
//   [26] s   how long the endings wait after the shutters come down. This one
//            is DERIVED rather than chosen — #1042 gives a climber 24 seconds to
//            reach the top — and it moves with that number rather than on its
//            own.
//   [68]/[66]  the parley's and the choice's objective priorities, one and two
//            rungs above #1042's window objective (65). The tether ladder's
//            60/70/80 are resolved seventy-two seconds before the window opens, so
//            nothing live outranks them; a tuning pass that lengthens Act 3 has
//            to check that again.
//   [75]/[5] what the workers make of a captain who carries them and of one who
//            tells them to their face that they are staying. The second is
//            #1036's force-open floor deliberately: being told is not a smaller
//            thing than being cleared off a rung.
//   [5]      what Havelock make of a captain who reads their own file back to
//            them in front of the authority that licenses them.

on_world_loaded("moor_the_claimants");
on_flag_set("skyway_storm_passed", "on_the_corridor_marshals");
on_flag_set("skyway_window_open", "on_the_choice_opens");
on_flag_set("skyway_window_closed", "on_the_window_shuts_for_good");

// The convoy's own hull, watched apart from #1037's four-craft canary: this band
// asks a question about THIS craft — can it still speak for itself — and
// `a2_traffic_lost` cannot answer it, because a dead hauler somewhere else in
// the corridor would suppress a claimant who is perfectly fine.
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name", "on_convoy_lost");

// The berth's three seams, on #1042's booking pattern and for its reasons: one
// flag per claimant rather than one taking a name, single-shot because an
// allocation IS the decision, and one place where the request is granted or
// refused against the live ledger.
on_flag_set("skyway_berth_ask_committee", "on_berth_ask_committee");
on_flag_set("skyway_berth_ask_havelock", "on_berth_ask_havelock");
on_flag_set("skyway_berth_ask_convoy", "on_berth_ask_convoy");

// Losing the hull changes what is feasible without anybody having picked
// anything, so it moves whichever ledger this act routed into (#1340).
// `the_ledger_moved` carries the window guard and the scene guard both, so a
// convoy lost before Act 3 — or in the berth scene, where there is no lift board
// to move — reaches the right board or none at all.
fn on_convoy_lost(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost = 1;
    // …AND THE CLAIM GOES WITH THE HULL (#1340). A request the corridor removes
    // is neither a refusal nor a silence, and this is the only place that fact
    // can be recorded: the comms engine takes a despawned sender's whole thread
    // out of reach the moment the entity is gone — every response on it is
    // stamped unavailable because its sender is out of range for good — so a
    // captain who had not yet answered this claimant CANNOT answer it now. No
    // grant, no refusal, not ever. Scoring that as an unanswered request would
    // fail a crew for a conversation the engine closed under them, and would
    // fail them for exactly the road where they were fighting the thing that
    // killed the convoy.
    //
    // A SEPARATE FLAG rather than clearing `skyway_claim_asked_convoy`, because
    // the ask really did happen and the record of it is worth keeping: the
    // debrief, the campaign row and any later reading of this act can still see
    // that three parties spoke. `resolve_the_choice` is the one place that has
    // to leave it out of the count.
    //
    // Only while the claim is still open. A convoy that was granted or refused
    // before the corridor took it was ANSWERED, and an answer already given is
    // not unmade by what happens to the hull afterwards — that decision is the
    // captain's and it stands.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_convoy > 0 &&
       !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_convoy", "skyway_refused_convoy") {
        ctx.flags.skyway_claim_lost_convoy = 1;
    }
    the_ledger_moved(ctx);
}

// ── Moored means moored ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// TWO HULLS THAT ARE NOT GOING ANYWHERE, told so on the first tick.
//
// The committee's picket boat and the rigger's skiff are civilian haulers with
// no `[civilian] route` and no `[behaviour]` block of their own, and a hull with
// neither drifts: measured off this world's own trace, the committee were 1,631
// units up the corridor from their mooring by the time the transfer window
// opened. That is not cosmetic. The destroyer's authored comms range is 1000 and
// a hauler's is 900, a transmission goes through at the SMALLER of the two, and
// #1043's scene is a captain standing off the ladder answering these people. A
// claimant who has quietly flown out of range cannot be answered, cannot be
// refused, and cannot be told what was decided about them.
//
// THE VERB IS `order_divert_anchor` AND NOT `order_hold`, and the difference is
// the whole fix rather than a preference. `Hold` is "no helm-relevant directive
// at all", which is EXACTLY the state these two are already in and exactly what
// they drift out of; measured, it moves them not one unit. An anchor order is an
// `AiDirective::Reach` at the mooring they are sitting on, so the helm has
// something to actuate to zero against — the same thing the shipped combat hulls
// get from a `hold-station` doctrine entry and that a template with no
// `[behaviour]` block cannot give. It is also why this is authored in script
// rather than as an `[entity.overrides] behaviour` on the two rows: the hauler
// template declares no `[behaviour]`, so there is no section for an instance
// override to edit, and the civilian traffic tick is the thing that owns these
// hulls' one doctrine entry in any case.
//
// Issued at WORLD LOAD rather than when the scene needs it, because these two
// are moored in Act 1's fiction and were moored before anybody sent a destroyer.
// It is the same reading `file_the_ladder_b_record` takes of the operator's
// file: the world stating its own opening state on the tick it loads.
//
// It is a REQUEST like any other civilian order, so it runs through the same
// acknowledge-and-decide delay and the same authored disposition — a hauler that
// refused orders would refuse this one, and the honest consequence would be a
// claimant who really did wander off.
fn moor_the_claimants(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.order_divert_anchor(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name", "worker_mooring");
    ctx.effects.order_divert_anchor(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.rigger_tacket.name", "rigger_mooring");
}

// ── The corridor marshals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The window is announced, so the traffic that wants a lift comes to where the
// lift is. One ordinary #1028 divert onto the LADDER RUN — the route the depot
// shuttle already flies, so no new lane is authored for a queue — and it is the
// convoy alone, because the other two claimants have been moored at Ladder B
// since before the crew arrived.
//
// Twenty seconds after the act opens rather than on the same beat, so #1037's
// close gets to put the corridor back to work first and this is a craft peeling
// off a working lane rather than two orders arguing on one tick. That leaves it
// a hundred and twelve seconds to close, which is comfortably more than the
// sixty-odd a bulk hauler at its authored twelve units a second needs to get
// from the far end of the lane to inside comms range of the ladder.
fn on_the_corridor_marshals(ctx) {
    ctx.schedule.after(20, |ctx| { marshal_the_convoy(ctx); });
}

fn marshal_the_convoy(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost > 0 { return; }
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name", "ladder_run");
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_convoy_marshalled", 1);
}

// ── The window opens, and the choice with it ────────────────────────────────
//
// Chained off the flag #1042's deadline handler writes rather than off the
// deadline itself, which is the `skyway_strike_settled` device again: the supply
// figure this band reads is banked by that handler, and a flag transition is a
// tick behind the call that wrote it, so by the time this runs the arithmetic is
// done and on the panel.
//
// TWO SECONDS LATER, and the delay is doing two jobs. Control's own announcement
// gets to be the news before three parties start asking, which is the order the
// scene reads in; and a beat that opened threads on the same tick as that
// announcement would be racing it on every console that shows the newest message
// first.
fn on_the_choice_opens(ctx) {
    ctx.schedule.after(2, |ctx| { the_claimants_ask(ctx); });
}

fn the_claimants_ask(ctx) {
    // Whatever is left of the corridor's traffic is called back in. #1040's
    // collapse handler puts the lane onto the holding run when the head goes,
    // which is right — there is nothing to queue for — and this is the answer
    // to that: there is one thing left to queue for, and it is down here.
    marshal_the_convoy(ctx);

    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_supply > 0 {
        the_parley_at_the_ladder(ctx);
    } else {
        the_last_berth(ctx);
    }
}

// ── The full scene: three claimants, and lift for two ───────────────────────

fn the_parley_at_the_ladder(ctx) {
    // TWO OBJECTIVES FOR ONE BEAT, split on the approach/work line for the
    // fourth time in this file and for the same reason every time:
    // `detect_reached_objective_completion` completes any objective whose Reach
    // anchor an AI-flown helm arrives at, so the one that carries the flying
    // cannot also be the one that records the deciding.
    //
    // `ladder_transit` is where the ship has to be, and that is arithmetic
    // rather than staging: the destroyer's authored comms range is 1000, a
    // civilian hauler's is 900 and the operator's cutter's is 800, and a
    // transmission goes through at the SMALLER of the two. From the act's own
    // station-keeping berth the committee are 947 units off and the cutter 1097
    // — so a crew who never close cannot answer either of them. From the transit
    // leg all three claimants and the witness are inside every one of those
    // numbers. Closing is helm's job, the objective names it, and a backfilled
    // helm flies it.
    //
    // Priority 68, above #1042's window objective (65) and below nothing that is
    // still live: the tether ladder's rungs resolved with the head's fate
    // seventy-two seconds before the window opened, which is the whole point of the
    // order those two deadlines are authored in.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-parley",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.parley.text",
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 68,
        directive_kind: "Reach",
        directive_anchor: "ladder_transit",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name"],
    });
    // …and the decision carries NO directive, for #1042's reason: there is
    // nowhere to fly in order to choose who is left behind.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-choice",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.choice.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 66,
        targets: [
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
            "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
        ],
    });

    // WHO ACTUALLY ASKED, latched as they ask (#1340). `resolve_the_choice`
    // scores the captain on the requests that reached them, and a claimant the
    // corridor lost before the parley never put one — counting a party who
    // could not speak as an unanswered request would fail a crew for silence
    // that was never theirs.
    // ONE THREAD PER CLAIMANT, and it is load-bearing rather than cosmetic
    // (#1343). A claim is asked once here, asked AGAIN twenty-two seconds after
    // a hold (`call_the_committee_back` and its two siblings), and re-asked at a
    // new price every time the board moves (`reprice_the_other_claims`) — four
    // roads to what is, to everyone in the room, one conversation about one
    // corridor slot. Naming the thread is what makes the runtime agree: the
    // client groups the thread, the inbox's live-thread reading takes the
    // LATEST message on it, and `console::comms::server::message_is_superseded`
    // cancels an unmanned console's pending choice on every earlier message of
    // the thread. Leave these off and a backfilled bridge answers the claim AND
    // its repricing separately, which is two answers to one question.
    ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_committee = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
        node_fn: "committee_claims",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-committee",
        urgent: true,
    });
    ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_havelock = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
        node_fn: "havelock_claims",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-havelock",
        urgent: true,
    });
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_convoy = 1;
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
            node_fn: "convoy_claims",
            thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-convoy",
            urgent: true,
        });
    }
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_parley_open", 1);
}

// What is still unspoken for, read off #1042's ledger rather than off Control's
// panel row — the counter a capacity mirrors onto is re-published by the
// infrastructure tick, so a row read inside the same tick as a booking is a tick
// stale. These two flags land between calls.
// `window_deliverable` rather than the banked supply since #1340: a chain that
// stopped delivering after the shutters went up cannot be offered against, and
// the same subtraction is what `book_lift` grants against — one arithmetic, so
// the option the crew are shown and the answer they get cannot disagree.
fn window_room(ctx) {
    window_deliverable(ctx) - ctx.flags.skyway_window_reserved
}

fn claim_decided(ctx, granted_flag, refused_flag) {
    ctx.flags[granted_flag] > 0 || ctx.flags[refused_flag] > 0
}

// ── What is still standing, and what still fits (issue #1340) ───────────────
//
// A claim is STANDING when it is still a thing the captain can answer with a
// lift: nobody has answered it, and there is still somebody there to answer.
// The convoy is the one claimant this corridor can lose outright, and a hull
// that is gone is neither a refusal nor an unanswered request — there is nobody
// left to put on a climber.
fn committee_standing(ctx) {
    !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_committee", "skyway_refused_committee")
}
fn havelock_standing(ctx) {
    !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_havelock", "skyway_refused_havelock")
}
fn convoy_standing(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0 &&
    !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_convoy", "skyway_refused_convoy")
}

// THE SHAPE OF THE CHOICE AS IT STANDS, in one word, and there are six of them
// because there are six things Control can truthfully say about this board — a
// crew who are in one of those states should not be read another one's
// sentence. Derived from the live ledger every time it is asked, never from a
// figure banked at the opening, so a rung that went under between the
// announcement and the answer changes the sentence as well as the option.
//
//   `none`            nothing still standing fits what is left. There is no
//                     lift to give anybody, whatever anybody asks.
//   `sole_*`          exactly one claim fits, and it is THAT one. The most
//                     specific thing the act can say, and the one that has to
//                     name a party.
//   `one`             several fit on their own but no two fit together. One
//                     name, and the captain picks which.
//   `particular`      some pairings fit and some do not. This is where the
//                     arithmetic stops being "any two" and starts being a
//                     choice about WHICH two.
//   `any_pair`        every pairing still standing fits, and the board is no
//                     longer the three the act opened with — somebody has been
//                     answered, or the corridor took one of them.
//   `undecided`       the same board, with all three claims still on it and
//                     nobody answered. The opening state of the choice,
//                     restated, and its body counts the three out loud.
fn window_shape(ctx) {
    let room = window_room(ctx);
    let c = committee_standing(ctx);
    let h = havelock_standing(ctx);
    let v = convoy_standing(ctx);
    let cn = ctx.flags["skyway_claim_committee"];
    let hn = ctx.flags["skyway_claim_havelock"];
    let vn = ctx.flags["skyway_claim_convoy"];

    let c_fits = c && cn <= room;
    let h_fits = h && hn <= room;
    let v_fits = v && vn <= room;

    let fits = 0;
    if c_fits { fits += 1; }
    if h_fits { fits += 1; }
    if v_fits { fits += 1; }

    if fits == 0 { return "none"; }
    if fits == 1 {
        if c_fits { return "sole_committee"; }
        if h_fits { return "sole_havelock"; }
        return "sole_convoy";
    }

    // The pairings, over the claims still standing. `all` counts the pairs the
    // scene still HAS; `fit` counts the ones the ledger can honour.
    let all = 0;
    let fit = 0;
    if c && h { all += 1; if cn + hn <= room { fit += 1; } }
    if c && v { all += 1; if cn + vn <= room { fit += 1; } }
    if h && v { all += 1; if hn + vn <= room { fit += 1; } }

    if fit == 0 { return "one"; }
    if fit < all { return "particular"; }
    // THE OPENING STATE IS THREE CLAIMS, not merely an unanswered one. Its body
    // says the number "is any two of the claims standing against it and not the
    // three", so a board with two claimants on it is a board that sentence is
    // false about — and the corridor can take the convoy before the parley ever
    // opens its thread, which leaves exactly that board with nothing decided on
    // it. Standing already carries the decision (a claim that was answered is not
    // standing), so this is the whole of the test: three of them, all still
    // waiting. Anything else is `any_pair`, whose body names whoever is left
    // rather than counting them.
    if c && h && v { return "undecided"; }
    "any_pair"
}

// Control's restatement of its own manifest, one body per shape. Terminal — no
// responses — for `window_opens_short`'s reason: the allocation is answered on
// the claimants' own threads, and a status line a backfilled console could
// answer would be a second way to spend the window.
fn window_stands(ctx) {
    let shape = window_shape(ctx);
    let body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_none";
    if shape == "sole_committee" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_sole_committee";
    } else if shape == "sole_havelock" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_sole_havelock";
    } else if shape == "sole_convoy" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_sole_convoy";
    } else if shape == "one" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_one";
    } else if shape == "particular" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_particular";
    } else if shape == "any_pair" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_any_pair";
    } else if shape == "undecided" {
        body = "world.falling_skyway.comms.window_stands_undecided";
    }
    // A room that has gone negative is a chain that failed under climbers
    // already on the ribbon. There is nothing left to offer either way, and a
    // manifest reading a minus figure is a bug on a panel rather than news.
    let room = window_room(ctx);
    if room < 0 { room = 0; }
    #{ message: body, params: #{ available: room }, responses: [] }
}

// ── The board moved ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// ONE ENTRY POINT for every reason the ledger can change, which is the whole of
// #1340's second criterion. A grant spends lift; a rung going under, a shift
// walking off, the head losing its certification or the convoy's own hull being
// destroyed all change what is feasible without anybody picking anything. Before
// this they had one trigger between them — a grant — so a window that got poorer
// on its own left three threads describing a chain that no longer existed.
//
// It republishes the manifest row as well as the copy: the panel is where a
// captain reads what is on offer, and a row that still says 40 after the ladder
// stopped is the same lie in a different place.
//
// GUARDED ON THE MARK, and that guard is what lets every trigger call this
// unconditionally. Two triggers landing on one tick would otherwise open the
// same three threads twice and publish the same absolute row twice — and an
// absolute publish computes its delta from a level the infrastructure tick has
// not re-mirrored yet, so the second one would move the row again by the whole
// of the first one's delta. One mark, checked before anything is spent.
fn board_mark(ctx) {
    window_room(ctx) * 2 + ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost
}

fn the_board_moved(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    let mark = board_mark(ctx);
    // THE SCENE THIS DESCRIBES, AND ONLY THAT ONE. `skyway_window_open` says the
    // shutters are up; it does not say there is a parley behind them. Two states
    // have the flag set and no board to move:
    //
    //   the berth scene, where `the_claimants_ask` routed to `the_last_berth`
    //   because the chain delivers nothing. There is no lift board, no repricing
    //   to do, and the claim threads carry no lift responses to reprice — and
    //   `committee_reprices` / `havelock_reprices` would open parley trees whose
    //   live `deny_*` responses collide with the berth scene's own refusals.
    //
    //   the two seconds between the shutters going up and the claimants speaking,
    //   where "the board has moved" is news about a board nobody has been shown.
    //
    // The mark is banked either way, so the opening announcement is measured
    // against what the ledger says when the room is finally told, not against
    // what it said before the room existed.
    //
    // THE ROW IS STILL BROUGHT TO THE LIVE FIGURE, and that is the half this
    // guard must not swallow (#1340). Having no board to move is a reason not to
    // SPEAK; it is not a reason to leave Control's manifest reading a number the
    // chain stopped being able to deliver. Banking the mark without republishing
    // would strand the row for the whole window — the mark says the movement has
    // been dealt with, so the watch three seconds later finds nothing to notice —
    // and "a row that still says 40 after the ladder stopped" is the same lie
    // this function exists to stop telling. The publisher is latched, so a
    // republish that agrees with the row emits nothing; in the berth scene the
    // chain delivers zero and the row is already there, so this is a no-op by
    // arithmetic rather than by a second guard.
    let room = window_room(ctx);
    if room < 0 { room = 0; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_only > 0 || ctx.flags.a3_parley_open == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_board_marked = 1;
        ctx.flags.skyway_board_seen = mark;
        publish_window_available(ctx, room);
        return;
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_board_marked > 0 && mark == ctx.flags.skyway_board_seen { return; }
    ctx.flags.skyway_board_marked = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_board_seen = mark;

    publish_window_available(ctx, room);
    reprice_the_other_claims(ctx);
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: "window_stands",
    });
}

// The berth scene's own ledger movement, on `the_board_moved`'s pattern and for
// its reason (#1340). One mooring, three names and a hull the corridor can lose,
// so this board moves for two reasons: a rung going under after Control has
// asked for a name, and the convoy being destroyed while its line is still on
// the offer. Both change which names are executable, and the offer is redrawn
// from the live ledger when either does.
fn berth_mark(ctx) {
    berth_room(ctx) * 2 + ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost
}

fn the_berth_moved(ctx) {
    let mark = berth_mark(ctx);
    if mark == ctx.flags.skyway_berth_seen { return; }
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_seen = mark;
    // A settled berth is not repriced. The mark is still banked above, so a
    // scene that moves twice after the decision stays silent both times.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided > 0 { return; }
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: "control_berth_offer",
    });
}

// ONE DOOR for every reason either of Act 3's two ledgers can move, and the only
// thing in the act that decides WHICH ledger a caller meant (#1340). A loss, a
// grant and the periodic watch all come through here, so none of them has to
// know which scene the window routed into.
fn the_ledger_moved(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_only > 0 {
        the_berth_moved(ctx);
    } else {
        the_board_moved(ctx);
    }
}

// The watch itself, three seconds at a time for as long as the window is open.
//
// A WATCH RATHER THAN A HANDLER PER LOSS, and that is the point: the supply
// arithmetic reads a head certification, two operational thresholds, two
// workforce stoppages and two published rung capacities, and a scene that hooked
// each of those separately would be seven registrations that go stale the moment
// somebody tunes the chain. This asks the arithmetic what it says NOW and
// notices when the answer is different, so any future term in `window_supply` is
// covered the day it is authored.
//
// It says nothing on a board that has not moved — `the_board_moved`'s own mark
// does that — so a quiet window is a silent one. Supply can only fall, and only
// through a small set of authored values, so the message count stays bounded
// whether a person or a backfilled console is answering.
fn watch_the_manifest(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    the_ledger_moved(ctx);
    ctx.schedule.after(3, |ctx| { watch_the_manifest(ctx); });
}

// A DIALOGUE NODE IS BUILT ONCE AND ANSWERED LATER, and this act is the first
// place in the mission where that matters: three threads open together against
// one ledger, so the moment a lift is granted, whatever is still on the other
// two screens is describing a window that has moved. The parties notice — they
// are watching the same manifest the captain is — and say so, and the node they
// say it on is rebuilt from the ledger as it stands now.
//
// Three seconds out from a grant, because the seam's booking lands a tick after
// the pick that set it and `skyway_window_reserved` has to have moved before a
// repricing can mean anything. The claimant who was just granted is skipped by
// `claim_decided`, so this only ever reaches parties who are still waiting on
// an answer.
//
// CALLED THROUGH `the_board_moved` since #1340, never directly, so that a grant
// and the chain failing under everybody reach these three threads by the same
// road and its mark bounds how often they hear about it. A window can hold two
// grants and its supply can only fall, and only through a small set of authored
// values, so the message count stays bounded whether a person or a backfilled
// console is answering.
fn reprice_the_other_claims(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    if !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_committee", "skyway_refused_committee") {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            node_fn: "committee_reprices",
            thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-committee",
        });
    }
    if !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_havelock", "skyway_refused_havelock") {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
            node_fn: "havelock_reprices",
            thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-havelock",
        });
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0 &&
       !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_convoy", "skyway_refused_convoy") {
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
            node_fn: "convoy_reprices",
            thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-convoy",
        });
    }
}

fn committee_reprices(ctx) { committee_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_reprices") }
fn havelock_reprices(ctx)  { havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_reprices") }
fn convoy_reprices(ctx)    { convoy_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_reprices") }

// WHAT AN EMPTY CHAIR DOES WITH A CLAIM (#1343). Every response on the three
// lift nodes carries `ai_weight` and `ai_delay_seconds`, and the three tables
// are deliberately identical: five seconds of silence, then grant or refuse with
// equal weight, never the hold.
//
// THE HOLD IS WEIGHT ZERO AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. It has to be index 0 —
// it is what a person reaches for while they think — and the backfill policy
// every hull authors answers by index, so before this the act's three claims
// would all have been stood by for ever and the window would have closed on
// nobody. Zero forbids it outright rather than making it merely unlikely.
//
// AND THE FIVE SECONDS ARE NOT DECORATION: `reprice_the_other_claims` reopens
// these threads on a three-second beat while the board moves, so a console that
// answered on sight would spend the window inside one watch tick. A pause longer
// than the beat means an unmanned bridge decides against a ledger that has
// settled, exactly as a crew reading the manifest would.
//
// THAT ONLY HOLDS BECAUSE THE REPRICING SHARES THE CLAIM'S THREAD. A reprice is
// a NEW message — it does not edit the one already on the screen — so the old
// node stays live and answerable beside it, and a wait still running on the old
// one is cancelled only because `message_is_superseded` can see the two are the
// same conversation. The `thread_id` on every one of these opens is what it
// sees; without it an empty chair answers the pre-move node and the repriced
// node both, and one claimant is decided twice.
//
// The confrontation options on Havelock's node author NOTHING, which keeps them
// out of the pool entirely — the comment there already said that was the last
// thing a backfilled console should reach for, and now it is structurally true.
fn committee_claims(ctx) { committee_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_claims") }

fn committee_node(ctx, body) {
    let responses = [];
    if !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_committee", "skyway_refused_committee") {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.claim_stand_by",
            on_pick: "on_committee_hold",
            ai_weight: 0,
            ai_delay_seconds: 5,
        });
        if window_room(ctx) >= ctx.flags["skyway_claim_committee"] {
            responses.push(#{
                text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lift_committee",
                on_pick: "on_lift_committee",
                important: true,
                ai_weight: 1,
                ai_delay_seconds: 5,
            });
        }
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.deny_committee",
            on_pick: "on_deny_committee",
            important: true,
            ai_weight: 1,
            ai_delay_seconds: 5,
        });
    }
    #{ message: body, responses: responses }
}

fn on_committee_hold(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_held_committee", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_held_committee == 1 {
        ctx.schedule.after(22, |ctx| { call_the_committee_back(ctx); });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_waits", responses: [] }
}

fn call_the_committee_back(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    if claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_committee", "skyway_refused_committee") { return; }
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
        node_fn: "committee_claims",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-committee",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

fn on_lift_committee(ctx) {
    // The guard for the seconds between a ledger moving and the repricing above
    // reaching this screen. It re-reads the ledger rather than trusting the
    // options this node was rendered with, and the body it falls back to is the
    // repricing's own — which is the right sentence either way: the board moved.
    if window_room(ctx) < ctx.flags["skyway_claim_committee"] {
        return committee_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_reprices");
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_granted_committee = 1;
    // #1042's seam. The booking is granted or refused against the live ledger in
    // ONE place, a tick from now; this pick does not move a capacity itself.
    ctx.flags.skyway_book_committee = 1;
    // [ai] Unratified. Giving these people the corridor after six weeks of
    // nobody giving them anything is worth more than either promise was.
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", 75);
    ctx.schedule.after(3, |ctx| { the_ledger_moved(ctx); });
    committee_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_lifting")
}

fn on_deny_committee(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_committee = 1;
    // [ai] Unratified, and it is the floor #1036's force-open uses: told to
    // their faces that they are staying is not a smaller thing than being
    // cleared off a rung.
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("skyway_workers", 5);
    committee_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_denied")
}

// ── The operator ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn havelock_claims(ctx) { havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_claims") }

fn havelock_node(ctx, body) {
    let decided = claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_havelock", "skyway_refused_havelock");
    let can_confront = ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized == 0 &&
        ctx.flags.skyway_confront_unlocked > 0 && ctx.flags.skyway_confronted == 0;

    let responses = [];
    // Index 0 stays the hold for as long as there is anything on this node at
    // all — including a node whose only remaining options are the confrontation,
    // which is the last thing a backfilled console should be able to reach for.
    if !decided || can_confront {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.claim_stand_by",
            on_pick: "on_havelock_hold",
            ai_weight: 0,
            ai_delay_seconds: 5,
        });
    }
    if !decided {
        if window_room(ctx) >= ctx.flags["skyway_claim_havelock"] {
            responses.push(#{
                text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lift_havelock",
                on_pick: "on_lift_havelock",
                important: true,
                ai_weight: 1,
                ai_delay_seconds: 5,
            });
        }
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.deny_havelock",
            on_pick: "on_deny_havelock",
            important: true,
            ai_weight: 1,
            ai_delay_seconds: 5,
        });
    }
    if can_confront {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.confront_unnamed",
            on_pick: "on_confront_unnamed",
            important: true,
        });
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.confront_named",
            on_pick: "on_confront_named",
            important: true,
        });
    }
    #{ message: body, responses: responses }
}

fn on_havelock_hold(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_held_havelock", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_held_havelock == 1 {
        ctx.schedule.after(22, |ctx| { call_havelock_back(ctx); });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_waits", responses: [] }
}

fn call_havelock_back(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    if claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_havelock", "skyway_refused_havelock") { return; }
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
        node_fn: "havelock_claims",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-havelock",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

fn on_lift_havelock(ctx) {
    if window_room(ctx) < ctx.flags["skyway_claim_havelock"] {
        return havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_reprices");
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_granted_havelock = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_book_havelock = 1;
    ctx.schedule.after(3, |ctx| { the_ledger_moved(ctx); });
    havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_lifting")
}

fn on_deny_havelock(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_havelock = 1;
    havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_denied")
}

// THE CONFRONTATION, and the promise inside it. #1039 left `obj-a3-confront`
// posted and Active for this beat to resolve; both forms resolve it, and the
// difference between them is whether Havelock hear Tacket's name. The protection
// promise remains open through this handler; mission close settles it against
// `skyway_witness_named`.
fn on_confront_unnamed(ctx) { confront_havelock(ctx, false) }
fn on_confront_named(ctx)   { confront_havelock(ctx, true) }

fn confront_havelock(ctx, name_the_witness) {
    // A retained confrontation response may outlive the mission. The campaign
    // and debrief are frozen once finalisation begins, so reject it before any
    // objective, dossier, disposition or relationship mutation.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_stands_off", responses: [] };
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_confronted = 1;
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-confront");
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.havelock_confronted",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    });
    // [ai] Unratified. Putting an operator's own file to them in front of the
    // authority that licenses them is the most expensive thing a captain can do
    // to this party, and the number says so.
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("havelock_operations", 5);
    ctx.flags["relationship.havelock_operations.damaged"] = 1;

    if name_the_witness {
        ctx.flags.skyway_witness_named = 1;
        return havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_confronted_named");
    }
    havelock_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_confronted")
}

// ── The convoy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn convoy_claims(ctx) { convoy_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_claims") }

fn convoy_node(ctx, body) {
    let responses = [];
    if !claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_convoy", "skyway_refused_convoy") {
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.claim_stand_by",
            on_pick: "on_convoy_hold",
            ai_weight: 0,
            ai_delay_seconds: 5,
        });
        // `convoy_standing` and not just the ledger (#1340): the corridor can
        // lose this hull outright while its thread is still on a console, and a
        // lift offered to a craft that is no longer there would spend the window
        // on nobody.
        //
        // The refusal below is still built, but nobody can pick it once the hull
        // is gone: the comms engine stamps every response on a despawned
        // sender's thread unavailable, so a claim the corridor removes cannot be
        // closed from the bridge at all. That is what `on_convoy_lost`'s
        // resolved-by-loss latch is for — the claim leaves the count rather than
        // waiting for an answer the engine will not carry. What the refusal line
        // covers is the ordinary case: a node drawn while the convoy was alive
        // and answered before it wasn't.
        if convoy_standing(ctx) && window_room(ctx) >= ctx.flags["skyway_claim_convoy"] {
            responses.push(#{
                text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.lift_convoy",
                on_pick: "on_lift_convoy",
                important: true,
                ai_weight: 1,
                ai_delay_seconds: 5,
            });
        }
        responses.push(#{
            text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.deny_convoy",
            on_pick: "on_deny_convoy",
            important: true,
            ai_weight: 1,
            ai_delay_seconds: 5,
        });
    }
    #{ message: body, responses: responses }
}

fn on_convoy_hold(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_held_convoy", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_held_convoy == 1 {
        ctx.schedule.after(22, |ctx| { call_the_convoy_back(ctx); });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_waits", responses: [] }
}

fn call_the_convoy_back(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost > 0 { return; }
    if claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_convoy", "skyway_refused_convoy") { return; }
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
        node_fn: "convoy_claims",
        thread_id: "falling-skyway-claim-convoy",
        urgent: true,
    });
}

fn on_lift_convoy(ctx) {
    if !convoy_standing(ctx) || window_room(ctx) < ctx.flags["skyway_claim_convoy"] {
        return convoy_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_reprices");
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_granted_convoy = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_book_convoy = 1;
    ctx.schedule.after(3, |ctx| { the_ledger_moved(ctx); });
    convoy_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_lifting")
}

fn on_deny_convoy(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_convoy = 1;
    convoy_node(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_denied")
}

// ── The smaller, worse scene: one berth on the working rung ─────────────────

// What Ladder A can tie up alongside it, under the rule every other supply
// figure in this act obeys: a rung has to be above its own operational line AND
// staffed by people who are at work. A crew who let the working rung go under,
// or who somehow have Havelock's own people out, get nothing at all — which is
// the fourth and worst reading of the act.
fn shelter_supply(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.depot_a_pumping == 0 { return 0; }
    if ctx.flags["workforce.havelock_operations.on_strike"] > 0 { return 0; }
    ctx.flags["depot_a_shelter_berths"]
}

// WHAT IS STILL TIED UP ALONGSIDE, on `window_room`'s rule and for its reason
// (#1340). The banked figure is what Ladder A could offer when the scene opened
// and is the ceiling; the live reading can only lower it, and the reservation
// comes off ONCE.
//
// AND "ONCE" IS THE WHOLE ARITHMETIC HERE, because a booking moves both terms.
// `book_berth` increments `skyway_shelter_reserved` AND takes the mooring off
// Ladder A's own row, which is the row `shelter_supply` reads back — so the live
// reading a moment after an allocation is already the post-allocation figure.
// Subtracting the reservation from THAT would spend one mooring twice: at the
// authored capacity of one it drives the room to -1, which reads the same as
// "nothing left" and hides the bug, and at a tuned capacity of two it would lose
// the second mooring outright and this road would quietly have half the shelter
// its designer authored.
//
// So the reservation is added back before the two are compared, and taken off
// after: the live rung is put back to what it could offer with nothing spoken
// for, capped against the banked ceiling exactly as the window's own ledger is,
// and the allocations come off the result. It is also insensitive to WHEN the
// mirrored row catches up — the capacity delta lands a tick behind the
// reservation, and both orders reach the same figure.
//
// A rung that goes under after Control asks for a name still lowers this, which
// is the case that made the live reading necessary in the first place: it has a
// name and nothing to put it against, and the offer has to say so.
fn berth_room(ctx) {
    let deliverable = ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_supply;
    let live = shelter_supply(ctx) + ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_reserved;
    if live < deliverable { deliverable = live; }
    deliverable - ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_reserved
}

fn the_last_berth(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_only = 1;
