    ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_supply = shelter_supply(ctx);
    // The berth ledger's own mark, on `board_mark`'s pattern: the mooring still
    // unspoken for and whether the corridor still has a convoy in it, as one
    // number. Nothing is reserved yet and the live reading is the banked one on
    // this tick, so what the room is about to be told is exactly what Ladder A
    // can offer.
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_seen = berth_mark(ctx);

    // No approach objective. There is nowhere to go: on the collapse road the
    // ship is in a debris field at priority 85 with people in it, and Skyway
    // Control is inside its own authored 800-unit range of both that field and
    // the act's station-keeping berth. The captain does not have to fly anywhere
    // to give a name over the corridor's own net, and telling them to would be
    // pulling a destroyer off a rescue to attend a formality.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-a3-berth",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.berth.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 66,
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name"],
    });

    // Each of them asks once, from their own hull, and none of them is answered.
    // A message is DELIVERED whatever the range; only a reply has to reach back.
    // That is the scene: three parties calling a ship that is somewhere else,
    // doing something else, with one berth to give away.
    ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_committee = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
        node_fn: "committee_pleads",
        urgent: true,
    });
    ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_havelock = 1;
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
        node_fn: "havelock_pleads",
        urgent: true,
    });
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0 {
        ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_convoy = 1;
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
            node_fn: "convoy_pleads",
            urgent: true,
        });
    }

    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: "control_berth_offer",
        urgent: true,
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_berth_open", 1);
}

fn committee_pleads(ctx) { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_pleads", responses: [] } }
fn havelock_pleads(ctx)  { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_pleads", responses: [] } }
fn convoy_pleads(ctx)    { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_pleads", responses: [] } }

// ONE node, one berth, four names to put on it — and the fourth is nobody.
// Index 0 is the hold, for the whole band's reason.
fn control_berth_offer(ctx) {
    // THE SETTLED READING FIRST, and the order is the point (#1340). Once a name
    // has been given, "the mooring is spoken for" is the true thing to say about
    // this scene and "there is nothing to give anybody" is not — the room is
    // zero BECAUSE the captain filled it, which is a different sentence from a
    // rung that went under with the berth still empty. Asking the room first put
    // the factually wrong body in front of every crew who actually decided.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided > 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.control_berth_settled", responses: [] };
    }
    // Then the live reading since #1340, not the figure banked when the scene
    // opened. `berth_room` counts an allocation once, so this is the honest
    // question — is there a mooring left to offer — rather than a conservative
    // one that happened to land on the right side of zero at a capacity of one.
    if berth_room(ctx) <= 0 {
        return #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.control_no_berth", responses: [] };
    }
    let responses = [
        #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.claim_stand_by", on_pick: "on_berth_hold" },
        #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_to_committee", on_pick: "on_berth_to_committee", important: true },
        #{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_to_havelock", on_pick: "on_berth_to_havelock", important: true },
    ];
    // `convoy_standing` for `convoy_node`'s reason, on the sibling ledger
    // (#1340): the corridor can destroy this hull at any point in the scene, and
    // this offer is rebuilt by the watch and by the hold's own callback with
    // whatever the ledger says then. A mooring given to a craft that is no
    // longer there spends the one berth Ladder A has on nobody — and the ending
    // would then count the convoy as having got out.
    if convoy_standing(ctx) {
        responses.push(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_to_convoy", on_pick: "on_berth_to_convoy", important: true });
    }
    // Refusing everybody is always answerable, whoever is left to refuse.
    responses.push(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_to_nobody", on_pick: "on_berth_to_nobody", important: true });
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.control_berth_offer", responses: responses }
}

fn on_berth_hold(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_held_berth", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_held_berth == 1 {
        ctx.schedule.after(22, |ctx| {
            if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 { return; }
            if ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided > 0 { return; }
            ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
                from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
                node_fn: "control_berth_offer",
                urgent: true,
            });
        });
    }
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_waits", responses: [] }
}

// The three names, each pulling its own seam. `skyway_granted_*` is written here
// because the CAPTAIN's answer is what `obj-a3-choice`'s twin records; whether
// the berth was actually free is the seam's business, a tick from now.
fn on_berth_to_committee(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_granted_committee = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_havelock = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_convoy = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_ask_committee = 1;
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_given_committee", responses: [] }
}

fn on_berth_to_havelock(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_granted_havelock = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_committee = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_convoy = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_ask_havelock = 1;
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_given_havelock", responses: [] }
}

fn on_berth_to_convoy(ctx) {
    // `on_lift_convoy`'s pick-time guard, on the sibling ledger (#1340). A node
    // is built once and answered later, so a hull the corridor lost between the
    // offer being drawn and the name being given is still on a console
    // somewhere. Redraw the offer rather than granting: the captain has not
    // decided anything yet, and the berth is still there for somebody.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost > 0 {
        return control_berth_offer(ctx);
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_granted_convoy = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_committee = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_havelock = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_ask_convoy = 1;
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_given_convoy", responses: [] }
}

// Refusing all three is a decision somebody made, and it is recorded as three
// refusals rather than as an absence — the mission has to be able to tell a
// captain who said no from a captain who never picked up the channel.
fn on_berth_to_nobody(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_decided = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_berth_withheld = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_committee = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_havelock = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_refused_convoy = 1;
    #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.berth_withheld", responses: [] }
}

// `still_there` is the seam's own version of `convoy_standing`'s question, asked
// the only way the seam can ask it: the captain's answer has ALREADY written
// `skyway_granted_*` and the other two refusals by the time this fires, so
// `claim_decided` would call every claimant settled. What is left to ask is
// whether there is a hull to tie up — and the convoy is the one claimant this
// corridor can lose. The other two are on the rock; they cannot go anywhere.
fn on_berth_ask_committee(ctx) { book_berth(ctx, "skyway_berth_committee", true) }
fn on_berth_ask_havelock(ctx)  { book_berth(ctx, "skyway_berth_havelock", true) }
fn on_berth_ask_convoy(ctx)    { book_berth(ctx, "skyway_berth_convoy", ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0) }

// The one place a berth is granted or refused, on `book_lift`'s pattern: the
// ledger flags rather than the panel row, because a capacity's mirrored counter
// is re-published by the infrastructure tick and would be a tick stale here.
// The row itself is moved by an exact delta, so the crew watch the berth leave
// the manifest as it is spoken for.
fn book_berth(ctx, taken_flag, still_there) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_window_open == 0 {
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_berth_refused_shut", 1);
        return;
    }
    // A third wall, recorded like the other two (#1340): there is a mooring and
    // there is a name, and there is no longer anything to put in it. Spending
    // the berth here would have the ending report a destroyed convoy as having
    // got out.
    if !still_there {
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_berth_refused_lost", 1);
        return;
    }
    // `berth_room` since #1340, so the one place a berth is granted asks the
    // same question the offer asked before it drew the three names.
    if berth_room(ctx) <= 0 {
        ctx.flags.increment("skyway_berth_refused_short", 1);
        return;
    }
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_shelter_reserved", 1);
    ctx.flags[taken_flag] = 1;
    ctx.effects.adjust_capacity(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_a.name", "depot_a_shelter_berths", -1);
}

// ── The mission closes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Twenty-six seconds after the shutters come down, because #1042 gives a climber
// twenty-four to reach the top and a lift booked on the last tick of the window
// has not landed or stood down yet. Reading the manifest before that would score
// the mission on a climber still on the ribbon. Finalisation then leaves ten
// seconds for retained dialogue choices to receive their guarded closed
// acknowledgements before the authoritative terminal victory stops all input.
fn on_the_window_shuts_for_good(ctx) {
    ctx.schedule.after(26, |ctx| { the_mission_closes(ctx); });
}

fn the_mission_closes(ctx) {
    // Finalisation freezes the evidence route before commitments, campaign facts
    // and debrief copy read it. A stale response admitted after this point can
    // still receive the closed acknowledgement, but cannot rewrite the ending.
    ctx.flags.skyway_mission_finalized = 1;
    ctx.flags.skyway_evidence_filing_open = 0;
    resolve_the_choice(ctx);
    // Corroboration is not filing. If the Control response is still waiting
    // when the mission closes, the optional line goes red rather than staying
    // Active forever or being credited by a confrontation elsewhere.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a2-corroborate");
    }
    // The ledger first: the left-behind beat below reads the promise's SETTLED
    // state, and `ctx.commitments.state` answers with what this call has already
    // written to it.
    resolve_the_promises(ctx);
    the_left_behind_ride_it_out(ctx);
    write_the_campaign_record(ctx);
    file_the_debrief(ctx);
    ctx.flags.skyway_mission_resolved = 1;
    ctx.flags.act3_resolved = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("a3_endings_written", 1);
    // A completed campaign episode must leave an authoritative terminal
    // outcome, not only a family of handoff counters. #1136 deliberately keeps
    // a narrow acknowledgement seam after the frozen record: retained choices
    // can receive their guarded closed reply, but cannot change any ending fact.
    // Partial and costly roads are still mission completion; collision/ship-loss
    // remain defeat paths throughout this final ten-second grace.
    ctx.schedule.after(10, |ctx| {
        ctx.effects.game_over("world.falling_skyway.game_over.mission_complete", "victory");
    });
}

// Whether a claimant actually got off the rock — by lift or by berth. The
// window's own `served` flag rather than the captain's `granted`, because a
// climber the shutters came down on is a claimant who is still here.
fn got_out(ctx, served_flag, berth_flag) {
    ctx.flags[served_flag] > 0 || ctx.flags[berth_flag] > 0
}

fn lifted_count(ctx) {
    let n = 0;
    if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_committee", "skyway_berth_committee") { n += 1; }
    if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_havelock", "skyway_berth_havelock") { n += 1; }
    if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_convoy", "skyway_berth_convoy") { n += 1; }
    n
}

// The crew's own job, scored: did the captain answer all three of them. A
// claimant who was never told anything is the failure this objective exists to
// name — not a claimant who was told no.
fn resolve_the_choice(ctx) {
    // Measured against the requests that actually reached the bridge (#1340),
    // not against the number three. A grant and a refusal are both ANSWERS and
    // score the same here — the mission distinguishes them everywhere it
    // matters, and refusing somebody to their face is a decision a captain
    // made. What this counts is silence.
    let asked = 0;
    let answered = 0;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_committee > 0 {
        asked += 1;
        if claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_committee", "skyway_refused_committee") { answered += 1; }
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_havelock > 0 {
        asked += 1;
        if claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_havelock", "skyway_refused_havelock") { answered += 1; }
    }
    // …and not against a claimant the corridor took off the board mid-window
    // (#1340). `skyway_claim_lost_convoy` is written by `on_convoy_lost` when
    // the hull goes while its claim is still open, and it is a THIRD outcome
    // beside granted and refused: the request was made, the engine put the
    // thread out of reach with its sender, and there is no answer the bridge
    // could have given after that. Counting it as asked would fail every
    // captain who had not answered it yet while passing the one who happened to
    // have answered it a beat earlier — the same crew, scored on the corridor's
    // timing rather than on their own.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_claim_asked_convoy > 0 && ctx.flags.skyway_claim_lost_convoy == 0 {
        asked += 1;
        if claim_decided(ctx, "skyway_granted_convoy", "skyway_refused_convoy") { answered += 1; }
    }
    ctx.flags.skyway_claims_asked = asked;
    ctx.flags.skyway_claims_answered = answered;
    ctx.flags.skyway_claims_unanswered = asked - answered;

    let id = "obj-a3-choice";
    if ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_only > 0 { id = "obj-a3-berth"; }
    if asked > 0 && answered >= asked {
        ctx.effects.complete_objective(id);
    } else {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective(id);
    }
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-a3-parley");

    // The lead #1039 handed this scene, and what happens to it if the scene
    // never uses it. An optional objective going red is this file's own way of
    // saying "that route is shut now" without a line of prose about it.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_confront_unlocked > 0 && ctx.flags.skyway_confronted == 0 {
        ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-a3-confront");
    }
}

// ── The ledger, settled ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Every promise this mission can make is resolved HERE, one way or the other,
// and each one is settled against a fact rather than against a mood. Guarded on
// `open` throughout, so a promise #1036's force-open already broke is not
// re-resolved and a promise that was never made is left `unknown` rather than
// counted as broken — "not yet" and "failed" are different facts about a
// captain, which is the rule the ledger itself is built on.
fn resolve_the_promises(ctx) {
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") == "open" {
        if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_committee", "skyway_berth_committee") {
            ctx.commitments.keep("skyway_safe_passage");
        } else {
            ctx.commitments.break_promise("skyway_safe_passage");
        }
    }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") == "open" {
        if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 {
            ctx.commitments.keep("skyway_surface_records");
        } else {
            ctx.commitments.break_promise("skyway_surface_records");
        }
    }
    // Hers is the one that is kept by NOT doing something, which is why it is
    // settled here rather than at the beat that would have broken it: a captain
    // who never confronted anybody has still kept her name back.
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_protect_witness") == "open" {
        if ctx.flags.skyway_witness_named > 0 {
            ctx.commitments.break_promise("skyway_protect_witness");
        } else {
            ctx.commitments.keep("skyway_protect_witness");
        }
    }
    // The picket's, and the only one in this ledger made to somebody the crew
    // could have shot (#1349). SETTLED AGAINST THE WORDS THAT WERE ACTUALLY
    // SAID, which are on the record twice and say the same thing both times:
    // the response is "we will come aboard you. We will not shoot you", and the
    // terms the ledger shows read "the picket will be taken by boarding party
    // and not by weapons fire".
    //
    // So the thing that breaks it is WEAPONS FIRE, not death. Three facts each
    // mean the crew used guns on that boat, and any one of them is enough:
    //
    //   destroyed        the plainest case.
    //   disabled         the mounts were shot off. The boat lived, which is the
    //                    outcome the beat is proud of and is still not what the
    //                    captain undertook — a promise that survived being shot
    //                    at would make containment, boarding and gunnery
    //                    disablement one commitment outcome wearing three
    //                    names, and AC5 asks for them to be distinct.
    //   picket_engaged   the crew opened on it at all, whatever it was that
    //                    finally settled the standoff.
    //
    // Everything else keeps it. Talked off the lane, contained from outside,
    // boarded without a shot, or left standing where it was: the word held.
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_picket_restraint") == "open" {
        if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_destroyed > 0 ||
           ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_disabled > 0 ||
           ctx.flags.picket_engaged > 0 {
            ctx.commitments.break_promise("skyway_picket_restraint");
        } else {
            ctx.commitments.keep("skyway_picket_restraint");
        }
    }
}

// ── What riding it out costs, and who says so ───────────────────────────────
//
// READ, NEVER ROLLED. Every term is a flag something earlier in this mission
// wrote, and the two shared ones are the two facts that decide whether there is
// anywhere at all to shelter in this corridor tonight.
//
// [ai] Every number here is unratified. The spread runs 0..5 and the terms are
// chosen so that no party's outcome is fixed: each of the three has one thing
// the crew could have done for them that is not the lift.
fn storm_cost(ctx, claimant) {
    // A party with no berth rides the corridor out in the open.
    let hurt = 2;
    // The head is gone, so there is no lee anywhere in the corridor and the
    // debris is still coming down through it.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_lost > 0 { hurt += 1; }
    // The rung is not moving, so nothing on the ladder has power at it or a
    // pumped berth to tie up against.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_strike_settled == 0 { hurt += 1; }

    if claimant == "committee" {
        // Their own people were cleared off that rung at somebody else's
        // authorisation, and their gear went over the rail with them.
        if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 { hurt += 1; }
        // …or they have the rung back, the gear back, and a full shift's rigs.
        else if ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation > 0 { hurt -= 1; }
    }
    if claimant == "havelock" {
        // The cutter and the picket are two hulls with power on them, and what
        // the standoff did to the second one is the LATER LIFT CONDITION this
        // beat feeds (#1349). Read as a ladder, worst first, because exactly one
        // of these is true of any run:
        //
        //   destroyed   the boat is wreckage. One fewer place to put people, and
        //               the crew who could have been in it are not.
        //   withdrawing it flew home — out of this corridor, and out of reach of
        //               anybody sheltering in it tonight. The same missing hull,
        //               without the bodies.
        //   boarded     it is still here and still powered, but it is under
        //               somebody else's flag and its own people are not aboard
        //               it. No help and no harm.
        //   contained / it is exactly where it was, with its mounts locked out —
        //   untouched   a warm hull with a hatch and its own crew in it, which
        //               is all a shelter is.
        //   disabled    the same hull, and a crew who have just been shot at.
        //               No bonus, because `picket_engaged` is up.
        if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_destroyed > 0 ||
           ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrawing > 0 {
            hurt += 1;
        } else if ctx.flags.picket_engaged == 0 && ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_boarded == 0 {
            hurt -= 1;
        }
    }
    if claimant == "convoy" {
        // They are the only claimant with no ground of their own, so the
        // corridor's shelter run is the whole of their cover. If it has already
        // failed once tonight it is not going to hold now.
        if ctx.flags.a2_traffic_lost > 0 { hurt += 1; }
        // …and a crew who pulled the Lyra out of the lane proved to them that
        // the lane can be worked in weather.
        else if ctx.flags.skyway_lyra_recovered > 0 { hurt -= 1; }
    }
    if hurt < 0 { hurt = 0; }
    hurt
}

fn the_left_behind_ride_it_out(ctx) {
    let toll = 0;

    if !got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_committee", "skyway_berth_committee") {
        let hurt = storm_cost(ctx, "committee");
        toll += hurt;
        ctx.flags.skyway_left_committee = 1;
        ctx.flags.skyway_left_committee_cost = hurt;
        // THE PROMISE, SAID BACK IN ITS OWN TERMS. It supersedes the severity
        // bodies because it is the louder fact: what these people are telling
        // the captain is not how bad it was, it is what they were told.
        let node = "committee_rides_it_out";
        if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") == "broken" {
            node = "committee_rides_it_out_promised";
        } else if hurt >= 3 {
            node = "committee_rides_it_out_hurt";
        }
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
            node_fn: node,
            urgent: true,
        });
        if hurt > 0 {
            ctx.dossier.append(#{
                subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.strike_committee.name",
                text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.committee_rode_it_out",
                provenance: "dialogue",
            });
        }
    }

    if !got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_havelock", "skyway_berth_havelock") {
        let hurt = storm_cost(ctx, "havelock");
        toll += hurt;
        ctx.flags.skyway_left_havelock = 1;
        ctx.flags.skyway_left_havelock_cost = hurt;
        let node = "havelock_rides_it_out";
        if hurt >= 3 { node = "havelock_rides_it_out_hurt"; }
        ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
            from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
            node_fn: node,
            urgent: true,
        });
        if hurt > 0 {
            ctx.dossier.append(#{
                subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.havelock_cutter.name",
                text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.havelock_rode_it_out",
                provenance: "dialogue",
            });
        }
    }

    if !got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_convoy", "skyway_berth_convoy") {
        let hurt = storm_cost(ctx, "convoy");
        toll += hurt;
        ctx.flags.skyway_left_convoy = 1;
        ctx.flags.skyway_left_convoy_cost = hurt;
        // A convoy that is not in the world any more does not get to report; the
        // toll is still theirs and still counted.
        if ctx.flags.skyway_convoy_lost == 0 {
            let node = "convoy_rides_it_out";
            if hurt >= 3 { node = "convoy_rides_it_out_hurt"; }
            ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
                from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
                node_fn: node,
                urgent: true,
            });
        }
        if hurt > 0 {
            ctx.dossier.append(#{
                subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.convoy_meridian.name",
                text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.convoy_rode_it_out",
                provenance: "dialogue",
            });
        }
    }

    ctx.flags.skyway_storm_casualties = toll;
}

fn committee_rides_it_out(ctx)          { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_rides_it_out", responses: [] } }
fn committee_rides_it_out_hurt(ctx)     { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_rides_it_out_hurt", responses: [] } }
fn committee_rides_it_out_promised(ctx) { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.committee_rides_it_out_promised", responses: [] } }
fn havelock_rides_it_out(ctx)           { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_rides_it_out", responses: [] } }
fn havelock_rides_it_out_hurt(ctx)      { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.havelock_rides_it_out_hurt", responses: [] } }
fn convoy_rides_it_out(ctx)             { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_rides_it_out", responses: [] } }
fn convoy_rides_it_out_hurt(ctx)        { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.convoy_rides_it_out_hurt", responses: [] } }

// ── The seven families ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fn write_the_campaign_record(ctx) {
    // 1. SAFE PASSAGE. One of the pair per claimant, always, so a later mission
    // reads a fact rather than an absence (#1037's invariant, three times over).
    // The refusals are recorded apart, because a party told to their face that
    // they were staying is a different neighbour from one nobody called.
    if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_committee", "skyway_berth_committee") {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.committee"] = 1;
    } else {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.left_committee"] = 1;
    }
    if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_havelock", "skyway_berth_havelock") {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.havelock"] = 1;
    } else {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.left_havelock"] = 1;
    }
    if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_convoy", "skyway_berth_convoy") {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.convoy"] = 1;
    } else {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.left_convoy"] = 1;
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_refused_committee > 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.refused_committee"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_refused_havelock > 0  { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.refused_havelock"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_refused_convoy > 0    { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.refused_convoy"] = 1; }
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.taken"] = lifted_count(ctx);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_only > 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.passage.berth_only"] = 1; }

    // 2. THE STRIKE. Exactly one, and the third is a real reading: a crew who
    // neither talked to the committee nor authorised the cutter leave the rung
    // stopped, and the next mission through here inherits that.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.strike.negotiated"] = 1;
    } else if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.strike.forced"] = 1;
    } else {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.strike.unresolved"] = 1;
    }

    // 3. THE EVIDENCE. The exclusive three say what the crew HOLD; the three
    // beside them say what they did with it. `holds` reads the fact sheet rather
    // than a flag beside one route's append, which is the rule #1039 set.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.evidence.corroborated"] = 1;
    } else if ctx.dossier.holds(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file" }) {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.evidence.records"] = 1;
    } else {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.evidence.none"] = 1;
    }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0   { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.evidence.filed"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_confronted > 0    { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.evidence.confronted"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_witness_named > 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.evidence.witness_named"] = 1; }

    // 4. THE CASUALTIES, itemised and summed. Three separate beats of this
    // mission can hurt somebody and the campaign wants both readings: which beat
    // it was, and how many people it came to.
    //
    // FOUR beats now, not three (#1349). `campaign.skyway.casualties.picket` is
    // an OLDER key than the picket boat is and it does not mean her: it is what
    // forcing the labour picket on Ladder B cost, written by
    // `force_the_picket`. The standoff's own count goes under `standoff`, and
    // the two are never added into one another — a later mission reading this
    // record is asking two different questions about two different sets of
    // people who happen to share a word.
    let total = ctx.flags.skyway_force_casualties
        + ctx.flags.skyway_picket_casualties
        + ctx.flags.skyway_head_casualties
        + ctx.flags.skyway_storm_casualties;
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.casualties.picket"] = ctx.flags.skyway_force_casualties;
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.casualties.standoff"] = ctx.flags.skyway_picket_casualties;
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.casualties.head"] = ctx.flags.skyway_head_casualties;
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.casualties.storm"] = ctx.flags.skyway_storm_casualties;
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.casualties.total"] = total;
    if total == 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.casualties.none"] = 1; }

    // 5. THE STRUCTURE. Mirrored off the pair #1040 guarantees rather than
    // re-derived, and written as two tests rather than an if/else, so a run that
    // somehow reached neither says neither instead of quietly claiming the head
    // is standing.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_lost > 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.skyhook.lost"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_held > 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.skyhook.held"] = 1; }

    // 6. THE CAPTAIN'S WORD. Counted off the ledger itself — which by now has
    // been settled — so a promise broken back in Act 2 by the force-open counts
    // here beside one broken tonight by a refusal.
    let kept = 0;
    let broken = 0;
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") == "kept" { kept += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_safe_passage") == "broken" { broken += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") == "kept" { kept += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_surface_records") == "broken" { broken += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_protect_witness") == "kept" { kept += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_protect_witness") == "broken" { broken += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_picket_restraint") == "kept" { kept += 1; }
    if ctx.commitments.state("skyway_picket_restraint") == "broken" { broken += 1; }
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.kept"] = kept;
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.broken"] = broken;
    if kept + broken == 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.none"] = 1;
    } else if broken == 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.clean"] = 1;
    }

    // 7. THE TRAFFIC. This is deliberately separate from human casualty tolls:
    // a destroyed hauler is a corridor-capacity fact even when its complement
    // is not modelled as a headcount. The exact complement is always written.
    ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.lost"] = ctx.flags.a2_traffic_lost;
    if ctx.flags.a2_traffic_lost == 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.none"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_meridian > 0 { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.meridian"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_lark > 0     { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.lark"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_pell > 0     { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.pell"] = 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_wick > 0     { ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.wick"] = 1; }
    // The lane itself, as the next crew through here inherits it. A corridor
    // with an armed boat still sitting across it is a corridor that is not
    // finished, whatever else this mission achieved — and it is a TRAFFIC fact
    // rather than a casualty one, which is the split section 7 already makes.
    write_the_picket_record(ctx);
    // The corridor obstruction's controlled demolition (issue #1350, scored for
    // the T2 refinement). A NEW scored category, read off the four operation-
    // quality flags the demolition consequences band froze. Omitted entirely if
    // the obstruction was never touched — an absence is a real answer, the same
    // convention the skyhook and civilians rows keep.
    write_the_demolition_record(ctx);

    // ── THE NARRATIVE REPORT (issue #1351) ──────────────────────────────────
    //
    // Six of the report's rows, written here at the one finalisation chokepoint
    // and in the authored narrative order the report reads top to bottom, each
    // off the frozen campaign facts the seven sections above just settled. This
    // block REGISTERS NO NEW STATE — it reads the same flags the handoff does.
    //
    // The other three rows ride the same `MissionReport` Vec in write order,
    // written at the tick each one's fate is actually decided rather than here:
    // the Lyra row in Act 2 (#1344), the civilians row when the head's
    // survivors are recovered (#1338's epilogue), and the picket row just
    // above. So a full run's rows come out [lyra, civilians?, picket, survey,
    // labour, traffic, skyhook, lifts, commitments] — the six below are in the
    // issue's order among themselves, and the three event-timed rows sit where
    // their own beats put them, which is the property #1344 chose deliberately.
    survey_report_row(ctx);
    labour_report_row(ctx);
    traffic_report_row(ctx);
    skyhook_report_row(ctx);
    lifts_report_row(ctx);
    commitments_report_row(ctx);
}

// ── The report-row helpers (issue #1351, PRD #1337) ─────────────────────────
//
// One helper per narrative category, each the `lyra`/`picket` shape: one stable
// row id, one heading String Id, one outcome String Id chosen off the frozen
// facts, one ReportRowState a player surface styles on, and one SIGNED score no
// player ever sees. The score is the diagnostic PRD #1337 ratified; lives and
// promises dominate it, which is why the traffic, civilian and commitment rows
// carry the heaviest swings. The outcome/state prose is [ai] unratified.
//
// Every helper reads flags and nothing else, so each is callable on its own —
// from `write_the_campaign_record` above, from `on_lark_collision`'s
// catastrophic ending, and from a headless unit test that hands it a flag store.
// Writing the same id twice UPDATES the one row in place (the report's own
// rule), so a fate that is re-stated never double-counts.

// SURVEY / EVIDENCE. The five numbers PRD #1337 lists for this row, summed
// because they are separate things one investigation did: the survey filed
// (+2) or missed (-2), the depot discrepancy found (+1), a worker put on the
// record (+2), and the bundle filed with Control (+3). The outcome names the
// deepest thing the crew came away holding; the score carries the rest.
fn survey_report_row(ctx) {
    let score = 0;
    let filed = ctx.flags.skyway_survey_reported > 0;
    if filed { score += 2; } else { score -= 2; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_diff_found > 0 { score += 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained > 0 { score += 2; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 { score += 3; }

    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.survey.missed";
    let state = "lost";
    if ctx.flags.skyway_worker_corroboration_obtained > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.survey.corroborated";
        state = "saved";
    } else if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 || ctx.flags.skyway_records_diff_found > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.survey.records";
        state = "partial";
    } else if filed {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.survey.filed";
        state = "neutral";
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "survey",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.survey.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// LABOUR SETTLEMENT. The three-way strike reading section 2 already made,
// scored: talked to a vote (+4), forced open over their heads (0), or left
// stopped (-3).
fn labour_report_row(ctx) {
    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.labour.unresolved";
    let state = "lost";
    let score = -3;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_settled_by_negotiation > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.labour.negotiated";
        state = "saved";
        score = 4;
    } else if ctx.flags.skyway_forced_open > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.labour.forced";
        state = "neutral";
        score = 0;
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "labour",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.labour.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// SURVIVING TRAFFIC. +1 for each corridor craft still flying, -3 for each one
// the sweep took — the four the campaign record itemises, read one at a time so
// the score is the exact tally and not a band. A capacity fact, kept apart from
// the human casualty tolls for the reason section 7 states.
fn traffic_report_row(ctx) {
    let score = 0;
    let lost = 0;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_meridian > 0 { score -= 3; lost += 1; } else { score += 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_lark > 0     { score -= 3; lost += 1; } else { score += 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_pell > 0     { score -= 3; lost += 1; } else { score += 1; }
    if ctx.flags.skyway_traffic_lost_wick > 0     { score -= 3; lost += 1; } else { score += 1; }

    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.traffic.clear";
    let state = "saved";
    if lost >= 4 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.traffic.scattered";
        state = "lost";
    } else if lost > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.traffic.thinned";
        state = "partial";
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "traffic",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.traffic.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// THE SKYHOOK. The pair section 5 mirrors, scored: held (+4) or lost (-4). If a
// run somehow reached neither the row is omitted rather than inventing a fate,
// the same defensiveness section 5 writes as two tests rather than an if/else.
fn skyhook_report_row(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_lost > 0 {
        ctx.effects.report_row(#{
            id: "skyhook",
            heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.skyhook.heading",
            outcome: "world.falling_skyway.report.skyhook.lost",
            state: "lost",
            score: -4,
        });
    } else if ctx.flags.skyway_skyhook_held > 0 {
        ctx.effects.report_row(#{
            id: "skyhook",
            heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.skyhook.heading",
            outcome: "world.falling_skyway.report.skyhook.held",
            state: "saved",
            score: 4,
        });
    }
}

// LIFT ALLOCATION. +2 for each claimant carried or berthed clear, -1 for each
// request the captain never answered; a refusal to somebody's face scores
// nothing, because it is a decision the mission records everywhere else and not
// a silence. `lifted_count` and `skyway_claims_unanswered` are both settled by
// `resolve_the_choice`, which the mission runs before this record.
fn lifts_report_row(ctx) {
    let lifted = lifted_count(ctx);
    let unanswered = ctx.flags.skyway_claims_unanswered;
    let score = lifted * 2 - unanswered;

    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.lifts.none";
    let state = "lost";
    if lifted >= 2 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.lifts.full";
        state = "saved";
    } else if lifted == 1 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.lifts.some";
        state = "partial";
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "lifts",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.lifts.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// THE CAPTAIN'S WORD. +3 for each promise kept, -4 for each broken, read off
// the counts section 6 settled onto the campaign flags. A run that made no
// promises has no row — an absence is a real answer, so nothing is written.
fn commitments_report_row(ctx) {
    let kept = ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.kept"];
    let broken = ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.broken"];
    if kept + broken == 0 { return; }
    let score = kept * 3 - broken * 4;

    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.commitments.broken";
    let state = "lost";
    if broken == 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.commitments.kept";
        state = "saved";
    } else if kept > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.commitments.mixed";
        state = "partial";
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "commitments",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.commitments.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// CIVILIANS. The survivors the falling head shed, newly discovered adrift in the
// debris and brought in by the tractor (#1338's epilogue). +1 for each one
// recovered, -2 for each one the debris took. Written from `head_epilogue_resolves`
// at the tick their fate is decided, and only ever then: a run that held the head
// never opened the epilogue, so it reports no civilians row at all — a genuinely
// inapplicable row, omitted. This is the mission's "newly discovered civilian"
// population; it is a DIFFERENT rescue mechanic from #1348's Engineering
// transporter, which this mission does not place, and the two never share a row.
fn civilians_report_row(ctx) {
    let saved = ctx.flags.skyway_survivors_recovered;
    let lost = ctx.flags.skyway_survivors_lost;
    if saved + lost == 0 { return; }
    let score = saved - lost * 2;

    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.civilians.none";
    let state = "lost";
    if lost == 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.civilians.all";
        state = "saved";
    } else if saved > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.civilians.some";
        state = "partial";
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "civilians",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.civilians.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// ── 8. THE STANDOFF (#1349) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// EXACTLY ONE of eight, in one place, read at finalisation — the shape section
// 2's three-way strike reading already has, widened to the number of endings
// this beat actually has. A later mission reads a fact about the picket rather
// than an absence, whichever road the crew took.
//
// THE ORDER IS THE PRECEDENCE, and it is not arbitrary. It is also the ladder
// `bank_picket_disposition` ranks the endings on, so that the goodwill the
// operator is left holding belongs to the ending this record names:
//
//   destroyed    a kill is a kill. A boat that was contained, boarded or
//                disabled first and then finished is recorded as finished, for
//                the reason `restraint_shown` is assigned rather than tested.
//   withdrew     the only other ending that takes the hull out of the corridor.
//   boarded      before contained: going through the hatch is the bigger act,
//                and a run that did both did the bigger one.
//   disabled     before holding: shooting the mounts off is an answer.
//   engaged      the guns came out, nothing was settled, and the boat is still
//                sitting there. Above `holding` because SHOOTING AT SOMEBODY IS
//                NOT A NON-INTERVENTION: a crew who opened on the boat and then
//                broke off did address the standoff, badly, and the two rows
//                under this one both say in words that nothing was done to her.
//   holding      the crew OPENED the channel and left the boat standing, and
//                never fired. A deliberate non-intervention, which is a
//                decision.
//   unresolved   nobody ever addressed it — no channel, no shot. The reading
//                section 2's own third branch is: not a failure, an absence, and
//                the two are different facts about a captain.
// Every campaign key here is a LITERAL, and the branch it sits in is the one
// place it is written — no composed `"campaign.skyway.picket." + state`, so the
// eight flags a later mission will read are greppable from this file exactly as
// the other seven families' are.
//
// [ai] Every score unratified. The spread is deliberately narrow and centred on
// nothing: this beat is a way the crew WERE, not the mission's result, and the
// report already has a claimant tally to be its verdict.
fn write_the_picket_record(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_destroyed > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.destroyed"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_cleared"] = 1;
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.destroyed", "lost", -5);
    } else if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_withdrawing > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.withdrew"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_cleared"] = 1;
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.withdrew", "saved", 5);
    } else if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_boarded > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.boarded"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_cleared"] = 1;
        // The one row in this list that makes a claim about people, so the one
        // that has to be chosen off the fact rather than off the branch: the
        // warning on the channel buys the boarding party a boat whose crew were
        // braced for them, and `on_picket_boarded` banked what that came to.
        // Printing "one of theirs hurt" over a standoff toll of nought would be
        // the epilogue contradicting its own ledger.
        let row = "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.boarded_clean";
        if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_boarding_toll > 0 {
            row = "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.boarded";
        }
        picket_report_row(ctx, row, "saved", 3);
    } else if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_contained > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.contained"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_cleared"] = 1;
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.contained", "saved", 4);
    } else if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_disabled > 0 {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.disabled"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_cleared"] = 1;
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.disabled", "partial", 1);
    } else if ctx.flags.picket_engaged > 0 {
        // FIRED ON AND LEFT STANDING. A crew who opened on the boat, did not
        // shoot the mounts off it and did not finish it, and then went back to
        // the corridor. The threshold is 65 hull points wide, so stopping short
        // of it is an ordinary thing for a bridge to do — a burst, a second
        // thought, and a boat still on station with holes in her.
        //
        // It is its own ending because the two rows below it both say, in words,
        // that nothing was done to her: `holding` reads "hailed and left
        // standing" and `unresolved` reads "never addressed". Neither is true of
        // a crew who exchanged fire with her, and the next mission reading this
        // record would conclude they never touched her.
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.engaged"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_picketed"] = 1;
        // [ai] Unratified: under `holding`'s nought because the lane is blocked
        // AND a neutral contract crew were shot at for it — the one reading in
        // this list where the crew got the worse of both roads.
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.engaged", "neutral", -2);
        ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_picket_left_shot");
    } else if ctx.flags.havelock_enforcer_channel_opened > 0 {
        // THE LANE IS STILL BLOCKED. A boat the captain chose to leave alone and
        // one nobody ever called block the corridor identically — which is why
        // the traffic key does not split where the picket key does.
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.holding"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_picketed"] = 1;
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.holding", "neutral", 0);
        // The story's own punctuation for the three endings that are not a fate
        // (issue #1338). `narrative_outcome` has five words and none of them
        // means "still there"; a beat does, and a beat is what this is — the
        // author saying that a standoff ended by not ending.
        ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_picket_left_standing");
    } else {
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.picket.unresolved"] = 1;
        ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.traffic.corridor_picketed"] = 1;
        picket_report_row(ctx, "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.unresolved", "neutral", 0);
        ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_picket_unaddressed");
    }
}

// One row id for all eight endings, the `lyra` rule: two ids would let a run
// that disabled the boat and then killed it report the standoff twice, in two
// moods. The OUTCOME string is the variable — nine of them, because the boarding
// has two depending on what it cost.
fn picket_report_row(ctx, outcome_id, state, score) {
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "picket",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.picket.heading",
        outcome: outcome_id,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// ── The debrief ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Control reads the manifest closed. The headline is the pairing, because the
// pairing is what the mission was about; everything else the crew need in order
// to read this run as finished is on the fact sheet beside it, filed under the
// provenance that says where it came from.
fn file_the_debrief(ctx) {
    let node = "debrief_none";
    let lifted = lifted_count(ctx);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_shelter_only > 0 {
        node = "debrief_berth_none";
        if lifted > 0 { node = "debrief_berth"; }
    } else if lifted >= 2 {
        node = "debrief_operator_and_convoy";
        if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_committee", "skyway_berth_committee") {
            node = "debrief_workers_and_operator";
            if got_out(ctx, "skyway_window_served_convoy", "skyway_berth_convoy") {
                node = "debrief_workers_and_convoy";
            }
        }
    } else if lifted == 1 {
        node = "debrief_one";
    }
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from: "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        node_fn: node,
        urgent: true,
    });

    // What became of the evidence bundle. Naming Tacket to Havelock never
    // manufactures a Control filing: the filed flag owns this branch first,
    // and the nested distinction records what happened in the later confrontation.
    if ctx.flags.skyway_records_put > 0 {
        if ctx.flags.skyway_witness_named > 0 {
            ctx.dossier.append(#{
                subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
                text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.record_named_witness",
                provenance: "records",
            });
        } else {
            ctx.dossier.append(#{
                subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
                text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.record_filed",
                provenance: "records",
            });
        }
    } else if ctx.dossier.holds(#{ text: "world.falling_skyway.evidence.ladder_b_maintenance_file" }) {
        ctx.dossier.append(#{
            subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
            text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.record_buried",
            provenance: "records",
        });
    } else {
        ctx.dossier.append(#{
            subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
            text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.record_never_found",
            provenance: "records",
        });
    }

    // What became of the captain's word.
    let entry = "world.falling_skyway.evidence.word_none";
    if ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.broken"] > 0 {
        entry = "world.falling_skyway.evidence.word_broken";
    } else if ctx.flags["campaign.skyway.commitments.kept"] > 0 {
        entry = "world.falling_skyway.evidence.word_kept";
    }
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.falling_skyway.entity.skyway_control.name",
        text:       entry,
        provenance: "dialogue",
    });
}

// ═══ THE CORRIDOR SHEDS (issue #1347) ═══════════════════════════════════════
//
// The storm has gone through and left the ribbon's structure working. Three
// masses come down out of its wake in the ~500 seconds between the corridor
// clearing (t=1072) and the transfer window opening (t=1600), and the crew have
// to find out what they are before they can do anything about them.
//
// It is a PARALLEL track in a window that already has one — the tether-strain
// ladder runs through the same minutes — and that is the point of putting it
// here rather than in a quiet stretch. The mission's question in Act 3 is what a
// four-seat crew do when two things need doing at once.
//
// ── Who owns what ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The ENGINE owns the geometry: `src/debris/` drifts each contact, and a scan
// taken through the ordinary lifecycle projects it against the asset it is
// aimed at and raises four world flags — read, confirmed, urgent, struck.
//
// THIS FILE owns every consequence. Nothing below is a special case in Rust:
// each handler is an ordinary `on_flag_set` / `on_destroyed`, and what a strike
// costs, what the computer says and which objective goes red are authored data
// that a designer retunes without a recompile.
//
// ── The one thing that does NOT happen here ─────────────────────────────────
//
// Nothing in this slice touches Tactical's Combat Lock, and there is no verb in
// the scenario vocabulary that could. Confirming a threat posts an OBJECTIVE and
// shows a MESSAGE; what Tactical does about it is Tactical's, whether that seat
// is a person or Backfill. The AI reaches the same rock the same way a person
// does — by looking at a panel that says something is on course — and never
// because the scenario reached into the console and set a target.
//
// ── Why a rock nobody has read is not a threat ──────────────────────────────
//
// The stray is the whole argument. It is the nearest contact, the first thing
// the radar shows, and it is going nowhere. A crew who assume and shoot spend
// the window on it; a crew who look know inside one scan. Backfilled Tactical
// cannot make that mistake at all — the candidate source that surfaces debris is
// assessment-gated — but a human Tactical is free to, which is the right
// asymmetry: the AI will not act on what the crew were not told, and a person
// may back their own judgement.

on_flag_set("skyway_storm_passed", "on_the_corridor_sheds");

on_flag_set("skyway_debris_lead_confirmed", "on_debris_lead_confirmed");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_trail_confirmed", "on_debris_trail_confirmed");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_lead_urgent", "on_debris_lead_urgent");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_trail_urgent", "on_debris_trail_urgent");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_lead_struck", "on_debris_lead_struck");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_trail_struck", "on_debris_trail_struck");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_stray_read", "on_debris_stray_read");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_lead_read", "on_debris_lead_read");
on_flag_set("skyway_debris_trail_read", "on_debris_trail_read");

on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_lead.name", "on_debris_lead_cleared");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_trail.name", "on_debris_trail_cleared");
// The stray gets one too, and by exactly the mistake the header above calls
// interesting: it is the nearest, most obvious return, so a human Tactical who
// assumes and shoots kills THIS one first. That ends the contact, and an ending
// closes every task it was the subject of — see `on_debris_stray_cleared`.
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_stray.name", "on_debris_stray_cleared");

// ONE CONTACT, ONE READING TASK, AND ONE PLACE THAT SPELLS ITS ID.
//
// The three ids are deliberately not uniform: the stray's task is authored
// "near" because that is what the crew see — the nearest return — while the two
// aimed masses are named for where they sit in the corridor. So every site that
// posts or ends a reading task asks this instead of building the id out of the
// contact key. The one rule that did (`"obj-a3-debris-scan-" + key`) quietly
// missed the stray, which is how its task came to be closable from exactly one
// place. A fourth contact costs one line here and cannot reintroduce that.
fn debris_scan_objective(key) {
    if key == "stray" { return "obj-a3-debris-scan-near"; }
    "obj-a3-debris-scan-" + key
}

// Six seconds after the corridor clears, so the shedding reads as a consequence
// of the weather rather than as part of it.
fn on_the_corridor_sheds(ctx) {
    ctx.schedule.after(6, |ctx| { shed_the_corridor(ctx); });
}

// One contact. Everything that varies between the three is an argument, so the
// three spawns below read as one authored table rather than three near-copies —
// and so a fourth contact costs one call.
//
// `mass` is what the survey suite's `[[scan.mass_class]]` ladder answers over,
// and the three are deliberately in three different classes: a crew reading
// "heavy, on course for Ladder A" have been told something a crew reading
// "on course for Ladder A" have not.
fn shed_one(ctx, name, anchor, mass, drift_x, drift_z, protects, radius, key) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_large.toml",
        name: name,
        anchor: anchor,
        groups: ["skyway_debris"],
        overrides: #{
            mass: mass,
            // THE ROCK'S OWN INTEGRITY, and the reason a survey suite has
            // anything to answer about it at all.
            //
            // `science::scan` refuses a subject with no readable condition
            // track, deliberately and for issue #1030's reason, so a mass with
            // no `[infrastructure]` is a mass no crew can read — including the
            // trajectory, because the projection is folded into the reading the
            // refusal replaces. Giving debris a condition track is not a
            // workaround for that gate: it is what the track MEANS here. A rock
            // has structural integrity, breaking it up is the whole of what
            // Tactical is asked to do to it, and "how solid is it" belongs
            // beside "where is it going" in the same reading.
            //
            // The shipped `hull_damage_share` default of 1.0 is left alone, so
            // weapons fire falls point for point onto this track — unlike the
            // skyhook's survivor craft, whose problem is that they have no way
            // home rather than that anybody is shooting at them.
            //
            // [ai] 60 points unratified. It is the size of the firing problem:
            // how much of the window an interception costs, against the same
            // banks the rest of Act 3 is competing for.
            infrastructure: #{
                condition_max: flt("60.0"),
                decay_per_sec: flt("0.0"),
            },
            debris: #{
                drift: [drift_x, flt("0.0"), drift_z],
                protected_target: protects,
                impact_radius: radius,
                // A minute's warning. It is a DOCTRINE number, not a physical
                // one: how long this ship needs to solve a firing problem on a
                // drifting mass, which is the designer's call and not the rock's.
                urgent_secs: flt("60.0"),
                // How long a reading stays current before the seat goes back for
                // another. Short enough that the deadline Tactical prioritises on
                // cannot rot through a whole approach; long enough that Sensors
                // moves on to the next unknown in between.
                reassess_secs: flt("45.0"),
                assessed_flag: "skyway_debris_" + key + "_read",
                confirmed_flag: "skyway_debris_" + key + "_confirmed",
                urgent_flag: "skyway_debris_" + key + "_urgent",
                impact_flag: "skyway_debris_" + key + "_struck",
            },
        },
    });
}

// The three contacts, and the numbers that decide what happens.
//
// The lead runs 480 units to Ladder A at 1.8 a second and crosses its 40-unit
// impact radius about 244 seconds out; the trailing mass runs 540 to Ladder B at
// 1.3 and arrives about 385 seconds out. Both land before the transfer window,
// and they are 140 seconds apart — far enough that a crew who work the nearer
// one first still have time for the second, and close enough that a crew who
// pick wrong do not.
//
// The stray protects nothing, so no closest approach is projected and it can
// never be confirmed however near it passes. That is an authored choice the
// engine supports directly, not an omission.
//
// [ai] Every number in this function is unratified. The two drifts and the
// 40-unit radii are the whole difficulty surface of the beat.
fn shed_the_corridor(ctx) {
    shed_one(ctx,
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_lead.name",
        "debris_lead_start", flt("48000.0"), flt("0.0"), flt("1.8"),
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_a.name", flt("40.0"), "lead");
    shed_one(ctx,
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_trail.name",
        "debris_trail_start", flt("9000.0"), flt("0.0"), flt("1.3"),
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name", flt("40.0"), "trail");
    shed_one(ctx,
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_stray.name",
        "debris_stray_start", flt("1200.0"), flt("-2.2"), flt("0.9"),
        "", flt("0.0"), "stray");

    // THE CUE THE CREW ACTUALLY GET. Three returns and no identification on any
    // of them, to the Captain, who holds the sensors target on this hull. It
    // says what is true — that there are contacts and nobody knows what they are
    // — and deliberately not which one matters, because that is the work.
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_debris_unidentified",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.debris_unidentified",
        "advisory",
        12,
        "captain",
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_corridor_shed");

    // Three Scan objectives, which is what makes a Backfilled Sensors seat go
    // and look: each names its own subject, so the directive resolves to one
    // contact and the seat works down the list as each reading lands. Priorities
    // descend in no particular order of danger — the crew have not been told
    // which is dangerous, and an objective list that quietly ranked them would
    // be answering the question the scan is supposed to answer.
    //
    // Above the transfer window's 54 (unknown masses in the corridor outrank
    // paperwork) and below Act 3's rescue work at 85, which is people.
    post_survey_scan_objective(ctx,
        debris_scan_objective("stray"),
        "world.falling_skyway.objective.debris_scan_near.text",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_stray.name",
        "skyway_debris_stray_read", 62);
    post_survey_scan_objective(ctx,
        debris_scan_objective("lead"),
        "world.falling_skyway.objective.debris_scan_lead.text",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_lead.name",
        "skyway_debris_lead_read", 61);
    post_survey_scan_objective(ctx,
        debris_scan_objective("trail"),
        "world.falling_skyway.objective.debris_scan_trail.text",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_trail.name",
        "skyway_debris_trail_read", 60);
}

// ── Confirmation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Raised by the engine only when an assessment SOMEBODY TOOK came back on a
// collision course. Two things follow, and neither of them is a firing order:
// the interception objective goes on the panel, and the computer says what the
// crew now know. The Destroy directive is how a Backfilled Tactical hears about
// it — the same way it hears about any other named target — and a human Tactical
// reads the same objective off the same list.
fn confirm_one(ctx, id, text, target, priority, key) {
    // FIRST TERMINAL EVENT WINS applies here too, and this was the one handler
    // in the beat standing outside it.
    //
    // A mass that has already LANDED is not a threat left to confirm. The engine
    // will not latch `confirmed` after `struck` (see `tick_debris_state`), and on
    // the one tick where both can be true at once — a reading that lands on the
    // very tick the rock crosses its impact radius — both flags are already in
    // the store by the time this runs, so the strike takes the contact. Without
    // these two lines that reading posts a MANDATORY interception order for a
    // rock that is already down and that nothing can ever resolve — `clear_one`
    // returns early on the impact flag, `strike_one` on the spent claim — and
    // shows the collision and impact-imminent cues AFTER the impact cue.
    if ctx.flags["skyway_debris_" + key + "_struck"] > 0 { return; }
    if !debris_pending(ctx, key) { return; }
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: id,
        text: text,
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: priority,
        directive_kind: "Destroy",
        target: target,
        targets: [target],
    });
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_debris_collision_" + key,
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.debris_collision_" + key,
        "warning",
        14,
        "tactical",
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_debris_confirmed_" + key);
}

fn on_debris_lead_confirmed(ctx) {
    confirm_one(ctx,
        "obj-a3-debris-lead",
        "world.falling_skyway.objective.debris_lead.text",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_lead.name",
        76, "lead");
}

fn on_debris_trail_confirmed(ctx) {
    confirm_one(ctx,
        "obj-a3-debris-trail",
        "world.falling_skyway.objective.debris_trail.text",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_trail.name",
        75, "trail");
}

// Running out of room. Critical, and the only place in this beat that shouts.
fn urge_one(ctx, key) {
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_debris_urgent_" + key,
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.debris_urgent_" + key,
        "critical",
        20,
        "tactical",
    );
}

fn on_debris_lead_urgent(ctx)  { urge_one(ctx, "lead"); }
fn on_debris_trail_urgent(ctx) { urge_one(ctx, "trail"); }

// Reading the stray. Nothing happens, loudly — the objective goes green and the
// panel says the mass is aimed at nothing, which is a finding and the reason the
// crew can stop thinking about it. A beat is recorded because "they checked"
// is a thing the debrief should be able to say.
fn on_debris_stray_read(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.complete_objective(debris_scan_objective("stray"));
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_debris_stray_clear",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.debris_stray_clear",
        "info",
        10,
        "captain",
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_debris_ruled_out");
}

// ── Reading one of the aimed masses ─────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The Scan objective ends on the READING, not on what the reading turned out to
// say. A crew who looked have done the job the panel gave them whether the
// answer was "on course for Ladder A" or "going nowhere at all", and the stray
// has been closed that way since this beat was written — these two make the
// aimed masses agree with it instead of hanging their Scan objective off the
// confirmation, which is a different question and one a reading may answer no to.
//
// Ending it on the flag rather than inside `confirm_one` is also what keeps the
// Backfilled Sensors seat honest. The Scan directive is live for exactly as long
// as its objective is Active, so a contact that has been read — or that has
// ENDED unread, which is what the two terminal handlers below now close — stops
// being re-requested on every AI snapshot.
fn read_one(ctx, key) {
    ctx.effects.complete_objective(debris_scan_objective(key));
}

fn on_debris_lead_read(ctx)  { read_one(ctx, "lead"); }
fn on_debris_trail_read(ctx) { read_one(ctx, "trail"); }

// ── The stray's ending ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The stray has no protected asset, so the engine never confirms it and never
// strikes it: `tick_debris_state` skips arrival for a contact with an empty
// `protected_target`. Its two possible endings are therefore the reading, above,
// and THIS — a Tactical who locked the nearest return and broke it up before
// anybody looked, which the header calls the interesting mistake and which
// `shed_one` makes reachable by giving the stray the same condition track as its
// siblings.
//
// What must follow is the closure the two aimed masses already get: the reading
// task ends with the rock rather than sitting Active on the crew's panel over a
// despawned entity — and, because a Backfilled Sensors seat's Scan directive is
// live for exactly as long as its objective is, the seat's TOP request is this
// one (posted at 62, above lead's 61 and trail's 60). Left Active it names a
// contact nothing can resolve for the rest of the mission, and the seat's one
// mission-Scan channel never reaches the two masses the beat is actually about.
//
// Failed rather than completed, for the same reason as the other two: for an
// unread contact the honest record is that nobody ever looked. A stray that WAS
// read completed this on its `_read` flag, and `ObjectiveManager::fail` moves
// `Active` records only, so this is a no-op there rather than a downgrade.
//
// And it does NOT resolve anything. `skyway_debris_resolved` counts the two
// AIMED masses — the corridor is clear when the things on course for a rung are
// settled — and the stray was never a threat, so shooting it must not carry the
// corridor-clear cue one mass closer. See `debris_resolved`.
fn on_debris_stray_cleared(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.fail_objective(debris_scan_objective("stray"));
}

// ── The three endings, per protected asset ──────────────────────────────────
//
// Which rung was saved or harmed is recorded as its own durable flag, so a
// debrief and any later mission read a fact about Ladder A rather than a score
// for "the debris". The three outcomes are genuinely different states and not
// three shades of one:
//
//   CLEARED   — intercepted with room to spare. The objective completes and the
//               rung is untouched.
//   LATE      — intercepted, but only after the urgency window opened. The rung
//               survives and the objective still completes: they did the job.
//               What is different is the record, and the debrief can say the
//               margin was gone.
//   STRUCK    — nobody stopped it. The rung takes authored damage on its own
//               condition track, which is the same track the whole mission
//               reads its thresholds off, so a struck rung may drop under its
//               pumping line and stop delivering into the window — the loss
//               arrives as arithmetic through the ladder the crew already know,
//               not as a scripted announcement.
//
// ── ONE CONTACT, ONE ENDING ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The two terminal handlers below are NOT mutually exclusive by construction,
// and the mission's own "late" band is what makes the overlap reachable. A mass
// that lands is not destroyed by landing: `tick_debris_state` sets `struck`,
// freezes the drift and leaves the rock in the world, still targetable, still
// carrying the condition track Tactical was shooting at. So a crew who break up
// the wreckage afterwards — or who land the killing shot on the very tick it
// crosses the impact radius, which is the last-instant interception this beat
// invites — fire `on_destroyed` for a contact `on_flag_set(..._struck)` has
// already accounted for.
//
// Ungoverned, that rung is recorded harmed AND saved, its objective is failed
// and then completed, and the shared counter reaches 2 off one mass — so the
// corridor is declared clear with the other rock still inbound, and AC4's three
// outcomes stop being three distinct records. FIRST TERMINAL EVENT WINS: each
// handler claims the contact through `debris_pending` before it writes anything,
// and closes it with `debris_resolved` after.
//
// `confirm_one` reads the same claim from the other side. A confirmation is not
// an ending, so it takes nothing and closes nothing — but it refuses to post an
// interception order for a contact whose ending has already been claimed, which
// is the case a reading taken after the impact would otherwise create.
//
// And an ending closes EVERY task the contact was the subject of: both handlers
// end its Scan objective as well as its interception one, so nothing on the
// crew's panel — or in a Backfilled seat's directive pool — outlives the rock.
// That is a rule about CONTACTS, not about the two aimed ones, which is why the
// stray has `on_debris_stray_cleared` above: it has no interception order to end
// and nothing to resolve, but it has a reading task like the other two and it
// dies like the other two.
fn debris_pending(ctx, key) {
    ctx.flags["skyway_debris_" + key + "_resolved"] < 1
}

fn clear_one(ctx, key, objective, saved_flag, late_flag) {
    // A mass that has ALREADY LANDED was not intercepted. Breaking up the
    // wreckage is a reasonable thing for a crew to do and the rock is still
    // there to be shot at; what it is not is a save, and the rung's record must
    // not say otherwise.
    if ctx.flags["skyway_debris_" + key + "_struck"] > 0 { return; }
    if !debris_pending(ctx, key) { return; }
    // Late is judged off the URGENCY flag rather than off a second clock: the
    // engine already decided when this contact entered its authored window, and
    // asking the same question twice is how two answers start disagreeing.
    if ctx.flags["skyway_debris_" + key + "_urgent"] > 0 {
        ctx.flags[late_flag] = 1;
        ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_debris_late_" + key);
    } else {
        ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_debris_cleared_" + key);
    }
    ctx.flags[saved_flag] = 1;
    ctx.effects.complete_objective(objective);
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.debris_" + key + ".name", "destroyed");
    // A contact that ENDS closes every task it was the subject of, not just the
    // one about shooting it.
    //
    // A human Tactical is free to lock and break up an unread mass — the file's
    // own header calls that legitimate — and when they do, the Scan objective
    // that named this contact would otherwise sit Active on the crew's panel for
    // the rest of the mission, pointing at an entity that no longer exists and
    // keeping a Backfilled Sensors seat asking for a reading of a name nothing
    // can resolve. Failed rather than completed, because for an unread contact
    // the honest record is that nobody ever looked; a mass that WAS read has
    // already completed this objective on its `_read` flag and
    // `ObjectiveManager::fail` moves `Active` records only, so this is a no-op
    // there rather than a downgrade.
    ctx.effects.fail_objective(debris_scan_objective(key));
    debris_resolved(ctx, key);
}

fn on_debris_lead_cleared(ctx) {
    clear_one(ctx, "lead", "obj-a3-debris-lead",
        "skyway_ladder_a_debris_saved", "skyway_ladder_a_debris_late");
}

fn on_debris_trail_cleared(ctx) {
    clear_one(ctx, "trail", "obj-a3-debris-trail",
        "skyway_ladder_b_debris_saved", "skyway_ladder_b_debris_late");
}

// The rung takes it.
//
// THE SIZE OF THIS NUMBER IS A CONSTRAINT, NOT A TASTE. A struck rung must read
// worse and must NOT, on its own, stop pumping.
//
// Act 3 already has a supply chain — the head's lift certification and the two
// rungs' pumping lines meet at one number in the transfer window — and the
// debris beat is a PARALLEL track laid beside it, not a lever on it. At 30
// points this silently became a lever: an unread mass landing on Ladder A took
// it from 62 to 32 through a 40 % line, so a crew who never went and looked lost
// the window's supply for a reason the window was never about, and the act's own
// isolation ("the working rung went on working, which is what makes this a fact
// about the HEAD") stopped being true. Three of the window's outcome tests said
// so.
//
// 12 keeps the whole of the beat — the objective goes red, the asset is recorded
// harmed, the computer says so, the strike is filed against the rung — while
// leaving a rung that was pumping when it was hit still pumping afterwards. A
// rung already run down by something ELSE can still be pushed under by this,
// which is the honest reading: the mass is the last straw rather than the whole
// of the failure. `a_mass_nobody_stops_lands_on_the_rung_it_was_aimed_at` asserts
