// that both halves of this hold, so the constraint is checkable rather than a
// paragraph.
//
// [ai] 12 unratified.
fn strike_one(ctx, key, objective, depot, harmed_flag) {
    // Claimed before anything is written, the same way `clear_one` claims it.
    // The struck flag rises once, so this guard only ever bites in the
    // same-tick race — a killing shot that lands on the tick the mass crosses
    // its impact radius — and there it decides the tie in favour of whichever
    // handler the engine ran first, rather than letting both write.
    if !debris_pending(ctx, key) { return; }
    ctx.flags[harmed_flag] = 1;
    ctx.effects.fail_objective(objective);
    ctx.effects.damage_infrastructure(depot, 12);
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_debris_struck_" + key,
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.debris_struck_" + key,
        "critical",
        18,
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_debris_struck_" + key);
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    depot,
        text:       "world.falling_skyway.evidence.debris_strike",
        provenance: "scan",
    });
    // The same closure `clear_one` makes, for the other ending: a mass nobody
    // read and nobody stopped has still ENDED, and the task that asked for a
    // reading of it ends with it rather than outliving the rock on the panel.
    ctx.effects.fail_objective(debris_scan_objective(key));
    debris_resolved(ctx, key);
}

fn on_debris_lead_struck(ctx) {
    strike_one(ctx, "lead", "obj-a3-debris-lead",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_a.name",
        "skyway_ladder_a_debris_harmed");
}

fn on_debris_trail_struck(ctx) {
    strike_one(ctx, "trail", "obj-a3-debris-trail",
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.depot_ladder_b.name",
        "skyway_ladder_b_debris_harmed");
}

// CORRIDOR CLEAR. Counted rather than tested against the two contacts by name,
// so it stays right if a later slice sheds a third.
//
// The count is only trustworthy because the contribution is PER CONTACT: this
// closes `skyway_debris_<key>_resolved` first, which is the flag both terminal
// handlers claimed the contact through, so a second terminal event for a mass
// that has already ended never reaches here and the counter can never run ahead
// of the number of masses actually settled. A bare increment would let one rock
// count twice and declare the corridor clear with the other still inbound.
//
// Only the two aimed masses are counted. The stray resolves nothing because it
// was never a threat, and a corridor-clear cue that waited for it would be
// waiting on a rock that is simply leaving.
fn debris_resolved(ctx, key) {
    ctx.flags["skyway_debris_" + key + "_resolved"] = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("skyway_debris_resolved", 1);
    if ctx.flags.skyway_debris_resolved < 2 { return; }
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_debris_corridor_clear",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.debris_corridor_clear",
        "info",
        10,
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_corridor_clear");
}

fn debrief_workers_and_convoy(ctx)   { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_workers_and_convoy", responses: [] } }
fn debrief_workers_and_operator(ctx) { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_workers_and_operator", responses: [] } }
fn debrief_operator_and_convoy(ctx)  { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_operator_and_convoy", responses: [] } }
fn debrief_one(ctx)                  { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_one", responses: [] } }
fn debrief_none(ctx)                 { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_none", responses: [] } }
fn debrief_berth(ctx)                { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_berth", responses: [] } }
fn debrief_berth_none(ctx)           { #{ message: "world.falling_skyway.comms.debrief_berth_none", responses: [] } }

// ═══ THE CORRIDOR OBSTRUCTION — CONSEQUENCES (issue #1350) ═══════════════════
//
// The ENGINE ran the four stages and raised the flags (see the [[entity]]
// corridor_obstruction block above). This is every consequence, hung off those
// flags exactly as the #1347 debris band hangs its strikes — nothing here is a
// special case in Rust.
//
//   skyway_obstruction_charges_placed  → the team's work landed. A quiet beat,
//                                         and the arming of the detonate control
//                                         (the [demolition_target] reads it).
//   skyway_obstruction_detonated       → any shot fired. The generic beat.
//   skyway_obstruction_cleared_safe    → charges + team clear + HELD.  SAFE.
//   skyway_obstruction_cleared_unsupp. → charges + team clear + UNHELD. UNSUPPORTED.
//   skyway_obstruction_premature       → charges + team STILL ON IT.  CASUALTIES.
//   on_destroyed(corridor_obstruction) → no charges, killed by gunnery. WEAPONS.
//
// ── ONE OBSTRUCTION, ONE ENDING ─────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// The four terminal handlers are not mutually exclusive by construction: a SAFE
// detonation `destroy_entity`s the mass, which fires `on_destroyed` on the same
// tick's next chaining pass — the weapons handler. FIRST TERMINAL EVENT WINS:
// every handler claims the obstruction through `skyway_obstruction_resolved`
// BEFORE it writes or destroys anything, so the `on_destroyed` a detonation
// causes finds the mass already resolved and does nothing. The debris band's
// `debris_pending` idiom, one obstruction instead of three contacts.

on_flag_set("skyway_obstruction_charges_placed", "on_obstruction_charged");
on_flag_set("skyway_obstruction_detonated", "on_obstruction_detonated");
on_flag_set("skyway_obstruction_cleared_safe", "on_obstruction_safe");
on_flag_set("skyway_obstruction_cleared_unsupported", "on_obstruction_unsupported");
on_flag_set("skyway_obstruction_premature", "on_obstruction_premature");
on_destroyed("world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name", "on_obstruction_weapons_fire");

fn obstruction_pending(ctx) {
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_resolved"] < 1
}

// One drifting fragment of the shed slab, spawned at an authored offset from the
// wedge so the pieces do not stack on one point. Count is what differs between
// the outcomes — a limited scatter, a heavy one, or the worst — so this is one
// call the endings spend a different number of times.
//
// Each fragment is NAMED: `spawn_entity` requires a name (issue #1033's required-
// field check), so a fragment authored without one aborts the whole clearance with
// a script error the moment the obstruction resolves. The endings are mutually
// exclusive (first-terminal-event-wins), so at most one ending's fragments are ever
// spawned in a run and the small per-ending name set never collides.
fn obstruction_fragment(ctx, name, pos) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_large.toml",
        name: name,
        position: pos,
        groups: ["skyway_obstruction_debris"],
        overrides: #{ mass: 40 },
    });
}

// Stage-one telemetry: the charges are SET. A beat only — the detonate control is
// now armed, but placement completing must never fire it. That the crew now have
// to WITHDRAW and DETONATE as two further deliberate acts is the whole point of
// the beat, and the engine enforces it; this just records that stage one landed.
fn on_obstruction_charged(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_obstruction_charges_set");
}

// The generic "the charges went off" beat, raised on ANY shot before the specific
// outcome handler runs. So a headless after-action reading carries the detonation
// as an authored beat regardless of how it turned out.
fn on_obstruction_detonated(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_obstruction_detonation");
}

// SAFE: charges placed, the team clear, and the mass held. It comes apart into a
// LIMITED, drifting debris field and the corridor is clear.
fn on_obstruction_safe(ctx) {
    if !obstruction_pending(ctx) { return; }
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_resolved"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_cleared"] = 1;
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_1", [95, 0, -45]);
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_obstruction_cleared",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.obstruction_cleared",
        "info",
        10,
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_obstruction_safe");
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name", "destroyed");
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name");
}

// UNSUPPORTED: charges placed and the team clear, but the mass was NOT held when
// it went off. It clears — but into a HEAVIER, wider debris field than a held
// shot leaves.
fn on_obstruction_unsupported(ctx) {
    if !obstruction_pending(ctx) { return; }
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_resolved"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_cleared"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_unsupported_scatter"] = 1;
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_1", [95, 0, -45]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_2", [60, 10, -80]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_3", [110, -10, -30]);
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_obstruction_unsupported",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.obstruction_unsupported",
        "warning",
        14,
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_obstruction_unsupported");
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name", "destroyed");
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name");
}

// PREMATURE: the charges were fired with a Security team still on the mass. It
// clears — but the team is caught. A durable casualty record and a critical cue,
// the honest cost of not waiting for the team to withdraw. (The engine also ends
// that team's task with `TargetLost` the tick the mass is destroyed, so the
// interruption reaches the shared task-lifecycle telemetry for free.)
fn on_obstruction_premature(ctx) {
    if !obstruction_pending(ctx) { return; }
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_resolved"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_cleared"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_casualties"] = 1;
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_1", [95, 0, -45]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_2", [70, 5, -75]);
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_obstruction_premature",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.obstruction_premature",
        "critical",
        18,
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_obstruction_premature");
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome(
        "world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name", "destroyed");
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.falling_skyway.entity.corridor_obstruction.name");
}

// WEAPONS: nobody placed charges — a crew who reached for gunnery broke the
// wedged slab up in place. It clears, but into the WORST, least-controlled debris
// field of the four, scattered across the lane. This is the `on_destroyed` the
// weapons kill fires; it claims the obstruction like the others, so a detonation
// that `destroy_entity`s the mass finds it already resolved here and this is a
// no-op — only a genuine gunnery kill with no prior ending reaches the writes.
fn on_obstruction_weapons_fire(ctx) {
    if !obstruction_pending(ctx) { return; }
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_resolved"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_cleared"] = 1;
    ctx.flags["skyway_obstruction_weapons_scatter"] = 1;
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_1", [95, 0, -45]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_2", [55, 15, -85]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_3", [115, -12, -25]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_4", [45, -8, -35]);
    obstruction_fragment(ctx, "skyway_obstruction_debris_5", [125, 8, -70]);
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_obstruction_weapons",
        "world.falling_skyway.computer_message.obstruction_weapons",
        "warning",
        14,
    );
    ctx.effects.narrative_beat("skyway_obstruction_weapons");
    // No `destroy_entity` and no `narrative_outcome` here: the weapons kill that
    // fired this handler already destroyed the mass and recorded its outcome.
}

// ── THE OBSTRUCTION REPORT ROW (issue #1350, scored for the T2 refinement) ───
//
// A NEW scored report category, surfaced to John for ratification. The demolition
// has FOUR terminal outcomes, graded by lives and by debris control in the PRD's
// stated spirit ("lives and promises intentionally dominate"):
//
//   SAFE         charges placed, team clear, mass HELD → clean, limited debris.
//                The only clean positive. +3.
//   UNSUPPORTED  team clear but the mass UNHELD → cleared, but a heavier debris
//                field. No lives lost, an infrastructure cost only. -1.
//   WEAPONS      broken up by ordinary gunnery — no charges, no attempt at
//                control → the worst, uncontrolled debris across the lane. -2.
//   PREMATURE    fired with the Security team STILL ON THE MASS → team casualties.
//                The ONLY outcome that costs lives, so the steepest negative. -4.
//
// DOUBLE-COUNT CHECK: this row scores the OPERATION QUALITY, never the deaths. The
// premature outcome's `skyway_obstruction_casualties` flag is written nowhere else
// and is NOT one of the four terms summed into `campaign.skyway.casualties.total`
// (section 4), so no casualties line scores those bodies — this is the one place
// the demolition is scored, and it scores the CHOICE to fire early, not a headcount.
// If a later change ever folds the premature casualties into the casualties sum,
// THAT is the moment to keep the two distinct; this row must stay operation-quality.
//
// Omitted entirely if `skyway_obstruction_resolved == 0` — the obstruction was
// never touched, an absence that is a real answer, the skyhook/civilians rule.
// [ai] Every score unratified — a first proposal for John.
fn write_the_demolition_record(ctx) {
    if ctx.flags.skyway_obstruction_resolved == 0 { return; }
    // Exactly one terminal handler wins (first-terminal-event-wins, guarded on
    // `skyway_obstruction_resolved`), so the four are mutually exclusive. The
    // default is SAFE: resolved with none of the other three flags set is the
    // clean, held detonation, which raises `skyway_obstruction_cleared_safe`.
    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.demolition.safe";
    let state = "saved";
    let score = 3;
    if ctx.flags.skyway_obstruction_premature > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.demolition.premature";
        state = "lost";
        score = -4;
    } else if ctx.flags.skyway_obstruction_weapons_scatter > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.demolition.weapons";
        state = "lost";
        score = -2;
    } else if ctx.flags.skyway_obstruction_cleared_unsupported > 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.demolition.unsupported";
        state = "partial";
        score = -1;
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "demolition",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.demolition.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}

// ── THE CASTAWAY LIFEBOAT (issue #1348 mechanism, T2 refinement) ─────────────
//
// The Engineering transporter's own rescue, scored as its OWN report row — never
// folded into the head-survivors "civilians" row (#1351). The two are DIFFERENT
// people: the head survivors exist only if the skyhook is lost and the epilogue
// opens; these civilians can be beamed any time, independent of the head's fate,
// so both can resolve in one run. Folding them into one id would let whichever
// resolved last silently clobber the other's row — the double-jeopardy #1351 was
// built to prevent, moved from double-counting into double-erasure. A separate,
// independently-omitted row keeps both legible and the report total honest.
//
// Discovery requires a SCAN: `reveal_civilian_contacts` latches the contact once
// `scan.corridor_castaway.taken` rises, so the life signs never announce before
// the crew have looked. The Rescue-directive objective makes a Backfilled
// Engineering seat serve the beam through the same transporter commands a human
// sends — at base_priority 40, so a life-safety tractor Tow/Stabilise always
// outscores it for the shared Engineering seat (the Lyra rescue in Act 2 is
// priority 70) and the AI never robs a life-save to beam a lifeboat.

on_flag_set("scan.corridor_castaway.taken", "on_castaway_discovered");
on_flag_set("rescue.corridor_castaway.recovered", "on_castaway_recovered");
on_flag_set("rescue.corridor_castaway.lost", "on_castaway_lost");

fn on_castaway_discovered(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("castaway_discovered", 1);
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_castaway_life_signs",
        "world.falling_skyway.cue.castaway_life_signs",
        "advisory",
        8,
    );
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-castaway",
        text: "world.falling_skyway.objective.castaway_rescue.text",
        mandatory: false,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 40,
        directive_kind: "Rescue",
        target: "world.falling_skyway.entity.castaway_lifeboat.name",
        targets: ["world.falling_skyway.entity.castaway_lifeboat.name"],
    });
}

fn on_castaway_recovered(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("castaway_recovered", 1);
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-castaway");
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_castaway_recovered",
        "world.falling_skyway.cue.castaway_recovered",
        "info",
        8,
    );
    castaway_report_row(ctx);
}

fn on_castaway_lost(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("castaway_lost", 1);
    ctx.effects.fail_objective("obj-castaway");
    ctx.effects.show_message(
        "skyway_castaway_lost",
        "world.falling_skyway.cue.castaway_lost",
        "critical",
        8,
    );
    castaway_report_row(ctx);
}

// The transporter-civilians row. Its OWN id, never "civilians". Scored off the PRD
// civilian figures: +1 per civilian recovered, -2 per one lost. Three souls aboard
// (matches the lifeboat's authored [civilian_rescue] count), so a clean rescue is
// +3 and losing the boat with all aboard is -6. Written at the tick the fate
// resolves (the Lyra/civilians rule) and re-callable — writing the same id updates
// the one row in place, so a run reports one coherent row. Omitted until a fate
// lands: an undiscovered or never-resolved contact reports no row at all.
fn castaway_report_row(ctx) {
    let recovered = ctx.flags["rescue.corridor_castaway.recovered"];
    let lost = ctx.flags["rescue.corridor_castaway.lost"];
    if recovered + lost == 0 { return; }
    // Three aboard — the lifeboat's authored count. [ai] Unratified; keep in step
    // with skyway_castaway_lifeboat.toml's [civilian_rescue] count.
    let aboard = 3;
    let outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.transporter_civilians.saved";
    let state = "saved";
    let score = aboard;
    if recovered == 0 {
        outcome = "world.falling_skyway.report.transporter_civilians.lost";
        state = "lost";
        score = -2 * aboard;
    }
    ctx.effects.report_row(#{
        id: "transporter_civilians",
        heading: "world.falling_skyway.report.transporter_civilians.heading",
        outcome: outcome,
        state: state,
        score: score,
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/patrol.toml:
# Patrol World
#
# A standalone world: a single pirate raider patrols three waypoints. Destroying
# the raider completes a mission objective. No stations, no comms, just combat
# practice.
#
# Anchors are inlined here (this world does not share state with default.toml).
#
# ── HOLDS at 11531679067393217131 over the thrust-band fix, and why ──────────
#
# The AI-thrust-burst fix banded the helm power rules of eight hulls, one of
# which this world fields (`ship_harrow_patrol`, the raider) alongside the player
# cruiser's inherited `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`. This digest does not
# move, and that is a claim.
#
# MEASURED: 0 helm power changes across the 900-tick window, banded or not. The
# raider patrols alone at the far side of its triangle with the player ship
# AI-backfilled and parked, so it stays at low LOD — and `ai_power_allocation` is
# `With<AiHighFidelity>`, so it never runs the helm rules at all. A band on a
# rule that never resolves folds nothing.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state — this world's own
# `on_world_loaded`/`on_destroyed` triggers are latches on
# `WorldContentRuntime::trigger_states`, now walked by
# `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records`, which did not happen when
# 11531679067393217131 was measured. The thrust-band A/B is untouched — it is a
# same-build comparison, and "0 helm power changes" is still the finding — but
# the absolute value predates the fold and does not reproduce on a clean tree.
# Re-measure before treating it as a baseline again.

[global]
seed = 42
title = "world.patrol.global.title"
description = "world.patrol.global.description"

[anchors]
patrol_alpha = [600.0, 0.0, -600.0]
patrol_beta  = [-600.0, 0.0, -400.0]
patrol_gamma = [0.0, 0.0, -1000.0]
# Where a mauled raider runs to. Referenced by the `retreat-when-hurt` doctrine
# this world authors on `raider_alpha` below; set well outside the patrol
# triangle so a retreat visibly breaks off the engagement rather than circling it.
pirate_haven = [-1200.0, 0.0, -1400.0]

# ── Static map entities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/star_sun.toml"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_field_main.toml"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── Named entities (trigger / comms-eligible) ────────────────────────────────
#
# PRD #337 slice 3: the patrol raider migrated from `[[spawn]]` to a named
# `[[entity]]` with `transform = { anchor = "patrol_alpha" }`. The unified
# pipeline assigns a UUID at spawn time, registers `raider_alpha` → uuid in
# `WorldConfig.name_to_uuid`, and `spawn_world_entities` wires the AI
# components (BehaviourSection, FactionComponent) via the shared
# `spawn_entity` helper.

#
# (#892) The hull was `pirate_raider.toml`, retired as a duplicate of
# `ship_harrow_destroyer.toml`'s display name. This world is a single-ship
# combat-practice encounter against a patrolling hull, so the replacement is the
# Ironveil-class patrol cruiser, not the Harrow Destroyer: the Destroyer authors
# no Patrol doctrine, so it would sit inert on `patrol_alpha` and this world's
# stated premise — "a single raider patrols three waypoints" — would be gone
# along with the two waypoints nothing else names.
#
# The two overrides restate what this world (not the hull) supplied: the
# Ironveil's `ironveil_patrol_*` circuit is retargeted onto the triangle
# declared above, and the `retreat-when-hurt` Retreat to `pirate_haven` is
# appended. See the fuller note in `default.toml`.
#
# Neither override touches `base_priority`, so the #892 picket rebase applies
# here unmodified: this hull now holds its route until fired upon (Patrol 45 >
# Destroy 38 undisturbed; attacked flips it to 63 > 30), superseding the old
# engage-on-sight reading. Flagged for review if engage-on-sight is actually
# wanted for this raider.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
name          = "world.entity.raider_alpha.name"
transform     = { anchor = "patrol_alpha" }
overrides = { tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"], behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "patrol-ironveil", directive_anchors = ["patrol_alpha", "patrol_beta", "patrol_gamma"] },
  { id = "retreat-when-hurt", directive_kind = "Retreat", directive_anchor = "pirate_haven",
    base_priority = 100.0, target_speed = 1.0,
    zero_gates = [{ condition = "hull_below", threshold = 0.3 }] },
] } }

# ── Script ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Tracer objective (issue #571): a Patrol directive added on world load, scored
# by the viewscreen aggregator and rendered as prose on the captain panel.
# Destroying the raider adds the completion objective.
[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");
on_destroyed("world.entity.raider_alpha.name", "on_raider_destroyed");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-patrol-sector",
        text: "world.patrol.trigger.action.obj_patrol_sector.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 40,
        directive_kind: "Patrol",
        directive_anchors: ["patrol_alpha", "patrol_beta", "patrol_gamma"],
        directive_loop: true,
        zero_gates: [#{ condition: "hull_below", threshold: flt("0.1") }]
    });
}

fn on_raider_destroyed(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-raider-destroyed",
        text: "world.patrol.trigger.action.obj_raider_destroyed.text",
        mandatory: false
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_aggressor.toml:
# Probe world for issue #842 — a backfilled player hull engages on its own
# template doctrine, with NO scenario objective in play.
#
# A player Alliance cruiser (AI-backfilled in a headless run) is placed next to a
# world-spawned Alliance destroyer that has been re-flagged to the Harrow faction
# and given an EMPTY doctrine (`behaviour = { doctrine = [] }`). Harrow and
# Alliance are made mutually hostile at world-load.
#
# An override array that is authored EMPTY clears the template's list — see
# "An authored empty array clears the list" in `src/entities/entity_override.rs`.
# That is what makes the line below a real subtraction rather than a no-op; while
# it merged by id and an empty list merged nothing, this hull kept its template
# `destroy-hostiles` doctrine and won the fight it is supposed to lose.
#
# The point is the asymmetry of intent: the destroyer, with no Destroy doctrine,
# has nothing standing that licenses it to engage. It may still be handed a lock
# by its own Sensors AI, and the `last-attacker` source can offer it whoever shot
# it (see `ai_target_selection` in `src/console/weapons/mod.rs`), but it never
# initiates — over this probe's 30 seconds it fires nothing at all. The player,
# on the other hand, now carries the default `[behaviour]` doctrine authored on
# its hull template (#842), whose UNTARGETED Destroy licenses the
# nearest-hostile scan. So the only ship that can open fire is the player — any
# damage it deals proves it engaged PROACTIVELY off its template doctrine, not
# reactively after being hit. There is deliberately no `add_objective` trigger:
# nothing but the template doctrine is driving the player.

[global]
seed = 842
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player ship — spawned by spawn_game_start_entities when the game starts.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# Make Harrow and Alliance mutually hostile before the destroyer spawns, then
# spawn the passive hostile destroyer inside the player's phaser range (40u) at
# t=0. The empty doctrine override strips the template's default combat doctrine,
# leaving a hull with nothing standing that licenses it to engage — never an
# initiator.
[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");
on_timer(0, "on_start");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}

fn on_start(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml",
        name: "probe_target",
        position: [35, 0, 0],
        overrides: #{
            faction: "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc",
            behaviour: #{ doctrine: [] }
        }
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_artillery_standoff.t:
# Probe world for issue #792 — regression harness for "the battleship never
# actually holds its firing position".
#
# The Harrow battleship's artillery doctrine parks it at `artillery_hold_range`
# (180 units) and stops. Every unit test of that doctrine runs on a bare `App`
# carrying the helm axes alone, and for a while none of them carried the impulse
# drive — so the doctrine was measured in a world without the one component that
# overrides it. In production `entities::spawner` attaches an
# `ImpulseConfigResource` to every hull with a `[helm_console]`, the impulse
# autopilot hard-overrides commanded throttle with `thrust = 1.0`, and the
# battleship flew straight through its own gun line at full speed.
#
# The geometry here is the whole point and is what no other world provides:
#
#   * The battleship starts 300 units out — OUTSIDE its own 200-unit artillery
#     envelope — so it has to fly a real run-in and the stopping point is
#     something it reaches rather than something it spawned on. `duel.toml`
#     anchors side B 55 units from the player — well below the default
#     `impulse_engage_distance` of 200, so the drive never engages there and the
#     standoff is never exercised at all.
#   * 300 is inside the hull's own 320-unit `sensor_range`, so it promotes to
#     high fidelity on the first tick and its helm doctrine actually runs.
#   * The doctrine is REPLACED by the `overrides` below, exactly as
#     `combat_test.toml`'s wave 8 replaces it, and — like it — the replacement
#     does not author `use_impulse`. So a fix that leaned on the hull's own
#     `[[behaviour.doctrine]] use_impulse = false` would be erased here. The fix
#     has to live somewhere a scenario doctrine cannot reach.
#
#     "Replaced" is by ID and not wholesale, which this file used to claim:
#     `merge_id_array` keeps every template entry the override does not name.
#     The `kill` entry below therefore lands ALONGSIDE `patrol-warhawk` and
#     `destroy-hostiles`, and the patrol it left in place routes between
#     `warhawk_patrol_a`/`_b` — anchors this probe declares nowhere, since it
#     declares no anchors at all. The second override entry says what the header
#     always meant: in this world the battleship has no patrol, only `kill`.
#     (Issue #888; it costs nothing behaviourally, because an unresolvable
#     Patrol was already steering the hull nowhere and `kill` outscores it 80
#     to 20 regardless.)
#
# ── Why the hostility is one-directional ──────────────────────────────────────
#
# Only Harrow is told that Alliance is an enemy. The battleship therefore
# acquires and closes on the player, while the player's own untargeted Destroy
# doctrine resolves no hostile and falls through to `alliance_cruiser`'s
# `hold-station` (target_speed 0.0). A stationary target is what makes "comes to
# rest at the hold range" a reading of the BATTLESHIP's travel rather than of two
# ships converging — the measurement would otherwise mix the player's approach
# into the number under test.

[global]
seed = 7920
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player ship — spawned by spawn_game_start_entities when the game starts, and
# AI-backfilled because nobody connects in a headless run.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

[script]
setup = """
// One direction only — see the header.
on_world_loaded("on_load");

// The battleship, 300 units out along +X.
on_timer(0, "spawn_battleship");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
}

fn spawn_battleship(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/ship_harrow_warhawk.toml",
        name: "artillery_platform",
        position: [300, 0, 0],
        overrides: #{
            faction: "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc",
            behaviour: #{ doctrine: [
                #{ id: "kill", directive_kind: "Destroy",
                   base_priority: 80, target_speed: flt("0.9"), maintain_range: 25 },
                #{ id: "patrol-warhawk", directive_kind: "None", directive_anchors: [], directive_loop: false },
            ] },
        },
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_attack_pass_cycle.to:
# Probe world for issue #937 — the destroyer must CYCLE its attack pass.
#
# `movement_attack_pass.toml`'s whole shape is a loop: line up, run in, commit to
# an outward heading, turn back, run in again. Every existing probe of it stops at
# the first leg. `probe_targeted_pass.toml` asserts that ONE escape happens and
# that its heading is held; `probe_duel.toml` asserts the hull moves at all.
# Neither can see the failure this world exists for, which is that the loop runs
# once and then stops.
#
# ── The geometry, and why it is a Harrow CRUISER on the other side ────────────
#
# The closest-approach detector that ends `inbound` is three conjuncts, and the
# load-bearing one is `fact(closing_rate) < param(closing_rate_epsilon)` — the
# gap has started opening. `closing_rate` is not a difference of two range
# readings: it is the radial component of the RELATIVE velocity, reconstructed
# from both ships' `(yaw, forward_speed)`. So it is only as good as the heading
# the world snapshot publishes for the OTHER ship, and a hull that reads its
# target's heading wrong reads "still closing" while it is flying away.
#
# That is exactly what happened (issue #937): `build_world_snapshot` published
# every entity's heading off its RENDER transform, which carries the negation
# `sync_ship_position` applies, so every target's velocity came back mirrored.
# The destroyer merged, never called closest approach, and ground along at
# contact range against the ship it had just rammed — the reported "orbits at
# ~range 5 instead of making attack runs".
#
# The other ship must therefore MANOEUVRE, and manoeuvre differently from the
# destroyer, or the error cancels: two hulls flying the same fly-through pass
# meet nearly head-on, where a mirrored velocity is still mostly radial and the
# detector fires anyway (which is why `probe_duel` passes either way). A Harrow
# cruiser flies `movement_broadside_orbit.toml` — it circles rather than passes
# — so at the merge its velocity is mostly TANGENTIAL, the component the mirror
# corrupts most, and it stays alongside afterwards instead of flying out. That
# pairing is the one that jams, and it is the pairing `combat_test.toml` wave 1
# actually puts in front of a destroyer player.
#
# 140 units of separation, along +X:
#
#   * inside the destroyer captain's `alert_on_hostile_within` (150), so the
#     alert is up on the first tick and `posture` presses the doctrine from the
#     start — this world is not a test of the posture gate, which
#     `authored_ai_pins::posture_guard_truth_table` already owns;
#   * OUTSIDE the destroyer's own `commit_range` (120), so `acquire` → `inbound`
#     is a transition it reaches by flying rather than one it spawns on;
#   * well inside both hulls' authored `sensor_range`, so neither drops to low
#     LOD mid-manoeuvre and freezes on a dead-reckoned heading.
#
# Hostility is mutual: a one-directional grudge would leave the cruiser passive,
# and a passive target does not orbit.

[global]
seed = 937
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player ship — the headless runner's `--ship` supersedes this template; the
# entry exists so `spawn_game_start_entities` has a player to spawn.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The orbiting hostile. Its own template doctrine (`destroy-hostiles`, an
# UNTARGETED Destroy) is what licenses the nearest-hostile scan, so no override
# is needed to make it engage — and none is authored, so this world exercises
# the shipped hull rather than a scenario-local variant of it.
[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");
on_timer(0, "on_start");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}

fn on_start(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/ship_harrow_cruiser.toml",
        name: "probe_orbiter",
        position: [140, 0, 0]
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_civilian_traffic.tom:
# Probe world for issue #1028 — civilian routes and orders, end to end.
#
# Four haulers on two authored lanes, one order each, chosen so that every
# outcome the compliance machine can produce is on screen at once and none of
# them can be mistaken for another:
#
#   kestrel  cooperative, on `depot_run`   -> divert onto `storm_detour`  -> COMPLIES
#   wren     refuses diverts, on `depot_run` -> divert onto `storm_detour` -> REFUSES
#   teal     cooperative, on `depot_run`   -> dock at the depot           -> COMPLIES
#   gull     cooperative, on `depot_run`   -> dock at a depot that is not
#                                              in this world              -> NON_COMPLIANT
#
# and then, at t = 12 s, kestrel is told to HOLD, which is the third verb and
# the one whose effect is the absence of a directive rather than a new one.
#
# The two refusal outcomes are the point of having four craft rather than two.
# `wren` REFUSED and `gull` NON_COMPLIANT are the states a console has to be
# able to tell apart — one declined and carried on down its own lane, the other
# agreed and got stuck — and a probe that only produced one of them would pass
# with the two folded together.
#
# No combat anywhere: every hull here is unarmed, neutral, and slow, so the run
# is a deterministic tripwire for the traffic chain rather than a fight that
# happens to involve civilians.
#
# Timeline (dt = 1/30 s in the headless test):
#
#   t  0     four haulers spawn on `depot_run` leg 0, flying north
#   t  2     the four orders are issued
#   t ~2-4   each craft answers: three acknowledge, `wren` refuses outright
#   t ~5-7   the three that acknowledged act on it (2 s ack + 3 s decide is the
#            default disposition; `wren`'s refusal needs only the ack)
#   t 12     kestrel is told to hold and comes off its lane entirely
#
# BASELINE. `--seed 42 --ticks 900` gives final digest 0xa878bb772b89f514
# (12139658916083135764), and 11547223486943852427 at tick 0.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state — the `orders_issued` and
# `hold_issued` flags `issue_orders`/`hold_the_kestrel` set above are FlagStore
# entries, and the flag store is now walked by `sim_digest::fold_scenario_flags`
# / `fold_scenario_records`, which did not happen when either number on this
# page was measured. Re-measure before treating either as a baseline again.
#
# MOVED in #1027 for one reason, and it has nothing to do with traffic: the
# depot `teal` docks at carries an `[[infrastructure.capacity]]`, and a
# capacity's LEVEL is folded into the authoritative digest now that a `transfer`
# operation can move it. Nothing about civilian routes, orders or compliance
# changed, and no craft in this world performs an operation.
#
# The #1028 baseline, for the record, was 7003882644112311952.

[global]
seed = 1028
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[anchors]
# The depot run: a short two-leg circuit, deliberately tight so a hauler
# actually completes a leg inside a probe-length run rather than merely setting
# off in the right direction. The arrival radius is 20 u, so ~140 u legs at
# 12 u/s are a real traverse and a real arrival.
lane_north = [0.0, 0.0, -70.0]
lane_south = [0.0, 0.0, 70.0]

# Where a diverted craft is sent instead: off the lane entirely, so "it took the
# detour" and "it is still on its circuit" cannot be confused positionally.
detour_west = [-160.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The berth. The depot itself sits here, and a docking craft closes on the
# ENTITY rather than on this anchor — the anchor exists so the world can place
# the depot without inline coordinates.
depot_berth = [170.0, 0.0, 40.0]

# ── Lanes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The standing traffic pattern. Loops, so a craft left alone keeps flying it for
# the whole mission — which is what makes "it stopped" and "it turned off"
# observable events rather than the end of its script.
[[route]]
id = "depot_run"
on_complete = "loop"

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "lane_north"
speed = 1.0
# A pause at the northern end, so the probe also exercises an authored dwell:
# the craft keeps its directive and its place on the lane, at zero throttle.
hold_secs = 3

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "lane_south"
speed = 1.0

# The alternate a divert order puts a craft on. Terminates rather than loops: a
# detour has somewhere to be, and a craft that reaches the end of it holds
# there.
[[route]]
id = "storm_detour"
on_complete = "terminate"

[[route.leg]]
anchor = "detour_west"
speed = 1.0

# ── The world ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[player_spawn]
position = [1200.0, 0.0, 1200.0]

# Player ship — spawned at game start so the world reaches InProgress and the
# NPC simulation runs. Parked far from the lanes and outside AI sensor range so
# it never interferes with the traffic under test.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [1200.0, 0.0, 1200.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The berth `teal` is ordered to dock at. A transfer depot rather than a bare
# marker, because a dock order names a STRUCTURE and this is the shipped one.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
name = "world.entity.probe_depot.name"
transform = { anchor = "depot_berth" }

# The cooperative hauler that takes its divert.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.entity.hauler_kestrel.name"
transform = { position = [-20.0, 0.0, 60.0] }
overrides = { civilian = { route = "depot_run" } }

# The one that will not. Its disposition refuses diverts and nothing else, so
# the hold it is never given would be obeyed — the refusal is per verb, not a
# personality that says no to everything.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.entity.hauler_wren.name"
transform = { position = [20.0, 0.0, 60.0] }
overrides = { civilian = { route = "depot_run", compliance = { divert = "refuse", refusal_reason = "world.probe_civilian_traffic.wren.refusal" } } }

# The one that docks.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.entity.hauler_teal.name"
transform = { position = [-20.0, 0.0, 40.0] }
overrides = { civilian = { route = "depot_run" } }

# The one that agrees to dock at something this world does not have. Its order
# is well-formed and it is addressed correctly — the craft resolves, the order
# is delivered, and only the DESTINATION is missing, which is the only way to
# reach `non_compliant` rather than a rejection bounce.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.entity.hauler_gull.name"
transform = { position = [20.0, 0.0, 40.0] }
overrides = { civilian = { route = "depot_run" } }

[script]
setup = """
on_timer(2, "issue_orders");
on_timer(12, "hold_the_kestrel");

fn issue_orders(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.entity.hauler_kestrel.name", "storm_detour");
    ctx.effects.order_divert_route("world.entity.hauler_wren.name", "storm_detour");
    ctx.effects.order_dock("world.entity.hauler_teal.name", "world.entity.probe_depot.name");
    // Well-formed, correctly addressed, and pointed at a berth nobody built.
    ctx.effects.order_dock("world.entity.hauler_gull.name", "world.entity.depot_that_never_was.name");
    ctx.flags.orders_issued = 1;
}

fn hold_the_kestrel(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.order_hold("world.entity.hauler_kestrel.name");
    ctx.flags.hold_issued = 1;
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_deadlines.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1024 — named mission deadlines, end to end.
#
# A player Alliance destroyer (AI-backfilled in a headless run) sits alone; no
# combat is involved on purpose. This is a deterministic tripwire for the whole
# deadline path — `[[deadline]]` parse → `on_deadline` pairing → arming onto the
# EXISTING `pending_callbacks` queue → `ctx.deadlines` inspection → slip/cancel
# re-keying that queue → firing on a `SimTick`.
#
# The authored timeline, in mission seconds:
#
#   t=2   `adjust` runs. It reads `window_opens`' remaining time (8 s: authored
#         for 10, two seconds in), SLIPS it by 5, and CANCELS
#         `stabiliser_failure`.
#   t=4   `first_warning` fires. Not slipped, not cancelled, not visible — the
#         control, proving arming works and that `visible = false` keeps a
#         deadline off the crew's panel without keeping it off the clock.
#   t=10  NOTHING. `window_opens`' authored time passes with its queued call
#         retracted. This is the assertion the whole slice turns on.
#   t=12  NOTHING. `stabiliser_failure`'s authored time passes; it was cancelled.
#   t=15  `window_opens` fires, at 10 + 5.
#
# Every handler increments a counter flag, so the headless test reads fire ORDER
# and fire COUNT out of the flag store rather than out of a log line, and
# `window_remaining_at_adjust` records what script read back mid-run.
#
# BASELINE (this world is new in #1024, so this is its first recorded digest):
# `--seed 42 --ticks 900` gives final digest 0xc419b89426b6013c
# (14130528252295774524). Measured on a clean tree at the commit that added this
# line. It is a NEW number, not a preserved one — nothing to compare it against
# yet — so it is written down here to be the thing a later change is A/B'd
# against, the way the shipped worlds' digests already are.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state — the flag stores, the
# trigger latches and the named records (deadlines, commitments, evidence,
# workforce) among them — so `WorldContentRuntime::deadlines`, the whole point
# of this world, is now walked by `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` rather
# than merely snapshotted. The number above predates that fold and does not
# reproduce on a clean tree. Re-measure before treating it as a baseline again.

[global]
seed = 1024
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player ship — spawned by spawn_game_start_entities when the game starts.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The named deadlines ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Authored data only: id, crew-facing label (a strings.csv id, never English),
# due time in whole seconds from mission start, and whether the crew sees it.
# The fn each one runs is named by `on_deadline` in the [script] block below.

[[deadline]]
id = "window_opens"
label = "world.probe_deadlines.deadline.window_opens.label"
due_secs = 10
visible = true

[[deadline]]
id = "stabiliser_failure"
label = "world.probe_deadlines.deadline.stabiliser_failure.label"
due_secs = 12
visible = true

# Deliberately invisible: it still arms, still fires, and still runs its handler
# — it simply never reaches the captain's panel.
[[deadline]]
id = "first_warning"
label = "world.probe_deadlines.deadline.first_warning.label"
due_secs = 4
visible = false

[script]
setup = """
on_timer(2, "adjust");

on_deadline("window_opens", "on_window_opens");
on_deadline("stabiliser_failure", "on_stabiliser_failure");
on_deadline("first_warning", "on_first_warning");

// The mutation beat. Reads a deadline back before touching it — the
// inspectability half — then moves one and calls the other off.
fn adjust(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("window_remaining_at_adjust", ctx.deadlines.remaining("window_opens"));
    ctx.deadlines.slip("window_opens", 5);
    ctx.deadlines.cancel("stabiliser_failure");
    // Read-after-write within the one call: both must already report the new
    // state to the rest of this handler.
    ctx.flags.increment("window_remaining_after_slip", ctx.deadlines.remaining("window_opens"));
    if ctx.deadlines.state("stabiliser_failure") == "cancelled" {
        ctx.flags.increment("stabiliser_reads_cancelled", 1);
    }
}

fn on_window_opens(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("window_fired", 1);
    // A deadline's own handler sees its state as fired while it runs.
    if ctx.deadlines.state("window_opens") == "fired" {
        ctx.flags.increment("window_reads_fired", 1);
    }
}

fn on_stabiliser_failure(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("stabiliser_fired", 1);
}

fn on_first_warning(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("warning_fired", 1);
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_debris.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1347 — one drifting mass, one thing under it, and a
# ship that can read the mass.
#
# It exists for the SAVE, not for the beat. `falling_skyway.toml` owns the beat
# and `tests/headless_runner.rs` drives it; what no test there can reach is the
# question this world is built to ask: what does a peer joining by snapshot
# transfer, or a crew resuming a save, get handed?
#
# A debris contact carries two things nothing else in a save carries:
#
#   1. WHERE IT HAS GOT TO. A rock has no `ShipPhysics`, so the entity
#      namespace's `physics` field — the thing that puts every other moving
#      object back where it flew to — is `None` for one of these, and
#      `SpawnOrigin` deliberately records where a mass was SHED rather than where
#      it has since travelled. `debris::server::tick_debris_drift` is the only
#      writer of that transform in the whole simulation.
#
#   2. WHAT THE CREW ESTABLISHED. `assessed` / `confirmed` / `urgent` / `struck`
#      are the record of somebody having looked, and the entire beat is the
#      difference between a mass the simulation privately knows is on course and
#      a mass a crew have READ. A joiner handed the geometry alone comes back
#      with every contact unread: its Backfilled Tactical drops the confirmed
#      lock (the candidate source filters on `confirmed`) and its Sensors seat
#      re-scans a field the host had already worked.
#
# So: one destroyer with its shipped `[scan]` ladder unmodified, one depot, and
# one mass aimed straight at the depot from up-track. The test flies the ship,
# takes a reading through the ordinary admitted `ScanTarget` path, captures, and
# resumes. Nothing here is scripted — there is no `[script]` block at all, which
# is deliberate: a scenario that raised the flags itself would prove the flag
# store round-trips, which is a different claim that already has its own tests.

[global]
seed = 1347
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The reading ship. The destroyer's own shipped `[scan]` ladder is used
# unmodified — this world overrides nothing about the suite — so the run is a
# test of the hull the demo actually flies rather than of a fixture.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── What is under the rock ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A published structure at the origin. Its condition track is not the subject
# here; what it is for is to be the `protected_target` the projection is taken
# against, which is the only way a contact can ever be CONFIRMED.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "probe_depot"
name = "world.probe_debris.entity.depot.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { infrastructure = { condition = 80.0, decay_per_sec = 0.0 } }

# ── The mass ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 600 units up-track of the depot, closing at 4 units a second on a 30-unit
# impact radius: about 142 seconds to arrive, which is far longer than any
# capture this world is used for, so the rock is always still in flight when the
# save is taken. It drifts on the x axis alone so a reader can check the
# translation by eye.
#
# The `[infrastructure]` table is not decoration. `science::scan` refuses a
# subject with no readable condition track, and the debris projection is folded
# into the reading that refusal would replace — so a mass with no condition
# track is a mass no crew can read, and there would be nothing to save.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_large.toml"
id = "probe_debris_mass"
name = "world.probe_debris.entity.mass.name"
transform = { position = [600.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition_max = 60.0
decay_per_sec = 0.0

[entity.overrides.debris]
drift = [-4.0, 0.0, 0.0]
protected_target = "world.probe_debris.entity.depot.name"
impact_radius = 30.0
# A minute's warning, and a reading that is taken once. Neither number is
# exercised by the save test; they are here because a `[debris]` table that
# authored no urgency window would be an unusual one to round-trip.
urgent_secs = 60.0
reassess_secs = 0.0
assessed_flag = "probe_debris_read"
confirmed_flag = "probe_debris_confirmed"
urgent_flag = "probe_debris_urgent"
impact_flag = "probe_debris_struck"
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_dock.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1159 — helm docking, end to end.
#
# One dock-fitted probe hull and one passive berth, drawn up close enough that the
# probe's helm dock control is in range. There is no combat and no scripted dock:
# the probe is a backfilled player ship, so the headless test drives the dock
# through the ordinary admitted Dock / Undock path (the only way to prove the
# command rides the same admission the helm console's own control would), and lets
# the dock manoeuvre fly the own ship onto its mate.
#
# WHAT THIS WORLD PROVES:
#
#   1. TWO HULLS REACH A MATED DOCK. With the berth in range and the dock engaged,
#      the probe's nearest viable dock-marker pair is flown onto the berth's — its
#      starboard plate meeting the berth's port plate — and the two hulls settle
#      into a published, folded docked relationship.
#
#   2. UNDOCK SEPARATES THEM. Undock backs the probe clear of the berth and the
#      docked relationship ends, returning ordinary flight.
#
#   3. EACH INTERRUPTION ENDS THE DOCK CLEANLY. The test drives them in turn —
#      drifting the berth out of range, cutting the dock's power, knocking the dock
#      out to Disabled, and destroying the berth — and after each the dock ends and
#      the probe is no longer mated.
#
# Nothing this world exercises is authored anywhere but the probe's own `[dock]`
# table, its `[[system]] kind = "dock"`, and the dock markers in the `dock_probe`
# rig sidecar. A hull that authored none carries no dock and is unchanged, which
# is why the shipped destroyer is deliberately NOT the operator here.

[global]
seed = 1159
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The probe — the backfilled player ship, spawned at game start, facing -Z.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/dock_probe.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The berth — a passive dockable structure 100 units to starboard, well inside the
# probe's 200-unit dock range. It carries dock markers (from the shared dock_probe
# sidecar) and a name the blackboard can report; the test never moves it under its
# own power, so it holds station until the test drifts or destroys it.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/dock_berth.toml"
name = "world.probe_dock.entity.berth.name"
transform = { position = [100.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_dossier.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1030 — the dossier projection, with the thing it must
# never show sitting right there in the world.
#
# Four subjects and one non-subject, chosen so that every branch of the roster
# rule and both hidden-truth gates are on screen at once and none can be
# mistaken for another. No combat: every fact here is authored, so the run is a
# deterministic tripwire for the projection rather than a fight that happens to
# damage something.
#
#   skyway_control      a hailable starbase, Alliance      -> affiliation + hailing range
#   strike_committee    a hailable hull, Requiem, and the
#                       party a promise is made to           -> affiliation + range + promise
#   skyway_depot        a PUBLISHED structure, not hailable  -> condition + the LABELLED
#                                                               threshold and capacity only
#   sealed_depot        a hailable structure the scenario
#                       keeps OFF the wire, sitting at 31/100 -> hailing range, and no
#                                                                condition of any kind
#   lonely_beacon       hailable by nobody, publishing
#                       nothing                              -> NOT a subject at all
#
# THE TWO GATES, both authored here rather than described:
#
#   1. `sealed_depot` authors `publish = false` and a real condition of 31
#      points. It is still a subject — the crew can see it out of the window and
#      can hail it — but its condition reaches no fact, because the projection
#      consumes `InfrastructureSnapshot::from_state`, which is #1025's publish
#      gate, and therefore never holds the number at all.
#   2. `skyway_depot` publishes two capacities and one threshold, and authors a
#      crew-facing `label` for only one capacity. The unlabelled
#      `depot_transfer_throughput` is published DATA a script can read and not
#      published PROSE, so it is not a row. A capacity id is a machine name in
#      the author's namespace (#1025 says so on the field itself) and putting one
#      on a fact sheet would be the first English on the wire.
#
# `lonely_beacon` is the fifth entity for the reason #1028's probe has four
# haulers: a rule that only ever admits is not a rule. It carries a name and a
# description and is hailable by nobody, so it proves the roster is a decision
# rather than "every entity in the world".
#
# The timeline, in mission seconds:
#
#   t=2   `give_word` records a promise to `strike_committee` — matched onto its
#         dossier by the world's own `[[entity]] id`, which is how #1029 records
#         a party. Nothing resolves it, so it stays OPEN, which is the state the
#         fact sheet has to be able to show.
#
# BASELINE (release headless, `--seed 42 --ticks 900`, no --ship, clean tree):
# final digest 0x481af0922239bfd2
# (5195729630555389906). Re-blessed once, from 0x7922703197b58ceb
# (8728662386098408683): that number was recorded before #1027 landed beneath
# this world and made capacity LEVELS movable, digest-folded state — the
# condition-track family the paragraph below names as this digest's legitimate
# movers. The projection itself is still folded by nothing.
#
# Nothing this world exists to exercise is IN that digest. A dossier is derived
# every tick and folded by nothing; what moves this number is the depot's
# condition track and the entity population, both of which #1025 already folds.
# If a later change makes the digest move without moving either, something
# started folding a projection, and that is the question to ask before
# re-blessing this line.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. The premise above ("folded by
# nothing") was true of the projection but never quite the whole story: the
# promise `give_word` records at t=2 is a `WorldContentRuntime::commitments`
# entry, and issue #1086's `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` now walks that
# ledger — so the SOURCE the dossier derives from is folded even though the
# projection itself still is not. The number above predates that fold and does
# not reproduce on a clean tree. Re-measure before treating it as a baseline
# again.

[global]
seed = 1030
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── Subject: a hailable starbase ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# On the roster through the comms door, which `station_axiom.toml` opens at the
# template level (`[comms] hailable = true`, issue #985). Alliance, so its
# affiliation row resolves through the faction's own authored `display_name`.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/station_axiom.toml"
id = "skyway_control"
name = "world.probe_dossier.entity.skyway_control.name"
transform = { position = [700.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

# ── Subject: the party a promise is made to ──────────────────────────────────
# A civilian hull the scenario has made hailable per-instance, which is the
# other half of "both authoring paths open the same door". Its `[[entity]] id`
# is what a `made_to` names — see the script below.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
id = "strike_committee"
name = "world.probe_dossier.entity.strike_committee.name"
transform = { position = [500.0, 0.0, 300.0] }
overrides = { comms = { hailable = true } }

# ── Subject: a published structure ───────────────────────────────────────────
# NOT hailable: this one is on the roster purely through the infrastructure
# door, which is what proves the two doors are independent. Its capacity and
# threshold tables are replaced wholesale by this instance (arrays replace at
# the instance layer), so the labelled/unlabelled split is authored here rather
# than pushed onto every world that fields a depot.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "skyway_depot"
name = "world.probe_dossier.entity.skyway_depot.name"
transform = { position = [900.0, 0.0, -200.0] }

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
# Labelled, so the crew can be told what the number is.
id = "depot_berths"
amount = 4
label = "world.probe_dossier.capacity.berths.label"

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
# Unlabelled on purpose. A script can read this; a fact sheet cannot show it.
id = "depot_transfer_throughput"
amount = 40

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "depot_transfer_capable"
fails_below = 0.4
label = "world.probe_dossier.threshold.transfer_capable.label"

# ── Subject: the structure the scenario is keeping back ──────────────────────
# Hailable, so it is on the roster; `publish = false`, so its condition is not.
# 31 of 100 points is a real, live, degraded track — the number a bug would
# leak, sitting in the world for the test to fail to find.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "sealed_depot"
name = "world.probe_dossier.entity.sealed_depot.name"
transform = { position = [1100.0, 0.0, 400.0] }
overrides = { comms = { hailable = true }, infrastructure = { condition = 31.0, publish = false, capacity = [], threshold = [] } }

# ── Not a subject ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Named, and reachable by neither door. A rule that only ever admits
# is not a rule.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/nav_beacon.toml"
id = "lonely_beacon"
name = "world.probe_dossier.entity.lonely_beacon.name"
transform = { position = [400.0, 0.0, -600.0] }

[script]
setup = """
on_timer(2, "give_word");

// The promise, made to a party the world also happens to field as an entity.
// `made_to` is the `[[entity]] id` — not a UUID, which #1029 refuses on purpose
// because a promise outlives the hull it was made to. Nothing resolves it, so
// the fact sheet shows a word still owed.
fn give_word(ctx) {
    ctx.commitments.record(#{
        id:            "safe_passage",
        made_to:       "strike_committee",
        terms:         "world.probe_dossier.commitment.safe_passage.terms",
        resolves_when: "world.probe_dossier.commitment.safe_passage.resolves",
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_duel.toml:
# Probe world for issue #838 — regression harness for the "world-spawned
# console hull never returns fire" bug.
#
# A player Alliance cruiser (AI-backfilled in a headless run) is placed a short
# distance from a world-spawned Alliance destroyer that has been re-flagged to
# the Harrow faction and given a standing combat doctrine. Harrow and Alliance
# are made mutually hostile at world-load. Because the two hulls start well
# inside AI sensor range (100 units default), the NPC promotes to high-LOD
# immediately and — once the invariant holds — engages and trades fire with the
# player until one side is destroyed.
#
# The doctrine here is authored as an UNTARGETED Destroy (no `directive_target`),
# which is what every shipped hostile TOML authors and what licenses the
# nearest-hostile acquisition tier. See the root-cause note in
# `src/console/weapons/mod.rs::ai_target_selection`.

[global]
# HISTORICAL (2026-08-02, issue #897) — superseded by the issue #896 re-sweep
# below. This table was measured after #897 swapped the simulation generator
# (`rand`'s SmallRng -> `vellum_rng::Pcg32`) but BEFORE #896 moved rapier's
# `PhysicsSet` chain onto the logical tick, which the next block explains
# re-rolled which duels close. In particular, seed 3's "GameOver at 18.5 s"
# below and the reasoning built on it (3 as "the pick" for resolving fastest)
# no longer hold: under the #896 re-sweep seed 3 is `InProgress`, not the
# resolving seed. Kept for the generator-swap context (still accurate) and as
# the record of where the 367-vs-4 arc-bearing count two paragraphs down
# originally came from; do not read the outcome table below as current.
#
# Nothing about this world's dynamics changed under #897; what changed is the
# numbers each seed names. Every hull roll in `SystemHull::apply_damage` now
# comes out of a different sequence, so which system each hit lands on — and
# with it which duels close and which settle into a standoff — is re-rolled
# wholesale. The #923 re-bless this replaces measured 10 as the fastest
# resolver; on this generator 10 stalls.
#
# Swept over a 60 sim-second window — built
# `phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/probe_duel.toml --seed N --hz 30
# --sim-seconds 60 --deterministic --report-format json` (--hz 30 to match
# the test harness's dt; irrelevant to the outcome since #895 — the
# simulation fixed-steps on `sim_tick_hz`, not the frame rate). The right-hand
# column is a second measurement over the 45 s window the composed-cruiser
# doctrine probes sample, counted the way those probes count it:
#
#   seed  60 s outcome           dealt      45 s ring ticks (of 1351)
#   3     GameOver at 18.5 s     332 v 34   1332   <- this seed, pre-#896
#   34    GameOver at 28.0 s     332 v 42   1334
#   1     InProgress             182 v 14    321
#   5     InProgress             182 v 14    297
#   838   InProgress             282 v 31    277   (the #923 pick)
#   2, 6, 7, 10, 13   InProgress            87-99
#   4, 8, 9, 21       InProgress               87
#
# 3 and 34 were the only two of the fourteen that resolved under this
# pre-#896 sweep. 3 was picked here for the larger margin under the 60 s
# budget and because it was much the stronger control condition for the ring
# probes: across the 45 s window the cruiser held a standing arc-bearing
# request on 367 of its ring ticks under seed 3 against only 4 under seed 34,
# and `the_composed_cruisers_ring_is_not_overwritten_by_an_arc_bearing_request`
# asserted on exactly that count to prove anything was ever declined. That
# specific count is pre-#896 and is not re-measured below; see the ring-probe
# note further down for what is currently evidenced instead.
#
# RE-SWEPT after issue #896 moved rapier onto the logical tick. This world has
# no asteroids, so the only thing physics does in it is the beam
# line-of-sight raycast — and that is now cast against colliders synchronised
# in the same tick rather than against last frame's, which is a real change to
# what the two hulls can see of each other and, in a scenario the header above
# already calls chaotically seed-sensitive, enough to re-roll which duels
# close. Same command line as the sweep above:
#
#   seed  60 s outcome            dealt (hostile v player)
#   34    GameOver at 27.6 s      342 v 61   <- the resolving seed
#   3     InProgress              264 v 34   (this world's default)
#   2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13         232 v 30
#   4, 21, 838                    182 v 27
#   1, 5                          182 v 12
#
# **The default stays 3, and it is no longer chosen for resolving.** Every
# other probe on this world — the ring probes, the doctrine probes, the power
# reserve probe — is measured against seed 3 and passes unchanged on it.
#
# RE-MEASURED again after the combat-freeze fix (the `[ai_profile]` blocks
# that give every Alliance hull an authored `sensor_range`, so a hull no
# longer loses AI fidelity — and freezes dead-reckoning — mid-manoeuvre).
# `the_composed_cruisers_ring_is_not_overwritten_by_an_arc_bearing_request`
# no longer finds a standing arc-bearing request on this seed at all: 346 ring
# ticks over the 45 s window, `requested == 0`, `overwritten == 0`. That is
# not the 367-vs-4 count above going stale into a false pass — it is a real
# change to this doctrine's own geometry, now that combat reliably sustains
# long enough to observe it in full:
#
#   * The phasers' `auto_arc_deg` banks always have at least one emitter
#     `Ready` on the ring's beam line, so the phaser family can never qualify
#     for a request while the hull holds the ring. (At the time this was
#     measured the pair abutted at 180 degrees; since issue #929 they overlap
#     at 270 and BOTH bear there, which makes the conclusion stronger rather
#     than different.)
#   * The torpedo tubes still cannot bear on the ring (90-degree fore/aft
#     arcs), but this hull's own `hold_torpedo_bearing` leg now reliably
#     claims a loaded, ready tube and breaks the ring to fire it BEFORE
#     Channel 3 ever observes a loaded-but-out-of-arc emitter — under the
#     freeze fix the leg actually completes (this run: `TorpedoLaunched: 4`,
#     450 damage dealt) instead of the hull losing fidelity mid-leg.
#
# RE-MEASURED AGAIN, AND THE BLOCK ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN (issue #929). Both of
# its readings were artefacts of a defect, not properties of the doctrine.
#
# The cruiser's tubes asked for a struck-down striking arc
# (`fact(target_facing_shields) <= 0`) that this hull's own guns could not open —
# one 180-degree auto-arc bank bears at a time on the ring, about 1 dmg/s at the
# `beam_damage_per_sec = 4` it then carried, into an arc the destroyer's Shields
# AI focuses to 6.5 hp/s — while its helm's `torpedo_run` leg opens on readiness
# alone and exits only on a round having LEFT a tube. The leg was therefore
# ABSORBING: the hull parked bow-on at `torpedo_bearing_speed = 0.0` for 39.7 s
# of a 90 s run on this seed and launched nothing. So:
#
#   * `TorpedoLaunched: 4` above was the world-spawned DESTROYER's rounds. The
#     player cruiser launched zero, here and on all 28 seeds swept.
#   * `requested == 0` followed from the same park: with the ring barely flown
#     there was almost nothing for Channel 3 to raise a request against, so the
#     bullet above has the causation backwards — the leg was not claiming a
#     tube before Channel 3 saw it, the hull was sitting still holding one.
#
# #929's FIRST PASS answered that by switching the launcher's shield conjunct
# off (`max_striking_shield_hp` past any arc reading). Its SECOND PASS reverted
# that and answered on the attack side instead: a torpedo no longer bypasses a
# raised arc, so the gate is worth ten times the round it delays, and the
# cruiser's phaser banks went `beam_damage_per_sec` 4 -> 24 to make the gate
# reachable. The measurements immediately below are that #929 tuning record;
# they stopped being the current trajectory when #1045 changed the scheduling
# phase of this world's zero-delay scripted opponent.
#
# `phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/probe_duel.toml --seed 3 --hz 30
# --sim-seconds 90 --deterministic --report-format json`, seed 3, over the 45 s
# window the ring probes sample:
#
#   ring ticks 654   requested 36   overwritten 0   worst error 0.0
#
# The standing request was back in this pre-#1045 trajectory, making
# `overwritten == 0` a real refusal again rather than a description of an empty
# inbox — the same shape the pre-#896 367-vs-4 count had, and the reason that
# history is still recorded above.
#
# The count has fallen twice across #929 and the trend is worth reading:
#
#   first pass  (gate off,  4 dmg/s, auto arcs 180)   478 of 1180 ring ticks
#   second pass (gate on,  24 dmg/s, auto arcs 180)    81 of  675
#   third pass  (gate on,  32 dmg/s, auto arcs 270)    36 of  654
#
# One mechanism drives both drops. The stronger the cruiser's guns, the sooner it
# opens the striking arc; the sooner it opens the arc, the sooner it spends the
# salvo — so "a loaded, in-reach, out-of-arc torpedo family" is a state the hull
# passes THROUGH rather than sits in, and that state is exactly what raises the
# request. The ring shrinks a little for the same reason, the bow-hold leg being
# genuinely flown now rather than skipped.
#
# RE-MEASURED after #1045 on both Linux CI and the local headless gate:
#
#   ring ticks 678   requested 0   overwritten 0   worst error 0.0
#
# The corrected script lifecycle changes the exact phase at which the opponent
# enters this chaotically sensitive engagement. This sample no longer passes
# through the brief loaded-and-out-of-arc state that raises Channel 3's request;
# `probe_aggressor`, the paired real-ring sample in
# `the_composed_cruisers_ring_is_not_overwritten_by_an_arc_bearing_request`,
# still does. That test therefore requires a real request across the PAIR while
# retaining independent ring-duration and `overwritten == 0` assertions for
# each run. No request in either sample still fails as vacuous.
#
# The following whole-90 s table is the same pre-#1045 #929 sweep, retained as
# the combat-retuning record rather than presented as the current trajectory:
#
#                       first pass    second pass   third pass
#                       (gate off,    (gate on,     (gate on, 270 arcs,
#                        4 dmg/s)      180, 24)      32)
#   cruiser launches     4 every seed  2-5, 28/28    2-4, 28/28
#   torpedo_run          0.0-3.9 s     12.2-27.2 s   0.5-13.4 s
#   cruiser dealt        290-489       350-623       272-591
#   destroyer hull dmg   240 on 25/28  198-433       150-422
#                        (240-306)     (mean 385)    (mean 389)
#   resolve inside 90 s  12/28         23/28         25/28
#   CRUISER WINS         0 of 28       22 of 28      25 of 28
#   cruiser DIES         12 of 28      1 of 28       0 in 90 s, 3 in 180 s
#
# THE DUEL NOW CLOSES, and which way. That 240 was the cruiser's whole six-round
# magazine at 40 points of pierce apiece and nothing else — its beams never once
# reached the destroyer's hull — on 25 of the 28 seeds; the three that differ (31,
# 55, 838) read 268, 306 and 273, the same magazine plus a few points from
# elsewhere. The RANGES in the two later columns are the full 28 seeds, and their
# low tails are the seeds the fight does not finish inside the window rather than
# a weaker salvo. With the beams able to collapse an arc the fight
# is two-sided and the bigger hull wins it: on seed 3 the destroyer dies at
# 60.7 s. At 180 s every one of the 28 resolves, 25 as cruiser wins and 3 as
# cruiser deaths (seeds 9 at 95.0 s, 2 at 142.1 s, 89 at 176.7 s) — which is the
# whole supply of player-death seeds this world still has, and the reason the two
# tests that need one pin it explicitly.
#
# Note that `outcome` still reports `draw` for a run the cruiser WINS — the run
# classifier ends a run on the PLAYER's death, so a cruiser win reads
# `InProgress` with the hostile simply absent from the world. Read
# `damage_by_ship`'s `death` / `kills` rather than `final_phase` when sweeping
# this world.
#
# Tests that need a particular ENDING pin their own seeds rather than leaning on
# this world's default, which is the discipline
# `ai_crewed_ships_actually_launch_torpedoes_in_a_real_run` already applied with
# its own pin of 10: that test's pin and this world's default agreed only
# incidentally under #923 and do not need to.
seed = 3
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player ship — spawned by spawn_game_start_entities when the game starts.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"

[script]

// Make Harrow and Alliance mutually hostile before the destroyer spawns.
on_world_loaded("on_load");
// Spawn the hostile Alliance destroyer close to the player at t=0.

fn on_load(ctx) {

}
