base_files.assets/worlds/probe_evidence.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1031 — evidence entries with provenance, gathered on
# two genuinely different paths.
#
# The point of the slice is that the crew can say HOW they know, so this world
# makes them learn the same subject's story twice, by two routes, and asserts
# both land on one fact sheet in the order they happened:
#
#   skyway_hook     a published structure with a labelled capacity, so its sheet
#                   carries BASELINE facts as well as gathered entries and the
#                   separation between the two is visible
#   line_foreman    a hailable hull — the witness, and the party whose testimony
#                   becomes the second entry
#
# THE TWO ROUTES, in mission seconds:
#
#   t=3   the `survey_window` deadline fires. Its handler appends a SCAN entry
#         to `skyway_hook`, then does two things that must be no-ops:
#           * appends the SAME entry again — same subject, same provenance, same
#             text — which the store deduplicates, keeping the first stamp;
#           * appends to `no_such_structure`, a name no entity in this world
#             answers to, which the applier warns about and drops. Neither costs
#             the handler its call, so the flag it sets afterwards is written.
#   t=5   `open_foreman_channel` opens a real scripted thread on `foreman_calls`.
#         The ship's Comms officer is AI-backfilled in a headless run and
#         answers with response 0 through the ordinary admitted
#         `RespondToMessage` path, so `on_press_foreman` runs as a genuine
#         dialogue `on_pick` — not a timer standing in for one — and appends the
#         DIALOGUE entry.
#
# TWO THINGS MAKE THAT ANSWER LAND, and both are authored deliberately:
#
#   1. The Comms response policy on the player ship: answer an open thread with
#      its first response while Comms is available and the sender is in range.
#      [ai] THIS LINE USED TO READ "as an override because
#      `alliance_destroyer.toml` declares none", AND THAT WAS WRONG TWICE — see
#      the defect found while reviewing #1036. The destroyer declares no
#      `[comms_console]` INLINE but COMPOSES that exact rule from
#      `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`, which every Alliance hull includes
#      (`alliance_courier.toml` authors the identical rule inline), so the
#      answer lands with or without this block. And until that defect was fixed
#      the block never reached the ship at all: `spawn_game_start_entities`
#      replaced the world's merged config with the lobby-selected hull
#      WHOLESALE, discarding every `[entity.overrides.*]` on a `player-ship`
#      row after the validator had approved it. It is LIVE now, and what being
#      live buys this world is independence from the lobby's pick: the one rule
#      this probe depends on belongs to the WORLD, so a hull composing a
#      different comms policy would still answer. Keep it for that, or delete
#      it as a restatement of the fragment — a content call, not a code one.
#   2. The thread is opened FROM the foreman's own hull, not from `_self`. The
#      response router range-gates a pick against the sender's live range flag,
#      so only a real, hailable, in-range sender can be answered — which is also
#      the more honest scene: somebody called, and the crew pressed them.
#
# NOTHING IS WITHHELD IN THIS WORLD, and that is deliberate: `probe_dossier.toml`
# is the tripwire for the hidden-truth rule and still is. What this one proves is
# the other half — that the ONLY way something reaches a fact sheet that the
# world did not already imply is an authored append, with a provenance attached.
#
# BASELINE (release headless, `--seed 42 --ticks 900 --digest-every 900`, clean
# tree, no `--ship` override — the invocation probe_commitments.toml and
# probe_stabilise.toml record): final digest 0x4567b7901a66ffe4
# (5001167740764356580). A NEW number — nothing to compare it against yet — so it
# is written down to be the thing a later change is A/B'd against, the way the
# shipped worlds' digests already are.
#
# The two anchors were re-measured on the same tree and are UNMOVED (combat_test
# 14942520827746055774, patrol 11531679067393217131), so the claim below is
# tested rather than asserted.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state, and the evidence log this
# world exists to exercise — `WorldContentRuntime::evidence`, along with the
# flag stores and trigger latches the two routes above also touch — is now
# walked by `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` rather than merely snapshotted.
# Every number above, the two anchors included, predates that fold and does not
# reproduce on a clean tree. Re-measure before treating any of it as a baseline
# again.
#
# STILL 0x4567b7901a66ffe4 after the player-ship override fix (the defect found
# in #1036), and that is a claim rather than an oversight. The fix makes this
# world's `comms_console.ai.rule` override reach the spawned hull for the FIRST
# time; the value it lands is the one `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml` was
# already giving that hull, so an override that restates what it overrides moves
# nothing. Every other anchor was swept on the same tree and is unmoved too.
#
# Nothing this world exists to exercise is IN that digest. An evidence entry is
# authoritative state, but it is SCENARIO state — the same "authoritative but not
# folded" bucket as the deadline table and the commitments ledger, and for their
# reason: it moves no hull, no shield and no reactor. What moves this number is
# the depot's condition track and the entity population. If a later change makes
# the digest move without moving either, something started folding scenario
# state, and that is the question to ask before re-blessing this line.

[global]
seed = 1031
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The player ship. The Comms response policy below RESTATES what every Alliance
# hull already composes from `fragments/ai/fleet_baseline.toml`; it is authored
# here so the one rule this probe depends on belongs to the world rather than to
# whichever hull the lobby picks — see the header.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

[[entity.overrides.comms_console.ai.rule]]
priority = 0
channel = "comms_respond"
when = "fact(comms_available) > 0 and fact(sender_in_range) > 0"
verb = "respond_to_message"
response_index = 0

# ── The subject both routes are about ────────────────────────────────────────
# A published structure, so its sheet already carries a condition row and a
# labelled capacity before the crew learn anything. Everything gathered about it
# has to stay visibly apart from those.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "skyway_hook"
name = "world.probe_evidence.entity.skyway_hook.name"
transform = { position = [900.0, 0.0, -200.0] }

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.capacity]]
id = "depot_berths"
amount = 4
label = "world.probe_evidence.capacity.berths.label"

# ── The witness ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Hailable, so it has a file of its own; its testimony is about the hook, which
# is why the entry lands on the HOOK's sheet rather than on the foreman's. A
# finding is filed under what it is about, not under who said it.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
id = "line_foreman"
name = "world.probe_evidence.entity.line_foreman.name"
transform = { position = [500.0, 0.0, 300.0] }
overrides = { comms = { hailable = true } }

# ── The clock the survey is read on ──────────────────────────────────────────
# There is no `[[evidence]]` block anywhere in this file, for the reason there is
# no `[[commitment]]` one: what the crew found out depends on what they did, so a
# world file cannot declare it. What a world file CAN declare is when the survey
# comes back, and that is an ordinary deadline.
[[deadline]]
id = "survey_window"
label = "world.probe_evidence.deadline.survey_window.label"
due_secs = 3
visible = true

[script]
setup = """
on_timer(5, "open_foreman_channel");
on_deadline("survey_window", "on_survey_window");

// ROUTE ONE: the scan. Also the two no-ops, authored deliberately so the probe
// proves they cost this handler nothing — the flag below is written either way.
fn on_survey_window(ctx) {
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.probe_evidence.entity.skyway_hook.name",
        text:       "world.probe_evidence.evidence.stress_fracture",
        provenance: "scan",
    });
    // The same finding again. A re-scan is an ordinary thing for a crew to do
    // and must not put a second identical line on the sheet.
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.probe_evidence.entity.skyway_hook.name",
        text:       "world.probe_evidence.evidence.stress_fracture",
        provenance: "scan",
    });
    // A subject this world does not field. Warned and dropped at the applier —
    // never a panic, and never a lost call.
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.probe_evidence.entity.no_such_structure.name",
        text:       "world.probe_evidence.evidence.stress_fracture",
        provenance: "scan",
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("survey_ran", 1);
}

// ROUTE TWO: the testimony. A real node fn, opened through the real
// `open_comms` pipeline and answered by the ship's own Comms officer.
fn foreman_calls(ctx) {
    #{
        message: "world.probe_evidence.comms.foreman_calls",
        responses: [
            #{ text: "world.probe_evidence.comms.press", on_pick: "on_press_foreman" },
            #{ text: "world.probe_evidence.comms.let_it_go", on_pick: "on_let_it_go" },
        ],
    }
}

// The pick that gets it out of him. Terminal — it returns nothing — so the
// thread closes and the officer does not answer it again.
fn on_press_foreman(ctx) {
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    "world.probe_evidence.entity.skyway_hook.name",
        text:       "world.probe_evidence.evidence.foreman_admission",
        provenance: "dialogue",
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("foreman_pressed", 1);
}

fn on_let_it_go(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.increment("foreman_let_go", 1);
}

// The thread comes from the foreman's own hull rather than from `_self`, and
// that is load-bearing: the response router range-gates a pick against the
// SENDER's live range flag, so a real, hailable, in-range sender is what makes
// the officer's answer land instead of being refused.
fn open_foreman_channel(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.open_comms(#{
        from:    "world.probe_evidence.entity.line_foreman.name",
        node_fn: "foreman_calls",
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_external_repair.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1161 — external repair-team dispatch, end to end.
#
# One repair-team-fitted tender and one ALLY STRUCTURE positioned close enough
# to send a team across. The tender carries a single repair team and, in its own
# `[repair.external_dispatch]` table, the reach a team can cross and the rate it
# works a target's condition track at. There is no combat and no scripted
# dispatch: the tender is a backfilled player ship, so the headless test drives
# the dispatch through the ordinary admitted DispatchExternalRepair /
# RecallExternalRepair path (the only way to prove the command rides the same
# admission the repair console's own control would), sets the ship's one Tactical
# lock the way `SetTarget` would, and moves the operator by hand.
#
# WHAT THIS WORLD PROVES (the headless test drives it):
#
#   1. A DISPATCHED TEAM RAISES THE ALLY'S CONDITION. With the ally designated
#      and in range, dispatching a team raises the ALLY's own condition track at
#      the authored rate — progress that lives on the ally, not the tender.
#
#   2. THE HULL'S OWN REPAIRS SLOW. While the one team is committed abroad it is
#      withdrawn from the tender's internal damage-control sweep: the tender's
#      own free-team count drops to zero and an internal dispatch of that team is
#      refused, so helping the ally is a real trade against fixing itself.
#
#   3. RECALL RETURNS THE TEAM AND LEAVES THE WORK DONE. Recalling brings the
#      team home — the sweep can use it again — and the condition it banked on the
#      ally stays. Drifting the tender out of range brings the team home the same
#      way.
#
# The dispatch reach and the repair rate are authored on the TENDER's own
# `[repair.external_dispatch]` table; the ally's condition track and thresholds
# are the ally's — nothing about either is in Rust. A hull that authored no
# `[repair.external_dispatch]` carries no dispatch capability, which is why the
# shipped destroyer is deliberately NOT the operator here.

[global]
seed = 1161
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The tender — the backfilled player ship, spawned at game start. The game-start
# spawn swaps the world's `player-ship` placeholder for the lobby-SELECTED hull,
# so the selection has to be the tender or its repair team never spawns.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/repair_tender.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The ally — a transfer depot 80 units off, well inside the tender's 600-unit
# reach. It starts at 40/100 and, for a crisp probe, declines at ZERO on its own
# (overridden below) so its condition only moves by the dispatched team's work —
# +20 points a second while a team is over there, nothing when the team is home.
# A structure that authors no `[held_response]` is untouched by tractors; a hull
# that authors no `[repair.external_dispatch]` is untouched by this slice.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
name = "world.probe_external_repair.entity.ally.name"
transform = { position = [80.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { infrastructure = { condition = 40.0, decay_per_sec = 0.0 } }
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_fleet_asteroids.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1116 — a two-ship fleet flying an ASTEROID field.
#
# The sibling of `probe_fleet_duel.toml`, and it exists for one reason
# `probe_fleet_duel` cannot cover: that world has no asteroids, and asteroid
# streaming is the last `LocalShip`-gated write that folds into the
# authoritative digest. `update_asteroid_window` used to centre its ring-buffer
# window on the single `LocalShip`, which is a DIFFERENT ship on each host of a
# two-host mission — so two hosts streamed different rocks and diverged on any
# asteroid world (the demo, `combat_test.toml`, included). `tests/
# local_ship_neutrality.rs` runs this world twice, moving the marker between
# runs, and folds every tick: the fix (a fleet-wide streaming centre) agrees,
# the pre-fix `LocalShip` centre does not.
#
# The two fleet ships sit 300 units apart on the X axis — 12 lattice cells at
# the field's 25-unit resolution, wider than the hysteresis band, so a window
# centred on one ship loads a visibly different cell set than one centred on the
# other. The field is a dense DISC (fill_gameplay = 0 admits every covered cell)
# large enough that every cell either window reaches carries a rock, so the
# differing edge cells are never empty and the divergence is real rather than
# incidental. There is deliberately no hostile: the fold already changes every
# tick because `SimTick` is in it, and a combat probe's seed-sensitive draws
# would only add noise to a test about which rocks are loaded, not who wins.

[global]
seed = 1116
# Authored for completeness — a fleet mission on this world would run at this
# delay — but `local_ship_neutrality` never joins a lockstep session, so it is
# inert there.
command_delay_ticks = 2

# Slot 1's ship takes `[player_spawn]`.
[player_spawn]
position = [-150.0, 0.0, 0.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "fleet-ship-1"
transform = { position = [-150.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# Slot 2's ship, 300 units (12 cells) away on the +X axis.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "fleet-ship-2"
transform = { position = [150.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The belt both ships fly. A disc around the origin (shape omitted → the legacy
# distance test, `inner_radius = 0`), out to 1000 units so every cell within
# reach of either ship's window is eligible, with `fill_gameplay = 0.0` so every
# eligible cell spawns a rock. `spawn_cells`/`despawn_cells` are pulled in from
# the default 10/12 to 6/7: at the 25-unit resolution that is a 6-cell spawn
# radius, so the two ships 12 cells apart have windows that touch at just one
# column — a per-ship centre loads an almost entirely different belt than its
# peer, while the fleet centroid loads the identical one on both. It also keeps
# the streamed rock count modest (~170) so three 1200-tick runs stay quick.
# Everything else — asteroid types, resolution, jitter — comes from the shared
# field template.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_field_main.toml"
id = "fleet-belt"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { asteroid_field = { inner_radius = 0.0, outer_radius = 1000.0, weight = 1.0, grid = { fill_gameplay = 0.0, spawn_cells = 6, despawn_cells = 7 } } }
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_fleet_backfill.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1119 — backfilling a disconnected ship host.
#
# A THREE-ship fleet, deliberately one larger than `probe_fleet_duel.toml`. The
# extra hull is what lets the crown proof drop ONE host and still have TWO
# survivors left to compare: #1119 AC6 is "both surviving views agree", and a
# two-ship fleet dropped to one survivor has nothing to hold that agreement
# against. Dropping slot 3 here leaves slots 1 and 2, which must
#
#   * agree the disconnect tick — derived from slot 3's own last watermark, not
#     from which of them noticed the close first;
#   * flip slot 3's ship to Backfill at that exact tick, identically; and
#   * keep folding the same authoritative digest every tick afterwards, with
#     slot 3's ship now AI-driven by both of them from the same ticks.

# A lone host still spawns one player ship and treats the other two rows as
# ordinary NPCs — the roster decides how many of the `ship`-tagged rows are
# crewed hulls, exactly as `probe_fleet_duel.toml` documents.
#
# A hostile is spawned close enough to engage so the fold covers combat: a lost
# ship coasting in a straight line under Backfill would agree far more cheaply
# than one whose helm AI is closing with a target and whose weapons are drawing
# from the beam/torpedo/jitter streams.
#
# Deliberately its OWN world rather than three rows added to
# `probe_fleet_duel.toml`: adding a row there would spawn an extra NPC in every
# #1116 test that plays that world with a two-ship roster, moving its digests.

[global]
seed = 1119
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0
# Two ticks at 60 Hz — 33 ms. Short on purpose, like the #1116 probe: a probe
# checks the future-tick and host-loss paths are exercised at all, and a longer
# delay only makes the test wait. A shipped fleet authors the schema default.
command_delay_ticks = 2

[player_spawn]

base_files.assets/worlds/probe_gm_idle_npc.toml:
# Idle-NPC advisory probe for #1435, with NOTHING authored under
# `[gm_attention]` — so this world exercises the shipped defaults: a thirty
# SIMULATION-second grace, and the Background band.
#
# Three hulls, one of each kind the advisory has to tell apart:
#
#   * `fleet-ship-1` — the crew's own cruiser. It carries `FleetSlotOf`, so it
#     is a player ship on every peer and is never watched, however little its
#     crew is doing.
#   * `world.probe_gm_idle_npc.picket` — a Harrow picket flying its template's
#     own `patrol-ironveil` Patrol entry. A standing patrol IS an order, so this
#     hull must never reach the queue no matter how long the probe runs.
#   * `world.probe_gm_idle_npc.drifter` — the same hull with its doctrine
#     cleared (`doctrine = []`, the documented way to empty an array in a
#     per-instance override). No doctrine, no Objective: idle from tick zero.
#
# `sim_tick_hz` sits on the 30 Hz floor so the default thirty-second grace is
# exactly 900 fixed steps — few enough for a headless test to walk to the
# boundary and check both sides of it, and still the real authored default
# rather than a shortened stand-in.
[global]

title = "world.patrol.global.title"
description = "world.patrol.global.description"
sim_tick_hz = 30.0
ai_tick_hz = 30.0
ai_snapshot_hz = 10.0

spawn_on = "game_start"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]

base_files.assets/worlds/probe_gm_workload_course.t:
# The Navigation half of the #1438 Station-workload probe.
#
# The workload advisory counts a Navigation clearance only when the clearance is
# actually DELIVERED to a person, which the router decides: an AI Navigation
# asking a human Helm raises a popup, while two people at the same table are
# suppressed on purpose. So the only case that is a demand at all is a course
# the ship's OWN Navigation plotted — and a hull only plots one when it has
# somewhere to be.
#
# This world gives it somewhere: one anchor and one mandatory Reach objective,
# scored positive and Helm-relevant, which is what `operate_navigation_ai` ranks
# to a destination and writes onto the shared waypoint. `[gm_attention]` is left
# alone here; the thresholds this world runs on are the shipped ones.
#
# The anchor is deliberately far from the hull's spawn, so a test can watch the
# demand stand while the hull is nowhere near it and then complete when the hull
# arrives inside the authored `waypoint_arrival_radius`.
[global]
seed = 1438
title = "world.patrol.global.title"
description = "world.patrol.global.description"
sim_tick_hz = 30.0
ai_tick_hz = 30.0
ai_snapshot_hz = 10.0
command_delay_ticks = 2

[anchors]

fn on_load(ctx) {

        id: "obj-workload-course",

        mandatory: true,

        directive_kind: "Reach",

base_files.assets/worlds/probe_held_response.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1158 — the arrest-decline held-response, end to end.
#
# One tractor-fitted tug and one FAILING STRUCTURE positioned close enough to
# couple. The structure declines on its own (an authored `decay_per_sec`), and
# it authors — in its OWN config — what being held does to it: `arrest-decline`,
# which stops the decline while the beam is on it and recovers it at an authored
# rate. The tractor supplies the geometry and knows nothing about which
# held-response the structure declared.
#
# WHAT THIS WORLD PROVES (the headless test drives it):
#
#   1. A DECLINING STRUCTURE DECLINES UNHELD. Left alone, the structure's
#      condition falls at its authored rate and crosses its own failure
#      threshold DOWN, dropping the operational flag a scenario reads.
#
#   2. HOLDING IT ARRESTS THE DECLINE AND RECOVERS IT. With the structure locked
#      and the beam engaged, the decline stops and the condition climbs at the
#      authored recover rate, crossing the structure's own restore threshold UP
#      and setting the operational flag again — the crossing detected and
#      mirrored by the one system that owns the flag edges, exactly as a scripted
#      repair's would be.
#
#   3. RELEASING RESUMES THE ORDINARY DECLINE ON THE NEXT TICK. Once the beam
#      lets go, nothing arrests the structure and it falls again.
#
# The held-response, the decline rate and the recover rate are authored on the
# STRUCTURE (through its `[[entity]].overrides`, the same authoring path #1025's
# `[infrastructure]` and #1026's `[operations]` use), never in Rust and never on
# the tug. A structure that authored no `[held_response]` would simply be held in
# place, which is why the shipped derelict of `probe_tractor.toml` is unchanged.

[global]
seed = 1158
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The tug — the backfilled player ship, spawned at game start. The same lean
# tractor hull `probe_tractor.toml` fields; its beam rides the ordinary admitted
# EngageTractor / ReleaseTractor path.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/tractor_tug.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The failing structure — a transfer depot 80 units off, well inside the tug's
# 600-unit reach. It starts at 55/100 (above its 40 % failure point, so the
# `depot_transfer_capable` flag begins UP), loses 6 condition points a second on
# its own, and authors an `arrest-decline` held-response that holds it steady and
# recovers it at 20 points a second while the beam is on it. Every one of those
# numbers is the STRUCTURE's, authored here — nothing about it is in Rust.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
name = "world.probe_held_response.entity.structure.name"
transform = { position = [80.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { infrastructure = { condition = 55.0, decay_per_sec = 6.0 }, held_response = { kind = "arrest-decline", recover_per_sec = 20.0 } }
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_huge_rock.toml:
# Probe world for issue #968 — a hull flying a straight lane through a belt
# whose centre rock is the `huge` class (collider radius 12) added in #947.
#
# The reported failure was a ship being TRAPPED by such a rock: seventeen
# consecutive collisions at the 1 Hz cooldown, the hull as much as 6.5 units
# INSIDE the collider, and the mission effectively over. This world is the
# geometry that produces it, held still so the behaviour can be asserted rather
# than sampled out of a live scenario.
#
# ── The lane ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `lane_far` and `lane_near` sit on the +Z/-Z axis with the belt exactly halfway
# between them, so the straight line between the two waypoints runs THROUGH the
# huge rock's centre. A ship that flies its route naively must hit it; a ship
# with working avoidance goes round and comes back to the line.
#
#     z = +40   lane_near   (also the player spawn)
#     z = -100  the belt
#     z = -240  lane_far
#
# The mission objective loops the two anchors, so a single run is several
# traversals in alternating directions rather than one — the rock is met from
# both sides, on both a north- and a south-bound heading.
#
# ── The belt ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# One `huge` rock (radius 12) dead on the lane, flanked by two `large` rocks
# (radius 4) at x = ±40 and two `small` ones (radius 2) staggered fore and aft.
# The flanking pair leaves a corridor of clear space 24 units wide on either
# side of the huge rock — comfortably threadable for a 1.2-radius destroyer
# with its authored 5-unit avoidance buffer, so the probe is testing whether the
# ship goes AROUND the rock, not whether it can fit through a gap that is too
# small for it.
#
# The rocks are placed as ordinary `[[entity]]` templates rather than through an
# `[asteroid_field]`: a field is streamed from a density function and a seed, so
# where its rocks land is not something a test can state. These are.
#
# ── Deliberately no combat ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# No hostiles, no factions, no weapons. The failure under test is a navigation
# one, and everything a shooting probe would add — who acquires whom, who dies
# first, how the run ends — is exactly the seed-sensitive noise that would make
# the assertion flaky. "Still on the job" is asserted here as "still flying the
# authored route, in bounds, in both directions", which is the property the
# reported ship lost when it left the map at a fixed 9 u/s and never came back.

[global]
seed = 968

[anchors]
lane_near = [0.0, 0.0, 40.0]
lane_far = [0.0, 0.0, -240.0]

# The picket's lane, 2 km east of the player's. The names are the ones
# `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` authors in its own `patrol-ironveil` doctrine, so the
# hull needs no override to fly this route — and the world-composition validator
# would refuse the load if this world fielded that hull without declaring them.
ironveil_patrol_a = [2000.0, 0.0, 200.0]
ironveil_patrol_b = [2000.0, 0.0, -200.0]

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 40.0]

# Player ship — spawned by spawn_game_start_entities when the game starts.
# The destroyer is the hull the issue was reported against.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 40.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The belt ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The rock the issue is about: `huge`, radius 12, sitting on the lane.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_huge.toml"
id = "belt-huge"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, -100.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_2_large.toml"
id = "belt-large-port"
transform = { position = [-40.0, 0.0, -100.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_3_large.toml"
id = "belt-large-starboard"
transform = { position = [40.0, 0.0, -100.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_4_small.toml"
id = "belt-small-fore"
transform = { position = [24.0, 0.0, -136.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_small.toml"
id = "belt-small-aft"
transform = { position = [-24.0, 0.0, -64.0] }

# ── The picket's belt, and why there is a second ship at all ─────────────────
#
# The player's leg above tests the HIGH-fidelity helm. The other half of the
# reported failure was a DEAD-RECKONED one: `combat_test`'s two Harrow pickets
# are far enough from the player to be LOD-demoted, and a demoted ship steers by
# `simulate_low_lod_ships`, which ran its hazard assessment as if the hull were a
# dimensionless point with the parse-default buffer. They ground 3.2 units into
# radius-4 rocks, were kicked back to the surface once a second by the collision
# response, and drove straight back in.
#
# So this picket flies its own lane 2 km east, through its own huge rock. The
# distance is the point: its authored `sensor_range` is 110, and LOD promotion
# needs the player inside that, so it stays demoted for the whole run no matter
# where the player's own patrol takes it. Harrow and the Alliance are left
# neutral (this world adds no `add_faction_enemy`), so the two ships never fight
# and the picket's own `patrol-ironveil` doctrine outscores its `destroy-hostiles`
# entry throughout.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
id = "picket"
transform = { position = [2000.0, 0.0, 200.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_2_huge.toml"
id = "picket-belt-huge"
transform = { position = [2000.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_1_large.toml"
id = "picket-belt-large-port"
transform = { position = [1960.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_common_4_large.toml"
id = "picket-belt-large-starboard"
transform = { position = [2040.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

# ── The route ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `base_priority = 80` outranks the destroyer template's own `destroy-hostiles`
# (45) and `hold-station` (20), so the ship flies this and nothing else. Far
# anchor first, so the very first leg is the one straight at the rock.
[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-cross-the-belt",
        text: "world.probe_huge_rock.trigger.action.obj_cross_the_belt.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 80,
        directive_kind: "Patrol",
        directive_anchors: ["lane_far", "lane_near"],
        directive_loop: true,
    });
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_infrastructure.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1025 — the infrastructure condition track, end to end.
#
# One transfer depot, far from the player, walked all the way round the loop the
# issue asks for: degrade → threshold crossed → operational flag flipped → a
# script hook reacts → repair → the flag flips BACK and a second hook reacts.
# No combat is involved on purpose; every condition move here is authored, so
# the run is a deterministic tripwire for the whole chain rather than a duel
# that happens to damage something.
#
# The depot spawns with its condition overridden DOWN to 80 points via the
# `[[entity]].overrides` path, which is the other half of the "both authoring
# paths accept it" claim — the template supplies the ceiling, the capacity and
# the threshold; the world supplies this instance's starting condition.
#
# Timeline (60 Hz):
#
#   tick   0   depot spawns at 80/100 → `depot_transfer_capable` publishes UP,
#              and the armed `on_flag_set` watcher does NOT fire, because its
#              `when` guard reads `counter(depot_offline) == 0`
#   tick  60   `on_storm_damage` takes 50 points → 30/100 = 30 %, below the
#              authored 40 % → the flag CLEARS
#   tick ~61   `on_depot_offline` fires, setting `depot_offline`
#   tick 180   `on_field_repair` puts 25 points back → 55/100 = 55 %, above the
#              45 % restore point → the flag SETS
#   tick ~181  `on_depot_restored` fires — its guard now reads true
#
# The intermediate value matters: 30 → 55 crosses 40 % on the way up but the
# flag only returns at 45 %, so the run also proves the restore point is the one
# being honoured rather than the failure point read backwards.
#
# BASELINE (recorded here for the first time in #1027, which moved it).
# `--seed 42 --ticks 900` gives final digest 0x2274bea11a99df66
# (2482818893733289830), and 15523228394889164256 at tick 0.
#
# It moved because a capacity's LEVEL is now folded into the authoritative
# digest. #1025 published capacity as a read-only number; #1027's `transfer`
# operation moves it, so two hosts that disagree about how much a depot holds
# now disagree about the digest too. Nothing in THIS world transfers anything —
# the depot's capacity sits where it was authored for the whole run — but the
# fold applies to every structure that declares one, which is what makes it a
# guarantee rather than a special case.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state, and this world's own
# `depot_offline` flag — set and cleared by the `on_flag_set`/`on_field_repair`
# handlers above — together with the trigger latches that watch it, are now
# walked by `sim_digest::fold_scenario_flags` / `fold_scenario_records`, neither
# of which happened when 2482818893733289830 was measured. Re-measure before
# treating it as a baseline again.

[global]
seed = 1025
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The structure under test. `name` is both the display String Id and the
# reference id the scripted effects address it by — the convention every named
# world entity follows (see patrol.toml / combat_test.toml).
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
name = "world.entity.skyhook_depot.name"
transform = { position = [600.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { infrastructure = { condition = 80.0 } }

[script]
setup = """
on_timer(1, "on_storm_damage");
on_timer(3, "on_field_repair");

// The failure direction. Single-shot, and it only ever has one crossing to see.
on_flag_cleared("depot_transfer_capable", "on_depot_offline");

// The restore direction. The same flag publishes UP on the depot's first tick,
// which would spend a bare single-shot watcher before the mission had started —
// so the registration carries a trigger-level `when` that leaves it ARMED until
// the depot has actually been offline. A test inside the handler would not do:
// `evaluate_triggers_with_flags` skips a false `when` BEFORE setting `fired`,
// while an in-handler `if` would have burned the trigger on the publication.
on_flag_set("depot_transfer_capable", "on_depot_restored").when("counter(depot_offline) > 0");

fn on_storm_damage(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.damage_infrastructure("world.entity.skyhook_depot.name", 50);
}

fn on_field_repair(ctx) {
    // Whole points, applied in one go. A timed field-repair operation calls the
    // same verb with a fractional flt() slice once a tick instead.
    ctx.effects.repair_infrastructure("world.entity.skyhook_depot.name", 25);
}

fn on_depot_offline(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.depot_offline = 1;
}

fn on_depot_restored(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.depot_restored = 1;
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_npc_resupply.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1163 — an ALLIED NPC tender docks with a stranded ship
# and transfers a capacity to it, with NO player involvement.
#
# The NPC-content mirror of `probe_umbilical.toml` (issue #1160). There the
# operator was the backfilled PLAYER ship and the test drove Dock + StartTransfer
# by hand; here the operator is a world-spawned NPC (`alliance_tender.toml`) that
# runs the WHOLE two-seat chain itself off one authored `Transfer` directive — the
# same `operate_dock_ai` then `operate_umbilical_ai` hosts (#1162), the same
# admission seam, no NPC-only branch.
#
# WHAT THIS WORLD PROVES (asserted on the stranded ship's OWN ledger):
#
#   1. THE TENDER RESUPPLIES THE STRANDED SHIP UNAIDED. Handed a `Transfer` order
#      naming the stranded ship, the tender's Helm docks once the ordered hull is
#      reported in range, then its Engineering flows `reserve_fuel` across the
#      umbilical — the stranded ship's empty ledger fills, unit for unit, at the
#      authored rate. No command is ever sent by a player.
#
# The tender starts within the 200-unit dock range of the stranded ship, so the
# dock host engages without a navigation leg (the dock manoeuvre flies it onto the
# berth). Its job is authored ENTIRELY as a spawn-time `behaviour.doctrine`
# override (by-id merge over the template's HOLD default). Nothing about the dock
# or umbilical is authored anywhere but the tender's own `[dock]` / `[umbilical]`
# tables and its `[[system]]` blocks.

[global]
seed = 1163
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

# Player spawn kept far off and outside AI sensor range, so the AI-backfilled
# player never interferes. The world still needs it to reach InProgress.
[player_spawn]
position = [4000.0, 0.0, 4000.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [4000.0, 0.0, 4000.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The allied tender — the fully AI-crewed operator ──────────────────────────
# Spawned at the origin, full of `reserve_fuel`. The template ships a HOLD
# default; this override hands it the job: TRANSFER to the stranded ship (Helm
# docks, Engineering runs the umbilical).
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_tender.toml"
name = "world.probe_npc_resupply.entity.tender.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "resupply-the-stranded", directive_kind = "Transfer", directive_operate_target = "world.probe_npc_resupply.entity.stranded.name", base_priority = 90.0 },
] } }

# ── The stranded ship — the docked partner with the empty receiving ledger.
# A passive dockable hull 100 units to starboard, well inside the tender's
# 200-unit dock range. It authors a `[dock]` opt-in (so it reads its dock markers)
# and an empty `reserve_fuel` ledger with headroom the tender delivers into. It
# runs no dock and no umbilical of its own and never moves under its own power —
# every unit of fuel it gains is the tender delivering it.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/umbilical_berth.toml"
name = "world.probe_npc_resupply.entity.stranded.name"
transform = { position = [100.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_npc_tow.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1163 — a HOSTILE NPC tug locks, tractors and tows a
# disabled craft off, with NO player involvement.
#
# This is the NPC-content mirror of `probe_tractor.toml` (issue #1156). There the
# operator was the backfilled PLAYER ship and the test drove the beam by hand;
# here the operator is a world-spawned NPC (`ship_harrow_tug.toml`) that runs the
# WHOLE procedure itself off authored doctrine — the same `operate_tractor_ai`
# host (#1162), the same admission seam, no NPC-only branch.
#
# WHAT THIS WORLD PROVES (asserted on the prize's OWN state):
#
#   1. THE TUG TOWS THE PRIZE OFF UNAIDED. Handed a `Tow` order naming the prize
#      and a `Retreat` order to its haven, the tug reaches a NON-hostile lock on
#      the prize (the `objective-operate` selector source, #1162 D2), engages its
#      tractor, and flies off — dragging the prize at the authored coupling offset
#      to a position it never started at. No command is ever sent by a player.
#
#   2. THE TOW IS SUBJECT TO THE SAME INTERRUPTIONS. Relocating the prize beyond
#      the tug's reach (range/lock lost) drops the coupling exactly as it would a
#      player's tow — the prize stops following and stays where the towline parted.
#
# The tug's job is authored ENTIRELY as a spawn-time `behaviour.doctrine` override
# (by-id merge over the template's HOLD default) plus the `tug_haven` anchor below
# — no scripting, no hardcoded engage. Nothing about the tug's tractor is authored
# anywhere but its own `[tractor]` table and `[[system]] kind = "tractor"`.

[global]
seed = 1163
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[anchors]
# Where the tug hauls the prize. Well clear of the spawn so a resolved tow is a
# visible haul rather than a nudge, and along -X so it never crosses the distant
# player spawn.
tug_haven = [-1200.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player spawn kept far off and outside AI sensor range, so the AI-backfilled
# player never detects or interferes with the tug. The world still needs it to
# reach InProgress and run the NPC sim.
[player_spawn]
position = [4000.0, 0.0, 4000.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [4000.0, 0.0, 4000.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The hostile tug — the fully AI-crewed operator ────────────────────────────
# Spawned at the origin. The template ships a HOLD default; this override hands it
# the actual job: TOW the prize (Engineering engages the tractor once locked) and
# RETREAT to the haven (Helm flies there, dragging the prize).
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_tug.toml"
name = "world.probe_npc_tow.entity.tug.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "tow-the-prize", directive_kind = "Tow", directive_operate_target = "world.probe_npc_tow.entity.prize.name", base_priority = 90.0 },
  { id = "retreat-to-haven", directive_kind = "Retreat", directive_anchor = "tug_haven", base_priority = 60.0, target_speed = 0.9 },
] } }

# ── The prize — a disabled craft, 80 units off, well inside the tug's 600-unit
# reach and its sensor horizon. A civilian hauler stands in for a hulk (the
# tractor probe uses it the same way): it carries a Transform the beam can
# override and a name the lock + blackboard resolve, and it is given no lane, so
# it drifts nowhere on its own — every metre it moves is the tug towing it.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.probe_npc_tow.entity.prize.name"
transform = { position = [80.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

# Probe world for issue #1167 (S13) — a silent crew completes the ship's external work.
#
# The cross-cutting marquee for PRD #1143. ONE hull — the shipped Alliance
# Destroyer, the only crew ship that carries all four external-work systems (a
# TRACTOR, a DOCK, a transfer UMBILICAL and external repair-team DISPATCH, added
# by #1164 S11a) — backfilled entirely by AI with NOBODY connected, completes a
# TOW, a TRANSFER and a FIELD REPAIR against three named targets. Every engage,
# dock, flow and dispatch is issued by the #1162 backfill hosts off authored
# operate directives on the shared admission seam; the test never sends a system
# command. Progress is read on the TARGETS' own state — the derelict held on the
# rig, the depot's ledger filled, the ally's condition raised.
#
# The name `probe_operations` is the one #1164 S11a freed when it retired the old
# `[operations]`-path world of the same name — this is its replacement, authored
# entirely on the NEW systems (the old operations path is deleted by #1166).
#
# THE CREW SHIP — the shipped destroyer, spawned as the backfilled player ship at
# game start. Three overrides, each the WORLD's own intent re-applied onto the
# picked hull (`server_app::player_hull_config`), never a change to the shipped
# destroyer's committed template:
#
#   * a `reserve_fuel` capacity ledger, so the transfer umbilical has a source to
#     draw from. The destroyer authors NO `[infrastructure]` of its own by design
#     (a ledger would fold into every combat world it flies); this is the same
#     ledger `umbilical_probe.toml` carries, added on this instance only.
#   * a wide tactical-radar horizon, so the weapons `objective-operate` selector
#     (issue #1162) can acquire the non-hostile tow and field-repair targets
#     across the tractor's 500-unit reach and the dispatch's 400 — the shipped
#     50-unit horizon is a close-combat range, not an operations one. The dock and
#     the umbilical need no lock, so only the two lock-driven verbs want this.
#   * a brisk external-dispatch rate, so the field repair reads on the ally's own
#     condition track inside a short deterministic run — the shipped 0.5/s is a
#     thirty-second mission rate. Only the rate is nudged; the 400-unit reach the
#     dispatch host gates on is the destroyer's own.
[global]
seed = 1167
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

overrides = { weapons_console = { radar = { range = 700.0 } }, repair = { external_dispatch = { repair_rate = 20.0 } }, infrastructure = { condition_max = 100.0, decay_per_sec = 0.0, hull_damage_share = 0.0, capacity = [{ id = "reserve_fuel", amount = 100, ceiling = 100 }] } }

base_files.assets/worlds/probe_picket.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1349 — the alternative-resolution half of a standoff.
#
# #1041's `probe_restraint.toml` proves the two GUNNERY endings: a hull driven
# under its own weapons threshold, and a hull destroyed. Those are still its
# tests. What this world proves are the three things #1349 adds, and each of
# them is a claim the shipped `falling_skyway.toml` beat rests on:
#
#   SECURITY RESOLVES IT   A neutral, armed picket authors `secure_contain` and
#                          `board` as ordinary `[[security_target.action]]`
#                          blocks. Nobody sends the teams: the #1346 backfill
#                          host does, through the same `DispatchSecurityTeam` a
#                          human at Tactical emits, and each action's authored
#                          `outcome_flag` is the whole of what reaches the
#                          script. No shot is fired to make either happen.
#
#   BACKFILL DOES NOT      …and the same run's crew never open fire at all. That
#   OPEN FIRE              is the invariant #1349's fourth criterion is about,
#                          and it is asserted on the SAME window that proves the
#                          teams worked: a picket that is merely PRESENT, armed,
#                          and carrying work a backfilled seat wants to do is
#                          still not something a backfilled seat shoots.
#
#   A HOSTILITY CAN END    `remove_faction_enemy` from script, which is the
#                          mechanism the mission's "crossing the threshold ends
#                          the hostile directive" is built on. Measured as a
#                          BEFORE and an AFTER on one hull with nothing else
#                          moving: the destroyer is shooting, the enmity is
#                          withdrawn, and it stops — through the applier's own
#                          AI-target re-validation (#710) rather than through
#                          anything this file knows about locks.
#
# The fourth claim is the timeline's (#1338): a hull the script removes AFTER
# recording an authored outcome is `escaped`, not `destroyed`. That is how the
# mission says a picket flew home rather than died, and it is asserted off the
# run report's own narrative counts.
#
# The comparison shape is `probe_restraint.toml`'s, and it is here for the same
# reason: every claim is a before/after on one hull, or a pair that differs in
# exactly one authored fact.
#
# ── Timeline (60 Hz), in mission seconds ────────────────────────────────────
#
#   t=0    nothing is hostile to anything. The Harrow are neutral by default and
#          this world declares no enmity at load — deliberately, because the
#          whole first window is about what a backfilled bridge does when there
#          is nothing to shoot.
#   ~t=1   the Security backfill sees two pieces of authored work in reach on
#          `probe_picket` and commits both teams: containment first (it is
#          `threat_containment`), boarding second (`optional`).
#   ~t=11  the containment lands: `probe_picket_contained` rises, the handler
#          chains, and the picket's own `weapons` group is commanded to 0.
#   ~t=13  the boarding lands: `probe_picket_boarded` rises.
#   t=10   `probe_leaver` withdraws — an authored `escaped` recorded FIRST, then
#          the removal, in one call. That order is the engine's own contract for
#          "this despawn was not a death".
#   t=18   Harrow and Alliance are made mutually hostile. The destroyer closes
#          on `probe_brawler`, forty units away, and opens fire. The picket is
#          three hundred units off and outside every gun in the world.
#   t=28   the enmity is WITHDRAWN. Both hulls' locks are re-validated away and
#          the shooting stops with both of them still floating.
#
# BASELINE. This world is new in #1349 and has no recorded digest yet. It is a
# probe rather than a shipped scenario, so nothing in `scenarios.toml` names it
# and no shipped world's digest can move because of it.

[global]
seed = 1349
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

# Every hull below is a Harrow patrol boat, and each one's single template
# doctrine entry is re-pointed by id at a station of its own — the per-id edit
# `falling_skyway.toml` and `probe_restraint.toml` both use, and for the same
# reason: a world has to declare every anchor a hull steers to, and naming
# somebody else's border here would be authoring a lie to satisfy a validator.
[anchors]
probe_picket_station = [0.0, 0.0, 300.0]
probe_leaver_station = [0.0, 0.0, -300.0]
probe_brawler_station = [40.0, 0.0, 0.0]

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The crew's own hull, and the ONE shipped hull that musters Security teams. A
# world that flew anything else here would be testing an empty roster.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The subject ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three hundred units out: inside the destroyer's authored Security reach of 400
# and outside every weapon in this world, including its own 50-unit beams. So
# "the teams got there" and "nobody shot anybody" are independent facts rather
# than two readings of one distance.
#
# Armed and neutral, which is the pairing the whole beat needs. Its condition
# threshold is here so the test can assert the mount was never touched: a
# containment that had actually been a quiet gunnery kill would have dropped
# `probe_picket_guns_online` on the way.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
name = "world.probe_picket.entity.picket.name"
narrative = true
transform = { anchor = "probe_picket_station" }

[entity.overrides]
behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "patrol-ironveil", directive_kind = "Reach", directive_anchors = [], directive_loop = false, directive_anchor = "probe_picket_station" },
] }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
publish = false
condition = 100.0
condition_max = 100.0

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "probe_picket_guns_online"
fails_below = 0.35

# The two jobs, in the shipped mission's own priority order and at a tenth of its
# durations — this is a mechanism probe, not a pacing one. No `warning`: the
# field is optional and a probe has no console to show one on.
[entity.overrides.security_target]

[[entity.overrides.security_target.action]]
action = "secure_contain"
duration_secs = 3.0
risk = 0.5
priority = "threat_containment"
outcome_flag = "probe_picket_contained"

[[entity.overrides.security_target.action]]
action = "board"
duration_secs = 5.0
risk = 0.75
priority = "optional"
outcome_flag = "probe_picket_boarded"

# ── The one that leaves ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Identical to the subject but for the two facts under test: it offers no
# Security work, and the script removes it after stating an outcome. Marked, so
# the timeline has something to be right or wrong about.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
name = "world.probe_picket.entity.leaver.name"
narrative = true
transform = { anchor = "probe_leaver_station" }
overrides = { behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "patrol-ironveil", directive_kind = "Reach", directive_anchors = [], directive_loop = false, directive_anchor = "probe_leaver_station" },
] } }

# ── The one that gets shot at ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Forty units out, so the destroyer has something inside its own thirty-unit
# beam once there is a reason to use it. NOT marked: the timeline claim above is
# "no death was recorded in this run", and a hull that could die would make that
# claim about luck.
#
# The hull is authored absurdly heavy for exactly that reason. The A/B this
# world is here for is "it was shooting, then the enmity ended, then it was not"
# — and a target that died in between would satisfy the second sample for the
# wrong reason.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
name = "world.probe_picket.entity.brawler.name"
transform = { anchor = "probe_brawler_station" }
overrides = { hull = { hull_integrity = 20000.0 }, behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "patrol-ironveil", directive_kind = "Reach", directive_anchors = [], directive_loop = false, directive_anchor = "probe_brawler_station" },
] } }

[script]
setup = """
// THE SECURITY SEAM. An action's authored `outcome_flag` is the whole of what a
// finished boarding party reaches the scenario with — an ordinary world flag,
// raised by the engine, meaning nothing to it. Both handlers below are this
// world's, exactly as `falling_skyway.toml`'s are.
on_flag_set("probe_picket_contained", "on_picket_contained");
on_flag_set("probe_picket_boarded", "on_picket_boarded");

on_timer(10, "on_leaver_withdraws");
on_timer(18, "on_enmity_declared");
on_timer(28, "on_enmity_withdrawn");

// CONTAINED. The mounts are locked out from outside, which this world makes real
// the same way the mission does: through the restraint lever (#1041, re-pointed
// at POWER by #1398), applied to an NPC through the same reactor an Engineering
// console commands. The verb name did not change and neither did this call; what
// it writes is now the picket's `weapons` group at level 0.
fn on_picket_contained(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.hold_fire("world.probe_picket.entity.picket.name");
    ctx.flags.picket_contained = 1;
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 1;
}

// BOARDED. A second team, a second job, a second flag — and the pair is the
// point: two teams working two actions on one target at once is what #1346's
// muster is for, and a scenario that could only hear one of them would not be
// able to tell the two endings apart.
fn on_picket_boarded(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.picket_boarded = 1;
}

// WITHDRAWN, not killed. The outcome is recorded BEFORE the removal and in the
// same call, which is the engine's contract for suppressing the automatic death
// beat: the authored `escaped` then stands alone.
fn on_leaver_withdraws(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.leaver_withdrew = 1;
    ctx.effects.narrative_outcome("world.probe_picket.entity.leaver.name", "escaped");
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.probe_picket.entity.leaver.name");
}

fn on_enmity_declared(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.enmity_declared = 1;
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}

// The half this world exists for. Nothing else changes: both hulls are in the
// same places, both are still armed, both are still in range of each other.
// Only the relationship is withdrawn.
fn on_enmity_withdrawn(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.enmity_withdrawn = 1;
    ctx.effects.remove_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.remove_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}
"""
