base_files.assets/worlds/probe_radiation.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1037 — a radiation storm as authored regions, end to
# end.
#
# This is the minimal, operations-free successor to the retired `probe_storm`
# world (#1164, S11a). The retired world proved two things: that a storm band
# SLOWS a tow (an operation consequence the per-system probes now own) and that a
# band is survivable to CROSS and fatal to LIVE IN (radiation DAMAGE, which is
# not an operation at all). Only the second survives here — but the tug/hulk
# pair that sat inside the tow band is KEPT as idle hulls rather than deleted,
# because `regions::server::apply_damage_zone_damage` (#1052) sorts every victim
# inside a damage zone by world id and walks them in one shared draw sequence:
# removing a victim would shift the draws the couriers receive and move the exact
# tick the loiterer dies and the hull fraction the crosser comes out on. So the
# only thing this file drops from the retired world is the `[operations]` tow
# capability and the two `tow` effects — the entity layout is untouched.
#
# The storm is not a system. It is `region_radiation_band.toml` spawned on a
# named deadline (#1024), doing what its composed effects do, and retired with
# `destroy_entity` (#1033).
#
#   loiterer      an Alliance Courier that never leaves the band    -> DESTROYED
#   crosser       the SAME hull, moved out at the authored crossing
#                 time by the test                                  -> survives
#   bystander     the same hull again, 3 km from anything           -> untouched
#
# ── The authored timeline, in mission seconds ────────────────────────────────
#
#   t=2    the `storm_front` deadline fires and spawns the TOW band over the idle
#          tug/hulk pair, into the `storm_bands` group, retiring 18 seconds out.
#   t=3    the `storm_dwell` deadline fires and spawns the DWELL band over the
#          damage pair, into the same group, retiring 97 seconds out.
#   t~89   the loiterer's 200 hull points are gone at the band's effective two
#          and a half points a second, and it is destroyed. The crosser, moved
#          out by the test at the authored crossing time, is not.
#   t=100  the dwell band is retired. NOW `on_all_destroyed("storm_bands")` fires:
#          the corridor is clear, no region entity is left behind.

[global]
seed = 1037
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [6000.0, 0.0, 6000.0]

# The player ship. Present because a world needs one; parked far from any band.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [6000.0, 0.0, 6000.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The idle pair inside the tow band ────────────────────────────────────────
#
# No longer towing anything: these two are kept solely so the damage-zone victim
# set the couriers share a draw sequence with is byte-identical to the retired
# world's. `tug_storm` sits at the tow band's centre; `hulk_storm` beside it.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.tug_storm.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.hulk_storm.name"
transform = { position = [70.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides = { hull = { hull_integrity = 900.0 }, infrastructure = { condition = 30.0, hull_damage_share = 0.0, threshold = [{ flag = "probe_storm_hulk_recovered", fails_below = 0.5 }] } }

# ── The idle pair in clear space ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three kilometres from any band, so never a damage-zone victim; kept only to
# leave the retired world's spawn order and world-id assignment undisturbed.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.tug_clear.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 3000.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_civilian_hauler.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.hulk_clear.name"
transform = { position = [70.0, 0.0, 3000.0] }
overrides = { hull = { hull_integrity = 900.0 }, infrastructure = { condition = 30.0, hull_damage_share = 0.0, threshold = [{ flag = "probe_clear_hulk_recovered", fails_below = 0.5 }] } }

# ── THE DAMAGE PAIR, and the bystander that makes it mean something ──────────
#
# Three Alliance Couriers: 200 hull points each. Two start 150 units either side
# of the dwell band's centre — inside; the bystander is three kilometres clear.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_courier.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.loiterer.name"
transform = { position = [-150.0, 0.0, -3000.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_courier.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.crosser.name"
transform = { position = [150.0, 0.0, -3000.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_courier.toml"
name = "world.probe_storm.entity.bystander.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, -6000.0] }

# ── The sweep's clock ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[deadline]]
id = "storm_front"
label = "world.probe_storm.deadline.storm_front.label"
due_secs = 2
visible = true

[[deadline]]
id = "storm_dwell"
label = "world.probe_storm.deadline.storm_dwell.label"
due_secs = 3
visible = true

[script]
setup = """
on_deadline("storm_front", "on_storm_front");
on_deadline("storm_dwell", "on_storm_dwell");

// Fires only when the LAST band goes. One of two is not the whole storm.
on_all_destroyed("storm_bands", "on_sweep_complete");

fn on_storm_front(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/region_radiation_band.toml",
        name: "storm_band_tow",
        position: [0, 0, 0],
        groups: ["storm_bands"],
    });
    // The band retires itself. A band's DWELL is a property of the band, and a
    // sweep is bands that each carry their own.
    ctx.schedule.in_seconds(18).destroy_entity("storm_band_tow");

    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-sweep-clear",
        text: "world.probe_storm.objective.sweep_clear.text",
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("front_arrived", 1);
}

fn on_storm_dwell(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/region_radiation_band.toml",
        name: "storm_band_dwell",
        position: [0, 0, -3000],
        groups: ["storm_bands"],
    });
    ctx.schedule.in_seconds(97).destroy_entity("storm_band_dwell");
    ctx.flags.increment("dwell_arrived", 1);
}

fn on_sweep_complete(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.complete_objective("obj-sweep-clear");
    ctx.flags.increment("sweep_complete", 1);
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_reach_anchor.toml:
# Probe world for the Reach-anchor regression (Rhai M6 / #984 content triage).
#
# Re-homes the Requiem Courier `Reach`-directive coverage that used to live on
# `before_the_fire.toml` (deleted with the BTF world tree). The courier hull
# (`assets/entities/ship_requiem_courier.toml`) has a single `Reach` directive
# whose `directive_anchor` names `requiem_courier_destination`. A plural/singular
# field mix-up once made that anchor resolve to `""`, so `anchors.get("")` missed,
# the objective produced no travel decision, and the hull sat on its spawn anchor
# for the whole run — nothing failed and nothing logged.
#
# This world reproduces exactly the chain that bug ran through — the template's
# directive fields, this world's anchor table, `plan_helm_travel`'s `Reach` arm,
# and the per-axis helm actuators — and nothing else. Declarative, single-purpose,
# `template_path` composition, like the other `probe_*` test-infra worlds.
#
# Anchor positions are carried over unchanged from the retired
# `before_the_fire.toml` so the re-homed headless test keeps its tuned leg length
# (~350 u) and timings.

[global]
seed = 984
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[anchors]
# The courier's spawn point and the destination its `Reach` directive names —
# both carried over from the retired before_the_fire.toml. The destination sits
# well clear of the spawn so a resolved route is a visible traverse rather than a
# nudge.
requiem_courier             = [-230.0, 0.0, -80.0]
requiem_courier_destination = [-320.0, 0.0, 260.0]

# Player spawn kept far from the courier's leg and well outside AI sensor range,
# so the AI-backfilled player never detects or interferes with the courier. The
# courier's faction (Requiem) is neutral to everyone and the hull is unarmed with
# no Destroy doctrine, so the two never engage regardless — this only keeps the
# radar/sim surfaces apart.
[player_spawn]
position = [1500.0, 0.0, 1500.0]

# Player ship — spawned by spawn_game_start_entities when the game starts, so the
# world reaches InProgress and the low-LOD NPC simulation runs.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [1500.0, 0.0, 1500.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The Requiem Courier — the hull under test. No world-level `name` override, so it
# keeps the template's own `entity.ship_requiem_courier.name`; the headless test
# finds it by that id. Its template `[behaviour]` `Reach` doctrine drives it to
# the `requiem_courier_destination` anchor above.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_requiem_courier.toml"
transform = { anchor = "requiem_courier" }
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_reinforce.toml:
# Probe world for issue #863 — a MID-RUN spawn, and whether a resume can put it
# back.
#
# Every other probe world in this repo spawns whatever it spawns at t=0, which
# is exactly the case a resume never has to think about: a fresh boot of the
# same scenario runs the same `on_timer(0, …)` before it has finished coming up,
# so the ship is already standing by the time a restore looks for it. That made
# `snapshot::restore` an overwrite and nothing else, and it hid a dependency
# nobody had written down — the resume was relying on the fresh app REPLAYING
# the run, not on the save carrying it.
#
# So the reinforcement here arrives at t=3, and the whole world exists to make
# that gap real:
#
#   t=0    the escort is authored, not spawned. It is what a fresh boot puts
#          back by itself, and the restore has to keep waiting for it — a world
#          with nothing authored could not tell the two kinds apart.
#   t=3    `on_reinforce` spawns TWO Harrow cruisers by script, each with an
#          `overrides` block that is the entire reason they are dangerous: the
#          template is the same Alliance cruiser the escort flies, and only the
#          override makes a raider of it. A rebuild from the bare template would
#          put back two friendly ships in the raiders' positions, which is a
#          worse answer than none — hence the assertion in
#          `tests/snapshot_resume.rs` reads the FACTION and the TAGS off the
#          restored hull rather than merely counting ships.
#   t=3+   the two sides are mutually hostile from `on_load`, so the run that
#          follows is a real fight and the capture is of a world in motion.
#
# A capture taken after t=3 therefore names four ships, two of which no fresh
# boot of this file will produce for another three mission seconds — and a
# browser session resuming with nobody at the consoles never produces them at
# all, because it is not replaying anything.
#
# The reinforcements are spawned into a group so `name_to_uuid` and
# `entity_groups` both carry runtime rows: the point of the payload's
# `name_to_uuid` (issue #863) is that a resumed scenario can still say which
# ship it means.
#
# No asteroid field, on purpose. The streamed-belt half of #863 is measured on
# combat_test, which has two; this world is about the roster and nothing else,
# so `belt_ready` is trivially true here and a failure is readable.
#
# BASELINE (this world is new in #863, so this is its first recorded digest):
# `--seed 42 --ticks 900` gives final digest 9446242647445422197
# (3905547180860912765 at tick 0). A NEW number with nothing to compare it
# against — written down here to be what a later change is A/B'd against, the
# way the shipped worlds' digests already are.
#
# The shipped worlds are unmoved by this file's existence, which is the trivial
# half of the claim: nothing here is shared with them. The half worth measuring
# is `probe_destroy`, which spawns two storm bands from script and therefore
# gains an `EntitySpawnOrigin` component on each: it reproduces
# 14665104268980394769 (9365114570161849778 at tick 0) exactly, because the
# record is written to the entity and folded by nothing.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state — the flag stores, the
# trigger latches, the scheduled queues, the named records and CommsState — so
# both this world's baseline and the `probe_destroy` numbers above have moved.
# The claim they support is unaffected: `EntitySpawnOrigin` is still folded by
# nothing, and that was an A/B on a single build.

[global]
seed = 863
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The player ship — spawned by `spawn_game_start_entities` at game start.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# The escort: AUTHORED, so a fresh boot puts it back without any help from a
# save. It is the control for every claim this world makes about the spawned
# pair — if a resume could not restore this one either, the failure would be
# about restores in general rather than about mid-run spawns.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
name = "world.probe_reinforce.entity.escort.name"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 260.0] }

[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");
on_timer(3, "on_reinforce");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}

// The mid-run arrival. Two hulls, one call each, both carrying the override
// that makes them Harrow raiders rather than a second pair of Alliance
// cruisers — the difference a rebuild has to reproduce.
fn on_reinforce(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml",
        name: "probe_raider_a",
        position: [420, 0, 60],
        groups: ["raiders"],
        overrides: #{
            faction: "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc",
            tags: ["ship", "probe_raider"],
        }
    });
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml",
        name: "probe_raider_b",
        position: [420, 0, -60],
        groups: ["raiders"],
        overrides: #{
            faction: "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc",
            tags: ["ship", "probe_raider"],
        }
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("reinforced", 1);
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_restraint.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1041 — the tactical restraint lever, and the one
# interaction that turns it into a choice. Re-pointed at POWER by issue #1398:
# the lever is the same lever and every verb below is unchanged, but what
# `hold_fire` writes is now the target ship's `weapons` power group at level 0
# rather than a hidden captain's boolean, and what a scenario listens for is
# `weapons_cold.*` rather than `weapons_hold.*`.
#
# Two things are under test here and they are deliberately kept apart.
#
#   THE LEVER      one always-armed hostile, held and then released, with its
#                  own fire the only thing that moves. The hull is a Harrow
#                  patrol boat on purpose: its gun line authors
#                  `min_alert_to_fire = 0`, so it is the hull a hold has to beat
#                  the hard way. An implementation that seeded a plain 0.0 for a
#                  hold would pass every test written against an Alliance hull
#                  and fail this one.
#
#   THE CHOICE     two claimants, spawned identical, taken out of the fight two
#                  different ways. One is DISABLED — its condition track driven
#                  below the threshold that owns its gun mount, which silences it
#                  and leaves it alive — and one is DESTROYED. Each writes its
#                  own campaign flags, and the pair is the control the other's
#                  flags are read against: a run that wrote both sets of flags on
#                  one claimant would have proved nothing about either.
#
# The comparison shape is `probe_strike.toml`'s and it is here for the same
# reason: a single held ship that never fired would pass whatever the code did.
# Every claim below is a BEFORE and an AFTER on the same hull, or a pair that
# differs in exactly one authored fact.
#
# ── Timeline (60 Hz), in mission seconds ────────────────────────────────────
#
#   t=0    the Harrow and the Alliance are made mutually hostile. The
#          enforcer is always-armed and in range; it opens fire on its own.
#   t=4    `hold_fire` on the enforcer — its `weapons` group to 0. Its guns
#          stop. Nothing else about the world changes — it is still hostile,
#          still in range, still at whatever alert its own captain policy has it
#          at. The hull authors `[power_groups.weapons] min_level = 0`, which is
#          what makes the order legal; a hull that authored 1 would refuse it.
#   t=8    `release_fire` on the enforcer, back to its authored `default_level`.
#          Its guns resume.
#   ~t=10  the CREW take their OWN weapons cold — an Engineering order, not this
#          script's, which is why no timer below issues it. The mirror flag
#          `weapons_cold.own_ship` goes up, `on_flag_set` chains off it, and the
#          operator watching the corridor reacts. That is the "an authored party
#          reacts to the restraint" half, proved through the flag rather than
#          through a Rust hook.
#   t=14   the disable branch: 80 points off `claimant_disabled`'s condition
#          drops `probe_claimant_guns_online`, `on_flag_cleared` chains, and the
#          handler holds its fire and writes the disabled flags. It is still in
#          the world afterwards, and that is the point.
#   t=18   the destroy branch: `claimant_destroyed` is destroyed outright,
#          `on_destroyed` chains, and the handler writes the destroyed flags.
#
# BASELINE (this world is new in #1041, so this is its first recorded digest).
# Recorded in the commit that added this line, on a clean tree:
#
#   target/release/phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/probe_restraint.toml \
#     --seed 42 --ticks 900 --record target/dig/probe_restraint.ron \
#     --digest-every 0
#
# gives final digest 0x0ef4be7b7d18b64e (1078282553163286478), and
# 18007679616836460502 at tick 0. It is a NEW number, not a preserved one —
# nothing to compare it against yet — so it is written down here to be the thing
# a later change is A/B'd against, the way the other probes' already are.
#
# What legitimately moves it: this file's entity list and positions, the
# authored condition and threshold numbers, the script's timings, the hulls it
# fields, and any engine change to what the authoritative digest folds — which
# under #1041 included the weapons-hold namespace, and this was the first world
# in the repository that put anything in it. What must NOT move with it are the
# shipped worlds — combat_test 14942520827746055774 and patrol
# 11531679067393217131 — because a lever nobody in those worlds pulls folds
# nothing at all.
#
# That last sentence was WRONG for two builds, and the corrections are worth
# recording because they are what the probe fleet is for. The lever's engine
# half moved `probe_storm.toml` — a world with no hold in it anywhere — twice
# over, and neither time through the fold: first because the flag mirror wrote
# through `DerefMut` on every ship's spawn tick and so marked
# `WorldContentRuntime` changed, and then because the new component arrived as a
# SECOND `insert` on the ship spawn path, whose extra queued command and
# archetype move reordered everything spawned after it. The mirror now reads
# before it writes and the component rides the existing bundle nested. Both
# fixes were confirmed the only way they can be: by putting
# 11434311098359716284 back.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state — the flag stores and the
# trigger latches this world's disable/destroy branches write (`on_flag_
# cleared`, `on_destroyed`) among them — so every number above, including the
# two shipped-world anchors, predates `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` and
# does not reproduce on a clean tree. Re-measure before treating any of it as a
# baseline again.
#
# STILL 1078282553163286478 AFTER the AI-thrust-burst fix, and this one is worth
# stating precisely because — unlike combat_test, patrol and falling_skyway,
# which record 0 helm power changes — this world's `ship_harrow_patrol` picket
# DOES resolve the banded rule. It makes exactly two helm power changes across
# the window, and they are BYTE-IDENTICAL banded or not: an elevate, and a shed
# driven by a throttle that falls clean past BOTH edges of the band rather than
# dithering between them. A band only changes an outcome where the throttle
# lingers inside it, so a world whose throttle crosses it outright folds the
# digest it always did. That is a stronger hold than the low-LOD ones above: the
# rule ran, and still decided the same thing.
#
# RECAPTURED IN #1398, AND THIS WORLD IS THE ONLY ONE THAT MOVED.
#
#   target/release/phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/probe_restraint.toml \
#     --seed 42 --ticks 900 --record target/dig/probe_restraint.ron \
#     --digest-every 0
#
# now gives 0x81d494ec84c5c262 (9355266069516108386), where the same command
# against a binary built before this change's Rust half — over these same world
# files, which are neutral, see below — gave 0xb8b06d57b3ae59a9
# (13308257122323945897). Both numbers are post-#1086 and reproduce; the
# pre-#1086 figures above still do not.
#
# THREE things moved it, all deliberate:
#
#   * the `weapons-hold` fold namespace is GONE with the lever it folded, and
#     this is the only world in the repository that ever put a ship in it — so
#     most of the delta is one fold stage's contribution subtracted rather than a
#     run behaving differently;
#   * `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` now authors a `[power_groups.*]` block, with
#     `min_level = 0` on weapons so `hold_fire` is legal on this hull at all;
#   * the two `hold_fire` calls and the `release_fire` move that reactor now
#     rather than a boolean, and the `weapons_cold.*` mirror emits its flag
#     events from `ship::power` rather than from the captain plugin.
#
# THE SHIPPED ANCHORS DID NOT MOVE, and that was A/B'd rather than assumed:
# combat_test folds 0xb912074f990e68a8 (13335729485049129128) and patrol folds
# 0x7044c4b72979b3c3 (8089807121618154435) both before and after the change — a
# lever nobody in those worlds pulls folds nothing at all, and the retired
# namespace folded nothing while nobody held. Reverting only the
# `[power_groups.*]` block on `ship_harrow_patrol.toml` and re-running the same
# two worlds gives those same two numbers again, which is the separate claim the
# block's own comment makes: it transcribes the canonical seeding, so it changes
# nothing except that weapons may now be commanded to 0.

[global]
seed = 1041
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

# Every hull below is a Harrow patrol boat, whose template doctrine patrols the
# Ironveil border. This world declares none of that, so each one's single
# doctrine entry is re-pointed by id at a station of its own — the per-id edit
# `falling_skyway.toml` uses on its corporate cutter, and for the same reason: a
# world has to declare every anchor a hull steers to, and naming somebody else's
# border here would be authoring a lie to satisfy a validator.

[anchors]
probe_enforcer_station = [40.0, 0.0, 0.0]
probe_claimant_a_station = [0.0, 0.0, 1400.0]
probe_claimant_b_station = [0.0, 0.0, 2800.0]

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The crew's own hull. Unnamed, like every other world's player entry: a
# game-start ship is spawned by its own path and a reference name declared here
# would be registered against a uuid that path never uses. The crew's OWN
# restraint is therefore ordered by their Engineering officer rather than by this
# script, and what the script does with it is listen — `weapons_cold.own_ship` is
# keyed by role for exactly this reason.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"

[script]
setup = """
// Mutual enmity first, so the enforcer has something to shoot at. Neither
// faction is hostile to the other by default — the Harrow are "a non-engaging
// neighbour the player must choose to provoke", which is the whole premise of a
// restraint lever.
on_world_loaded("on_load");

on_timer(4, "on_hold_the_enforcer");
on_timer(8, "on_release_the_enforcer");
on_timer(14, "on_cripple_the_claimant");
on_timer(18, "on_kill_the_claimant");

// The two branch chains. Both are the REAL chains: a condition crossing raises
// and drops its own flag through `tick_infrastructure_condition`, and
// `destroy_entity` pushes the same `WorldEvent::Destroyed` a combat kill does.
on_flag_cleared("probe_claimant_guns_online", "on_claimant_disabled");
on_destroyed("world.probe_restraint.entity.claimant_destroyed.name", "on_claimant_destroyed");

// The authored party's reaction to the crew's own restraint (AC3). It reads the
// MIRROR flag, exactly as a scenario condition reads `workforce.<id>.on_strike`
// — no scenario ever touches ship state. Re-keyed from `weapons_hold.own_ship`
// in issue #1398, when the state behind the mirror became the reactor.
on_flag_set("weapons_cold.own_ship", "on_crew_restraint_noticed");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}

fn on_hold_the_enforcer(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.hold_fire("world.probe_restraint.entity.enforcer.name");
    ctx.flags.enforcer_ordered_to_hold = 1;
}

fn on_release_the_enforcer(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.release_fire("world.probe_restraint.entity.enforcer.name");
    ctx.flags.enforcer_released = 1;
}

// The operator watching the corridor notices that the destroyer has taken its
// guns cold, and says so in the only way a probe can: a flag, and a count of
// how many times it has seen it.
fn on_crew_restraint_noticed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.operator_saw_restraint = 1;
    ctx.flags.increment("operator_restraint_notices", 1);
}

fn on_cripple_the_claimant(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.damage_infrastructure("world.probe_restraint.entity.claimant_disabled.name", 80);
}

fn on_kill_the_claimant(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.destroy_entity("world.probe_restraint.entity.claimant_destroyed.name");
}

// ── The two outcomes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Distinct handlers, distinct flags. `restraint_shown` is the campaign-level
// answer and it is written by BOTH, to opposite values, because "how did you
// take it out of the fight?" is one question with two answers rather than two
// unrelated facts.
fn on_claimant_disabled(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.hold_fire("world.probe_restraint.entity.claimant_disabled.name");
    ctx.flags.claimant_disabled = 1;
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 1;
}

fn on_claimant_destroyed(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.claimant_destroyed = 1;
    ctx.flags.restraint_shown = 0;
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_scan.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1032 — the science scan, with everything the reading
# must be derived FROM sitting in the world and nothing it could be copied from
# anywhere at all.
#
# One scanning destroyer and three contacts, chosen so that every branch of the
# derivation and both refusal classes are reachable in one run. No combat and no
# scripted scan: the readings are taken by the TEST, through the ordinary
# admitted `ScanTarget` path, which is the only way to prove the command rides
# the same admission the crew's own console would.
#
#   skyway_depot    a PUBLISHED structure, decaying under its own authored
#                   `decay_per_sec`                  -> a reading that changes on
#                                                       its own, with no author
#                                                       touching a line of copy
#   sealed_depot    a structure the scenario keeps OFF the wire, sitting at
#                   31/100                           -> refused, with the SAME
#                                                       reason a bare rock gets
#   lonely_beacon   no `[infrastructure]` at all     -> refused, same reason
#
# WHAT THIS WORLD PROVES, and why each piece is here:
#
#   1. THE READING IS A DERIVATION. `skyway_depot` loses four condition points a
#      second, authored on the entity and driven by nobody. Two scans taken from
#      the SAME position a few seconds apart therefore report different numbers,
#      and cross the depot's own 40 % threshold in between so the operational
#      flag reads out as failed on the second. There is no scan text in this
#      file, in the entity template, or in `strings.csv` — the only prose ids
#      anywhere near it are the labels the depot's own capacity and threshold
#      authored, which name the QUANTITIES rather than the finding.
#
#   2. FIDELITY IS AUTHORED AND THE CREW CONTROL IT. The destroyer's shipped
#      `[scan]` ladder is used as authored — detailed inside 120 units, coarse
#      out to 260, nothing past that — so the test flies the ship rather than
#      editing a number. The same depot at the same instant reads whole percent
#      from close in and quarters from further out, and stops reporting berths
#      at all, because the coarse band authors `report_capacities = false`.
#
#   3. THE PUBLISH GATE IS NOT A DOOR THE SCAN OPENS. `sealed_depot` authors
#      `publish = false` and a real, live 31 points. #1025's `from_state` is the
#      single gate every console surface goes through and the scan is one, so it
#      is refused — and refused with the identical reason `lonely_beacon` gets,
#      because an error that distinguished "nothing to read" from "something I am
#      not telling you" would leak the secret by its shape.
#
# The two labelled fields on `skyway_depot` are the second gate, the same one
# #1030 uses: a capacity or threshold id is a machine name in the author's
# namespace, so it reaches a readout only where the scenario also authored a
# `strings.csv` label for it. `depot_transfer_throughput` is left unlabelled on
# purpose — published data a script can read, and prose the console never shows.
#
# BASELINE (headless, `--seed 42 --ticks 900`, no --ship, clean tree):
# final digest 0x6cf7680c58c8e132 (7851858877582205234).
#
# The three shipped anchors are UNMOVED by this slice, measured rather than
# assumed: combat_test 14942520827746055774, patrol 11531679067393217131,
# falling_skyway 1501629821237961665. All three fly the destroyer, which now
# authors a `[scan]` table and therefore carries a scan record and publishes a
# scan channel — and neither is folded, which is exactly the claim.
#
# Nothing this world exists to exercise is IN that digest. A scan reading is
# authoritative but unfolded, in the same bucket as the deadline table, the
# commitments ledger and the evidence log; what moves this number is the depot's
# condition track and the entity population, both of which #1025 already folds —
# and the decay authored below is exactly that, walking every tick. If a later
# change moves this digest without moving either, something started folding a
# scan, and that is the question to ask before re-blessing this line.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER SAFE TO ASSUME. The BUCKET named above just
# emptied: issue #1086's `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` now walks the
# deadline table, the commitments ledger and the evidence log this paragraph
# names as a scan reading's unfolded company. This world puts nothing in any of
# them — no `[script]` block, no deadline, no commitment, no evidence entry —
# so a scan reading stays exactly as unfolded as the paragraph above claims, and
# the number MAY still reproduce on the empty-walk affordance the fold gives a
# scenario-free world. "May" is doing the work: this line has not been
# re-measured since #1086, so it is recorded here as pre-#1086 provenance
# rather than re-blessed as current. Re-measure before treating it as a
# baseline again.

ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

# The scanning ship. The destroyer's own shipped `[scan]` ladder is used

# ── The subject: a published structure coming apart on its own ───────────────
# 62 of 100 points, losing four a second. Its capacity and threshold tables are

base_files.assets/worlds/probe_scandiff.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1038 — the scan-versus-dossier diff, with the two
# facts it is made of pulled apart so neither can be mistaken for the other.
#
# The slice's claim is that the mismatch is a GENUINE COMPARISON: it falls out of
# the structure's authored condition measured against the standard its own
# paperwork claims, and it is only ever reached by a crew who went and took a
# reading. A world that fired the beat off "the player pressed scan" would look
# identical from the outside on a single run — so this world runs the whole
# truth table at once, on four rungs authored IDENTICALLY except for the one
# number under test.
#
#   ladder_frayed     31/100, static, under the recorded standard
#                     SCANNED     -> the diff is filed
#   ladder_sound      78/100, static, over the recorded standard
#                     SCANNED     -> nothing is filed, ever. The derivation.
#   ladder_unread     31/100, static, under the recorded standard — the same
#                     structure as `ladder_frayed` in every authored respect
#                     NEVER SCANNED -> nothing is filed. The control.
#   ladder_slipping   78/100, losing four points a second under its own authored
#                     `decay_per_sec`
#                     SCANNED EARLY, while the paperwork still holds up ->
#                     nothing at the time, and the diff files itself later, on
#                     the tick the condition crosses the claim.
#
# Read the first three together and the two dimensions separate cleanly. Frayed
# against Sound is the DERIVATION: the only difference between them is
# `condition`, and it decides whether the crew find anything — nobody edits a
# line of copy to make that happen. Frayed against Unread is the ACT: the only
# difference is whether the crew took a reading, and it decides the same thing.
# Neither structure knows which run it is in.
#
# `ladder_slipping` is the fourth corner, and it is what proves the beat is a
# comparison rather than a scan handler wearing one's clothes. The scan comes
# back at a moment the record is still defensible and files nothing. The finding
# arrives afterwards, with nobody scanning anything, because the OTHER half of
# the comparison moved. A flag flip triggered by the scan could not do that.
#
# ── How the two halves are authored ─────────────────────────────────────────
#
# WHAT THE PAPERWORK SAYS is one authored number and one authored string, and
# they are the same claim written for two different readers:
#
#   `<id>_meets_record` / `fails_below = 0.6`   for the simulation
#   `…evidence.record_certified` (BRIEFING)     for the crew, on the fact sheet
#
# WHAT THE STRUCTURE IS is `condition`, and #1025 mirrors the threshold into the
# world flag store every tick. So "does this rung still support what its file
# says about it" is a question the flag store answers, live, and the script that
# asks it holds no copy of either number.
#
# WHETHER THE CREW LOOKED is `scan.<id>.taken` (issue #1038), latched by
# `tick_scans` the first time a reading of that structure comes back. The scans
# are taken by the TEST through the ordinary admitted `ScanTarget` path — there
# is no scripted scan in this file — which is the only way to prove the gate is
# the crew's own act.
#
# There is no scan text anywhere here, in the template, or in `strings.csv`. The
# two prose ids are the record's CLAIM and the finding that it does not hold,
# and neither describes a reading.
#
# BASELINE (release headless, `--seed 42 --ticks 900 --digest-every 0`, no
# `--ship` override — the invocation probe_scan.toml and probe_evidence.toml
# record): final digest 0x2287d33988fc6bbe (2488189563210329022). A NEW number —
# nothing to compare it against yet — so it is written down to be the thing a
# later change is A/B'd against, the way the shipped worlds' digests already are.
# Tick 0 is 16510709998228443533.
#
# The anchors were measured on the same clean tree and are UNMOVED: combat_test
# 14942520827746055774, patrol 11531679067393217131, probe_evidence
# 5001167740764356580, probe_scan 7851858877582205234, probe_strike
# (--ticks 1800) 535291289754814419, and probe_storm (--ticks 6480)
# 11434311098359716284. `falling_skyway` DID move, and its own header carries
# the A/B that attributes the move to one authored threshold rather than to
# anything this world does.
#
# What is IN that digest is the four condition tracks and the entity population,
# both of which #1025 folds, and `ladder_slipping`'s decay walks one of them
# every tick. What is NOT in it is everything this world exists to exercise: an
# evidence entry, a flag-store counter and a scan reading are all authoritative
# but unfolded, in the same bucket as the deadline table and the commitments
# ledger. If a later change moves this number without moving a condition track,
# something started folding scenario state, and that is the question to ask
# before re-blessing this line.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. The BUCKET named above just
# folded: issue #1086's `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records` now walks the
# deadline table and the commitments ledger this paragraph names, and this
# world's own `record_filed`/`records_diff_found` flag counters and its five
# `on_world_loaded`/`on_flag_set`/`on_flag_cleared` trigger latches are exactly
# the FlagStore and `trigger_states` entries that fold walks. The evidence entry
# and the raw scan reading are still unfolded — nothing above puts either in a
# folded field — but the number above predates the fold that now walks the
# flags and triggers around them, so it does not reproduce on a clean tree.
# Re-measure before treating it as a baseline again.

[global]
seed = 1038
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The scanning ship. The destroyer's shipped `[scan]` ladder is used unmodified,
# so the run tests the hull the demo actually flies rather than a fixture.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# ── The rung whose file does not survive a look ──────────────────────────────
# 31 of 100 against a record that claims 60. Every other line below is repeated
# verbatim on the three rungs that follow; this is the one that is different.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "ladder_frayed"
name = "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_frayed.name"
transform = { position = [600.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 31.0
# The template's shared `depot_transfer_throughput` is dropped rather than
# inherited four times: a capacity id is the SCENARIO's namespace, and four
# rungs publishing one counter would be declaring one number between them.
capacity = []

# THE RECORDED STANDARD, in the form the simulation can check. The operator's
# file says this rung was inspected and re-rated at the certified load standard;
# `fails_below` is that claim as a number, and #1025 mirrors the answer into
# `ladder_frayed_meets_record` every tick off the LIVE condition. Move the
# condition above 60 and the flag comes up and the diff goes away, which is
# exactly what `ladder_sound` is.
[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "ladder_frayed_meets_record"
fails_below = 0.6
label = "world.probe_scandiff.threshold.certified_load.label"

# ── The rung whose file is true ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# 78 of 100. Identical authoring, identical record, identical handler, scanned
# by the same test from the same distance — and nothing is ever filed about it.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "ladder_sound"
name = "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_sound.name"
transform = { position = [1200.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 78.0
capacity = []

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "ladder_sound_meets_record"
fails_below = 0.6
label = "world.probe_scandiff.threshold.certified_load.label"

# ── The rung the crew never looked at ────────────────────────────────────────
# The same 31 points as `ladder_frayed`, sitting there being wrong for the whole
# run with nobody pointing anything at it. Its file stays as clean as the sound
# rung's, which is the point: the discrepancy is discoverABLE, not automatic.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "ladder_unread"
name = "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_unread.name"
transform = { position = [2400.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 31.0
capacity = []

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "ladder_unread_meets_record"
fails_below = 0.6
label = "world.probe_scandiff.threshold.certified_load.label"

# ── The rung that goes wrong after the crew have read it ─────────────────────
# Starts at 78 — over the standard, so a scan taken now agrees with the file —
# and sheds four points a second, driven by nobody. Somewhere past the fourth
# second it crosses 60, the flag falls, and the comparison that already had half
# its answer completes itself. Nothing scans anything in between.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/depot_transfer.toml"
id = "ladder_slipping"
name = "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_slipping.name"
transform = { position = [1800.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[entity.overrides.infrastructure]
condition = 78.0
decay_per_sec = 4.0
capacity = []

[[entity.overrides.infrastructure.threshold]]
flag = "ladder_slipping_meets_record"
fails_below = 0.6
label = "world.probe_scandiff.threshold.certified_load.label"

[script]
setup = """
// The record is handed over at world load, before anybody has looked at
// anything — a crew are given the operator's paperwork with the mission.
on_world_loaded("file_the_official_record");

// THE TWO HALVES OF THE COMPARISON, each arriving on its own event. Neither is
// a scan handler: both call the same `compare`, which asks its two questions in
// the same order whichever side woke it.
on_flag_set("scan.ladder_frayed.taken",   "on_frayed_read");
on_flag_set("scan.ladder_sound.taken",    "on_sound_read");
on_flag_set("scan.ladder_unread.taken",   "on_unread_read");
on_flag_set("scan.ladder_slipping.taken", "on_slipping_read");
on_flag_cleared("ladder_slipping_meets_record", "on_slipping_slipped");

// ── What the paperwork says ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
// A BRIEFING entry, because being handed a document is itself a provenance: the
// crew can tell the operator's claim from their own reading, and a crew who
// cannot do that cannot argue with the claim. Every rung gets the same file.
fn file_the_official_record(ctx) {
    record_claim(ctx, "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_frayed.name");
    record_claim(ctx, "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_sound.name");
    record_claim(ctx, "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_unread.name");
    record_claim(ctx, "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_slipping.name");
    ctx.flags.increment("record_filed", 1);
}

fn record_claim(ctx, subject) {
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    subject,
        text:       "world.probe_scandiff.evidence.record_certified",
        provenance: "briefing",
    });
}

// ── The comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// TWO READS OF THE WORLD AND NO MEMORY OF ITS OWN. `scanned` is the crew's act
// (#1038's mirror, latched by the tick that took the reading); `meets_record` is
// #1025's live answer to the standard the rung's own file claims. Nothing here
// knows what the reading SAID, which is what keeps this a comparison rather than
// a reveal: re-author the condition over the standard and the second guard
// returns, with no line of copy touched.
fn compare(ctx, subject, scanned, meets_record) {
    if ctx.flags[scanned] == 0 { return; }
    if ctx.flags[meets_record] > 0 { return; }
    ctx.dossier.append(#{
        subject:    subject,
        text:       "world.probe_scandiff.evidence.record_contradicted",
        provenance: "records",
    });
    ctx.flags.increment("records_diff_found", 1);
}

fn on_frayed_read(ctx) {
    compare(ctx,
        "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_frayed.name",
        "scan.ladder_frayed.taken",
        "ladder_frayed_meets_record");
}

fn on_sound_read(ctx) {
    compare(ctx,
        "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_sound.name",
        "scan.ladder_sound.taken",
        "ladder_sound_meets_record");
}

fn on_unread_read(ctx) {
    compare(ctx,
        "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_unread.name",
        "scan.ladder_unread.taken",
        "ladder_unread_meets_record");
}

fn on_slipping_read(ctx) {
    compare(ctx,
        "world.probe_scandiff.entity.ladder_slipping.name",
        "scan.ladder_slipping.taken",
        "ladder_slipping_meets_record");
}

// The other side of the same comparison, and the same function. The crew read

        "scan.ladder_slipping.taken",
        "ladder_slipping_meets_record");
}
"""
base_files.assets/worlds/probe_strike_min.toml:
# Probe world for issue #1035 — the labour-dispute REGISTER, end to end.
#
# This is the minimal, operations-free successor to the retired `probe_strike`
# world (#1164, S11a). The retired world proved the whole strike slice: that a
# `work_stoppage` interrupt REFUSES a transfer and SLOWS a repair. Those are
# consequences the operation verbs impose, and the per-system probes now own
# that ground — so what survives here is the part that is NOT about operations:
# the workforce register itself, its mirror into the ordinary flag store, and
# the settlement lever a dialogue pulls.
#
# ── The dispute ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Two sides, and the second one exists to be the control. `probe_operator` is
# never on strike, so a run reads both halves of a side's state — the status the
# operations tick used to read, and the disposition a negotiation moves.
#
# ── The reversal, and the lever that drives it ───────────────────────────────
#
# At t=10 s a handler sets an ordinary world flag. `on_flag_set` chains off it
# and settles the strike — the SAME seam #1036's negotiation pulls, authored
# here so the restoration is proved through the path a dialogue pick will take
# rather than by a test reaching into the register.
#
# Timeline (60 Hz), in mission seconds:
#
#   t=0    the register arms from `[[workforce]]`: `probe_workers` OUT at a
#          disposition of 20, `probe_operator` at work at 60. Both mirror into
#          ordinary world flags a script condition can read.
#   t=10   `settle_the_strike` sets `probe_strike_settled`; `on_flag_set` fires
#          `on_settled`, which settles `probe_workers` and moves what they make
#          of the crew from 20 to 70.

[global]
seed = 1035
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

# ── The dispute ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[workforce]]
id = "probe_workers"
label = "world.probe_strike.workforce.workers.label"
on_strike = true
# [ai] Low, and it moves at the settlement — so the run exercises both halves of
# a side's state.
disposition = 20

[[workforce]]
id = "probe_operator"
label = "world.probe_strike.workforce.operator.label"
disposition = 60

[player_spawn]
position = [6000.0, 0.0, 6000.0]

# The player ship. Present because a world needs one; parked far away and idle.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_cruiser.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [6000.0, 0.0, 6000.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

[script]
setup = """
on_timer(10, "settle_the_strike");

// THE SEAM. The settlement is chained off an ordinary world flag rather than
// wired straight into the timer, because that is the shape #1036's negotiation
// needs: whoever sets the flag — a dialogue pick, a deadline, a later act — gets
// the same settlement, applied in one place.
on_flag_set("probe_strike_settled", "on_settled");

fn settle_the_strike(ctx) {
    ctx.flags.probe_strike_settled = 1;
}

fn on_settled(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.settle_strike("probe_workers");
    // The other half of a side's state, moved at the same beat: they are back
    // at work AND they think better of the crew for it. [ai] Unratified.
    ctx.effects.set_workforce_disposition("probe_workers", 70);
    ctx.flags.increment("strike_settled_handled", 1);
}
"""

base_files.assets/worlds/probe_targeted_pass.toml:
# Probe world for issue #875 — a TARGETED Destroy objective over a backfilled
# attack-pass hull.
#
# The sibling probe (`probe_duel.toml`) authors an UNTARGETED Destroy, which is
# what every shipped hostile TOML authors. This world authors the other kind, and
# the difference is not cosmetic: a *named* Destroy target is the only shape that
# reaches `operate_navigation_ai`'s objective arm, which guards on
# `!target.is_empty()`. That arm sets the ship's own `NavigationWaypoint`,
# ANCHORED to the named target, and `issue_navigate_to_clearance` latches the
# clearance for the whole engagement (re-setting an anchored waypoint that merely
# moves is idempotent, so the generation never bumps again).
#
# So on any hull that declares a navigation system — every Alliance hull does,
# and backfill automates every station-owned system — a mission that names a
# Destroy target puts a permanently-cleared waypoint on the ship's own Helm. That
# is the exact state in which the planner's "a navigation order outranks the
# authored manoeuvre" precedence must NOT fire, because the order and the
# manoeuvre name the same destination. Every mission in the campaign that names a
# Destroy target sits in this state; `probe_duel` sits in none of it.
#
# The target is a second copy of the SAME hull, re-factioned. It is therefore
# not inert: it ships `destroy-hostiles` at `base_priority = 45`, the attack-pass
# class doctrine, and the Alliance captain's first-contact red-alert rule, so it
# manoeuvres and returns fire and the engagement is real. Using the player hull
# for both sides is deliberate — the state under test is the interaction between
# a hull's OWN backfilled Navigation and its OWN authored manoeuvre, and the
# quickest way to be sure the target reproduces every part of that is to make it
# the same hull.
#
# Because the target manoeuvres, the metric cannot be a range trace. A range
# trace was tried first and rejected: both a hull that flew its pass and one
# whose Navigation stood the doctrine down carry ~15 units/s of momentum out of
# the merge and open comparable daylight before either can turn, and a target
# closing under its own doctrine moves the range further still. So the range
# assertion in the test (`min_range < 40.0`) is only the weak claim that the two
# hulls met at all — it can be satisfied by the TARGET doing the closing.
#
# The load-bearing assertion is the escape-heading one: per-tick, the hull's own
# yaw against the `escape_heading_rad` its Steering policy froze at the merge.
# Only the pass arm flies that frozen heading and deliberately stops looking at
# the target for the authored dwell; a hull whose Navigation redirected it curls
# back onto the anchored waypoint and ends up flying the reciprocal.

[global]
seed = 875
ai_helm_tick_hz = 30.0

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# Player ship — the headless runner's `--ship` supersedes this template; the
# entry exists so `spawn_game_start_entities` has a player to spawn.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id = "player-ship"
transform = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on = "game_start"

# Make Harrow and Alliance mutually hostile before the target spawns, so the
# Alliance captain doctrine's first-contact rule raises Red Alert on sight and the
# movement `posture` fact presses the class doctrine. Then spawn the named target
# and author the mission `Destroy` objective that names it. `objectives.rs` gives
# every Destroy objective `SystemAffinity::Helm`, which is what makes it the top
# Helm-relevant objective both `helm_destroy_target` and `operate_navigation_ai`
# read.
[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");
on_timer(0, "on_start");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
}

fn on_start(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.spawn_entity(#{
        template_path: "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml",
        name: "probe_target",
        position: [0, 0, -70],
        overrides: #{ faction: "cccccccc-3333-4333-8333-cccccccccccc" }
    });
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-destroy-target",
        text: "world.probe_targeted_pass.trigger.action.obj_destroy_target.text",
        mandatory: true,
        targets: ["probe_target"],
        target: "probe_target",
        directive_kind: "Destroy",
        base_priority: 80
    });
}
"""

base_files.assets/worlds/reinforcements.toml:
# Reinforcements Layer
#
# Loaded as a layer on top of default.toml when raider_alpha first takes
# damage (on_attacked trigger in default.toml).  Spawns a second raider at
# the patrol_beta position (~370 units from player start).
#
# (#892) The hull was `pirate_raider_reinforcement.toml`, retired alongside
# `pirate_raider.toml`: it was the same 30-hull stat block under the same
# "Harrow Destroyer" display string, differing only in omitting the retreat
# doctrine, so keeping it would have preserved the exact name collision the
# retirement exists to fix. It is now the same Ironveil-class hull default.toml
# flies for `raider_alpha`, which is what a reinforcement for that ship should
# be — and the ONE thing that made the variant a variant is preserved by
# omission rather than by a second file: this layer authors no
# `retreat-when-hurt` entry, so raider_beta fights to the death where
# raider_alpha runs for the haven.
#
# This file is intentionally minimal — it defines only what is needed
# for the reinforcement encounter.  Anchors from default.toml (patrol_alpha,
# patrol_beta, patrol_gamma) are used by the AI for patrol waypoints after
# the pursue/attack phase ends.

[global]
seed = 43
title = "world.reinforcements.global.title"
description = "world.reinforcements.global.description"

[anchors]
# The raider's patrol circuit, copied verbatim from default.toml (the only
# world that loads this layer).
#
# `patrol_beta` is also the spawn anchor, and has to be here for that reason
# alone: entity position resolution uses the LAYER's own anchor map, not the
# base world's, so `spawn_immediate_entities_internal` could not place the ship
# without it.
#
# `patrol_alpha` and `patrol_gamma` are the other two waypoints of the patrol
# route this ship flies after the pursue/attack phase ends — retargeted onto
# this circuit by the spawn override below, exactly as default.toml retargets
# raider_alpha's. At runtime they resolve against default.toml's
# table (doctrine anchors are read from the base world), so the route worked
# without them — but a layer that names three waypoints and declares one
# cannot be checked, and reads as two typos to anything that tries
# (`validate_composition`, issue #888). Declaring the whole circuit states the
# route this layer expects rather than leaving two thirds of it implied.
patrol_alpha = [600.0, 0.0, -600.0]
patrol_beta  = [500.0, 0.0, -300.0]
patrol_gamma = [200.0, 0.0, -600.0]

# ── Named entities ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Override only retargets `patrol-ironveil`'s anchors and does not touch
# `base_priority`, so the #892 picket rebase applies here unmodified: this hull
# now holds its route until fired upon (Patrol 45 > Destroy 38 undisturbed;
# attacked flips it to 63 > 30), superseding the old engage-on-sight reading.
# Flagged for review if engage-on-sight is actually wanted for this raider.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/ship_harrow_patrol.toml"
name          = "world.entity.raider_beta.name"
transform     = { anchor = "patrol_beta" }
overrides = { tags = ["ship", "npc", "enemy"], behaviour = { doctrine = [
  { id = "patrol-ironveil", directive_anchors = ["patrol_alpha", "patrol_beta", "patrol_gamma"] },
] } }
base_files.assets/worlds/rng_coverage.toml:
# RNG Coverage Scenario (issue #837)
#
# A test fixture, not a playable mission. It exists to drive *all five* seeded
# damage chokepoints — beam, torpedo, blaster, collision and region — inside a
# short headless run, so `tests/rng_determinism.rs`'s determinism guard fails
# when any one of them regresses to OS entropy.
#
# The guard it backs used to run on `combat_test.toml`, which over the tested
# window produced beam traffic and nothing else: four of the five sites could
# be neutered with the whole suite still green. Everything here is arranged to
# make each site fire quickly and to make its result *observable* in the exit
# report, which means every one of them has to land on the player ship — only
# the player's `damaged_systems` reveals which system `apply_hull_damage`
# picked. Damage dealt to NPCs is invisible to the report, because the total a
# hull absorbs is RNG-independent; only the distribution varies.
#
# ── BASELINE ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# No digest was recorded here until the AI-thrust-burst fix moved it. Measured on
# a clean tree with the debug binary:
#
#   target/debug/phoenix-headless --world assets/worlds/rng_coverage.toml \
#     --seed 42 --ticks 900 --record target/rng_coverage.ron --digest-every 0
#
# CURRENT VALUE: 8393867315677906854, moved from 8980983873395264945 by the
# `thrust_release_threshold` band on `entities/test/rng_coverage_lancer.toml`
# (and on the player cruiser's inherited fleet baseline). The old number was only
# ever measured, never claimed here; it is the lineage, not a former assertion.
#
# THIS WORLD IS WHERE THE DEFECT WAS CAUGHT, which is why it moves. Its two
# lancers fly a geometry that parks a throttle right on 0.70 and dithers there,
# and before the band `lancer_alpha` changed helm power level 18 times across an
# 1800-tick run — sixteen of them inside 38 ticks, battery at 57-59 %, nowhere
# near its 50 % shed floor. Banded, the same run makes 4 changes, and
# `tests/headless_runner.rs`'s
# `a_helm_power_level_holds_instead_of_strobing_at_the_thrust_threshold` pins
# that here rather than leaving it to this digest.
#
# What must NOT move with this: the two shipped worlds, combat_test
# 14942520827746055774 and patrol 11531679067393217131, and the pure-content
# probes. Both shipped worlds field banded hulls and both hold, because their
# NPCs stay at low LOD across the window and `ai_power_allocation` is
# `With<AiHighFidelity>`.
#
# RECORDED PRE-#1086, AND NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. Issue #1086 widened the
# authoritative digest over the scenario's own state, and this world's
# `on_world_loaded` trigger — the one that makes Harrow and Alliance mutually
# hostile and posts the patrol objective — is a latch on
# `WorldContentRuntime::trigger_states`, now walked by
# `sim_digest::fold_scenario_records`, which did not happen when any number
# above (this world's own, or the two shipped-world anchors) was measured.
# Re-measure before treating any of it as a baseline again.
#
# UNMOVED BY ISSUE #1053, and worth writing down because a reader who got this
# far would expect the opposite. #1053 changed what happens when a helm power
# shed leaves a hull ABOVE its new speed cap: the excess used to be deleted in
# the tick the modifier changed, and is now bled off on the hull's own
# `deceleration`. This world sheds helm power — four times across the window,
# which is the whole point of the paragraph above — and its digest does not
# move by a bit.
#
# A shed is not the condition. Being over the cap when one lands is, because
# that is the only case the old clamp ever bit. Instrumenting the over-cap
# branch itself and counting the integration steps that take it: 761 in `duel`,
# ZERO here. The lancers dither a throttle around 0.70, so they sit well below
# any cap the helm channel can hand them, and a shed moves their ceiling without
# ever touching their speed. `duel` is a ten-ship brawl with every hull at
# flank, which is where the two conditions coincide — and it is the only one of
# the seventeen anchors that moves.
#
# Layout — everything sits on top of everything else at the origin:
#   - Player spawns at [0, 0, 0].
#   - Two RNG-coverage escorts 45u away, inside their own weapons envelope from
#     tick one. That hull is the only one carrying phasers *and* blasters *and*
#     torpedoes, which is what covers three of the five sites — and since #954
#     it is a TEST FIXTURE (`assets/entities/test/rng_coverage_lancer.toml`)
#     rather than a shipped fleet hull, because "fires everything" is a shape
#     no ship the game actually ships has. This world is its only consumer.
#   - A radiation zone centred on the spawn: region damage from t=0.
#   - An asteroid field whose inner radius reaches the spawn point, so the
#     player is manoeuvring inside rocks and collides while it fights.
#
# Deliberately no `[global] seed`: the guard passes `--seed` explicitly, and a
# world seed here would make the "world" tier of the precedence chain the thing
# under test rather than the CLI tier.

[global]
title = "world.rng_coverage.global.title"
description = "world.rng_coverage.global.description"

# A tight patrol triangle, all of it well inside the radiation zone's 120u
# sphere. The player has to be *moving* for the collision chokepoint to matter
# — collision damage is proportional to speed, so a ship parked at the origin
# rides through asteroids for free — but it also has to stay inside the zone
# and inside the escorts' weapons envelope, hence the small radius.
[anchors]
patrol_a = [55.0, 0.0, 0.0]
patrol_b = [-30.0, 0.0, 45.0]
patrol_c = [-30.0, 0.0, -45.0]

# ── Static map entities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Radiation zone over the whole engagement, so the region chokepoint fires
# every tick from t=0. Stock is 8 dps / 0.3 pierce; both are overridden below.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/region_radiation_zone.toml"
name          = "world.entity.rng_coverage_zone.name"
transform     = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
# Turned right down from the stock 8 dps and set to full pierce. The zone only
# has to keep the region chokepoint landing hull damage every tick; at stock
# strength it kills the player long before the slower weapons have had a turn.
# Full pierce also sidesteps `apply_uniform_damage`'s integer rounding, which
# silently discards any per-tick shield damage below half a point.
#
# 0.9375 is not a rounded-off number, it is an exact one: at the 30 Hz tick this
# scenario runs at, `dps * dt` is 0.03125 — a power of two, and so exactly
# representable in f32. The zone fires thousands of times over the run and the
# report sums every hit into `damage_taken`; at a dps whose per-tick damage is
# not exactly representable, that sum accumulates rounding and the last printed
# decimal place stops being reproducible. The guard compares reports byte for
# byte, so "close enough" is not.
overrides     = { effects = { damage_zone = { damage_per_second = 0.9375, shield_pierce = 1.0 } } }

# Asteroid field pulled in to the origin. `asteroid_field_main` normally rings
# r=300..350; overridden to start at 0 so rocks stream in around the player
# instead of somewhere it would have to fly to.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/asteroid_field_main.toml"
id            = "coverage-belt"
transform     = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
overrides     = { asteroid_field = { inner_radius = 0.0, outer_radius = 400.0, density = 0.02 } }

# ── Hostiles ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Two of them, close in and on opposite sides, so the player is inside somebody's
# firing arc regardless of which way it turns.

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/test/rng_coverage_lancer.toml"
name          = "world.entity.lancer_alpha.name"
transform     = { position = [45.0, 0.0, 0.0] }

[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/test/rng_coverage_lancer.toml"
name          = "world.entity.lancer_beta.name"
transform     = { position = [-45.0, 0.0, 20.0] }

# ── Player ship ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

[player_spawn]
position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

# The player ship is spawned from the headless `--ship` template, not from this
# `[[entity]]` block, so a world-file `overrides` on it would be ignored. The
# one thing the scenario needs done to the player that TOML cannot reach — its
# shields dropped to zero so the escorts' torpedoes will engage it — the test
# harness does directly after spawn. See `rng_determinism.rs`.
[[entity]]
template_path = "assets/entities/alliance_destroyer.toml"
id            = "player-ship"
transform     = { position = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] }
spawn_on      = "game_start"

# ── Triggers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Harrow and Alliance default to neutral in the faction TOMLs so the same
# hulls can appear as ambient patrols elsewhere; without this both escorts sit
# next to the player without ever acquiring it as a target, and three of the
# five chokepoints never fire. Both directions, on world load, before the first
# targeting tick — the same pattern `combat_test.toml` uses.
[script]
setup = """
on_world_loaded("on_load");

fn on_load(ctx) {
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Harrow", "Alliance");
    ctx.effects.add_faction_enemy("Alliance", "Harrow");
    // The player's AI helm needs somewhere to be going. Without a directive the
    // backfilled crew parks at the spawn point at zero speed, and collision
    // damage — which scales with speed — rounds to nothing.
    ctx.effects.add_objective(#{
        id: "obj-rng-coverage-patrol",
        text: "world.rng_coverage.trigger.action.obj_patrol.text",
        mandatory: true,
        source: "mission",
        base_priority: 40,
        directive_kind: "Patrol",
        directive_anchors: ["patrol_a", "patrol_b", "patrol_c"],
        directive_loop: true
    });
}
"""
